SA_MB_IPV_HK.summary: The Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī is Abhinavagupta's commentary on Utpaladeva's foundational treatise, the Īśvarapratyabhijñā / Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā, transmitted here with the sub-commentary Bhāskarī by Bhāskara. It expounds non-dual Śaivism and the philosophy of Pratyabhijñā.
SA_MB_IPV_HK.attribution: The root kārikās are by Utpaladeva. The primary commentary (vimarśinī) is by Abhinavagupta. The sub-commentary (ṭīkā/vyākhyā titled Bhāskarī) is by Bhāskara.
SA_MB_IPV_HK.edition: K. C. Pandey (ed.), Bhāskarī: a commentary on the īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī of Abhinavagupta, Princess of Wales Sarasvati Bhavana Text Series no. 70, Allahabad: Print and Stationery, United Provinces, 1938.
SA_MB_IPV_HK.coverage: complete — Ends with the concluding colophon 'iti pratyabhijñāsūtravimarśinīvyākhyā samāptā'.
translations: Raffaele Torella (trans.), The Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā of Utpaladeva with the Author's Vṛtti: Critical edition and annotated translation, Motilal Banarsidass Publishers, Delhi, 2002 (Rome: IsMEO, 1994). (English)

SA_MB_IPVV_1_hk.title: Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī (adhikāra 1, āhnikas 1–3)
SA_MB_IPVV_1_hk.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_IPVV_1_hk.summary: This text comprises Volume 1 of Abhinavagupta's Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī, his extensive philosophical commentary on Utpaladeva's Vivṛti/Ṭīkā to the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā. It encompasses the first three chapters (āhnikas) of the Jñānādhikāra, establishing the purpose of the treatise (Upodghātāhnika), refuting the Buddhist argument regarding the non-apprehension (anupalabdhi) of the Self, and critiquing externalist and reductionist rival schools (paradarśana). The work serves as a foundational text for non-dual Kashmir Śaiva epistemology and remains the primary witness for reconstructing Utpaladeva's lost Vivṛti.
SA_MB_IPVV_1_hk.attribution: Authored by Abhinavagupta. The work is a commentary on Utpaladeva's Ṭīkā / Vivṛti.
SA_MB_IPVV_1_hk.edition: The Īśvarapratyabhijñā vivṛtivimarśinī by Abhinavagupta, Vol. 1, edited by Śāstrī M. K. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS). Bombay: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1938.
SA_MB_IPVV_1_hk.coverage: partial — Volume 1 of the KSTS edition (KSTS 60). Contains Adhikāra 1 (Jñānādhikāra), āhnikas 1–3, concluding on p. 299 of the print edition.

SA_MB_IPVV_2_hk.title: Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī (adhikāra 1, āhnikas 4–8)
SA_MB_IPVV_2_hk.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_IPVV_2_hk.summary: The Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī is Abhinavagupta's philosophical commentary on Utpaladeva's Vivṛti to the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā. This volume contains the conclusion of the Jñānādhikāra (ending with vimarśa 8).
SA_MB_IPVV_2_hk.attribution: Abhinavagupta composed this commentary on Utpaladeva's Vivṛti to the Īśvarapratyabhijñā.
SA_MB_IPVV_2_hk.edition: The īśvarapratyabhijñā vivṛtivimarśinī by Abhinavagupta, Vol. 2, edited by Śāstrī M. K., Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies, Bombay: Research Department Jammu and Kashmir State, 1941.
SA_MB_IPVV_2_hk.coverage: partial — Contains Adhikāra 1 (Jñānādhikāra), concluding with vimarśa 8 (Volume 2 of KSTS 62).

SA_MB_IPVV_3_hk.title: Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī (adhikāras 2–4)
SA_MB_IPVV_3_hk.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_IPVV_3_hk.summary: The Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī (also known as the Bṛhatī Vimarśinī) is Abhinavagupta's monumental philosophical commentary on Utpaladeva's auto-commentary (Vivṛti) to the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā. This third volume covers the Kriyādhikāra (examining divine agency, temporal and spatial succession, causality, and relations), the Āgamādhikāra (integrating philosophical analysis with scriptural revelation and the 36 tattvas), and the concluding Tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra (summarizing the ontology and soteriology of recognizing oneself as Śiva). It represents one of the most sophisticated masterworks of classical non-dual Kashmir Śaivism.
SA_MB_IPVV_3_hk.attribution: The Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī is Abhinavagupta's commentary on Utpaladeva's Vivṛti on the Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā. Verses from Utpaladeva's root kārikās are embedded and commented upon sequentially throughout.
SA_MB_IPVV_3_hk.edition: The Īśvarapratyabhijñā vivṛtivimarśinī by Abhinavagupta, Vol. 3, edited by M. K. Shāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies. Bombay: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1943.
SA_MB_IPVV_3_hk.coverage: partial — Contains the text of the third and final volume of the printed KSTS edition, comprising Adhikāra 2 (Kriyādhikāra, 4 āhnikas), Adhikāra 3 (Āgamādhikāra, 2 āhnikas), and Adhikāra 4 (Tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra / Samastanigamana). Adhikāra 1 (Jñānādhikāra) constitutes Volumes 1 and 2 (KSTS 60 and 62).

SA_MB_IISVARASIDDHI_hk.title: Īśvarasiddhi with Vṛtti
SA_MB_IISVARASIDDHI_hk.author: Utpaladeva
SA_MB_IISVARASIDDHI_hk.summary: The Īśvarasiddhi ('Establishment of the Lord') is one of the three monographs comprising the Siddhitrayī by Utpaladeva, a master of the Pratyabhijñā school of Kashmir Shaivism. Consisting of 56 kārikās and the author's own prose vṛtti, the work defends the necessity of an intelligent conscious agent (Īśvara) behind the cosmos. It critically examines rival models—particularly the Sāṅkhya theory of insentient material transformation (pariṇāmavāda) and the Nyāya inferential proof—before resolving divine agency into recognition (pratyabhijñā).
SA_MB_IISVARASIDDHI_hk.attribution: Both the root kārikās and the autocommentary (vṛtti) are composed by Utpaladeva (son of Udayākara), as confirmed in concluding verse 56 and the final colophon (iti śrīmanmahāmāheśvarācāryotpaladevenodayākarasūnunā viracitā īśvarasiddhiḥ samāptā).
SA_MB_IISVARASIDDHI_hk.edition: Madhusūdan Kaul Shāstrī (ed.), The Siddhitrayi and the Pratyabhijna-karika-vritti of Rajanaka Utpala Deva, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1921.
SA_MB_IISVARASIDDHI_hk.coverage: complete — Text of the treatise (56 kārikās interspersed with prose vṛtti).

SA_MB_jnaanakaarikaaHK.title: Jñānakārikā
SA_MB_jnaanakaarikaaHK.author: Matsyendranātha
SA_MB_jnaanakaarikaaHK.summary: The Jñānakārikā is a short Kaula verse text in three chapters (paṭalas) traditionally ascribed to Matsyendranātha. Preserved alongside the Kaulajñānanirṇaya, the treatise expounds non-dual gnosis (jñāna), liberation detached from mental supports and dualistic constructs (nirāśraya), and internalizes Kaula ascetic conduct (caryā), outward signs, and sacred sites.
SA_MB_jnaanakaarikaaHK.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Mahāmachindranātha (Matsyendranātha). Transmitted together with the Kaulajñānanirṇaya.
SA_MB_jnaanakaarikaaHK.edition: Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (ed.), Kaulajñānanirṇaya and Some Minor Texts of the School of Matsyendranātha. Calcutta Sanskrit Series. Calcutta: Metropolitan Printing and Publishing House, 1934.
SA_MB_jnaanakaarikaaHK.coverage: complete — Complete as printed in P. C. Bagchi's editio princeps, comprising three paṭalas (prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ, dvitīyaḥ paṭalaḥ, caryādhikāraḥ tṛtīyaḥ paṭalaḥ).

SA_MB_kaamakalaavilaasaHK.title: Kāmakalāvilāsa with Cidvallī
SA_MB_kaamakalaavilaasaHK.author: Puṇyānanda, Naṭanānanda
SA_MB_kaamakalaavilaasaHK.summary: The Kāmakalāvilāsa is a Śrīvidyā treatise by Puṇyānanda expounding the non-dual cosmogonic and metaphysical doctrine of the Supreme Goddess Tripurasundarī. It details the emanation of the universe from the primordial union of illumination (prakāśa) and reflexive awareness (vimarśa) via the kāmakalā—the creative principle embodied in the three primal bindus. The text articulates the manifestation of sacred speech through the four levels of sound and maps this cosmogony onto the geometry and presiding deities of the Śrīcakra. The accompanying Cidvallī commentary by Naṭanānanda provides essential elucidation of the esoteric terminology and ritual correlations.
SA_MB_kaamakalaavilaasaHK.attribution: The root text is composed by Puṇyānanda. The commentary Cidvallī is composed by Naṭanānanda.
SA_MB_kaamakalaavilaasaHK.edition: Kāmakalāvilāsaḥ of Puṇya Nanda [with the commentary Cidvallī by Naṭanānanda], Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Bombay: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918.
SA_MB_kaamakalaavilaasaHK.coverage: complete — Contains the Kāmakalāvilāsa along with the Cidvallī commentary.

SA_MB_kamkaalamaaliniitantraHK.title: Kaṅkālamālinītantra
SA_MB_kamkaalamaaliniitantraHK.summary: The Kaṅkālamālinītantra ('Tantra of the Goddess Garlanded with Skeletons') is a five-paṭala Śākta text of the Kālīkula tradition, internally attributed to the Southern transmission (Dakṣiṇāmnāya). Framed as a dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī, it expounds the esoteric correspondence between the fifty phonemes of the Sanskrit alphabet (mātṛkā) and Śiva-Śakti, followed by yogic teachings on the six cakras, yonimudrā, and the ascent and descent of Kuṇḍalinī. It further prescribes the worship of the Goddess and her attendant ḍākinīs, along with instructions on puraścaraṇa and devotion to the guru.
SA_MB_kamkaalamaaliniitantraHK.attribution: Canonical Śākta tantra cast in the form of a dialogue between Śrībhairavī and Śrībhairava (Śiva).
SA_MB_kamkaalamaaliniitantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text across five chapters (paṭalas 1–5), ending with the colophon 'iti dakṣiṇāmnāye śrīkaṅkālamālinītantre pañcamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ' and 'granthaśca samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_kaulajnaananirnayaHK.title: Kaulajñānanirṇaya
SA_MB_kaulajnaananirnayaHK.author: Matsyendranātha
SA_MB_kaulajnaananirnayaHK.summary: The Kaulajñānanirṇaya is a foundational Śaiva-Śākta scripture of the Yoginī Kaula (Matsyendramata) lineage, traditionally held to have been transmitted by the mahāsiddha Matsyendranātha in Candradvīpa. In 24 chapters (paṭalas), it expounds esoteric Kaula teachings, including the nonduality of Śiva and Śakti, the metaphysics of kula and akula, subtle yogic physiology (bindu, nāda, cakras), siddhi acquisition, and antinomian yoginī rituals.
SA_MB_kaulajnaananirnayaHK.attribution: The scripture is traditionally attributed to the mahāsiddha Matsyendranātha (under names such as Macchaghnapāda, Matsyendrapāda, Mīnanātha) as its revealer (avatāraka) in Candradvīpa.
SA_MB_kaulajnaananirnayaHK.edition: P. C. Bagchi (ed.), kaulajñānanirṇaya and some minor texts of the school of matsyendrānātha, Calcutta Sanskrit Series, Calcutta: Metropolitan Printing and Pub. House, 1934.
SA_MB_kaulajnaananirnayaHK.coverage: complete — Contains the text of the Kaulajñānanirṇaya in 24 paṭalas followed by three concluding verses (marked 25/1–3 in the Muktabodha e-text) and the final colophon as edited by P. C. Bagchi.

SA_MB_kaulopanisadsHK.title: Kaulopaniṣadaḥ with the commentaries of Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_kaulopanisadsHK.author: Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_kaulopanisadsHK.summary: This compendium contains esoteric Śākta/Kaula Upaniṣads—including the Bhāvanopaniṣad, the Bahvṛcavedīyā Lalitāmahātripurasundaryupaniṣad, the Devyatharvaśīrṣopaniṣad, and the Kaulopaniṣad—along with commentaries and liturgical texts by Bhāskararāya.
SA_MB_kaulopanisadsHK.attribution: The collection of texts and commentaries is attributed in the colophons and catalog metadata to Bhāskararāya.
SA_MB_kaulopanisadsHK.edition: Kaula Upanishads with commentaries by Bhāskararāya [Bhāvanopaniṣat, Śrīlalitāmahātripurasundaryupaniṣat and commentary called Bahvṛcavedīyā, Devyatharvaśīrṣopaniṣat, Śrīkaulopaniṣat], Bangalore: Asthana Vidwan K. P. Narayana Sastry, 1946.
SA_MB_kaulopanisadsHK.coverage: complete — Text of the Upaniṣads together with commentaries as found in the 1946 Bangalore publication by Asthana Vidwan K. P. Narayana Sastry.

SA_MB_kramadipikaHK.title: Kramadīpikā
SA_MB_kramadipikaHK.author: Keśava Bhaṭṭa
SA_MB_kramadipikaHK.summary: The Kramadīpikā is a Vaiṣṇava ritual manual in eight chapters (paṭalas) dealing with mantric worship, nyāsas, mudrās, pūjā, and homa centered on Gopāla/Kṛṣṇa.
SA_MB_kramadipikaHK.attribution: Attributed in the catalog record / scholarship to Keśavakāśmīrin Bhaṭṭācārya (Sanderson 2012-13, p. 69). Rasikamohana Caṭṭopādhyāya was the 19th-century collector and publisher who included it in his Tantrasārādivividhatantrasaṃgraha.
SA_MB_kramadipikaHK.edition: Kramadīpikā, in: Tantrasārādivividhatantrasaṃgraha, collected and published by Rasikamohana Caṭṭopādhyāya, Calcutta: pre-1900, Bengali script.
SA_MB_kramadipikaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 8 paṭalas, concluding with 'iti kramadīpikāyāmaṣṭamaḥ paṭalaḥ || iti kramadīpikā samāptā'.

SA_MB_kubjikaatantramHK.title: Kubjikātantra
SA_MB_kubjikaatantramHK.summary: The Kubjikātantra is a Śākta scripture in seventeen paṭalas framed as a dialogue between Sadāśiva and Pārvatī. The text treats general Śākta ritualism, including mantras, yantras, nyāsa, and protective talismans, concluding in chapter 17 with the Mṛtavatsākavaca.
SA_MB_kubjikaatantramHK.attribution: Revealed Śākta-Tantric scripture presented as a dialogue between Sadāśiva and Pārvatī.
SA_MB_kubjikaatantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 17 chapters (paṭalas), beginning with paṭala 1 (prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ) and concluding with the colophon of paṭala 17 (iti kubjikātantre mṛtavatsā kavacaṃ nāma saptadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ).

SA_MB_kularnavaHK.title: Kulārṇavatantra
SA_MB_kularnavaHK.summary: The Kulārṇavatantra ('Ocean of the Kula') is one of the foundational scriptural texts of the Kaula tradition within Śākta Tantrism, framed as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva and the Goddess. Comprising seventeen ullāsas (chapters) and more than two thousand verses, the text presents the doctrine and ritual praxis of the Ūrdhvāmnāya (upper transmission). It systematically expounds the necessity of human embodiment for liberation, guru-śiṣya relations, dīkṣā, mantra-sādhana, and the sacramental integration of enjoyment (bhukti) with liberation (mukti) through the esoteric rites of the pañcamakāras.
SA_MB_kularnavaHK.attribution: Revealed scripture cast in the form of an esoteric dialogue between Śiva (Bhairava) and Pārvatī (Devī).
SA_MB_kularnavaHK.coverage: complete — Complete Sanskrit text in 17 ullāsas (chapters 1–17).

SA_MB_LallesvarivakyaniHK.title: Lalleśvarīvākyāni with the Sanskrit translation of Bhāskarakaṇṭha
SA_MB_LallesvarivakyaniHK.author: Lalleśvarī, Bhāskarakaṇṭha
SA_MB_LallesvarivakyaniHK.summary: The Lalleśvarīvākyāni ('Sayings of Lalleśvarī') comprises 60 mystical Kashmiri quatrains (vākhs) by the 14th-century poet-saint Lallā (Lal Dĕd), accompanied verse-for-verse by Sanskrit metrical translations (arthacchāyāpadya) composed by the 18th-century Kashmiri Śaiva scholar Rājānaka Bhāskarakaṇṭha. Rooted in nondual Trika and Pratyabhijñā Śaivism, the verses convey internal yogic absorption, prāṇāyāma, mind control, critique of ritualism and external caste distinctions, and the nondual realization of the Self as Śiva. As the earliest attested literary compositions in the Kashmiri language, Lallā's verses hold foundational importance in Kashmiri literary and religious culture, while Bhāskarakaṇṭha's translation represents their earliest formal reception in classical Sanskrit scholarship.
SA_MB_LallesvarivakyaniHK.attribution: The root verses are Kashmiri quatrains attributed to the 14th-century female mystic Lallā (Lalleśvarī / Lal Dĕd). Each Kashmiri verse is paired with a metrical Sanskrit verse translation (arthacchāyāpadya) composed by Rājānaka Bhāskara (Bhāskarakaṇṭha, 18th century).
SA_MB_LallesvarivakyaniHK.edition: Lalleśvarīvākyāni. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS). Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918.
SA_MB_LallesvarivakyaniHK.coverage: complete — Comprising 60 Kashmiri vākhs, 60 Sanskrit metrical verses, and concluding dedicatory śloka and colophon.
translations: Grierson, George A., and Lionel D. Barnett, Lallā-Vākyāni. 1920. (English)

SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa2HK.title: Mahānayaprakāśa
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa2HK.author: Śitikaṇṭha
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa2HK.summary: The Mahānayaprakāśa of Rājānaka Śitikaṇṭha is a tantric/āgamic treatise belonging to the non-dual Śaivism of Kashmir (Kālīkula / Krama tradition), divided into udayas / melāpas.
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa2HK.attribution: Attributed to Śitikaṇṭha (Rājānaka Śitikaṇṭha / Śrī Mahāmāheśvarācāryavarya Śrī Śitikaṇṭhācārya).
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa2HK.edition: The Mahānaya-Prakāśa of Rājanaka Śiti Kaṇṭha, ed. Mukunda Rāma Śāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS) 21. Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State / Bombay, 1918.
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa2HK.coverage: complete — Text of the work as published in KSTS 21, concluding with editor Mukundarāma Śāstrī's metrical colophon (tilaka).

SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa1HK.title: Mahānayaprakāśa
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa1HK.summary: The Mahānayaprakāśa ('Illumination of the Great Way') is an anonymous Sanskrit verse treatise belonging to the esoteric Krama (Mahānaya/Mahārtha) school of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism. Divided into nine ullāsas, it systematically presents the sequential and non-sequential cycles of divine manifestation and reabsorption, focusing on the wheels of deities (cakras), the pīṭhas, and the twelve forms of Kālī. It emphasizes the direct transmission of non-dual realization through the grace and penetrating glance of the guru (gurudṛkpāta) as superior to external ritual practices.
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa1HK.attribution: The treatise is anonymous. In the TSS edition, editor K. Sāmbaśiva Śāstrī tentatively suggested Abhinavagupta, while Navjivan Rastogi (The Krama Tantrism of Kashmir, p. 257) proposed Śivānanda II. It is distinct from the Mahānayaprakāśa of Rājānaka Śitikaṇṭha.
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa1HK.edition: Mahānayaprakāśa, edited by K. Sāmbaśiva Śāstrī, Trivandrum Sanskrit Series No. 130 (Śrī Citrodayamañjarī Series), Trivandrum: Government Press, 1937.
SA_MB_mahanayaprakasa1HK.coverage: partial — Incomplete: contains ullāsas 1–9 but breaks off abruptly with lacunae at verse 9.69½ ('tat * * * * * * * * || 9/69 ½ ||'), lacking an explicit and the final colophon of the ninth ullāsa and work.

SA_MB_maharthamanjariHK.title: Mahārthamañjarī with Parimala
SA_MB_maharthamanjariHK.author: Maheśvarānanda
SA_MB_maharthamanjariHK.summary: The Mahārthamañjarī accompanied by the Parimala auto-commentary is a work of non-dual Śaiva philosophy (Krama / Mahārtha) composed by Maheśvarānanda (Gorakṣa).
SA_MB_maharthamanjariHK.attribution: The Mahārthamañjarī and the auto-commentary Parimala were composed by Maheśvarānanda (also known as Gorakṣa, disciple of Mahāprakāśa).
SA_MB_maharthamanjariHK.edition: The Mahārthamañjarī with the Commentary Parimala of Maheśvarānanda, edited by T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī, Trivandrum Sanskrit Series No. 66, Trivandrum, 1919.
SA_MB_maharthamanjariHK.coverage: complete — Text of the Mahārthamañjarī with Maheśvarānanda's Parimala commentary and colophons.
translations: Lilian Silburn, La Mahārthamañjarī de Maheśvarānanda, avec des extraits du Parimala, Paris: Éditions E. de Boccard, 1968. (French)

SA_MB_makutaagamaHK.title: Makuṭāgama (Kriyāpāda, chapters 1–12)
SA_MB_makutaagamaHK.summary: The Makuṭāgama is a Śaiva Siddhānta āgama. This section of the Kriyāpāda treats ritual procedures, seat/throne characteristics (āsanalakṣaṇa), offerings, and preceptor qualifications (ācāryalakṣaṇa).
SA_MB_makutaagamaHK.attribution: Canonical scriptural revelation of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition.
SA_MB_makutaagamaHK.coverage: partial — Contains 12 paṭalas of the Kriyāpāda. The text ends at verse 12.11 followed by the colophon 'iti makuṭe kriyāpāde ācāryalakṣaṇavidhirnāma dvādaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || 12 ||'. The Muktabodha header labels the coverage as 'chapters 1 - 11', while ilx_skt lists 12 chapters.

SA_MB_mrgendraHK.title: Mṛgendrāgama with Mṛgendravṛtti and Dīpikā (Vidyāpāda and Yogapāda)
SA_MB_mrgendraHK.author: Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha, Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_mrgendraHK.summary: The Mṛgendrāgama (or Mṛgendratantra) is an authoritative scripture of dualistic Śaiva Siddhānta, traditionally regarded as an upāgama of the Kāmikāgama. This e-text contains its philosophical Vidyāpāda and practical Yogapāda, which formulate core Siddhānta ontology across the categories of pati (the Lord), paśu (the bound individual), and pāśa (fetters/bonds), followed by an exposition of tantric yoga. The root text is accompanied by the commentary (Mṛgendravṛtti) of Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha and the sub-commentary (Dīpikā) of Aghoraśiva.
SA_MB_mrgendraHK.attribution: The Mṛgendrāgama (Mṛgendratantra) is an anonymous scriptural revelation of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition. The primary commentary (Mṛgendravṛtti) is by Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha (son of Vidyākaṇṭha). The sub-commentary (Dīpikā) is by Aghoraśivācārya.
SA_MB_mrgendraHK.edition: Śrīmṛgendram Kāmikopāgamam (Vidyāyogapādadvayamilitam) śrībhaṭṭanārāyaṇakaṇṭhaviracitayā vṛttyā tadvyākhyayāghoraśivācāryaviracitayā dīpikayā cālaṅkṛtam, edited by N. Kṛṣṇa Śāstrī and K. M. Subrahmaṇya Śāstrī, Śivāgamasiddhāntaparipālanasaṃgha Series, Devakottai: Śivāgama Siddhānta Paripālana Saṅgham, 1928.
SA_MB_mrgendraHK.coverage: partial — Contains the Vidyāpāda and Yogapāda of the Mṛgendrāgama with Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha's Vṛtti and Aghoraśiva's Dīpikā. It does not contain the Kriyāpāda or Caryāpāda.
translations: Mṛgendrāgama: Sections de la doctrine et du yoga (Vidyāpāda et Yogapāda) avec la Vṛtti de Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇakaṇṭha et la Dīpikā d'Aghoraśivācārya, traduction, introduction et notes par Michel Hulin, Publications de l'Institut Français d'Indologie, Pondichéry: Institut Français d'Indologie, 1980. (French)

Mṛgendrāgama: Section des rites et section du comportement (Kriyāpāda et Caryāpāda) avec la vṛtti de Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇakaṇṭha, traduction, introduction et notes par Hélène Brunner-Lachaux, Publications de l'Institut Français d'Indologie No. 69, Pondichéry: Institut Français d'Indologie, 1985. (French)

SA_MB_netratantra_HK.title: Netratantra with Netroddyota
SA_MB_netratantra_HK.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_netratantra_HK.summary: The Netratantra is a Śaiva scripture accompanied by the commentary Netroddyota (or Netrodyota) by Kṣemarāja, student of Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_netratantra_HK.attribution: The commentary Netroddyota is composed by Kṣemarāja, disciple of Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_netratantra_HK.edition: Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies volumes 46 and 61, edited by M. K. Śāstrī.
SA_MB_netratantra_HK.coverage: complete — Netratantra with Kṣemarāja's commentary Netroddyota, concluding with the colophon: 'samāpto'yaṃ netroddyotākhyo granthaḥ || kṛtirmahāmāheśvaraśrīmadabhinavaguptapādapadmaparāgāsvādatatparaśrīkṣemarājasyeti śivam ||'.

SA_MB_naresvarapariiksaaHK.title: Nareśvaraparīkṣā with Nareśvaraparīkṣāprakāśa
SA_MB_naresvarapariiksaaHK.author: Sadyojyoti, Rāmakaṇṭha
SA_MB_naresvarapariiksaaHK.summary: The Nareśvaraparīkṣā ('Examination of the Soul and the Lord') by Sadyojyoti is an early systematic treatise of dualistic Śaiva Siddhānta. Comprising verses across three kāṇḍas, it establishes the distinct ontologies of the individual soul (nara/paśu) and the supreme Lord (īśvara/pati), countering Buddhist, Sāṅkhya, and Advaitin models. The accompanying Prakāśa commentary by Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha significantly elaborates the philosophical argumentation, mounting a sustained defense of the enduring, self-luminous self against Buddhist Sautrāntika and Yogācāra-Vijñānavāda critique.
SA_MB_naresvarapariiksaaHK.attribution: The root kārikās are authored by Sadyojyoti. The Prakāśa commentary is by Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha, son of Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha.
SA_MB_naresvarapariiksaaHK.edition: The Nareshvarapariksha of Sadyojyotih with Commentary by Ramakantha, edited by M. K. Shāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS). Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1926.
SA_MB_naresvarapariiksaaHK.coverage: complete — Includes the Prakāśa commentary, ending with Kāṇḍa 3 (Paradarśanaprasiddheśvarapratikṣepa) and Rāmakaṇṭha's concluding verses and colophon.
translations: Watson, Alex. The Self's Awareness of Itself: Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha's Arguments against the Buddhist Doctrine of No-Self. Publications of the De Nobili Research Library. Vienna: Institut für Südasien-, Tibet- und Buddhismuskunde der Universität Wien, 2006. (English)
Lal, Magan Bihari. Nareśvara-Parīkṣā, a Critical and Comparative Study with Hindi translation. Ph.D. dissertation, University of Lucknow. (Hindi)

SA_MB_pancaratraraksa1HK.title: Pāñcarātrarakṣā
SA_MB_pancaratraraksa1HK.author: Vedāntadeśika
SA_MB_pancaratraraksa1HK.summary: The Pāñcarātrarakṣā is an apologetic and liturgical treatise by the Śrīvaiṣṇava teacher Vedānta Deśika (Veṅkaṭanātha). It establishes the scriptural authority and excellence of the Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra system with respect to other traditions, quoting widely from Vaiṣṇava and non-Vaiṣṇava sources.
SA_MB_pancaratraraksa1HK.attribution: Authored by the Viśiṣṭādvaita philosopher and Śrīvaiṣṇava teacher Veṅkaṭanātha, popularly known as Vedānta Deśika (traditional dates 1269–1369).
SA_MB_pancaratraraksa1HK.edition: Pāñcarātrarakṣā by Vedānta Deśika, edited by Pandit M. Duraisvami Aiyangar and Pandit T. Venugopalacharya, Adyar, Madras: The Adyar Library and Research Center, 1942.
SA_MB_pancaratraraksa1HK.coverage: complete — Text concludes with: 'iti śrīkavitārkikasiṃhasya sarvatantrasvatantrasya śrīmadveṅkaṭanāthasya vedāntācāryasya kṛtiṣu śrīpāñcarātrarakṣāyāṃ nityavyākhyānākhyaḥ tṛtīyo'dhikāraḥ śrīpāñcarātrarakṣāṃ saṃpūrṇā'.

SA_MB_paramarthasaraHK.title: Paramārthasāra with Vivṛti
SA_MB_paramarthasaraHK.author: Abhinavagupta, Yogarāja
SA_MB_paramarthasaraHK.summary: The Paramārthasāra ('Essence of the Supreme Truth') is a concise manual of nondual Kashmir Śaivism in 105 verses by Abhinavagupta. It surveys the nondual nature of absolute consciousness, cosmic manifestation across the thirty-six categories (tattvas), the mechanisms of contraction and ignorance, and liberation. Yogarāja's Vivṛti, composed by a direct student of Kṣemarāja at Vitastāpurī, offers an indispensable running prose commentary elucidating Abhinavagupta's verses in light of Trika and Pratyabhijñā doctrine.
SA_MB_paramarthasaraHK.attribution: The Vivṛti (or Paramārthasārasaṃgrahavivṛti) was composed by Rājānaka Yogarāja at Vitastāpurī; as stated in his concluding verses, he was a direct disciple of Kṣemarāja.
SA_MB_paramarthasaraHK.edition: The Paramārtha-Sāra by Abhinavagupta with the Commentary of Yogarāja, edited by Jagadisha Chandra Chatterji (J. C. Chatterji), Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1916.
SA_MB_paramarthasaraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 105 verses of Abhinavagupta's Paramārthasāra with Yogarāja's full Vivṛti commentary, including introductory mangala verses and final colophons.

SA_MB_paraatriisikaalaghuvrttiHK.title: Parātrīśikā with Parātrīśikālaghuvṛtti
SA_MB_paraatriisikaalaghuvrttiHK.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_paraatriisikaalaghuvrttiHK.summary: The Parātrīśikālaghuvṛtti (also known as Anuttaratattvavimarśinī) is a concise commentary on the Parātrīśikā. Attributed to Abhinavagupta, the work elucidates the nature of the Supreme Reality (anuttara), phonematic emanation, and mantric realization.
SA_MB_paraatriisikaalaghuvrttiHK.attribution: The Laghuvṛtti (titled Anuttaratattvavimarśinī in its concluding colophon) is ascribed to Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_paraatriisikaalaghuvrttiHK.edition: Śāstrī J. Z. (ed.), Parātrīśikālaghuvṛtti, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies Volume 68, Shrinigar: Research Departement Jammu and Kashmir State, 1947.
SA_MB_paraatriisikaalaghuvrttiHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Parātrīśikā together with the Laghuvṛtti commentary.
translations: André Padoux (1975), La Parātrīśikālaghuvṛtti de Abhinavagupta, Texte Traduit et Annoté, Paris, Institut de Civilisation Indienne, 1975, (Publications de L'Institute de Civilisation Indienne, Série In-8°, Fascicule 38). (French)

SA_MB_paraatrisikaataatparyadiipikaaHK.title: Parātrīśikātātparyadīpikā
SA_MB_paraatrisikaataatparyadiipikaaHK.summary: The Parātrīśikātātparyadīpikā is an anonymous metrical commentary comprising 536 verses on the Parātrīśikā, expanding on Abhinavagupta's exposition (vivṛti/laghuvṛtti).
SA_MB_paraatrisikaataatparyadiipikaaHK.attribution: The work is an anonymous metrical commentary on the Parātrīśikā.
SA_MB_paraatrisikaataatparyadiipikaaHK.edition: Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), No. 74, edited by Zadoo J D, Srinagar: Research Department Jammu and Kashmir State, 1947.
SA_MB_paraatrisikaataatparyadiipikaaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Parātrīśikātātparyadīpikā in 536 verses (vv. 1–536, ending 'iti śrīparātrīśikātātparyadīpikā saṃpūrṇā'). The second text of KSTS 74 (Somānanda's Śāktavijñāna) is not present in this file.

SA_MB_ParaatrisikaavivrttiHK.title: Parātrīśikā with Parātrīśikāvivṛti
SA_MB_ParaatrisikaavivrttiHK.author: Lakṣmīrāma
SA_MB_ParaatrisikaavivrttiHK.summary: The Parātrīśikā is a scripture of Kashmir Śaivism's Trika lineage, traditionally received as an extract from the Rudrayāmalatantra. In 35 verses, Śiva (Bhairava) expounds to the Goddess the mystery of the supreme reality (anuttara), the Goddess Parā as non-dual awareness, and the esoteric phonemic emanations (mātṛkā) through which cosmos and mantra manifest. In this vivṛti, Rājānaka Lakṣmīrāma provides an exposition of the text in light of Abhinavagupta's earlier work.
SA_MB_ParaatrisikaavivrttiHK.attribution: The root text consists of the 35 verses of the canonical Trika scripture Parātrīśikā (traditionally regarded as part of the Rudrayāmala). The vivṛti (referred to in the closing verse as Trīśikāvivṛti and in the concluding colophon as Parātrīśikālaghuvivṛti) is authored by Rājānaka Lakṣmīrāma (also known as Lasa Kāk).
SA_MB_ParaatrisikaavivrttiHK.edition: Parātrīśikāvivṛti of Lasa Kāka [Rājānaka Lakṣmīrāma], ed. Jagaddhara Zadu Shastri, KSTS 69, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1947.
SA_MB_ParaatrisikaavivrttiHK.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on all 35 verses of the Parātrīśikā, including introductory remarks, embedded kārikās, Lakṣmīrāma's two closing verses, and the final colophon.

SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-I-HK.title: Puraścaryārṇava (chapters 1–4)
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-I-HK.author: Pratāpasiṃha Śāha
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-I-HK.summary: The Puraścaryārṇava is a Śākta-Tāntrika ritual compendium (nibandha) compiled under the patronage of King Pratāpasiṃha Śāha of Nepal. Organized into taraṅgas ('waves'), it synthesizes scriptural injunctions from numerous Tantras and Purāṇas on the requirements and performance of puraścaryā (preparatory mantra realization) and ritual worship. This first volume encompasses taraṅgas 1 to 4, concluding with kriyāvatī dīkṣā.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-I-HK.attribution: Nominally authored by Mahārājādhirāja Pratāpasiṃha Śāha, King of Nepal, as stated in the colophon and catalog metadata.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-I-HK.edition: Muralidhara Jhā (ed.), Puraścaryārṇavaḥ, Benaras: Prabhakari and Co, 1901.

SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-2-HK.title: Puraścaryārṇava (taraṅgas 5–8)
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-2-HK.author: Pratāpasiṃha Śāha
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-2-HK.summary: The Puraścaryārṇava is an encyclopedic Tantric digest compiled under the auspices of King Pratāpasiṃha Śāha of Nepal. This volume comprises taraṅgas 5 through 8, expounding tantric initiation procedures (dīkṣāprayoga), general rules and purificatory rituals for mantra practice (puraścaraṇa, rosary conventions, japa methods), sacrificial oblations and auxiliary rites (homa, tarpaṇa, mārjana), and puraścaraṇa routines for various mantras including Gaṇeśa and Rāma.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-2-HK.attribution: Attributed to King Pratāpasiṃha Śāha of Nepal (Śrīman Mahārājādhirāja Pratāpa Siṃha Sāha / Pratapa Simha Saha Bahadur of Nepal).
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-2-HK.edition: Muralīdhara Jhā (ed.), Puraścaryārṇava, Benaras: Prabhakari and Co, 1901, starting p. 319.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-2-HK.coverage: partial — Contains volume 2 of the work, spanning taraṅgas 5 through 8 (commencing with dīkṣāprayoga in taraṅga 5 and ending with the colophon of taraṅga 8: gaṇeśādimantrapuraścaraṇavivecana), starting from p. 319.

SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-3-HK.title: Puraścaryārṇava (chapters 9–12)
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-3-HK.author: Pratāpasiṃha Śāha
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-3-HK.summary: The Puraścaryārṇava ('Ocean of Preliminary Ritual Practice') is an encyclopedic Śākta and Tāntrika ritual digest (nibandha) compiled under the auspices of King Pratāpasiṃha Śāha of Nepal (r. 1775–1777). This third volume contains taraṅgas 9 through 12, completing the twelve-chapter digest. It covers the mantras and puraścaraṇa rituals of the Daśamahāvidyās (taraṅga 9), other deities including Sarasvatī alongside Vaidika mantras like the Gāyatrī (taraṅga 10), the worship of Durgā with an extensive manual for the autumnal Durgotsava / Navarātri (taraṅga 11), and the mantras, yantras, stotras, and kavacas of Brāhmī and various other deities (taraṅga 12). Citing scores of canonical tantras, Purāṇas, and earlier ritual paddhatis, it is an essential reference for northern Indian and Nepalese tantric liturgy.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-3-HK.attribution: Attributed in all chapter colophons to King Pratāpasiṃha Śāha of Nepal (r. 1775–1777). In keeping with traditional royal digests, the compilation was executed under his patronage by court scholars.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-3-HK.edition: Puraścaryārṇavaḥ (Tṛtīyaḥ Khaṇḍaḥ: 9–12 taraṅgāḥ), edited by Muralīdhara Jhā, Benares: Prabhakari & Co., 1901.
SA_MB_purascaryaarnava-3-HK.coverage: partial — Contains the third and final volume (tṛtīyakhaṇḍa) of the work, comprising taraṅgas 9 to 12 in full. Taraṅgas 1–8 are contained in volumes 1 and 2.

SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAAhk.title: Parāprāveśikā
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAAhk.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAAhk.summary: The Parāprāveśikā ('Initiation into the Supreme') is a concise prose primer (prakaraṇa) of non-dual Kashmirian Śaiva (Trika / Pratyabhijñā) philosophy authored by Kṣemarāja. It serves as an accessible introduction to the school's doctrine, expounding ultimate reality as luminous consciousness (prakāśa) endowed with dynamic self-awareness (vimarśa). The work outlines the manifestation of the thirty-six cosmic principles (tattvas) and explicates the esoteric significance of phonemic emanation centered on the seed syllable of the Supreme Goddess (hṛdayabīja / Parā).
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAAhk.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short prose treatise.

SA_MB_mahaanirvaanatantramHK.title: Mahānirvāṇatantra with the commentary of Hariharānanda Bhāratī
SA_MB_mahaanirvaanatantramHK.author: Hariharānanda Bhāratī
SA_MB_mahaanirvaanatantramHK.summary: The Mahānirvāṇatantra is an influential Śākta work structured as a discourse between Sadāśiva and the Goddess (Ādyā Śakti) on ritual and moral duty in the degraded Kali Yuga. It combines monotheistic Advaita Vedānta and the meditation on formless Brahman with devotional worship of Ādyā Kālī, while reforming traditional Kaula rituals such as the pañcatattva. Unusually among Tantras, it devotes extensive sections to social ethics, duties of the householder, sacramental ceremonies (saṃskāras), and civil law regarding marriage, property, and inheritance.
SA_MB_mahaanirvaanatantramHK.attribution: The root scripture is framed as an Āgamic dialogue between Sadāśiva and the Devī. The accompanying commentary is authored by Hariharānanda Bhāratī.
SA_MB_mahaanirvaanatantramHK.edition: Arthur Avalon [Sir John Woodroffe] (ed.), Mahānirvāṇa Tantra with the Commentary of Hariharānanda Bhāratī, Tantrik Texts, Vol. 13, London: Luzac & Co. / Calcutta, 1926.
SA_MB_mahaanirvaanatantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete in all 14 chapters (ullāsas), designated as the Pūrvakāṇḍa / Pūrvārdha, which constitutes the entire text preserved in tradition and printed editions.
translations: Arthur Avalon [Sir John Woodroffe], Tantra of the Great Liberation (Mahānirvāṇa Tantra), London, 1913; 2nd edition with commentary, Madras: Ganesh & Co., 1927. (English)
Manmatha Nath Dutt, A Prose English Translation of Mahānirvāṇa Tantram, Calcutta: H.C. Dass, 1900. (English)

SA_MB_kriyaasaara2HK.title: Kriyāsāra (upadeśas 5–14)
SA_MB_kriyaasaara2HK.author: Nīlakaṇṭha Śivācārya
SA_MB_kriyaasaara2HK.summary: The Kriyāsāra ('Essence of Practice') by Nīlakaṇṭha Śivācārya (c. 14th–15th century CE) is a major Vīraśaiva metrical treatise harmonizing Śaiva ritual, ethical conduct, and devotional observance with the philosophical framework of the Brahmasūtras. Structured into thirty-one chapters (upadeśas), the text systematically expounds the doctrine of the 101 stages (ekottaraśatasthala) and daily religious duties. This portion comprises Upadeśas 5 through 14, focusing on regular and occasional duties (ācāra), the theological symbolism and rites of holy ash (bhasma) and rudrākṣa, ablutions, sandhyā, and the liturgical manual of Śiva worship (śivapūjā).
SA_MB_kriyaasaara2HK.attribution: Composed by Nīlakaṇṭha Śivācārya, who characterizes himself in the colophons as an authority on the 101 stages of Vīraśaiva philosophy ('śrīmadviśiṣṭādvaitasiddhāntarahasyaikottaraśatasthalābhijña').
SA_MB_kriyaasaara2HK.edition: The Kriyāsāra of Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha Śivācārya (5 to 14 Upadeśas), edited by N. S. Venkatanathacharya. Oriental Research Institute Publications, Sanskrit Series. Mysore: Oriental Research Institute, University of Mysore, 1954.
SA_MB_kriyaasaara2HK.coverage: partial — Contains Upadeśas 5 through 14 (corresponding to Volume 2 of the Mysore ORI edition) of the 31 total Upadeśas of the complete work. Opens with 'atha pañcamopadeśaḥ' and concludes with 'caturdaśopadeśaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_kalpavrksaHK.title: Kalpavṛkṣa
SA_MB_kalpavrksaHK.author: Sāhib Kaul
SA_MB_kalpavrksaHK.summary: The Kalpavṛkṣa is a Śaiva work by Sāhib Kaul of Kashmir.
SA_MB_kalpavrksaHK.attribution: Attributed to Sāhib Kaul, who lived in Kashmir in the 19th century according to the Muktabodha catalog.
SA_MB_kalpavrksaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: MS No. 1353, Oriental Research Library, University Campus, Hazratbal (37 folios / 74 pages).
SA_MB_kalpavrksaHK.coverage: not determined — Transcribes an unpublished manuscript (MS No. 1353 of Oriental Research Library, University Campus, Hazratbal; 37 folios / 74 pages).

SA_MB_nityaasodasikaarnavaHK.title: Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava and Yoginīhṛdaya with Setubandha (pp. 25–40 and 105–112 of the edition missing)
SA_MB_nityaasodasikaarnavaHK.author: Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_nityaasodasikaarnavaHK.summary: The Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava (the pūrvacatuḥśatī of the Vāmakeśvaratantra) and the Yoginīhṛdaya (its uttaracatuḥśatī) are foundational scriptures of Śākta Śrīvidyā. The first sets out the outer worship of Tripurasundarī and the sixteen Nityās: mantras, the Śrīcakra, mudrās and ritual applications. The second treats the inner meaning of cakra, mantra and pūjā. This e-text gives both with the Setubandha, the extensive commentary by the 18th-century scholar Bhāskararāya, which uses Mīmāṃsā methods to treat the two parts as one tantra in eight viśrāmas.
SA_MB_nityaasodasikaarnavaHK.attribution: Both root texts are anonymous scriptural tantras of Śrīvidyā. The Setubandha is by Bhāskararāya (dīkṣā name Bhāsurānandanātha), son of Gambhīrarāja Dīkṣita. The final colophon reads 'iti ... gambhīrarājabhāratīdikṣitasūnunā bhāsurānandanāthadīkṣābhidhānena bhāskararāyeṇa praṇīto nityāṣoḍaśikārṇavavyākhyānātmā setubandhaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ'.
SA_MB_nityaasodasikaarnavaHK.edition: Vāmakeśvaratantrāntargatanityāṣoḍaśikārṇavaḥ śrībhāskararāyonnītasetubandhākhyavyākhyānasahitaḥ, ed. K. V. Abhyaṅkara, Ānandāśramasaṃskṛtagranthāvaliḥ 56, Pune: Ānandāśrama, 1946 (as stated in the Muktabodha header).
SA_MB_nityaasodasikaarnavaHK.coverage: partial — The e-text runs from the edition's title and Bhāskararāya's introductory verses to the final colophon, i.e. all eight viśrāmas: 1–5 on the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava and 6–8 on the Yoginīhṛdaya. Page markers of ASS 56 run from p. 2 to p. 388. Two passages are missing: printed pp. 25–40 and pp. 105–112.

SA_MB_iisvarapratyabhijnakaumudiHK.title: Īśvarapratyabhijñākaumudī
SA_MB_iisvarapratyabhijnakaumudiHK.author: Bhaṭṭāraka Sundara
SA_MB_iisvarapratyabhijnakaumudiHK.summary: The Īśvarapratyabhijñākaumudī is a commentary by Bhaṭṭāraka Sundara on Utpaladeva's philosophical treatise, the Īśvarapratyabhijñā.
SA_MB_iisvarapratyabhijnakaumudiHK.attribution: The work is a commentary on Utpaladeva's Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā composed by Bhaṭṭāraka Sundara (Sundara Bhaṭṭāraka), son of Śrīśaṅkarācāryavarya. The colophon dates the completion of the work to year 74 ('saṃ 74 śrāvaṇe kṛṣṇapakṣe saptamyāṃ revatyāṃ...').
SA_MB_iisvarapratyabhijnakaumudiHK.edition: Manuscript transcription: Research and Publications department, Jammu and Kashmir Government Srinagar manuscript no. 1089 (paper, śaradā script, 82 folios / 164 pages, size 20.3 cm x 14.5 cms). E-text transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, revision dated February 9, 2009 (catalog no. M00053).
SA_MB_iisvarapratyabhijnakaumudiHK.coverage: complete — Commentary on the Īśvarapratyabhijñā text, ending with the author's final colophon.

SA_MB_saaktapramodaHK.title: Śāktapramoda
SA_MB_saaktapramodaHK.author: Devanandanasiṃha
SA_MB_saaktapramodaHK.summary: The Śāktapramoda ('Delight of the Śāktas') is a liturgical digest (paddhati) compiled by Rājā Devanandanasiṃha Bahādur of Sheohar/Śivahara. It gathers individual ritual manuals ('tantras') for śākta and related divinities, including the Mahāvidyās, Kumārī, and Pañcāyatana deities, providing meditation verses (dhyāna), mantras, nyāsa rites, worship sequences, kavacas, and sahasranāmas.
SA_MB_saaktapramodaHK.attribution: Compiled by Rājā Devanandanasiṃha Bahādur of Śivahara (śivahararājadhānīpati / śivahararājadhānīrājabhiḥ śrīrājadevanandanasiṃhabahāduranarādhipaiḥ). Concluding verses date the completion to 1946 (ṣaṭvedāṅkendu yukte śaradi, in the month of Mādhava).
SA_MB_saaktapramodaHK.edition: Śāktapramoda, Bombay: Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara Press, 1949 (reprint of edition published in 1892).
SA_MB_saaktapramodaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Śāktapramoda compendium, comprising ritual manuals ('tantras') of mainly śākta divinities (described in header as 17 individual tantras), including Kālyādidaśamahāvidyātantra, Kumārītantra, Pañcāyatana deities, ending with chapter 17 and concluding index/verses.

SA_MB_taaraabhaktisudhaarnavaHK.title: Tārābhaktisudhārṇava
SA_MB_taaraabhaktisudhaarnavaHK.author: Narasiṃha Ṭhakkura
SA_MB_taaraabhaktisudhaarnavaHK.summary: The Tārābhaktisudhārṇava ('Ocean of the Nectar of Devotion to Tārā') is an extensive Śākta ritual digest (nibandha) dedicated to the worship of the Mahāvidyā Tārā in her various forms (including Ugratārā, Ekajaṭā, and Nīlasarasvatī). Divided into eleven taraṅgas ('waves'), it provides comprehensive ritual guidance on guru-disciple requirements, initiation (dīkṣā), daily worship, mantra recitation (japa), yantra designs, nyāsa, puraścaraṇa, and esoteric rites such as śavasādhana, compiling canonical passages from scriptures such as the Rudrayāmala, Brahmayāmala, and Tārātantra.
SA_MB_taaraabhaktisudhaarnavaHK.attribution: Attributed in the colophons to Mahāmahopādhyāya Ṭhakkura Śrī-Narasiṃha (Narasiṃha Ṭhakkura).
SA_MB_taaraabhaktisudhaarnavaHK.edition: Tārābhaktisudhārṇavaḥ. Edited by Pañcānana Tarka and Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe). Tantrik Text Series. Calcutta: Sanskrit Book Depot, 1940.
SA_MB_taaraabhaktisudhaarnavaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 11 taraṅgas ('waves'), ending with the colophon of the eleventh taraṅga (ekādaśastaraṅgaḥ).

SA_MB_saubhagyabhaskariHK.title: Lalitāsahasranāmastotra with Saubhāgyabhāskara
SA_MB_saubhagyabhaskariHK.author: Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_saubhagyabhaskariHK.summary: The Lalitāsahasranāmastotra is a hymn associated with the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa. Bhāskararāya's Saubhāgyabhāskara provides an exhaustive commentary on the hymn, elucidating the significance of each divine epithet.
SA_MB_saubhagyabhaskariHK.attribution: The root hymn is attributed to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa. The commentary Saubhāgyabhāskara was composed by Bhāskararāya (dīkṣā-name Bhāsurānandanātha), son of Gambhīrarāya Dīkṣita.
SA_MB_saubhagyabhaskariHK.edition: Lalitāsahasranāma with the Saubhāgyabhāskara of Bhāskararāya, edited by Vāsudeva Lakṣmaṇa Śāstrī Paṇśīkar, Bombay: Pāṇḍuraṅga Jāvajī, Nirṇaya Sāgara Press, 1935.
SA_MB_saubhagyabhaskariHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Lalitāsahasranāma together with Bhāskararāya's commentary.

SA_MB_sivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.title: Śivāgamādimāhātmyasaṃgraha
SA_MB_sivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.author: Jñānaprakāśa
SA_MB_sivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.summary: A Śaiva Siddhānta doctrinal and apologetic compendium compiled by Jñānaprakāśa of Śālivāṭipura. Opening with a defense of the validity (prāmāṇya) of the Śaivāgamas against opposing views asserting their non-authoritativeness, the text collates passages from Āgamic and scriptural sources to establish the authority of the Śaivāgamas, Śaiva initiation (dīkṣā), and observances such as the wearing of tripuṇḍra.
SA_MB_sivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.attribution: Authored by Jñānaprakāśa of Śālivāṭipura. In the closing homage, he venerates his preceptors Devaśikhāmaṇi and Ṣaṇmukha.
SA_MB_sivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.edition: Manuscript transcript: IFP transcript 1059 copied from a ms belonging to g. swaminatha gurukkal, tiruvadudurai. MS l no. 154 a.
SA_MB_sivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the compendium according to the manuscript transcript, concluding with the final colophon 'iti śālivāṭipuranivāsi-jñānaprakāśaguruviracitaśivāgamādimāhātmyasaṅgrahaḥ samāptaḥ'. Lacunae in the exemplar are represented by asterisks and dashes.

SA_MB_vyomavyaapistavaHK.title: Vyomavyāpistava with Laghuṭīkā
SA_MB_vyomavyaapistavaHK.author: Bhaṭṭarāmakaṇṭha, Vedajñāna
SA_MB_vyomavyaapistavaHK.summary: The Vyomavyāpistava is a Śaiva hymn expounding the significance of the 81 padas of the Vyomavyāpin mantra. It is preserved here with the commentary (Laghuṭīkā / Laghuṭippaṇī) of Vedajñāna.
SA_MB_vyomavyaapistavaHK.attribution: The root hymn is attributed in the opening of the commentary (guruṇā rāmakaṇṭhena kṛtasya...) to Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha. The commentary is by Vedajñāna, who also references his Bṛhaṭṭīkā at the end of the text.
SA_MB_vyomavyaapistavaHK.edition: Manuscript transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T0128, copied from a paper manuscript of the Vyomavyāpistava belonging to the Tiruvāvaṭutuṟai Ātīṉam (tiruvavaduthurai adheenam).
SA_MB_vyomavyaapistavaHK.coverage: complete — Text of the Vyomavyāpistava (analyzing the 81 padas of the Vyomavyāpin mantra) accompanied by the Laghuṭīkā of Vedajñāna.

SA_MB_Pranatosini_5_BhaktiKandaHK.title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī (kāṇḍa 5: Bhaktikāṇḍa, paricchedas 1–3)
SA_MB_Pranatosini_5_BhaktiKandaHK.author: Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya
SA_MB_Pranatosini_5_BhaktiKandaHK.summary: The Prāṇatoṣiṇī is a tantric compendium compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya from tantraśāstra texts. This portion contains paricchedas 1 to 3 of the fifth kāṇḍa (Bhaktikāṇḍa), concluding with the third pariccheda on Śiva (śivaprakaraṇa).
SA_MB_Pranatosini_5_BhaktiKandaHK.edition: Prāṇatoṣiṇī, śrīrāmatoṣaṇa bhaṭṭācāryeṇa tantraśāstrāt saṃkalayya viracitā, Calcutta: Jivanand Vidyasagar, 1898 (third edition).
SA_MB_Pranatosini_5_BhaktiKandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains Kāṇḍa 5 (Bhaktikāṇḍa), paricchedas 1–3, terminating with 'iti śrīprāṇatoṣiṇyāṃ pañcame bhaktikāṇḍe śivaprakaraṇakathanarūpastṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ'.

SA_MB_pranotisini_6_HK.title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī (Bhaktikāṇḍa in part, Jñānakāṇḍa, and Nirguṇakāṇḍa)
SA_MB_pranotisini_6_HK.author: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra
SA_MB_pranotisini_6_HK.summary: The Prāṇatoṣiṇī is an extensive Śākta tantric digest (nibandha) compiled in 1820 CE by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra. Bringing together citations from scores of Tantras, Purāṇas, and ritual compendia, it forms an encyclopedic reference work of the late traditional Bengali Śākta school. This segment contains the latter part of the Bhaktikāṇḍa (worship of sacred stones and Kumārīpūjā), the entire Jñānakāṇḍa (yogic subtle physiology, cakras, and breath divination in Svarodaya), and the entire Nirguṇakāṇḍa (the three spiritual temperaments or bhāvas, Kaula worship, and culminating verses of the entire text).
SA_MB_pranotisini_6_HK.attribution: Compiled in 1820 CE by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṃkāra.
SA_MB_pranotisini_6_HK.edition: Prāṇatoṣiṇī: tantraśāstrāt saṃkalayya viracitā, compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya, published by Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara Bhaṭṭācārya. Calcutta: Jivanand Vidyasagar, 1898.
SA_MB_pranotisini_6_HK.coverage: partial — Contains the concluding portion of Kāṇḍa 5 (Bhaktikāṇḍa, pariccheda 4, pp. 691–782, covering Dvārakāśilā, Viṣṇu, Devī/Mahāvidyā rituals, and Kumārīpūjā), the full Kāṇḍa 6 (Jñānakāṇḍa, lines 2816–7038, covering yogic anatomy, nāḍīs, cakras, and svarodaya), and the full Kāṇḍa 7 (Nirguṇakāṇḍa, lines 7038–11609, treating paśu, vīra, and divya bhāvas, Kaula worship, and closing recipes), ending at line 11609 with 'iti śrīprāṇatoṣiṇī samāptā'.

SA_MB_paraatantraHK.title: Parātantra
SA_MB_paraatantraHK.summary: The Parātantra is a Śākta-Kaula scripture framing its revelation within the Śiraścheda tradition. It systematically harmonizes the six transmissions (ṣaḍāmnāya) by assigning major Śākta lineages and deities—including Kubjikā (Western), Tripurasundarī (Southern), Guhyakālī and Siddhilakṣmī (Northern), and Vajrayoginī (Lower)—to six thrones, synthesizing them as manifestations of the singular supreme Goddess Parā.
SA_MB_paraatantraHK.attribution: A Śākta-Kaula scripture, framed as claiming affiliation with the Śiraścheda lineage in the colophons.
SA_MB_paraatantraHK.edition: Parātantram, edited by Dhana Śamśera Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā (Lieutenant Colonel Dhana Shamsher Jung Bahadur Rana), Prayāga: Caṇḍī Kāryālaya, Saṃvat 2016 [ CE].
SA_MB_paraatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 9 paṭalas, concluding at verse 9.101 with the colophon 'iti śrī śrotaśiraśchede mahākaravīrayoge parātantre navamo paṭalaḥ' and 'samāpta'.

SA_MB_sakalaagamasaarasangrahaHK.title: Sakalāgamasārasaṅgraha with other Śaiva ritual texts (incomplete)
SA_MB_sakalaagamasaarasangrahaHK.summary: An anonymous Śaiva Siddhānta ritual compilation containing ritual instructions including tooth cleaning, bathing, and daily worship, together with appended texts including a Vināyakavratavidhipaṭala from the Aṃśumat and an incomplete nityapūjā section.
SA_MB_sakalaagamasaarasangrahaHK.coverage: partial — The e-text covers IFP transcript T0351. The Sakalāgamasārasaṅgraha itself is acephalous (begins at fol. 4a in the middle of dantadhāvana rules) and is incomplete, containing further excerpts such as the Vināyakavratavidhipaṭala from the Aṃśumat tantra, followed by a prose nityapūjā section ending abruptly at 'karaśuddhidaśa ---'.

SA_MB_yoginiitantramHK.title: Yoginītantra
SA_MB_yoginiitantramHK.summary: Cast as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī, the text is a Śākta tantra whose second part (kāmarūpādhikāra) deals with sacred geography and worship.
SA_MB_yoginiitantramHK.coverage: partial — Lacks final work colophon/explicit; paṭala 15 of Part 2 breaks off abruptly at verse 33 ('atra paṭalasamāptirnāsti') and paṭala 16 is preserved only as a 4-verse excerpt ('ṣoḍaśapaṭalasya kecit ślokāḥ').

SA_MB_pratisthalaksanasarasamuccayaHK.title: Pratiṣṭhālakṣaṇasārasamuccaya
SA_MB_pratisthalaksanasarasamuccayaHK.author: Vairocana
SA_MB_pratisthalaksanasarasamuccayaHK.summary: The Pratiṣṭhālakṣaṇasārasamuccaya is a 32-chapter Sanskrit handbook on Śaiva-dominated temple ritual, iconography, and image consecration (pratiṣṭhā), attributed to Vairocana. It details temple building, iconometric proportions, ritual bathing, installation of lingas and deities, and ceremonies such as pavitrārohaṇa.
SA_MB_pratisthalaksanasarasamuccayaHK.attribution: The compendium is attributed to Vairocana, as stated in the closing verse of the text (chapter 32, verse 81: 'tāvadvairocanīyā jagati ciramiyaṃ pustarūpāstu kīrtiḥ').
SA_MB_pratisthalaksanasarasamuccayaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 32 chapters (vidhis), ending with chapter 32 (Pavitrārohaṇavidhi).

SA_MB_AnandatantramHK.title: Ānandatantra
SA_MB_AnandatantramHK.summary: The Ānandatantra is a South Indian Kaula scripture in 20 chapters (paṭalas) framed as an esoteric dialogue between Śrīdevī and Kāmeśvara. Affiliating itself with the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava corpus, the text details transgressive and non-dual Kaula ritual practices, emphasizing liṅgapūjā, yonipūjā, and internal subtle physiology, before concluding with expositions on philosophical systems, tantric sects, and social classifications.
SA_MB_AnandatantramHK.attribution: A Kaula scripture affiliated with the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava corpus.
SA_MB_AnandatantramHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript collation / working edition prepared by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski based on two manuscripts: Ms. K (IFP transcript no. 333 / T0333, copied from GOML Chennai Ms. 5562) and Ms. Kh (British Library, London, Ms. 2541 / IO ** ? 3 (or 8) 011).
SA_MB_AnandatantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 20 paṭalas (ending at paṭala 20, verse 109 with the concluding colophon 'ānaṃdataṃtraṃ saṃpūrṇam').

SA_MB_SpKaavrittivivrtiHK.title: Spandakārikā with the commentaries of Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa and Rāmakaṇṭha
SA_MB_SpKaavrittivivrtiHK.author: Vasugupta, Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa, Rāmakaṇṭha
SA_MB_SpKaavrittivivrtiHK.summary: The Spandakārikā is a foundational philosophical treatise of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism. This composite electronic text contains the root kārikās accompanied by two commentaries: the Spandakārikāvṛtti by Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa, accompanied by marginal explanatory notes (tippaṇī), and the Spandakārikāvivṛti by Utpaladeva's disciple Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha.
SA_MB_SpKaavrittivivrtiHK.attribution: Authorship of the root Spandakārikā is traditionally disputed between Vasugupta and Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa. The Spandakārikāvṛtti is attributed to Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa. The Spandavivṛti was composed by Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha, disciple of Utpaladeva.
SA_MB_SpKaavrittivivrtiHK.edition: Spandakārikā with vṛtti by Kallaṭa Bhaṭṭa, tippaṇī and vivṛti by Rāmakaṇṭha, with textual corrections by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski matching his 1992 translation (The Stanzas on Vibration, SUNY Press). Photographic facsimiles from Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies volume 5.
SA_MB_SpKaavrittivivrtiHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Spandakārikā together with Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa's Spandakārikāvṛtti (annotated with printed footnotes/tippaṇī) and Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha's Spandavivṛti concluding with its colophon.
translations: Dyczkowski, Mark S. G. The Stanzas on Vibration. Albany: State University of New York Press, 1992. (English)
Singh, Jaideva. Spanda-Kārikās: The Divine Creative Pulsation. Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass. (English)

SA_MB_Kulapradiipa-HK.title: Kulapradīpa
SA_MB_Kulapradiipa-HK.author: Śivānandācārya
SA_MB_Kulapradiipa-HK.summary: The Kulapradīpa ('Lamp of the Kula') is a Sanskrit Śākta-Kaula compendium (nibandha) in seven chapters (prakāśa) composed in verse by Śivānandācārya. Drawing heavily upon authoritative Āgamic sources such as the Kulārṇavatantra, it provides an exposition of the doctrines and ritual practices of the Kaula path, including the distinction between dakṣiṇa and vāma conduct, the purification and use of the five substances (pañcamakāra), dūtīyāga, and cakra worship.
SA_MB_Kulapradiipa-HK.attribution: Attributed in chapter colophons to Śivānandācārya.
SA_MB_Kulapradiipa-HK.coverage: complete — Complete text in seven prakāśas, ending with the scribal colophon dated Saṃvat 1788 (1731 CE) and recording a verse count of 1,800 ślokas.

SA_MB_JnanarnavaTantraHK.title: Jñānārṇavatantra
SA_MB_JnanarnavaTantraHK.summary: The Jñānārṇavatantra ('Ocean of Knowledge') is an authoritative scripture of the Śākta Tantric tradition and one of the principal scriptural sources for the Kādi division of Śrīvidyā. Cast in 26 paṭalas as a revelation by Īśvara to Devī, the work begins with esoteric expositions of the sacred alphabet (akṣamālā / mātṛkā), the phonematic matrix, and the threefold bindu. The remaining chapters detail the internal and ritual pūjā of Mahātripurasundarī and her attendants, yantra meditations, mantra recitation, and seasonal observances, culminating in the damanāropaṇa rite.
SA_MB_JnanarnavaTantraHK.attribution: Canonical Śākta Tantra of the Śrīvidyā (Kādi) transmission, framed traditionally as a divine revelation between Īśvara (Śiva) and Devī.
SA_MB_JnanarnavaTantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 26 paṭalas, concluding with chapter 26 (Śrīvidyādamanāropaṇavidhi).

SA_MB_Pranatosini_1_SargaKandaHK.title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī (kāṇḍa 1: Sargakāṇḍa)
SA_MB_Pranatosini_1_SargaKandaHK.author: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra
SA_MB_Pranatosini_1_SargaKandaHK.summary: The Prāṇatoṣiṇī is a Śākta-Tāntrika digest (nibandha) compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra under the patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa. This opening section, the Sargakāṇḍa (ten paricchedas), covers cosmogony, the manifestation of sound and language (śabdasṛṣṭi, sphoṭa, and varṇotpatti), bodily mysticism, embryology, and the classification of Tantric scriptures. The compendium preserves extensive extracts from numerous earlier tantras and digests.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_1_SargaKandaHK.attribution: Compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra (Bhaṭṭācārya) under the patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_1_SargaKandaHK.edition: Prāṇatoṣiṇī, compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya, published by Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara Bhaṭṭācārya, Calcutta, 1898.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_1_SargaKandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains the first kāṇḍa (Sargakāṇḍa) ending with the tenth pariccheda of the Prāṇatoṣiṇī.

SA_MB_Pranatosini_2_DharmaKandaHK.title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī (kāṇḍa 2: Dharmakāṇḍa)
SA_MB_Pranatosini_2_DharmaKandaHK.author: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra
SA_MB_Pranatosini_2_DharmaKandaHK.summary: The Dharmakāṇḍa is the second kāṇḍa forming part of the Prāṇatoṣiṇī, compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra Bhaṭṭācārya under the patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa. Across six paricchedas, it compiles scriptural testimonia from diverse tantras regarding rules of life, guru and disciple characteristics (guru-śiṣyalakṣaṇa), and the ritual procedures, merits, and theological significance of tantric initiation (dīkṣā).
SA_MB_Pranatosini_2_DharmaKandaHK.attribution: Compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra Bhaṭṭācārya under the patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_2_DharmaKandaHK.edition: Prāṇatoṣiṇī, compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya, Calcutta: Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara, 1898.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_2_DharmaKandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains the second kāṇḍa (Dharmakāṇḍa), ending with the sixth pariccheda.

SA_MB_Pranatosini_3_ArthaKandaHK.title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī (kāṇḍa 3: Arthakāṇḍa)
SA_MB_Pranatosini_3_ArthaKandaHK.author: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra
SA_MB_Pranatosini_3_ArthaKandaHK.summary: The Prāṇatoṣiṇī is a Śākta compendium compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra Bhaṭṭācārya under the patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa. This third section, the Arthakāṇḍa, treats daily rites and practices including guru devotion, kuṇḍalinī, snāna, and pūjā.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_3_ArthaKandaHK.attribution: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra Bhaṭṭācārya compiled this work under the patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_3_ArthaKandaHK.edition: Prāṇatoṣiṇī, compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya, Calcutta: Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara, 1898 (3rd edition).

SA_MB_Pranatosini_4_KamyaKandaHK.title: Prāṇatoṣiṇī (kāṇḍa 4: Kāmyakāṇḍa)
SA_MB_Pranatosini_4_KamyaKandaHK.author: Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra
SA_MB_Pranatosini_4_KamyaKandaHK.summary: The Kāmyakāṇḍa forms the fourth book of the Prāṇatoṣiṇī, a Śākta Tantric digest (nibandha) compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra under the auspices of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa. This section focuses on kāmya rituals (optional rites directed at specific worldly and spiritual fruits), detailing mantra practice, puraścaraṇa, rosary rites (mālāprakaraṇa), pilgrimage/pīṭha rules, prayogas for deities such as Kārtavīrya, Dhūmāvatī, and Ucchiṣṭacaṇḍālinī, as well as an exhaustive treatment of the autumn Durgotsava. It functions as an indispensable textual compendium preserving liturgical quotations from numerous otherwise obscure Tantras and Purāṇas.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_4_KamyaKandaHK.attribution: Compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Vidyālaṅkāra Bhaṭṭācārya under the commission and patronage of Prāṇakṛṣṇa Viśvāsa.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_4_KamyaKandaHK.edition: Prāṇatoṣiṇī, compiled by Rāmatoṣaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya, edited by Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara, Calcutta, 1898.
SA_MB_Pranatosini_4_KamyaKandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains the complete fourth kāṇḍa (Kāmyakāṇḍa) of the Prāṇatoṣiṇī, ending on page 587.

SA_MB_RudraYamalaHK.title: Rudrayāmalatantra (Uttaratantra)
SA_MB_RudraYamalaHK.summary: The Rudrayāmala is traditionally celebrated as one of the major early Śaiva-Śākta Yāmala tantras, although the ancient scripture cited by non-dual Kashmirian Śaiva authors survives only in fragmentary quotations. The extant Uttaratantra (presented here in its extensive 90-paṭala recension) is a later Kaula-Śākta compilation devoted to esoteric yoga, ritual, and mantra practice. It provides detailed expositions of Kuṇḍalinī yoga, subtle bodily physiology, the cakras along with their presiding Śaktis (Ḍākinī, Rākinī, Lākinī, Kākinī, Śākinī, and Hākinī), guru-sevā, and the worship of goddesses such as Kumārī, Tripurasundarī, and Mahākālī.
SA_MB_RudraYamalaHK.attribution: Revealed Tantric scripture cast as a dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī.
SA_MB_RudraYamalaHK.coverage: complete — Text of the 90-paṭala recension of the Uttaratantra (paṭalas 1–90, ending at verse 90.51).

SA_MB_saivaparibhasaHK.title: Śaivaparibhāṣā
SA_MB_saivaparibhasaHK.author: Śivāgrayogin
SA_MB_saivaparibhasaHK.summary: The Śaivaparibhāṣā is a Sanskrit manual of Śaiva Siddhānta philosophy composed by Śivāgrayogin, patterned after dialectical manuals such as the Vedāntaparibhāṣā. In five chapters, the work methodically details the epistemology (pramāṇa) and the three central ontological categories—the Lord (pati), the bound soul (paśu), and the fetters of bondage (pāśa)—before concluding with the path of initiation and liberation (mukti). Drawing heavily on the Saiddhāntika Āgamas (particularly the Pauṣkarāgama), it represents a major milestone in the late Sanskrit scholasticism of the school.
SA_MB_saivaparibhasaHK.edition: Devanagari edition, Oriental Research Institute (Sanskrit Series no. 90), Oriental Research Institute, University of Madras, Madras, 1950.
SA_MB_saivaparibhasaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 5 paricchedas (chapters), concluding with muktinirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ.

SA_MB_SAAMBAPA_NCAASIKAAhk.title: Sāmbapañcāśikā with Sāmbapañcāśikāvivṛti
SA_MB_SAAMBAPA_NCAASIKAAhk.author: Sāmba, Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_SAAMBAPA_NCAASIKAAhk.summary: The Sāmbapañcāśikā is a hymn celebrating Sūrya / Cidbhānu, attributed to Sāmba. In his Vivṛti, Rājānaka Kṣemarāja comments on the hymn, integrating solar devotion with philosophical concepts such as Vāk and Paraśiva.
SA_MB_SAAMBAPA_NCAASIKAAhk.attribution: The root hymn is attributed to Sāmba. The commentary (Vivṛti or Ṭīkā) is by Rājānaka Kṣemarāja, disciple of Abhinavagupta (iti mahāmāheśvarācāryavaryaśrīmadabhinavaguptapādapadmopajīvirājānakaśrīkṣemarājapraṇītavivṛtisametā śrīsāmbapañcāśikā samāptā).
SA_MB_SAAMBAPA_NCAASIKAAhk.edition: Sāmba, Sāmbapañcāśikā, édition par R. Sambasiva Sastri (Trivandrum Sanskrit Series 104), Trivandrum 1930.
SA_MB_SAAMBAPA_NCAASIKAAhk.coverage: complete — Accompanied by Kṣemarāja's Vivṛti, including closing verses and final colophon.

SA_MB_saradatilakaHK.title: Śāradātilaka with Padārthādarśa
SA_MB_saradatilakaHK.author: Lakṣmaṇadeśikendra, Rāghavabhaṭṭa
SA_MB_saradatilakaHK.summary: The Śāradātilaka of Lakṣmaṇadeśikendra is a compendium of tantric and ritual literature. Across 25 paṭalas, it integrates cosmology, phonic creation (śabdabrahman, nāda, bindu, kuṇḍalinī), dīkṣā, yantras, mudrās, and ritual procedures and dhyānas for deities. This e-text contains the root text together with the Padārthādarśa commentary of Rāghavabhaṭṭa.
SA_MB_saradatilakaHK.attribution: The root work is attributed to Lakṣmaṇadeśikendra. The Padārthādarśa commentary was composed by Rāghavabhaṭṭa in Viśveśapurī (Vārāṇasī) as recorded in the verse containing the chronogram 'ākāśeṣuśarakṣamā' in the colophon of the 25th paṭala.
SA_MB_saradatilakaHK.edition: Śāradātilakatantram, edited by Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe), 2 vols. (Tāntrik Texts), Calcutta: Āgamānusandhāna Samiti.
SA_MB_saradatilakaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 25 paṭalas of the Śāradātilaka with the Padārthādarśa commentary of Rāghavabhaṭṭa.

SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAMhk.title: Śataratnasaṃgraha with Śataratnollekhanī
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAMhk.author: Umāpatiśivācārya
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAMhk.summary: The Śataratnasaṃgraha is an anthology attributed to Umāpatiśivācārya.

SA_MB_sivaarcanacandrikaaHK.title: Śivārcanacandrikā
SA_MB_sivaarcanacandrikaaHK.author: Appayadīkṣita
SA_MB_sivaarcanacandrikaaHK.summary: The Śivārcanacandrikā ('Moonlight on the Worship of Śiva') is a ritual manual (paddhati) composed by Appayadīkṣita mentioning King Bomma. It covers stages of Śiva worship, including preliminary purification, mental preparation, installation of the deity, linga worship, and related ritual prescriptions.
SA_MB_sivaarcanacandrikaaHK.attribution: A liturgical manual composed by Appayadīkṣita mentioning King Bomma (Bomma Bhūpati) in the concluding verses, along with praise for Jvarakaṇṭheśa.
SA_MB_sivaarcanacandrikaaHK.edition: Śivārcanacandrikā, Devakottai: śivāgama siddhānta paripalana saṅgham, 1922.
SA_MB_sivaarcanacandrikaaHK.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual from the opening maṅgalācaraṇa ('yasyāhur āgamavidaḥ...') down to the dedication to King Bomma, the invocation of Jvarakaṇṭheśa, and the final colophon ('śivārcanācandrikā samāptā').

SA_MB_SAMBANDHASIDDHIHhk.title: Sambandhasiddhi with Sambandhasiddhivṛtti
SA_MB_SAMBANDHASIDDHIHhk.author: Utpaladeva
SA_MB_SAMBANDHASIDDHIHhk.summary: The Sambandhasiddhi ('Establishment of Relation') is one of the three foundational polemical monographs constituting Utpaladeva's Siddhitrayī. Composed in verse with an integral prose autocommentary (vṛtti), the text defends the ontological and linguistic reality of relations (sambandha) against Buddhist nominalist critiques, particularly Dharmakīrti's Sambandhaparīkṣā. Integrating Bhartṛhari's grammatical philosophy with non-dual Pratyabhijñā metaphysics, Utpaladeva argues that relation as identity-in-difference cannot subsist purely among insentient entities, but necessarily depends on the synthesizing, reflective awareness (vimarśa, anusaṃdhāna) of universal consciousness (Śiva).
SA_MB_SAMBANDHASIDDHIHhk.attribution: Utpaladeva explicitly identifies himself as the author in the final colophon as the son of Udayākara (śrīmadudayākaraputrotpaladevācāryaviracitā saṃbandhasiddhiḥ samāptā). He composed both the kārikā stanzas and the prose vṛtti.
SA_MB_SAMBANDHASIDDHIHhk.edition: The Siddhitrayī and the Pratyabhijñā-kārikā-vṛtti of Rājānaka Utpala Deva, edited with notes by Madhusūdan Kaul Shāstrī, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State / Kashmir Pratap Steam Press, 1921 (Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies), Sambandhasiddhi section.
SA_MB_SAMBANDHASIDDHIHhk.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Sambandhasiddhi and its autocommentary, comprising 20 numbered verses, one unnumbered concluding stanza, and the interspersed prose vṛtti, corresponding precisely to pp. 1–15 of KSTS 34.

SA_MB_sivadrstiHK.title: Śivadṛṣṭi with Śivadṛṣṭivṛtti (Vṛtti on 1.1–4.74 only)
SA_MB_sivadrstiHK.author: Somānanda, Utpaladeva
SA_MB_sivadrstiHK.summary: The Śivadṛṣṭi of Somānanda is a foundational text accompanied by Utpaladeva's commentary (Śivadṛṣṭivṛtti).
SA_MB_sivadrstiHK.attribution: The root treatise Śivadṛṣṭi was authored by Somānanda (Somānandanātha), and the commentary (Śivadṛṣṭivṛtti) was composed by Utpaladeva.
SA_MB_sivadrstiHK.edition: Śāstrī M. K. (ed.), Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies 54, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1934.
SA_MB_sivadrstiHK.coverage: partial — Root text ends with the colophon 'iti samāptisaṃjñakaṃ saptamamāhnikam || samāptā śivadṛṣṭiriyam | kṛtiḥ śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryasomānandaprabhupādānām'.

SA_MB_sivasamhita-HK.title: Śivasaṃhitā
SA_MB_sivasamhita-HK.summary: The Śivasaṃhitā is a Sanskrit manual on yoga. Structured as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī (Haragaurīsaṃvāda), it discusses philosophy, subtle anatomy, prāṇāyāma, mudrās, and meditation. It affirms that householders (gṛhastha) as well as renunciants can attain liberation through yoga.
SA_MB_sivasamhita-HK.attribution: Traditional yoga treatise structured as an exposition delivered by Śiva to Pārvatī/Gaurī (Haragaurīsaṃvāda); the historical author is unknown.
SA_MB_sivasamhita-HK.coverage: complete — Complete text in five paṭalas (chapters 1–5), ending at 5.212.

SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKAhk.title: Śivasūtra with Śivasūtravārttika
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKAhk.author: Vasugupta, Bhāskara
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKAhk.summary: The Śivasūtravārttika is an early metrical commentary composed by Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara on the Śivasūtra, the fundamental revelation of non-dual Kashmir Shaivism. Expounding 79 sūtras across three sections structured by the three means of liberation (śāmbhava-, śākta-, and āṇavopāya), Bhāskara interprets the aphorisms in close alignment with the Spanda lineage inherited through Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa. It serves as an indispensable witness to an exegetical tradition independent of Kṣemarāja's Pratyabhijñā-oriented prose Śivasūtravimarśinī.
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKAhk.attribution: The Śivasūtra is associated with Vasugupta. The metrical commentary (Vārttika) is by Bhāskara. It must be distinguished from the Śivasūtravārttika by Varadarāja (KSTS 43).
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKAhk.coverage: complete — Contains all 79 sūtras in Bhāskara's recension across the three sections (Śāmbhavopāya, Śāktopāya, and Āṇavopāya) with Bhāskara's complete metrical Vārttika commentary.
translations: Dyczkowski, Mark S. G., The Aphorisms of Śiva: The Śivasūtra with Bhāskara's Commentary, the Vārttika, Albany: State University of New York Press, 1992. (English)

SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHAhk.title: Spandasaṃdoha
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHAhk.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHAhk.summary: The Spandasaṃdoha ('Essence/Collection of Vibration') is an early exegetical work by Rājānaka Kṣemarāja dedicated exclusively to commenting on the opening verse of the Spandakārikā ('yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ...'). In this text, Kṣemarāja demonstrates how this single benedictory stanza encapsulates the full metaphysical doctrine of Spanda—the dynamic pulsation and self-awareness of Śiva—along with the divine fivefold cosmic act (pañcakṛtya). Integrating Spanda doctrine with Pratyabhijñā and Krama concepts, it serves as an introduction to his later, comprehensive commentary on the entire kārikā corpus, the Spandanirṇaya.
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHAhk.attribution: The Spandasandoha is a work of Kṣemarāja.
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHAhk.edition: The Spanda Sandoha of Kṣemarāja, ed. Mukunda Rāma Shāstrī. KSTS 16. Bombay, 1917.
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHAhk.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Spandasaṃdoha, which constitutes an exhaustive commentary on the first verse of the Spandakārikā.

SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_1-5_HK.title: Śrītattvacintāmaṇi with the commentary of Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha (chapters 1–5)
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_1-5_HK.author: Pūrṇānanda, Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_1-5_HK.summary: The Śrītattvacintāmaṇi is a tantric compendium composed by Pūrṇānanda. This e-text contains chapters 1 to 5, which address foundational metaphysical concepts (brahmasvarūpa, tattvajñāna), mantra classifications and qualifications, and rites of initiation (dīkṣā), together with the commentary of Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_1-5_HK.attribution: The root work is by Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. The Sanskrit commentary was composed by Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_1-5_HK.edition: Pūrṇānanda's Śrītattvacintāmaṇi, critically edited from original manuscripts with original commentary by Bhuvanmohan Saṅkhyatīrtha and with notes by Chintamani Bhattacharya. Calcutta, 1936.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_1-5_HK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters (prakāśas) 1 through 5, accompanied by Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha's commentary.

SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_6-10_HK.title: Śrītattvacintāmaṇi (chapters 6–10)
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_6-10_HK.author: Pūrṇānanda
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_6-10_HK.summary: The Śrītattvacintāmaṇi is a tantric work by Pūrṇānanda. This section comprises chapters 6 through 10, accompanied by a commentary by Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_6-10_HK.attribution: The commentary accompanying the text was composed by Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha (Bhuvanmohan Saṅkhyatirtha).
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_6-10_HK.edition: Pūrṇānanda's Śrītattvacintāmaṇi, ed. by Bhuvanmohan Sankhyatirtha and Chintamani Bhattacharya. Calcutta, 1936.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_6-10_HK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters (prakāśas) 6 through 10 of the work.
translations: Arthur Avalon, The Serpent Power, London: Luzac & Co., 1919 (reprint: New York: Dover Publications. (English)

SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_11-15_HK.title: Śrītattvacintāmaṇi with the commentary of Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha (chapters 11–15)
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_11-15_HK.author: Pūrṇānanda, Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_11-15_HK.summary: Prakāśas 11–15 of Pūrṇānanda's Śrītattvacintāmaṇi detail the ritual worship and esoteric mantras of goddess Tripurasundarī according to the Śrīvidyā tradition. The chapters treat the unlocked (niṣkīlita) mantras of Śāktakāmarāja, Lopāmudrā, and Śāktapañcamī across different āmnāyas, daily worship, and the intricate nyāsa rites of the Śrīcakra.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_11-15_HK.attribution: Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa is the author of the root compendium Śrītattvacintāmaṇi. The Sanskrit commentary was written by Bhuvanamohan Sāṅkhyatīrtha for the 1936 Calcutta edition.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_11-15_HK.edition: Pūrṇānanda's Śrītattvacintāmaṇi: Critically Edited from Original Manuscripts with Original Commentary by Bhuvanmohan Sankhyatirtha and with Notes by Chintamani Bhattacharya. Calcutta, 1936.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamani_11-15_HK.coverage: partial — Contains prakāśas 11–15 (verses with commentary) of Śrītattvacintāmaṇi.

SA_MB_Sritattvacintamanii_16-End_HK.title: Śrītattvacintāmaṇi (chapters 16–26)
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamanii_16-End_HK.author: Pūrṇānanda
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamanii_16-End_HK.summary: The Śrītattvacintāmaṇi is a tantric compendium composed by Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. This section (prakāśas 16–26) covers antaryāga, ritual worship, nyāsas, mudrās, and related rites according to Tantric traditions.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamanii_16-End_HK.attribution: The root text was composed by Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa. In the 1936 edition, it was critically edited from original manuscripts with an original commentary by Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha and with notes by Cintāmaṇi Bhaṭṭācārya.
SA_MB_Sritattvacintamanii_16-End_HK.coverage: partial — Contains prakāśas 16 through 26 (ending with the colophon iti śrīpūrṇānandaparamahaṃsaviracite śrī-tattvacintāmaṇau ṣaḍviṃśatitamaḥ prakāśaḥ || 26 || śrītattvacintāmaṇiḥ samāptaḥ) along with commentary and notes.
translations: Arthur Avalon, The Serpent Power. London: Luzac & Co., 1919. (English)

SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANIhk.title: Stavacintāmaṇi with Stavacintāmaṇivivṛti
SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANIhk.author: Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa, Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANIhk.summary: The Stavacintāmaṇi ('Wish-fulfilling Jewel of Praise') is a devotional hymn composed by Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa, accompanied by the commentary (Vivṛti) of Kṣemarāja.
SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANIhk.attribution: The root text is by Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa and the commentary is by Kṣemarāja.
SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANIhk.coverage: unclear — Database record currently contains no text excerpts.

SA_MB_suprabhedagamaHK.title: Suprabhedāgama
SA_MB_suprabhedagamaHK.summary: The Suprabhedāgama is one of the twenty-eight canonical Mūlāgamas of dualist Śaiva Siddhānta, traditionally categorized among the five Śivabhedas emanating from the Vāmadeva face of Śiva. It is one of the relatively few Āgamas preserved across all four classical divisions (pādas): Kriyāpāda (temple layout, iconography, installation of liṅgas, and daily/occasional worship rituals), Caryāpāda (initiation, duties of devotees, royal rites, and expiation), Yogapāda (subtle anatomy, prāṇāyāma, and meditation), and Jñānapāda (cosmogony, thirty-six tattvas, and the adhvans). It has long served as a prominent ritual authority for South Indian temple architecture and liturgical performance.
SA_MB_suprabhedagamaHK.attribution: Canonical Śaiva Siddhānta scripture; anonymous revealed text.
SA_MB_suprabhedagamaHK.edition: Suprabhedāgama. Devakottai: Śivāgama Siddhānta Paripālana Saṅgham, 1931.
SA_MB_suprabhedagamaHK.coverage: partial — Contains all four pādas—Kriyāpāda, Caryāpāda, Yogapāda, and Jñānapāda—but terminates abruptly at verse 3.230 of the Jñānapāda without an explicit or final colophon.

SA_MB_SvacchandatantraHK.title: Svacchandatantra with Uddyota
SA_MB_SvacchandatantraHK.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_SvacchandatantraHK.summary: The Svacchandatantra is an āgamic/tantric scripture. Presented with the running Uddyota commentary of Kṣemarāja, it covers ritual worship (arcādhikāra), cosmology, initiation, mantras, and esoteric sign-language (chummakā).
SA_MB_SvacchandatantraHK.attribution: The root Svacchandatantra is an anonymous scriptural tantra. The Uddyota commentary was composed by Kṣemarāja.
SA_MB_SvacchandatantraHK.edition: The Swacchanda-Tantra with commentary [Udyota] by Kṣemarāja, I-VI, edited with notes by Madhusudan Kaul Shāstrī, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies, 31, 38, 44, 48, 51/53, 56, Bombay, 1921-35.
SA_MB_SvacchandatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 15 paṭalas (concluding with the chummakāprakāśa colophon), containing both the root text and Kṣemarāja's running Uddyota commentary.

SA_MB_Tantraloka-1-14-HK.title: Tantrāloka with Tantrālokaviveka (chapters 1–14)
SA_MB_Tantraloka-1-14-HK.author: Abhinavagupta, Jayaratha
SA_MB_Tantraloka-1-14-HK.summary: The Tantrāloka ('Light on the Tantras') is Abhinavagupta's monumental encyclopedic synthesis of nondual Kashmir Śaivism (Trika and Kaula), presenting a comprehensive exposition of Śaiva metaphysics, yoga, and ritual based primarily upon the Mālinīvijayottaratantra. Accompanied by Jayaratha's indispensable Viveka commentary, āhnikas 1–14 set forth the philosophical and soteriological core of the system. This includes the four means to liberation (anupāya, śāmbhavopāya, śāktopāya, and āṇavopāya), the cosmology of the six paths (ṣaḍadhvan), the doctrine of time (kāla), and the preliminary requirements for initiation (dīkṣā).
SA_MB_Tantraloka-1-14-HK.attribution: The root work Tantrāloka was composed by Abhinavagupta. The Viveka commentary was composed by Rājānaka Jayaratha.
SA_MB_Tantraloka-1-14-HK.coverage: partial — Contains āhnikas 1 through 14 of 37, accompanied by Jayaratha's Viveka commentary, terminating at the colophon of the 14th āhnika (dīkṣopakramaprakāśana).

SA_MB_Tantraloka-15-37-HK.title: Tantrāloka with Tantrālokaviveka (chapters 15–37)
SA_MB_Tantraloka-15-37-HK.author: Abhinavagupta, Jayaratha
SA_MB_Tantraloka-15-37-HK.summary: Āhnikas 15 through 37 form the extensive ritual, yogic, and canon-defining second half of Abhinavagupta's Tantrāloka, accompanied by Jayaratha's Viveka commentary.
