The text systematically expounds daily and occasional Trika worship, multiple grades and variations of initiation (dīkṣā), post-initiatory practice, construction of maṇḍalas, funerary and ancestral rites (antyeṣṭi, śrāddha), and esoteric Kaula ritual (āhnika 29). The work concludes in āhnika 37 with an evaluation of the Śaiva scriptural hierarchy, the transmission of the teaching, and Abhinavagupta's personal lineage.
SA_MB_Tantraloka-15-37-HK.attribution: Root text composed by Abhinavagupta. The Viveka commentary was composed by Jayaratha.
SA_MB_Tantraloka-15-37-HK.edition: The Tantrāloka of Abhinava Gupta. With Commentary of Rājānaka Jayaratha. 12 vols., ed. Mukund Rām Shāstrī a. o., Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), 28, 30, 36, 35, 29, 41, 47, 59, 52, 57, 58, Allahabad etc., 1918–1938.
SA_MB_Tantraloka-15-37-HK.coverage: partial — Contains āhnikas 15 through 37 (the concluding chapter) of both the root text and Viveka. Āhnika 37 is the actual final chapter of the text, ending with 'samāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ'.
translations: Luce delle Sacre Scritture (Tantrāloka), translated by Raniero Gnoli, Turin: Unione Tipografico-Editrice Torinese, 1972 (2nd revised ed. 1999). (Italian)
The Tantrāloka of Abhinavagupta, Chapter 29: A Study of the Kula Ritual, translated by John R. Dupuche, 2003. (English)

SA_MB_taaraatantramHK.title: Tārātantra
SA_MB_taaraatantramHK.summary: The Tārātantra is a short Śākta scripture in six paṭalas formatted as a dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī, devoted to the worship of the Mahāvidyā goddess Tārā (in forms such as Ugratārā and Ekajaṭā). It details her five-syllable root mantra, visualizations (dhyāna), daily liturgy (prātaḥkṛtya, guru-pūjā), and magical rites (ṣaṭkarman). The text is especially renowned for its integration of the Mahācīnakrama ('Chinese/Tibetan rite'), recounting how both the sage Vasiṣṭha and the Buddha attained spiritual perfection (siddhi) through this esoteric discipline.
SA_MB_taaraatantramHK.attribution: Revealed Śākta scripture framed as a dialogue between Śiva (Bhairava) and the Devī (Bhairavī). No human author is attributed.
SA_MB_taaraatantramHK.edition: Tārātantram, edited by Girīśacandra Vedāntatīrtha, with an introduction by A. K. Maitra. 1913; reprinted Delhi: Bani Prakashan, 1983.
SA_MB_taaraatantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Tārātantra in 6 paṭalas (concluding at segment 328 with '[ samāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ ]'), followed by the editor's three appendices of related extracts on Mahācīnācāra from the Brahmayāmala, Rudrayāmala, and Mīnanātha's Smaradīpikā (segments 329–575).

SA_MB_tararahasyaHK.title: Tārārahasya
SA_MB_tararahasyaHK.author: Brahmānandagiri
SA_MB_tararahasyaHK.summary: The Tārārahasya ('Secret of Tārā') by Brahmānandagiri is a fundamental ritual manual (nibandha) dedicated to the worship, mantras, and meditative forms (dhyāna) of the Mahāvidyā Tārā and her manifestations (such as Ugratārā, Nīlasarasvatī, and Ekajaṭā). Divided into four chapters (paṭalas), it incorporates both normative tantric ritual procedures and the esoteric Mahācīnakrama. Synthesizing citations from older authorities such as the Nīlatantra, Mahācīnatantra, and Rudrayāmala, it served as one of the primary handbooks of the Tārā cult across Bengal and Assam.
SA_MB_tararahasyaHK.attribution: Authored by Brahmānandagiri (also referred to as Śrī Brahmānanda Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka).
SA_MB_tararahasyaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 4 paṭalas, matching the 82 pages of the Calcutta print edition.

SA_MB_taaraarahasyavrttikaaHK.title: Tārārahasyavṛttikā (paṭalas 1–8, incomplete)
SA_MB_taaraarahasyavrttikaaHK.author: Śaṅkara
SA_MB_taaraarahasyavrttikaaHK.summary: The Tārārahasyavṛttikā by Śaṅkara is a Śākta tantric commentary/manual focusing on Tārā (Nīlasarasvatī). It cites works such as the Nīlatantra on ritual procedures. This e-text is incomplete, containing only 8 of the 15 chapters.
SA_MB_taaraarahasyavrttikaaHK.attribution: Incipit / opening colophon: 'kṛtā śrīśaṅkareṇaiṣā tārārahasyavṛttikā'; Muktabodha names the commentator Gauḍīya Śaṅkara (gauḍīyaśaṅkarācārya). Citations include the Nīlatantra.
SA_MB_taaraarahasyavrttikaaHK.edition: Tārārahasyavṛttikā of Śaṅkara, ed. Pandita Manindra Mohan Chowdhury Kavyatirtha, Calcutta Press (first publisher), Calcutta, Pre-1900.
SA_MB_taaraarahasyavrttikaaHK.coverage: partial — ilx_skt Muktabodha metadata records 'incomplete ... 8 chapters present out of 15', lacking final colophon. The e-text breaks off at 'devadravyantu kubjikāyāṃ'.

SA_MB_VamakesvarimataHK.title: Vāmakeśvarīmata with Vāmakeśvarīmatavivaraṇa
SA_MB_VamakesvarimataHK.author: Jayaratha
SA_MB_VamakesvarimataHK.summary: The Vāmakeśvarīmata (more commonly known as the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava) is a foundational scriptural tantra of the Kaula Śrīvidyā tradition dedicated to the goddess Tripurasundarī. It details the geometry and esoteric worship of the Śrīcakra, the mantras and iconography of the fifteen Nityā goddesses, ritual hand gestures (mudrās), and mantric practices. In this commentary (Vivaraṇa), the Kashmiri master Rājānaka Jayaratha interprets the Śākta liturgy through the non-dualistic philosophical lens of the Kashmir Śaiva Trika and Pratyabhijñā traditions.
SA_MB_VamakesvarimataHK.attribution: The root work, Vāmakeśvarīmata (commonly titled Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava), is an anonymous revelation of the Kaula Śrīvidyā tradition. The commentary (Vivaraṇa) was authored by Rājānaka Jayaratha.
SA_MB_VamakesvarimataHK.edition: The Vāmakeśvarīmatam with the Commentary of Rājānaka Jayaratha, edited with introduction and notes by Madhusudan Kaul Shāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies. Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1945.
SA_MB_VamakesvarimataHK.coverage: complete — Text of the Vāmakeśvarīmata with Jayaratha's Vivaraṇa, corresponding to KSTS 66.
translations: The Kulacūḍāmaṇi Tantra and The Vāmakeśvara Tantra with the Jayaratha Commentary, introduced, translated and annotated by Louise M. Finn. Wiesbaden: Otto Harrassowitz, 1986. (English)
Vamakesvarimatam, text with English translation by Michael Magee. Tantra Granthamala No. 11. Varanasi, 1986. (English)

SA_MB_varivasyaarahasyaHK.title: Varivasyārahasya with Prakāśa
SA_MB_varivasyaarahasyaHK.author: Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_varivasyaarahasyaHK.summary: The Varivasyārahasya ('Secret of Worship') is an influential manual of Śrīvidyā theology, mantra-śāstra, and internal contemplative worship composed by the polymath Bhāskararāya Makhin, accompanied by his autocommentary, the Prakāśa. The text provides an esoteric analysis of the fifteen-syllable Śrīvidyā mantra (pañcadaśākṣarī), demonstrating how each letter and component encodes cosmological principles, subtle yogic centers, deities, and philosophical correspondences across multiple hermeneutical registers. Synthesizing Śākta ritual theology with Advaita Vedānta, Bhāskararāya argues that the culmination of mantra worship is the non-dual realization of identity between the practitioner, the mantra, and the supreme Goddess as pure consciousness.
SA_MB_varivasyaarahasyaHK.attribution: Composed by Bhāskararāya Makhin (initiatory dīkṣā name: Bhāsurānandanātha), son of Gambhīrarāya Bhāratīdīkṣita and disciple of Nṛsiṃhānandanātha, as declared in the concluding colophon.
SA_MB_varivasyaarahasyaHK.edition: Varivasyārahasya with commentary Prakāśa by Bhāskararāya, edited by Subrahmanya Śāstrī. Adyar: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1932 (DLI item 2015.202793).
SA_MB_varivasyaarahasyaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Varivasyārahasya together with its commentary, concluding with the final colophon.

SA_MB_vatulanathasutraHK.title: Vātūlanāthasūtra with Vātūlanāthasūtravṛtti
SA_MB_vatulanathasutraHK.author: Vātūlanātha, Anantaśaktipāda
SA_MB_vatulanathasutraHK.summary: The Vātūlanāthasūtra is a short Kashmiri Krama/Kaula text of thirteen aphorisms traditionally regarded as an oral revelation from the Yoginīs to the master Vātūlanātha. Accompanied by the commentary (vṛtti) of Anantaśaktipāda, the work articulates the Sāhasa ('sudden leap') transmission of nondual Śaivism, expounding the immediate entry (mahāsāhasa-vṛtti) into transcendent Śiva-consciousness that bypasses gradual contemplative disciplines. It constitutes an essential witness to the non-systematic, esoteric lineage of the Mahārtha school.
SA_MB_vatulanathasutraHK.attribution: The thirteen root aphorisms are traditionally attributed to the siddha Vātūlanātha as an oral revelation received directly from the Yoginīs; the commentary (vṛtti) is composed by Anantaśaktipāda.
SA_MB_vatulanathasutraHK.edition: The Vātūlanātha-Sūtras with the Vṛtti of Anantaśaktipāda, edited with English translation and notes by Pandit Madhusudan Kaul Shastri, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Bombay: Printed at the Nirnaya Sagar Press for the Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1923.
SA_MB_vatulanathasutraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all 13 sūtras with the introductory verses, complete vṛtti of Anantaśaktipāda, and concluding verses.
translations: The Vātūlanātha-Sūtras with the Vṛtti of Anantaśaktipāda, edited with English translation and notes by Pt. Madhusudan Kaul Shāstrī, KSTS 39, Bombay, 1923. (English)

SA_MB_visvasaaratantramHK.title: Viśvasāratantra
SA_MB_visvasaaratantramHK.summary: The Viśvasāratantra is a Śākta-Śaiva tantric work structured around dialogue between Śiva and the Devī, addressing ritual procedure, mantras, yantras, deities, and protective hymns such as the Durgāsahasranāmastotra and Sarasvatīkavaca.
SA_MB_visvasaaratantramHK.attribution: Tantric scripture presented as a teaching involving Śiva (Mahākāla / Īśvara) and the Devī.
SA_MB_visvasaaratantramHK.edition: Rasikamohana Caṭṭopādhyāya (ed.), Viśvasāratantra, in Tantrasārādi-vividhamūlatantrasaṃgrahe viśvasāra nāma mahātantra, Calcutta, end of 19th century (printed in Bengali characters).
SA_MB_visvasaaratantramHK.coverage: complete — Text concluding with the Sarasvatīkavaca and the Bengali publication colophon of Rasikamohana Caṭṭopādhyāya's edition.

SA_MB_advayataarakopanisatHK.title: Advayatārakopaniṣad with Advayatārakopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_advayataarakopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_advayataarakopanisatHK.summary: The Advayatārakopaniṣad is a short Yoga Upaniṣad reckoning as the 53rd text in the Muktikā canon and traditionally belonging to the Śuklayajurveda. It expounds Tārakayoga ('the deliverer yoga'), detailing the meditative absorption in internal and external light signs (antarlakṣya, bahirlakṣya, and madhyamalakṣya), the practice of the śāmbhavī mudrā, and the crossing over of saṃsāra into nondual Brahman. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa interprets the yogic physiology and photic visions in terms of Advaita Vedānta metaphysics.
SA_MB_advayataarakopanisatHK.attribution: The Advayatārakopaniṣad is a Yoga Upaniṣad counted as no. 53 in the 108 Upaniṣads and traditionally assigned to the Śuklayajurveda. The Vivaraṇa commentary is by Śrī Vāsudevendraśiṣya Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_advayataarakopanisatHK.edition: The Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad-Brahma-Yogin, edited by A. Mahadeva Sastri, Madras: The Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_advayataarakopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Advayatārakopaniṣad (19 sections) along with the complete Vivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, corresponding to pp. 1–10 of the 1920 Adyar edition.

SA_MB_amrtabinduupanisatHK.title: Amṛtabindūpaniṣad with Amṛtabindūpaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_amrtabinduupanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_amrtabinduupanisatHK.summary: The Amṛtabindūpaniṣad is a concise Yoga Upaniṣad in 22 verses expounding the nature and control of the mind as the prime cause of bondage and liberation (bandhāya viṣayāsaktaṃ muktyai nirviṣayaṃ smṛtam). It distinguishes the mind attached to objects from the unattached mind, teaching the dissolution of thought into Brahman. In this e-text, the root text is accompanied verse-by-verse by the complete Vivaraṇa commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, who concludes by identifying the transcendental Brahman with Vāsudeva.
SA_MB_amrtabinduupanisatHK.attribution: The root Upaniṣad is an anonymous Yoga Upaniṣad. The Vivaraṇa commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra), commenting as part of the 108 Upaniṣad commentary series (śrīmadīśādyaṣṭottaraśatopaniṣacchāstravivaraṇa).
SA_MB_amrtabinduupanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_amrtabinduupanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Amṛtabindūpaniṣad in 22 verses accompanied verse-by-verse by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's complete Vivaraṇa, concluding with his final verses and colophon.

SA_MB_amrtanaadopanisatHK.title: Amṛtanādopaniṣad with Amṛtanādopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_amrtanaadopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_amrtanaadopanisatHK.summary: The Amṛtanādopaniṣad is a classical Yoga Upaniṣad that outlines a sixfold yoga (ṣaḍaṅgayoga: pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, tarka, and samādhi). It uses the allegory of ascending the chariot of Oṃkāra to transcend worldly existence, details breath retention measured by specific mātrā counts, and describes the ascent of prāṇa through the crown of the head as the path to immortality. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary (Vivaraṇa) integrates these yogic techniques into an Advaita Vedāntic framework culminating in non-dual Self-realization.
SA_MB_amrtanaadopanisatHK.attribution: The root text is an anonymous Yoga Upaniṣad included as the 21st text in the Muktikā collection of 108 Upaniṣads (ekaviṃśatiṃsaṃkhyāpūrakam in the colophon). The commentary (Vivaraṇa) was composed by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra) as part of his commentary on the 108 Upaniṣads.
SA_MB_amrtanaadopanisatHK.edition: Mahādeva Śāstrī (ed.), Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_amrtanaadopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 38 verses of the Amṛtanādopaniṣad with the complete Vivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
translations: K. Narayanasvami Aiyar, Thirty Minor Upaniṣads: English Translation with Sanskrit Text. (English)

SA_MB_brahmavidyaopanisatHK.title: Brahmavidyopaniṣad with Brahmavidyopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_brahmavidyaopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_brahmavidyaopanisatHK.summary: The Brahmavidyopaniṣad is a minor Yoga Upaniṣad (canonically numbered 40 in the 108 Upaniṣad collection). It sets forth the esoteric meditation upon Brahman by means of the sacred syllable Om (praṇava) and the haṃsa mantra, analyzing the constituent acoustic elements (mātrās), bodily loci, internal resonance (nāda), and dissolution into non-dual consciousness. This e-text provides the root text accompanied by the commentary (Vivaraṇa) of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_brahmavidyaopanisatHK.attribution: The Brahmavidyopaniṣad is an anonymous minor Upaniṣad (numbered 40 in the Muktikā list: catvāriṃśatsaṃkhyāpūrakaṃ). The commentary (Brahmavidyopaniṣadvivaraṇa) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_brahmavidyaopanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_brahmavidyaopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Brahmavidyopaniṣad together with the Vivaraṇa commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, corresponding to pp. 250–272 of the 1920 Adyar edition.

SA_MB_dhyaanabinduupanisatHK.title: Dhyānabindūpaniṣad with the commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_dhyaanabinduupanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_dhyaanabinduupanisatHK.summary: The Dhyānabindūpaniṣad is one of the twenty Yoga Upaniṣads, traditionally grouped with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda and listed as the 39th text in the Muktikā canon of 108 Upaniṣads. In this 106-verse South Indian recension, it expounds meditation (dhyāna) on the sacred syllable Om and its subtle drop (bindu), emphasizing that such contemplation destroys karmic residues. The treatise delineates a six-limbed yoga (ṣaḍaṅgayoga) omitting yama and niyama, subtle physiological structures (cakras and nāḍīs), the involuntary haṃsa breath, prāṇāyāma, and bodily mudrās including mahāmudrā, mahābandha, and khecarīmudrā. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary interprets these practices from an Advaita Vedāntic perspective as instruments for realizing the non-dual Brahman.
SA_MB_dhyaanabinduupanisatHK.attribution: The root Dhyānabindūpaniṣad is an anonymous śruti text traditionally affiliated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (or Atharvaveda in some recensions). The embedded commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_dhyaanabinduupanisatHK.edition: śāstrī mahādeva (ed.), Dhyānabindūpaniṣat with commentary of Brahmayogin, Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_dhyaanabinduupanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Dhyānabindūpaniṣad with the commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.

SA_MB_hamsopanisadHK.title: Haṃsopaniṣad with Haṃsopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_hamsopanisadHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_hamsopanisadHK.summary: The Haṃsopaniṣad is a minor Yoga Upaniṣad framed as an esoteric dialogue between Gautama and Sanatkumāra. It elaborates on the ajapā-mantra ('haṃsa'/'so'ham') in relation to breath, the petals of the heart lotus, and internal meditative absorption through the manifestation of ten internal sounds (nāda). Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa commentary interprets these disciplines from an Advaita Vedānta perspective.
SA_MB_hamsopanisadHK.attribution: The Haṃsopaniṣad is an anonymous minor Yoga Upaniṣad (number 15 in the Muktikā canon). The commentary (Vivaraṇa) was authored by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, pupil of Vāsudevendra.
SA_MB_hamsopanisadHK.edition: Yoga upaniṣads with the commentary of śrī upaniṣad brahmayogin, edited by śāstrī mahādeva, Madras: Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_hamsopanisadHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Haṃsopaniṣad in 21 sections/mantras together with the complete Haṃsopaniṣadvivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.

SA_MB_ksurikopanisatHK.title: Kṣurikopaniṣad with Kṣurikopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_ksurikopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_ksurikopanisatHK.summary: The Kṣurikopaniṣad is an early Yoga Upaniṣad affiliated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, counted as the 31st Upaniṣad in the Muktikā canon. It expounds yogic practice through the metaphor of a razor-sharp instrument of dhāraṇā and discriminative knowledge that cuts through karmic bonds, bodily attachment, and the knot of the heart (hṛdayagranthi). The text details steady posture, breath control coordinated with the twelve-mātrā praṇava, sense withdrawal, and subtle meditative ascension along the nāḍīs up to liberation. The e-text contains the entire mūla along with the vivaraṇa of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_ksurikopanisatHK.attribution: The Kṣurikopaniṣad is an anonymous Yoga Upaniṣad belonging traditionally to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda and listed as #31 in the 108 Upaniṣad collection. The commentary (vivaraṇa) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_ksurikopanisatHK.edition: Mahādeva Śāstrī (ed.), Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_ksurikopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Kṣurikopaniṣad in 24 verses together with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's complete Kṣurikopaniṣadvivaraṇa.

SA_MB_mahaavaakyopanisatCSX.title: Mahāvākyopaniṣad with Mahāvākyopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_mahaavaakyopanisatCSX.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_mahaavaakyopanisatCSX.summary: The Mahāvākyopaniṣad is an Upaniṣad numbered 92 in the 108 Upaniṣad collection. Across twelve concise sections, it expounds the direct non-dual realization of Brahman and the dissolution of phenomenal existence. This e-text provides the root text alongside the complete Vivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_mahaavaakyopanisatCSX.attribution: The root Mahāvākyopaniṣad is traditionally numbered 92 in the 108 Upaniṣad collection. The commentary (vivaraṇa) is by Śrī Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (disciple of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_mahaavaakyopanisatCSX.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_mahaavaakyopanisatCSX.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Mahāvākyopaniṣad across 12 sections together with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's complete Vivaraṇa commentary (62 granthas).

SA_MB_mandalabraahmanopanisaHK.title: Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇopaniṣad with Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_mandalabraahmanopanisaHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_mandalabraahmanopanisaHK.summary: The Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇopaniṣad is a minor Yoga Upaniṣad affiliated with the Śukla Yajurveda, framed as a dialogue between the sage Yājñavalkya and the deity residing in the solar disc (ādityamaṇḍala, identified with Nārāyaṇa). In five brāhmaṇas, it synthesizes Haṭhayogic bodily techniques with Rājayoga and Advaita Vedāntic metaphysics, detailing a redefined eight-limbed yoga (aṣṭāṅgayoga), contemplation of internal and external luminosity (tārakayoga), the five voids (vyomapañcaka), and the trans-mental absorption of amanaskayoga leading to manonāśa and jīvanmukti. In this file, the root text is accompanied by the complete Vivaraṇa commentary of the 18th-century Advaitin Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_mandalabraahmanopanisaHK.attribution: The commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra), confirmed in the concluding colophon.
SA_MB_mandalabraahmanopanisaHK.edition: Śāstrī Mahādeva (ed.), Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_mandalabraahmanopanisaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all five brāhmaṇas of the Upaniṣad along with the full Vivaraṇa commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.

SA_MB_naadabinduupanisatHK.title: Nādabindūpaniṣad with Nādabindūpaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_naadabinduupanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_naadabinduupanisatHK.summary: The Nādabindūpaniṣad is one of the classical Yoga Upaniṣads belonging to the Muktikā canon. It opens by mapping the cosmic Praṇava (Oṃkāra) and its twelve constituent mātrās onto the sacred Haṃsa bird, delineating the respective planes attained through contemplation of each measure. It then expounds Nādānusandhāna (meditation on the inner mystic sound) seated in the Siddha posture, detailing the progression from coarse internal sounds to increasingly subtle vibrations, leading to dissolution of the mind (manolaya) into the supreme soundless Absolute. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa interprets the entire yogic progression through the lens of non-dual Advaita Vedānta culminating in videhamukti.
SA_MB_naadabinduupanisatHK.attribution: The Nādabindūpaniṣad is an anonymous Yoga Upaniṣad numbered 38 in the 108 Muktikā canon. The commentary (vivaraṇa) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, disciple of Vāsudevendra.
SA_MB_naadabinduupanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_naadabinduupanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete root text (56 verses) together with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's full Vivaraṇa commentary.

SA_MB_paasupatabrahmopanisatHK.title: Pāśupatabrahmopaniṣad with Pāśupatabrahmopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_paasupatabrahmopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_paasupatabrahmopanisatHK.summary: The Pāśupatabrahmopaniṣad is a Yoga Upaniṣad structured around a dialogue between the creator Brahmā and his son Vaiśravaṇa (Vālakhilya). Across two sections (Pūrvakāṇḍa and Uttarakāṇḍa), the text internalizes Vedic sacrificial concepts, reinterpreting the sacrificial thread (yajñasūtra) and external ritual offerings as internal spiritual awareness, the Haṃsa mantra, and continuous contemplation of the Paramātman. It fuses Pāśupata Śaiva imagery with non-dual Vedāntic metaphysics. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary (Vivaraṇa) interprets the text from an Advaita Vedānta perspective, emphasizing the realization of unconditioned Brahman (niṣpratiyogika-brahman).
SA_MB_paasupatabrahmopanisatHK.attribution: The root Pāśupatabrahmopaniṣad is a scriptural text. The colophon identifies it as number 77 in the collection of 108 Upaniṣads (saptasaptatisaṃkhyāpūrakaṃ). The commentary (Vivaraṇa) was composed by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, a pupil of Śrī Vāsudevendra.
SA_MB_paasupatabrahmopanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Śāstrī Mahādeva, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_paasupatabrahmopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of both the Pūrvakāṇḍa and Uttarakāṇḍa of the Pāśupatabrahmopaniṣad along with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's complete Vivaraṇa.

SA_MB_saandilyopanisatHK.title: Śāṇḍilyopaniṣad with Śāṇḍilyopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_saandilyopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_saandilyopanisatHK.summary: The Śāṇḍilyopaniṣad is a classical Yoga Upaniṣad framed as an instruction given by Atharvan to the sage Śāṇḍilya. Its first and longest chapter details an eight-limbed yoga (aṣṭāṅga-yoga) incorporating Haṭha-yogic practices, including ten yamas, ten niyamas, eight āsanas, detailed instructions on nāḍī-purification, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna, and samādhi. The second and third chapters expound the non-dual nature of Brahman in both saguṇa/sakala and nirguṇa/niṣkala aspects, integrating bodily yoga into Advaita Vedānta. In this edition, the text is accompanied by the complete Advaitic commentary (vivaraṇa) of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_saandilyopanisatHK.attribution: The root work is an anonymous minor Yoga Upaniṣad. The commentary (vivaraṇa) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_saandilyopanisatHK.edition: Mahādeva Śāstrī (ed.), Yoga Upanishads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_saandilyopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all three adhyāyas of the Śāṇḍilyopaniṣad accompanied by the complete commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.

SA_MB_tejobinduupanisatHK.title: Tejobindūpaniṣad with Tejobindūpaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_tejobinduupanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_tejobinduupanisatHK.summary: The Tejobindūpaniṣad is an Upaniṣad dealing with yoga and non-dual Advaita Vedānta philosophy, concluding with teachings on the nature of Brahman and jīvanmukti. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa commentary provides an exposition interpreting the text from the perspective of radical non-duality (advaita).
SA_MB_tejobinduupanisatHK.attribution: The Vivaraṇa commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (Śrīvāsudevendraśiṣya), closing with the statement identifying it as commentary no. 37 in the 108 Upaniṣad commentary corpus (itīśādyaṣṭottaraśatopaniṣacchāstravivaraṇe saptatriṃśatsaṃkhyāpūrakaṃ tejobindūpaniṣadvivaraṇaṃ saṃpūrṇam).
SA_MB_tejobinduupanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Śāstrī Mahādeva, Madras: Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_tejobinduupanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete across all six adhyāyas of the Tejobindūpaniṣad together with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa commentary, closing with the commentary colophon identifying it as commentary no. 37.

SA_MB_yoginiihrdayamHK.title: Yoginīhṛdaya with Yoginīhṛdayadīpikā
SA_MB_yoginiihrdayamHK.author: Amṛtānanda
SA_MB_yoginiihrdayamHK.summary: The Yoginīhṛdaya ('Heart of the Yoginī') is a canonical scripture of the Śrīvidyā Kaula lineage, regarded as the Uttaracatuḥśatī (second part of 400 verses) of the Vāmakeśvaratantra. Across three chapters—Cakrasaṃketa, Mantrasaṃketa, and Pūjāsaṃketa—it presents the cosmogenetic and subtle-body symbolism of the Śrīcakra, the phonic emanation of Tripurasundarī's fifteen-syllable Vidyā, and esoteric internal ritual meditation. The accompanying Dīpikā by Amṛtānanda is the earliest extant commentary on the treatise, systematically interpreting its Śākta ritual liturgy through non-dual Pratyabhijñā and Trika philosophy.
SA_MB_yoginiihrdayamHK.attribution: The commentary Yoginīhṛdayadīpikā is by Amṛtānanda, disciple of Puṇyānanda.
SA_MB_yoginiihrdayamHK.edition: Yoginīhṛdaya with the Dīpikā by Amṛtānanda, ed. Gopīnātha Kavirāja. Sarasvatībhavana Sanskrit Series, Queen's College, Benares, 1923.
SA_MB_yoginiihrdayamHK.coverage: complete — Contains all three chapters (saṃketas): Cakrasaṃketa (1), Mantrasaṃketa (2), and Pūjāsaṃketa (3), containing the root verses along with Amṛtānanda's Dīpikā commentary.

SA_MB_brhannilatantram-HK.title: Bṛhannīlatantra
SA_MB_brhannilatantram-HK.summary: The Bṛhannīlatantra ('Great Nīla Tantra') is an important Kaula Śākta ritual work in 24 chapters (paṭalas) framed as an esoteric dialogue between Mahākālabhairava and the Goddess. Centered on the worship of the Mahāvidyās Tārā (specifically Nīlasarasvatī / Ugratārā) and Kālī, the text details mantras, yantras, dīkṣā procedures, puraścaryā, kavacas, and sahasranāmas. It also contains significant material on the Mahācīnācāra path, vīrasādhana, alchemical transmutation (rasaśāstra / dhātuvāda), and the worship of Annapūrṇā.
SA_MB_brhannilatantram-HK.attribution: Anonymous Kaula Śākta scripture framed as a dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī.
SA_MB_brhannilatantram-HK.edition: Bṛhannīlatantram, edited by Madhusudan Kaul Shastri (catalog header) / prepared by Harabhatta Shastri assisted by Shivanatha Shastri under Ramchandra Kak, Srinagar, 1941.
SA_MB_brhannilatantram-HK.coverage: complete — Complete in 24 chapters (paṭalas 1–24), followed by the 3 editorial Sanskrit praśasti verses.

SA_MB_agamakalpalataHK.title: Āgamakalpalatā
SA_MB_agamakalpalataHK.author: Yadunātha Cakravartin
SA_MB_agamakalpalataHK.summary: The Āgamakalpalatā is an extensive ritual compendium (nibandha) attributed to Yadunātha Cakravartin. Structured into sections designated as pallavas, it covers various ritual matters including mantras and pūjā for deities such as Viṣṇu, Śiva, and forms of the Devī (such as Chinnamastā and Jvālāmukhī), citing texts such as the Rudrayāmala and Phetkāriṇītantra.
SA_MB_agamakalpalataHK.attribution: The Muktabodha metadata records the alternate name yadunāthacakravartti, and the final colophon names the author as Yadunātha Cakravartin (iti śrīyadunāthacakravartti viracitā yām āgamakalpalatāyāṃ...).
SA_MB_agamakalpalataHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) reel no. A 145/3, copied in Saṃvat 1955.
SA_MB_agamakalpalataHK.coverage: complete — Work ending with chapter 21 (labeled corruptly as ṣṭaviṃśaḥ pallavaḥ, verse 21-202) on folio 356, concluding with the scribal date Saṃvat 1955.

SA_MB_kriyasaraHK.title: Kriyāsāra (upadeśas 1–4)
SA_MB_kriyasaraHK.author: Nīlakaṇṭha
SA_MB_kriyasaraHK.summary: The Kriyāsāra (also titled Nigamāgamasārasaṅgraha) by Nīlakaṇṭha is a theological and philosophical work synthesizing Śaiva traditions with Vedānta. This portion covers up through Upadeśa 4, engaging extensively with Brahmasūtra commentary, Śaiva doctrines, and Viśiṣṭādvaita philosophy.
SA_MB_kriyasaraHK.attribution: Attributed to Nīlakaṇṭha (styled Nīlakaṇṭha Śivācārya). The colophon describes the author as śrīmadviśiṣṭādvaitasiddhāntarahasyaikottaraśatasthalābhijña.
SA_MB_kriyasaraHK.edition: Kriyāsāra, Volume 1, edited by N. S. Veṅkaṭanāthācārya, Sanskrit Series volume 95 of Oriental Research Institute Publications, Mysore: Oriental Research Institute, 1954.
SA_MB_kriyasaraHK.coverage: partial — Contains Upadeśas concluding with the fourth upadeśa (caturthopadeśaḥ), corresponding to Volume 1 of the Mysore edition.

SA_MB_saktisamgama_tantra_tarakhandaHK.title: Śaktisaṅgamatantra (Tārākhaṇḍa, chapters 1–47)
SA_MB_saktisamgama_tantra_tarakhandaHK.summary: The Tārākhaṇḍa ('Book of Tārā') forms the second section (dvitīyakhaṇḍa) of the Śaktisaṅgamamahātantrarāja. Framed as a revelatory dialogue between Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā, it delineates mantras, yantras, nyāsas, initiation rituals, and esoteric practices associated with the worship of Tārā and allied Śākta deities. This digital file is an incomplete transcription covering chapters 1–47 (concluding at page 182 of Benoytosh Bhattacharyya's 1941 Baroda edition).
SA_MB_saktisamgama_tantra_tarakhandaHK.attribution: Scriptural Śākta tantra cast as a revelation between Śiva (Akṣobhya) and the Goddess (Mahogratārā).
SA_MB_saktisamgama_tantra_tarakhandaHK.edition: Śaktisaṃgamatantra, Vol. II: Tārākhaṇḍa, critically edited by Benoytosh Bhattacharyya, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1941.
SA_MB_saktisamgama_tantra_tarakhandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters (paṭalas) 1–47, ending at verse 47.79 on p. 182.

SA_MB_sarvollaasatantraHK.title: Sarvollāsatantra
SA_MB_sarvollaasatantraHK.author: Sarvānandanātha
SA_MB_sarvollaasatantraHK.summary: The Sarvollāsatantra is a Tantric work attributed to Sarvānandanātha. In 63 chapters (ullāsas), it compiles extensive citations from older tantras and āgamas on essential Kaula practices, including initiation (dīkṣā), guru veneration, the pañcatattvas, cakra-pūjā, and internal Kuṇḍalinī yoga.
SA_MB_sarvollaasatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 63 chapters (ullāsas), concluding with 'iti śrīsarvānandanātha viracite sarvollāse triṣaṣṭyullāsaḥ'.

SA_MB_yogavishayaHK.title: Yogaviṣaya
SA_MB_yogavishayaHK.author: Matsyendranātha
SA_MB_yogavishayaHK.summary: The Yogaviṣaya is a short yoga text of 33 verses ascribed to Matsyendranātha (Mīnanātha). It treats the guru lineage, the qualified disciple, the cakras, the nāḍīs iḍā, piṅgalā, and suṣumnā, the repetition of the haṃsa mantra, and inner anatomy/vital points.
SA_MB_yogavishayaHK.attribution: Ascribed to Matsyendranātha (Mīnanātha): the speaker introduces himself as 'umāṣaṅkaraputro 'haṃ mīnanātho munīśvaraḥ' (v. 7) and the colophon reads 'iti matsyendranāthaviracitaṃ bhaktisaṃ sampūrṇam'.
SA_MB_yogavishayaHK.coverage: complete — Complete short text of 33 verses, concluding with the colophon 'iti matsyendranāthaviracitaṃ bhaktisaṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_MB_tantrarajatantraHK.title: Tantrarājatantra with Manoramā
SA_MB_tantrarajatantraHK.author: Subhagānandanātha, Prakāśānandanātha
SA_MB_tantrarajatantraHK.summary: The Tantrarājatantra is one of the primary canonical scriptures of the Kādimata lineage within the Śākta Śrīvidyā tradition, structured in 36 chapters as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva and the Devī. It presents comprehensive instruction on the worship of Lalitā Mahā-Tripurasundarī and the fifteen Nityā goddesses, detailing mantra formulas, yantra geometry, the nyāsa rites of the Śrīcakra, and non-dual Śākta metaphysics. In this edition, the scripture is accompanied by the running Manoramā commentary, written up through chapter 22 by Subhagānandanātha and finished for chapters 23–36 by his disciple Prakāśānandanātha.
SA_MB_tantrarajatantraHK.attribution: The root Tantrarājatantra is an anonymous scriptural revelation of the Kādimata division of Śrīvidyā Śāktism, framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Devī. The running commentary Manoramā was composed through paṭala 22 by Subhagānandanātha and completed for the remaining fourteen chapters (paṭalas 23–36) by his disciple Prakāśānandanātha (Prakāśānandadeśika), as explicitly recorded in the closing verses of paṭala 36.
SA_MB_tantrarajatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 36 paṭalas, containing both the root kārikā verses and the running Manoramā commentary up to the closing praśasti and final colophon.

SA_MB_jayakhyasamhitaHK.title: Jayākhyasaṃhitā
SA_MB_jayakhyasamhitaHK.summary: The Jayākhyasaṃhitā is an authoritative canonical scripture of the Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra tradition. Spanning 33 paṭalas, it expounds Vaiṣṇava theology, cosmology, mantra systems, initiation (dīkṣā), daily and temple rituals, and yoga.
SA_MB_jayakhyasamhitaHK.attribution: A revealed Vaiṣṇava scripture of the Pāñcarātra tradition.
SA_MB_jayakhyasamhitaHK.edition: Embar Krishnamacharya (ed.), Jayākhyasaṃhitā of Pāñcarātra Āgama, critically edited with an Introduction in Sanskrit, Indices etc., Gaekwad's Oriental Series, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1931 / 1967 (Muktabodha record gives 1957).
SA_MB_jayakhyasamhitaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 33 paṭalas (chapters 1–33), concluding at 33.87 with the colophon 'iti śrīpāñcarātre jayākhyasaṃhitāyāṃ yogākhyānaṃ nāma trayastriṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ || 33 || samāpteyaṃ jayākhyasaṃhitā |'.
translations: Marion Rastelli, Philosophisch-theologische Grundanschauungen der Jayākhyasaṃhitā: Mit einer Darstellung des täglichen Rituals, Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften, philosophisch-historische Klasse, Sitzungsberichte 668 = Beiträge zur Kultur- und Geistesgeschichte Asiens 33, Wien: Verlag der Österreichischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, 1999. (German)

SA_MB_kamikapurvabhagaHK.title: Kāmikāgama (Pūrvabhāga)
SA_MB_kamikapurvabhagaHK.summary: The Kāmikāgama is a canonical scripture of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition. Its Pūrvabhāga comprises seventy-five chapters (paṭalas) dealing comprehensively with rituals, architecture, iconometry, and installation rites, concluding with the gopurasthāpanavidhi.
SA_MB_kamikapurvabhagaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Pūrvabhāga in 75 paṭalas (ending with gopurasthāpanavidhiḥ pañcasaptatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ, v. 77/97).

SA_MB_kaamikaagamauttarabhaagaHK.title: Kāmikāgama (Uttarabhāga)
SA_MB_kaamikaagamauttarabhaagaHK.summary: The Kāmikāgama is a canonical scripture of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition. Its Uttarabhāga concludes with chapter 98 (vidhiraṣṭanavatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ) and opens with paścimadvārārcanavidhiḥ, containing ritual injunctions for worship, installation, festivals, and related rites.
SA_MB_kaamikaagamauttarabhaagaHK.attribution: Canonical scripture of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition.
SA_MB_kaamikaagamauttarabhaagaHK.coverage: complete — Uttarabhāga ending with vidhiraṣṭanavatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ (chapter 98), opening with paścimadvārārcanavidhiḥ.

SA_MB_kriyaakramadyotikaaHK.title: Kriyākramadyotikā with Prabhā (up to Damanavidhi)
SA_MB_kriyaakramadyotikaaHK.author: Aghoraśiva, Nirmalamaṇi
SA_MB_kriyaakramadyotikaaHK.summary: The Kriyākramadyotikā is a ritual handbook of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition by Aghoraśiva. This e-text transmits the paddhati alongside Nirmalamaṇi's commentary Prabhā (Asphuṭārthaprakāśikā) up through the Damanavidhi section.
SA_MB_kriyaakramadyotikaaHK.attribution: The root paddhati was composed by Aghoraśiva. The commentary Prabhā (formally titled Asphuṭārthaprakāśikā) was composed by Nirmalamaṇi, son of Tyāgarājācārya, resident in Kamalālaya.
SA_MB_kriyaakramadyotikaaHK.edition: Kriyākramadyotikā of Aghoraśiva with the Commentary of Nirmalamaṇi. Cidambaram: Jñānasambandham Press, 1927 (Grantha script, 523 pp.).
SA_MB_kriyaakramadyotikaaHK.coverage: partial — Corresponds to pages 1–523 of the 1927 Chidambaram edition, breaking off at the end of the Damanavidhi. It contains daily worship (nityakarma/śivapūjā), initiations (dīkṣā), and seasonal renewal rites (pavitrāropaṇa, damanāropaṇa), but lacks later sections such as funerary and post-mortuary rites (antyeṣṭi, śrāddha), temple installation (pratiṣṭhā), the festival manual (mahotsava), and expiations (prāyaścitta).
translations: Davis, Richard H. Ritual in an Oscillating Universe: Worshipping Śiva in Medieval India. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1991. (English)
Davis, Richard H. A translation and study of the Mahotsavavidhi attributed to Aghoraśiva (2010). (English)

SA_MB_nirvanatantraHK.title: Nirvāṇatantra
SA_MB_nirvanatantraHK.summary: The Nirvāṇatantra is a Śākta scripture framed as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva and Caṇḍikā. In this 14-chapter recension, the text expounds cosmogony, identifying Kālī with supreme Brahman and prime source of the universe, along with the significance of the Gāyatrī mantra, spiritual lineage and devotion to the guru, and rituals of the five makāras. The concluding paṭalas delineate the duties of the four varṇas and āśramas, culminating in an exposition of the avadhūta ascetic path.
SA_MB_nirvanatantraHK.attribution: Revealed Śākta tantric scripture framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Caṇḍikā (iti śrīnirvāṇataṃtre caṃḍikāśaṃkarasaṃvāde). Traditional scriptural work with no historical author.
SA_MB_nirvanatantraHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from NGMCP reel C 24/2 manuscript 217b.
SA_MB_nirvanatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 14 paṭalas, concluding at verse 14.29 with the final colophon: iti śrīnirvāṇataṃtre caṃḍikāśaṃkarasaṃvāde avadhūtāśramavivaraṇaṃ nāma caturdaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || 14 || samāptaḥ.

SA_MB_saktisa.mgamatantra_kalikhandaHK.title: Śaktisaṅgamatantra (Kālīkhaṇḍa only)
SA_MB_saktisa.mgamatantra_kalikhandaHK.summary: The Śaktisaṅgamatantra is a voluminous compendium divided into four books on Kālī, Tārā, Sundarī, and Chinnamastā. This first section, the Kālīkhaṇḍa (comprising 21 paṭalas), expounds the theology, mantras, yantras, nyāsas, and ritual worship of Kālī.
SA_MB_saktisa.mgamatantra_kalikhandaHK.attribution: Anonymous Śākta Kaula scripture, framed traditionally as a divine dialogue between Śiva and the Devī (and in subsequent chapters between Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā).
SA_MB_saktisa.mgamatantra_kalikhandaHK.edition: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (ed.), Śaktisaṅgamatantram, Vol. I: Kālīkhaṇḍa, Gaekwad's Oriental Series, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1932.
SA_MB_saktisa.mgamatantra_kalikhandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains the complete Kālīkhaṇḍa (paṭalas 1–21), the first of the four major khaṇḍas of the Śaktisaṅgamatantra (the remaining three being Tārākhaṇḍa, Sundarīkhaṇḍa, and Chinnamastākhaṇḍa).

SA_MB_saktisamgama_sundarikhandaHK.title: Śaktisaṅgamatantra (Sundarīkhaṇḍa)
SA_MB_saktisamgama_sundarikhandaHK.summary: The Sundarīkhaṇḍa is the third section of the extensive Śākta compendium Śaktisaṅgamatantra, framed as a dialogue between Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā. In 21 chapters (paṭalas), it expounds rituals, mantras, and esoteric doctrines centering on the goddess Tripurasundarī (Lalitā) and the Śrīvidyā tradition, detailing initiation (dīkṣā), nyāsas, Śrīcakra worship, and related Mahāvidyās such as Dhūmāvatī. The section is also well known in South Asian historiography for its seventh paṭala (the Deśavyavasthāniyama / Ṣaṭpañcāśaddeśavibhāga), which provides a valuable late-medieval geographical gazetteer dividing the subcontinent into fifty-six regions.
SA_MB_saktisamgama_sundarikhandaHK.attribution: A Śākta tantric scripture framed as a dialogue between Akṣobhya and Mahogratārā.
SA_MB_saktisamgama_sundarikhandaHK.edition: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (ed.), Śaktisaṅgamatantram, Vol. III: Sundarīkhaṇḍa, Gaekwad's Oriental Series, 1947.
SA_MB_saktisamgama_sundarikhandaHK.coverage: partial — Contains the complete Sundarīkhaṇḍa (the third of four khaṇḍas comprising the Śaktisaṅgamatantra), consisting of 21 paṭalas.

SA_MB_bhutasuddhitantra-HK.title: Bhūtaśuddhitantra
SA_MB_bhutasuddhitantra-HK.summary: An anonymous Śākta tantra in 17 paṭalas, a dialogue between Śrīdevī and Īśvara. It treats the preliminaries of Tantric worship as a 'triad' (tattvatraya) of bhūtaśuddhi, nyāsa and prāṇāyāma, together with inner bathing and inner sandhyā, ajapā recitation, kuṇḍalinī and the six cakras, the dissolution of the 24 tattvas and inner worship. It ends with a praise of the book itself and a short prose summary of the bhūtaśuddhi procedure.
SA_MB_bhutasuddhitantra-HK.attribution: Scriptural Tantra framed as a dialogue between Śrīdevī and Śiva/Īśvara.
SA_MB_bhutasuddhitantra-HK.coverage: complete — Text in 17 paṭalas followed by a short closing prose passage describing the bhūtaśuddhi procedure, ending at 'iti śrībhūtaśuddhitantraṃ samāptam'.

SA_MB_mahotsavavidhikramaHK.title: Mahotsavavidhi
SA_MB_mahotsavavidhikramaHK.author: Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_mahotsavavidhikramaHK.summary: A section of Aghoraśiva's Kriyākramadyotikā on festival rites (mahotsava), including yāgaśālā, balidāna, ratha procession, and ending with vārotsava and the colophon brahmattālādiṛkṣotsavāntavidhiḥ samāptaḥ.
SA_MB_mahotsavavidhikramaHK.attribution: The colophon ascribes the text to Aghoraśiva's Kriyākramadyotikā: 'iti parameśvara nāmadheya śrīmadaghoraśivācāryaviracitāyāṃ kriyākramadyotikāyāṃ brahmattālādiṛkṣotsavāntavidhiḥ (k: bṛhattā- -vidhis) samāptaḥ'.
SA_MB_mahotsavavidhikramaHK.coverage: complete — The text ends with the colophon 'iti parameśvara nāmadheya śrīmadaghoraśivācāryaviracitāyāṃ kriyākramadyotikāyāṃ brahmattālādiṛkṣotsavāntavidhiḥ (k: bṛhattā- -vidhis) samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_kaamaakhyaatantraHK.title: Kāmākhyātantra
SA_MB_kaamaakhyaatantraHK.summary: The Kāmākhyātantra is a Śākta-Kaula tantric text in nine chapters (paṭalas) structured as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva and Devī. Centered on the goddess Kāmākhyā of Kāmarūpa (Assam) venerated as the cosmic Yoni and supreme Shakti, the work outlines mantra extraction, nyāsa, pañcatattva worship, yoni-pūjā, guru-śiṣya qualifications, pūrṇābhiṣeka, and rituals geared towards both siddhi and liberation.
SA_MB_kaamaakhyaatantraHK.attribution: Scriptural text presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Devī (Pārvatī).
SA_MB_kaamaakhyaatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 9 paṭalas, concluding at verse 9.28 with 'iti śrīkāmākhyātantre pārvatīśvarasaṃvāde navamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ' and 'samāptaścāyaṃ granthaḥ'.

SA_MB_kaamadhenutantraHK.title: Kāmadhenutantra
SA_MB_kaamadhenutantraHK.summary: The Kāmadhenutantra is a Śākta Tantra in twenty-four paṭalas structured as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī. It focuses primarily on phonematic mysticism (mātṛkā- and varṇa-vidyā), treating the fifty letters of the Sanskrit alphabet as vibrational sound-manifestations of Kālī and Vāc/Sarasvatī. The work details the esoteric values, bodily correlation (nyāsa), cakra centers, and meditative visualisations (dhyāna) for individual letters and key bījamantras.
SA_MB_kaamadhenutantraHK.attribution: Anonymous Śākta Tantra framed as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva (Mahādeva) and the Goddess (Pārvatī/Devī).
SA_MB_kaamadhenutantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 24 paṭalas, concluding at verse 23/12 followed by the 24th paṭala colophon ('iti śrīkāmadhenutantre devīśvarasaṃvāde caturviṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ') and final completion formula 'samāptamidaṃ kāmadhenutantram'.

SA_MB_saaktaanandataramginiiHK.title: Śāktānandataraṅgiṇī
SA_MB_saaktaanandataramginiiHK.author: Brahmānandagiri
SA_MB_saaktaanandataramginiiHK.summary: The Śāktānandataraṅgiṇī ('River of the Bliss of Śakti') is a Śākta tantric nibandha attributed to Brahmānandagiri in eighteen chapters (ullāsas). Topics include initiation (dīkṣā), guru-śiṣya relations, subtle anatomy (brahmanāḍī, ṣaṭcakra, suṣumnā), ratnamaṇḍapa meditation, japa and rosaries, pūjā injunctions and prohibitions, prāyaścitta for accidental faults, and homa rites.
SA_MB_saaktaanandataramginiiHK.attribution: Attributed to Brahmānandagiri (also referred to as Śrī Parivrājakācārya Paramahaṃsa Tīrthāvadhūta Śrīmad Brahmānandagiri in colophons).
SA_MB_saaktaanandataramginiiHK.edition: Paramahaṃsa-Parivrājaka Śrīmad-Brahmānandagiri-Saṅkalitā Śāktānanda-Taraṅginī, edited by Pañcānana Śāstrī, Tantra-Prakāśa Granthamālā, vol. 1, N.p.: Āgamānusandhāna Samiti, 1942/43 (noted also as 'Publisher: unknown-pree 1900 Bengali Script').
SA_MB_saaktaanandataramginiiHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 18 chapters (ullāsas), concluding with the 18th chapter colophon (iti śrīparivrācakācārya paramahaṃsatīrthāvadhūtaśrīmadbrahmānandagirikṛtāyāṃ śāktānandataraṅgiṇyāṃ homādinirṇayo nāmāṣṭādaśollāsaḥ samāptaḥ || 18 || samāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ).

SA_MB_sattrimsattattvasamdohaHK.title: Ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasaṃdoha with the Vivaraṇa of Rājānaka Ānanda
SA_MB_sattrimsattattvasamdohaHK.author: Amṛtānanda, Rājānaka Ānanda
SA_MB_sattrimsattattvasamdohaHK.summary: The Ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasaṃdoha consists of 21 āryā verses that outline the ontology of Kashmir Shaivism. It describes the gradual unfoldment (sṛṣṭi) of the thirty-six tattvas from ultimate consciousness to gross earth. The work is accompanied by the commentary (Vivaraṇa) composed by Rājānaka Ānanda.
SA_MB_sattrimsattattvasamdohaHK.attribution: The root text contains 21 āryā verses summarizing the 36 principles. The commentator Rājānaka Ānanda introduces its author anonymously as 'kaścin mahāmāheśvaraḥ'.
SA_MB_sattrimsattattvasamdohaHK.edition: Ṣaṭtriṃśāttattvasandoha with commentary by Rājānakānanda, edited by M. R. Śāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies. Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918.
SA_MB_sattrimsattattvasamdohaHK.coverage: complete — Complete e-text containing all 21 āryā stanzas of the root text and the full Vivaraṇa commentary by Rājānaka Ānanda, followed by the editorial concluding stanzas of the KSTS edition.

SA_MB_tantrasaaraHK.title: Tantrasāra
SA_MB_tantrasaaraHK.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_tantrasaaraHK.summary: The Tantrasāra ('Essence of Tantra') is an influential prose compendium composed by the Kashmiri polymath Abhinavagupta as an accessible digest of his monumental encyclopedic treatise, the Tantrāloka. Arranged into 22 āhnikas ('daily lessons'), the work systematically expounds the metaphysics, ritual, yoga, and soteriology of the non-dual Trika and Pratyabhijñā traditions. It is centrally structured around the hierarchy of means to spiritual liberation—anupāya, śāmbhavopāya, śāktopāya, and āṇavopāya—alongside an extensive treatment of the descent of divine grace (śaktipāta) and initiation rituals (dīkṣā).
SA_MB_tantrasaaraHK.edition: Tantrasāra of Abhinavagupta, edited by Mukunda Rāma, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies, no. 17, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918.
SA_MB_tantrasaaraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text concluding with 'samāptaṃ cedaṃ tantrasārākhyaṃ śāstram'.
translations: Raniero Gnoli (trans.), Essenza dei Tantra, Turin: Boringhieri, 1960. (Italian)

SA_MB_paratrimsikavivaranaHK.title: Parātrīśikā with Parātrīśikāvivaraṇa
SA_MB_paratrimsikavivaranaHK.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_paratrimsikavivaranaHK.summary: The Parātrīśikāvivaraṇa is Abhinavagupta's commentary on the Parātrīśikā, a foundational Trika scripture. The work develops an exposition of non-dual Śaivism, phonematic emanation, and mantra. This edition (KSTS 18) presents the root verses with Abhinavagupta's text accompanied by explanatory editorial glosses by Mukunda Rāma Śāstrī.
SA_MB_paratrimsikavivaranaHK.attribution: The root verses belong to Trika Śaivism. Abhinavagupta's commentary is designated in the colophon as Parātriṃśikātattvavivaraṇa. The Sanskrit glosses were supplied by Mukunda Rāma Śāstrī.
SA_MB_paratrimsikavivaranaHK.edition: The Parā-Trimshikā with Commentary, the Latter by Abhinava Gupta, edited by Mukunda Rāma Shāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies. Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918.
SA_MB_paratrimsikavivaranaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Parātrīśikā root verses and Abhinavagupta's full Vivaraṇa, ending with the concluding verses and the editor's colophon (tilakam).

SA_MB_janmamaranavicaaraHK.title: Janmamaraṇavicāra
SA_MB_janmamaranavicaaraHK.author: Vāmadeva
SA_MB_janmamaranavicaaraHK.summary: The Janmamaraṇavicāra ('Investigation into Birth and Death') is a Kashmiri Śaiva treatise composed by Bhaṭṭa Vāmadeva. Integrating non-dual Śaiva metaphysics with embryology and physiology, the text explains embodiment, gestation, birth, and death.
SA_MB_janmamaranavicaaraHK.edition: Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918, edited by Śāstrī M. R.
SA_MB_janmamaranavicaaraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Janmamaraṇavicāra (ending with 'samāpto 'yaṃ janmamaraṇavicārākhyo granthaḥ'), preceded by Mukund Rām Shāstrī's Sanskrit introduction (bhūmikā) and followed by his concluding verses.

SA_MB_maliniijayavartikaHK.title: Mālinīvijayavārttika
SA_MB_maliniijayavartikaHK.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_maliniijayavartikaHK.summary: The Mālinīvijayavārttika (also known as the Mālinīślokavārttika) is a major verse commentary composed by Abhinavagupta interpreting the opening sentence of the Mālinīvijayottaratantra, the foundational scriptural authority of the Trika Śaiva lineage. Arranged in two books (kāṇḍas), the text formulates a comprehensive theology of revelation (āgama), hermeneutics, and nondual metaphysics while mounting extensive polemics against Buddhist epistemologists, Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika, and Mīmāṃsā.
SA_MB_maliniijayavartikaHK.attribution: Firmly attributed to Abhinavagupta in the opening verses and the colophons of both kāṇḍas.
SA_MB_maliniijayavartikaHK.edition: Madhusūdan Kaul Śāstrī (ed.), The Mālinīvijaya Vārttikam of Śrīmad Abhinavagupta, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS) [recte 32], Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1921.
SA_MB_maliniijayavartikaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in two books (kāṇḍas): Kāṇḍa 1 contains 1,079 verses and Kāṇḍa 2 contains 335 verses. Although the treatise itself expounds only the opening verse/portion (ādimavākya) of the Mālinīvijayottaratantra, both surviving kāṇḍas that comprise the full work are present.
translations: Jürgen Hanneder, Abhinavagupta's Philosophy of Revelation: An Edition and Annotated Translation of Mālinīślokavārttika I, 1–399, Groningen Oriental Studies 14, Groningen: Egbert Forsten, 1998. (English)

SA_MB_maliniivijayottaraHK.title: Mālinīvijayottaratantra
SA_MB_maliniivijayottaraHK.summary: The Mālinīvijayottaratantra is an important Śaiva tantra. It expounds mantra phonology, ritual worship, and initiation (dīkṣā), and is particularly renowned for its systematic presentation of yoga and stages of spiritual mastery.
SA_MB_maliniivijayottaraHK.attribution: A revealed scripture (āgama). Spoken through Kārttikeya to the ṛṣis.
SA_MB_maliniivijayottaraHK.edition: Madhusūdana Kaula Śāstrī (ed.), Mālinīvijayottaratantram, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS) 37, Srinagar / Bombay: Research Department Jammu and Kashmir State, 1922.
SA_MB_maliniivijayottaraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 23 adhikāras (chapters), concluding at 23.43 and the final colophon.

SA_MB_spandanirnayaHK.title: Spandakārikā with Spandanirṇaya
SA_MB_spandanirnayaHK.author: Vasugupta, Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_spandanirnayaHK.summary: The Spandanirṇaya is Kṣemarāja's commentary on the Spandakārikā. The work establishes that reality and all experiential states are grounded in the dynamic pulsation (spanda) of supreme consciousness (parasaṃvit).
SA_MB_spandanirnayaHK.attribution: The Spandakārikā root stanzas are traditionally attributed either to Vasugupta or to his disciple Bhaṭṭa Kallaṭa. The commentary Spandanirṇaya is by Kṣemarāja, pupil of Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_spandanirnayaHK.edition: The Spandakārikās of Vasugupta with the Nirṇaya by Kṣemarāja, edited by Madhusūdan Kaul Shāstrī, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS) No. 42, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1925.
SA_MB_spandanirnayaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the kārikās along with Kṣemarāja's Spandanirṇaya prose commentary and closing verses.

SA_MB_devinamalavilasaHK.title: Devīnāmavilāsa
SA_MB_devinamalavilasaHK.author: Sāhib Kaul
SA_MB_devinamalavilasaHK.summary: The Devīnāmavilāsa is an ambitious devotional mahākāvya composed by the Kashmiri author Sāhib Kaul. Divided into cantos styled as bhaktis, it provides an ornate poetic and philosophical exegesis of the names of the Goddess (incorporating the Bhavānīsahasranāmastotra). The work synthesizes Śākta devotionalism with non-dual metaphysics in classical Sanskrit metre.
SA_MB_devinamalavilasaHK.attribution: The work is attributed to Sāhib Kaul, who appears as mahāmāheśvarācāryavaryasāhibakaulānandanātha and sāhibakaulapāda in the opening and colophons.
SA_MB_devinamalavilasaHK.edition: Devīnāmavilāsa by Sāhib Kaul, edited by Madhusūdan Kaul Shāstrī. Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS). Lahore: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1942.
SA_MB_devinamalavilasaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text matching up to page 324 of the editio princeps, concluding with the daṇḍaka hymn and full colophon (iti śrīnāmavilāsaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ).

SA_MB_bhagavadgiitaa_ramakanthaHK.title: Bhagavadgītā with Sarvatobhadra (chapters 1–14)
SA_MB_bhagavadgiitaa_ramakanthaHK.author: Rāmakaṇṭha
SA_MB_bhagavadgiitaa_ramakanthaHK.summary: The Sarvatobhadra (also called Bhagavadgītāvivaraṇa) is a commentary on the Bhagavadgītā by Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha. This digital text contains the root text and commentary for chapters 1 through 14.
SA_MB_bhagavadgiitaa_ramakanthaHK.attribution: The commentary Sarvatobhadra is authored by Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha.
SA_MB_bhagavadgiitaa_ramakanthaHK.edition: Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), edited by Śāstrī Kṛṣṇa, Publisher: Research Department Jammu and Kashmir State, Publication city: Bombay, 1943.
SA_MB_bhagavadgiitaa_ramakanthaHK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters 1–14 only, terminating at page 317 with the colophon: 'iti śrīmadrājānakarāmakaṇṭhaviracite vākyārthānvayamātre sarvatobhadranāmni bhagavadgītāvivaraṇe caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ || 14 ||'.

SA_MB_uddamaresvaratantramHK.title: Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra
SA_MB_uddamaresvaratantramHK.summary: The Uḍḍāmareśvaratantra (also styled Uḍḍāmareśvaramahātantra) is a 15-chapter applied Tantric manual dedicated primarily to pragmatic magic and ritual pharmacology (ṣaṭkarman rites such as vaśīkaraṇa, uccāṭana, stambhana, and māraṇa). It details incantations, herbal and mineral recipes (auṣadhi), and counter-sorcery remedies for curing fevers, expelling demonic and planetary possession (bhūtas, grahas, brahmarākṣasas), counteracting poisons, and evoking yakṣiṇīs and related semi-divine entities for material acquisition. The work is structured as an instruction delivered by Śiva to Gaurī and belongs to the wider milieu of practical medieval grimoire literature closely allied with the Uḍḍīśa/Uḍḍāmara traditions.
SA_MB_uddamaresvaratantramHK.attribution: Anonymous Śaiva-Śākta tantra cast as a dialogue between Gaurī and Śiva. The colophons at the conclusion of each chapter describe the work as an extraction from the Vīrabhadreśvaratantra (iti śrīśivaprokte vīrabhadreśvaratantroddhṛte uḍḍāmareśvaramahātantre).
SA_MB_uddamaresvaratantramHK.edition: Jagaddhar Zadoo (ed.), The Uddamareshvara Tantram, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research Department of Jammu and Kashmir State, 1947.
SA_MB_uddamaresvaratantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all 15 paṭalas (chapters), preceded by the introductory table of contents (viṣayānukramaṇī) and followed by the editor's comparative index/glossary of 140 botanical and mineral preparations with Hindi names and Latin binomial identifications.

SA_MB_bodhapancadasikaaHK.title: Bodhapañcadaśikā with Vivaraṇa
SA_MB_bodhapancadasikaaHK.author: Abhinavagupta, Harabhaṭṭaśāstrin
SA_MB_bodhapancadasikaaHK.summary: The Bodhapañcadaśikā is a philosophical work composed by Abhinavagupta. This e-text also provides the Sanskrit commentary (Vivaraṇa) composed by Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.
SA_MB_bodhapancadasikaaHK.attribution: The root work is composed by Abhinavagupta. The accompanying Vivaraṇa commentary was authored by Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī on the 11th tithi of the dark half of Phālguna in Laukika year 4990, as recorded in his concluding chronogram verse (bhūnandanandavedābde).
SA_MB_bodhapancadasikaaHK.edition: Bodhapañcadaśikā and Paramārthacarcā of Mahāmāheśvarācārya Śrīmad Abhinavagupta with the Vivaraṇa by Pt. Hara Bhatta Shastri, edited with notes by Jagaddhara Zadoo Shastri, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1947.
SA_MB_bodhapancadasikaaHK.coverage: complete — Text of Bodhapañcadaśikā with the Vivaraṇa commentary by Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.

SA_MB_saivakaalavivekaHK.title: Śaivakālaviveka with the commentary of Gaṇapatibhaṭṭa
SA_MB_saivakaalavivekaHK.author: Nigamajñānamuni, Gaṇapatibhaṭṭa
SA_MB_saivakaalavivekaHK.summary: The Śaivakālaviveka is a Śaivasiddhānta manual attributed to Nigamajñāna Śivācārya. It details the astrological considerations required for temple and ritual performance, from ground preparation (karṣaṇa) to deity installation (pratiṣṭhā). The text is accompanied by Gaṇapatibhaṭṭa's commentary (vyākhyā), citing canonical tantras and Siddhāntāgamas.
SA_MB_saivakaalavivekaHK.attribution: The root verses are ascribed to Nigamajñāna Śivācārya. The commentary is by Gaṇapatibhaṭṭa (Śrīvatsakulatilaka Gaṇapatibhaṭṭa).
SA_MB_saivakaalavivekaHK.coverage: complete — Contains root verses and Gaṇapatibhaṭṭa's commentary (vyākhyā), concluding with 'iti deśakālādhikāraḥ'.

SA_MB_phetkaariniitantramHK.title: Phetkāriṇītantra
SA_MB_phetkaariniitantramHK.summary: The Phetkāriṇītantra is a tantric scripture framed as a dialogue between Īśvara and the Devī, emphasizing mantra practice, yantras, and rituals such as kṛtyā-sādhana, māraṇa, and ceṭikā-sādhana, including descriptions of fierce goddesses.
SA_MB_phetkaariniitantramHK.attribution: Scripture presented as a dialogue between the Devī and Īśvara (devīśvarasaṃvāda).
SA_MB_phetkaariniitantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 21 paṭalas (concluding at verse 21.58 with the colophon: 'iti śrīphetkāriṇītantre devīśvarasaṃvāde ceṭikāsādhanaṃ nāma ekaviṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ').

SA_MB_jnaanasankaliniitantramHK.title: Jñānasaṅkalinītantra
SA_MB_jnaanasankaliniitantramHK.summary: The Jñānasaṅkalinītantra ('Tantra of the Collection of Gnosis') is a concise Śākta-Śaiva tantric treatise framed as a dialogue on Mount Kailāsa between Śiva and the Devī. It subordinates external ritualism, caste prescriptions, and scholastic learning to internal non-dual knowledge (brahmajñāna) and subtle yogic contemplation. The text expounds the esoteric anatomy of the body (piṇḍa) as identical to the cosmos (brahmāṇḍa), identifying the internal channels iḍā, piṅgalā, and suṣumnā with sacred rivers (Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī), and explains the symbolic significance of the Praṇava (Oṃ) alongside inner mudrās such as khecarī and śāmbhavī.
SA_MB_jnaanasankaliniitantramHK.attribution: Scriptural tantric revelation cast as a dialogue between the Goddess (Śakti/Umā) and Śiva (Maheśvara/Īśvara); no human author is attributed.
SA_MB_jnaanasankaliniitantramHK.edition: Jñānasaṅkalinītantram, edited by Rasika Mohana Caṭṭopādhyāya, Calcutta, late 19th century (in Bengali script).
SA_MB_jnaanasankaliniitantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete text concluding with 'iti jñānasaṅkalinītantraṃ samāptam'.

SA_MB_kaalaanalatantraHK.title: Kālānalatantra (incomplete)
SA_MB_kaalaanalatantraHK.summary: The Kālānalatantra (also referred to as the Nailalohitīya Kālānalatantra) is an unpublished Śākta-Śaiva tantric scripture preserved in Nepalese manuscripts, presented as a teaching delivered by Nīlalohita (Śiva) to Nārada. It focuses on esoteric goddess mantravidyās, protective formulas, and ritual diagrams, centering on Siddhilakṣmī, Caṇḍakāpālinī, and Pratyaṅgirā, and culminates in chapter 22 with the Ayutākṣarā (ten-thousand-syllable) formula of Siddhilakṣmī.
SA_MB_kaalaanalatantraHK.attribution: Scriptural tantric revelation structured as a dialogue between Nīlalohita (Śiva) and Brahmaputra (Nārada).
SA_MB_kaalaanalatantraHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives, Kathmandu / NGMPP Reel B 157/27, MS (Śaivatantra), 50 leaves (leaves 1–4 missing). Unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_kaalaanalatantraHK.coverage: partial — Manuscript transcription covering folios 5a–50b (folios 1–4 missing at the beginning), ending with chapter 22 (iti nailalohitīye śrīkālānalataṃtre siddhilakṣmyayutākṣarākathanannāmadvāviṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ).

SA_MB_svacchandapaddhatiHK.title: Svacchandapaddhati
SA_MB_svacchandapaddhatiHK.author: Cidānandanātha
SA_MB_svacchandapaddhatiHK.summary: The Svacchandapaddhati by Cidānandanātha is a ritual manual organized in nine chapters (spandas) dedicated to the worship of Goddess Mahātripurasundarī, treating topics such as mantrayoga, nyāsa, and pūjā.
SA_MB_svacchandapaddhatiHK.attribution: The colophon attributes the work to Cidānandanātha.
SA_MB_svacchandapaddhatiHK.edition: Svacchandapaddhati of Cidānandanātha, edited by Prof. Sītalāprasad Ūpādhyāya from manuscripts (khistejī se - ka; saṃ. vi. 88137 - kha; saṃ vi. - ga).
SA_MB_svacchandapaddhatiHK.coverage: complete — Ends with the colophon 'iti śrīmaccidānandanāthaviracitāyāṃ svacchandapaddhatyāṃ navamaspandaḥ || oṃ oṃ śubhaṃ bhavatu svacchandapaddhatīḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_merutantraHK.title: Merutantra with Ṭippanī
SA_MB_merutantraHK.summary: The Merutantra is an encyclopedic Śaiva-Śākta tantric manual comprising 35 chapters (prakāśas), framed as a revelation given by Sadāśiva on Mount Meru to the gods after their distress under the demon Jalandhara. Functioning much like a nibandha (digest) of mantra-śāstra and ritual practice, it details initiation (dīkṣā), preliminary discipline (puraścaraṇa), nyāsa, and rituals for numerous deities, including Mahākāla, Devī, Sūrya, Viṣṇu, Gaṇeśa, and Kārtavīryārjuna. Containing notable historical anachronisms, such as predictions naming London, Christianity, and the British (chapter 35), the text in its present form dates to the early modern period (ca. 16th–18th century CE).
SA_MB_merutantraHK.attribution: Revealed scriptural tantra presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Śivā (śrīśivaśivāsaṃvādopanibaddha, śrīmahāmāyāmahākālānumate merutantre śivapraṇīte). The bracketed glosses, liturgical clarifications, and variant readings (ṭippanī) embedded in the text are by Paṇḍita Raghunātha Śāstrī Ojha.
SA_MB_merutantraHK.edition: Merutantram. Edited by R. Ojha (Raghunātha Śāstrī). Bombay: Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara Steam Press, 1908.
SA_MB_merutantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 35 prakāśas (chapters), concluding with the final colophon of prakāśa 35 ('iti śrīmahāmāyāmahākālānumate merutantre śivapraṇīte kārttavīryyārjunamantrakathanaṃ nāma pañcatriṃśattamaḥ prakāśaḥ || 35 || samāptaścāyaṃ granthaḥ ||').

SA_MB_pauskarvrttiHK.title: Pauṣkaravṛtti
SA_MB_pauskarvrttiHK.author: Jñānaprakāśācārya
SA_MB_pauskarvrttiHK.summary: The Pauṣkaravṛtti is a commentary by Jñānaprakāśācārya on the Jñānapāda (Vidyāpāda) of the Pauṣkarāgama in seven chapters, expounding Śaiva Siddhānta philosophy.
SA_MB_pauskarvrttiHK.attribution: Jñānaprakāśācārya (of Śālivāṭipura) is named in the colophon ('iti śrīśālivāṭipuranivāsi jñānaprakāśācārya viracitāyāṃ śrīmatpauṣkarajñānapādavṛttau saptamaḥ paṭalaḥ') and in the opening verse: 'praṇamya pauṣkarīṃ vyākhyāṃ vidyāṃśāntu karomyaham'.
SA_MB_pauskarvrttiHK.edition: Manuscript transcription: IFP transcript 110 (paper transcript, 936 pp.), copied from a 219-leaf palm-leaf manuscript belonging to Tondaimandalam jñānaprakāśaswamigal maṭham, Kanchipuram.
SA_MB_pauskarvrttiHK.coverage: complete — Commentary on the Jñānapāda of the Pauṣkarāgama (7 chapters), corresponding to all 936 pages of IFP transcript 110.

SA_MB_isvarapratyabhijnavimarsinivyakhya.title: Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinīvyākhyā
SA_MB_isvarapratyabhijnavimarsinivyakhya.summary: The Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinīvyākhyā (also titled Īśvarapratyabhijñānasūtravimarśinīvyākhyā) is an anonymous sub-commentary on Abhinavagupta's Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī on Utpaladeva's Īśvarapratyabhijñā.
SA_MB_isvarapratyabhijnavimarsinivyakhya.attribution: Anonymous sub-commentary on Abhinavagupta's Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī, copied from IFP transcript 762 which was copied from manuscript no. R. 4353 belonging to G.O.N.L. [GOML], Madras.
SA_MB_isvarapratyabhijnavimarsinivyakhya.edition: Transcript: IFP transcript 762, copied from manuscript no. R. 4353 belonging to G.O.N.L. [GOML], Madras.
SA_MB_isvarapratyabhijnavimarsinivyakhya.coverage: complete — Sub-commentary on Abhinavagupta's Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī, concluding with devotional verses to Śiva and Mukunda/Kṛṣṇa.

SA_MB_amsumatkaasyapaamgamaHK.title: Aṃśumatkāśyapāgama
SA_MB_amsumatkaasyapaamgamaHK.summary: The Aṃśumatkāśyapāgama is an authoritative Śaiva Siddhānta Āgamic treatise centered on temple architecture (vāstu), sacred iconography (mūrtilakṣaṇa / citra), and ritual consecration. Framed as an exposition delivered by Śiva to the sage Kāśyapa summarizing the ancient Aṃśumān tantra, it details temple layout, ground examination, foundation deposits, and structural elements of vimānas, maṇḍapas, and prākāras, followed by extensive rules on iconometric proportions (tālamāna) and iconographic forms of Śiva, Devī, and associated divinities.
SA_MB_amsumatkaasyapaamgamaHK.edition: Pondicherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), Transcript (T. 1), copied from palm-leaf manuscript RE. 19987 (beginning leaf (25)19a) [unpublished manuscript transcript].
SA_MB_amsumatkaasyapaamgamaHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete; transcribes Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript No. 1 (T. 1, based on palm-leaf RE. 19987), but lacks a final chapter colophon and final work explicit, ending abruptly after a dhyāna verse with '(śubhamastu)'.

SA_MB_kincittantraHK.title: Kiñcitatantra (fragment)
SA_MB_kincittantraHK.summary: An acephalous and truncated Kaula Śākta-Śaiva ritual fragment preserved in an unedited Nepalese manuscript, focusing on Guhyakālikā and associated fierce deities such as Cāmuṇḍā, Siddhilakṣmī, and the Aṣṭamātṛkās. The text details esoteric mantra vidyās, nyāsa prescriptions, samayavidyā recitation, and fierce Kaula rites (including māraṇa and samādhividhi). The Sanskrit exhibits extensive non-standard orthography and vernacular corruption characteristic of medieval Nepalese tantric transmission.
SA_MB_kincittantraHK.attribution: Anonymous Kaula Śākta-Śaiva tantric text. The title 'Kiñcitatantra' appears to stem from a descriptive cataloguer's label in Nepal (kiñcit tantram, i.e., 'a certain [unidentified] tantra') rather than an intrinsic textual title.
SA_MB_kincittantraHK.edition: Transcribed from unedited manuscript: NGMPP manuscript 4-1867 śaivatantra 199 ga Reel no: b 142/7.
SA_MB_kincittantraHK.coverage: fragment — Acephalous and truncated transcription of a single manuscript witness; the text opens abruptly in the midst of ritual/mantra instructions on folio 18b/19a and breaks off mid-word at line 712 ('paraśi----------------') without a concluding colophon or formal chapter division.

SA_MB_dvisatikaalottaramHK.title: Dviśatikālottara with Dviśatikālottaravṛtti
SA_MB_dvisatikaalottaramHK.author: Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_dvisatikaalottaramHK.summary: The Dviśatikālottara is accompanied by the commentary (vṛtti) of Aghoraśivācārya, discussing Śaiva doctrines, initiation (dīkṣā), mantras, and concluding with the prāsādanirṇayaprakaraṇa.
SA_MB_dvisatikaalottaramHK.attribution: The root scripture Dviśatikālottara is accompanied by the commentary (vṛtti) composed by Aghoraśivācārya (Aghoraśiva).
SA_MB_dvisatikaalottaramHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) Transcript 176, preserved in the IFP/EFEO collection, Pondicherry.
SA_MB_dvisatikaalottaramHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete at the beginning (lacking incipit), starting mid-sentence in commentary ('bhedabhinnaiḥ saṃkulamaneka padārthābhidheyamityarthaḥ...'), but extends to the conclusion of the text, ending with the prāsādanirṇayaprakaraṇa and final colophon ('dviśatikālottara vṛttiḥ samāptā').

SA_MB_candrajnaanaagamaHK.title: Candrajñānāgama (Kriyāpāda and Caryāpāda)
SA_MB_candrajnaanaagamaHK.summary: The Candrajñānāgama is an āgama text framed as an exposition delivered by Anantarudra to Bṛhaspati, transmitted in the Vīraśaiva tradition. The surviving portion in this recension comprises the Kriyāpāda and Caryāpāda, followed by the Mūlapañcākṣaramantranyāsa. It treats Śaiva observances, including rules on guru characteristics, tripuṇḍra and bhasma, japa, iṣṭaliṅga, and expiatory rites (prāyaścitta).
SA_MB_candrajnaanaagamaHK.attribution: A traditional Śaiva revelation presented as a dialogue between Anantarudra and Bṛhaspati (anantarudrabṛhaspatisaṃvāda). This recension preserves traditions associated with the Vīraśaiva community.
SA_MB_candrajnaanaagamaHK.coverage: partial — Contains the Kriyāpāda and Caryāpāda followed by the Mūlapañcākṣaramantranyāsa; misses the pūrvabhāga.

SA_MB_makutaagama_viirasaivaHK.title: Makuṭāgama (Uttarabhāga: Kriyāpāda and Caryāpāda)
SA_MB_makutaagama_viirasaivaHK.summary: The Uttarabhāga of the Makuṭāgama (also designated Makuṭottara) is a canonical Śaiva scripture preserved in the Vīraśaiva tradition, cast as an esoteric dialogue between Paraśiva and Rudra. It comprises two sections: the Kriyāpāda, detailing the theology of the Śāmbhavavrata (Śirovrata), daily observance (āhnika), and personal worship; and the Caryāpāda, regulating post-mortem funerary rites (śivamedha / antyeṣṭi), commemorative ceremonies, and ritual purity (āśauca).
SA_MB_makutaagama_viirasaivaHK.attribution: Scripture framed as a dialogue between Paraśiva and Rudra on Śāmbhavavrata, daily worship, and funerary orthopraxy.
SA_MB_makutaagama_viirasaivaHK.coverage: partial — Preserves the Uttarabhāga (Kriyāpāda and Caryāpāda) of the Makuṭāgama.

SA_MB_Tridasadaamaratantresiddhikaaliist.title: Siddhikālīstotra with other stotras, kavacas and pūjāvidhis (Nepalese ritual compilation)
SA_MB_Tridasadaamaratantresiddhikaaliist.summary: A Nepalese Śākta ritual manuscript with Newari rubrics, combining navagraha worship, the Mahāmāryāṣṭaka (a protective hymn to Mahāmārī/Kālī ascribed to the Rudrayāmala), a mantra-laden Śyāmā-sahasranāma, a Pañcamukhī-Hanumat-kavaca, a Pratyaṅgirā hymn ascribed to the Kubjikāmata, and the brief Siddhikālīstotra and Siddhikālī mantroddhāra ascribed to the Tridaśaḍāmara, framed by pūjā, bali and cakrapūjā procedures. It documents the Newar practice of assembling stotras and kavacas from different tantric sources into a single liturgical handbook.
SA_MB_Tridasadaamaratantresiddhikaaliist.attribution: Anonymous Nepalese (Newar) ritual compilation; individual pieces are ascribed in their colophons to the Rudrayāmala, Sudarśanasaṃhitā, Kubjikāmata and Tridaśaḍāmara(tantra). The Mahāmāryāṣṭaka names Vararuci as its ṛṣi (traditional viniyoga), not as an author.
SA_MB_Tridasadaamaratantresiddhikaaliist.edition: No printed edition; unpublished transcription of the Nepalese manuscript microfilmed by the NGMCP as reel H 334/6 (Muktabodha catalog no. M00203).
SA_MB_Tridasadaamaratantresiddhikaaliist.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript on NGMCP reel H 334/6 as filmed (ms pp. 1b–71b), ending 'śubhaṃ || pūrṇam'. The first lines (segs 7–10) duplicate the closing cakrapūjā rubrics (a misplaced final leaf). The Siddhikālīstotra itself is complete but forms only a small part of the e-text.

SA_MB_TridasadaamaraapratyaHK.title: Tridaśaḍāmarāpratyaṅgirāviṣayakanānātantra
SA_MB_TridasadaamaraapratyaHK.summary: A composite Nepalese Śākta-Tantric manuscript codex (nānātantra) compiled by Kālīdāsa in NS 738 (1617/1618 CE) preserving ritual procedures, mantroddhāras, and divination rites dedicated to Pratyaṅgirā and associated deities of the Tridaśaḍāmara stream, as well as Siddhalakṣmī / Kālī traditions. It compiles chapters and sections from the Tridaśaḍāmara, the Jayadrathayāmala (ṣaṭka 2), the Mahākulakrama, the Kālasaṅkarṣaṇīmata, the Kulaḍāmara, and the Mahākullālikā. The digital text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 3-30 (NGMCP reel B 173/22).
SA_MB_TridasadaamaraapratyaHK.attribution: Anonymous composite tantric codex containing multiple Śākta scriptural and ritual treatises collected by Kālīdāsa in Nepāla Saṃvat 738 (1617/1618 CE).
SA_MB_TridasadaamaraapratyaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of manuscript no. 3-30 (NGMCP reel no. B 173/22). Unpublished diplomatic transcription.
SA_MB_TridasadaamaraapratyaHK.coverage: partial — A composite codex of tantric excerpts and texts (nānātantra). The digital text transcribes manuscript no. 3-30 (NGMCP reel B 173/22) and ends with additional text lacking an explicit and colophon.

SA_MB_MahaayaagakramaHK.title: Mahāyāgakrama
SA_MB_MahaayaagakramaHK.author: Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_MahaayaagakramaHK.summary: The Mahāyāgakrama is an elaborate Śrīvidyā ritual manual associated with Bhāskararāya, centered on the Bhāvanopaniṣad. This edition also incorporates Bhāskararāya's commentary on the Kaulopaniṣad.
SA_MB_MahaayaagakramaHK.attribution: Bhāskararāya is named in the closing colophon: 'iti kaulamārgapārāvārapārīṇa śrīmadbhāskararāyaviracitaṃ kaulopaniṣadbhāṣyaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.
SA_MB_MahaayaagakramaHK.edition: Śrī Lalitāmahātripurasundarī Mahāyāgakramaḥ, ed. and publ. Āsthāna Vidvān K. P. Nārāyaṇa Śāstrī, Bangalore, 1946.
SA_MB_MahaayaagakramaHK.coverage: complete — Complete e-text of the 1946 Bangalore edition, containing the Mahāyāgakrama / Bhāvanopaniṣad and commentaries including Kaulopaniṣadbhāṣya.

SA_MB_laksmiitantraHK.title: Lakṣmītantra with Tattvaprakāśanī
SA_MB_laksmiitantraHK.summary: The Lakṣmītantra is an influential Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava Āgama in 57 chapters, notable for elevating Lakṣmī, the dynamic Śakti of Viṣṇu-Nārāyaṇa, to the primary cosmological and soteriological agent. It integrates classical Pāñcarātra doctrines—including the vyūha emanation system and absolute self-surrender (prapatti/nyāsa)—with Śākta-oriented mantra-śāstra, mātṛkānyāsa, and esoteric yogic practices. This e-text provides the complete scripture together with Pandit V. Krishnamacharya's Sanskrit gloss.
SA_MB_laksmiitantraHK.attribution: The Lakṣmītantra is a revealed Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava āgama. The Sanskrit gloss was composed by Pandit V. Krishnamacharya for the 1959 Adyar Library edition.
SA_MB_laksmiitantraHK.edition: Lakṣmī-Tantra. A Pāñcarātra Āgama, edited with Sanskrit gloss and introduction by V. Krishnamacharya, The Adyar Library Series 87, Madras: The Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1959.
SA_MB_laksmiitantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 57 chapters (adhyāyas 1–57), ending with chapter 57 (colophon at verse 55: 'iti śrīpāñcarātrasāre lakṣmītantroddhāre (tantrārthasaṃgrahe) rahasyaśāstrārthasāro nāma saptapañcāśo'dhyāyaḥ | lakṣmītantraṃ samāptam'). Contains the root text, commentary, and editorial variant apparatus.

SA_MB_sidhaantasikhaamaniHK.title: Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi with Tattvapradīpikā
SA_MB_sidhaantasikhaamaniHK.author: Śivayogiśivācārya, Maritoṇḍadārya
SA_MB_sidhaantasikhaamaniHK.summary: The Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi is a systematic Sanskrit doctrinal treatise of the Vīraśaiva tradition. Arranged in 21 paricchedas, it includes dialogue and philosophical exposition of Śaiva principles. Maritoṇḍadārya's commentary, the Tattvapradīpikā, substantiates the philosophical and theological positions of the root kārikās.
SA_MB_sidhaantasikhaamaniHK.attribution: The root treatise is attributed to Śivayogiśivācārya and the commentary Tattvapradīpikā is by Maritoṇḍadārya (Maritoṇṭadārya).
SA_MB_sidhaantasikhaamaniHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 21 paricchedas (chapters 1–21), covering root text and commentary through the colophon of pariccheda 21 (Reṇukavibhīṣaṇasaṃvāde reṇukaśivaliṅgaikyaprasaṅgaḥ). The Muktabodha release notes document revision 0 (chs. 1–15, April 2010) and revision 1 (chs. 15 to the end added, September 2010).

SA_MB_karanagamaHK.title: Kāraṇāgama (Kriyāpāda)
SA_MB_karanagamaHK.summary: The Kāraṇāgama is traditionally ranked fourth among the twenty-eight canonical Siddhāntāgamas; this e-text contains the ten-chapter Kriyāpāda section of its Uttarabhāga preserved in the Vīraśaiva (Liṅgāyata) tradition. Structured as a divine discourse between Pārvatī and Śiva, the text establishes the supremacy of Vīraśaiva dharma, the observance of the śāmbhavavrata, and the transmission of the threefold initiation (vedhā-, mantra-, and kriyādīkṣā).
