It provides extensive ritual prescriptions for the worship, wearing, and maintenance of the personal liṅga (iṣṭaliṅga), culminating in expiatory rites (prāyaścitta) to be performed in the event of ritual errors or the loss of the liṅga (naṣṭaliṅga).
SA_MB_karanagamaHK.attribution: Revealed Śaiva scripture presented as a dialogue between Pārvatī and Parameśvara (Śiva). In the Vīraśaiva (Liṅgāyata) tradition, the Uttarabhāgas of the Siddhāntāgamas are regarded as foundational revelations establishing Vīraśaiva ritual and theological doctrines.
SA_MB_karanagamaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the 10 paṭalas comprising the Kriyāpāda in this recension, closing with the tenth paṭala colophon: iti śrīkāraṇāgame uttarabhāge pārvatīparameśvarasaṃvāde kriyāpāde prāyaścittavidhikathanaṃ nāma daśamaḥ paṭalaḥ.

SA_MB_sivadharmaHK.title: Śivadharmaśāstra
SA_MB_sivadharmaHK.summary: The Śivadharmaśāstra is a Śaiva text in twelve adhyāyas presenting religious practices, including temple building and maintenance, gifts and offerings, protective invocations, ascetic rules, and the teaching of Śiva's knowledge, framed in its colophons as spoken by Nandi (Nandiprokta).
SA_MB_sivadharmaHK.attribution: Traditional Śaiva smṛti narrated by Nandikeśvara (Nandi).
SA_MB_sivadharmaHK.edition: Puducherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient, Transcript No. 860 (copied from ms no. R2442 belonging to G.O.N.L., Madras)
SA_MB_sivadharmaHK.coverage: complete — Ending with the 12th chapter colophon (Śivavidyāśākhopaśākhāsamuddeśa) and 'śivadharmassamāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_sivadharma_nandiproktaHK.title: Nandiproktaśivadharma (chapters 1–5)
SA_MB_sivadharma_nandiproktaHK.summary: Framed as a dialogue between Nandikeśvara and Sanatkumāra, the text expounds Śaiva religious observances, including aṣṭāṅgabhakti, liṅga worship, and the application of sacred ash (tripuṇḍra and uddhūlana). This Muktabodha transcription covers chapters 1 through 5 copied from pages 1–24 of IFP/EFEO transcript 72, which was copied from Adyar Library Madras MS 75429.
SA_MB_sivadharma_nandiproktaHK.attribution: A Śaiva scriptural work belonging to the Śivadharma corpus, framed as a dialogue where Sanatkumāra questions Nandikeśvara.
SA_MB_sivadharma_nandiproktaHK.edition: Unpublished transcript of Adyar Library (Madras) MS 75429, preserved as Institut Français de Pondichéry / EFEO transcript (pp. 1–24).
SA_MB_sivadharma_nandiproktaHK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters 1 through 5 (concluding at the end with 'iti śivadharme pañcamodhyāyaḥ'), covering pp. 1–24 of IFP/EFEO transcript 72.

SA_MB_sivadharmottaraHK.title: Śivadharmottara
SA_MB_sivadharmottaraHK.summary: The Śivadharmottara is a Śaiva religious treatise structured across twelve chapters as a discourse delivered by Nandin/Nandikeśvara. It expounds Śaiva religious practice (śivadharma), devotional liturgy, gifts, penances, and yoga leading to liberation (mukti).
SA_MB_sivadharmottaraHK.attribution: A Śaiva scripture recounted by Nandikeśvara (colophon: iti śaivaśāstre śivadharmottare nandikeśvaraprokte dvādaśodhyāyaḥ).
SA_MB_sivadharmottaraHK.edition: Manuscript transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) Transcript No. T. 72 (from p. 25), a Devanāgarī paper transcript of Adyar Library (Chennai) Grantha palm-leaf manuscript no. 75425.
SA_MB_sivadharmottaraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 12 chapters (adhyāyas 1–12), ending at verse 12.146 and the final colophon: 'iti śaivaśāstre śivadharmottare nandikeśvaraprokte dvādaśodhyāyaḥ || śubhamastu | om || śivadharmottarassamāptaḥ | dakṣiṇāmūrtaye namaḥ ||'.

SA_MB_mrigendrapaddhatitiikaaHK.title: Mṛgendrapaddhati with Mṛgendrapaddhatiṭīkā
SA_MB_mrigendrapaddhatitiikaaHK.author: Aghoraśiva, Vaktraśambhu
SA_MB_mrigendrapaddhatitiikaaHK.summary: The Mṛgendrapaddhati is a Śaiva Siddhānta ritual handbook attributed to Aghoraśivācārya, accompanied by the Mṛgendrapaddhatiṭīkā of Vaktraśambhu (Naṭeśvara). The work covers daily worship (nityārcana), expiatory rites (prāyaścitta), pavitravidhi, and icon consecration (pratiṣṭhāvidhi).
SA_MB_mrigendrapaddhatitiikaaHK.attribution: The root paddhati is attributed to Aghoraśivācārya (in the scribe's note and colophons). The commentary is attributed in its final colophon to Vaktraśambhu (referred to also as Naṭeśvara), son of Śaṅkara ('śrīnaṭeśvareṇa guruṇā vaktrādinā śambhunā śrīmacchaṅkarasūnunā viracitā ṭīkā samāptā').
SA_MB_mrigendrapaddhatitiikaaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T. 1021 (copy of IFP manuscript RE 40086).
SA_MB_mrigendrapaddhatitiikaaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the paddhati and commentary as preserved in the transcript, extending through daily worship rituals (nityārcanavidhi), prāyaścitta, pavitravidhi, and ending with pratiṣṭhāvidhi.

SA_MB_yogasarasamgrahaHK.title: Yogasārasaṃgraha
SA_MB_yogasarasamgrahaHK.summary: The Yogasārasaṃgraha is a yoga compendium in sixteen chapters (adhyāyas), concluding with ātmasvarūpanirūpaṇa. It draws on diverse authorities including Bhagavadgītā, Dattātreya, and Ādinātha.
SA_MB_yogasarasamgrahaHK.attribution: This work is an anonymous yoga compendium in 16 chapters, preserved in Madras GOML MS D. 4373 and IFP transcript T0859. Muktabodha and Intellexus list Vaktraśambhu under commentator / author of a vṛtti.
SA_MB_yogasarasamgrahaHK.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T0859 (copied from Government Oriental Manuscripts Library [GOML], Madras, MS D. 4373).
SA_MB_yogasarasamgrahaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 16 chapters (adhyāyas), concluding with chapter 16 (ātmasvarūpanirūpaṇa) and a final verse confirming the 16-chapter structure (ṣoḍaśādhyāyaiḥ).

SA_MB_parasuramakalpasutraHK.title: Paraśurāmakalpasūtra with Saubhāgyodaya
SA_MB_parasuramakalpasutraHK.author: Paraśurāma, Rāmeśvara
SA_MB_parasuramakalpasutraHK.summary: The Paraśurāmakalpasūtra is a foundational manual of Śākta ritual worship in the Śrīvidyā (Kaula) tradition, composed in ten khaṇḍas of concise aphorisms. Traditionally attributed to Paraśurāma, it codifies ritual procedures, mantra transmission, dīkṣā, and Śrīcakra worship for Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī and affiliated deities such as Bālā, Mātaṅgī, and Vārāhī. This e-text presents the sūtras together with the commentary Saubhāgyodaya by Rāmeśvara.
SA_MB_parasuramakalpasutraHK.attribution: The root sūtra is traditionally attributed to Paraśurāma. The commentary Saubhāgyodaya (Vṛtti) was composed by Rāmeśvara.
SA_MB_parasuramakalpasutraHK.edition: Paraśurāmakalpasūtra with Rāmeśvara's Commentary, edited by A. Mahadeva Sastri and S. Y. Sastri Dave, Gaekwad's Oriental Series, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1950.
SA_MB_parasuramakalpasutraHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete; terminates abruptly at '- tantrāntaropasaṃhāravicāraḥ -', lacking the final explicit and closing colophon.

SA_MB_Paraatrisikaavivrtti_berlinHK.title: Parātriṃśikāvivṛti (conclusion) and Mantravivaraṇa
SA_MB_Paraatrisikaavivrtti_berlinHK.author: Lakṣmīrāma, Śivasvāmyupādhyāya
SA_MB_Paraatrisikaavivrtti_berlinHK.summary: This e-text preserves two late Kashmirian Śaiva-Śākta works transcribed directly from Berlin manuscript Hs. or. 11633. The first is the concluding fragment and colophon of Rājānaka Lakṣmīrāma's Parātriṃśikāvivṛti. The second is the Mantravivaraṇa by Kāśmīrika Śivasvāmyupādhyāya, which expounds the kūṭas of the Parā/Tripurasundarī mantrarāja within a non-dual Śaiva/Śākta framework.
SA_MB_Paraatrisikaavivrtti_berlinHK.attribution: Contains the colophons 'iti śrīparātriṃśikāvivṛtī rājānakalakṣmīrāmaviracitā samāptā || saṃvat 43 kānnatyaikādaśyāṃ likhiteyam' and 'kāsmīrikaviśudhaśivasvāsyupādhyāyanāmnā vyākhyāto mantrarājaḥ ... sampūrṇamidaṃ mantravivaraṇam'.
SA_MB_Paraatrisikaavivrtti_berlinHK.edition: Manuscript Hs. or. 11633, Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Orientabteilung (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_Paraatrisikaavivrtti_berlinHK.coverage: partial — Contains the conclusion of Lakṣmīrāma's Parātriṃśikāvivṛti, followed by Śivasvāmyupādhyāya's Mantravivaraṇa.

SA_MB_gurustutiratnavaliHK.title: Gurustutiratnāvalī
SA_MB_gurustutiratnavaliHK.author: Govindakaula
SA_MB_gurustutiratnavaliHK.summary: The Gurustutiratnāvalī is an 18th-century Sanskrit hymn (stotra) composed by the Kashmiri author Govindakaula in praise of Sāhib Kaula. The work exalts the guru as non-dual Śiva and the source of all manifestation, serving as an important document of post-classical Kashmirian Śaiva-Śākta gurubhakti.
SA_MB_gurustutiratnavaliHK.attribution: The colophon attributes the work to Govindakaula, disciple of Jyotiṣprakāśakaula (iti śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryaśrīmacchrījyotiṣprakāsakaulānandapādapadmānujīviśrīgovindakaulaviracitā śrīgurustutiratnāvalī samāptā), composing in devotion to the revered preceptor Sāhib Kaula.
SA_MB_gurustutiratnavaliHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Orientabteilung, Hs. or. 11126 (unpublished digital transcription)
SA_MB_gurustutiratnavaliHK.coverage: complete — The text of the hymn is complete up to its author colophon, followed by extra manuscript verses on tantric samaya and pūjā.

SA_MB_srividyarnavatantramHK.title: Śrīvidyārṇavatantra (Pūrvārdha)
SA_MB_srividyarnavatantramHK.author: Vidyāraṇyayati
SA_MB_srividyarnavatantramHK.summary: The Śrīvidyārṇavatantra is an encyclopedic Śākta and Śrīvidyā compendium attributed to Vidyāraṇyayati. It synthesizes various lineages and ritual streams (including Kādimata and Kālikāmata), detailing yantras, nyāsas, mantraśāstra, initiation rituals, and deity worship. This file contains the complete Pūrvārdha (śvāsas 1–18).
SA_MB_srividyarnavatantramHK.attribution: Colophons attribute the work to Śrīvidyāraṇyayati, tracing his paramparā via Govindācārya -> Śaṅkarācārya -> Viṣṇuśarmācārya -> Pragalbhācārya -> Vidyāraṇyayati.
SA_MB_srividyarnavatantramHK.edition: Śrīvidyārṇavatantram, edited by Ram Chandra Kak and Harabhatta Shastri, Varanasi Tantrika Text Series, Varanasi, 1947.
SA_MB_srividyarnavatantramHK.coverage: partial — Contains śvāsas 1 to 18, ending with 'samāptamidaṃ pūrvārdham'. The Uttarārdha is not included in this file.

SA_MB_paramesvariitantraHK.title: Parameśvarīmatatantra
SA_MB_paramesvariitantraHK.summary: The Parameśvarīmatatantra is a scripture of the Western Transmission (Paścimāmnāya) of Kaula Śaivism, intimately connected with the Kubjikā cycle. Set as a dialogue between Mahābhairava and the Devī, the text treats the esoteric symbolism of Mount Meru (Meruddhāra), the sixfold lineage (ṣaḍvidha kulāmnāya), mantras, mudrās, and yantras. In this manuscript transcription, paṭala 24 marks the conclusion of the 24-chapter Meruddhāra of the Pārameśvarīmata, while the remainder continues through to chapter 56, ending with a colophon to the Kubjikāmata.
SA_MB_paramesvariitantraHK.attribution: Anonymous canonical Śākta/Śaiva scripture revealed by Śrī Mahābhairava to the Devī.
SA_MB_paramesvariitantraHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: NGMPP reel no: B 133/3 manuscript no. 5-5148, transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (Muktabodha Catalog No. M00218, 2010–2011).
SA_MB_paramesvariitantraHK.coverage: unclear — Transcribes 56 chapters (paṭalas) preserved in National Archives Kathmandu MS 5-5148 (NGMPP reel B 133/3). Internal colophons indicate a composite manuscript or sections from two closely related texts: paṭala 24 concludes the Meruddhāra section of the Pārameśvarīmata ('iti pārameśvarīmate navakoṭisaṃhitāyāṃ caturāśītisahasrameruddhāraḥ caturviṃśatimaḥ paṭalaḥ'), while the final colophon at paṭala 56 reads 'iti śrīkubjikāmate ṣaṭpañcāśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_vatulottaraHK.title: Vātulottarāgama (selected paṭalas, with extracts from the Parameśvaratantra and Candrajñāna)
SA_MB_vatulottaraHK.summary: The Vātulottara is a Śaiva āgama text presenting rituals and expiations (prāyaścitta). This transcript contains selections from the text along with extracts ascribed to the Parameśvaratantra and Candrajñāna.
SA_MB_vatulottaraHK.attribution: Ascribed to the Śaiva Siddhānta āgama corpus.
SA_MB_vatulottaraHK.edition: Unpublished transcription of IFP transcript 624 (Muktabodha catalog no. M00219).
SA_MB_vatulottaraHK.coverage: partial — Transcription from IFP transcript 624 containing incomplete/selected paṭalas of the Vātulottara (including Prāyaścittakāṇḍa), ending with extracts from the Parameśvaratantra ('iti parameśvaratantre aṣṭatriṃśatpaṭalaḥ') and Candrajñāna ('iti candrajñāne').

SA_MB_somasambhupaddhativyakhyaHK.title: Somaśambhupaddhativyākhyā (incomplete)
SA_MB_somasambhupaddhativyakhyaHK.author: Trilocanaśiva
SA_MB_somasambhupaddhativyakhyaHK.summary: Commentary (Spaṣṭabodhinī) attributed to Tryaṃbakaśambhu on Somaśambhu's ritual manual (Somaśambhupaddhati).
SA_MB_somasambhupaddhativyakhyaHK.attribution: Commentary on Somaśambhu's Somaśambhupaddhati. The final colophon attributes the commentary (Spaṣṭabodhinī) to Tryaṃbakaśambhu ('iti śrī somaśambhuviracitāṃ śrīmatsomaśambhupaddhatau vā spaṣṭabodhinī tryaṃbakaśambhuviracite caturdaśa ṭīkā samāptā').
SA_MB_somasambhupaddhativyakhyaHK.edition: Pondicherry, Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), transcript T0170 (Devanāgarī transcript).
SA_MB_somasambhupaddhativyakhyaHK.coverage: partial — Lacks incipit (opens: 'lebhe sekottarāṃ dīkṣāṃ...'). Ends with chapter 14 ('caturdaśa ṭīkā samāptā').

SA_MB_tripuraarahasyamHK.title: Tripurārahasya: Māhātmyakhaṇḍa (chapters 51–80)
SA_MB_tripuraarahasyamHK.summary: The Māhātmyakhaṇḍa is one of the sections of the Tripurārahasya, a Śākta text. It presents the purāṇic mythic glorification of Lalitā Tripurasundarī, including the conquest of Bhaṇḍāsura and the cosmography of the Śrīcakra. This partial e-text contains chapters 51 through 80, concluding the section.
SA_MB_tripuraarahasyamHK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters 51 through 80 (the conclusion of Māhātmyakhaṇḍa at colophon: 'samāptamidaṃ tripurārahasye māhātmyakhaṇḍam'), followed by brief closing devotional verses/stotras.

SA_MB_vaarunapaddhatiHK.title: Vāruṇapaddhati with Vāruṇapaddhativyākhyā
SA_MB_vaarunapaddhatiHK.author: Varuṇaśivācārya, Nigamajñānadeva
SA_MB_vaarunapaddhatiHK.summary: The Vāruṇapaddhati (also known as Ātmārthapūjāpaddhati) by Varuṇaśivācārya is a Śaiva manual outlining personal daily worship (ātmārthapūjā) and ritual procedures.
SA_MB_vaarunapaddhatiHK.attribution: The paddhati is attributed to Varuṇaśivācārya, with a ṭīkā attributed to Nigamajñānadeva.
SA_MB_vaarunapaddhatiHK.edition: Unpublished transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO) transcript No. T00055.
SA_MB_vaarunapaddhatiHK.coverage: uncertain — Transcription of IFP/EFEO transcript T00055.

SA_MB_sivajnaanasiddhiHK.title: Śivajñānasiddhisvapakṣadṛṣṭāntasaṅgraha
SA_MB_sivajnaanasiddhiHK.author: Vedajñāna Śivācārya
SA_MB_sivajnaanasiddhiHK.summary: The Śivajñānasiddhisvapakṣadṛṣṭāntasaṅgraha is a Śaiva Siddhānta anthology compiled by Vedajñāna Śivācārya of Vyāghrapura, disciple of Nigamajñāna Śivayogin. It collates Sanskrit canonical citations and analogies (dṛṣṭānta) from numerous Śaivāgamas (such as the Svāyambhuva, Ajita, Cintyaviśva, Śivadharmottara, and Devīkālottara) to provide the Sanskrit scriptural sources and parallels for the 327 verses of the Svapakṣa section of Aruḷnandi Śivācārya's Tamil Śivajñānasiddhiyār.
SA_MB_sivajnaanasiddhiHK.attribution: Compiled by Vedajñāna Śivācārya (disciple of Nigamajñāna Śivayogin of Vyāghrapura).
SA_MB_sivajnaanasiddhiHK.edition: Manuscript transcript IFP/EFEO T00317, pp. 968–1118 (Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient, Pondicherry).
SA_MB_sivajnaanasiddhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete anthology of Āgamic citations corresponding to the 12 sūtras of the Svapakṣa, ending with 'dvādaśatamasūtraṃ sampūrṇam' and the final colophon.

SA_MB_sarvajnaanottaravrittiHK.title: Sarvajñānottaravṛtti (Yogaprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_sarvajnaanottaravrittiHK.author: Aghoraśivācārya
SA_MB_sarvajnaanottaravrittiHK.summary: The Yogaprakaraṇa of the Sarvajñānottaravṛtti is a commentary by Aghoraśivācārya on the yoga chapter of the Sarvajñānottaratantra. Aghoraśiva interprets the scripture's teachings on Śiva-yoga within the Saiddhāntika scheme of three realities (pati, paśu, pāśa), quoting authorities such as Patañjali and the Mataṅgapārameśvaratantra.
SA_MB_sarvajnaanottaravrittiHK.attribution: The concluding colophon confirms authorship: 'iti lakṣadvayādhyāpaka śrīmadaghoraśivācāryaviracitāyāṃ śrīmatsarvajñānottaravṛttau yogaprakaraṇam'.
SA_MB_sarvajnaanottaravrittiHK.edition: Unpublished transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO) transcript T0985 (T. 985), Pondicherry.
SA_MB_sarvajnaanottaravrittiHK.coverage: partial — Contains only the Yogaprakaraṇa of the Sarvajñānottaratantra along with Aghoraśiva's commentary.

SA_MB_saivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.title: Śivāgamādimāhātmyasaṃgraha
SA_MB_saivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.author: Jñānaprakāśa
SA_MB_saivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.summary: The Śivāgamādimāhātmyasaṃgraha by Jñānaprakāśa of Śālīvāṭipura is a Saiddhāntika anthology and doctrinal treatise asserting the supreme scriptural authority of the Śaiva Āgamas over rival and non-Śaiva philosophical systems. Gathering testimonies from primary Āgamas (including Pauṣkara, Kāmika, Kiraṇa, and Aṃśumat) as well as Purāṇas, the text explains the emanation of scriptural wisdom as sound (nāda) from Sadāśiva and glorifies Śaiva initiation (dīkṣā), devotional duties, and observances.
SA_MB_saivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.attribution: Attributed in the final colophon to Jñānaprakāśaguru of Śālīvāṭipura in Tamil Nadu. Muktabodha description dates him to the 15th century.
SA_MB_saivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.edition: Manuscript transcript: IFP/EFEO transcript T00372, pp. 1192–1261.
SA_MB_saivaagamaadimaahaatmyamHK.coverage: complete — Complete: e-text covers IFP/EFEO transcript T00372 pp. 1192–1261 (with page markers up to 'p. 1261)') and ends with the colophon 'iti śrīśālīvāṭipuranivāsi jñānaprakāśaguruviracita śivāgamādimāhātmya saṃgrahassamāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_mantrakaumudiiHK.title: Mantrakaumudī
SA_MB_mantrakaumudiiHK.author: Devanātha Ṭhakkura
SA_MB_mantrakaumudiiHK.summary: The Mantrakaumudī is a 16th-century Maithila Tantric nibandha by Devanātha Ṭhakkura. Synthesizing citations from numerous earlier Tantric works, it deals with aspects of the practice of Mantra, free of Vāma practices.
SA_MB_mantrakaumudiiHK.attribution: Composed by Mahāmahopādhyāya Devanātha Ṭhakkura Tarkapañcānana, son of Govinda Ṭhakkura, in Mithila. In verse 24 at the conclusion, the author dates the composition to year 400 of the Lakṣmaṇasena era (abde lakṣmaṇasenasya viyacchūnyābdhilakṣite).
SA_MB_mantrakaumudiiHK.coverage: complete — Text of the digest, ending with concluding verses (vv. 22–24) and final colophon (iti śrītarkapañcānanamahāmahopādhyāyaśrīdevanathakṛtā mantrakaumudī samāptā).

SA_MB_kaulaavaliinirnayaHK.title: Kaulāvalīnirṇaya
SA_MB_kaulaavaliinirnayaHK.author: Jñānānandaparamahaṃsa
SA_MB_kaulaavaliinirnayaHK.summary: The Kaulāvalīnirṇaya is a Kaula Śākta ritual compendium composed by Jñānānandaparamahaṃsa. In 21 chapters (ullāsas), it treats Tantric ritual and doctrine, including guru and disciple qualifications, worship, and the status of an avadhūta.
SA_MB_kaulaavaliinirnayaHK.attribution: The author names himself Jñānānandaparamahaṃsa in the colophons.
SA_MB_kaulaavaliinirnayaHK.edition: Kaulāvalīnirṇaya of Jñānānanda Paramahaṃsa, edited by Arthur Avalon, Tantrik Text Series, 1927.

SA_MB_kriyaasaaratattvaprakaasiniivyaakh.title: Kriyāsāratattvaprakāśinīvyākhyā (paṭalas 3–15) with an anonymous commentary on Sureśvara's Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣyavārttika (fragment)
SA_MB_kriyaasaaratattvaprakaasiniivyaakh.author: Nārāyaṇa
SA_MB_kriyaasaaratattvaprakaasiniivyaakh.summary: Nārāyaṇa's Tattvaprakāśinī is a commentary on the Kriyāsāra, an āgamic/tantric ritual manual; the preserved paṭalas 3-15 explain site purification, the maṇḍapa and Kumbheśa worship, adhivāsana, fire ritual, expiations, and installation preparations. The same IFP transcript (T00934) continues with an unrelated fragment of a commentary on Sureśvara's Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣyavārttika covering roughly BĀU 2.1-3.8.
SA_MB_kriyaasaaratattvaprakaasiniivyaakh.attribution: The opening rubric of the transcript ('śrīḥ nārāyaṇaviracitā') and the Muktabodha header name Nārāyaṇa as author of the Kriyāsāra commentary. The author of the Vārttika commentary is not named in the fragment.
SA_MB_kriyaasaaratattvaprakaasiniivyaakh.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcript: IFP/EFEO transcript T00934 (Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient, Pondicherry), transcribed from a palm-leaf manuscript belonging to Nārāyaṇankuññu Nambūdiripad, Ernakulam.
SA_MB_kriyaasaaratattvaprakaasiniivyaakh.coverage: partial — Part 1: the Tattvaprakāśinī starts at paṭala 3 ('tṛtīyapaṭalādārabhyate'), with colophons for paṭalas 3-14, and breaks off within paṭala 15. Part 2: a Vedāntic commentary on Sureśvara's Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣyavārttika, starting around BĀU 2.1 and breaking off in the Gārgī section (BĀU 3.8, 'kasmin na khalv ākāśa ...'), marked 'īncomplete'.

SA_MB_iisaanasivagurudevapaddhati4HK.title: Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati (volume 4)
SA_MB_iisaanasivagurudevapaddhati4HK.author: Īśānaśivagurudeva
SA_MB_iisaanasivagurudevapaddhati4HK.summary: The Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati (also known as Siddhāntasāra or Siddhāntasārapaddhati) is an extensive Śaiva ritual work. This volume includes rituals of installation (vimānapratiṣṭhādhikāraḥ), altars/pedestals (pīṭha), chariots (ratha), homa, and concludes with the Yogapāda treating prāṇāyāma and related yogic topics.
SA_MB_iisaanasivagurudevapaddhati4HK.attribution: Attributed in colophons to Īśānaśivagurudeva (also referred to as Īśānaśiva).
SA_MB_iisaanasivagurudevapaddhati4HK.coverage: partial — Volume 4 (described in Muktabodha header as Volume 3 of 4 volume edition), concluding with Yogapāda paṭala 3 and the final work colophon.

SA_MB_diiksaadarsaHK.title: Dīkṣādarśa
SA_MB_diiksaadarsaHK.author: Vedajñāna
SA_MB_diiksaadarsaHK.summary: The Dīkṣādarśa is a Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual (paddhati) composed by Vedajñāna (son of Vāmadeva) of Vyāghrapura. It systematically structures the rites of Śaiva initiation (dīkṣā) and associated ceremonies, substantiating the procedures with scriptural quotations.
SA_MB_diiksaadarsaHK.attribution: The colophons identify the author as Vedajñāna, son of Vāmadeva (vāmadevātmaja), resident of Vyāghrapura.
SA_MB_diiksaadarsaHK.edition: Manuscript transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / EFEO transcript T. 0372 (pp. 1262–1670), copied from a manuscript belonging to Sundaradīkṣitar, Tirunelveli (unpublished transcript)
SA_MB_diiksaadarsaHK.coverage: complete — Transcribed across pages 1262 to 1670 of IFP transcript T0372 (T00372), ending with the final concluding colophon (iti śrī vyāghrapuranivāsī vāmadevātmaja vedajñāna viracita dīkṣādarśassamāptaḥ).

SA_MB_kaalahastiisavilaasaHK.title: Kālahastīśavilāsa (vilāsa 1)
SA_MB_kaalahastiisavilaasaHK.summary: The Kālahastīśavilāsa is a Śaiva theological and polemical treatise written in mixed prose and verse to establish the supremacy (sarvotkarṣa) of Śiva as Kālahastīśa. It debates sectarian opponents (chiefly Vaiṣṇavas) by interpreting Vedic, Upaniṣadic, and Purāṇic passages to argue that terms like Brahman and Parameśvara refer exclusively to Śiva. This e-text contains the first chapter (vilāsa 1), transcribed from IFP/EFEO transcript T0378.
SA_MB_kaalahastiisavilaasaHK.attribution: The concluding lines record praise of Cārukīrti Yatīndra ('ṣaṇmatasthāpanāryaḥ ... śrīcārukīrtiryatīndraḥ') and scribal execution by Veṅkaṭeśa; authorial attribution remains undetermined.
SA_MB_kaalahastiisavilaasaHK.edition: Transcript T0378 of the Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO).
SA_MB_kaalahastiisavilaasaHK.coverage: partial — Contains only the first chapter (vilāsa 1), ending with 'siṃhāruṇe bhūt prathamovilālaḥ' followed by scribal/dedicatory verses.

SA_MB_karpuuraadistotramHK.title: Karpūrādistotra with Svarūpavyākhyā
SA_MB_karpuuraadistotramHK.author: Vimalānandasvāmī
SA_MB_karpuuraadistotramHK.summary: The Karpūrādistotra (or Dakṣiṇakālikāsvarūpastotra) is an influential Śākta hymn celebrating Dakṣiṇakālikā, traditionally attributed to Mahākāla. It systematically encodes the esoteric bījamantras (mantroddhāra), visualization (dhyāna), and Kaula ritual practices of Kālī. This e-text provides the root stotra together with the Sanskrit commentary Svarūpavyākhyā (also known as Vimalānandadāyinī) by Vimalānandasvāmī (Satīśacandra Rāya Caudhurī).
SA_MB_karpuuraadistotramHK.attribution: The root hymn is traditionally attributed to Mahākāla in the colophon. The commentary Svarūpavyākhyā (or Vimalānandadāyinī) was composed by Vimalānandasvāmī, identified in the concluding colophon verses as Satīśacandra Rāya Caudhurī of Koṭālipāḍa.
SA_MB_karpuuraadistotramHK.edition: Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe), ed., Karpūrādistotram with Introduction and Commentary by Vimalānanda Svāmī. Tāntrik Texts. London: Luzac & Co. / Calcutta, 1922.
SA_MB_karpuuraadistotramHK.coverage: complete — Complete Karpūrādistotra with the Sanskrit commentary (Svarūpavyākhyā / Vimalānandadāyinī) and concluding biographical verses of Vimalānandasvāmī.
translations: Arthur Avalon, Karpūrādistotram with Introduction and Commentary by Vimalānanda Svāmī, translated by Arthur Avalon. Tantrik Texts. London: Luzac & Co. / Calcutta, 1922. (English)

SA_MB_aasaucadiipikaaHK.title: Āśaucyadīpikā
SA_MB_aasaucadiipikaaHK.author: Vedajñāna
SA_MB_aasaucadiipikaaHK.summary: The Āśaucyadīpikā is a Śaiva Siddhānta treatise on ritual impurity (āśauca / sūtaka) composed by a disciple bearing the name of Vedajñāna of Vyāghrapura. Citing Siddhāntāgamas and smṛti traditions, it determines periods and procedures of purification resulting from birth and death, particularly in relation to an initiate's eligibility for Śiva worship (śivapūjā).
SA_MB_aasaucadiipikaaHK.attribution: The concluding verses specify that the author is a disciple of Vedajñāna who took the name of his teacher, residing in Vyāghrapura.
SA_MB_aasaucadiipikaaHK.edition: Transcript No. T00370, pp. 326–400 (IFP/EFEO), copied from a manuscript belonging to Sundaradiksitar Tirunelveli.
SA_MB_aasaucadiipikaaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text as preserved in IFP/EFEO transcript T00370 (pp. 326–400), ending with the colophon 'iti śrīmadvyāghrapurinivāsi vedajñānadevaśiracitāśaucyadīpikā samāptā'.

SA_MB_sriitatvanidhiHK.title: Śrītattvanidhi
SA_MB_sriitatvanidhiHK.author: Kṛṣṇarāja Voḍeyar III
SA_MB_sriitatvanidhiHK.summary: The Śrītattvanidhi ('Treasure of Realities') is an encyclopedic Sanskrit compendium attributed to Maharaja Kṛṣṇarāja of Mysore. Organized into nine thematic 'nidhis' (treasures), it compiles iconographic descriptions, dhyāna verses, astronomical lore, temple practices, and esoteric lore culled from Purāṇas, Āgamas, and Tantras. The final section (Kautukanidhi) contains descriptions of traditional games and yoga postures.
SA_MB_sriitatvanidhiHK.attribution: Attributed in colophons to Śrī Kṛṣṇarāja Mahārāja of Mysore (śrīmanmahīśūrapuravarādhīśaśrīkṛṣṇarājamahārāja).
SA_MB_sriitatvanidhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete text containing nine nidhis concluding with the colophon of the ninth nidhi (kautukanidhi) and end of the entire work on p. 416.

SA_MB_kaamaratnatantraHK.title: Kāmaratna
SA_MB_kaamaratnatantraHK.author: Nityanātha
SA_MB_kaamaratnatantraHK.summary: A manual of practical magic and medicine in sixteen upadeśas ascribed to Nityanātha, framed as a dialogue of Īśvara and the Goddess. It covers the six magical rites (vaśīkaraṇa, ākarṣaṇa, stambhana, mohana, uccāṭana, māraṇa), aphrodisiacs (vājīkaraṇa), remedies against poison (viṣanivāraṇa), yakṣiṇī-sādhana, treasure-finding and other kautukas, and the purification of mercury and minerals (rasādiśodhana).
SA_MB_kaamaratnatantraHK.attribution: Ascribed in the colophon to Nityanātha ("śrīnityanāthaviracite kāmaratne").
SA_MB_kaamaratnatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 16 upadeśas (chapters 1–16), ending with the colophon of the 16th upadeśa (rasādiśodhana).

SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaaT1034HK.title: Varuṇapaddhati with Vilocana (dīkṣā section and beginning of pratiṣṭhā section)
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaaT1034HK.author: Varuṇaśiva, Nigamajñāna II
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaaT1034HK.summary: The Vilocana of Nigamajñānadeva is a commentary on Varuṇaśiva's Varuṇapaddhati. This e-text contains the commentary on dīkṣā and the opening of the pratiṣṭhā section, breaking off incomplete.
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaaT1034HK.attribution: The root Varuṇapaddhati is by Varuṇaśiva. The commentary Vilocana is by Nigamajñānadeva of Vyāghrapura (colophon: 'śrīmadvyāghrapuravāsinīgamajñānadevaviracitavaruṇapaddhativyākhyāne vilocanākhyāne'), identified in Muktabodha metadata as Nigamajñāna 2.
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaaT1034HK.edition: Unpublished transcription of IFP transcript T01034 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), Muktabodha catalog no. M00240.
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaaT1034HK.coverage: partial — Covers IFP transcript T. 1034, pp. 800–891ff. Contains the dīkṣā section followed by the beginning of the pratiṣṭhā section, breaking off at 'atha pratiṣṭhāyāmūrtimūrtīśvaratatvatatveśvaranyāsaḥ'.

SA_MB_hathayogapradiipikaaHK.title: Haṭhayogapradīpikā with Jyotsnā (incomplete)
SA_MB_hathayogapradiipikaaHK.author: Svātmārāma, Brahmānanda
SA_MB_hathayogapradiipikaaHK.summary: The Haṭhayogapradīpikā is the principal medieval manual of Haṭhayoga, composed by Svātmārāma. Synthesizing Nātha lineage teachings and earlier haṭha treatises, it details āsana, purification techniques (ṣaṭkarma), prāṇāyāma (kumbhaka), and mudrā/bandha as an essential physical progression culminating in Rājayoga (samādhi and nādānusandhāna). This e-text reproduces the root text alongside Brahmānanda's prominent ṭīkā, the Jyotsnā, which explicates the physiological and philosophical terminology.
SA_MB_hathayogapradiipikaaHK.attribution: The root text is traditionally ascribed in colophons to Sahajānandasaṃtānacintāmaṇi Svātmārāma Yogīndra; the Sanskrit commentary Jyotsnā is by Brahmānanda.
SA_MB_hathayogapradiipikaaHK.coverage: partial — Covers Upadeśas 1 to 4, but breaks off abruptly towards the end of chapter 4 (samādhi/nāda), marked explicitly at line 5263 as 'īncomplete'.

SA_MB_gitarthasamgrahaHK.title: Bhagavadgītā with Gītārthasaṃgraha
SA_MB_gitarthasamgrahaHK.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_gitarthasamgrahaHK.summary: The Gītārthasaṃgraha is Abhinavagupta's philosophical commentary on the Bhagavadgītā written from the perspective of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism (Pratyabhijñā). It interprets Kṛṣṇa's instruction to Arjuna as a revelation of supreme non-dual consciousness (anuttara-saṃvid), synthesizing action (karma), knowledge (jñāna), and devotion (bhakti) as integrated expressions of divine sovereignty and self-awareness (svātantrya). The work reflects the Kashmirian recension of the Bhagavadgītā, containing distinct textual variants and additional verses.
SA_MB_gitarthasamgrahaHK.attribution: The Gītārthasaṃgraha is attributed to Abhinavagupta, explicitly attested in chapter colophons and closing verses.
SA_MB_gitarthasamgrahaHK.edition: The Bhagavadgītā with the Commentary of Abhinavagupta, edited by Lakṣmaṇa Raina Brahmacārī [Swami Lakshman Joo], Srinagar: Kashmiri Pratap Steam Press, 1933.
SA_MB_gitarthasamgrahaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in all 18 adhyāyas of the Bhagavadgītā along with Abhinavagupta's commentary up to the closing verse and final colophon.

SA_MB_diiksaapaddhatiHK.title: Dīkṣāpaddhati (incomplete)
SA_MB_diiksaapaddhatiHK.summary: An anonymous Kashmiri manual for Śaiva (Bhairava-oriented) initiation, which Muktabodha describes as showing an intensely tantric local pantheon like Nepal's. The surviving part covers the preparatory days in detail: purification of the officiant, kalaśa installation, fire consecration, caru, and preparation of the disciple. It also maps the six paths (kalās, tattvas, bhuvanas) onto the disciple's body and gives the dream rite of the adhivāsa night. It then begins the third day (interpretation of dreams, drawing of the maṇḍala) before breaking off. Extensive marginal glosses in the manuscript are transcribed in round brackets.
SA_MB_diiksaapaddhatiHK.edition: No printed edition; transcription of manuscript no. 2379, Research Library, Jammu & Kashmir Government, Srinagar (Muktabodha catalog no. M00245, revision 0, 5 Feb. 2012). Marginal additions are given in round brackets.
SA_MB_diiksaapaddhatiHK.coverage: partial — Day 1 (preliminary rites, kalaśa, fire), day 2 (adhivāsa, caru, the disciple's preparation, mapping of kalās and bhuvanas, the disciple's bed and dream rite; ends 'ity adhivāsaḥ') and the start of day 3 ('atha tṛtīya dine…': interpretation of dreams, then construction of the maṇḍala). It breaks off mid-word ('pūrvapatraṃ prasādyaivami') without a colophon.

SA_MB_agnikaaryapaddhatiHK..title: Agnikāryapaddhati (incomplete)
SA_MB_agnikaaryapaddhatiHK..summary: An anonymous Kashmiri ritual manual (paddhati) for the fire ritual (agnikārya/homa) in a Bhairava/Kaula-oriented Śaiva setting. It begins with worship of Pustakavāgīśvarī (Sarasvatī) and Gaṇapati, kalaśa worship, purification of the subtle body, and preparation and consecration of the kuṇḍa and fire. It then gives oblation and tarpaṇa sequences for many deities, including Durgā, the Lokeśas and the planets, and ends with an incomplete section on animal sacrifice. The Muktabodha description stresses its incidental information on Kashmiri cults, e.g. the goddess Siddhalakṣmī.
SA_MB_agnikaaryapaddhatiHK..attribution: Anonymous manual of the Kashmiri Tantric Śaiva/Śākta ritual tradition.
SA_MB_agnikaaryapaddhatiHK..edition: No printed edition; the e-text is an unpublished transcription of manuscript no. 781, Research Library, Jammu & Kashmir Government, Srinagar (Muktabodha catalog no. M00246, revision 0, 5 Feb. 2012).
SA_MB_agnikaaryapaddhatiHK..coverage: partial — Starts at the beginning (maṅgala to Bhairavāgama, then 'atha vistare satyagnikāryapaddhatirlikhyate'). It breaks off mid-verse in the rules for the sacrificial animal (paśu), where it distributes the victim's parts to the deities. Muktabodha marks the end 'uncomplete', and there is no final colophon.

SA_MB_uddharakosaHK.title: Uddhārakośa
SA_MB_uddharakosaHK.author: Dakṣiṇāmūrti
SA_MB_uddharakosaHK.summary: The Uddhārakośa is a tantric lexicon (kośa) traditionally attributed to Dakṣiṇāmūrti that decodes esoteric tantric syllabic codes and mantras across seven kalpas.
SA_MB_uddharakosaHK.edition: Raghuvīra and Taki Shodo (eds.), Uddhārakośa śrīdakṣiṇaamūrti viracita (Secondary title: A Dictionary of the Secret Tantric Syllabic Code: Daksinamurti Uddarakosa). Lahore, 1938.
SA_MB_uddharakosaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in seven kalpas, concluding with the saptama kalpa colophon.

SA_MB_kalottaragamaHK.title: Kālottarāgama (incomplete)
SA_MB_kalottaragamaHK.summary: A recension of the Kālottara, a Śaiva Siddhānta scripture treating mantra extraction, worship, yoga, liṅga characteristics, and samaya rules.
SA_MB_kalottaragamaHK.edition: Unpublished transcript: IFP/EFEO transcript T0059, copied from Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (GOML), Madras, MS No. R 14343.
SA_MB_kalottaragamaHK.coverage: partial — Missing ch. 9 to 12; lacking explicit and final colophon; ends with '(īncomplete yāvanmātṛkaṃ likhitam |)'.

SA_MB_satsahasrakalottaragamaHK.title: Ṣaṭsahasrakālottarāgama (selected chapters) with an anthology of extracts from other Āgamas
SA_MB_satsahasrakalottaragamaHK.summary: The e-text begins with selected chapters of the Ṣaṭsahasra ('6,000-verse') recension of the Kālottara, a Śaiva Siddhānta scripture known in recensions of very different length; they deal with Gaṇapati worship, an Aghora ritual (aghorakalpa), the rite of pacification (rudraśānti), the āśramas, astrological suitability (gocara), the conduct of ācāryas and initiates, the examination of the guru and the aṃśaka division. Most of the transcript, however, is a South Indian temple-ritual compilation quoting the Kāraṇa, Sūkṣma, Dīpta, Vijaya and other Āgamas on homa and kuṇḍas, images, liṅgas, installation, festivals and Śivarātri.
SA_MB_satsahasrakalottaragamaHK.attribution: Revealed scriptural work belonging to the Siddhāntatantra / Kālottara corpus of the Śaiva tradition.
SA_MB_satsahasrakalottaragamaHK.edition: Unpublished transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient Transcript No. T0767 (transcribed from IFP MS RE 20294).
SA_MB_satsahasrakalottaragamaHK.coverage: partial — Transcript T0767 pp. 2–158, verses numbered continuously 1–2343. Kālottara section (pp. 2–36, vv. 1–495): opens without title in a passage on maṇḍala and exegesis (vv. 1–2 repeated as 20–21), then chapters with Ṣaṭsahasrikālottara colophons: gaṇapatipūjā, aghorakalpa, rudraśānti, āśrama, gocara (paṭala 14), samayācāra, guruvicāra (16) and aṃśakatālakṣaṇa (17); paṭala numbering is irregular and many chapters of a 6,000-verse work are absent. From v. 496 (p. 36) the text is a compilation on worship, homa, kuṇḍas, iconography, pratiṣṭhā, festivals and Śivarātri, with source rubrics such as 'iti kāraṇe', 'iti bhīmakāraṇe pratiṣṭhātantre vināyakavratavidhipaṭalaḥ', 'sūkṣmatantre', 'dīptatantre', 'iti vijayākhya mahātantre śivarātrividhiḥ'; it ends abruptly at v. 2343 (flower/leaf substitutes in worship) with no colophon.

SA_MB_yogajagamaHK.title: Yogajāgama (selected paṭalas, incomplete)
SA_MB_yogajagamaHK.summary: Ritual āgama text containing ritual procedures, mantras, homa, offerings, and temple/prāsāda dimensions.
SA_MB_yogajagamaHK.edition: No printed edition; unpublished transcription of IFP/EFEO transcript T0024, copied from a manuscript belonging to M.K.S. Bhattar, Madurai (Muktabodha catalog no. M00250).
SA_MB_yogajagamaHK.coverage: partial — IFP/EFEO transcript T. 24 (pp. 1–400). The e-text opens with a stray passage followed by the note 'asamāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ'. It contains ritual chapters (colophon: 'iti yogaje pratiṣṭhātantre mantrāddhāravidhiḥ paṭalaḥ'), breaking off at p. 400 verse 177.

SA_MB_nisvasakarikatantramHK.title: Niśvāsakārikā (chapters 11–53)
SA_MB_nisvasakarikatantramHK.summary: The Niśvāsakārikā is an extensive metrical scripture belonging to the later layer of the Niśvāsa corpus of the Śaiva Mantramārga. Expanding considerably upon the foundational sūtras of the Niśvāsatattvasaṃhitā, it treats theology, cosmology (tattvas, bhuvanas), phonology/mantra theory (varṇa, bindu, nāda), initiation rituals (dīkṣā), and yoga. This e-text transcribes the first volume (pages 1–635, chapters 11–53) of transcript T0017 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry.
SA_MB_nisvasakarikatantramHK.attribution: Anonymous Śaiva scriptural text (Mantramārga / Śaiva Siddhānta), constituting the later metrical expansion associated with the early Niśvāsatattvasaṃhitā corpus.
SA_MB_nisvasakarikatantramHK.edition: Unpublished transcript: IFP transcript T0017A (pp. 1–635), Institut Français de Pondichéry / EFEO; transcribed from a manuscript belonging to M. K. S. Bhattar, Madurai.
SA_MB_nisvasakarikatantramHK.coverage: partial — Covers chapters 11 through 53, corresponding to pages 1–635 of IFP transcript T0017A. The remainder of the transcript continues in T0017B.

SA_MB_lalitaagamaHK.title: Lalitāgama
SA_MB_lalitaagamaHK.summary: The Lalitāgama is an Āgama text dealing with ritual subjects, including temple installation, rites of passage and initiation, and temple ceremonies.
SA_MB_lalitaagamaHK.edition: Transcribed from IFP transcript T0202 which is copied from a manuscript of Swaminatha Gurukkal Tiruvanadudurai; digitized by the staff of Muktabodha under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski.
SA_MB_lalitaagamaHK.coverage: unclear — Transcribed from IFP transcript T0202.

SA_MB_viiraagamaHK.title: Vīrāgama (paṭalas 1–89 and beginning of 90)
SA_MB_viiraagamaHK.summary: The Vīrāgama (Vīratantra, 'Ṣaṭsahasrasaṃhitā') is one of the 28 Mūlāgamas of the Śaiva Siddhānta. The transcribed text, a Brahmā–Īśvara dialogue, covers mantroddhāra, ācārya qualifications, dīkṣā and abhiṣeka, the domestic saṃskāras from garbhādhāna to funerary rites, daily worship, mudrās, homa, festivals and expiations, and an extensive series of installation (pratiṣṭhā/sthāpana) and snapana rites for Śiva, Gaurī, Skanda, Jyeṣṭhā and other deities.
SA_MB_viiraagamaHK.attribution: Anonymous Śaiva Siddhānta scripture, counted among the 28 Mūlāgamas; the colophons call it Vīratantra in 6,000 verses (ṣaṭsahasrasaṃhitā).
SA_MB_viiraagamaHK.edition: Unpublished transcription of IFP transcript T0029, copied from a manuscript from Kilvelūr, with an appended chapter from a Tiruvāvaḍuturai manuscript (Muktabodha catalog no. M00253).
SA_MB_viiraagamaHK.coverage: partial — IFP/EFEO transcript T0029. Chapter colophons run consecutively up to 89 (agrāśanavidhi) and paṭala 90 is incomplete; followed by an appended fuller version of the Kumārasthāpanavidhi from a Tiruvāvaḍuturai manuscript ending 'iti śrī vīratantre ṣaṭsahasrasaṃhitāyāṃ guhasthāpanavidhipaṭalaḥ'.

SA_MB_saivasiddhantaparibhasamanjariHK.title: Śaivasiddhāntaparibhāṣāmañjarī
SA_MB_saivasiddhantaparibhasamanjariHK.author: Vedajñāna
SA_MB_saivasiddhantaparibhasamanjariHK.summary: The Śaivasiddhāntaparibhāṣāmañjarī (also referred to in the closing colophon as Paryāyamañjarī) by Vedajñāna / Nigamajñānadeva is a versified terminological manual and digest of the Śaiva Siddhānta tradition. Arranged enumeratively in ten sections (vargas/sargas) covering groups of items from one to ten, it systematically outlines theological, ritual, and philosophical doctrines of Saiddhāntika dualism.
SA_MB_saivasiddhantaparibhasamanjariHK.attribution: Authored by Nigamajñānadeva (pupil of Nigamajñānaśivayogin of Puṇḍarīkapura). Muktabodha headers attribute the text to Vedajñāna.
SA_MB_saivasiddhantaparibhasamanjariHK.edition: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T0171 (copied from a manuscript belonging to śiva śri elukarai nātthu namabi sadāśivapaṇḍita sivācāryar maṭhādhipati ṭirueehengodu).
SA_MB_saivasiddhantaparibhasamanjariHK.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising the upodghāta (introductory section) and ten vargas/sargas (chapters 1–10), concluding with the final colophon.

SA_MB_mrgendravrttidiipikaHK.title: Mṛgendravṛttidīpikā (fragment)
SA_MB_mrgendravrttidiipikaHK.author: Aghoraśivācārya
SA_MB_mrgendravrttidiipikaHK.summary: The Mṛgendravṛttidīpikā is a sub-commentary (dīpikā) by Aghoraśivācārya on Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha's Vṛtti to the Mṛgendratantra. This e-text is an incomplete transcription of IFP transcript T0265, breaking off abruptly.
SA_MB_mrgendravrttidiipikaHK.attribution: Aghoraśivācārya provides a sub-commentary (dīpikā) on Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha's Mṛgendravṛtti.
SA_MB_mrgendravrttidiipikaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription: IFP transcript T0265 (copied from S.V.U. Oriental Research Institute, Tirupati, ms. no. 6409).
SA_MB_mrgendravrttidiipikaHK.coverage: fragment — Only a short portion of the commentary is present; breaks off abruptly mid-sentence ('ataśca śabdetaratve').

SA_MB_prodgitagamaHK.title: Prodgītāgama (chapters 25–26: Vivāhavidhi)
SA_MB_prodgitagamaHK.summary: A liturgical section comprising chapters 25 and 26 of the Prodgītāgama, one of the 28 canonical Śaiva Siddhānta Āgamas. The two chapters describe the marriage ritual (Vivāhavidhi): chapter 25 recounts the mythological wedding of Śiva and Pārvatī, while chapter 26 details the ritual procedures for temple divine marriage ceremonies (kalyāṇotsava).
SA_MB_prodgitagamaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T0201 (copied from an original manuscript belonging to Swaminatha Gurukkal, Tiruvavadudurai).
SA_MB_prodgitagamaHK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters 25 and 26 (pañcaviṃśati and ṣaḍviṃśati paṭalas), both titled Vivāhavidhi.

SA_MB_siddhalaksmipujapaddhatiHK.title: Siddhalakṣmīpūjāpaddhati
SA_MB_siddhalaksmipujapaddhatiHK.summary: The Siddhalakṣmīpūjāpaddhati is a Kashmiri Śākta ritual manual detailing the worship (pūjā), nyāsas, mantras, and visualization for the goddess Siddhalakṣmī (also addressed as Kulavāgīśvarī). This manuscript codex additionally gathers shorter procedural texts for related regional Kashmiri goddesses and deities, including Vanadurgā, Gaurī, Śārikā, Śāradā, Svacchandabhairava (Svacchandapatrikā), and Śivarātrivrata.
SA_MB_siddhalaksmipujapaddhatiHK.attribution: A Kashmiri Śākta/Śaiva ritual compilation preserved in manuscript form; the individual liturgical manuals are anonymous.
SA_MB_siddhalaksmipujapaddhatiHK.edition: Manuscript transcription: Srinagar, Kashmir Research Centre, Ms. Acc. No. 2376 (Serial No. 936, items 2376.1–2376.12).
SA_MB_siddhalaksmipujapaddhatiHK.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic/manuscript transcription of Kashmir Research Centre manuscript Acc. No. 2376 (items 2376.1–2376.12), comprising the Saṃkṣiptā Siddhalakṣmīpūjāpaddhati and related liturgical texts.

SA_MB_timirodghataHK.title: Timirodghāṭatantra (paṭalas 1–12, with other texts from the same manuscript)
SA_MB_timirodghataHK.summary: A transcription of an incomplete manuscript from the NGMPP (access no. 5/690 reel no. A 1380/9) containing an Arjuna–Kṛṣṇa dialogue followed by the Timirodghāṭatantra (Timirodghāṭana), a Śaiva tantric text.
SA_MB_timirodghataHK.edition: Unpublished transcription of NGMPP access no. 5/690 reel no. A 1380/9 (Muktabodha catalog no. M00258).
SA_MB_timirodghataHK.coverage: partial — Composite NGMPP manuscript (access no. 5/690, reel no. A 1380/9). The e-text opens with an Arjuna–Kṛṣṇa dialogue framed by Saṃjaya, followed by the Timirodghāṭana (with a colophon for paṭala 2: 'iti timirodghāṭanai dvitīyaḥ paṭalaḥ'). Described as incomplete.

SA_MB_pauskarasamhitaHK.title: Pauṣkarasaṃhitā
SA_MB_pauskarasamhitaHK.summary: The Pauṣkarasaṃhitā is one of the principal canonical scriptures of the Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra tradition, revered alongside the Sāttvatasaṃhitā and Jayākhyasaṃhitā as one of the 'Three Gems' (ratnatraya). Across 43 chapters, it provides detailed instructions on ritual diagrams (maṇḍala), initiatory grades (samayī, putraka, sādhaka), installation (pratiṣṭhā), iconography, temple architecture, and caturvyūha theology. It is a major classical source for Śrīvaiṣṇava temple liturgy and ritual philosophy.
SA_MB_pauskarasamhitaHK.attribution: A revealed canonical saṃhitā of the Pāñcarātra tradition.
SA_MB_pauskarasamhitaHK.edition: Śrī Yātirāja Sampatkumāra Rāmānujamuni (ed.), pauṣkara saṃhitā one of the three gems of the pañjarātra, Bangalore: A. Śrīnivāsa and M. C. Thirumalachariar, 1934.
SA_MB_pauskarasamhitaHK.coverage: partial — Lacking explicit and final colophon; ends abruptly at 43.205 with the editor's bracketed note '[etāvadavadhireva grantho labdhaḥ]' (pp. 1–272 of the 1934 edition).

SA_MB_stutikusumaanjaliHK.title: Stutikusumāñjali with Premamakaranda
SA_MB_stutikusumaanjaliHK.author: Jagaddhara Bhaṭṭa, Premavallabha Tripāṭhī
SA_MB_stutikusumaanjaliHK.summary: The Stutikusumāñjali is a Śaiva devotional work by the Kashmiri poet Jagaddhara Bhaṭṭa, comprising 38 hymns dedicated to Śiva. This e-text presents the work accompanied by prose word-order (anvaya) and the Sanskrit commentary Premamakaranda by Premavallabha Tripāṭhī.
SA_MB_stutikusumaanjaliHK.attribution: Premavallabha Tripāṭhī, a disciple of Svāmī Hariharānanda Sarasvatī (Karapātrī Jī Mahārāja), composed the Sanskrit commentary Premamakaranda along with anvaya.
SA_MB_stutikusumaanjaliHK.edition: Stutikusumāñjaliḥ, kāśmīrakamahākaviśrīmajjagaddharabhaṭṭaviracitaḥ, Tripāṭhyupāhva-Premavallabhaśarmaṇā kṛtayā Premamakarandanāmnyā ṭīkayā sametaḥ, Benares: Sanskrit Book Depot, 1939.
SA_MB_stutikusumaanjaliHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 38 stotras with anvaya and Premavallabha Tripāṭhī's Premamakaranda commentary.

SA_MB_satcakranirnayaHK.title: Ṣaṭcakranirṇaya
SA_MB_satcakranirnayaHK.summary: An anonymous Kaula/Tantric yoga treatise on subtle-body physiology centered on the standard schema of the six cakras (ṣaṭcakra), sixteen bodily supports (ṣoḍaśādhāra), three gazing targets (trilakṣya), and five internal spaces (vyomapañcaka). The work combines kārikā verses with prose explanation and comparative citations ('anyaśāstrābhiprāyaḥ'), concluding with a stuti section. It is distinct from Pūrṇānanda's well-known Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa.
SA_MB_satcakranirnayaHK.attribution: An anonymous Kaula subtle-body yoga treatise, distinct from Pūrṇānanda's Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa.
SA_MB_satcakranirnayaHK.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription based on manuscript BHU C4253.
SA_MB_satcakranirnayaHK.coverage: partial — Lacks an explicit and closing colophon; the transcription of manuscript BHU C4253 ends after phalaśruti verse 62 without a formal concluding statement.

SA_MB_brahmasandhanaHK.title: Brahmasandhāna (incomplete)
SA_MB_brahmasandhanaHK.summary: An anonymous Śaiva yoga text in which Śiva instructs Skanda. It covers the subtle body (the nine doors, nāḍīs such as piṅgalā and suṣumṇā, the vital winds), the 'joining to brahman' (brahmasandhāna) through the brahmadvāra, and yogic exit at death (utkrānti). It also treats the cosmogony from cicchakti, the composition of the human body, the nāda as brahman, and a purely mental worship (mānasayāga) with bathing at the inner Śivatīrtha. It closes with an internal fire worship (agnipūjā), in which the five breaths are offered into the fire in the heart.
SA_MB_brahmasandhanaHK.attribution: Anonymous; a dialogue in which Śiva (Īśvara) teaches Skanda (addressed as Guha, Śikhidhvaja, Śikhivāhana).
SA_MB_brahmasandhanaHK.coverage: partial — The text begins at verse 5, contains internal breaks/lacunae, and ends with the colophon 'iti śrībrahmasandhānāgni * jā * cā * ni * yo * mā'.

SA_MB_candrajnanaHK.title: Candrajñānāgama
SA_MB_candrajnanaHK.summary: The Candrajñānāgama (or Candrajñāna) is a Śaiva revealed text framed as a teaching imparted on Mount Kailāsa by Śiva (Bhairava) to Candra. Distressed by the transient and illusory nature of worldly phenomena (māyā, indrajāla) and questioning the efficacy of conventional ritual and verbalized mantras, Candra receives esoteric instruction resolving these doubts into transcendent non-dual awareness. This digital text represents a diplomatic transcription of Banaras Hindu University MS C4243 (fols. 55a–67b).
SA_MB_candrajnanaHK.attribution: Canonical Śaiva scripture presented as an esoteric dialogue between Śiva (Maheśvara/Bhairava) and Candra.
SA_MB_candrajnanaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Banaras Hindu University MS C4243, fols. 55a–67b (Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, E-text M00263).
SA_MB_candrajnanaHK.coverage: partial — Transcription of Banaras Hindu University manuscript C4243, fols. 55a–67b; lacks an explicit and closing colophon, terminating at verse 42.

SA_MB_hamsasaraHK.title: Haṃsasāra
SA_MB_hamsasaraHK.summary: A short Kaula tantric tract in 44 verses framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Maheśvarī, purporting to deliver the inner essence of the Haṃsayāmala. It expounds the nature of the supreme Haṃsa as the all-pervading, vibrant (spandana) consciousness dwelling in all embodied creatures, deals with the signs of death (kālajñāna), and presents esoteric yogic practice leading to jīvanmukti within the Yoginīkula tradition.
SA_MB_hamsasaraHK.attribution: Tantric revelation framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Maheśvarī, presented as extracting the quintessence of the Haṃsayāmala.
SA_MB_hamsasaraHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Banaras Hindu University MS C4244, fols. 68b–72b (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_hamsasaraHK.coverage: unclear — Contains 44 verses preserved on fols. 68b–72b of Banaras Hindu University MS C4244; verse 44 serves as an internal concluding injunction, but the text lacks a final scribal colophon/explicit.

SA_MB_jnanasaraHK.title: Jñānasāra
SA_MB_jnanasaraHK.summary: The Jñānasāra (also titled Nāthajñānasāra) is an anonymous Śaiva-Nātha dialogue between Śiva and Devī concerning the emergence of speech (vāk), mind (manas), and the vital breath (prāṇa). It expounds the nature, bodily loci, and guṇa-manifestations of the individual soul (jīva), yogic practices such as khecarīmudrā and bandhas, contrasting mere textual recitation with the realization of the partless absolute (niṣkala brahma).
SA_MB_jnanasaraHK.attribution: A short anonymous Śaiva dialogue between Śiva and the Goddess (Devī), designated 'nāthajñānasāra' in the opening line.
SA_MB_jnanasaraHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Banaras Hindu University Library MS C4251.
SA_MB_jnanasaraHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete manuscript transcription of BHU MS C4251 (covering folios/pages marked p. 174a to p. 178b); ends abruptly after verse 17 without an explicit or final colophon.

SA_MB_niruttaravadaHK.title: Niruttaravāda
SA_MB_niruttaravadaHK.summary: An esoteric Śaiva/Śākta doctrinal work that expounds the realization of the unsurpassed supreme reality (niruttara). Presenting an effortless path (āyāsarahitaṃ jñānam) transcending external ritual, prāṇāyāma, and mental constructs, it articulates radical nondual awareness through apophatic discourse and traditional analogies.
SA_MB_niruttaravadaHK.attribution: Anonymous nondual Śaiva/Śākta esoteric text presented as part of a Paramarahasya dialogue.
SA_MB_niruttaravadaHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the text preserved in BHU Ms. C4247, folios 93b–116b.

SA_MB_nirvanayogottaraHK.title: Nirvāṇayogottara
SA_MB_nirvanayogottaraHK.summary: A short Śaiva yoga text of 90 anuṣṭubh verses structured as an instruction delivered by Bhagavān to Guha. It details internal breath retention (pūraka and kumbhaka), cessation of mental fluctuation (niścala citta), the contemplation of voidness (triśūnya, sāmarasya), five symbolic mudrās, and the synthesis of ascetic vows (vrata) with yoga practice leading to liberation (mokṣa).
SA_MB_nirvanayogottaraHK.attribution: Cast as a divine dialogue between the Bhagavān (Śiva) and his son Guha; no human author is named.
SA_MB_nirvanayogottaraHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Banaras Hindu University manuscript BHU C4246 (fols. 86a–93a), transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00267).
SA_MB_nirvanayogottaraHK.coverage: complete — Complete short tract of 90 verses as preserved in MS BHU C4246 (fols. 86a–93a), ending with the final concluding statement, a damaged colophon string (transcribing [iti] śrī-nirvāṇayogottaraṃ samāptam), and the closing benediction 'śivaṃ bhavatu'.

SA_MB_pranagnihotraHK.title: Prāṇāgnihotra (incomplete)
SA_MB_pranagnihotraHK.summary: A short anonymous Śaiva text in verse and prose on the 'agnihotra in the breath' (prāṇāgnihotra), taught by Śiva to Ṣaṇmukha for people who cannot afford the Vedic fire ritual. It maps the elements of the sacrifice onto the body, its faculties and the cosmos. It then describes the vital breaths and their deities, and the eating of food as an inner fire offering. The surviving text breaks off in this section.
SA_MB_pranagnihotraHK.attribution: An anonymous Śaiva dialogue. Ṣaṇmukha (Skanda) asks Śiva (addressed as Śūlabhṛt) for the prāṇāgnihotra on behalf of 'alpavittā narāḥ' who cannot keep the Vedic agnihotra, and Śiva answers. Its question list ('śarīre'smin katy agnayaḥ, ko yajamānaḥ, kā patnī ...') belongs to the tradition of the inner, bodily fire sacrifice. No source for the text was identified.
SA_MB_pranagnihotraHK.edition: Unedited manuscript: Banaras Hindu University Library MS BHU C4257. Transcription of the manuscript.
SA_MB_pranagnihotraHK.coverage: partial — Transcription of a short text within a manuscript, BHU C4257 (beginning at leaf marker 'p. 251a)'). The e-text ends mid-word with 'sa', with no closing colophon. ilx_skt metadata: 'incomplete', colophon 'no'.

SA_MB_subodhamanjariHK.title: Subodhamañjarī
SA_MB_subodhamanjariHK.author: Vāmanadatta
SA_MB_subodhamanjariHK.summary: The Subodhamañjarī (also referred to in verse 44 as Svabodhodayamañjarī) is a short Sanskrit treatise in 44 verses by Vāmanadatta, son of the Mīmāṃsaka Harṣadatta. It outlines an effortless method of mental absorption (samāveśa / nirodha) by dissolving sensory perceptions into the nature of the self (ātman), leading to jīvanmukti.
SA_MB_subodhamanjariHK.attribution: Verse 44 names the author as Vāmanadatta, son of Harṣadatta ('mīmāṃsāvanasiṃha').
SA_MB_subodhamanjariHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of Banaras Hindu University MS BHU C4255, folios 245a–248b (unpublished transcription).
SA_MB_subodhamanjariHK.coverage: complete — Complete short tract in 44 anuṣṭubh verses, from the opening maṅgala through the authorial signature in verse 44.

SA_MB_sukavakyaHK.title: Śukavākya
SA_MB_sukavakyaHK.summary: The Śukavākya is a didactic dialogue in Purāṇic verse recounting an exchange between the sage Vyāsa and his son Śuka. Narrated within a traditional frame addressed to King Janamejaya, Śuka describes the suffering and transience of saṃsāra, detailing his past incarnations across various animal and plant forms, before reflecting on dispassion (vairāgya), devotion, and release from rebirth.
SA_MB_sukavakyaHK.attribution: A traditional didactic dialogue framed between King Janamejaya and an interlocutor, recounting an exchange between Vyāsa and his son Śuka.
SA_MB_sukavakyaHK.edition: Banaras Hindu University Library (BHU), MS C4252, pp./ff. 181a–192a (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_sukavakyaHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete manuscript transcription; ff. 189–190 are missing in the manuscript, and the text breaks off mid-verse at v. 20 on p. 192a without an explicit or closing colophon.

SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaHK.title: Vijñānabhairava
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaHK.summary: The Vijñānabhairava is a celebrated nondual Śaiva tantric scripture of the Trika tradition, cast as a dialogue between Bhairava and the Goddess (Bhairavī). In response to questions on the ultimate nature of reality beyond ritual forms and dualistic concepts, Bhairava presents 112 dhāraṇās (meditative centering practices) utilizing the breath, void, sound, sensory perception, and direct nondual awareness to realize spontaneous identity with divine consciousness.
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaHK.attribution: Revealed scriptural tantra traditionally presented as an excerpt or essence of the Rudrayāmala.
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaHK.edition: Banaras Hindu University Library, Manuscript BHU C4245, folios 73a–85b (diplomatic transcription)
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaHK.coverage: partial — Transcribed from folios 73a–85b of BHU manuscript C4245; the text preserves the verse sequence up to the traditional concluding verse (ityuktvā nanditā devī kaṇṭhe lagnā śivasya tu), but lacks a closing scribal colophon or explicit.
translations: Jaideva Singh, Vijñānabhairava or Divine Consciousness: A Treasury of 112 Types of Yoga, Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1979. (English)
Lilian Silburn, Le Vijñāna Bhairava, Paris: 1961. (French)

SA_MB_acintyavisvasadakhyaHK.title: Acintyaviśvasādākhya
SA_MB_acintyavisvasadakhyaHK.summary: The Acintyaviśvasādākhya is an Upāgama belonging to the Cintyāgama cycle within the Śaiva Siddhānta canon. It deals with āgamic ritual (kriyā), ascetic and daily observances (caryā, dāsamārga, putramārga, sahamārga), temple worship, nyāsa, and prāsādamantra theology. The e-text preserves a direct transcription of the IFP/EFEO transcripts T0007A and T0007B.
SA_MB_acintyavisvasadakhyaHK.attribution: Scriptural text presented as divine revelation.
SA_MB_acintyavisvasadakhyaHK.edition: Transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO) transcripts T0007A and T0007B.
SA_MB_acintyavisvasadakhyaHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of IFP/EFEO transcripts T0007A and T0007B through to the final closing formula ('... midaṃ samāptamāsīt'), though final verses and the closing colophon are partially illegible with lacunae.

SA_MB_candrajnanagamaHK.title: Candrajñānāgama (selected chapters)
SA_MB_candrajnanagamaHK.summary: A Śaiva Siddhānta text (upāgama / pratiṣṭhātantra) dealing with ritual worship, mantras (such as the pañcākṣara), installations (including Mahālakṣmī), festivals and offerings, observances, impurity rules (āśauca), and ending with a jñānadarśanapaṭala.
SA_MB_candrajnanagamaHK.attribution: Muktabodha describes Candrajñāna as a Siddhānta upāgama which defines itself as a pratiṣṭhātantra dealing with ritual procedures concerning the installation and worship of representations of Śaiva deities, including liṅgas.
SA_MB_candrajnanagamaHK.coverage: incomplete — IFP/EFEO transcript T0012 (catalogued as incomplete in ilx_skt). The transcript ends with the colophon 'iti candrajñāne jñānadarśanapaṭalaḥ samāptam' followed by the name 'es ār śivasubrahmaṇyaṃśāstriṇaḥ'.

SA_MB_kulalasastraHK.title: Kulālaśāstra
SA_MB_kulalasastraHK.summary: A ritual manual associated with the Kulāla (potter) tradition and the worship of Śāstā (identified in the header description with Skanda), structured as an Āgamic/Tantric revelation through Kulālaṛṣi. It contains ritual procedures (vidhi) including pratiṣṭhā, purificatory rites, and related observances.
SA_MB_kulalasastraHK.attribution: Revealed through Kulālaṛṣi; colophon also mentions īśvaraprokte śāstrāgame.
SA_MB_kulalasastraHK.edition: Unpublished transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO) transcript T0452.
SA_MB_kulalasastraHK.coverage: complete — Transcription of IFP/EFEO transcript T0452.

SA_MB_unmattabhairavaHK.title: Unmattabhairavahṛdaya
SA_MB_unmattabhairavaHK.summary: The Unmattabhairavahṛdaya is a Śaiva tantric ritual manual focused on Unmatta Bhairava, one of the classical eight Bhairavas (Aṣṭabhairava). Claimed in its colophon to belong to the Pārameśvaratantra (Vārāṇasīpaṭala), the text presents instructions for drawing the yantra (yantroddhāra), the kīlaka, nyāsa, dhyāna, and the protective 'heart' recitation (hṛdaya), along with standard tantric applications (ṣaṭkarman) such as māraṇa, vaśīkaraṇa, and uccāṭana.
SA_MB_unmattabhairavaHK.attribution: Ascribed in the colophon to the Vārāṇasīpaṭala (Unmattabhairavopākhyāna) of the Pārameśvaratantra.
SA_MB_unmattabhairavaHK.edition: Diplomatic transcript of Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient transcript T1020 (IFP/EFEO transcript T1020).
SA_MB_unmattabhairavaHK.coverage: complete — Complete ritual text as preserved in IFP/EFEO transcript T1020, comprising the yantroddhāra, kīlaka, nyāsa, dhyāna, gāyatrī, and the hṛdaya hymn ending with verse 54 and colophon.

SA_MB_umasamhitaHK.title: Umāsaṃhitā
SA_MB_umasamhitaHK.summary: The Umāsaṃhitā preserved in this transcript is a Purāṇic narrative text recounting dialogues regarding the liberating efficacy of the Rāmamantra (Tāraka mantra) at Kāśī, the observance of Rāmanavamī, and illustrative moral tales such as that of the brāhmaṇa Vidyādhara. It is distinct from the well-known fifth book (Umāsaṃhitā) of the Śivapurāṇa.
SA_MB_umasamhitaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T0081, copied by Naṭarājaśarman from Adyar Library Grantha palm-leaf manuscript MS 73868.
SA_MB_umasamhitaHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete; lacks a final colophon or explicit for the Umāsaṃhitā. Breaks off after a Rāmamāhātmya and dhyāna section, concluding directly with the modern scribe's note.

SA_MB_bhavachudamaniHK.title: Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi (incomplete: fols. 1a–15a)
SA_MB_bhavachudamaniHK.summary: This is a tantric text in the form of a dialogue in which Bhairava questions the Goddess. Its prose opening says that mantras do not succeed without bhāva. The text covers lineages of gurus, deities including Kālikā, and the disposition of practitioners, breaking off in the discussion of paśubhāva.
SA_MB_bhavachudamaniHK.attribution: The Muktabodha catalogue (M00277) gives the author as Vidyākaṇṭha. However, the text itself is an anonymous tantric revelation structured as a dialogue between Bhairava and Devī.
SA_MB_bhavachudamaniHK.edition: Unedited manuscript: NGMCP 6/1748 reel number A 989/23 (transcription of fols. 1a–15a).
SA_MB_bhavachudamaniHK.coverage: partial — Transcription of fols. 1a–15a of NGMCP 6/1748 (reel A 989/23), with folio markers 'p. 1a)' to 'p. 15a)'. It breaks off mid-verse ('yathāvidhi paśorddāṃ'), with no final colophon.

SA_MB_kriyakalagunottaramHK.title: Kriyākālaguṇottara (incomplete)
SA_MB_kriyakalagunottaramHK.summary: The Kriyākālaguṇottara is an early Śaiva scriptural tantra surviving in early Nepalese palm-leaf manuscripts, representing the Mantramārga traditions of Gāruḍatantra (anti-venom and snakebite healing) and Bhūtatantra (exorcism and protection from spirits). It details serpent classifications, signs of envenomation, prognostic omens, therapeutic mantras, protective mandalas, and medicinal preparations.
SA_MB_kriyakalagunottaramHK.attribution: A traditional scriptural text presented as a dialogue between Kārttikeya and Śiva/Īśvara.
SA_MB_kriyakalagunottaramHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript 3/392 (reel B 25/32), folios 1a–141b (unpublished).
SA_MB_kriyakalagunottaramHK.coverage: partial — Transcription of NAK 3-392 (NGMPP B 25/32), fols. 1a-141b with continuous foliation. Begins with the opening maṅgala and Kārttikeya's questions; contains paṭalas on nāga classes, bhūta, Khaḍgarāvaṇa and other kalpas, jvara, child-diseases, rakṣā, ḍākinīs, gonasa, lūtā, śvāna-bites etc.; breaks off in a medical recipe on fol. 141a, fol. 141b is marked "not clear", with no final colophon.

SA_MB_diiksottaraHK.title: Niśvāsakārikā (Dīkṣottaraprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_diiksottaraHK.summary: The Dīkṣottaraprakaraṇa constitutes the concluding nineteen-chapter section of the Niśvāsakārikā, an early metrical scripture of the Niśvāsa corpus of the Mantramārga. It systematically covers the rites and theology of tantric initiation (dīkṣā), the purification of the six cosmic pathways (ṣaḍadhvan), and interiorized yogic absorptions (lakṣya). The work represents an indispensable transitional witness for the development of classical Śaivasiddhānta ritual liturgy.
SA_MB_diiksottaraHK.attribution: Early Śaivasiddhānta scripture belonging to the Niśvāsa corpus of Mantramārga Śaivism.
SA_MB_diiksottaraHK.edition: Pondicherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry, Transcript T0017B, pp. 795–1152 (unpublished Devanagari manuscript transcript).
SA_MB_diiksottaraHK.coverage: partial — Complete text of the Dīkṣottaraprakaraṇa (chapters 1–19, corresponding to pp. 795–1152 of IFP Transcript T0017B), which forms the final section of the Niśvāsakārikā.

SA_MB_nisvaasakaarikaatantram1HK.title: Niśvāsakārikā (chapters 11–53)
SA_MB_nisvaasakaarikaatantram1HK.summary: The Niśvāsakārikā is an extensive metrical scripture belonging to Śaiva literature. It details phonological cosmology (mātṛkā, praṇava, bindu, nāda), initiation rituals (dīkṣā), and yoga. This e-text transcribes the first transcript volume preserved at the French Institute of Pondicherry (IFP T0017A), comprising chapters 11 through 53.
SA_MB_nisvaasakaarikaatantram1HK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry transcript IFP T0017A (pp. 1–635), input under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (Digital Library text M00280, Revision 0: December 16, 2013).
SA_MB_nisvaasakaarikaatantram1HK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters (paṭalas) 11 through 53 (pp. 1–635 of IFP Transcript T0017A). Chapters 1–10 are missing from this transcript, and the remainder of the work continues in IFP Transcript T0017B.

SA_MB_yogapiithakramodayaHK.title: Yogapīṭhakramodaya
SA_MB_yogapiithakramodayaHK.summary: The Yogapīṭhakramodaya (also titled Kramodaya) is an early Kaula work influenced by the Kubjikā tradition. Preserved in manuscript witness NGMCP 4-31 /vi (reel A4319) dated Saṃvat 307, the work deals with Kaula tantric and yogapīṭha ritual and esoteric subjects across multiple paṭalas.
SA_MB_yogapiithakramodayaHK.attribution: Scriptural Kaula tantric text. The colophon names Mahādeva as the scribe who copied the manuscript in Saṃvat 307.
SA_MB_yogapiithakramodayaHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript 4-31 /vi (reel A4319), dated Saṃvat 307, prepared by Muktabodha staff under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (catalog no. M00281).
SA_MB_yogapiithakramodayaHK.coverage: complete — Text complete, MS incomplete according to the catalog metadata; includes the scribal colophon dated Saṃvat 307 and appended verses mentioning Kubjikā.

SA_MB_kamakalavilasaHK.title: Kāmakalāvilāsa with Cidvallī
SA_MB_kamakalavilasaHK.author: Puṇyānanda, Naṭanānanda
SA_MB_kamakalavilasaHK.summary: The Kāmakalāvilāsa is a foundational doctrinal treatise of the Śrīvidyā tradition of Śākta Tantra, attributed to Puṇyānandanātha. In 55 verses, it sets forth the non-dual metaphysics of Kāmakalā—the creative pulsation and self-manifestation of pure consciousness (Prakāśa-Vimarśa / Śiva-Śakti)—and elaborates the esoteric emergence and symbolic structure of the Śrīcakra and the fifteen-syllabled mantra (Kādimata / Hādimata). The text is accompanied by the Cidvallī, the classic Sanskrit commentary by Naṭanānanda, which elucidates its dense philosophical vocabulary and meditative correspondences.
SA_MB_kamakalavilasaHK.attribution: Puṇyānanda is credited with the root kārikās; Naṭanānanda composed the Cidvallī commentary.
SA_MB_kamakalavilasaHK.edition: Kāmakalāvilāsa of Puṇyānanda with the Commentary Cidvallī by Naṭanānanda, ed. Sudhakar Malaviya, electronic typesetting files (New York: Sudhakar Malaviya, 2005), digitized by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00282).
SA_MB_kamakalavilasaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Kāmakalāvilāsa (55 verses) together with Naṭanānanda's complete Cidvallī commentary, ending with the closing colophon: 'iti śrīnaṭanānandakṛtaṃ kāmakalācidvallīvyākhyānaṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_MB_haharavatantraHK.title: Hāhārāvatantra
SA_MB_haharavatantraHK.summary: The Hāhārāvatantra is a Nepalese Śākta-Kaula tantra affiliated with the Atharvaveda tradition (Atharvaṇasaṃhitā), centering on the worship of Kaula goddesses with an emphasis on Guhyakālī and Pratyaṅgirā. The text details dhyānas, yantras, a thousand names (sahasranāma) of Guhyakālī, protective hymns (kavaca), indrajāla and other magical rites, and Kaula ritual worship using sacrificial vessels (pātras). It survives primarily in Kathmandu Valley manuscript collections.
SA_MB_haharavatantraHK.attribution: Canonical Śākta-Kaula tantric scripture presenting itself as an Atharvaṇasaṃhitā (associated with the Atharvaveda tradition).
SA_MB_haharavatantraHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Nepalese manuscript catalogued as NGMCP 5-4798 (reel no. A 204/6), data-entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, e-text M00283, 2003/2011).
SA_MB_haharavatantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript up to the concluding colophon (catalog records note 18 chapters; description notes chapters up to chapter 15).

SA_MB_kulanandadiHK.title: Kulānanda, with Kapālalakṣaṇa from the Picumata and fragments of Kaula ritual texts
SA_MB_kulanandadiHK.author: Matsyendranātha
SA_MB_kulanandadiHK.summary: A transcription of a Kaula manuscript (NGMCP 1-1376/ v). It opens with the Kulānanda, a dialogue attributed to Matsyendranātha dealing with Kaula Yoga, subtle body piercing (vedha), and the rising of Kuṇḍalinī. This is followed by a section on the characteristics of skull-bowls (kapāla) drawn from the Picumata (Brahmayāmala), and prescriptions for Kaula rituals addressing goddesses including Kubjikā, Kālasaṃkarṣiṇī, Bhagamālinī, and Kāmeśvarī.
SA_MB_kulanandadiHK.attribution: The Kulānanda colophon reads 'iti matsyendrapādāvatārikaṃ kulānandasamāptam'. The skull-bowl passage has the colophon 'iti kapālakṣaṇaṃ picumate', referring to the Picumata / Brahmayāmala. The ritual sections are anonymous.
SA_MB_kulanandadiHK.edition: Manuscript NGMCP 1-1376/ v reel number A40/6.
SA_MB_kulanandadiHK.coverage: partial — A collection of fragments marked 'īncomplete' at the end. Contains the Kulānanda (first 7 folios), a 4-folio passage on kapāla from the Picumata, and ritual texts ending after 'bhairava vali'.

SA_MB_KulasaaraHK.title: Kulasārasaṃgraha (chapters 24–26), Kulācāranirṇaya (chapters 1–5) and Antyeṣṭikrama (ullāsa 18)
SA_MB_KulasaaraHK.summary: A manuscript labelled Kulasāra containing fragments of three Kaula works in Tantra format: chapters 24–26 of Kaulsārasaṃgraha (part of Somabhujavalī), chapters 1–5 of Kulācāranirṇaya, and chapter 18 of a work belonging to the Śrīvidyā lineage of Subhagānandanātha dealing with the funerary rites (antyeṣṭi) of a Kaula. Muktabodha dates such Kaula works to after the 13th century.
SA_MB_KulasaaraHK.attribution: According to Muktabodha, the manuscript is a collection of fragments of three Kaula tracts in the format of Tantras outlining Kaula ritual and practice, belonging to the period after the 13th century. After the final chapter, a note reports that in the view of Subhagānandanātha (subhagānandanāthamate tu) it cannot be said whether this 18th ullāsa was spoken by Īśvara or composed by ācāryas. The manuscript text concludes with 'samvat 1929 śubham'.
SA_MB_KulasaaraHK.coverage: fragment — Manuscript NGMCP 3-251 reel number A 150/16 contains fragments of three Kaula works: Kaulsārasaṃgraha (begins with chapter 24 and extends up to chapter 26), Kulācāranirṇaya (chapters 1 to 5), and an 18th ullāsa dealing with funerary rites of a Kaula ('iti tatvāmarśāṃtyaṣṭikramaḥ aṣṭādaśollāsaḥ saṃpūrṇaṃ'), ending with 'samvat 1929 śubham'.

SA_MB_ascaryayogamalaHK.title: Āścaryayogamālā with Laghuvṛtti
SA_MB_ascaryayogamalaHK.author: Nāgārjuna, Guṇākara
SA_MB_ascaryayogamalaHK.summary: The Āścaryayogamālā ('Rosary of Wondrous Recipes/Applications'), also known as Yogaratnamālā or Yogaratnāvalī, is a medieval manual of magic and occult recipes (ṣaṭkarman) attributed to Nāgārjuna. It details preparations and spells for subjugation (vaśīkaraṇa), immobilization (stambhana), and other powers. It is accompanied by the concise commentary (Laghuvṛtti) of the Śvetāmbara Jaina scholar Guṇākara.
SA_MB_ascaryayogamalaHK.attribution: Ascribed to Nāgārjuna, a legendary figure associated with medieval tantric magic (ṣaṭkarman). The commentary (Laghuvṛtti) is explicitly authored by the Śvetāmbara Jaina paṇḍita Guṇākara (iti śrīśvetāmbarapaṇḍitaguṇākaraviracitā āścaryayogamālālaghuvṛtti samāptābhūt).
SA_MB_ascaryayogamalaHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) reel no. B-114/19, running; transcribed under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00286).
SA_MB_ascaryayogamalaHK.coverage: complete — Text with Guṇākara's Laghuvṛtti commentary, concluding at the colophons, followed by brief scribal addenda on bath rules (snāna) and virility.

SA_MB_kakacandesvarimataHK.title: Kākacaṇḍeśvarīmata
SA_MB_kakacandesvarimataHK.summary: The Kākacaṇḍeśvarīmata is an early Śākta-Śaiva alchemical (rasaśāstra) and iatrochemical tantra presented as a dialogue on Mount Kailāsa between Bhairava and the goddess Kākacaṇḍeśvarī (a form of Kālī/Cāmuṇḍā). The text details mercurial processing, calcination, mineral operations, and herbal recipes (kalpas) for rejuvenation (rasāyana) and therapeutic medicine. Preserved in Nepalese manuscripts, it represents an important early stratum in medieval Indian tantric alchemy.
SA_MB_kakacandesvarimataHK.attribution: Revealed tantric and rasaśāstra treatise framed as a dialogue between Bhairava and the goddess Kākacaṇḍeśvarī (Kākacāmuṇḍā).
SA_MB_kakacandesvarimataHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu MS 3-118 (NGMCP reel no. A 211/8).
SA_MB_kakacandesvarimataHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript witness from folio 1a to 57a, concluding with 'iti śrīkākacaṇḍeśvarīmataṃ samāptam'.

SA_MB_GoraksayogasastraHK.title: Gorakṣayogaśāstra
SA_MB_GoraksayogasastraHK.author: Gorakṣanātha
SA_MB_GoraksayogasastraHK.summary: The Gorakṣayogaśāstra (also called Mūlasāra) is a short Nātha yoga text of 65 verses framed in the style of a stotra/saṃvāda opened by Īśvara. It describes the subtle body as an internal microcosm containing the sacred Kaula sites, sacred rivers, sun, moon, and cakras, and teaches prāṇāyāma, bandhas, and the unification of prāṇa and apāna for physical and spiritual liberation.
SA_MB_GoraksayogasastraHK.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Nātha mahāsiddha Gorakṣanātha, though framed as taught by Īśvara. It represents the internal yogic microcosm of the later Nātha/Kaula milieu.
SA_MB_GoraksayogasastraHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) manuscript 5-332 (reel no. B24/44).
SA_MB_GoraksayogasastraHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 65 verses with manuscript folio markers (fols. 1b–10a), concluding with the colophon 'mūlasāreti iti gorakṣajogaśāstrasamāptaṃ'.

SA_MB_TattvaratnaavaliiHK.title: Tattvaratnāvalī (incomplete: fols. 2a–17b)
SA_MB_TattvaratnaavaliiHK.author: Vimalaśiva
SA_MB_TattvaratnaavaliiHK.summary: The Tattvaratnāvalī of Vimalācārya (Vimalaśiva) is a brief liturgical manual for the basic rites of Siddhānta Śaivism. The first chapter deals with the regular daily rite (nitya) and the second with occasional rites (naimittika). The third chapter deals with the worship of the basic Navanābhamaṇḍala with the 81 parts (pada) of the Vyomavyāpin mantra.
SA_MB_TattvaratnaavaliiHK.attribution: Muktabodha calls the author Vimalaśiva, a South Indian Siddhāntin; the colophon names him Vimalācārya (iti śrīvimalācāryanirmite tyaṃtanirmale(?) tatvaratnāvalīgraṃthe nityakarmavinirṇayaḥ).
SA_MB_TattvaratnaavaliiHK.edition: Unpublished: transcription of the manuscript NGMCP 1-1697-7/6, microfilm reel B 26/16; fols. 2a–17b.
SA_MB_TattvaratnaavaliiHK.coverage: partial — Transcribes NGMCP MS 1-1697-7/6 (reel B 26/16) from fol. 2a to 17b. Fol. 1 is marked 'unclear' and fols. 18–27 are marked 'unclear' and not transcribed. Lacunae and doubtful readings marked '*' and '?'.

SA_MB_goraksagutikaHK.title: Gorakṣaguṭikā
SA_MB_goraksagutikaHK.summary: The Gorakṣaguṭikā ('Pill/Amulet of Gorakṣa') is a late Nātha liturgical and mythological text framed as a Tantric Haragaurīsaṃvāda (dialogue between Śiva and Gaurī), claiming affiliation to the Kalpadrumavivekinī. Unlike standard Haṭha Yoga treatises, it centers on devotional ritual and Guru worship, recounting the miraculous birth and deeds of Gorakṣanātha in its opening chapter, followed by protective kavacas, mantras, and stotras (including his dvādaśanāma, aṣṭottaraśatanāma, and sahasranāma) across nine chapters (taraṅgas).
SA_MB_goraksagutikaHK.attribution: Traditionally catalogued by Muktabodha under Gorakṣanātha, but the internal text is cast as a Tantric dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī (Haragaurīsaṃvāda) from the Kalpadrumavivekinī praising Gorakṣanātha.
SA_MB_goraksagutikaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from Kathmandu: Nepal-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (NGMCP) reel no. A 62/3 (running no. 2120), National Archives, Kathmandu
