SA_MB_goraksagutikaHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of all 9 taraṅgas of the Gorakṣaguṭikā preserved in manuscript NGMCP reel A 62/3.

SA_MB_mantrakosaHK.title: Mantrakoṣa
SA_MB_mantrakosaHK.author: Āśāditya Tripāṭhin
SA_MB_mantrakosaHK.summary: The Mantrakoṣa of Āśāditya Tripāṭhin is a tantric ritual compendium (mantranibandha) organized into sixteen chapters (paricchedas). It outlines procedures and mantras for pūjā, dīkṣā, guru-śiṣya qualification, bhūtaśuddhi, mātṛkānyāsa, yantras, and mudrās, drawing upon authorities such as the Prapañcasāratantra. The deity sections encompass pañcāyatana worship (Sūrya, Gaṇapati, Śiva, Viṣṇu/Nṛsiṃha, Sarasvatī/Śrī) along with protective and astrā mantras.
SA_MB_mantrakosaHK.attribution: Colophons in the e-text confirm authorship/compilation by Āśāditya Tripāṭhin (e.g., 'iti śrīmadāśādityatripāṭhīsaṃgṛhīte').
SA_MB_mantrakosaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 5-470 (reel no. A 169/8), copied in Śaka 1565 (1643 CE) by Anantarāma son of Manohara (unpublished diplomatic transcription).
SA_MB_mantrakosaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 16 paricchedas as transcribed from the manuscript, concluding with scribal verses dated Śaka 1565 (1643 CE).

SA_MB_kalikalpalataHK.title: Kālīkalpalatā
SA_MB_kalikalpalataHK.author: Vimarśānandanātha
SA_MB_kalikalpalataHK.summary: The Kālīkalpalatā (or Dakṣiṇakālīkalpalatā) by Vimarśānandanātha is concerned with the ritual procedures for the worship of the goddess Dakṣiṇakālī and her consort Mahākāla. It is divided into two sections (kusuma): the first deals with preliminary purifications, bathing, and offering of libations, while the second describes the pūjā itself.
SA_MB_kalikalpalataHK.attribution: Attributed in chapter colophons to Vimarśānandanātha (e.g. concluding colophon: 'iti śrīvimarśānaṃdanāthaviricitāyāṃ kālikalpalatāyāṃ dvitīyaṃ kusumaṃ || samāptaṃ').
SA_MB_kalikalpalataHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) manuscript MS 5-6521, reel B 120/9, copied in Nepal in Saṃvat 1754.
SA_MB_kalikalpalataHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 2 sections (kusuma), concluding with 'dvitīyaṃ kusumaṃ || samāptaṃ'.

SA_MB_kulasaraHK.title: Kulasāra (fragment)
SA_MB_kulasaraHK.summary: The Kulasāra is an early Kaula Śaiva scripture surviving in archaic Nepalese manuscripts and cited by non-dual Kashmiri Śaiva authors prior to the eleventh century. It expounds Kaula metaphysics—including the categories of piṇḍa, pada, rūpa, and rūpātīta, as well as Akula and Kula—combined with yogic practices for bodily internalization, mantra protection, visualization of Bhairava and yoginīs, non-dual ritual purity, and internal pilgrimage (caryā). This e-text preserves an unedited diplomatic transcript of chapters 4 (fragment) and 8–17 (incomplete).
SA_MB_kulasaraHK.attribution: Scriptural Kaula tantra presented as divine revelation in dialogue form.
SA_MB_kulasaraHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (NGMCP) MS 4-137/vi (microfilm reel A 40/11), transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, 2011.
SA_MB_kulasaraHK.coverage: fragment — Preserved fragment of an incomplete Nepalese manuscript; opens abruptly in chapter (paṭala) 4, followed by chapters 8 to 17, where it ends abruptly.

SA_MB_vimalavatiitantraHK.title: Vimalāvatītantra
SA_MB_vimalavatiitantraHK.author: Vimalaśiva
SA_MB_vimalavatiitantraHK.summary: The Vimalāvatītantra (also termed Vimalāvatī) is an extensive Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual composed by Vimalaśiva, who lived in the thirteenth century and took a vow of residing in Benares (kāśīvāsa). The work details worship procedures (pūjāsiddhi), fire sacrifices (vahnikārya, homa), festive ritual observances such as pavitra and dāmana, subtle breath yoga with Kuṇḍalinī, and various degrees of initiation (dīkṣā) alongside conduct codes for initiates.
SA_MB_vimalavatiitantraHK.attribution: Attributed in the text and colophon tradition to Vimalaśiva, a 13th-century Śaiva Siddhānta master who resided in Benares.
SA_MB_vimalavatiitantraHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of National Archives Kathmandu (NAK) MS 1-431 (NGMCP reel no. A 186/10), folios up to 161b.
SA_MB_vimalavatiitantraHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete; transcribed from NAK MS 1-431, breaking off on folio 161b ('ūnclear End') lacking explicit and final colophon.

SA_MB_darsanopanisatHK.title: Darśanopaniṣad with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa
SA_MB_darsanopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_darsanopanisatHK.summary: The Darśanopaniṣad is one of the twenty minor Yoga Upaniṣads in the Muktikā canon, affiliated with the Sāmaveda. Framed as an instructional dialogue between Dattātreya and Sāṃkṛti, it details an eightfold yoga (aṣṭāṅga-yoga) integrated with Advaita Vedānta, covering the ten yamas and niyamas, āsanas, the subtle anatomy of fourteen principal nāḍīs and ten prāṇas, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna, and samādhi. This e-text presents the root Upaniṣad along with the Vivaraṇa of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_darsanopanisatHK.attribution: The root Darśanopaniṣad is an anonymous Upaniṣad. The vivaraṇa is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (disciple of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_darsanopanisatHK.edition: yoga upaniṣads with the commentary of śrī upaniṣad brahmayogin, ed. śāstrī mahādeva, Madras: Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_darsanopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 10 khaṇḍas of the Darśanopaniṣad with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa.

SA_MB_trisikhibrahmanopanisatHK.title: Triśikhibrāhmaṇopaniṣad with Triśikhibrāhmaṇopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_trisikhibrahmanopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_trisikhibrahmanopanisatHK.summary: The Triśikhibrāhmaṇopaniṣad is a Yoga Upaniṣad affiliated with the Śukla Yajurveda. Structured as a dialogue between the sage Triśikhin and the sun-deity Āditya, it commences with a cosmogonic and non-dual Śiva-Brahman metaphysical inquiry in prose before detailing an eight-limbed yoga (aṣṭāṅgayoga) integrating Haṭhayoga techniques (āsana, nāḍīs, prāṇāyāma) toward Advaita Vedāntic liberation. This e-text includes the standard Vivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_trisikhibrahmanopanisatHK.attribution: The Vivaraṇa commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_trisikhibrahmanopanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, ed. Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_trisikhibrahmanopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the prose Brāhmaṇa section and the Mantra portion through verse 165, along with the full commentary (Vivaraṇa) concluding at segment 776.

SA_MB_varahopanisatHK.title: Varāhopaniṣad with Varāhopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_varahopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_varahopanisatHK.summary: The Varāhopaniṣad is a minor Yoga Upaniṣad (reckoned as the 98th in the Muktikā canon) attached to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, framed as an instruction imparted by Viṣṇu in his boar form (Varāha) to the sage Ṛbhu. Across five adhyāyas, it enumerates the 24, 36, and 96 tattvas, details subtle yogic physiology (cakras, nāḍīs, and kuṇḍalinī), outlines prāṇāyāma and haṭhayogic disciplines, and elucidates the seven stages of spiritual knowledge (jñānabhūmikās) culminating in jīvanmukti. Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary (Vivaraṇa) interprets the yogic practices in the light of Advaita Vedāntic non-dualism.
SA_MB_varahopanisatHK.attribution: The root text is an Upaniṣad of the Muktikā canon. The commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (disciple of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_varahopanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, ed. Śāstrī Mahādeva, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_varahopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all five adhyāyas of the Varāhopaniṣad with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa (matching up to p. 517 of the 1920 Adyar Library edition).

SA_MB_yogacudamanyupanisatHK.title: Yogacūḍāmaṇyupaniṣad with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa
SA_MB_yogacudamanyupanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_yogacudamanyupanisatHK.summary: The Yogacūḍāmaṇyupaniṣad is a Yoga Upaniṣad expounding yoga doctrines, subtle anatomy, prāṇāyāma, mudrās, bandhas, kuṇḍalinī, and meditation on Om. This e-text provides the 121 verses of the Upaniṣad along with the Vivaraṇa commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_yogacudamanyupanisatHK.attribution: The commentary (Vivaraṇa) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Śrī Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_yogacudamanyupanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Śāstrī Mahādeva, Madras: Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_yogacudamanyupanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad in 121 verses along with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's full Vivaraṇa, concluding with verse 121 and the colophon 'ṣaṭcatvāriṃśatsaṃkhyāpūrakaṃ yogacūḍāmaṇyupaniṣadvivaraṇaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_MB_yogakundalyupanisatHK.title: Yogakuṇḍalyupaniṣad with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa
SA_MB_yogakundalyupanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_yogakundalyupanisatHK.summary: The Yogakuṇḍalyupaniṣad is one of the twenty Yoga Upaniṣads belonging to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. In three chapters, it presents haṭha- and laya-yogic practices directed toward awakening kuṇḍalinī, including breath restraint (prāṇāyāma), dietary discipline (mitāhāra), āsana, bandhas, and lambikā (khecarī) mudrā, integrated into a non-dual Advaita Vedānta soteriology. This e-text includes both the root Upaniṣad and the running Vivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_yogakundalyupanisatHK.attribution: The Yogakuṇḍalyupaniṣad is an anonymous Yoga Upaniṣad (Muktikā canon no. 86). The commentary (Vivaraṇa) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (pupil of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_yogakundalyupanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, ed. Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_yogakundalyupanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in three adhyāyas along with complete Vivaraṇa commentary.

SA_MB_yogasikhopanisatHK.title: Yogaśikhopaniṣad with Yogaśikhopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_yogasikhopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_yogasikhopanisatHK.summary: The Yogaśikhopaniṣad is a classical Yoga Upaniṣad traditionally grouped under the Kṛṣṇayajurveda and counted as the 63rd text in the Muktikā list. Arranged in six adhyāyas, it synthesizes Mantra-, Laya-, Haṭha-, and Rājayoga, detailing the subtle body, nāḍīs, cakras, kuṇḍalinī, and non-dual realization. This e-text preserves the entire scripture alongside the Advaita commentary (vivaraṇa) composed by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_yogasikhopanisatHK.attribution: The vivaraṇa commentary was written by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (disciple of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_yogasikhopanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, ed. Śāstrī Mahādeva, Madras: Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_yogasikhopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text across all six adhyāyas (adhyāyas 1–6) of the Yogaśikhopaniṣad accompanied by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary.

SA_MB_yogatattvopanisatHK.title: Yogatattvopaniṣad with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa
SA_MB_yogatattvopanisatHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_yogatattvopanisatHK.summary: The Yogatattvopaniṣad is a Yoga Upaniṣad expounding four branches of yoga: mantrayoga, layayoga, haṭhayoga, and rājayoga. It details eightfold yoga (aṣṭāṅga) with concrete instructions on āsana, prāṇāyāma, purification of the nāḍīs, bandhas, mudrās, and absorption leading to kaivalya. In this edition, it is accompanied by the commentary (Vivaraṇa) of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_yogatattvopanisatHK.attribution: The Yogatattvopaniṣad is reckoned as the 41st Upaniṣad in the 108 Upaniṣad canon. The commentary (Vivaraṇa) was authored by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin (disciple of Vāsudevendra).
SA_MB_yogatattvopanisatHK.edition: Yoga Upaniṣads with the commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad Brahmayogin, edited by Mahādeva Śāstrī, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_yogatattvopanisatHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad (142 verses) interspersed with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's Vivaraṇa and concluding metrical colophon.

SA_MB_prayascittasamuccayaHK.title: Prāyaścittasamuccaya
SA_MB_prayascittasamuccayaHK.author: Hṛdayaśiva
SA_MB_prayascittasamuccayaHK.summary: The Prāyaścittasamuccaya of Hṛdayaśiva is an early Śaiva Siddhānta digest on expiatory rites (prāyaścitta). In 46 sections, it compiles and systematizes scriptural prescriptions for correcting ritual infractions, handling damage or contamination to liṅgas and shrines, and atoning for violations of samaya vows, drawing extensively upon early Tantras such as the Niḥśvāsa, Kāmika, Picumata, and Vātula.
SA_MB_prayascittasamuccayaHK.attribution: Authored by Hṛdayaśiva, a disciple of Īśvaraśiva, associated in the closing verses with King Sīyaka of Dhārā.
SA_MB_prayascittasamuccayaHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of National Archives, Kathmandu / NGMCP Reel B 427/2, MS.2402.
SA_MB_prayascittasamuccayaHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript in 46 prakaraṇas, ending with the author's closing verses and colophon at segment 3192 ('prāyaścittasamuccayaḥ samāptamiti || 46 ||').

SA_MB_mohacudottaramHK.title: Mohacūḍottara
SA_MB_mohacudottaramHK.summary: The Mohacūḍottara is an early Śaiva scriptural manual on installation (pratiṣṭhā-tantra) framed as a dialogue between Skanda and Śakra (Indra). It focuses on the ritual selection and testing of materials (stone, wood, metals), iconometry, the architecture of temples (prāsāda) and ritual halls (maṇḍapa), and the rites of consecration for liṅgas and deities. Preserved primarily in early Nepalese manuscripts, it forms an important witness to early medieval Śaiva architectural and ritual doctrine.
SA_MB_mohacudottaramHK.attribution: Revealed scriptural text (Tantra / Āgama upabheda) framed as an instruction delivered by Skanda to Śakra (Indra).
SA_MB_mohacudottaramHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of Kathmandu, National Archives MS 5-1977 (NGMCP Reel A 182/2), a modern Devanāgarī paper copy transcribed in VS 1982 by Gaṇeśadatta Śarman for Rājaguru Hemarāja from an ancient palm-leaf manuscript dated Saṃvat 806.
SA_MB_mohacudottaramHK.coverage: complete — Complete text as transmitted in the manuscript tradition, terminating with the final scribal colophons.

SA_MB_pingalamataHK.title: Piṅgalāmata
SA_MB_pingalamataHK.summary: The Piṅgalāmata (also titled Jayadrathādhikāra) is an early Śaiva pratiṣṭhātantra associated with the Brahmayāmala and Jayadrathayāmala. Practically all early surviving Pratiṣṭhātantras are Saiddhāntika, but the Piṅgalāmata incorporates ritual procedures and iconographic details of the Vāma, Yāmala, and Trika traditions alongside pratiṣṭhā rites (consecration and installation of deities, temples, monasteries, palaces, and towns).
SA_MB_pingalamataHK.attribution: A revealed Śaiva scripture affiliated with the Brahmayāmala and Jayadrathayāmala corpus.
SA_MB_pingalamataHK.coverage: partial — Transcription of manuscript NGMCP 3-376 / vi śaivatantra 113; the text breaks off at the end before the scribal colophon of Samvat 297.

SA_MB_laghustavaHK.title: Laghustava with Laghustavaṭīkā
SA_MB_laghustavaHK.author: Dharmācārya, Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī
SA_MB_laghustavaHK.summary: The Laghustava is the first of the five hymns comprising the Pañcastavī. In 21 verses, it praises the supreme goddess Mahātripurasundarī. This e-text preserves the complete hymn along with the commentary (Laghustavaṭīkā / Harabhaṭṭī) by Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.
SA_MB_laghustavaHK.attribution: The Laghustava in the Pañcastavī is ascribed in the colophon to Dharmācārya ('iti śrīdharmācāryaviracitāyāṃ pañcastavyāṃ laghustave...'). The commentary is by Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.
SA_MB_laghustavaHK.edition: Laghustavacarcāstavau: Harabhaṭṭīvyākhyopetau (Pañcastavīmālā 1), ed. Pandit Dinanath Shastri Yaksha, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research and Publication Department, Jammu & Kashmir Government (printed at Fine Art Press), 1963.
SA_MB_laghustavaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Laghustava (21 verses) along with Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī's commentary.

SA_MB_carcastavaHK.title: Carcāstava with Pañcastavīṭīkā
SA_MB_carcastavaHK.author: Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī
SA_MB_carcastavaHK.summary: The Carcāstava is the second hymn of the Kashmiri hymnological pentad, the Pañcastavī. Consisting of stanzas addressed to the Goddess, it is accompanied in this e-text by the Sanskrit commentary (ṭīkā/vivaraṇa) by Mahāmāheśvara Paṇḍita Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.
SA_MB_carcastavaHK.attribution: The root hymn Carcāstava is ascribed in colophons to Dharmācārya. The commentary was written by Mahāmāheśvara Paṇḍita Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī.
SA_MB_carcastavaHK.edition: Pañcastavī with commentary of Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Fine Art Press, 1963.
SA_MB_carcastavaHK.coverage: complete — Text of the Carcāstava with Harabhaṭṭa Śāstrī's commentary thereon (second hymn of the Pañcastavī).

SA_MB_bhuvanesvarimahastotramHK.title: Bhuvaneśvarīmahāstotra with Padmanābha's Bhāṣya and other texts
SA_MB_bhuvanesvarimahastotramHK.author: Pṛthvīdharācārya, Padmanābha, Anantadeva
SA_MB_bhuvanesvarimahastotramHK.summary: A comprehensive compendium of Śākta liturgical, hymnological, and mantric literature centered on the Mahāvidyā goddess Bhuvaneśvarī. It opens with the Bhuvaneśvarīmahāstotra attributed to Pṛthvīdharācārya alongside the commentary by Kavi Padmanābha, and collects various ancillary texts including a pañcāṅga, pūjāpaddhati, kavaca, sahasranāma, aṣṭottaraśatanāma, and hṛdaya attributed largely to the Rudrayāmala, Anantadeva's ritual manual Bhuvaneśvarīkramacandrikā, and Pṛthvīdharācārya's Laghusaptaśatīstotra.
SA_MB_bhuvanesvarimahastotramHK.attribution: Tradition attributes the root Bhuvaneśvarīmahāstotra (also designated Siddhasārasvata) and Laghusaptaśatīstotra to Pṛthvīdharācārya, traditionally claimed as a direct disciple of Śaṅkara, though modern scholars consider this attribution unhistorical given the developed Daśamahāvidyā framework. The Bhāṣya is by Kavi Padmanābha, and the Kramacandrikā is by Anantadeva of Mātṛpura.
SA_MB_bhuvanesvarimahastotramHK.edition: Gopal Narayan Bahura (ed.), Śrī Bhuvaneśvarī Mahāstotram by Pṛthvīdharācārya, with the commentary of Kavi Padmanābha and other texts. Jodhpur: Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute, 1960.
SA_MB_bhuvanesvarimahastotramHK.coverage: complete — Complete e-text of the composite printed volume containing texts related to Bhuvaneśvarī (pp. 1–158), ending with the colophon of Pṛthvīdharācārya's Laghusaptaśatīstotra on p. 158.

SA_MB_DeviirahasyaHK.title: Devīrahasya with Uddhārakośa
SA_MB_DeviirahasyaHK.summary: The Devīrahasya is a Śākta tantric digest and ritual compilation framed as part of the Rudrayāmala, composed in Kashmir. It is structured into a Pūrvārdha of 25 paṭalas dealing with initiation, mantra vitalization and unlocking, puraścaraṇa, yantras, and ritual ingredients, followed by an Uttarārdha of 35 paṭalas providing pañcāṅgas (paṭala, kavaca, paddhati, sahasranāma, and stotra) for various deities. The appended text is the Uddhārakośa of Dakṣiṇāmūrtimuni, a 7-kalpa lexicon defining and deciphering tantric mantras.
SA_MB_DeviirahasyaHK.attribution: The Devīrahasya is presented as belonging to the Rudrayāmala. Its regional focus on Kashmiri shrines (Śārikā, Jvālāmukhī, Mahārājñī, Śāradā) and late vocabulary indicate medieval Kashmiri compilation. The appended Uddhārakośa is attributed in its colophons to Dakṣiṇāmūrtimuni.
SA_MB_DeviirahasyaHK.edition: Ram Chandra Kak and Harabhatta Shastri (eds.), The Devīrahasya with Pariśiṣṭas, Srinagar, 1941.
SA_MB_DeviirahasyaHK.coverage: complete — Complete e-text of the printed edition, covering the Devīrahasya (Pūrvārdha in 25 paṭalas and Uttarārdha in 35 paṭalas), the Kashmiri goddess Pariśiṣṭas, and the Uddhārakośa in 7 kalpas.

SA_MB_asesakulavallariHK.title: Aśeṣakulavallarī (fragment)
SA_MB_asesakulavallariHK.author: Gaṇananāthabhaṭṭa
SA_MB_asesakulavallariHK.summary: The Aśeṣakulavallarī is a liturgical manual (paddhati) composed by Gaṇananāthabhaṭṭa, a Brahmin of the Garga gotra and disciple of Mahādevabhaṭṭa, based on the Vāmakeśvaramata (the root Tantra of Tripurāsundarī). The work covers visualization and worship of the teacher and lineage, preliminary purifying ablution, and door worship/preliminary nyāsa before breaking off.
SA_MB_asesakulavallariHK.attribution: The opening identifies the author as Gaṇananāthabhaṭṭa, a Brahmin of the Garga gotra whose teacher was Mahādevabhaṭṭa.
SA_MB_asesakulavallariHK.coverage: fragment — Fragmentary text containing the opening through chapter 1 (visualization and worship of the teacher and lineage), chapter 2 (purifying ablution / snānavidhi), and the beginning of chapter 3 (door worship and preliminary nyāsa), breaking off soon after.

SA_MB_saubhagyataranginiHK.title: Saubhāgyataraṅgiṇī (incomplete)
SA_MB_saubhagyataranginiHK.author: Mukunda
SA_MB_saubhagyataranginiHK.summary: The Saubhāgyataraṅgiṇī is a Śrīvidyā liturgical manual (paddhati) dedicated to the worship of Mahātripurasundarī, composed by Mukunda. The text harmonizes Tantric ritual practice with orthodox Purāṇic and Vedic traditions, quoting extensively from Vedic texts, numerous Purāṇas (especially Kālikā and Kūrma), and Tantras including the Vāmakeśvara, Jñānārṇava, and Tantrarāja. Divided into chapters called 'waves' (laharī), the text sets forth daily ritual, mantra meditation, and yantra pūjā.
SA_MB_saubhagyataranginiHK.attribution: Colophons attribute the text to Mukunda (e.g., 'iti śrīmanmukundaviracitāyāṃ saubhāgyataraṅgiṇyāṃ...').
SA_MB_saubhagyataranginiHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from National Archives, Kathmandu, Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 5-4656, Reel A 175/11 (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_saubhagyataranginiHK.coverage: partial — Text breaks off in the fifth chapter (taraṅga/laharī) without a final colophon.

SA_MB_trotalamahatantramHK.title: Troṭalātantra
SA_MB_trotalamahatantramHK.summary: The Troṭalātantra (or Troṭalamahātantra) is an early medieval Śaiva/Śākta tantric scripture framed as an exposition delivered by Śiva to Garuḍa (Tārkṣya). It centers on the goddess Troṭalā—identified with Tvaritā and linked with the Kubjikā tradition—so named because she shatters (troṭana) worldly bonds. The work covers her visual iconography, mantra formulas, internal yogic ascent through the centers to union with Bhairava, and rites for protection against poison and the subjugation of spirits.
SA_MB_trotalamahatantramHK.attribution: A scriptural Tantra presented as teaching delivered by Parameśvara (Śiva) to Tārkṣya (Garuḍa).
SA_MB_trotalamahatantramHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription based on National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP Ms. 5-4852 (Reel B 126/9).
SA_MB_trotalamahatantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 9 paṭalas (c. 700 verses), concluding at 9.66 with the final colophon 'ityādye troṭale mahātantre tvaritāmūlasūtre navamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_TantracintamaniHK.title: Tantracintāmaṇi with Pañjikā (chapters 1–30)
SA_MB_TantracintamaniHK.author: Navamīsiṃha
SA_MB_TantracintamaniHK.summary: The Tantracintāmaṇi is an extensive Śākta Tantric digest (nibandha) composed in the late seventeenth century by Navamīsiṃha (Ādyānanda), a minister in the Newar Malla kingdom of Kathmandu. Organized in forty prakāśas, it compiles citations from numerous Āgamic and Tantric authorities to delineate cosmology, mantra lore, the worship of the Daśamahāvidyās (focusing particularly on Dakṣiṇakālikā/Śyāmā), Kulācāra rites, and dīkṣā ceremonies. This digital transcription covers chapters 1 through 30 with its autocommentary (Pañjikā).
SA_MB_TantracintamaniHK.attribution: Navamīsiṃha (also named Ādyānanda) was a minister under the Kathmandu Malla rulers (specifically associated with King Bhūpālendra Malla, c. late 17th century). He also authored the Kulamuktikallolinī.
SA_MB_TantracintamaniHK.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcription of National Archives, Kathmandu, MS (Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project / NGMCP Reel no. B 131/2), unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_TantracintamaniHK.coverage: partial — Contains prakāśas 1–30 of the 40-chapter work; prakāśa 25 is missing in the manuscript witness. The text concludes at fol. 244a with the colophon of the 30th prakāśa (mālābhedādipratiṣṭhāntanirṇaya).

SA_MB_moksasopanaHK.title: Mokṣasopāna with Ṭīkā
SA_MB_moksasopanaHK.author: Kāṇḍadvayātītayogī
SA_MB_moksasopanaHK.summary: The Mokṣasopāna ('Staircase to Liberation') is a Śākta-Śaiva treatise on esoteric yoga, cakra meditation, and internal worship affiliated with the Kubjikā tradition. It outlines the graded stages of spiritual ascent through the phonic and cosmological hierarchy (from praṇava and subtle sound vibrations up to unmanā) and meditation on the kuṇḍalinī and the goddess Kubjikā/Mahāmāyā. The e-text preserves the root text together with an anonymous prose commentary (Ṭīkā) transcribed directly from a Nepalese manuscript.
SA_MB_moksasopanaHK.attribution: According to the Catalogus Catalogorum, the author was called Kāṇḍadvayātītayogī. Mark S. G. Dyczkowski notes that nothing is known about the author of the Mokṣasopāna or the author of the Ṭīkā.
SA_MB_moksasopanaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 1-1397, Reel No. A-179/8.
SA_MB_moksasopanaHK.coverage: complete — Concludes with the colophon 'iti mokṣasopānaṭīkā samāptā'.

SA_MB_NityatantraHK.title: Nityākaulatantra (fragment)
SA_MB_NityatantraHK.summary: The Nityākaulatantra (also known as Nityātantra) is an early Kaula tantra surviving only in fragmentary leaves of a single manuscript. Considered certainly prior to the 10th century CE, it represents an important testimony to the early worship of Tripurāsundarī as Tripurabhairavī, preceding the emergence of the Śrīvidyā tradition.
SA_MB_NityatantraHK.attribution: Revealed Śākta/Kaula scripture, traditionally considered an āgama/tantra.
SA_MB_NityatantraHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives, Kathmandu, MS 2-226 (NGMCP Reel No. B26/21a), prepared by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (Muktabodha catalog no. M00316).
SA_MB_NityatantraHK.coverage: fragment — Fragmentary diplomatic transcription of surviving damaged manuscript folios from NGMCP MS 2-226 (Reel B26/21a).

SA_MB_varahitantramHK.title: Vārāhītantra
SA_MB_varahitantramHK.summary: An extensive Śākta Kaula Tantra belonging to the Dakṣiṇāmnāya (Southern transmission) and associated in its opening verses with the Kāmarūpa pīṭha. It centers on the worship of the goddess Vārāhī along with Sundarī and Kālikā, serving as a comprehensive manual of ritual procedures, mantras, yantras, nyāsa, and yogic practices. The text is cited in several major Tantric digests, providing a terminus ante quem prior to the late 18th-century Puraścaryārṇava.
SA_MB_varahitantramHK.edition: Manuscript transcription from National Archives, Kathmandu / NGMCP ms. (Reel no. B 144/9), 233 folios (unpublished diplomatic e-text).
SA_MB_varahitantramHK.coverage: unclear — Complete transcription of the 233-folio Nepalese manuscript (4,631 verses), concluding at folio 233 with 'vārāhītaṃtrapūrvakhaṇḍa || śrīvārāhītaṃtrasamāpti patra 233 ||'. Because the final colophon specifically designates this as the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, it is uncertain whether it constitutes the entirety of the work or only the prior section of a two-part tantra.

SA_MB_kulamuktikalloliniHK.title: Kulamuktikallolinī
SA_MB_kulamuktikalloliniHK.author: Navamīsiṃha
SA_MB_kulamuktikalloliniHK.summary: The Kulamuktikallolinī is an extensive late 17th-century Kaula Śākta ritual compendium (nibandha) in 22 chapters (paṭalas) compiled by Navamīsiṃha (Ādyānanda), a minister under King Bhūpālendra Malla of Kathmandu. It gathers thousands of scriptural citations from Śākta, Śaiva, and Vaiṣṇava Tantras to form a comprehensive manual for the worship of Kālī, detailing dīkṣā, kuṇḍa preparation, fire rituals, and daily pūjā.
SA_MB_kulamuktikalloliniHK.attribution: The compiler Navamīsiṃha, who also uses the name Ādyānanda (found in the colophons: 'iti śrī-ādyānandanaviracitāyāṃ kulamuktikallolinyāṃ...'), was a court minister under King Bhūpālendra Malla of Kathmandu (late 17th century).
SA_MB_kulamuktikalloliniHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP MS 1-1675 (Reel No. B 120/6).
SA_MB_kulamuktikalloliniHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 22 chapters (paṭalas), ending with 'iti śrī-ādyānandanaviracitāyāṃ kulamuktikallolinyāṃ dvāviṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_BrahmayamalaHK.title: Brahmayāmala (South Indian; paṭalas 1–51, incomplete)
SA_MB_BrahmayamalaHK.summary: A ritual text associated with the cult of the Mothers (Mātṛs), styled a part of the Brahmayāmala Śatasahasrasaṃhitā. It opens with the narrative of the gods and the demon Dāruka. Topics include the festival of the Mothers (mātrotsava), ekavīrā worship, installation and ritual procedures, and expiation / funerary rites.
SA_MB_BrahmayamalaHK.edition: Transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry paper transcript T00522 (Muktabodha catalog no. M00319, revision 0, Nov. 21, 2014).
SA_MB_BrahmayamalaHK.coverage: partial — Incomplete. Paṭala 1 begins with the Mothers' festival ('iti brahmayāmale śatasahasrasaṃhitāyāṃ mātrotsavo nāma prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ'), and paṭala 50 is 'nāgapāśavidhirnāma pañcāśatpaṭalaḥ'. The text breaks off in mid-sentence ('punassaṃskāra karveṇa astisañcaya') at p. 192.

SA_MB_KalasamkarsinitippaniHK.title: Kālasaṃkarṣiṇīmatatantraṭippaṇī (fragment)
SA_MB_KalasamkarsinitippaniHK.summary: A fragmentary Kaula-Krama commentary (ṭippaṇī) on the Kālasaṃkarṣiṇīmatatantra, an esoteric scripture related to the Jayadrathayāmala corpus, embedding mūla verses within the glosses. The surviving text focuses largely on the secret Ādiyāga (Ādyayāga) ritual, outlining the worship of yoginīs, samaya disciplines, and the ceremonial use of Kaula ritual substances.
SA_MB_KalasamkarsinitippaniHK.attribution: Anonymous Kaula/Krama gloss preserved in a manuscript from Nepal.
SA_MB_KalasamkarsinitippaniHK.coverage: fragment — Manuscript transcription covering folios up to 36a; breaks off incomplete. Includes embedded mūla verses alongside commentary.

SA_MB_NigamasaranirnayaHK.title: Nigamasāranirṇaya
SA_MB_NigamasaranirnayaHK.author: Ramāramaṇadeva
SA_MB_NigamasaranirnayaHK.summary: The Nigamasāranirṇaya is a late Śākta/Kaula ritual digest (nibandha) composed by Ramāramaṇadeva. Drawing on and quoting numerous medieval and early modern tantric scriptures and manuals—including the Tantrakaumudī of Govinda Ṭhakkura (16th century), Tantracūḍāmaṇi, Gandharvatantra, Phetkāriṇītantra, and Jñānārṇava—it systematically establishes the mantras, cakras, nyāsa rituals, and worship procedures of Kaula goddesses, particularly Kālikā and various Vidyās, while addressing doctrinal consistency (ekavākyatā) across tantric sources.
SA_MB_NigamasaranirnayaHK.attribution: Attributed in the colophon (śrīramāramaṇadevaśarmaṇā nirmite nigamasāranirṇaye) to Ramāramaṇadeva (Ramāramaṇadevaśarman).
SA_MB_NigamasaranirnayaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS, Reel no. B 129/5 (119 folios).
SA_MB_NigamasaranirnayaHK.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the manuscript (fol. 1b–119b).

SA_MB_saktisutramHK.title: Śaktisūtra
SA_MB_saktisutramHK.summary: A ritual manual belonging to the Kubjikā school (Paścimāmnāya), containing details of basic ritual procedures of this school. The text includes the Śaktisūtra towards the beginning and ends with the colophon 'iti nityanaimittikavidhiḥ samāptāḥ'. A colophon reference 'iti sūtrasaṃgrahe śrīkauṃkaṇādhikāre' points to Koṅkaṇa, suggesting it may have been composed there.
SA_MB_saktisutramHK.attribution: A tantric ritual manual of the Kubjikā / Paścimāmnāya school, anonymous and associated with the Koṅkaṇa region and transmitted in Nepal.
SA_MB_saktisutramHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Kathmandu, National Archives MS 1-619 (NGMPP reel No. 628/9); transcribed under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00322), 2011 (revised 2014).
SA_MB_saktisutramHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of manuscript NAK 1-619 (NGMPP reel 628/9), covering folios 1a through the concluding colophon 'iti nityanaimittikavidhiḥ samāptāḥ'.

SA_MB_kriyakramadyotikavyakhyaHK.title: Kriyākramadyotikāvyākhyā
SA_MB_kriyakramadyotikavyakhyaHK.author: Kacchapeśvaraśivācārya
SA_MB_kriyakramadyotikavyakhyaHK.summary: A Sanskrit commentary (vyākhyā) by Kacchapeśvaraśivācārya on the Kriyākramadyotikā of Aghoraśivācārya. The root text guides ritual procedure in major Śaiva temples of South India. The commentary ends with the damanapūjāvidhi.
SA_MB_kriyakramadyotikavyakhyaHK.attribution: Composed by Kacchapeśvaraśivācārya who lived in Kāñcī (according to Dyczkowski). In the description by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, it is noted that 'At the beginning he refers to Aghoraśiva as his teacher telling us that he wrote it impelled by his grace.' He describes himself in the closing verses as 'ekamākaṃdanāmāṃghri pūjakena dvijanmanā'.
SA_MB_kriyakramadyotikavyakhyaHK.edition: Unpublished: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00109, copied from a manuscript belonging to Siva Sri Swaminatha Sivacharya of Tiruvaduturai Tanjavur Dt.
SA_MB_kriyakramadyotikavyakhyaHK.coverage: complete — The commentary ends with the section colophon 'iti damana pūjāvidhiḥ samāptaḥ', the commentator's closing verses and the final colophon 'iti śrīmatkacchapeśvara śivācāryaviracitā śrīmadaghoraśivācāryakṛtakriyākramadyotikāvyākhyā samāptam anaiṣīt || śrīśivābhyānnamaḥ', followed by the Muktabodha footer.

SA_MB_KaularahasyaHK.title: Kaularahasya (incomplete)
SA_MB_KaularahasyaHK.summary: A Kaula Śākta ritual compendium preserved in a Nepalese manuscript. It treats topics including the pañcamakāra, mantra-japa, homa, yantra-dhyāna, and protective kavacas.
SA_MB_KaularahasyaHK.attribution: A tantric ritual compendium of the Kaula Śākta tradition.
SA_MB_KaularahasyaHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of NGMCP Ms. No. 1-257 (Reel no. A-146/8).
SA_MB_KaularahasyaHK.coverage: partial — Transcription of NGMCP Ms. No. 1-257 (Reel no. A-146/8). Folios 1-8 are missing, the header notes many further missing folios, and the end breaks off with "samāptaṃ / apūrṇamasti".

SA_MB_T-334-sarvajnanottaramHK.title: Sarvajñānottaratantra
SA_MB_T-334-sarvajnanottaramHK.summary: A Śaiva scripture containing sections on yoga (Yogapāda) and ritual/observance topics including initiation and ascetic requisites, concluding with the kamaṇḍaluprakaraṇa.
SA_MB_T-334-sarvajnanottaramHK.attribution: Revealed Śaiva scripture (classified in subject cataloguing as Śaiva-Siddhānta / tantric / āgamic literature).
SA_MB_T-334-sarvajnanottaramHK.edition: IFP/EFEO transcript T00334 from D5550 GOML, Madras.
SA_MB_T-334-sarvajnanottaramHK.coverage: complete — Transcription of transcript T0334 (140 pages), beginning with the Yogapāda and ending with the kamaṇḍaluprakaraṇa.

SA_MB_siddhantarthasamuccayaHK.title: Siddhāntārthasamuccaya
SA_MB_siddhantarthasamuccayaHK.summary: An anonymous Śaiva Siddhānta doctrinal compendium in mixed prose and verse that synthesizes tenets of the Śaivāgama tradition. It quotes foundational scriptures and commentaries including the Svāyambhuvasūtrasaṃgraha, Kiraṇatantra, Mālinīvijayottara, Rauravatantra, and Mataṅgapārameśvara, as well as Rāmakaṇṭha. The treatise addresses the divine origin and transmission lineages of scriptural revelation (mahaughakrama and pratisaṃhitākrama), the ontological categories of pati, paśu, and pāśa, and initiatory praxis (dīkṣā).
SA_MB_siddhantarthasamuccayaHK.attribution: No author is named in the manuscript transcript. The opening homage is addressed to Padmarasa Ārādhya (śrīmatpadmarasārādhyapadābhyāṃ namaḥ).
SA_MB_siddhantarthasamuccayaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO), transcript T00206.
SA_MB_siddhantarthasamuccayaHK.coverage: unclear — Transcribed from IFP/EFEO transcript T00206, pp. 57–111. The closing transcript note remarks that it is uncertain whether the text is complete or incomplete ('atra granthaḥ samāptimagamat | na jñāyate saṃpūrṇo vāsampūrṇoveti').

SA_MB_suksmagamaHK.title: Sūkṣmāgama (paṭalas 1–60, incomplete)
SA_MB_suksmagamaHK.summary: The Sūkṣmāgama is an Āgama/Tantra text covering ritual procedures (arcanavidhi, etc.).
SA_MB_suksmagamaHK.attribution: Colophons designate the work as Sūkṣmatantra / Sūkṣmaśāstra.

SA_MB_suksmagamaHK.coverage: partial — The transcript breaks off at v. 218½ and ends with 'apūrṇaḥ'; ilx_skt catalog lists completeness as 'incomplete' lacking explicit/final colophon.

SA_MB_bhagavadgitavirashaivabhashyamHK.title: Bhagavadgītā with Bhagavadgītāvīraśaivabhāṣya
SA_MB_bhagavadgitavirashaivabhashyamHK.author: T. G. Siddapparādhya
SA_MB_bhagavadgitavirashaivabhashyamHK.summary: A modern 20th-century Sanskrit commentary on the Bhagavadgītā interpreting the scripture from the perspective of Vīraśaivism (Śaktivisiṣṭādvaita). Composed by Dr. T. G. Siddapparādhya and published in 1965 by the Murugharājendra Maṭha, the commentary correlates Vedāntic and epic concepts with Liṅgāyat theology, Basaveśvara, Allama Prabhu, and Śaiva devotion.
SA_MB_bhagavadgitavirashaivabhashyamHK.attribution: Authored by modern scholar Dr. T. G. Siddapparādhya under the inspiration of his father.
SA_MB_bhagavadgitavirashaivabhashyamHK.edition: Śrīmadbhagavadgītāvīraśaivabhāṣyam, commentary by Dr. T. G. Siddapparadhya, Śrī Jagadguru Murugharājendra Vidyāpīṭha Granthamālā, 1965.
SA_MB_bhagavadgitavirashaivabhashyamHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 18 adhyāyas (1–18), terminating at 18.78 followed by the commentator's praśasti verses and final colophon.

SA_MB_KulavrttiHK.title: Kulavṛtti (Ādyakhaṇḍa)
SA_MB_KulavrttiHK.author: Pūrṇānanda
SA_MB_KulavrttiHK.summary: The Kulavṛtti is an extensive Śākta-Kaula ritual digest (nibandha) composed by Pūrṇānanda. Drawing upon numerous Tantras and Āgamas, it provides a comprehensive manual of Kaula theology, guru-paramparā, mantra and yantra initiation, ritual purification, mudrās, and internal yogic worship. This e-text preserves the first section (Ādyakhaṇḍa) in thirty paṭalas transcribed directly from a Nepalese manuscript.
SA_MB_KulavrttiHK.attribution: In the text he names himself as Pūrṇānanda and Pūrṇānandanātha (final colophon: śrīpūrṇānaṃdanāthenakṛtāyāṃ gurubhāvataḥ kulavṛttau svataṃtrāyāṃ triṃśat paṭalaḥ īritaḥ).
SA_MB_KulavrttiHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of NGMCP Manuscript (Reel No. B 119/2).
SA_MB_KulavrttiHK.coverage: partial — Preserves the complete Ādyakhaṇḍa in 30 paṭalas (colophon: śrīpūrṇānaṃdanāthenakṛtāyāṃ gurubhāvataḥ kulavṛttau svataṃtrāyāṃ triṃśat paṭalaḥ īritaḥ || saṃpūrn.āścādyakhaṃḍakaḥ ||); whether further sections existed or survive is unestablished.

SA_MB_laksmiitantramHK.title: Lakṣmītantra with Tattvaprakāśanī
SA_MB_laksmiitantramHK.summary: The Lakṣmītantra is a major canonical Pāñcarātra scripture (saṃhitā), notable for presenting the goddess Lakṣmī (Śrī) as the supreme creative and dynamic power (Śakti) of Nārāyaṇa. In 57 chapters, the text expounds Pāñcarātra cosmogony, the six divine gunas, the theory of vyūha emanations, mantraśāstra, ritual diagram construction (maṇḍala/yantra), and devotional surrender (nyāsa/prapatti). In this e-text, the root verses are accompanied by a Sanskrit commentary gloss by Pandit V. Krishnamacharya.
SA_MB_laksmiitantramHK.attribution: The root scripture is an anonymous Pāñcarātra Āgama. The Sanskrit commentary gloss is attributed to the editor, Pandit V. Krishnamacharya (Paṇḍita Kṛṣṇamācārya).
SA_MB_laksmiitantramHK.edition: Lakṣmī-Tantra. A Pāñcarātra Āgama, edited with Sanskrit gloss and introduction by V. Krishnamacharya. The Adyar Library Series 87. Madras: The Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1959.
SA_MB_laksmiitantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 57 adhyāyas with commentary.

SA_MB_LingadhaaranachandrikaHK.title: Liṅgadhāraṇacandrikā with Śivā
SA_MB_LingadhaaranachandrikaHK.author: Nandikeśvara, Śivakumāra Śāstrī
SA_MB_LingadhaaranachandrikaHK.summary: The Liṅgadhāraṇacandrikā is a Vīraśaiva apologetic and theological treatise composed by Nandikeśvara. Applying Mīmāṃsā hermeneutical principles to Vedic, Upaniṣadic, Āgamic, and Smṛti citations, the work establishes the scriptural validity, necessity, and orthodoxy of constantly bearing the personal liṅga on the body (iṣṭaliṅgadhāraṇa) and examines associated funerary practices. The accompanying Sanskrit commentary, written by Mahāmahopādhyāya Śivakumāra Śāstrī in 1903, provides glosses and defends the dialectical arguments against rival philosophical schools.
SA_MB_LingadhaaranachandrikaHK.attribution: Attributed to Nandikeśvara (Nandīśvara / Nandikeśvara Śivācārya, son of Maheśācārya and grandson of Basaveśvara). The commentary was written in 1903 by the Benares pandit Mahāmahopādhyāya Śivakumāra Miśra Śāstrī.
SA_MB_LingadhaaranachandrikaHK.edition: Liṅgadhāraṇacandrikā of Nandikeśvara, with the commentary by Śivakumāra Śāstrī. Varanasi: Medical Hall, 1905.
SA_MB_LingadhaaranachandrikaHK.coverage: complete — Contains the text with the commentary and the terminal abbreviation list of cited sources.

SA_MB_samnyaasaupanisadHK.title: Saṃnyāsopaniṣadaḥ with Vivaraṇa
SA_MB_samnyaasaupanisadHK.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_samnyaasaupanisadHK.summary: A collection of minor Upaniṣads of the Saṃnyāsa class accompanied by the Vivaraṇa commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin. The texts describe the stages and rituals of renunciation, the classes of ascetics (kuṭīcaka, bahūdaka, haṃsa, paramahaṃsa, turīyātīta, avadhūta), the abandonment of exterior ritual emblems, and the realization of Brahman. Digitized from the 1929 Adyar Library publication.
SA_MB_samnyaasaupanisadHK.attribution: The commentary (Vivaraṇa / Vyākhyā) is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, pupil of Śrī Vāsudevendra.
SA_MB_samnyaasaupanisadHK.edition: The Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, Adyar: The Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1929.
SA_MB_samnyaasaupanisadHK.coverage: complete — Collection of Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads (including Avadhūta, Āruṇi, Kaṭharudra, Kuṇḍika, Jābāla, Turīyātītāvadhūta, Nāradaparivrājaka, Nirvāṇa, Parabrahma, Paramahaṃsaparivrājaka, Brahma, Bhikṣuka, Maitreya, Yājñavalkya, Śāṭyāyanīya, Saṃnyāsa) along with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary.
translations: Patrick Olivelle, trans., Samnyāsa Upaniṣads: Hindu Scriptures on Asceticism and Renunciation, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1992. (English)

SA_MB_Yvaasistha1vairaagyaprakaranamHK.title: Yogavāsiṣṭha with Tātparyaprakāśa (prakaraṇa 1: Vairāgyaprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_Yvaasistha1vairaagyaprakaranamHK.author: Vālmīki, Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī
SA_MB_Yvaasistha1vairaagyaprakaranamHK.summary: The first book (Vairāgyaprakaraṇa, 33 sargas) of the Yogavāsiṣṭha describes the profound disillusionment and existential grief of the young prince Rāma after his pilgrimage across the country. Confronting the transience of life, wealth, youth, and the physical body, Rāma articulates his despair before king Daśaratha and the royal assembly, creating the need for sage Vasiṣṭha's extensive exposition of non-dual liberation. Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī's accompanying commentary Tātparyaprakāśa provides word-by-word glosses and an orthodox Advaita Vedānta framing.
SA_MB_Yvaasistha1vairaagyaprakaranamHK.attribution: The commentary Tātparyaprakāśa is composed by Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_Yvaasistha1vairaagyaprakaranamHK.edition: The Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha of Vālmīki with the Commentary Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇa-Tātparyaprakāśa, edited by Vasudeva Laxmana Sharma Pansikar, 2 vols., Bombay, 1918.
SA_MB_Yvaasistha1vairaagyaprakaranamHK.coverage: partial — Contains Prakaraṇa 1 (Vairāgyaprakaraṇa), sargas 1–33 complete with the root kārikās and Tātparyaprakāśa commentary.
translations: Venkatesananda, Swami, State University of New York Press, 1993. (English)
Mitra, Vihari Lala, The Yoga-Vasistha-Mahārāmāyana of Valmiki. (English)

SA_MB_YvaasisthaBmumuksuvyavaharaprakara.title: Yogavāsiṣṭha with Tātparyaprakāśa (Mumukṣuvyavahāraprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_YvaasisthaBmumuksuvyavaharaprakara.author: Vālmīki, Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī
SA_MB_YvaasisthaBmumuksuvyavaharaprakara.summary: The Mumukṣuvyavahāraprakaraṇa is the second book of the Yogavāsiṣṭha (or Mokṣopāya), consisting of twenty chapters. Addressing Rāma's spiritual disaffection introduced in the opening book (Vairāgyaprakaraṇa), this section analyzes the nature of human striving (pauruṣa) versus fate (daiva), details the narrative of Śuka's attainment of peace through King Janaka, and introduces the four 'gatekeepers of liberation' (dvārapālas: śama, vicāra, santoṣa, and sādhasaṅgama). The root text is accompanied throughout by the Advaita Vedāntic commentary Tātparyaprakāśa of Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_YvaasisthaBmumuksuvyavaharaprakara.attribution: The Yogavāsiṣṭha is traditionally attributed to Vālmīki, and the commentary Tātparyaprakāśa is attributed to Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_YvaasisthaBmumuksuvyavaharaprakara.edition: The Yogavāsiṣṭha of Vālmīki with the Commentary Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇatātparyaprakāśa, edited by Wāsudeva Laxmaṇa Śāstrī Paṇśīkar, Bombay, 1918.
SA_MB_YvaasisthaBmumuksuvyavaharaprakara.coverage: partial — Contains the complete second book (Mumukṣuvyavahāraprakaraṇa), sargas 1–20, of the Yogavāsiṣṭha together with the commentary Tātparyaprakāśa.

SA_MB_vyasishtaCutpattiprakarnamHK.title: Yogavāsiṣṭha with Tātparyaprakāśa (prakaraṇa 3: Utpattiprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_vyasishtaCutpattiprakarnamHK.author: Vālmīki, Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī
SA_MB_vyasishtaCutpattiprakarnamHK.summary: The Utpattiprakaraṇa ('Section on Origin/Creation') is the third book of the Yogavāsiṣṭha (traditionally ascribed to Vālmīki), an extensive philosophical poem expounding non-dualism through dialogues between the sage Vasiṣṭha and Prince Rāma. This section demonstrates how the external universe arises as a mental illusion or conceptual vibration (saṃkalpa/cittaspanda) within unconditioned consciousness (cit/Brahman), using extended allegories such as the story of Queen Līlā and the story of Karkaṭī. The root verses are accompanied by Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī's classic Advaita Vedānta commentary, the Tātparyaprakāśa.
SA_MB_vyasishtaCutpattiprakarnamHK.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vālmīki; the commentary Tātparyaprakāśa is by Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī.
SA_MB_vyasishtaCutpattiprakarnamHK.edition: The Yogavāsiṣṭha of Vālmīki with the commentary Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇatātparyaprakāśa, edited by Vasudeva Laxmana Sharma Pansikar, Bombay: Nirṇaya Sāgara Press, 1918.
SA_MB_vyasishtaCutpattiprakarnamHK.coverage: partial — Contains the third book (Utpattiprakaraṇa, ending at sarga 122) with Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī's Tātparyaprakāśa commentary.

SA_MB_vyasishthaDsthitiprakaranamHK.title: Yogavāsiṣṭha with Tātparyaprakāśa (prakaraṇa 4: Sthitiprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_vyasishthaDsthitiprakaranamHK.author: Vālmīki, Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī
SA_MB_vyasishthaDsthitiprakaranamHK.summary: The Sthitiprakaraṇa constitutes the fourth book of the Yogavāsiṣṭha (consisting of 62 sargas), elucidating the apparent preservation and sustenance (sthiti) of the manifest phenomenal cosmos from the perspective of radical non-dualism. Sage Vasiṣṭha instructs Prince Rāma through philosophical discourse and pedagogical narratives—such as the allegorical tales of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa, and the story of the ascetic Dāśūra—demonstrating that the universe possesses no independent reality and is merely an ungrounded vibration of consciousness (cittaspanda) sustained by delusion. The accompanying commentary, the Tātparyaprakāśa by Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī, elucidates the text in terms of classical Advaita Vedānta epistemology and metaphysics.
SA_MB_vyasishthaDsthitiprakaranamHK.attribution: The Yogavāsiṣṭha is traditionally attributed to Vālmīki. The commentary Tātparyaprakāśa is by Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī, pupil of Gaṅgādharendra Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_vyasishthaDsthitiprakaranamHK.edition: The Yogavāsiṣṭha of Vālmīki with the Commentary Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇatātparyaprakāśa, edited by Vasudeva Laxmana Sharma Pansikar. 2 vols. Bombay, 1918.
SA_MB_vyasishthaDsthitiprakaranamHK.coverage: partial — Complete for the fourth book (Sthitiprakaraṇa, sargas 1–62) of the Yogavāsiṣṭha together with the Tātparyaprakāśa commentary.
translations: Vihari-Lala Mitra, The Yoga-Vasistha-Mahārāmāyana of Valmiki. (English)
Swami Venkatesananda, The Supreme Yoga: A New Translation of the Yoga Vasistha, 2 vols. (English)

SA_MB_yogavyasishthaEupasamaprakaranamHK.title: Yogavāsiṣṭha with Tātparyaprakāśa (prakaraṇa 5: Upaśamaprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_yogavyasishthaEupasamaprakaranamHK.author: Vālmīki, Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī
SA_MB_yogavyasishthaEupasamaprakaranamHK.summary: The Upaśamaprakaraṇa is the fifth prakaraṇa of the Yogavāsiṣṭha (or Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇa), an encyclopedic philosophical text framed as instruction given by the sage Vasiṣṭha to Prince Rāma. It focuses on the calming or pacification (upaśama) of mental fabrications and the dissolution of worldly bondage through philosophical discourses and narrative parables (including the stories of Janaka, Bali, Prahlāda, and Uddālaka). The text is accompanied by the extensive commentary Tātparyaprakāśa of Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_yogavyasishthaEupasamaprakaranamHK.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vālmīki with commentary Tātparyaprakāśa by Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_yogavyasishthaEupasamaprakaranamHK.edition: The Yogavāsiṣṭha of Vālmīki with the commentary Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇatātparyaprakāśa, ed. Wāsudeva Laxmaṇa Śāstrī Paṇśīkar, Bombay, 1918.
SA_MB_yogavyasishthaEupasamaprakaranamHK.coverage: partial — Contains the complete fifth prakaraṇa (Upaśamaprakaraṇa), sargas 1–93, with both root text and the Tātparyaprakāśa commentary.

SA_MB_durgarcanasrtiHK.title: Durgārcanasṛti
SA_MB_durgarcanasrtiHK.author: Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Gosvāmī
SA_MB_durgarcanasrtiHK.summary: The Durgārcanasṛti is a 20th-century Śākta/Smārta liturgical digest and manual (paddhati) for the autumnal worship of goddess Durgā during Navarātri. Composed by Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Gosvāmī of Agra and published with a Hindi commentary by his son Ghanaśyāma Gosvāmī, it provides detailed step-by-step instructions for kalaśasthāpana, daily nyāsas, offerings, animal sacrifice substitutes/bali, and the liturgical recitation of the Durgāsaptaśatī.
SA_MB_durgarcanasrtiHK.attribution: The root ritual digest was composed by Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, a Bengali brahmin scholar who taught Yajurveda at the Vidyādharmavarddhinī Pāṭhaśālā in Agra. The accompanying vernacular Hindi commentary (bhāṣāṭīkā) is by his son Ghanaśyāma Gosvāmī.
SA_MB_durgarcanasrtiHK.edition: Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, Durgārcanasṛti, with Hindi commentary (Bhāṣāṭīkā) by Ghanaśyāma Gosvāmī. Agra: Published by Ghanaśyāma Gosvāmī, 1952.
SA_MB_durgarcanasrtiHK.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual from kalaśasthāpanavidhi on pratipad through the Navarātri pūjā sequences, concluding colophon, vijayādaśamī rites, and the embedded 13 chapters of the Durgāsaptaśatī (Devīmāhātmya).

SA_MB_matrkacakravivekaHK.title: Mātṛkācakraviveka with the commentary of Śivānanda
SA_MB_matrkacakravivekaHK.author: Svatantrānandanātha, Śivānanda
SA_MB_matrkacakravivekaHK.summary: The Mātṛkācakraviveka is an esoteric Śākta/Tantric treatise addressing the symbolism of the Sanskrit alphabet (mātṛkācakra). It treats phonemes in relation to vimarśa, waking/dream/deep sleep/turya states, and the Śrīcakra. The e-text includes the mūla along with a vyākhyāna.
SA_MB_matrkacakravivekaHK.attribution: The root work is composed by Svatantrānandanātha.
SA_MB_matrkacakravivekaHK.edition: Pandit Lalita Prasada Dabral (ed.), Princess of Wales Saraswati Bhavana Texts, Benares, 1934.
SA_MB_matrkacakravivekaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the root work together with commentary, concluding with colophons 'iti mātṛkācakraviveke turyavivekaḥ pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ || mātṛkācakravivekamūlaṃ sampūrṇam' and 'iti mātṛkācakravyākhyānaṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_MB_sadhanamala1IHK.title: Sādhanamālā (volume 1)
SA_MB_sadhanamala1IHK.summary: The Sādhanamālā is a Sanskrit anthology of Buddhist tantric ritual and meditation texts (sādhanas), especially those of the Anuttarayoga Tantras, detailing the visualization, iconography, mantras, and ritual applications for propitiating deities. Volume 1 concludes with the Bhṛkuṭīsādhana.
SA_MB_sadhanamala1IHK.attribution: A collection of sādhanas composed by a large range of Buddhist teachers (including Saraha, Nāgārjuna, Kukkuripa, Indrabhūti, Kṛṣṇapāda, and Śabara) from around 630 CE down to the 12th century.
SA_MB_sadhanamala1IHK.edition: Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (ed.), Sādhanamālā, Vol. I, Baroda: Baroda Oriental Institute, 1925.
SA_MB_sadhanamala1IHK.coverage: partial — Contains volume 1 of Benoytosh Bhattacharyya's edition, ending with Bhṛkuṭīsādhana.

SA_MB_saadhanamaalaa-IIHK.title: Sādhanamālā (vol. 2)
SA_MB_saadhanamaalaa-IIHK.summary: A collection of sādhanas, that is, procedures for the worship of Buddhist Tantric deities especially those of the Anuttarayoga Tantras. A description of the deity, its form and colour, vehicle, etc., along with its related visualization is supplied in each sādhana together with that deity's mantra and its applications in worship and yogic practice.
SA_MB_saadhanamaalaa-IIHK.attribution: A collection of sādhanas (Buddhist Tantric meditation and worship procedures) composed by a large range of Buddhist teachers, including Saraha (dated to around 630 CE), Nāgārjuna, Kukkuripa, Indrabhūti, Kṛṣṇapāda, Śabara, and others of the 7th and 8th century, down to contributors of the 12th century.
SA_MB_saadhanamaalaa-IIHK.edition: Benoytosh Bhattacharya (ed.), Sādhanamālā Vol. 2, Baroda: Baroda Oriental Institute, 1925 / 1928.
SA_MB_saadhanamaalaa-IIHK.coverage: partial — Volume 2 (incomplete), beginning with sādhana 171 on p. 343 and breaking off at the balimantra of Mahākāla.

SA_MB_tripuraarahasyaHK.title: Tripurārahasya with Tātparyadīpikā (Jñānakhaṇḍa only)
SA_MB_tripuraarahasyaHK.author: Hāritāyana, Śrīnivāsa
SA_MB_tripuraarahasyaHK.summary: The Jñānakhaṇḍa of the Tripurārahasya, ascribed to Hāritāyana, accompanied by the commentary Tātparyadīpikā of Śrīnivāsa, son of Vaidyanātha Dīkṣita.
SA_MB_tripuraarahasyaHK.attribution: The root text is ascribed to Hāritāyana and the commentary to Śrīnivāsa, son of Vaidyanātha Dīkṣita.
SA_MB_tripuraarahasyaHK.coverage: complete — Jñānakhaṇḍa of the Tripurārahasya with the commentary Tātparyadīpikā.

SA_MB_YogavaasisthaSampurnamIIORGHK.title: Yogavāsiṣṭha with Tātparyaprakāśa (Nirvāṇaprakaraṇa)
SA_MB_YogavaasisthaSampurnamIIORGHK.author: Vālmīki, Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī
SA_MB_YogavaasisthaSampurnamIIORGHK.summary: The Nirvāṇaprakaraṇa is the sixth book of the Yogavāsiṣṭha, divided into two halves (Pūrvārdha and Uttarārdha). It brings the philosophical instructions of sage Vasiṣṭha to Prince Rāma to their culmination, expounding the nature of ultimate liberation (nirvāṇa), the total dissolution of the conceptual mind and world-appearance into pure non-dual consciousness, and the state of the living-liberated sage (jīvanmukta). This volume preserves the text according to the vulgate tradition along with the Advaita commentary Tātparyaprakāśa by Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī.
SA_MB_YogavaasisthaSampurnamIIORGHK.attribution: The root work is attributed to sage Vālmīki. The commentary Tātparyaprakāśa was composed by Ānandabodhendrasarasvatī, pupil's pupil of Sarvajñasarasvatī.
SA_MB_YogavaasisthaSampurnamIIORGHK.edition: The Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha of Vālmīki with the Commentary Vāsiṣṭhamahārāmāyaṇatātparyaprakāśa, Part II (containing Nirvāṇa-Pūrvārdha and Uttarārdha), edited by Vāsudeva Lakṣmaṇa Śarmā Paṇaśīkar, Bombay: Nirṇaya Sāgara Press, 1918.
SA_MB_YogavaasisthaSampurnamIIORGHK.coverage: partial — Contains the sixth prakaraṇa (Nirvāṇaprakaraṇa) along with the commentary Tātparyaprakāśa.

SA_MB_SriikarabhaashyacombinedHK.title: Brahmasūtra with Śrīkarabhāṣya
SA_MB_SriikarabhaashyacombinedHK.author: Bādarāyaṇa, Śrīpati
SA_MB_SriikarabhaashyacombinedHK.summary: The Śrīkarabhāṣya is the primary Vīraśaiva (Liṅgāyat) bhāṣya on Bādarāyaṇa's Brahmasūtras, expounding the doctrine designated as Viśeṣādvaita or Bhedābhedātmaka-Śaktiviśiṣṭādvaita. Śrīpati establishes Paraśiva as the supreme non-dual Brahman, arguing for a relation of natural difference during bondage and non-difference upon liberation (bhedābheda) between the individual soul (jīva) and Brahman. The text also integrates and validates distinctive Vīraśaiva socio-religious practices such as liṅgadhāraṇa, bhasma, and rudrākṣa on Vedic and Upaniṣadic authorities.
SA_MB_SriikarabhaashyacombinedHK.attribution: Śrīpati Paṇḍitācārya was a Vīraśaiva philosopher who composed the Śrīkarabhāṣya on the Vedāntasūtras.
SA_MB_SriikarabhaashyacombinedHK.edition: The Śrīkara Bhāṣya: Being the Vīraśaiva Commentary on the Vedāntasūtras by Śrīpati, ed. C. Hayavadana Rao. Bangalore: Bangalore Press, 1936.
SA_MB_SriikarabhaashyacombinedHK.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on all four adhyāyas of the Brahmasūtra, concluding at Brahmasūtra 4.4.22 (anāvṛttiḥ śabdād anāvṛttiḥ śabdāt).

SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaanandabhattaHK.title: Vijñānabhairava with Vijñānakaumudī
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaanandabhattaHK.author: Ānandabhaṭṭa
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaanandabhattaHK.summary: The Vijñānabhairava is an authoritative non-dual Śaiva tantra presented as an esoteric dialogue between Bhairava and Bhairavī, setting forth 112 dhāraṇās (yogic and meditative contemplations) to attain union with the supreme Bhairava consciousness. This e-text provides the complete tantra alongside the Vijñānakaumudī (or Kaumudī), a commentary by Ānandabhaṭṭa that explicates the contemplative practices.
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaanandabhattaHK.attribution: Vijñānabhairava is an anonymous scriptural tantra belonging to the Trika tradition of Kashmir Śaivism. The commentary Vijñānakaumudī is by Bhaṭṭa Ānanda (Ānandabhaṭṭa).
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaanandabhattaHK.edition: Mukunda Rāma Śāstrī (ed.), Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), 1936.
SA_MB_vijnanabhairavaanandabhattaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Vijñānabhairava with Ānandabhaṭṭa's Vijñānakaumudī commentary, corresponding to pages 1–64 of KSTS vol. 9.
translations: Jaideva Singh, Vijñānabhairava or Divine Consciousness: A Treasury of 112 Types of Yoga, Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1979. (English)

SA_MB_sivastotraavaliiHK.title: Śivastotrāvalī with Vivṛti
SA_MB_sivastotraavaliiHK.author: Utpaladeva, Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_sivastotraavaliiHK.summary: The Śivastotrāvalī is an anthology of devotional hymns composed by the Kashmirian non-dualist philosopher Utpaladeva (c. 10th century CE), celebrating ecstatic devotion (bhakti) to Śiva integrated with the non-dual metaphysics of the Pratyabhijñā school. The accompanying Vivṛti commentary by Kṣemarāja elucidates the philosophical and esoteric Śaiva meanings underlying Utpaladeva's poetic stanzas.
SA_MB_sivastotraavaliiHK.attribution: The Śivastotrāvalī is an anthology of hymns by Utpaladeva. The Vivṛti commentary is by Kṣemarāja.
SA_MB_sivastotraavaliiHK.edition: Śivastotrāvalī with the Commentary Vivṛti of Kṣemarāja, edited by Rai Pramadasa Mitra Bahadur, Benares: Chowkhamba Sanskrit Book Depot, 1902.
SA_MB_sivastotraavaliiHK.coverage: complete — Complete text containing the stotras along with Kṣemarāja's Vivṛti commentary, concluding with Kṣemarāja's closing verses.
translations: Bailly, Constantina Rhodes. Shaiva Devotional Songs of Kashmir. Albany: State University of New York Press, 1987. (English)

SA_MB_sivasuutravimarsiniiHK.title: Śivasūtra with Śivasūtravimarśinī
SA_MB_sivasuutravimarsiniiHK.author: Vasugupta, Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_sivasuutravimarsiniiHK.summary: The Śivasūtra is an aphoristic text of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism, traditionally associated with Vasugupta. Kṣemarāja's Śivasūtravimarśinī is a commentary on it arranged in three unmeṣas.
SA_MB_sivasuutravimarsiniiHK.attribution: The Śivasūtras are ascribed to Vasugupta, and the Vimarśinī commentary was composed by Kṣemarāja, a disciple of Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_sivasuutravimarsiniiHK.edition: The Shiva Sūtra Vimarshinī being the Sūtras of Vasu Gupta, with the Commentary called Vimarshinī by Kṣemarāja, edited by Chatterji J C, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1911 (Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies).
SA_MB_sivasuutravimarsiniiHK.coverage: complete — Text of the three unmeṣas.

SA_MB_pratyabhijnahrdayaHK.title: Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya
SA_MB_pratyabhijnahrdayaHK.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_pratyabhijnahrdayaHK.summary: The Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya ('Heart of Recognition') is an introductory compendium of the Pratyabhijñā philosophy of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism composed by Kṣemarāja. Formulated in twenty aphorisms (sūtras) accompanied by his auto-commentary, the work expounds how universal consciousness contracts to manifest as the individual experiencer and how recognition of one's innate divine nature brings liberation.
SA_MB_pratyabhijnahrdayaHK.attribution: Composed by Kṣemarāja. The work consists of 20 sūtras with his own prose vṛtti (auto-commentary).
SA_MB_pratyabhijnahrdayaHK.edition: The Pratyabhijñā Hṛdaya being a Summary of the Doctrines of the Advaita Shaiva Philosophy of Kashmir, ed. Jagadisha Chandra Chatterji. KSTS 3. Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1911.
SA_MB_pratyabhijnahrdayaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all 20 sūtras with Kṣemarāja's auto-commentary and variant readings recorded from manuscripts (k, kh, g, ṅ).
translations: Singh, Jaideva. 1963. Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam, Sanskrit text with English translation and notes. Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass. (English)
Leidecker, Kurt F. 1938. The Secret of Recognition, published with Sanskrit text. Adyar. (English)

SA_MB_LaghuYV-combinedHK.title: Laghuyogavāsiṣṭha with Vāsiṣṭhacandrikā and Saṃsārataraṇī
SA_MB_LaghuYV-combinedHK.author: Abhinanda, Ātmasukha, Mummaḍi Devarāya
SA_MB_LaghuYV-combinedHK.summary: The Laghuyogavāsiṣṭha is an abridgement attributed to Abhinanda based on the Mokṣopāya / Yogavāsiṣṭha. Framed as a dialogue between Sage Vasiṣṭha and Prince Rāma across six prakaraṇas, it expounds non-dual Vedānta, the nature of the mind, and liberation through philosophical narratives. The e-text includes the commentary Vāsiṣṭhacandrikā.
SA_MB_LaghuYV-combinedHK.attribution: The Laghuyogavāsiṣṭha is attributed in its colophons to Abhinanda (described as tarkavāgīśvara sāhityācārya gauḍamaṇḍalālaṃkāra). The commentary is attributed in catalog metadata to Ātmasukha.
SA_MB_LaghuYV-combinedHK.edition: Laghuyogavāsiṣṭha with commentary Vāsiṣṭhacandrikā, edited by Vasudeva Sharma Panasikara. Bombay, 1933.
SA_MB_LaghuYV-combinedHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of all six prakaraṇas (Vairāgya, Mumukṣuvyavahāra, Utpatti, Sthiti, Upaśama, Nirvāṇa) with accompanying commentary, concluding with Nirvāṇaprakaraṇa sarga 18.

SA_MB_SpandakarikaRamakanthaHK.title: Spandakārikā with Spandavivṛti
SA_MB_SpandakarikaRamakanthaHK.author: Vasugupta, Rāmakaṇṭha
SA_MB_SpandakarikaRamakanthaHK.summary: The Spandakārikā is a foundational treatise of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism. This text contains the kārikās together with the Spandavivṛti by Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha, disciple of Utpaladeva.
SA_MB_SpandakarikaRamakanthaHK.attribution: The commentator here is Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha, a disciple of Utpaladeva (mahāmāheśvarācāryaśiromaṇirājānakaśrīmadutpaladevapādapadmānujīvino rājānakaśrīrāmakaṇṭhasya).
SA_MB_SpandakarikaRamakanthaHK.edition: The Spanda Kārikās with the Vivṛti of Rāma-kaṇṭha, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies, no. 6, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir Government, 1913.
SA_MB_SpandakarikaRamakanthaHK.coverage: complete — Text with Rājānaka Rāmakaṇṭha's Spandavivṛti (pp. 1–168).

SA_MB_aniruddhasamhitaaHK.title: Aniruddhasaṃhitā
SA_MB_aniruddhasamhitaaHK.summary: The Aniruddhasaṃhitā is a Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava āgama in 34 chapters framed as a discourse given by the sage Bhṛgu on Mount Himavat. It covers the core ritual and temple curriculum of the tradition: initiation (dīkṣā), yantras and maṇḍalas, town and temple layout, iconometry and image consecration (pratiṣṭhā), daily and annual festival liturgies (mahotsava, pavitrārohaṇa, etc.), expiatory rites (prāyaścitta), and the installation of Viṣvaksena and the Āḻvārs/devotees (bhakta).
SA_MB_aniruddhasamhitaaHK.attribution: Canonical Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava saṃhitā presented as a dialogue between the sage Bhṛgu and other sages.
SA_MB_aniruddhasamhitaaHK.edition: Aniruddhasaṃhitā, edited by A. Shrinivasa Iyengar, Mysore: published by the editor, 1956.
SA_MB_aniruddhasamhitaaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 34 adhyāyas (adhyāyas 1–34), ending with the final colophon 'aniruddhasaṃhitā samāptā', corresponding to the entire published Mysore 1956 edition.

SA_MB_laghustutiHK.title: Laghustuti with Laghustutivṛtti
SA_MB_laghustutiHK.author: Laghubhaṭṭāraka, Rāghavānanda
SA_MB_laghustutiHK.summary: The Laghustuti is a 21-verse Śākta hymn praising goddess Tripurasundarī, encapsulating the esoteric theology, mantra doctrines, and visualizations of the Śrīvidyā tradition. The accompanying commentary by the ascetic Rāghavānanda Muni unpacks the hymn's non-dualistic Śākta philosophy and its mantric encodings.
SA_MB_laghustutiHK.attribution: The root stotra is traditionally attributed to Laghubhaṭṭāraka. The commentary (vṛtti) is by Rāghavānanda Muni, pupil of Kṛṣṇānanda Muni.
SA_MB_laghustutiHK.coverage: complete — Complete text of the 21-verse hymn together with Rāghavānanda's vṛtti, introductory verses, and final colophons.

SA_MB_paraanandasutraHK.title: Pārānandasūtra (pp. 8 and 43 of the edition missing)
SA_MB_paraanandasutraHK.summary: The Pārānandasūtra (also called Pārānandamīmāṃsā) is an anonymous Śākta-Kaula ritual code written in sūtras, in two adhyāyas of seven āhnikas each, modelled on the Vedic and Mīmāṃsā sūtra style. It teaches one supreme Self, the Īśvaras and the countless souls. It describes the three paths of practice (dakṣiṇa, vāma and uttara), the qualifications of guru and disciple, initiation and order of precedence, daily and special worship, sacrificial sessions (satra) with offerings of wine and animals, expiations, and rules of conduct, and it often cites the differing opinions of named authorities.
SA_MB_paraanandasutraHK.attribution: Anonymous. The Muktabodha header gives 'Author : parānanda muni', but no such attribution appears in the text.
SA_MB_paraanandasutraHK.edition: Pārānanda Sūtra, critically edited by Swami Trivikrama Tīrtha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series, Baroda: Baroda Oriental Institute, 1931.
SA_MB_paraanandasutraHK.coverage: partial — The whole work is present: the pūrvādhyāya with 7 āhnikas and the uttarādhyāya with 7 āhnikas, ending with the final colophons 'iti pārānandasūtre uttarādhyāye saptamamāhnikam || samāptaṃ cedaṃ pārānandasūtram | samāptā ceyaṃ pārānandamīmāṃsā'. The text itself refers to its 'two adhyāyas and fourteen āhnikas'. Two printed pages were not transcribed: page 8 is missing and page 43 is missing.

SA_MB_parasambhumahimnastavaHK.title: Paraśambhumahimnastava
SA_MB_parasambhumahimnastavaHK.author: Durvāsas
SA_MB_parasambhumahimnastavaHK.summary: A devotional and philosophical hymn (mahimnastava) in thirteen prakaraṇas praising Paraśambhu (Supreme Śiva). Composed in the idiom of non-dual Śaivism and Śrīvidyā esotericism, it integrates cosmogony, mantra, kuṇḍalinī yoga, and mātṛkā metaphysics into the praise of transcendent consciousness.
SA_MB_parasambhumahimnastavaHK.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Durvāsas, who bears the initiate title Krodhabhaṭṭāraka.
SA_MB_parasambhumahimnastavaHK.edition: Paraśambhumahimnastava by Durvāsas (Krodhabhaṭṭāraka). Madras: N. Rajam & Co., 1946.
SA_MB_parasambhumahimnastavaHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 13 prakaraṇas, ending with the Upasaṃhāraprakaraṇa and a full concluding colophon.

SA_MB_natyasatrav1HK.title: Nāṭyaśāstra with Abhinavabhāratī (chapters 1–7)
SA_MB_natyasatrav1HK.author: Bharata, Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_natyasatrav1HK.summary: The Nāṭyaśāstra is the foundational Sanskrit treatise on dramaturgy, performance, dance, music, and aesthetic theory, ascribed to the mythic sage Bharata Muni. This volume comprises chapters 1 through 7 accompanied by the Abhinavabhāratī commentary of Abhinavagupta. These chapters cover the mythological origins of drama, stagecraft and playhouse architecture (prekṣāgṛha), stage rituals (pūrvaraṅga), classical dance movements (karaṇas and aṅgahāras), and the foundational exposition of rasa (aesthetic relish) and bhāva (affective states).
SA_MB_natyasatrav1HK.attribution: The commentary Abhinavabhāratī is by Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_natyasatrav1HK.edition: Nāṭyaśāstra with the commentary of Abhinavagupta ch. 1 - 7, edited by M. Ramakrishna Kavi, second revised edition by K. S. Ramaswami Shastri, Gaekwad's Oriental Series no. 36, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1956.
SA_MB_natyasatrav1HK.coverage: partial — Chapters 1 to 7 of the work. The e-text concludes with the chapter 7 colophon: 'iti śrībhāratīye nāṭyaśāstre bhāvavyañjako nāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ'.
translations: Gnoli, Raniero. 1956: The Aesthetic Experience according to Abhinavagupta, Rome (Second Edition, Varanasi: Chowkhamba, 1968). (English)

SA_MB_guhyasamaajatantraHK.title: Guhyasamājatantra
SA_MB_guhyasamaajatantraHK.summary: The Guhyasamājatantra is the foundational scripture of the Buddhist Mahāyoga / Anuttarayoga tantric class, centered on Akṣobhya and the fivefold Buddha family maṇḍala. Structured in eighteen chapters, it details deity visualization, mantras, ritual enactments, and subtle-body meditation forming the basis of generation (utpattikrama) and completion (niṣpannakrama) stage yogas. Celebrated for its paradoxical, antinomian imagery representing non-dual gnosis, it gave rise to two prominent Indian exegetical schools: the Jñānapāda school and the Ārya school.
SA_MB_guhyasamaajatantraHK.attribution: Esoteric Buddhist scripture (Anuttarayogatantra) traditionally attributed to the Buddha as Buddhavacana.
SA_MB_guhyasamaajatantraHK.edition: Benoytosh Bhattacharya (ed.), Guhyasamāja Tantra or Tathāgataguhyaka, Baroda: Baroda Oriental Institute, 1931.
SA_MB_guhyasamaajatantraHK.coverage: complete — Text of the eighteen chapters (paṭalas) of the mūlatantra (designated as pūrvārdhakāya in the closing colophon), concluding with paṭala 18 (sarvaguhyanirdeśavajrajñānādhiṣṭhāna).
translations: Francesca Fremantle, A Critical Study of the Guhyasamāja Tantra, PhD thesis, University of London, 1971. (English)
Alex Wayman, Yoga of the Guhyasamājatantra: The Arcane Lore of Forty Verses, Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1977. (English)

SA_MB_natyrasatrav2HK.title: Nāṭyaśāstra with Abhinavabhāratī (chapters 8–18)
SA_MB_natyrasatrav2HK.author: Bharata, Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_natyrasatrav2HK.summary: Chapters 8 through 18 of the Nāṭyaśāstra along with the Abhinavabhāratī commentary of Abhinavagupta. This middle block of the treatise focuses extensively on physical and gestural representation (āṅgikābhinaya), including movements of the head, hands (hasta), waist, and feet (cārī, maṇḍala, gati), followed by stage production conventions (pravṛtti, dharmi), poetic meter (chandas), literary qualities and figures of speech (guṇa, doṣa, alaṃkāra), and the formal dramatic genres (daśarūpaka).
SA_MB_natyrasatrav2HK.attribution: The commentary Abhinavabhāratī (or Nāṭyavedavivṛti) is by Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_natyrasatrav2HK.edition: Nāṭyaśāstra of Bharatamuni, with the Commentary of Abhinavagupta, Vol. II (Chapters VIII-XVIII), ed. M. Ramakrishna Kavi / K. S. Ramaswami Shastri, Gaekwad's Oriental Series no. 68, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1934.
SA_MB_natyrasatrav2HK.coverage: partial — Covers chapters (adhyāyas) 8 through 18, corresponding to Volume 2 of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series edition.

SA_MB_natyasatrav3HK.title: Nāṭyaśāstra with Abhinavabhāratī (chapters 19–27)
SA_MB_natyasatrav3HK.author: Bharata, Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_natyasatrav3HK.summary: Chapters 19–27 of the foundational treatise on ancient Indian theatre, dramaturgy, and poetics (Nāṭyaśāstra) alongside the commentary Abhinavabhāratī by Abhinavagupta. These chapters treat dramatic structure and junctures (sandhi and sandhyaṅga), the major and minor play types (daśarūpaka), dramatic styles (vṛtti), costuming and make-up (āhāryābhinaya), character classification and acting conventions, and theatrical success (siddhi). Abhinavagupta's commentary integrates dramatic practice with non-dual Kashmir Śaiva philosophy and rasa aesthetics.
SA_MB_natyasatrav3HK.attribution: The Nāṭyaśāstra is attributed to Bharata. The commentary Abhinavabhāratī is by Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_natyasatrav3HK.edition: Nāṭyaśāstram with the commentary of Abhinavagupta ch. 19-27, edited by M. Ramakrishna Kavi, second revised edition by K. S. Ramaswami Shastri, Gaekwads Oriental Series no. 124, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1934.
SA_MB_natyasatrav3HK.coverage: partial — Chapters 19–27 and appendix, corresponding to Volume 3 of the Gaekwad's Oriental Series edition.
translations: Gnoli, Raniero. 1956: The Aesthetic Experience according to Abhinavagupta, Rome (2nd ed. Varanasi: Chowkhamba. (English)

SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa1HK.title: Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa (part 1)
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa1HK.summary: The Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa is an extensive early Buddhist Mantrayāna ritual manual (kalpa), framed as a Mahāyāna sūtra, focused on the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī. It details iconographic conventions, maṇḍala construction, mantras, mudrās, dhāraṇīs, astrology, and apotropaic rituals.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa1HK.edition: T. Gaṇapatiśāstrī (ed.), Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpam Part 1. Government Press Travancore, 1920.
translations: phags pa 'jam dpal gyi rtsa ba'i rgyud (Derge Kangyur D 543): translated by Kumārakalaśa, shAkya blo gros (Tibetan)

SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa2HK.title: Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa (chapters 23–47)
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa2HK.summary: The Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa is an encyclopedic Buddhist ritual work belonging to the early Mantrayāna (traditionally classified in Tibetan canonical taxonomies as a Kriyātantra), framed as a Mahāyāna vaipulyasūtra delivered by Śākyamuni Buddha. This second volume (chapters 23–47) details ritual procedures including mantroddhāra (extraction of mantras), extensive mudrāvidhi (hand gestures and seals), maṇḍala construction, and karmavidhi rites associated with Mañjuśrī and retinue. It represents one of the earliest preserved Indian Buddhist tantric sourcebooks, integrating esoteric ritual technology with classic Mahāyāna doctrine.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa2HK.attribution: Scriptural Buddhist Mahāyāna-vaipulyasūtra / Kriyātantra text traditionally framed as the teaching of the Buddha Śākyamuni.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa2HK.edition: T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī (ed.), The Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa, Part II, Trivandrum Sanskrit Series No. 76, Travancore: Government Press, 1922.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa2HK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters 23–47, corresponding to Volume II (TSS 76) of T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī's edition (beginning p. 253).

SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa3HK.title: Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa (chapters 50–55)
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa3HK.summary: The Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa is an encyclopedic Buddhist ritual scripture centered on the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, classified in Tibetan tradition as a Kriyā-tantra. This concluding third volume (chapters 50–55) contains rituals for the wrathful deity Yamāntaka, alchemical practices (hemasādhana), and the celebrated fifty-first chapter (Rājavyākaraṇaparivarta), which records dynastic prophecies concerning ancient and early-medieval Indian monarchs.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa3HK.attribution: A composite Buddhist canonical work combining Mahāyānasūtra and Mantrayāna ritual and astrological traditions, traditionally presented as the words of Śākyamuni Buddha and Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa3HK.edition: T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī (ed.), The Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa, Part III, Trivandrum Sanskrit Series No. 84, Government Press Travancore, 1922, pp. 544–722.
SA_MB_aryamanjusrimulakalpa3HK.coverage: partial — Chapters 50–55 (ending with the colophon of scribe Ravicandra of the Śrīmūlaghoṣavihāra), corresponding to volume 3 (pp. 544–722) of T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī's edition.
translations: phags pa 'jam dpal gyi rtsa ba'i rgyud (Derge Kangyur D 543): translated by Kumārakalaśa, shAkya blo gros (Tibetan)

SA_MB_tantrabhidanaHK.title: Tantrābhidhāna
SA_MB_tantrabhidanaHK.summary: Tantrābhidhāna is an anthology of traditional Sanskrit Tantric lexica, seed-syllable glossaries (koṣa, nighaṇṭu), and gesture manuals compiled and published as Volume 1 of Arthur Avalon's Tantrik Texts series. The compilation provides technical keys for decoding secret seed-syllables (bīja), coded letter designations (saṅketa), and ritual gestures (mudrā) in Śākta and Tantric liturgical literature. Major texts included are Puruṣottamadeva's Ekākṣarakoṣa, Bhairava's Bījanighaṇṭumantrakoṣa, sections from the Rudrayāmala, Bhūtaḍāmara, Varadā, and Vāmakeśvara Tantras, and the exhaustive Varṇabījakoṣa.
SA_MB_tantrabhidanaHK.attribution: A modern compilation of medieval Sanskrit Tantric dictionaries, seed-syllable glossaries, and hand gesture manuals, edited under the direction of Arthur Avalon (Sir John Woodroffe).
SA_MB_tantrabhidanaHK.edition: Tantrābhidhāna with Bījanighaṇṭu, Bījābhidhāna, Mantrārthābhidhāna, Varṇabījakoṣa and Mudrānighaṇṭu, ed. Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya Tarkasāṃkhyavedāntatīrtha, Tantrik Texts, London: Luzac & Co. / 1937.
SA_MB_tantrabhidanaHK.coverage: complete — Text of the expanded edition of Tantrik Texts Vol. 1, containing the initial index (Sūcīpatra), nine root lexica/tracts, and the concluding Varṇabījakoṣa.

SA_MB_kamalanamniHK.title: Kamalā
SA_MB_kamalanamniHK.author: Prāṇamañjarī
SA_MB_kamalanamniHK.summary: The Kāmyakarmakamalā (also known as Kamalā or Kamalānāmnī Tripurasundarīpaddhati) is an extensive Śrīvidyā liturgical manual for the worship of Tripurasundarī, detailing yantras, nyāsas, and rituals.
SA_MB_kamalanamniHK.attribution: The introductory line identifies the work as 'kamalānāmnī śrīpremanidhipaṇḍitadharmapatnyā prāṇamañjaryākhyayā racitā', composed by Prāṇamañjarī, the wife of Premanidhi Paṇḍita. The colophon attributes the work to Premanidhi Śarman of Kūrmācala.
SA_MB_kamalanamniHK.edition: Manuscript transcription: Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) Reel No. B 181/1, Manuscript No. 5-1922.
SA_MB_kamalanamniHK.coverage: complete — Transcription of the manuscript (NGMCP Reel No. B 181/1, Manuscript No. 5-1922).

SA_MB_kulacuu.daama.nitantraHK.title: Kulacūḍāmaṇitantra
SA_MB_kulacuu.daama.nitantraHK.summary: The Kulacūḍāmaṇitantra is an important Śākta Kaula scripture comprising seven chapters (paṭalas). Unusually structured as a nigama—wherein Śiva (Bhairava) serves as the questioner while the Goddess (Bhairavī/Kālī) reveals teachings—the text expounds the inner and outer rites of Kula worship, including mantra-sādhana, nyāsa, kulācāra practices, and philosophical discussions on Śiva and Śakti.
