SA_MB_kulacuu.daama.nitantraHK.attribution: Revealed Śākta scripture formatted as a nigama, in which Bhairavī instructs Bhairava.
SA_MB_kulacuu.daama.nitantraHK.edition: Arthur Avalon [John Woodroffe] (ed.), Kulacūḍāmaṇi Nigama, Madras: Ganesh and Co., 1915.
SA_MB_kulacuu.daama.nitantraHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 7 chapters (paṭalas 1–7), with embedded editorial apparatus and notes.

SA_MB_mahaalak.smiipuujaavidhiHK.title: Mahālakṣmīpūjāvidhi (incomplete: fols. 1a–17a)
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiipuujaavidhiHK.summary: An anonymous Nepalese ritual manual for the worship of Mahālakṣmī. It details the preliminary rites including worship of the guru and Gaṇapati, the sun offering, nyāsa, worship of the doorway, maṇḍala deities, and lokapālas, followed by offerings of flowers, leaves, and other articles accompanied by verses. The text breaks off incomplete during the damana offering on fol. 17a.
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiipuujaavidhiHK.attribution: Anonymous liturgical handbook preserved in a Nepalese manuscript.
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiipuujaavidhiHK.coverage: partial — Folio markers run continuously from '1a)' to '17a)'. The text covers the preliminaries and nyāsa, ātma- and dvārapūjā, the maṇḍala deities and lokapālas, and offerings to Mahālakṣmī. It breaks off mid-word in the damana offering ('mahālakṣmī mahādevī damanaṃ pra', fol. 17a); the remaining rites and colophon are missing. ilx_skt metadata: 'incomplete, lacking explicit+final colophon'.

SA_MB_mantradaanavidhiHK.title: Mantradānavidhi
SA_MB_mantradaanavidhiHK.summary: A brief Tantric ritual manual on the procedure for mantra transmission (mantradāna), extracted from or attributed to the Mahākālasaṃhitā. It details the eightfold fragrant mixtures (gandhāṣṭaka) for Śaiva, Vaiṣṇava, Gāṇapatya, and Śākta devotions, guidelines for placing ritual lamps, incense, and naivedya offerings, the rules for whispering mantras into the initiate's ear according to varna and gender, and concluding recitations exchanged between guru and disciple.
SA_MB_mantradaanavidhiHK.attribution: Ascribed in the colophon to the Mahākālasaṃhitā.
SA_MB_mantradaanavidhiHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript NGMCP 2690 (Reel no. 154/10), dated Vikrama Saṃvat 1952 CE), scribed by Dharmarāja Tripāṭhī.
SA_MB_mantradaanavidhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete short ritual tract of 2 folios transcribed from manuscript NGMCP reel 154/10.

SA_MB_kalaagniyajnavidhiHK.title: Kālāgniyajñavidhi
SA_MB_kalaagniyajnavidhiHK.summary: The Kālāgniyajñavidhi is an unpublished ritual manual providing practical liturgical instructions, bījamantras, and ritual steps for conducting a fire sacrifice (yajña/homa) dedicated to Bhairava, Mātṛkās, Yoginīs, and associated deities, incorporating offerings of clarified butter, meat oblations (māṃsāhuti), tantric life-cycle rites (saṃskāras), and protective boundary rituals.
SA_MB_kalaagniyajnavidhiHK.attribution: Preserved in manuscript form in Nepal (NGMCP manuscript 1696/2203, reel no. B 178/36).
SA_MB_kalaagniyajnavidhiHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) reel no. B 178/36 (ms. no. 1696/2203).
SA_MB_kalaagniyajnavidhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript NGMCP reel B 178/36 (ms. no. 1696/2203).

SA_MB_kalasaarcanavidhiHK.title: Siddhilakṣmīkalaśārcanavidhi
SA_MB_kalasaarcanavidhiHK.summary: A Nepalese Śākta ritual manual (paddhati) in Sanskrit mixed with Newari liturgical rubrics, detailing the vessel-worship rite (kalaśārcana) for the goddess Siddhilakṣmī. Associated with offerings at the Nyātāpola temple of Bhaktapur, the text encompasses opening stotras to Bhairava, Kubjikā, Siddhilakṣmī, and Mahākāla, followed by pātrapūjā, bhūtaśuddhi, nyāsa, and mantra japa.
SA_MB_kalasaarcanavidhiHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of NGMCP manuscript 1-1496 (reel no.: A 1232/17), unpublished e-text prepared by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00411), 2011/2017.
SA_MB_kalasaarcanavidhiHK.coverage: complete — Transcription of manuscript NGMCP 1-1496 (p. 1a–38), concluding with ritual requisites and a figure/diagram on p. 38.

SA_MB_madhyapii.thapujavidhiHK.title: Madhyapīṭhapūjāvidhi
SA_MB_madhyapii.thapujavidhiHK.summary: A Newar Śākta-Śaiva ritual worship manual (pūjāvidhi / paddhati) dedicated to the worship of the central seat (madhyapīṭha) of the Goddess in the Kubjikā/Tripurā/Siddhilakṣmī tradition (specifically Kulacakreśvarī and Siddhilakṣmī). Prepared for the Malla king of Bhaktapur, Jaya Bhūpatīndramalla, for the Viśvajātrā, it sets out nyāsa, offerings (bali), stotras (including the Gālinīdaṇḍaka and Mahāmāyāstotra), and Gaṇeśa āveśamantras.
SA_MB_madhyapii.thapujavidhiHK.attribution: Anonymous ritual manual composed or copied for the Malla king of Bhaktapur, Jaya Bhūpatīndramalla, named as the patron (yajamāna) in the saṃkalpa on fol. 1a–b.
SA_MB_madhyapii.thapujavidhiHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of NGMCP reel no. A 245/10 (ms. no. 1062).
SA_MB_madhyapii.thapujavidhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript (fol. 1a–35b).

SA_MB_m.rtyunjayakalpaHK.title: Mṛtyuñjayakalpa
SA_MB_m.rtyunjayakalpaHK.summary: The Mṛtyuñjayakalpa (as preserved in NGMCP MS 4-286, Reel A 172/6) is an astrological and ritual pacification (śānti) compendium. It sets forth Sanskrit verses on auspicious timing for lifecycle rituals (saṃskāras such as puṃsavana), planetary positions and transits, astrological afflictions, and various pacification rites to avert death and illness (mṛtyubhaya-śānti).
SA_MB_m.rtyunjayakalpaHK.attribution: Preserved anonymously in a manuscript under this title in the NGMCP collection.
SA_MB_m.rtyunjayakalpaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 4-286, Reel No. A 172/6.

SA_MB_phe.takapratis.thacandikagnividhiH.title: Pheṭakapratiṣṭhācaṇḍikāgnividhi
SA_MB_phe.takapratis.thacandikagnividhiH.summary: A Newar Śākta ritual liturgy (vidhi/paddhati) detailing the consecration and installation (pratiṣṭhā) of a ritual box/casket (pheṭaka) combined with a fire sacrifice to Caṇḍikā (caṇḍikāgniyajña). Folio 1a names King Bhūpatīndra Malla as the patron (yajamāna) performing the rite for the gratification of his tutelary deity (svaṣṭadevatā). The manual prescribes preliminary ancestral rites (ābhyudayikaśrāddha), nyāsa, homa with various offerings, animal sacrifice (paśujāga), and final dismissals (visarjana).
SA_MB_phe.takapratis.thacandikagnividhiH.attribution: A Newar ritual liturgy mentioning King Bhūpatīndra Malla (śrīśrījayabhūpatīndramala) as the yajamāna on folio 1a.
SA_MB_phe.takapratis.thacandikagnividhiH.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) Reel No. V 192/15.
SA_MB_phe.takapratis.thacandikagnividhiH.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript from fol. 1a to fol. 262a, concluding with 'śrī 3 caṇḍikāgni yajñavidhi saṃpūrṇaḥ'.

SA_MB_siddhilak.smii-aramikaHK.title: Siddhilakṣmīpūjāpaddhati
SA_MB_siddhilak.smii-aramikaHK.summary: A Śākta-Tāntrika liturgical manual (paddhati) for the esoteric worship of the goddess Siddhilakṣmī. It details purification rites, cakra worship, bali offerings, stotras, and concluding wave-offering (ārātrika) procedures.
SA_MB_siddhilak.smii-aramikaHK.edition: Manuscript transcription of NGMCP manuscript 1399 (Reel No. V 199/9).
SA_MB_siddhilak.smii-aramikaHK.coverage: complete — Transcription of manuscript NGMCP 1399 (Reel V 199/9), ending at fol. 57b.

SA_MB_siddhilaksmiidevyarcanaHK.title: Siddhilakṣmīdevyārcana
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiidevyarcanaHK.summary: An anonymous ritual manual (pūjāpaddhati) composed in Sanskrit with Newari ritual instructions for the worship of the goddess Siddhilakṣmī, a major protective deity associated with the Kubjikā, Kālīkrama, and royal Malla religious traditions of Nepal. It contains procedures for pot installation (kalaśasthāpana), purification of vessels (arghapātraśodhana), various nyāsas, invocations on behalf of the patron (yajamāna), mudrās, and mantra sequences.
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiidevyarcanaHK.attribution: Anonymous liturgical manual preserved in the Newar Tantric ritual tradition of the Kathmandu Valley.
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiidevyarcanaHK.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of NGMCP MS 1373, Reel No. V 199/13 (ca. la. naṃ. 2254), Kathmandu, Nepal.
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiidevyarcanaHK.coverage: partial — Lacks explicit and final colophon; ends abruptly with ritual bīja/mantra tables on p. 19.

SA_MB_siddhilasmiikotyahutidinakrtyaHK.title: Siddhilakṣmīkoṭyāhutidinakṛtya
SA_MB_siddhilasmiikotyahutidinakrtyaHK.summary: A Nepalese Śākta ritual manual (dinakṛtya) detailing the day-to-day procedures for performing a koṭyāhuti dedicated to the goddess Siddhilakṣmī. Associated with King Sumati Jayajitāmitramalla Deva, the text specifies daily sequences including pūjā of kalaśas, nyāsas, offerings to deities and homa offerings.
SA_MB_siddhilasmiikotyahutidinakrtyaHK.attribution: Anonymous Nepalese Śākta ritual manual. The colophon records the date Samvat 811 Kārttika-śukla-navamī during the reign of King Sumati Jayajitāmitramalla Deva.
SA_MB_siddhilasmiikotyahutidinakrtyaHK.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) manuscript 1365 RA 250/1 (reel no. unstated in header), dated Samvat 811.
SA_MB_siddhilasmiikotyahutidinakrtyaHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript, extending from p. 1a to the concluding colophon ('iti dinakṛtya samāptaṃ ||').

SA_MB_siddhilaksmiyutaksaramalamamtraHK.title: Siddhilakṣmyayutākṣaramālāmantra
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiyutaksaramalamamtraHK.summary: The Siddhilakṣmyayutākṣaramālāmantra ('Ten-Thousand-Syllable Garland Mantra of Siddhilakṣmī') is an extensive Śākta ritual mantra text attributed to the Kālānalatantra. The text opens with viniyoga formulas (naming Bharadvāja as ṛṣi) and unfolds a massive litany of bījamantras and invocations praising the goddess in her terrifying and auspicious forms.
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiyutaksaramalamamtraHK.attribution: Ascribed in the final colophon to the Śrīkālānalatantra.
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiyutaksaramalamamtraHK.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcribed from Kathmandu, National Archives / NGMCP manuscript no. 11397 (reel no. V 199/90).
SA_MB_siddhilaksmiyutaksaramalamamtraHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript text spanning folios 1–38a, ending with the colophon 'iti śrīkālānalatantre siddhilakṣmyāyutākṣaramālāmantraḥ samāptam'.

SA_MB_ucchistacandaaliniikalpaHK.title: Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālinīkalpa
SA_MB_ucchistacandaaliniikalpaHK.summary: A Śākta Tantric ritual manual (kalpa) dedicated to Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālinī (also invoked as Sumukhī or Ucchiṣṭa-Mātaṅgī), an outcaste form associated with the Mahāvidyā Mātaṅgī. The text sets forth her mantra system, iconography and visualization (dhyāna), oblations of impure food leftovers (ucchiṣṭa-bali), homa procedures, and nyāsa rites for protection, vaśīkaraṇa (subjugation), and the removal of adversities.
SA_MB_ucchistacandaaliniikalpaHK.attribution: Scriptural dialogic revelation attributed to Mahādeva (Śiva) and Pārvatī; colophons and introductory lines invoke the Ugrarudrayāmala, Śāradātilaka, and Viśvasāratantra.
SA_MB_ucchistacandaaliniikalpaHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 52, Reel no. B 116/13.
SA_MB_ucchistacandaaliniikalpaHK.coverage: incomplete — Noted as incomplete (lacking explicit+final colophon) in ilx_skt catalog; transcribed from folios 1a–7b of the manuscript, with a colophon towards the end ('iti śrīvisvasāro ucāramahādevatraṇītaṃ śrīpārvatiyodhasanmukhī kalpaṃ samāptaḥ') followed on fol. 7b by nyāsa and dhyāna formulas.

SA_MB_ugracandapujapaddhatiHK.title: Ugracaṇḍāpūjāpaddhati
SA_MB_ugracandapujapaddhatiHK.summary: The Ugracaṇḍāpūjāpaddhati is an anonymous Śākta-Tāntrika liturgical manual preserved in Nepal, prescribing the worship of Ugracaṇḍā (associated with Kubjikā and Siddhilakṣmī ritual cults). It details karanyāsa, aṅganyāsa, vaktranyāsa, preparation of water and argha vessels, liṅgārcana, and deity visualizations (dhyāna) with attendant bījamantras and Newar ritual rubrics.
SA_MB_ugracandapujapaddhatiHK.attribution: Anonymous Śākta/Tantric ritual paddhati transmitted in Nepalese manuscripts.
SA_MB_ugracandapujapaddhatiHK.edition: Transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript 1696/979 (Reel no. B 177/22), folios 1a–23 (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_ugracandapujapaddhatiHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript covering folios 1a through 23.

SA_MB_urdhvamnayadamanarohanapaddhatiHK.title: Ūrdhvāmnāyadamanārohaṇapaddhati
SA_MB_urdhvamnayadamanarohanapaddhatiHK.summary: A Śākta-tantric ritual manual (paddhati) detailing the damanārohaṇa rite (the springtime ritual offering of the fragrant damanaka plant) according to the Ūrdhvāmnāya stream of Tripura/Śrīvidyā worship. The text combines Sanskrit verses, bījas, and mantra invocations to Tripurā, kṣetrapālas, and yoginīs with practical rubrics written in classical Newari (Nepal Bhasa). The surviving manuscript witness was transcribed in the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal Saṃvat 796 (1675/1676 CE).
SA_MB_urdhvamnayadamanarohanapaddhatiHK.attribution: Anonymous Śākta-tantric ritual manual containing Sanskrit mantras and liturgical verses interspersed with ritual performance directions in classical Newari (Nepal Bhasa).
SA_MB_urdhvamnayadamanarohanapaddhatiHK.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) reel no. B 178/18 (manuscript 126), dated NS 796 / CE). Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, digital library catalog no. M00421 (2011/2017).
SA_MB_urdhvamnayadamanarohanapaddhatiHK.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual transcribed from folios 1 to 31b, concluding with the ritual completion colophon and a scribal date of Nepal Saṃvat 796 (c. 1675/1676 CE).

SA_MB_urddhvamnayapujavidhiHK.title: Ūrdhvāmnāyapūjāvidhi
SA_MB_urddhvamnayapujavidhiHK.summary: An anonymous Śākta ritual manual (pūjāvidhi / paddhati) detailing the worship procedure of the Ūrdhvāmnāya ('upward transmission') current, focusing on Mahātripurasundarī. It details preliminary rites (bhūtaśuddhi, prāṇapratiṣṭhā), extensive nyāsa sequences (mātṛkā-, kara-, and vaśinī-nyāsa), the guru lineage (divyaugha, siddhaugha, mānavaugha), the nine āvaraṇas of the Śrīcakra, the six āmnāyas, and bali offerings to subsidiary deities.
SA_MB_urddhvamnayapujavidhiHK.attribution: Anonymous ritual paddhati preserved in Nepalese manuscript transmission.
SA_MB_urddhvamnayapujavidhiHK.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (NGMCP) MS 126 (Reel no. B 179/3), unpublished.
SA_MB_urddhvamnayapujavidhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of NGMCP manuscript 126 (Reel no. B 179/3, fol. 1 to fol. 106b).

SA_MB_T0274makutagamaHK.title: Makuṭāgama (Sārasaṅgraha recension in 3,000 verses)
SA_MB_T0274makutagamaHK.summary: A 3,000-verse 'Sārasaṅgraha' recension of the Makuṭāgama (Makuṭatantra), one of the 28 Siddhāntāgamas of Śaiva Siddhānta, transmitted in an IFP transcript. It begins with the descent of the scripture (tantrāvatāra) and treats bathing and ācamana, daily worship, initiation, the festival, expiation, kṛttikādīpa, snapana, iconography and installation, pavitrārohaṇa, prāṇāyāma, the qualities of the ācārya, Kālī and Bhairava worship, funerary rites, and the ūrdhva- and ambā-cakras, ending with a meditation on Śiva as dancer and Dakṣiṇāmūrti in Cidambaram.
SA_MB_T0274makutagamaHK.coverage: complete — Complete as a recension: the transcript T0274 pp. 648–873 contains the table of contents (19 sections from tantrāvatāra to ambācakra) and all listed sections from 'tantrāvatāraḥ prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ' to the ambācakravidhi, followed by a short closing section on the Dakṣiṇeśvara/Naṭarāja meditation (pp. 870–873), and ends with the final colophon 'iti makuṭasaṃhitāyāṃ sārasaṅgrahe trisahasras samāptaḥ'. Internal gaps: the end of the kṛttikādīpa chapter is missing (transcript note 'paṭalasya antyabhāgo na vidyate', p. 812), and there are many lacunae marked '* * (?)'.

SA_MB_jnaanaratnaavaliiHK.title: Jñānaratnāvalī (opening missing)
SA_MB_jnaanaratnaavaliiHK.author: Jñānaśiva
SA_MB_jnaanaratnaavaliiHK.summary: The Jñānaratnāvalī is a comprehensive Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual (paddhati) composed in Vārāṇasī by Jñānaśiva. The work expounds Saiddhāntika ritual praxis, including purificatory rites, daily worship (nityapūjā), initiation rituals (dīkṣā), installation, and related ceremonies.
SA_MB_jnaanaratnaavaliiHK.attribution: Composed at Vārāṇasī by Jñānaśiva, pupil of Vyomaśambhu (closing verses: Somaśambhu, Dharmaśambhu "Lakṣādhyāyī", Vyomaśambhu, "vāraṇasīvāsinā śrīmajjñānaśivena").
SA_MB_jnaanaratnaavaliiHK.edition: IFP/EFEO transcript T0231, Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient, Pondicherry, 643 pp. (modern transcript).
SA_MB_jnaanaratnaavaliiHK.coverage: partial — Nearly complete: the transcript (IFP T0231, 643 pp.) begins with the note "prathama patraṃ na dṛśyate" (first leaf not found), so the opening is lost; the text then runs to the closing verses and the final colophon "śrīmajjñānaratnāvalī samāptā". Scattered lacunae marked "* *".

SA_MB_kuladiipikaaHK.title: Uttaraṣaṭka with Kuladīpikā, Tripurāsārasamuccaya with Saṃpradāyadīpikā (Uttaraṣaṭka incomplete at beginning)
SA_MB_kuladiipikaaHK.author: Bhaṭṭanāga
SA_MB_kuladiipikaaHK.summary: The e-text transcribes a South Indian composite manuscript of Kaula and Śrīvidyā works. It contains (1) the Uttaraṣaṭka or Ṣaḍvidyāprakāśa, ascribed to the Rudrayāmala (Nityaklinnā section), on yonimudrā, the revival of defective mantras, kuṇḍalinī yoga and the six vidyās; (2) the Kuladīpikā, an anonymous commentary on it in five chapters; (3) Bhaṭṭanāga's Tripurāsārasamuccaya, a ten-chapter Śrīvidyā manual on Tripurasundarī worship, nyāsa, the cakras, yantras and homa; and (4) the Saṃpradāyadīpikā, a commentary on the Tripurāsārasamuccaya.
SA_MB_kuladiipikaaHK.attribution: The text itself nowhere names Tryambakabhaṭṭāraka; the attribution in the Muktabodha catalogue header is unverified and rejected as author in ilx_skt. The Tripurāsārasamuccaya colophons read 'iti śrī bhaṭṭanāgaviracite tripurāsārasamuccaye ... paṭalaḥ'. The verse following the Saṃpradāyadīpikā, 'tejānandasya śiṣyena kṛṣṇānandasya sūriṇā | likhitaṃ saṃpradāyasya dīpikā cāmbikājñayā', likely identifies Kṛṣṇānanda merely as copyist ('likhitam').
SA_MB_kuladiipikaaHK.coverage: partial — Composite transcript. The Uttaraṣaṭka begins abruptly mid-verse ('koṭisamaprabham |'). It runs to the colophon 'iti śrīrudrayāmale ... uttarabhāge nityaklinnāprakaraṇe ṣaḍvidyāprakāśāyāmuttaraṣaṭkaṃ saṃpūrṇam'. The Kuladīpikā has the colophons 'ityuttaraṣaṭkavivaraṇe kuladīpikāyāṃ prathamaḥ paṭaḥ' to '... pañcamaḥ paṭalaḥ'. The Tripurāsārasamuccaya has paṭalas 1–10, ending 'iti śrī bhaṭṭanāgaviracite tripurāsārasamuccaye daśamaḥ paṭalaḥ'. The Saṃpradāyadīpikā has paṭalas 1–10, followed by the scribal verse. After that, a short unidentified passage of Tripurā pūjā prose breaks off mid-sentence.

SA_MB_parakramapujaHK.title: Parākramapūjā
SA_MB_parakramapujaHK.summary: An unpublished Kaula Śākta ritual manual (pūjāpaddhati) centered on the worship of the goddess Parā (also addressed as Nityā/Tripurā), affiliated with the Śāmbhava stream (Aśeṣāmbhavīmata). The text details internal yogic contemplation (kuṇḍalinī, nāḍīs, cakra-piercing) as well as external Kaula ritual procedures, nyāsa sequences, and extensive mantras exhibiting affinities with the Kubjikā and Śrīvidyā traditions.
SA_MB_parakramapujaHK.attribution: The text is an untitled ritual manual within a composite manuscript; the descriptive title Parākramapūjā was assigned by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski.
SA_MB_parakramapujaHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: National Archives, Kathmandu / Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 5-4656, Reel No. A 175/11 (ending at fol. 77b).
SA_MB_parakramapujaHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the final text in the manuscript (ending at fol. 77b with 'samāptam').

SA_MB_hayasirsapancaraatramHK.title: Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra (Ādikāṇḍa, paṭalas 1–14)
SA_MB_hayasirsapancaraatramHK.summary: A Vaishnava Pancharatra Samhita dealing entirely with matters related to the construction and re-construction of temples and consecration of images. This initial section (Ādikāṇḍa, paṭalas 1–14) treats topics including vāstumaṇḍala layout, iṣṭakānyāsa (laying of bricks/stones), and prāsādadevatāsaṃsthāpana (installation of shrine deities).
SA_MB_hayasirsapancaraatramHK.attribution: A Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra Saṃhitā dealing with temple architecture and image consecration. Accompanied by Sanskrit commentary notes.
SA_MB_hayasirsapancaraatramHK.edition: Hayaśīrṣapañcarātram, edited by Pandit Bhuban Mohan Sankhyatiratha, Rajshahi: Varendra Research Society, 1952 (pp. 1–88).
SA_MB_hayasirsapancaraatramHK.coverage: partial — Contains paṭalas 1–14 of the Ādikāṇḍa (ending with prāsādadevatāsaṃsthāpanapaṭala on p. 88 of the printed edition, verse 325 of the section).

SA_MB_kalikapuranaHK.title: Kālikāpurāṇa
SA_MB_kalikapuranaHK.summary: The Kālikāpurāṇa is a Śākta text detailing the mythology and worship of the Goddess in her various manifestations, containing extensive narrative, ritual, and devotional teachings.
SA_MB_kalikapuranaHK.edition: Pañcānana Tarkavāgīśa (ed.), Kālikāpurāṇam, Calculta: Vangavasi Pree, 1909.
SA_MB_kalikapuranaHK.coverage: complete — Complete text in 90 adhyāyas, ending at 90.42 with 'iti śrīkālikāpurāṇe navatitamo'dhyāyaḥ || 90 || iti śrīkālikāpurāṇaṃ samāptam |'.

SA_MB_mahaaguhyakaaliividhaanamHK.title: Mahāguhyakālīvidhāna (incomplete: fols. 1a–32)
SA_MB_mahaaguhyakaaliividhaanamHK.summary: A ritual manual for the worship of Mahāguhyakālī. The surviving portion covers preliminary rites including nyāsa, deharakṣakakavaca, and invocation rites, breaking off during the āvāhana.
SA_MB_mahaaguhyakaaliividhaanamHK.attribution: A ritual manual (vidhāna/paddhati) for the worship of Mahāguhyakālī.
SA_MB_mahaaguhyakaaliividhaanamHK.edition: Unedited manuscript: Nepal, NGMCP manuscript no. 2048, reel No. B 139/2. Transcription entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski.
SA_MB_mahaaguhyakaaliividhaanamHK.coverage: partial — Folio markers run from 'p. 1a)' to 'p. 32)'. The text covers preliminary rites including svalpaṣoḍhānyāsa, deharakṣakakavaca, and invocation (āvāhana), breaking off mid-formula ('śrīmahāguhya kālī karālī ihāgacchehā', p. 32) without a colophon. Ilx_skt catalog records the text as incomplete. Muktabodha has a nearly identical transcription, M00516.

SA_MB_mahaalak.smiidiipadaanavidhiHK.title: Mahālakṣmīdīpadānavidhi
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiidiipadaanavidhiHK.summary: A Nepalese Śākta-Tantric ritual manual (paddhati/vidhi) for the solemn offering and lighting of the great lamp (mahādīpa / Newari mahādīpacchoyā) to Mahālakṣmī, closely linked with Siddhilakṣmī and the Kubjikā tradition. The manual specifies the patron (yajamāna) as King Bhūpatīndra Malla of Bhaktapur (r. 1696–1722 CE) and incorporates nyāsa rites, pūjā recitations to the Mātṛkās and Bhairavas, and Newari rubrics.
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiidiipadaanavidhiHK.attribution: Anonymous Nepalese liturgical manual combining Sanskrit verses and mantras with Newari ritual stage directions. Names King Jaya Bhūpatīndra Malla ('jayarūpatīndramallavarvaṇa' / 'jaya rūpatīndramalla devasya') as yajamāna.
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiidiipadaanavidhiHK.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Kathmandu, National Archives / NGMCP ms. no. 1571, reel no. A 246/2.
SA_MB_mahaalak.smiidiipadaanavidhiHK.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript across folios 1a–51b, closing with the final colophon 'iti śrī śrī śrīmahālakṣmīsake mahādīpacchota kāyā vidhiḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_ParaatrimsikavivaranaHK.title: Parātriṃśikā with Parātriṃśikāvivaraṇa
SA_MB_ParaatrimsikavivaranaHK.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_MB_ParaatrimsikavivaranaHK.summary: The Parātriṃśikāvivaraṇa is Abhinavagupta's commentary on the Parātriṃśikā. The text elaborates non-dual Trika metaphysics, phonemic mysticism, the nature of ultimate reality (anuttara), and related tantric topics.
SA_MB_ParaatrimsikavivaranaHK.attribution: The Vivaraṇa commentary was composed by Abhinavagupta.
SA_MB_ParaatrimsikavivaranaHK.edition: Mukunda Rāma Shāstrī (ed.), The Parā-trimśikā with commentary. The latter by Abhinava Gupta, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Bombay / Srinagar: Kashmir and Jammu Research Dept., 1918.
SA_MB_ParaatrimsikavivaranaHK.coverage: complete — Parātriṃśikā with Abhinavagupta's Vivaraṇa commentary spanning pp. 1–283 of KSTS 18.
translations: Raniero Gnoli (trans.), Il commento di Abhinavagupta alla Parātriṃśikā (Parātriṃśikātattvavivaraṇam), Serie Orientale Roma 58, Rome: Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente, 1985. (Italian)

SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaanamT0143HK.title: Vāruṇapaddhati with Vāruṇapaddhativyākhyāna
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaanamT0143HK.author: Varuṇa, Śivottama
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaanamT0143HK.summary: The Vāruṇapaddhati is a Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual composed by Varuṇa outlining the essential framework for initiation (dīkṣā) and temple consecration/installation (pratiṣṭhā). This e-text provides the 119 kārikās together with the commentary (vyākhyāna or vṛtti) by Bhaṭṭa Śivottama, concluding with the Pratiṣṭhāviveka prakaraṇa.
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaanamT0143HK.attribution: The root paddhati names its author as Śrīvaruṇa in verse 119. The commentary is ascribed to Bhaṭṭa Śivottama in the introductory heading and final colophon.
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaanamT0143HK.edition: Transcript IFP/EFEO T00143 (Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient).
SA_MB_varunapaddhativyaakhyaanamT0143HK.coverage: complete — Complete in two prakaraṇas (dīkṣā and pratiṣṭhā), ending with the colophon of the second prakaraṇa (iti bhaṭṭa śivottamakṛtau pratiṣṭhāviveka prakaraṇaṃ dvitīyam) after 119 verses.

SA_MB_kaalikaarahasyamHK.title: Kālikārahasya (chapter 5)
SA_MB_kaalikaarahasyamHK.summary: A Śākta tantric text presented as chapters of the Kālikārahasya within the Mahābhairavatantra, framed as a dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara. It provides ritual instructions for the worship, nyāsa, and mantra-japa of the goddess Dakṣiṇākālikā, detailing auspicious times and procedures to attain protection, destruction of sins, and worldly and spiritual rewards.
SA_MB_kaalikaarahasyamHK.attribution: Scriptural tantric work presented as a dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara (Umāmaheśvarasaṃvāda) belonging to the Mahābhairavatantra.
SA_MB_kaalikaarahasyamHK.edition: Manuscript transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry / École française d'Extrême-Orient (IFP/EFEO) transcript T00900 (copied from Adyar Library manuscript 1273). Unpublished transcript.
SA_MB_kaalikaarahasyamHK.coverage: partial — Contains chapters 3 to 5 (ending with 'īśvaraprokto nāma tṛtīyaḥ paṭalaḥ', 'caturthodhyāyaḥ', and 'pañcamaḥ paṭalaḥ') in 8 pages of manuscript transcript.

SA_MB_maahesvaratantramHK.title: Māheśvaratantra
SA_MB_maahesvaratantramHK.summary: The Māheśvaratantra is a Sanskrit tantric scripture presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī. While situated within a Śaiva dialogic frame, the work combines Śaiva and Vaiṣṇava elements, featuring devotion to Kṛṣṇa alongside ritual instruction, initiation (dīkṣā), mantras, and cosmogonic teachings.
SA_MB_maahesvaratantramHK.attribution: Revealed scriptural tantra framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī / Umā (Śivomāsaṃvāda).
SA_MB_maahesvaratantramHK.coverage: complete — Complete in 51 paṭalas with 3,060 verses, concluding with colophon 'iti śrīmanmāheśvaratantre uttarakhaṇḍe śivomāsaṃvāde ekapañcāśatamaṃ paṭalam' and verse total count 3060.

SA_MB_Tararahasyavrtti2HK.title: Tārārahasyavṛtti
SA_MB_Tararahasyavrtti2HK.author: Śaṅkara
SA_MB_Tararahasyavrtti2HK.summary: The Tārārahasyavṛtti (or Tārārahasyavṛttikā) is a 15-chapter Śākta ritual manual and commentary focusing on the cult of Tārā and her related forms (Mahānīlasarasvatī, Ugratārā, Ekajaṭā), ancillary to the Tārārahasya tradition. Authored by the Bengali tantric writer Śaṅkara, the text systematizes daily worship (nityapūjā), initiation (dīkṣā), preliminary recitation (puraścaraṇa), desire-oriented rites (kāmya), kumārī worship, stotras, oblations (homa), and esoteric contemplative meanings (vāsanā) drawn from scriptures like the Nīlatantra, Matsyasūkta, and Vīratantra.
SA_MB_Tararahasyavrtti2HK.attribution: The author identifies himself in the concluding verses as Śaṅkara, grandson of Lambodara and son of Kamalākara. He is a medieval Bengali Śākta digest compiler commonly referred to as Gauḍīya Śaṅkara, distinct from Ādi Śaṅkarācārya and Brahmānanda Giri.
SA_MB_Tararahasyavrtti2HK.edition: Manuscript transcription from Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS No. A 1337, Reel No. D 28/26 (dated Saṃvat 1957), transcribed under the supervision of Mark S.G. Dyczkowski for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. m00323).
SA_MB_Tararahasyavrtti2HK.coverage: complete — Complete in 15 paṭalas as concluded at paṭala 15.

SA_K10_sf140_sc.title: Mahāsamājasūtra
SA_K10_sf140_sc.summary: An Āgama sūtra parallel to the Pāli Mahāsamayasutta (DN 20). While the Buddha stays in the Great Wood near Kapilavastu with five hundred arhats, gods from the ten-thousand world system gather. Four Brahmakāyika gods praise the assembly in verse, and the Buddha then names the assembled classes of yakṣas, nāgas, gandharvas and devas in verse. The sūtra ends with Māra's failed attempt to disturb the assembly.
SA_K10_sf140_sc.attribution: Early Buddhist canonical scripture preserved in the Central Asian Sanskrit Āgama tradition (Sarvāstivāda/Mūlasarvāstivāda), corresponding to the Mahāsamaya Sutta of the Pāli Dīgha Nikāya (DN 20) and Chinese Dīrghāgama 19 (T 1).
SA_K10_sf140_sc.edition: Lore Sander, 1987 (pp. 165–179; reprinting Ernst Waldschmidt's revised version: 'Central Asian Sūtra Fragments and their Relation to the Chinese Āgamas', in H. Bechert [ed.], Die Sprache der ältesten buddhistischen Überlieferung, 1980, pp. 148–162).
SA_K10_sf140_sc.coverage: complete — Reconstructed text ending with the antaroddāna and 'mahāsamājasūtraṁ samāptaḥ samāptañ ca iti'.
translations: Maurice Walshe, The Long Discourses of the Buddha, Boston: Wisdom Publications, 1987 (DN 20, Pāli parallel). (English)

SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAA_hk.title: Parāprāveśikā
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAA_hk.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAA_hk.summary: The Parāprāveśikā is a short prose primer of nondual Kashmir Śaivism (Trika/Pratyabhijñā) composed by the 11th-century master Kṣemarāja. It expounds the nature of Parameśvara as pure light (prakāśa) and reflective awareness (vimarśa), details the thirty-six principles of cosmic manifestation (tattvas) from Śiva down to earth (pṛthivī), and introduces the supreme Śakti (Parā) and the esoteric significance of the mantra aham.
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAA_hk.attribution: Explicitly attributed to Kṣemarāja in the opening and closing colophons (śrīmanmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryakṣemarājaviracitā parāprāveśikā). The bracketed glosses and final verses are editorial additions by Paṇḍit Mukundarāma Śāstrī and his staff.
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAA_hk.edition: The Parāprāveśikā of Kṣemarāja, edited with notes by Paṇḍit Mukunda Rāma Śāstrī, Bombay: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1918 (Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies).
SA_MB_PARAAPRAAVESIKAA_hk.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Parāprāveśikā together with the bracketed glosses and concluding editorial verse apparatus from the KSTS editio princeps.

SA_K10_sf107_sc.title: Daśottarasūtra
SA_K10_sf107_sc.summary: The Daśottarasūtra is a canonical Sanskrit sūtra belonging to the Dīrghāgama of the Sarvāstivāda tradition, corresponding to the Pāli Dasuttara Sutta. Spoken by Śāriputra, it organizes fundamental doctrinal categories (dharmas) into ten numerical sections (1 to 10), each classified under ten functional sets (dharmas to be developed, abandoned, cultivated, realized, etc.). It served as a major mnemonic compendium and scholastic matrix in early Buddhism.
SA_K10_sf107_sc.attribution: Spoken by the venerable Śāriputra; corresponds to Chinese Dīrghāgama (T 1).
SA_K10_sf107_sc.edition: Kusum Mittal, Dogmatische Begriffsreihen im älteren Buddhismus, I: Fragmente des Daśottarasūtra aus zentralasiatischen Sanskrit-Handschriften (Sanskrittexte aus den Turfanfunden 4), Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1957; and Dieter Schlingloff, Dogmatische Begriffsreihen im älteren Buddhismus, Ia: Daśottarasūtra IX–X, Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1962.
SA_K10_sf107_sc.coverage: complete — Reconstructed composite text covering all ten numerical sections (adhyāyas 1–10) and opening/closing frames based on Central Asian Sanskrit manuscript fragments.
translations: Kusum Mittal (1957) & Dieter Schlingloff (1962), Dogmatische Begriffsreihen im älteren Buddhismus, Berlin: Akademie-Verlag. (German)

SA_K14_n3013u.title: Mahāvastvavadāna (volume 1)
SA_K14_n3013u.summary: The Mahāvastu (or Mahāvastvavadāna) is an extensive canonical biography of the Buddha in Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit belonging to the Vinayapiṭaka of the Lokottaravādin Mahāsāṃghika lineage. Volume 1 recounts the past karmic preparations of Śākyamuni Buddha under earlier Buddhas such as Dīpaṅkara, presents the four bodhisattva practices (caryās) and an early version of the ten stages (daśabhūmi), depicts cosmological realms including the naraka hells, and relates numerous jātakas up to the Bodhisattva's residence in Tuṣita heaven prior to descent.
SA_K14_n3013u.attribution: Canonical scripture preserved as part of the Vinayapiṭaka of the Lokottaravāda branch of the Mahāsāṃghika school (madhyadeśikānāṃ pāṭhena vinayapiṭakasya mahāvastuye ādi).
SA_K14_n3013u.edition: S. Bagchi (ed.), Mahāvastu-Avadāna, Buddhist Sanskrit Texts No. 14, Darbhanga: The Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning (reprinting Émile Senart's 1882 text with Sanskrit introductions).
SA_K14_n3013u.coverage: partial — Volume 1 only (of 3 volumes). Covers the Nidāna, Bodhisattvacaryā, Daśabhūmika, hell descriptions, and various avadānas and jātakas, ending with the announcement of the Bodhisattva's descent from Tuṣita heaven (Senart vol. 1, p. 366).
translations: J. J. Jones (tr.), The Mahāvastu, 3 vols., London: Luzac & Co. / Pali Text Society, 1949, 1952, 1956 (Sacred Books of the Buddhists, 18, 19). (English)

SA_GSP29_nysvbh_u.title: Nyāyasūtra with Nyāyabhāṣya
SA_GSP29_nysvbh_u.author: Gautama, Vātsyāyana
SA_GSP29_nysvbh_u.summary: The Nyāyasūtra of Akṣapāda Gautama is the foundational text of the Nyāya school of classical Indian philosophy, systematically organizing epistemology, dialectics, debate methodology, and realist metaphysics across five books centered on sixteen topics (ṣoḍaśapadārtha). Vātsyāyana's Nyāyabhāṣya is the earliest extant commentary on the sūtras, providing authoritative expositions of the four pramāṇas (perception, inference, analogy, and verbal testimony) and defending the Nyāya philosophical framework.
SA_GSP29_nysvbh_u.attribution: The Nyāyasūtra is traditionally attributed to Gautama (Akṣapāda); the commentary (Nyāyabhāṣya) is by Vātsyāyana.
SA_GSP29_nysvbh_u.coverage: complete — Complete in five adhyāyas: the e-text runs from the bhāṣya's opening (pramāṇato 'rthapratipattau ...) through NyS 5.2.24, Vātsyāyana's closing verse (yo 'kṣapādam ṛṣiṃ nyāyaḥ ...) and the colophons 'iti vidvadvaravātsyāyanaviracite nyāyabhāṣye pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ // nyāyadarśanaṃ cedaṃ samāptam'.
translations: Nyayasutras of Gautama: A System of Indian Logic with Vatsyayana's Nyāyabhāṣya, ed./trans. Ganganatha Jha. (English)
Nyāya Philosophy, tr. with Vatsyāyana's bhāṣya, D. Chattopadhyaya and M. Gangopadhyaya, Calcutta. (English)

SA_GSP27_motik_1u.title: Mokṣopāya with Mokṣopāyaṭīkā (prakaraṇa 1: Vairāgyaprakaraṇa)
SA_GSP27_motik_1u.author: Vālmīki, Bhāskarakaṇṭha
SA_GSP27_motik_1u.summary: The Mokṣopāya is a philosophical work associated with the Kashmirian recension of the Yogavāsiṣṭha. This initial section, the Vairāgyaprakaraṇa (32 sargas), portrays the deep existential disillusionment and world-weariness of young prince Rāma. Bhāskarakaṇṭha's commentary Mokṣopāyaṭīkā elucidates the text.
SA_GSP27_motik_1u.attribution: The Mokṣopāyaṭīkā is by Bhāskarakaṇṭha, son of Avatārakaṇṭha and grandson of Vaiḍūryakaṇṭha.
SA_GSP27_motik_1u.edition: Bhāskarakaṇṭhas Mokṣopāya-Ṭīkā, ed. Walter Slaje, 4 vols., Graz 1993-1996 / Aachen 2002 [here: 1. Prakaraṇa (Vairāgya)].
SA_GSP27_motik_1u.coverage: partial — Complete text of Prakaraṇa 1 (Vairāgyaprakaraṇa, sargas 1–32), including root strophes and commentary.

SA_K14_sf273_sc.title: Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra (excerpt)
SA_K14_sf273_sc.summary: The Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra is a canonical Āgama narrative belonging to the (Mūla-)Sarvāstivāda tradition recounting the final months, decease, cremation, and relic distribution of Gautama Buddha, paralleling the Pāli Mahāparinibbānasutta (DN 16). In this excerpt, the Buddha moves to the Gandhamādana Caitya, assembles the Saṅgha at the upasthānaśālā, exhorts the monks to practice harmony and master the twelvefold scripture (dvādaśāṅgapravacana), and formally announces that his parinirvāṇa will take place in Kuśinagara after three months.
SA_K14_sf273_sc.attribution: Canonical Sanskrit Āgama sūtra, surviving in Central Asian and Gilgit manuscript fragments, generally associated with the Sarvāstivāda and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions.
SA_K14_sf273_sc.edition: Ernst Waldschmidt, Das Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra: Text in Sanskrit und Tibetisch, verglichen mit dem Pāli nebst einer Übersetzung der chinesischen Entsprechung im Vinaya der Mūlasarvāstivādins, auf Grund von Turfan-Handschriften herausgegeben und bearbeitet, 3 Bde. (Abhandlungen der Deutschen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin, Klasse für Sprachen, Literatur und Kunst, Jg. 1949 Nr. 1, 1950 Nr. 2, 1950), Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1950–1951.
SA_K14_sf273_sc.coverage: excerpt — Short excerpt consisting of 20 paragraphs (labeled Wal_1–Wal_20) from Ernst Waldschmidt's composite edition, recording the episode at the Gandhamādana Caitya where the Buddha summarizes the twelvefold pravacana and predicts his parinirvāṇa in three months at Kuśinagara.

SA_GV01_rvh1-10u.title: Ṛgveda
SA_GV01_rvh1-10u.summary: The Ṛgveda (or Ṛgvedasaṃhitā) is an ancient canonical scripture of the Vedic tradition. It is arranged into ten maṇḍalas containing 1,028 hymns (sūktas) dedicated to deities including Agni, Indra, Soma, and Varuṇa, designed for solemn śrauta rituals alongside cosmogonic, philosophical, and elegiac verse.
SA_GV01_rvh1-10u.edition: Theodor Aufrecht (ed.), Die Hymnen des Rigveda, 2nd ed., 2 vols., Bonn: Adolph Marcus, 1877.
SA_GV01_rvh1-10u.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 10 maṇḍalas (1,028 sūktas, from RV 1.1.1 to RV 10.191.4).
translations: Stephanie W. Jamison and Joel P. Brereton, trs., The Rigveda: The Earliest Religious Poetry of India. An English Translation, 3 vols., New York: Oxford University Press, 2014. (English)

Karl Friedrich Geldner (transl.), Der Rig-Veda: aus dem Sanskrit ins Deutsche übersetzt und mit einem laufenden Kommentar versehen, Harvard Oriental Series, Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press, 1951. (German)
Louis Renou (transl.), Études védiques et pāṇinéennes, 17 vols., 1955–. (French)

SA_GSP29_antarkpu.title: Tarkasaṃgraha
SA_GSP29_antarkpu.author: Annambhaṭṭa
SA_GSP29_antarkpu.summary: The Tarkasaṃgraha is an introductory manual of syncretic Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika philosophy by Annambhaṭṭa. It synthesizes the seven Vaiśeṣika ontological categories (padārthas) with the Nyāya epistemological framework and four means of valid knowledge (pramāṇas). Celebrated for its succinctness and pedagogical clarity, it remains the most widely studied elementary primer of Indian logic in traditional and modern curricula.
SA_GSP29_antarkpu.attribution: Attributed to Annambhaṭṭa, explicitly named in the concluding verse (AnTs_81: annaṃbhaṭṭena viduṣā racitas tarkasaṃgrahaḥ).
SA_GSP29_antarkpu.coverage: complete — Complete root text comprising 81 numbered sections (AnTs_1 to AnTs_81), including the opening maṅgala verse and concluding verse.

SA_GP12_garup1_u.title: Garuḍapurāṇa (part 1: Ācārakāṇḍa)
SA_GP12_garup1_u.summary: The Pūrvakhaṇḍa (also termed Ācārakāṇḍa or Karmakāṇḍa) forms the first and largest section of the Garuḍapurāṇa, comprising 240 adhyāyas. It functions as an encyclopedic digest of classical Indian sciences and religious practice, covering cosmogony, Vaiṣṇava worship and ritual iconography, temple architecture and installation of deities (pratiṣṭhā), sacred geography and Gayā pilgrimage (Gayāmāhātmya), gemmology (ratnaparīkṣā), medicine (Āyurvedic nidāna and cikitsā), astrology, and dharmaśāstra rules.
SA_GP12_garup1_u.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the legendary sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa; framed as Viṣṇu's teaching to Garuḍa narrated by Sūta Lomaharṣaṇa/Ugraśravas to the sages in Naimiṣāraṇya.
SA_GP12_garup1_u.edition: Bombay: Venkatesvara Steam Press (or a reprint thereof)
SA_GP12_garup1_u.coverage: partial — Adhyāyas 1–240 (GarP_1,1.1 – GarP_1,240.43), complete from the opening to the colophon 'iti śrīgāruḍe prathamāṃśa ācārakāṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ'. This is the Pūrvakhaṇḍa/Ācārakāṇḍa of the Veṅkaṭeśvara vulgate. The Uttarakhaṇḍa (Dharmakāṇḍa/Pretakalpa, 49 adhyāyas, entry garup2_u) and the Brahmakāṇḍa (29 adhyāyas, entry garup3_u) are not included.
translations: The Garuda Purânam, translated by Manmatha Nath Dutt, Calcutta: 1908 (reprint: Chowkhamba Sanskrit Series Office, Varanasi, 1968). (English)

SA_GV00_avs___u.title: Atharvavedasaṃhitā (Śaunaka)
SA_GV00_avs___u.summary: The Atharvavedasaṃhitā in the Śaunaka recension is the fourth canonized Vedic saṃhitā, comprising twenty kāṇḍas of metrical hymns and prose mantras. Unlike the predominantly śrauta sacrificial orientation of the Ṛgveda, Sāmaveda, and Yajurveda, this collection largely focuses on domestic rites, healing, protection against curses and sorcery, royal rituals, and speculative cosmogonic hymns on cosmic principles such as Skambha, Prāṇa, and Rohita.
SA_GV00_avs___u.attribution: Canonical Vedic text traditionally associated with the seer lineages of Atharvan, Aṅgiras, and Bhṛgu, but classified as authorless (apauruṣeya) revelation.
SA_GV00_avs___u.edition: Gli inni dell' Atharvaveda (Saunaka), trasliterazione a cura di Chatia Orlandi, Pisa 1991, collated with the ed. R. Roth and W. D. Whitney: Atharva Veda Sanhita, Berlin 1856; with numbering in [...] in Books 11–20 following ed. by Vishva Bandhu: Atharvaveda (Saunaka), with the Pada-Patha and Sayanacarya's commentary, Hoshiarpur 1960–1964 (Vishveshvaranand indological series, 13–17).
SA_GV00_avs___u.coverage: complete — Complete text across all 20 kāṇḍas of the Śaunaka recension, running from AVŚ 1.1.1a to AVŚ 20.143.9c.
translations: William Dwight Whitney, Atharva-Veda Samhitā, translated with a critical and exegetical commentary, revised and edited by Charles Rockwell Lanman, 1905. (English)
Maurice Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharva-Veda, Together with Extracts from the Ritual Books and the Commentaries, Sacred Books of the East, Oxford, 1897. (English)
Ralph T. H. Griffith, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, Translated with a popular commentary, 1895–. (English)

SA_K10_sf75_sc.title: Śaktisūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_sf75_sc.summary: A Central Asian Sanskrit manuscript fragment of the Śaktisūtra. The discourse commends the cultivation of loving-kindness (maitracitta) towards all living beings, teaching that even brief meditation for the time it takes to milk a cow (godohanamātram) protects one from beasts, yakṣas, and harmful non-human spirits.
SA_K10_sf75_sc.attribution: Canonical Buddhist sūtra of the Sarvāstivāda tradition.
SA_K10_sf75_sc.coverage: fragment — A short fragment consisting of 5 lines/segments from a Central Asian manuscript leaf.

SA_GK23_jonart_pu.title: Rājataraṅgiṇī
SA_GK23_jonart_pu.author: Jonarāja
SA_GK23_jonart_pu.summary: Rājataraṅgiṇī chronicle from the pen of Jonarāja, court Paṇḍit to Sulṭān Zayn al-'Ābidīn, covering kingship in Kaśmīr (ad 1148–1459), continuing from Kalhaṇa's chronicle up to Jayasiṃha, together with additions and continuation attributed to Pseudo-Jonarāja.
SA_GK23_jonart_pu.attribution: Chronicled by Jonarāja at the court of Sulṭān Zayn al-'Ābidīn; contains interpolations and continuation designated as Pseudo-Jonarāja.
SA_GK23_jonart_pu.edition: Slaje, Walter: Kingship in Kaśmīr (ad 1148-1459). From the pen of Jonarāja, court Paṇḍit to Sulṭān Zayn al-'Ābidīn. Halle: 2014.
SA_GK23_jonart_pu.coverage: complete — Text of Jonarāja's chronicle along with the interpolations and continuation of Pseudo-Jonarāja (verses 1–901 and JRt_B.434–1334) as edited by Walter Slaje.

SA_GK21_sokss_pu.title: Kathāsaritsāgara
SA_GK21_sokss_pu.author: Somadeva
SA_GK21_sokss_pu.summary: The Kathāsaritsāgara ('Ocean of the Streams of Story') is an encyclopedic 11th-century Sanskrit narrative poem composed in Kashmir by Somadeva for Queen Sūryavatī. Arranged into 18 lambakas and 124 taraṅgas, it preserves a major Kashmiri verse recension of Guṇāḍhya's lost Paiśācī epic, the Bṛhatkathā. The central frame tale follows Prince Naravāhanadatta's romantic adventures and quest to attain sovereignty over the Vidyādharas, embedding numerous cycles of folk tales, fables, and romances, including the Vetālapañcaviṃśatikā.
SA_GK21_sokss_pu.attribution: Somadeva, son of the Brahmin Rāma, composed the work at the court of King Kalaśa of Kashmir for Queen Sūryavatī (c. 1063–1081 CE), adapting Guṇāḍhya's Bṛhatkathā into Sanskrit verse.
SA_GK21_sokss_pu.edition: Durgaprasad and Parab, Bombay: Nirnaya-Sagar Press 1915.
SA_GK21_sokss_pu.coverage: complete — Complete text in 18 lambakas comprising 124 taraṅgas and over 21,000 verses, ending with Somadeva's epilogue verses praising Queen Sūryavatī and King Kalaśa.
translations: The Kathá sarit ságara; or, Ocean of the streams of story, translated from the original Sanskrit by C. H. Tawney, Calcutta, 1880 and 1884. (English)

The Ocean of Story, being C. H. Tawney's translation of Somadeva's Kathā Sarit Sāgara, edited with introduction, fresh explanatory notes and terminal essay by N. M. Penzer, 10 vols., London, 1924–1928. (English)

SA_GV05_chupsb_u.title: Chāndogyopaniṣad with Chāndogyopaniṣadbhāṣya
SA_GV05_chupsb_u.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GV05_chupsb_u.summary: The Chāndogyopaniṣad is one of the earliest and most important mukhya (principal) Upaniṣads, belonging to the Kauthuma/Rāṇāyanīya recension of the Sāmaveda. In eight adhyāyas, it progresses from esoteric meditations on the chanting of the Sāman and the sacred syllable Om (udgītha) to quintessential metaphysical doctrines of early Vedānta, including the Śāṇḍilya-vidyā, the dialogue of Satyakāma Jābāla, Uddālaka Āruṇi's instruction to Śvetaketu culminating in the mahāvākya 'tat tvam asi' (6.8.7), and Prajāpati's teachings on the four states of the self. The accompanying commentary by Śaṅkarācārya interprets the text as an exposition of non-dual reality (advaita), demonstrating that ritual action produces transient heavenly realms, whereas direct knowledge of the non-dual Brahman-Ātman leads to absolute liberation (mokṣa).
SA_GV05_chupsb_u.attribution: Mūla: Chāndogyopaniṣad (Sāmaveda), anonymous. Commentary: Śaṅkara's Chāndogyopaniṣadbhāṣya (final colophon: '... śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpādakṛtau cchāndogyopaniṣadvivaraṇe aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ').
SA_GV05_chupsb_u.coverage: complete — Complete across all 8 adhyāyas (chapters) and their respective khaṇḍas, covering both the mūla text and Śaṅkara's bhāṣya up to the final colophon at 8.15.
translations: Patrick Olivelle (trans.), The Early Upaniṣads: Annotated Text and Translation, New York, Oxford 1998. (English)

SA_K10_sf265_sc.title: Satyasūtra
SA_K10_sf265_sc.summary: A short canonical Buddhist sūtra set at Śrāvastī. The discourse explains that monks go forth into homelessness purely for the direct realization and comprehension of the Four Noble Truths (catur-āryasatya), enjoining ardent effort, mindfulness, and clear comprehension. The text concludes with a short protective (rakṣā) benediction.
SA_K10_sf265_sc.coverage: complete — Preserves the short sūtra from nidāna through the colophon, concluding with a rakṣā formula.

SA_K10_uvs_sc.title: Udānavarga (fragments of chapters 1–33)
SA_K10_uvs_sc.summary: The Udānavarga is the Sarvāstivāda anthology of verses (udāna) arranged by topic in 33 chapters (varga), parallel to the Pali Dhammapada and in part to the Udāna. This e-text holds the Subaši recension, preserved in a Sanskrit manuscript on wooden boards from Subaši near Kucha (Pelliot collection, Paris). That recension is notable for its strongly Prakritic, partly Gāndhārī-influenced language; the manuscript is fragmentary throughout.
SA_K10_uvs_sc.attribution: Early Buddhist tradition and Tibetan/Chinese sources attribute the compilation/redaction of the Sanskrit Udānavarga to the Sarvāstivādin master Bhadanta Dharmatrāta.
SA_K10_uvs_sc.edition: Hideaki Nakatani (ed.), Udānavarga de Subaši: Édition critique du manuscrit sanskrit sur bois provenant de Subaši, Paris: Collège de France, Institut de Civilisation Indienne, 1987 (Publications de l'Institut de Civilisation Indienne, série in-8°, fasc. 53).
SA_K10_uvs_sc.coverage: partial — All 33 vargas present (1 Anityavarga … 33 Brāhmaṇavarga, ending with the varga colophon 'brāhmaṇa-varggo trayas-trīṣa samāptaḥ' and the closing uddāna), but the wooden-board manuscript is badly damaged: whole stanza ranges are marked lost (e.g. ch. 1 '[Stances 1–40 ? perdues]', so ch. 1 survives only in fragments of the last stanzas) and many pādas are lacunose. About 38,000 characters, far less than the complete Udānavarga (c. 1,000 stanzas in Bernhard's edition).

SA_K10_sf73_sc.title: Pravāraṇasūtra
SA_K10_sf73_sc.summary: The Pravāraṇasūtra is a canonical Buddhist discourse set on the full moon day marking the conclusion of the rainy season retreat (pravāraṇā). The disciple Vāgīśa extemporaneously recites seven verses praising the purity, unshakeable liberation, and detachment of the assembly of five hundred arhats surrounding the Buddha.
SA_K10_sf73_sc.attribution: Canonical discourse belonging to the Saṃyuktāgama (extant in Sanskrit Central Asian fragments).
SA_K10_sf73_sc.edition: A. F. Rudolf Hoernle (ed.), Manuscript Remains of Buddhist Literature found in Eastern Turkestan, Oxford: Clarendon Press.
SA_K10_sf73_sc.coverage: complete — Complete short sūtra preserved in this fragment manuscript, containing the introductory frame, seven stanzas spoken by Āyuṣmat Vāgīśa (Hoe_1 to Hoe_7), the final approval of the Buddha, and the closing colophon 'pravāraṇa sūtraṁ'.

SA_K10_sf279_sc.title: Māratajjanīyasūtra (fragments)
SA_K10_sf279_sc.summary: Central Asian Sanskrit fragments of the Māratajjanīyasūtra, corresponding to Chinese versions T 26 and T 66. The text preserves the narrative of the past Buddha Krakasunda and his chief disciple Vidūra, focusing on the harassments committed by the previous Māra named Dūṣin and Dūṣin's subsequent condemnation to Avīci hell.
SA_K10_sf279_sc.attribution: Canonical Sarvāstivāda/Mūlasarvāstivāda Madhyamāgama sūtra preserved in Central Asian manuscript fragments; corresponds to Chinese translations T 26 (Madhyamāgama) and T 66.
SA_K10_sf279_sc.edition: Ernst Waldschmidt, Bruchstücke buddhistischer Sūtras aus dem zentralasiatischen Sanskritkanon I, Kleinere Sanskrit-Texte IV, Leipzig: F. A. Brockhaus, 1932.
SA_K10_sf279_sc.coverage: fragment — Contains two fragmentary sections (marked WalA.1–A.9 and WalB.1–B.11 in Waldschmidt 1932) recounting the deeds of Dūṣī Māra against Krakasunda Buddha and his disciple Vidūra.

SA_K10_sf258_sc.title: Upasenasūtra
SA_K10_sf258_sc.summary: The Upasenasūtra is an Āgama discourse preserved in the Sarvāstivāda Saṃyuktāgama (with parallels in the Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya and the Pāli Upasena Sutta, SN 35.69). It recounts the fatal snakebite of the monk Upasena in a charnel ground near Rājagṛha, who remains entirely undisturbed because he has eradicated notions of 'I' and 'mine' regarding the aggregates and sense bases. After his death, the Buddha presents protective gāthās and mantrapadas against snake venom, emphasizing maitrī and truth declarations.
SA_K10_sf258_sc.attribution: Canonical discourse preserved in the Central Asian Sarvāstivāda Saṃyuktāgama and Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinayavibhaṅga tradition.
SA_K10_sf258_sc.edition: Ernst Waldschmidt, 'Das Upasenasūtra, ein Zauber gegen Schlangenbiss aus dem Samyuktāgama', Nachrichten der Akademie der Wissenschaften in Göttingen, Philologisch-historische Klasse, Jg. 1957, Nr. 2, Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht, 1957, pp. 27–44 (reprinted in: Von Ceylon bis Turfan, Göttingen 1967, pp. 329–346).
SA_K10_sf258_sc.coverage: complete — Complete text of the reconstructed Sanskrit sūtra in numbered paragraphs matching Waldschmidt's edition (§§ 1–35).

SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHA_hk.title: Spandasaṃdoha
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHA_hk.author: Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHA_hk.summary: The Spandasaṃdoha is an extensive exegetical treatise by the non-dual Kashmir Śaiva philosopher Kṣemarāja (early 11th century CE) on the opening verse of the Spandakārikā ('yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ jagataḥ pralayodayau...'). Kṣemarāja expounds the core doctrine of spanda—the dynamic pulsation of divine consciousness (Śiva)—systematically unfolding Trika metaphysics, the five cosmic acts (pañcakṛtya), and contemplative methods encoded within the introductory kārikā.
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHA_hk.attribution: Spandasaṃdoha is an independent commentary composed by Kṣemarāja specifically on the first kārikā of the Spandakārikā ('yasyonmeṣanimeṣābhyāṃ...').
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHA_hk.edition: The Spanda Sandoha of Kṣemarāja, ed. Mukunda Rāma Shāstrī. KSTS 16. Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1917.
SA_MB_SPANDASAMDOHA_hk.coverage: complete — Complete text of the commentary, terminating with 'iti spandasaṃdohaḥ samāptaḥ ||'.

SA_GV03_sb_03_u.title: Śatapathabrāhmaṇa (kāṇḍa 3)
SA_GV03_sb_03_u.summary: Kāṇḍa 3 of the Mādhyandina Śatapathabrāhmaṇa is devoted to the ritual procedures and theological expositions of the Soma sacrifice (Agnīṣṭoma). It details the preparatory rites, including the patron's consecration (dīkṣā), the preliminary sacrifice (prāyaṇīyā), the purchase and welcoming of King Soma, the construction of the sacrificial enclosure and altars (havirdhāna, uttaravedi), the animal sacrifice (paśubandha), and the pressing of the Soma with associated libations.
SA_GV03_sb_03_u.coverage: complete — The whole of kāṇḍa 3 (Soma sacrifice: dīkṣā to the pressing and grahas), from the opening 'devayajanaṃ joṣayante …' (= 3.1.1.1) to the end of 3.9.4 ('… tasmāddhotṛcamasāt'). GRETIL's bracketed numbers were 'added mechanically' and come after each paragraph, so the first paragraph is labelled 3.1.1.[2]. This is a numbering artefact; no text is missing.

SA_T07_vakobha9.title: Abhidharmakośabhāṣya (chapter 9: Pudgalaviniścaya)
SA_T07_vakobha9.author: Vasubandhu
SA_T07_vakobha9.summary: Chapter 9 of Vasubandhu's Abhidharmakośabhāṣya, commonly titled Pudgalaviniścaya ('Examination of the Person') or Ātmavādapratiṣedha ('Refutation of the Self Theory'), is an independent prose treatise appended to the main eight-chapter auto-commentary. Vasubandhu demonstrates that liberation is impossible without relinquishing belief in an enduring self, establishing that 'person' (pudgala) or 'self' (ātman) is merely a conventional designation (prajñapti) applied to the causal continuum of the psycho-physical aggregates (skandha). The work contains an extensive critique of both the Buddhist Personalist (Vātsīputrīya/Pudgalavādin) concept of an ineffable pudgala and the Brahmanical (Vaiśeṣika and Nyāya) ontologies of a substantial ātman.
SA_T07_vakobha9.attribution: Vasubandhu's authorship of this prose treatise, appended as the ninth chapter to his Abhidharmakośabhāṣya, is unanimously accepted in Indian, Tibetan, Chinese, and modern scholarship.
SA_T07_vakobha9.edition: Jong Cheol Lee (ed.), Abhidharmakośabhāṣya of Vasubandhu, Chapter IX: Ātmavādapratiṣedha, Bibliotheca Indologica et Buddhologica 11, Tokyo: Sankibo Press, 2005.
SA_T07_vakobha9.coverage: complete — Complete text of Chapter 9 (prose treatise without root kārikās), from the opening inquiry ('kiṃ khalvato 'nyatra mokṣo nāsti') to the final verse, concluding colophon, and scribal dedication ('uttarāpathikapaṇḍitasthaviraśrīlāmāvākasya').
translations: Duerlinger, James (2003), Indian Buddhist Theories of Persons: Vasubandhu's 'Refutation of the Theory of a Self', London & New York: RoutledgeCurzon. (English)

SA_GSP27_motik_3u.title: Mokṣopāya with Mokṣopāyaṭīkā (prakaraṇa 3: Utpattiprakaraṇa, fragments)
SA_GSP27_motik_3u.author: Bhāskarakaṇṭha
SA_GSP27_motik_3u.summary: This e-text contains fragments of the third section, the Utpattiprakaraṇa, of the Mokṣopāya together with the commentary (Mokṣopāyaṭīkā / Vivṛti) by Bhāskarakaṇṭha.
SA_GSP27_motik_3u.attribution: The opening verse states that the Utpattyākhyāvagāhiprakaraṇavivṛti is composed by Bhāskara (Bhāskarakaṇṭha).
SA_GSP27_motik_3u.edition: Slaje, Walter: Bhāskarakaṇṭhas Mokṣopāya-Ṭīkā. Die Fragmente des 3. (Utpatti-)Prakaraṇa. Graz, 1995.
SA_GSP27_motik_3u.coverage: fragment — Surviving manuscript fragments of prakaraṇa 3 (Utpatti): 3,1.1–41; 3,3.13–3,12.4; 3,13.50–3,16.41.

SA_K10_sf89_sc.title: Śroṇasūtra (1)
SA_K10_sf89_sc.summary: A canonical Sanskrit discourse. The elder Śāriputra explains to the householder's son Śroṇa that recluses and brahmins who construct conceits of superiority, equality, or inferiority based on the impermanent five skandhas do not see reality as it is. Realizing that the aggregates are neither self nor belonging to self ('naitan mama naiṣo ’ham asmi naiṣa me ātmā'), Śroṇa attains the dharma-eye (dharmacakṣu) and takes refuge as an upāsaka.
SA_K10_sf89_sc.coverage: fragment — Substantially preserved manuscript folio; lacks the standard opening nidāna and has minor lacunae.

SA_K10_sf18_sc.title: Ṣaṭṣaṭkasūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_sf18_sc.summary: A fragmentary Central Asian Sanskrit sūtra belonging to the Sarvāstivāda Saṁyuktāgama, parallel to the Pāli Chachakka Sutta (MN 148 / SN 35.107). The text expounds sensory experience through groups of six phenomena (internal and external sense bases, consciousnesses, contacts, sensations, and volitions), emphasizing that these conditioned dharmas are impermanent (anitya), contaminated (sāsrava), and worthy of disenchantment (nirvid) and cessation (nirodha).
SA_K10_sf18_sc.attribution: Canonical Sarvāstivāda Saṁyuktāgama discourse transmitted anonymously in Buddhist Āgama collections.
SA_K10_sf18_sc.coverage: fragment — Fragmentary manuscript remains from the Turfan collection (SHT Kat.-Nr. 1879), preserving portions of recto and verso across two fragments covering the six sense spheres, contacts, sensations, and volitions.

SA_K10_sf241_sc.title: Śakrapraśnasūtra (fragments)
SA_K10_sf241_sc.summary: An Āgama sūtra preserved in fragmentary Central Asian Sanskrit manuscripts. Śakra, lord of the gods, comes with the gandharva Pañcaśikha to the Buddha. Pañcaśikha sings to his lute, and the Buddha answers Śakra's questions. Śakra and eighty thousand deities gain the dharma-eye, and Śakra takes refuge.
SA_K10_sf241_sc.edition: Ernst Waldschmidt, Bruchstücke buddhistischer Sūtras aus dem zentralasiatischen Sanskritkanon, Kleine Sanskrit-Texte 4, Leipzig 1932, pp. 58–113.
SA_K10_sf241_sc.coverage: fragment — Begins mid-sentence ('… magadheṣu viharati pūrvavad yāvac chailaguhāyām') and ends mid-sentence with Śakra's words to Pañcaśikha ('… yo hi nāma tvaṁ bhagavantam'); many lacunae ('…'). Covers the approach to the cave, Pañcaśikha's song, Śakra's questions and the Buddha's answers, Śakra's attainment of the dharma-eye and his going for refuge.

SA_GSD36_visnu_pu.title: Viṣṇusmṛti
SA_GSD36_visnu_pu.summary: The Viṣṇusmṛti is an extensive Dharmaśāstra work in 100 adhyāyas covering varṇāśramadharma, rājadharma, civil and criminal law, domestic rituals, funeral offerings (śrāddha), prāyaścitta, and yoga. It is set inside an overarching frame dialogue between the boar incarnation of Viṣṇu and the goddess Earth.
SA_GSD36_visnu_pu.attribution: Traditionally represented as sacred law expounded by Viṣṇu in Varāha form to the Earth goddess.
SA_GSD36_visnu_pu.edition: V. Krishnamacharya (ed.), Viṣṇusmṛti with the Commentary Keśavavaijayantī of Nandapaṇḍita, 2 vols., Adyar Library Series 93, Madras: The Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1964.
SA_GSD36_visnu_pu.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 100 adhyāyas (mūla text only, without Nandapaṇḍita's commentary).
translations: Julius Jolly (trans.), The Institutes of Vishnu, Sacred Books of the East, Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1880. (English)

SA_K10_sf284_sc.title: Veṇukātyāyanasagotrīsūtra
SA_K10_sf284_sc.summary: A canonical discourse from the Sanskrit Saṃyuktāgama (parallel to Taishō 99). The elder Udāyin is asked by a female brahmin of the Veṇukātyāyana clan how arhats describe the origin of pleasure and pain. Udāyin explains that experience arises dependently upon sense faculties and sensory contact and ceases with their cessation, resulting in her attainment of the Dharma-eye and conversion as a lay follower (upāsikā).

SA_K10_sf90_sc.title: Śroṇasūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_sf90_sc.summary: A fragmentary Sanskrit discourse from the Saṃyuktāgama. Set at Gṛdhrakūṭa in Rājagṛha, it depicts the householder's son Śroṇa visiting Śāriputra, who instructs him that ascetic or brāhmaṇa recluses who do not understand the five aggregates, their arising, cessation, and path cannot master them, before initiating a standard catechism on the impermanence of material form (rūpa).
SA_K10_sf90_sc.attribution: Canonical discourse of the Sanskrit Saṃyuktāgama, recording a dialogue between the elder Śāriputra and the householder's son Śroṇa.
SA_K10_sf90_sc.coverage: fragment — Fragment breaking off during the catechism on the aggregates.

SA_K10_sf264_sc.title: Svāgatasūtra
SA_K10_sf264_sc.summary: A short canonical Sanskrit sūtra from Central Asian manuscript remains, closely parallel to Saṃyuktāgama T 99. In Śrāvastī, the Buddha welcomes the monks and emphasizes the exceptional rarity (sudurlabha) of attaining human birth in an āryāyatana with faculties intact, encountering the appearance of a Tathāgata, and hearing the teaching of dependent origination leading to liberation.
SA_K10_sf264_sc.attribution: Canonical discourse of the Sanskrit Āgama tradition (parallel to Saṃyuktāgama discourse T 99).
SA_K10_sf264_sc.edition: Ernst Waldschmidt, 'Ein zweites Daśabalasūtra', Mitteilungen des Instituts für Orientforschung 6 (1958), pp. 392–397.
SA_K10_sf264_sc.coverage: complete — Complete short sūtra preserved across paragraphs Wal_1 to Wal_7, ending with the colophon 'svāgatasūtraṁ / samāptaḥ // samā //'.
translations: Ernst Waldschmidt, 'Ein zweites Daśabalasūtra', Mitteilungen des Instituts für Orientforschung 6 (1958), pp. 392–397. (German)

SA_K14_sf259_sc.title: Catuṣpariṣatsūtra (sections 0–21)
SA_K14_sf259_sc.summary: The Catuṣpariṣatsūtra ('Sūtra on the Fourfold Assembly') is an early Buddhist canonical text belonging to the Dīrghāgama of the Sarvāstivāda/Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition, reconstructed primarily from Sanskrit manuscripts discovered in Turfan (Central Asia). It presents a continuous narrative of the events following the Buddha's Awakening, including the First Sermon at Ṛṣipatana (Sārnāth) and the establishment of the four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen). This e-text contains the first 21 narrative episodes (Vorgänge), culminating in the Buddha dispatching his first sixty enlightened disciples to wander and propagate the Dharma.
SA_K14_sf259_sc.attribution: A canonical Dīrghāgama text preserved in the (Mūla-)Sarvāstivāda tradition, reconstructed from Turfan manuscript fragments.
SA_K14_sf259_sc.edition: Ernst Waldschmidt, Das Catuṣpariṣatsūtra: Eine kanonische Lehrschrift über die Begründung der buddhistischen Gemeinde. Text in Sanskrit und Tibetisch, verglichen mit dem Pāli nebst einer Übersetzung der chinesischen Entsprechung im Vinaya der Mūlasarvāstivādins. Teil I (Vorgang 1–9), Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1952; Teil II (Vorgang 10–21), Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1957 (Abhandlungen der Deutschen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin, Klasse für Sprachen, Literatur und Kunst).
SA_K14_sf259_sc.coverage: partial — Covers Vorgänge 0–21 (from the Enlightenment through the dispatch of the first sixty disciples), corresponding to Teile I–II of Ernst Waldschmidt's edition; Vorgänge 22–28 (the conversion of the three Kāśyapa brothers, King Bimbisāra, and the two chief disciples Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana) are absent.
translations: Ria Kloppenborg, The Sūtra on the Foundation of the Buddhist Order (Catuṣpariṣatsūtra), Leiden: E. J. Brill, 1973. (English)
Ernst Waldschmidt, Das Catuṣpariṣatsūtra, Teile I–III, Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1952–1962. (German)
Víctor Giménez Morote, El Sūtra de las cuatro asambleas: Catuṣpariṣatsūtra, Barcelona: Universitat de Barcelona, 1995. (Spanish)

SA_GSP30_tantralu.title: Tantrāloka
SA_GSP30_tantralu.author: Abhinavagupta
SA_GSP30_tantralu.summary: The Tantrāloka ('Illumination of the Tantras') by Abhinavagupta (c. 1000 CE) is the encyclopedic masterwork of non-dual Trika Śaivism. Structured in 37 chapters (āhnikas) as an exhaustive exegesis of the Mālinīvijayottaratantra, it synthesizes the Krama, Kaula, Spanda, and Pratyabhijñā traditions into a comprehensive framework encompassing metaphysics, the four means of liberation (anupāya, śāmbhava-, śākta-, and āṇavopāya), ritual procedure, mantra theory, initiation (dīkṣā), and esoteric yogic practices.
SA_GSP30_tantralu.attribution: Composed by Abhinavagupta (c. 1000 CE). Jayaratha's Viveka commentary, which accompanied the root text in the printed KSTS edition from which this text was extracted, is omitted from this digital file.
SA_GSP30_tantralu.edition: The Tantraloka of Abhinavagupta With commentary of Rajanaka Jayaratha, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies, No. 23, 28, 30, 36, 35, 29, 41, 47, 59, 52, 57, 58 (1918-1938).
SA_GSP30_tantralu.coverage: complete — Complete root text in 37 chapters (āhnikas), concluding with āhnika 37, verse 85 (colophon verse).
translations: Gnoli, Raniero, Luce dei Tantra: Tantrāloka. (Italian)

SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKA_hk.title: Śivasūtra with Śivasūtravārttika
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKA_hk.author: Vasugupta, Bhāskara
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKA_hk.summary: The foundational scripture of Kashmir Shaivism, the Śivasūtra, expounds non-dual Śaiva metaphysics and yogic realization across three sections corresponding to the divine (śāmbhava), cognitive (śākta), and individual (āṇava) means. The Śivasūtravārttika by Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara is an early metrical commentary representing the direct lineage of Vasugupta and Kallaṭa. It provides an important alternative exegetical perspective to Kṣemarāja's later prose Śivasūtravimarśinī.
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKA_hk.attribution: According to the colophon, the author of the Vārttika is Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, son of Bhaṭṭa Divākara.
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKA_hk.edition: Shiva Sūtra Vārttika by Bhāskara, edited by J. C. Chatterji, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS), Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1916.
SA_MB_SIVASUUTRAVARTIKA_hk.coverage: complete — Complete text of all three prakāśas of the Śivasūtra and Bhāskara's Śivasūtravārttika, including the initial sūtrapāṭha and the concluding index of technical terms (pāribhāṣikapadāni).
translations: The Aphorisms of Śiva: The Śivasūtra with Bhāskara's Commentary, the Vārttika, trans. Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, Albany: State University of New York Press, 1992. (English)

SA_K10_sf74_sc.title: Candropamasūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_sf74_sc.summary: A canonical discourse belonging to the Sarvāstivāda Saṃyuktāgama, corresponding to the Pāli Candūpamasutta (SN 16.3). In this fragment, the Buddha addresses the monks at Rājagṛha regarding Devadatta's desire for gain and fame, instructing them to approach householder families like the moon (candropama)—modest, cautious, and holding body and mind aloof—holding up the elder Mahākāśyapa as the exemplary practitioner.
SA_K10_sf74_sc.attribution: Canonical discourse of the early Buddhist tradition (Saṃyuktāgama), traditionally transmitted as the word of the Buddha (buddhavacana).
SA_K10_sf74_sc.edition: A. F. Rudolf Hoernle, Manuscript Remains of Buddhist Literature found in Eastern Turkestan.
SA_K10_sf74_sc.coverage: fragment — Preserves only the opening section of the sūtra breaking off at 'kiṁ manyatha …'.

SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAM_hk.title: Śataratnasaṃgraha with Śataratnollekhanī
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAM_hk.author: Umāpatiśivācārya
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAM_hk.summary: The Śataratnasaṃgraha is a Śaiva Siddhānta anthology compiled by Umāpatiśivācārya, selecting verses from Āgamas such as the Mṛgendra, Pauṣkara, Niśvāsa, and Sarvajñānottara. In this e-text, the verses are accompanied throughout by the Śataratnollekhanī commentary.
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAM_hk.attribution: The root collection is attributed to Umāpatiśivācārya. The commentary is titled Śataratnollekhanī (closing with the colophon: 'iti umāpatiśivācārya-saṃgṛhīta-śataratnollekhanī samāptā').
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAM_hk.edition: Tantrik Texts Series volume 22 of John Woodroffe. Calcutta: Luzac and Co., 1944.
SA_MB_SATARATNASAMGRAHAM_hk.coverage: complete — Text of the anthology and commentary closing with the colophon: 'iti umāpatiśivācārya-saṃgṛhīta-śataratnollekhanī samāptā'.

SA_GSP30_utipk_pu.title: Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā with Īśvarapratyabhijñāvṛtti
SA_GSP30_utipk_pu.author: Utpaladeva
SA_GSP30_utipk_pu.summary: The Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā along with its auto-commentary (vṛtti) by Utpaladeva constitutes the foundational philosophical treatise of the Pratyabhijñā ('Recognition') system of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism. Structured into four sections (adhikāras on knowledge, action, scriptural authority, and a summary of tattvas), the work argues dialectically against Buddhist epistemologists and other rivals to establish that all reality and individual consciousness are identical with the autonomous, self-luminous Lord (Maheśvara / Śiva), and that liberation consists in the explicit recognition of this identity.
SA_GSP30_utipk_pu.attribution: Both the root kārikās and the vṛtti are the work of Utpaladeva.
SA_GSP30_utipk_pu.edition: Madhusudan Kaul Shastri, Srinagar 1921. (Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies; 34) Revised according to the edition by Raffaele Torella, Roma 1994 (Serie Orientale Roma; 71)
SA_GSP30_utipk_pu.coverage: complete — Complete across all four adhikāras: Jñānādhikāra, Kriyādhikāra, Āgamādhikāra, and Tattvasaṃgrahādhikāra, concluding with verse 4.18 and the closing colophon 'samāpteyam īśvarapratyabhijñāvṛttiḥ'.
translations: Raffaele Torella, The Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā of Utpaladeva with the Author's Vṛtti (critical edition and annotated translation), Serie Orientale Roma, LXXI (Roma: Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente, 1994). (English)

SA_K10_sf68_sc.title: Bodhasūtra (section on the five factors of striving)
SA_K10_sf68_sc.summary: Prince Bodha asks how many factors a noble disciple needs to reach the destruction of the āsravas quickly. Using the analogy of learning hereditary arts (elephant and horse riding, archery, writing and calculation, etc.), the Buddha teaches the five factors of striving (prādhānikāṅga): faith, health/freedom from illness, honesty, energy, and wisdom. Bodha concludes with an udāna.
SA_K10_sf68_sc.attribution: A Buddhist sūtra preserved in Sanskrit (associated with Jens-Uwe Hartmann's edition/research on the Dīrghāgama).
SA_K10_sf68_sc.coverage: partial — Text marked Hart_1 through Hart_20, dealing with prince Bodha and the five prādhānikāṅgas.

SA_K10_sf101_sc.title: Rāṣṭrapālasūtra (partial)
SA_K10_sf101_sc.summary: An Āgama sūtra text. After hearing the Buddha at Sthūlakoṣṭhaka in the Kuru country, the young householder Rāṣṭrapāla fasts until his parents allow him to go forth. Later he returns home as a monk and turns down the wealth and former wives his parents offer him. In this e-text that part concludes with the final sentence mentioning King Kauravya.
SA_K10_sf101_sc.coverage: partial — Sections Mat_0–Mat_49: the ordination of Rāṣṭrapāla, his fast to get his parents' consent, his return to Sthūlakoṣṭhaka, the scene with his former wives and the meal in his parents' house. Then only the line 'grahāyakapaṁñña śrāmaṇyam eva śreyaḥ' of his verses and the closing sentence on King Kauravya's departure. The verses and the dialogue with Kauravya are missing.

SA_GP12_sivap1_u.title: Śivapurāṇa (Vidyeśvarasaṃhitā)
SA_GP12_sivap1_u.summary: The Vidyeśvarasaṃhitā constitutes the introductory and liturgical foundational book of the Śivapurāṇa (in its seven-saṃhitā recension). It establishes the greatness and salvific efficacy of Śiva worship, particularly in the Kaliyuga, expounding the significance of the liṅga, the mythical origins of the fiery Liṅgodbhavamūrti, daily rituals, and the sacred emblems of Śaivism including the sacred ash (bhasma/vibhūti) and rudrākṣa beads.
SA_GP12_sivap1_u.attribution: Traditional Purāṇic attribution to Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa; related by Sūta Romaharṣaṇa to the sages in Prayāga.
SA_GP12_sivap1_u.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Vidyeśvarasaṃhitā, the first saṃhitā of the Śivapurāṇa in the standard seven-saṃhitā recension, consisting of 25 adhyāyas.

SA_GSD36_manu2p_u.title: Manusmṛti
SA_GSD36_manu2p_u.summary: The Manusmṛti (or Mānavadharmaśāstra), comprising twelve chapters and roughly 2,685 verses, is the classical benchmark treatise of Brahmanical dharma. Structured as a discourse delivered by Bhṛgu upon instruction from Manu, it systematically articulates the duties of the four varṇas and āśramas, rites of passage (saṃskāras), rules of marriage and domestic life, civil and criminal law (the eighteen vyavahārapadas), the obligations of kingship (rājadharma), ritual expiations (prāyaścitta), and the doctrines of karma and liberation.
SA_GSD36_manu2p_u.attribution: Attributed traditionally to the primordial sage Manu through his pupil Bhṛgu.
SA_GSD36_manu2p_u.edition: Manusmṛti with the Sanskrit Commentary Manvartha-Muktāvalī of Kullūka Bhaṭṭa, ed. J. L. Shastri, Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1983; collated with the Kashi Sanskrit Series 114 edition by Haragovinda Śāstrī and Gopāla Śāstrī Nene (Varanasi: Chaukhambha Sanskrit Sansthan, 1982), with variants from Medhātithi's commentary (ed. Calcutta, 1967; ed. Gaṅgānātha Jhā, Parimal Sanskrit Series 33, Delhi: Parimal Publications, repr. 1992).
SA_GSD36_manu2p_u.coverage: complete — Complete root text in 12 adhyāyas (1.1 to 12.126) with Medhātithi's pāda variants and numbering differences noted in-line.
translations: Patrick Olivelle, Manu's Code of Law: A Critical Edition and Translation of the Mānava-Dharmaśāstra, New York: Oxford University Press, 2005. (English)
Bühler 1886. (English)

SA_GSP27_motik_4u.title: Mokṣopāya with Mokṣopāyaṭīkā (chapter 4: Sthitiprakaraṇa, fragments)
SA_GSP27_motik_4u.author: Bhāskarakaṇṭha
SA_GSP27_motik_4u.summary: The Sthitiprakaraṇa is the fourth book of the Mokṣopāya, an influential 10th-century Kashmirian philosophical epic that represents the original recension later reworked into the vulgate Yogavāsiṣṭha. It addresses the apparent preservation or maintenance (sthiti) of phenomenal reality in consciousness, demonstrating through philosophical exposition and allegorical narratives (notably the accounts of Śukra and the demons Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa) that the world possesses no independent ontological existence outside pure awareness. This e-text provides the critical text of the surviving fragments of book 4 accompanied by Bhāskarakaṇṭha's commentary.
SA_GSP27_motik_4u.attribution: The Mokṣopāyaṭīkā was composed by Bhāskarakaṇṭha.
SA_GSP27_motik_4u.edition: Slaje, Walter: Bhāskarakaṇṭhas Mokṣopāya-Ṭīkā. Die Fragmente des 4. (Sthiti-)Prakaraṇa. Aachen, 2002.
SA_GSP27_motik_4u.coverage: fragment — Prakaraṇa 4 (Sthitiprakaraṇa) only, preserving the fragmentary sections 4.1.1–4.24.19 and 4.25.12–4.33.26.

SA_GK19_ragh1-6u.title: Raghuvaṃśa (cantos 1–6)
SA_GK19_ragh1-6u.author: Kālidāsa
SA_GK19_ragh1-6u.summary: The Raghuvaṃśa is a celebrated classical mahākāvya by Kālidāsa recounting the genealogy, heroic exploits, and virtues of the Raghu dynasty (the solar lineage of Ayodhyā). Cantos 1–6 cover King Dilīpa's service to the sacred cow Nandinī, the birth and digvijaya (world conquest) of Raghu, the youth of Prince Aja, and the svayaṃvara of Princess Indumatī. This specific e-text provides the root verses constituted according to the northern/Kashmiri recension preserved by the 10th-century commentator Vallabhadeva.
SA_GK19_ragh1-6u.attribution: Although extracted from Dominic Goodall and Harunaga Isaacson's critical edition of Vallabhadeva's Raghupañcikā, this digital file includes only Kālidāsa's verses according to the Kashmiri recension (siglum Ragh(K)) and omits Vallabhadeva's commentary.
SA_GK19_ragh1-6u.edition: Dominic Goodall and Harunaga Isaacson: The Raghupañcikā of Vallabhadeva, being the earliest commentary on the Raghuvaṃśa of Kālidāsa, Critical Edition with Introduction and Notes, Volume 1. Groningen: Egbert Forsten 2003.
SA_GK19_ragh1-6u.coverage: partial — Cantos 1–6 only (concluding at verse 6.86), matching the coverage of Volume 1 of the Goodall & Isaacson edition.

SA_GP12_skp031pu.title: Skandapurāṇa (chapters 1–31.14)
SA_GP12_skp031pu.summary: The early Skandapurāṇa is a Śaiva Purāṇa. This section (adhyāyas 1–31.14) covers the dialogue between Vyāsa and Sanatkumāra, cosmological narratives, the birth and myths of Skanda/Kārttikeya, the marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī, and the beginning of the Vārāṇasī cycle recounting the story and elevation of the Yakṣa Harikeśa.
SA_GP12_skp031pu.edition: Rob Adriaensen, Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson, Groningen: Egbert Forsten 1998- (Groningen Oriental Studies).
SA_GP12_skp031pu.coverage: partial — Contains adhyāyas 1 to 31.14 (ending at SkP 31.14 with the installation of the yakṣa Harikeśa as Gaṇeśvara/Daṇḍapāṇi in Vārāṇasī).

SA_K10_sf137_sc.title: Dhvajāgrasūtra
SA_K10_sf137_sc.summary: The Buddha tells monks in the forest, at the foot of a tree or in empty houses to recollect his qualities when fear arises. He compares this with Śakra's advice to the gods to look at the top of his banner in battle with the asuras, which cannot remove fear because Śakra himself is not free from passion, hatred and delusion.
SA_K10_sf137_sc.attribution: Canonical discourse belonging to the early Sanskrit tradition, preserved in Central Asian manuscript witnesses.
SA_K10_sf137_sc.coverage: complete — The whole short sūtra, Sand_1–Sand_20, from 'evaṁ mayā śrutam' to 'dhvajāgrasūtraṁ / samāptaḥ //'; some passages abbreviated with 'yāvat' as in the manuscript.

SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANI_hk.title: Stavacintāmaṇi with Vivṛti
SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANI_hk.author: Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa, Kṣemarāja
SA_MB_STAVACINTAAMANI_hk.summary: The Stavacintāmaṇi ('Wish-Fulfilling Gem of Hymns') is a 120-verse devotional hymn to Lord Śiva by Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa, synthesizing non-dual Kashmiri Śaiva metaphysics (Pratyabhijñā and Spanda) with ecstatic devotional surrender (bhakti).
