SA_T02_ilx_hh_ksitigarbha_dasatattvasamg.coverage: complete — Covers all ten tattvas announced in v. 2 (rakṣācakra, cakra, jāpa, two sekas, haṭha, bali, two pratyaṅgirās, puṭodghāta) up to the concluding verse and colophon, but with lacunae from the incomplete manuscript: a folio is missing at the beginning of the rakṣācakra section (segment 'FOLIO MISSING') and another near the end of the puṭodghāta section (segment '[folio missing]'). The ilx/Hamburg header marks the file as '(not final)'.
translations: Sabine Gudrun Klein-Schwind, annotated English translation in her dissertation (Universität Hamburg, 2012). (English)

SA_GR12_ilx_hh_mallisenasuri_bhairavapad.title: Bhairavapadmāvatīkalpa with Vivaraṇa
SA_GR12_ilx_hh_mallisenasuri_bhairavapad.author: Malliṣeṇasūri, Bandhuṣeṇa
SA_GR12_ilx_hh_mallisenasuri_bhairavapad.summary: The Bhairavapadmāvatīkalpa is an 11th-century Digambara Jaina tantric manual dedicated to the goddess Padmāvatī / Bhairavapadmāvatī. Composed across ten chapters, it expounds mantra lore, diagrammatic amulets (yantra), the six magical arts (ṣaṭkarmāṇi, including stambhana, vaśīkaraṇa, and ākarṣaṇa), and snake/poison lore (gāruḍatantra). The accompanying Sanskrit commentary (Vivaraṇa) is by Bandhuṣeṇa.
SA_GR12_ilx_hh_mallisenasuri_bhairavapad.attribution: The root text was composed by the Digambara author Malliṣeṇa / Malliṣeṇasūri (composed in the Dharwar region in 1057 A.D.). The Sanskrit commentary (Vivaraṇa) is by Bandhuṣeṇa, as stated in the opening invocation ('padmāvatyā hi kalpapravaravivaraṇaṃ vakṣyate banduṣeṇaiḥ').
SA_GR12_ilx_hh_mallisenasuri_bhairavapad.edition: Mohanlal Bhagwandas Jhavery, Comparative and Critical Study of Mantraśāstra (Sri Jain Kala Sahitya Samsodhak Series, no. 1), Ahmedabad, 1944.
SA_GR12_ilx_hh_mallisenasuri_bhairavapad.coverage: complete — Complete text of all ten paricchedas/adhikāras (from 1.1 through 10.57) along with Bandhuṣeṇa's Vivaraṇa commentary.

SA_T02_ilx_hh_padmavajra_guhyasiddhi.title: Guhyasiddhi
SA_T02_ilx_hh_padmavajra_guhyasiddhi.author: Padmavajra
SA_T02_ilx_hh_padmavajra_guhyasiddhi.summary: The Guhyasiddhi ('Secret Accomplishment') is an influential late 8th- or 9th-century Vajrayāna treatise by Padmavajra. The work expounds esoteric yoga in connection with the Guhyasamājatantra. Across nine chapters, it treats sacraments including consort practice (vidyāvrata) and antinomian conduct (unmattavrata), and guru worship (paramārthācāryapūjā).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_padmavajra_guhyasiddhi.attribution: Attributed to Padmavajra (Padmavajrapāda; also identified in Tibetan tradition as mtsho skyes), dated to the 9th century (or late 8th–9th century).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_padmavajra_guhyasiddhi.edition: Samdhong Rinpoche and Vrajavallabh Dwivedi (eds.), Guhyādi-aṣṭasiddhisaṃgraha, Sarnath, 1987 (Rare Buddhist Text Series 1)
SA_T02_ilx_hh_padmavajra_guhyasiddhi.coverage: complete — Complete text in nine chapters (paricchedas 1–9), concluding with chapter 9 and the final work colophon: 'iti sakalatantrasadbhāvasaṃcodanī guhyasiddhiḥ parisamāptā'.
translations: rgyud ma lus pa'i don nges par skul bar byed pa/_dpal gsang ba grub pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 2217): translated by Kṛṣṇapa, nag 'tsho lo tsA ba tshul khrims rgyal ba (Tibetan)

SA_GR14_ilx_hh_paramasamhita.title: Paramasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_paramasamhita.summary: The Paramasaṃhitā is an early canonical scripture of the Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra tradition, framed as a dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Devala reporting revelation received from Sanaka on Śvetadvīpa. In 31 chapters, it treats Vaiṣṇava cosmology, ritual worship, icon consecration, initiation (dīkṣā), and yoga, reconciling meditative visualization with temple and image devotion.
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_paramasamhita.attribution: A traditional Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra canonical scripture, traditionally framed as teaching imparted by Sanaka at Śvetadvīpa to Mārkaṇḍeya, who transmits it to Devala.
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_paramasamhita.edition: Probably keyed from S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (ed. and tr.), Paramasaṃhitā [of the Pāñcarātra], Gaekwad's Oriental Series 86, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1940 — the only printed edition known to us. E-text from the Hamburg Sanskrit etext collection (producer not named), TEI conversion by the Intellexus project (ilx_skt corpus/hamburg/paramasaṃhitā.xml). (probable)
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_paramasamhita.coverage: complete — 31 adhyāyas (chapter verse-numbering restarts 31 times, 1.1 to 31.57+), ending with Mārkaṇḍeya's concluding instruction to Devala; followed by a detached block of variant readings with sigla k./ka. and kh./kha. (diacritics partly corrupted).
translations: S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar, English translation included in the GOS 86 volume (Baroda 1940). (English)

SA_GSP33_ilx_hh_prakasatmayati_sabdanirn.title: Śābdanirṇaya
SA_GSP33_ilx_hh_prakasatmayati_sabdanirn.author: Prakāśātman
SA_GSP33_ilx_hh_prakasatmayati_sabdanirn.summary: The Śābdanirṇaya is an epistemological and linguistic treatise by the Advaita Vedāntin Prakāśātman (c. 10th–11th century CE). Consisting of 75 kārikās and an auto-commentary, it establishes verbal testimony (śabda) as an independent pramāṇa against Buddhist and Vaiśeṣika reductions to inference, critically examines Mīmāṃsā semantic theories (anvitābhidhāna and abhihitānvaya), and defends the capacity of Vedic language to impart immediate knowledge of non-dual Brahman.
SA_GSP33_ilx_hh_prakasatmayati_sabdanirn.attribution: The concluding verses (vv. 74–75) confirm authorship by Prakāśātmayatīndra (Prakāśātman), disciple of Ananyānubhava.
SA_GSP33_ilx_hh_prakasatmayati_sabdanirn.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all 75 kārikās with the author's prose auto-commentary (vṛtti).

SA_GR14_ilx_hh_padmasamhita.title: Pādmasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_padmasamhita.summary: The Pādmasaṃhitā is a Saṃhitā of the Pāñcarātra tradition structured in pādas (including Jñānapāda, Yogapāda, Kriyāpāda, and Caryāpāda), framed as Kaṇva's report of Saṃvarta's teaching. Daniel Smith places the Pādmasaṃhitā in the 'middle period' of the Pāñcarātra.
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_padmasamhita.attribution: A scriptural Pāñcarātra Āgama saṃhitā traditionally transmitted through Saṃvarta and Kaṇva; canonical and anonymous.
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_padmasamhita.coverage: complete — Includes Jñānapāda, Yogapāda, Kriyāpāda, Caryāpāda, followed by textual apparatus/variant readings (including sigla such as T, P1, P2, M1, M2).

SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_ascribed_ga.title: Gaṇacakravidhi with Saṃkṣiptā Pañjikā (commentary fragment on verses 1–11)
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_ascribed_ga.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_ascribed_ga.summary: A short late Indian Vajrayāna manual in 48 verses on the gaṇacakra (tantric feast gathering). It covers the qualifications of the presiding yogin, the setting and preliminary worship, bali offerings to supramundane and mundane deities, the consumption of the mahāmṛta, songs and dances, the treatment of transgressions, and the concluding dismissal and meditation. The e-text adds a fragmentary anonymous prose gloss (saṃkṣiptā pañjikā), edited diplomatically from the manuscript, which comments on verses 1–11.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_ascribed_ga.attribution: The Tibetan translation (Toh. 1995) and the e-text title ascribe the root text to Ratnākaraśānti. Szántó's 2019 edition is titled 'the Gaṇacakravidhi attributed to Ratnākaraśānti', so the ascription is treated as uncertain. The gloss is anonymous.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_ascribed_ga.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, 'Minor Vajrayāna texts V: The Gaṇacakravidhi attributed to Ratnākaraśānti', in: Nina Mirnig, Marion Rastelli, Vincent Eltschinger (eds.), Tantric Communities in Context, Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2019, pp. 275–314.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_ascribed_ga.coverage: partial — The root text is complete: 48 verses, ending with verse 48. The commentary is a fragment: segment reads 'Diplomatic edition of the fragmentary gloss', and the gloss covers verses 1–11.
translations: rdo rje 'jigs byed kyi tshogs kyi 'khor lo zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1995): translated by Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, rwa lo tsA ba rdo rje grags (Tibetan)

SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_khasamatika.title: Khasamaṭīkā
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_khasamatika.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_khasamatika.summary: The Khasamaṭīkā (also entitled Khasamā) is an Anuttarayogatantra commentary by the Vikramaśīla scholar Ratnākaraśānti on the Khasamatantra. Ratnākaraśānti explicates the root text's Sanskrit and Apabhraṃśa verses (dohās/dvipadikās) through the framework of Vijñānavāda/Alīkākāravāda, maintaining that the ultimate nature of mind and the dharmakāya is innately pure, luminous, and 'equal to space' (khasama). The work is complete across five chapters (paṭala).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_khasamatika.attribution: Attribution to Ratnākaraśānti is attested in the Sanskrit colophon (kṛtir iyaṃ mahāpaṇḍitaśrīratnakaraśāntipādānām) and confirmed by the Tibetan translation (D 1424).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_ratnakarasanti_khasamatika.coverage: complete — Complete, ending with chapter 5 (pañcamaḥ paṭalaḥ) and work colophon (samāptā ceyaṃ khasamā nāma ṭīkā).
translations: nam mkha' dang mnyam pa zhes bya ba'i rgya cher 'grel pa (Derge Tengyur D 1424): translated by Śūnyatāsamādhi, shes rab ye shes (Tibetan)

SA_T02_ilx_hh_samantabhadra_saramanjari_.title: Sāramañjarī (excerpts ad Samantabhadrasādhana 109–120)
SA_T02_ilx_hh_samantabhadra_saramanjari_.author: Samantabhadra
SA_T02_ilx_hh_samantabhadra_saramanjari_.summary: An excerpted critical section of the Sāramañjarī (Caturaṅgasādhanaṭīkā), Samantabhadra's commentary on Buddhajñānapāda's Guhyasamāja meditation manual (Samantabhadrasādhana / Caturaṅgasādhana), focusing on verses 109–120. In this passage, the author synthesizes Buddhist epistemological theory (Pramāṇa) with tantric generation-stage practice (binduyoga), refuting external objects and grāhya-grāhaka duality through citations of Dignāga and Dharmakīrti to substantiate deity yoga on the foundation of non-dual awareness and ultimate emptiness.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_samantabhadra_saramanjari_.attribution: Composed by the Indian Buddhist tantric master Samantabhadra, commenting on Buddhajñānapāda's Caturaṅgasādhana / Samantabhadrasādhana.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_samantabhadra_saramanjari_.edition: Saccone, Margherita Serena, and Péter-Dániel Szántó. 2023. Tantra and Pramāṇa: A Study of the Sāramañjarī. Series Minor XCVIII. Napoli: UniorPress.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_samantabhadra_saramanjari_.coverage: excerpt — Excerpts covering the Pramāṇa and ontology excursus commenting on Samantabhadrasādhana verses 109–120 (edited on pp. 94–119 of Saccone & Szántó 2023).
translations: yan lag bzhi pa'i sgrub thabs kyi rgya cher bshad pa snying po snye ma zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1869): translated by Nyāyaśrī, rngog blo ldan shes rab; at bal yul mthil (Tibetan)

SA_GK19_ilx_hh_somesvaradeva_surathotsav.title: Surathotsava
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_somesvaradeva_surathotsav.author: Someśvaradeva
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_somesvaradeva_surathotsav.summary: A 15-canto Sanskrit mahākāvya composed in the 13th century CE by Someśvaradeva, court priest to the Caulukya rulers of Gujarat. Elaborating on the foundational framing story of the Devīmāhātmya from the Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa, the epic narrates the life of King Suratha: his loss of sovereignty, forest retreat, devotion and rigorous penance to the Goddess, her destruction of the demon army, and Suratha's restoration to power. The final canto (kavipraśasti) provides significant historical and genealogical information regarding Someśvara's family and his praise of the Jain minister Vastupāla.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_somesvaradeva_surathotsav.attribution: Authored by Someśvaradeva, hereditary royal purohita to the Caulukya kings of Gujarat and member of the literary circle of minister Vastupāla.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_somesvaradeva_surathotsav.edition: Surathotsava, Someśvara, edited by Śivadatta and Kāśīnāth Pāṇḍurang Parab, KM. 73, 1902.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_somesvaradeva_surathotsav.coverage: complete — Contains all 15 cantos (sargas 1–15), concluding with the poet's praśasti celebrating his lineage and patron Vastupāla in canto 15.

SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktimuktavali.title: Sūktimuktāvalī
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktimuktavali.author: Jalhaṇa
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktimuktavali.summary: The Sūktimuktāvalī is a large thematically arranged subhāṣita anthology compiled in the 13th century under Bhagadatta Jalhaṇa, associated with King Kṛṣṇa of the Yādava dynasty. It collects verses by many named poets across various paddhatis covering ethical, erotic, devotional, and miscellaneous topics.
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktimuktavali.attribution: The anthology was compiled in the name of Bhagadatta Jalhaṇa, a contemporary of King Kṛṣṇa of the Yādava dynasty (13th century). The anthologised verses are by many poets, and attributions follow each verse or group of verses.
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktimuktavali.edition: The Sūktimuktāvalī of Bhagadatta Jalhaṇa, ed. Embar Krishnamacharya, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 82, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1938. (probable)
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktimuktavali.coverage: unclear — The e-text runs from the maṅgala through thematic paddhatis, ending inside a Śiva-stuti section with no closing colophon.

SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktiratnakosa.title: Sūktiratnakośa
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktiratnakosa.author: Lakṣmaṇa
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktiratnakosa.summary: The Sūktiratnakośa is a subhāṣita anthology of 659 verses compiled by Lakṣmaṇa Dīkṣita. It opens with verses in praise of the Jina and continues through various thematic sections.
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktiratnakosa.attribution: The compiler names himself Lakṣmaṇa in v. 1 ('lakṣmaṇo lakṣasūktikaḥ') and Lakṣmaṇa Dīkṣita in the closing praśasti (v. 655). The anthology opens with a Jinastuti.
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_suktiratnakosa.coverage: complete — 659 running-numbered verses, from the maṅgala (v. 1) through the opening Jinastuti and other thematic sections to the compiler's praśasti and closing verse 659.

SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_kumarasambha.title: Kumārasambhava with Laghuṭīkā (cantos 1–8)
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_kumarasambha.author: Kālidāsa, Vallabhadeva
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_kumarasambha.summary: The Kumārasambhava ('The Birth of the War-God') is a celebrated poem composed by Kālidāsa, depicting the penance of Pārvatī, her marriage to Śiva, and their union, accompanied by the commentary of Vallabhadeva covering cantos 1 to 8.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_kumarasambha.attribution: In verse 3 of the introductory verses the commentator refers to his commentary as a pañjikā ('tathāpi kriyate 'smābhiḥ pañjikā skandasambhave').
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_kumarasambha.coverage: partial — Contains cantos (sargas) 1–8 of the Kumārasambhava along with Vallabhadeva's commentary.
translations: Hank Heifetz (trans.), The Origin of the Young God: Kālidāsa's Kumārasambhava, Berkeley: University of California Press, 1985. (English)

SA_GK22_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_subhasitaval.title: Subhāṣitāvalī
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_subhasitaval.author: Vallabhadeva
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_subhasitaval.summary: The Subhāṣitāvalī is a major classical Sanskrit anthology (kośa/saṅgraha) compiled by Vallabhadeva. Structured into paddhatis (such as namaskārapaddhati) encompassing invocations, gnomic and didactic verses, descriptions, and varied sentiments, it contains 3,527 stanzas that preserve selections from numerous classical poets.
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_subhasitaval.attribution: A compendium of the twelfth to fifteenth century compiled by Vallabhadeva.
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_subhasitaval.edition: The Subhâshitâvali of Vallabhadeva, edited by Peter Peterson and Pandit Durgâprasâda. Bombay: Education Society's Press, 1886 (Bombay Sanskrit Series).
SA_GK22_ilx_hh_vallabhadeva_subhasitaval.coverage: complete — Contains all 3,527 numbered verses (Subhv_0001 to Subhv_3527), matching Peterson and Durgāprasāda's edition.

SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vedantadesika_yadavabhyud.title: Yādavābhyudaya with the commentary of Appayya Dīkṣita (canto 1)
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vedantadesika_yadavabhyud.author: Vedāntadeśika, Appayya Dīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vedantadesika_yadavabhyud.summary: Canto 1 of the Yādavābhyudaya, a Sanskrit mahākāvya on the life of Kṛṣṇa and the genealogy of the Yādavas composed by Vedāntadeśika (Veṅkaṭanātha). The text is accompanied by the commentary of Appayya Dīkṣita. This first canto includes Appayya Dīkṣita's opening verses mentioning Cinna Timmarāja, followed by 100 root verses treating the lunar dynasty, Vasudeva's marriage, and Devakī's pregnancy with Kṛṣṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vedantadesika_yadavabhyud.attribution: Yādavābhyudaya was composed by Vedāntadeśika (Veṅkaṭanātha). The commentary was composed by Appayya Dīkṣita.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vedantadesika_yadavabhyud.edition: Based on the edition by Sri Vani Vilas Press, 1907.
SA_GK19_ilx_hh_vedantadesika_yadavabhyud.coverage: partial — Contains canto 1 complete (100 verses plus commentary and introductory verses of Appayya Dīkṣita).

SA_T02_ilx_hh_vilasavajra_namamantrartha.title: Nāmamantrārthāvalokinī (chapters 1–5)
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vilasavajra_namamantrartha.author: Vilāsavajra
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vilasavajra_namamantrartha.summary: The Nāmamantrārthāvalokinī is an influential late 8th-century Sanskrit commentary by Vilāsavajra on the Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti, interpreting the root text through the esoteric framework of the Māyājālatantra and the Vajradhātumaṇḍala of the Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha. This critical edition covers chapters 1 through 5 (adhikāras 1–5), which detail the preliminary overview (śarīravyavasthāpana), the setting, the request of Vajrapāṇi, the response of Śākyamuni, and the exposition of the 86 name-mantras mapped onto the Vajradhātu mandala deities. It is the earliest surviving dated Sanskrit commentary on the Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vilasavajra_namamantrartha.attribution: Traditional attribution to Vilāsavajra (Tibetan: sGeg pa'i rdo rje).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vilasavajra_namamantrartha.edition: Anthony Tribe, Tantric Buddhist Practice in India: Vilāsavajra's commentary on the Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti (Routledge Studies in Tantric Traditions), London / New York: Routledge, 2016, pp. 221–289.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vilasavajra_namamantrartha.coverage: partial — Contains chapters (adhikāras) 1 to 5 only, ending with the colophon of chapter 5: āryanāmasaṃgītiṭīkāyāṃ nāmamantrārthāvalokinyāṃ bodhicittavajrasya vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalādhikāraḥ pañcamaḥ. The complete work comprises 14 chapters.
translations: phags pa mtshan yang dag par brjod pa'i rgya cher 'grel pa mtshan gsang sngags kyi don du rnam par lta ba zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 2533): translated by Smṛtijñānakīrti; revised by Vajrapāṇi, shes rab brtsegs pa (Tibetan)

SA_T02_ilx_hh_vagisvarakirti_tattvaratna.title: Tattvaratnāvaloka with Tattvaratnāvalokavivaraṇa
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vagisvarakirti_tattvaratna.author: Vāgīśvarakīrti
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vagisvarakirti_tattvaratna.summary: The Tattvaratnāvaloka and its autocommentary Vivaraṇa by Vāgīśvarakīrti offer a doxographical and philosophical analysis of ultimate reality (tattva) and the soteriological goal (sādhya). The text reviews non-Buddhist views before systematizing Buddhist views of the goal according to the Pāramitānaya and Mantranaya, culminating in a detailed discussion of non-dual awareness, cognitive forms (ākāra), and the fourth consecration (caturthābhiṣeka) within the Guhyasamāja tantric lineage.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vagisvarakirti_tattvaratna.attribution: Both the 21 kārikās and the accompanying prose commentary are attributed in their colophons to Vāgīśvarakīrti (Paṇḍitavāgīśvarakīrtipāda / Paṇḍitācāryavāgīśvarakīrtipāda).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vagisvarakirti_tattvaratna.edition: Ryan Conlon (ed.), provisional critical draft edition (March 9, 2024), based on manuscript witnesses collated with the printed edition (siglum E~DH~).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_vagisvarakirti_tattvaratna.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 21 verses of the Tattvaratnāvaloka interlinearly embedded within the prose autocommentary (Tattvaratnāvalokavivaraṇa), ending with both works' colophons.
translations: de kho na nyid rin po che snang ba (Derge Tengyur D 1889): translated by 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)
de kho na nyid rin po che snang ba'i rnam par bshad pa (Derge Tengyur D 1890): translated by 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_GR14_ilx_hh_isvarasamhita.title: Īśvarasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_isvarasamhita.summary: The Īśvarasaṃhitā is a prominent canonical text of the Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava Āgama, traditionally treated as an elaboration of the foundational Sāttvatasaṃhitā. Spanning 25 chapters, it systematically sets forth temple rituals, daily worship (nityapūjā), the fivefold division of time (pañcakāla), temple layout, iconography, image consecration (pratiṣṭhā), initiation (dīkṣā), and expiation (prāyaścitta). It is historically significant in the South Indian Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition, notably informing ritual practice at Melkote (Yadugiri).
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_isvarasamhita.edition: Īśvarasaṃhitā, ed. Prativādibhayaṅkara Anantācārya, Śāstramuktāvalī series, Kāñcī, 1923.
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_isvarasamhita.coverage: complete — Complete text in 25 adhyāyas (1.1 to 25.217), terminating with the colophon of chapter 25 ('iti śrīpāñcarātre īśvarasaṃhitāyāṃ kuṇḍasruksruvalakṣaṇahaviḥpākavidhānaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ') and final completion statement 'īśvarasaṃhitā samāptā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_hh_sarvavarman_katantra_w_co.title: Kātantra with Kātantravṛtti
SA_GS24_ilx_hh_sarvavarman_katantra_w_co.author: Śarvavarman, Durgasiṃha
SA_GS24_ilx_hh_sarvavarman_katantra_w_co.summary: The Kātantra (also known as Kalāpa or Kaumāra), attributed to Śarvavarman, is the foundational work of the earliest post-Pāṇinian Sanskrit grammatical school. Designed as an accessible alternative to Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī without employing the complex Śivasūtra pratyāhāra apparatus, it systematically treats phonology and sandhi, nominal morphology and compounds, verbal conjugation, and primary derivatives across four books. Durgasiṃha's Kātantravṛtti is the canonical commentary elucidating the sūtras, which established the school's doctrinal authority and ensured its widespread transmission throughout Kashmir, eastern India, Central Asia, and Tibet.
SA_GS24_ilx_hh_sarvavarman_katantra_w_co.attribution: The root grammatical sūtras of the Kātantra (or Kalāpa) are traditionally attributed to Śarvavarman (revealed by Kumāra/Kārtikeya). The primary vṛtti is composed by Durgasiṃha.
SA_GS24_ilx_hh_sarvavarman_katantra_w_co.edition: Śarvavarman: The Kātantra. With the commentary of Durgasiṃha. Ed., with notes and indexes by Julius Eggeling. Reprint of the ed. Calcutta, Austin, 1874-1878. - Osnabrück: Biblio- Verl., 1991. [Bibliotheca Indica; Vol. 81]
SA_GS24_ilx_hh_sarvavarman_katantra_w_co.coverage: complete — Complete text of the four canonical books (sandhi, nāman, ākhyāta, kṛt) along with Durgasiṃha's commentary, concluding at Kāt 4.6.116 (iti daurgasiṃhyāṃ vṛttau kṛtsu ṣaṣṭhaḥ pādaḥ samāptaḥ; iti kātantraṃ samāptam).

SA_GR14_ilx_hh_sriprasnasamhita.title: Śrīpraśnasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_sriprasnasamhita.summary: The Śrīpraśnasaṃhitā is a canonical Pāñcarātra Āgama framed as teachings delivered by the Lord to the goddess Śrī. It provides comprehensive rules for Śrīvaiṣṇava temple ritual and worship, covering temple architecture, iconographic specifications, consecration rites (pratiṣṭhā), regular and festive rituals (pavitrotsava, brahmotsava), mantra systems, and initiation (dīkṣā).
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_sriprasnasamhita.attribution: A canonical saṃhitā of the Pāñcarātra tradition, presented as instruction originating from Nārāyaṇa upon queries posed by the goddess Śrī.
SA_GR14_ilx_hh_sriprasnasamhita.coverage: complete — 53 adhyāyas (apparatus notes mention chapter 54 in the Grantha book). Includes detached apparatus notes recording readings from a Grantha printed book ('gra. pustake').

SA_T02_ilx_hh_sakyaraksita_abhisamayaman.title: Abhisamayamañjarī
SA_T02_ilx_hh_sakyaraksita_abhisamayaman.author: Śākyarakṣita
SA_T02_ilx_hh_sakyaraksita_abhisamayaman.summary: The Abhisamayamañjarī is a Sanskrit sādhana and visualization manual dedicated to Vajrayoginī/Vajravārāhī. It covers purification rituals, mantras, balis, and various visual forms and maṇḍala configurations of the deity.
SA_T02_ilx_hh_sakyaraksita_abhisamayaman.attribution: The colophon of the text reads: 'śrīvajrayoginīsādhanam abhisamayamañjarīnāma mahācāryaśubhākaraguptaracitaṃ samāptam'. However, the work is attributed to Śākyarakṣita in manuscript and scholarly literature. The Tibetan translation (D 1582) attributes the work to Śubhākara (dge ba'i 'byung gnas sbas pa).
SA_T02_ilx_hh_sakyaraksita_abhisamayaman.coverage: complete — Complete text matching pages 123–154 of Dhīḥ vol. 12, running from the initial maṅgala to the concluding verses and final colophon.
translations: mngon par rtogs pa'i snye ma (Derge Tengyur D 1582): translated by Dānaśīla (Tibetan)

SA_MB_ilx_mb_Agamagrantha_I00041.title: Āgamagrantha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_Agamagrantha_I00041.summary: An unpublished Śaivasiddhānta liturgical compendium transcribed from palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 30718. It contains practical temple ritual chapters, drawing extensively on Aghoraśivācārya's Kriyākramadyotikā (including Dvārādipratiṣṭhāvidhi, Vināyakotsava, Bṛhattālādiṛkṣotsava, and Prāyaścittavidhi) alongside extracts from the Svāyambhuvāgama, Suprabhedāgama, and Siddhāntaśekhara detailing the Śivarātri observance, movable liṅga consecration, and snapana rituals.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_Agamagrantha_I00041.attribution: A practical South Indian Śaivasiddhānta temple priest's liturgical notebook (pustaka) collating excerpts from canonical dualistic Āgamas alongside ritual procedures from Aghoraśivācārya's Kriyākramadyotikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_Agamagrantha_I00041.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 30718 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), 119 folios (390 x 33 mm), transcribed by the IFP Indology team under the direction of Deviprasad Mishra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_Agamagrantha_I00041.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the 119-folio palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 30718.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgrahaH_I00020.title: Āgamavacanasaṅgraha (fragment)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgrahaH_I00020.summary: An anonymous anthology of āgamic quotations used in South Indian Śaiva temple ritual, transmitted in a damaged IFP manuscript. It collects verses on abhiṣeka substances, kinds of liṅga, darbha grasses and leaves for worship, and offerings. It also gives many iconographic meditation verses (dhyāna) for Reṇukā, Kālī, Somāskanda, Ekapādamūrti, Trimūrti, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, Liṅgodbhava, Gaurī and Sadāśiva, some from the Kāraṇa, Santāna and Sahasra āgamas, alongside vrata instructions and Tamil and astrological notes.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgrahaH_I00020.attribution: Anonymous South Indian (Tamil-area) Śaiva Siddhānta anthology of quotations. Some sections are headed by their sources, e.g. kāraṇe, santāne, sahasre (Kāraṇa-, Santāna- and Sahasrāgama). The manuscript also contains Tamil passages.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgrahaH_I00020.edition: Transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf manuscript RE 32446, by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra; IFP and Muktabodha, ©2023 (Muktabodha catalog no. I00020; CC BY-NC 4.0), via the ilx_skt TEI corpus.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgrahaH_I00020.coverage: fragment — The transcription of IFP manuscript RE 32446 starts at fol. 7a (folios 1–6 lost). It runs to fol. 55a with gaps: no markers for fols. 19b–20a, 23b–25b, 27a, 34a, 43b, and fol. 53b follows at the end. Many lines are damaged ('…'). The final leaves contain astrological terms and Tamil verses. The original extent is unknown.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgraha_I00024.title: Āgamavacanasaṅgraha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgraha_I00024.summary: An Āgamic ritual compilation (saṅgraha) preserved in IFP palm-leaf manuscript RE 20082, collecting authoritative passages from various Śaiva Āgamas (such as the Kāraṇāgama, Vātulāgama, and an Aṣṭāviṃśatyāgamasaṅgraha). It details deity installation (pratiṣṭhā), nyāsa techniques including the six paths (ṣaḍadhvanyāsa), dhyāna-ślokas, oblation rules, and ablutions (snāna/abhiṣeka).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgraha_I00024.attribution: A Tamil/Grantha scribal note at the opening attributes ownership and copying to Tirumenināthan, son of Daivaśikhāmaṇi Paṭṭar (teyvaśikāmaṇipaṭṭarputran tirumenināthan nyāsapratiṣṭhā pradoṣādyānirvacana pustakam ... svahastalikhitam).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgraha_I00024.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) MS RE 20082 (49 palm leaves). Transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra; IFP and Muktabodha Indological Research Institute collaboration (2023/2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AgamavacanasaGgraha_I00024.coverage: partial — Compilation of excerpted Āgama passages transcribed from the 49 palm leaves of IFP MS RE 20082; lacks a concluding colophon, ending without an explicit after verses on abhiṣeka.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandavanaH_mukundavanaziSy.title: Rāmārcanacandrikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandavanaH_mukundavanaziSy.author: Ānandavana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandavanaH_mukundavanaziSy.summary: The Rāmārcanacandrikā is a five-chapter (paṭala) Vaiṣṇava ritual manual (paddhati) on the worship of Rāma, composed by Ānandavana, disciple of Mukundavana. Synthesizing Vaiṣṇava Āgama, Pāñcarātra, and Purāṇic authorities (including the Rāmatāpanīya Upaniṣad and Agastyasaṃhitā), the work details mantra purification (śodhana), initiation (dīkṣā), daily ritual worship, yantra construction, and vow observances.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandavanaH_mukundavanaziSy.attribution: The author identifies himself in the opening verses and concluding colophons as Ānandavana, disciple of Mukundavana (iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryyaśrīmanmukuṃdavanaśrīcaraṇaśiṣyānandavanaviracitāyām).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandavanaH_mukundavanaziSy.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library (Jammu) MS No. 4740 (dated Saṃvat 1929, 69 folios), digitized by eGangotri on archive.org
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandavanaH_mukundavanaziSy.coverage: complete — Complete work in five paṭalas, comprising 69 folios (approx. 2300 ślokas) as stated in the manuscript header and colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandezvarapaddhatiH_M00624.title: Ānandeśvarapaddhatiḥ
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandezvarapaddhatiH_M00624.summary: A comprehensive ritual manual (paddhati) and liturgical codex representing the Kashmirian Śākta-Śaiva tradition. It sets out elaborate procedural instructions for pūjā and fire oblations (homa/agnikārya) directed to Kashmirian regional goddesses and Śākta deities, including Śārikā, Śāradā, Mahārājñī, Kubjikā, and Tripurasundarī. The manuscript codex additionally incorporates several ancillary ritual tracts and hymns such as the Amṛteśvarapatrikā, the eighth mayūkha of the Arcāratna, and the Pañcamīstavarāja from the Rudrayāmalatantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandezvarapaddhatiH_M00624.attribution: A paddhati codex compiling Kashmirian Śaiva-Śākta ritual procedures, homa manuals, and stotras without named personal authorship.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandezvarapaddhatiH_M00624.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS 5520 gh (Alm. 25, Shlf. 2, Gha, Devanagari script, 206 folios), Dharmartha Trust at Raghunath Temple, Jammu, J&K.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AnandezvarapaddhatiH_M00624.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the 206-folio manuscript codex, including the initial sūcīpatra, the main Ānandeśvarapaddhati, and appended auxiliary texts concluding with the Pañcamīstavarāja.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AtmArpaNastava_I00018.title: Ātmārpaṇastava, Śivatattvaviveka (incomplete), Śivajñānabodhopanyāsa, Śrīcakranirmāṇavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AtmArpaNastava_I00018.author: Appayya Dīkṣita, Nigamajñānadeśika
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AtmArpaNastava_I00018.summary: A transcription of a damaged South Indian palm-leaf bundle containing multiple Śaiva works, including the Ātmārpaṇastava, the Śivatattvaviveka, Nigamajñānadeśika's Śivajñānabodhopanyāsa, and the Śrīcakranirmāṇavidhi.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AtmArpaNastava_I00018.attribution: The colophon of the Śivajñānabodhopanyāsa names Nigamajñānadeśika of Vyāghrapura (recorded in the Muktabodha metadata as 'Nigamajñānadeśika (I.E. Nigamajñānadeva)'). The other works are listed as Unknown in the source metadata.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AtmArpaNastava_I00018.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP 30504 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), Muktabodha catalog no. I00018, revision 0, 2023/11/28.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AtmArpaNastava_I00018.coverage: partial — Diplomatic transcription of damaged palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 30504 (133 folios/pictures, 4–5 blank folios, damaged manuscript with marked lacunae). ilx_skt metadata classifies the completeness as 'fragments'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzIrvAdaparamparA_samudrasn.title: Āśīrvādaparamparā, Samudrasnānavidhi, Kālaprakāśikā, Sudhivilocana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzIrvAdaparamparA_samudrasn.summary: A composite South Indian manuscript transcription comprising short ritual and astrological texts: an Āśīrvādaparamparā (Śrīvaiṣṇava benedictory formulas for rites, invoking Godā, Rājagopālasvāmin, Rāmānuja, and Vedāntadeśika), a Samudrasnānavidhi (prescriptions for ritual ocean bathing), and astrological/muhūrta tables related to the Kālaprakāśikā and Sudhivilocana traditions (including lists of nakṣatras for siddhayoga and maraṇayoga glossed with Tamil weekday names).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzIrvAdaparamparA_samudrasn.attribution: A composite manuscript containing miscellaneous South Indian Śrīvaiṣṇava benedictory formulas, snānavidhi, and muhūrta/astrological tables.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzIrvAdaparamparA_samudrasn.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript RE 31158 (folios 1a–9a), transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra (Pondicherry: IFP / Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzIrvAdaparamparA_samudrasn.coverage: partial — Transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 31158 (folios 1a–9a); contains miscellaneous astrological excerpts/notes and ritual prayers without final colophon or complete texts for the major works cited.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzaucanirNaya_I00056.title: Āśaucanirṇaya with Maṇipravāḷavyākhyā (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzaucanirNaya_I00056.summary: The Āśaucanirṇaya is a South Indian ritual manual concerning the rules, duration, and purificatory observances for ceremonial impurity (āśauca) caused by birth (sūtaka) and death (mṛtāśauca). The Sanskrit kārikās are accompanied by an explanatory Maṇipravāḷa commentary in Tamil and Sanskrit discussing day-to-day exceptions, commensality, and purificatory rites.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzaucanirNaya_I00056.attribution: A South Indian Dharmaśāstra digest consisting of Sanskrit verses and an extensive Maṇipravāḷa (Tamil/Sanskrit) commentary. Folio 6b invokes or attributes material via 'vaidīkasārvabhauman', but specific authorship is not confirmed in the surviving folios.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzaucanirNaya_I00056.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 30577, Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), Grantha and Tamil scripts, 61 folios.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_AzaucanirNaya_I00056.coverage: partial — Defective at the beginning; folios 1–5a are missing in this transcript (text begins at fol. 5b, l. 1). The manuscript bundle also contains the Śrīlalitāsahasranāmāvalī and ritual verse fragments up to folio 61a.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_DAkinIkalpa_M00642.title: Ḍākinīkalpa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_DAkinIkalpa_M00642.summary: A Tantric ritual manual (kalpa) dealing with diagnosis, demonological afflictions (ḍākinī, bhūta, piśāca), and pacification of fever and somatic diseases classified by temporal coordinates such as days of the week (vāra), lunar tithis, and nakṣatras. It specifies bali offerings, mantric spells, and protective prognostic diagrams including the mṛtyucakra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_DAkinIkalpa_M00642.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library Jammu MS no. 1202gha (14 folios), unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_DAkinIkalpa_M00642.coverage: incomplete — Incomplete manuscript transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library Jammu no. 1202gha (14 folios). The text contains sections on vāradoṣa, Tithiḍākinīkalpa, nakṣatra afflictions, and begins a section on kālacakra / mṛtyucakra, breaking off after verse 1 without a concluding colophon or explicit.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_SaDAmnAyapUjAvidhi_M00556.title: Ṣaḍāmnāyapūjāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SaDAmnAyapUjAvidhi_M00556.summary: The Ṣaḍāmnāyapūjāvidhi is an anonymous Śākta ritual manual (paddhati) detailing daily worship rituals focused on Mahātripurasundarī structured by the six regional traditions (ṣaḍāmnāya) of Kaulism and Śrīvidyā. It prescribes the preliminary rites including morning ablutions, guru contemplation, bodily purification (bhūtaśuddhi), extensive nyāsa sequences (such as mātṛkā- and śrīkaṇṭhanyāsa), and the worship of surrounding retinue goddesses and cakras. The surviving manuscript witness was transcribed in Nepal in 1922 CE by Śāradāvilāsa Śarman for Nepalese Royal Preceptor Hemarāja Śarman from an older palm-leaf codex.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SaDAmnAyapUjAvidhi_M00556.attribution: An anonymous Śākta/Kaula ritual manual (paddhati) describing worship according to the six transmissions (ṣaḍāmnāya) centered on Tripurasundarī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SaDAmnAyapUjAvidhi_M00556.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMPP/NGMCP) MS 5/1932 (Reel no. A 248/40), copied in VS 1979 [ CE] by Śāradāvilāsa Śarman for Rājaguru Hemarāja Śarman from an older palm-leaf manuscript (unpublished digital transcription).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SaDAmnAyapUjAvidhi_M00556.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual transcribed from manuscript NGMCP 5/1932 (Reel A 248/40), concluding with the scribal colophon dated VS 1979 [1922 CE].

SA_MB_ilx_mb_SeSazAstrI_NatvabAdhAvidhUn.title: Tattvamālā with Ṇatvabādhāvidhūnana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SeSazAstrI_NatvabAdhAvidhUn.author: Śeṣaśāstrī
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SeSazAstrI_NatvabAdhAvidhUn.summary: Tattvamālā with its auto-commentary Ṇatvabādhāvidhūnana is a South Indian Śaiva theological-grammatical tract authored by Śeṣaśāstrī (Śeṣādri). Across 36 verses corresponding to the 36 tattvas of Śaiva philosophy, the author applies Pāṇinian vyākaraṇa (especially the rules of ṇatva in the compound name Nārāyaṇa) to defend the Appayya Dīkṣita tradition's thesis that Nārāyaṇa ultimately and etymologically refers to Paraśiva.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SeSazAstrI_NatvabAdhAvidhUn.attribution: Identified in the opening and closing verses as Śeṣaśāstrī (also called Śeṣādri), son of Veṅkaṭeśa and disciple of Rāmasvāmi Makhīndra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SeSazAstrI_NatvabAdhAvidhUn.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 30989 (34 folios) preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi, supervised by Deviprasad Mishra; Muktabodha Indological Research Institute & IFP, 2023 (Catalog no. I00019).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SeSazAstrI_NatvabAdhAvidhUn.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 30989 (34 folios), containing the work from the initial maṅgala through to the final dedication verses to Paraśiva, the guru-stuti of Rāmasvāmi Makhin, and the scribal colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_SoDazasubhrahmanyadhyAnam_I.title: Ṣoḍaśasubrahmaṇyadhyāna with Ṣoḍaśagaṇapatidhyāna, Pañcaviṃśatimaheśarūpabheda and Jātakaśiromaṇi (Jātakaśiromaṇi: bhāvas 1–7 only)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SoDazasubhrahmanyadhyAnam_I.summary: A South Indian palm-leaf bundle (IFP RE 10778) with dhyāna verses for sixteen forms of Subrahmaṇya/Skanda (Ṣoḍaśasubrahmaṇyadhyāna), sixteen forms of Gaṇapati and twenty-five iconographic forms of Śiva (Somāskanda, Naṭarāja, Liṅgodbhava, etc.). It ends with an incomplete astrological tract, the Jātakaśiromaṇi, on the results of the twelve houses, which reaches only the seventh. A Tamil loan deed is written on the last leaves.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SoDazasubhrahmanyadhyAnam_I.attribution: Anonymous ritual-iconographic and astrological texts preserved together in a South Indian palm-leaf manuscript bundle.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SoDazasubhrahmanyadhyAnam_I.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 10778 (Institut Français de Pondichéry, 30 folios), transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; published online by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute and IFP, 2024 (Catalog no. I00035).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_SoDazasubhrahmanyadhyAnam_I.coverage: partial — IFP bundle RE 10778 (30 images). The three dhyāna collections are complete, each with a samāpta colophon. The Jātakaśiromaṇi ("śrī jātakaśiromaṇīṃ dvādaśabhāvam", p.18b) treats the results of the twelve houses but breaks off in the 7th (kalatrabhāva) at p.26b. Then follow blank images p.27a–28a, a note on two palm leaves in a different hand, and a Tamil loan deed (kaṭan cīṭṭu, p.28b–29a).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_UrdhvAmnAya_M00640.title: Ūrdhvāmnāya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_UrdhvAmnAya_M00640.summary: The Ūrdhvāmnāya is an esoteric Śaiva-Śākta Tantric dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī establishing the transcendent authority of the 'upper transmission' (ūrdhvāmnāya) emerging from Śiva's upper face above the other four directional transmissions. It treats the nature of spiritual liberation, qualifications of the Kaula practitioner and guru, and esoteric mantra rituals, concluding here with the praises of the Prāsādaparā mantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_UrdhvAmnAya_M00640.attribution: Revealed scripture in dialogic form between Īśvara (Śiva) and Devī expounding the superiority and esoteric practices of the upper transmission (ūrdhvāmnāya).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_UrdhvAmnAya_M00640.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 4894 (35 folios) preserved at the Shri Raghunatha Temple MSS Library, Jammu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_UrdhvAmnAya_M00640.coverage: unclear — Diplomatic transcription of 35 folios of Jammu MS 4894; breaks off abruptly at segment [604] after verses on the recitation of the Śrīprāsādaparāmantra without a final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_aMzumattantrazaGkhAbhiSekam.title: Aṃśumattantraśaṅkhābhiṣeka (with miscellaneous ritual texts)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aMzumattantrazaGkhAbhiSekam.summary: A collection of Śaiva ritual procedures transcribed from IFP palm-leaf bundle RE 31392. It opens with the Śaṅkhābhiṣekavidhi attributed to the Aṃśumattantra, expounding the characteristics, classification, and sanctification of conches (śaṅkha) for ritual lustration of Śiva. This is followed by complementary temple festival rites including seed sprouting (aṅkurārpaṇa), flag hoisting (dhvajārohaṇa from the Kāmikāgama), and a day-by-day temple festival sequence (utsavavidhi) through the powder festival (cūrṇotsava).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aMzumattantrazaGkhAbhiSekam.attribution: The primary section invokes the Aṃśumattantra (Aṃśumadāgama); the manuscript also includes Dhvajārohaṇavidhi from the Kāmikāgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aMzumattantrazaGkhAbhiSekam.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 31392 (29 folios), Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP). Transcribed by the IFP Indology team under Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; published online by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog I00046, 2025).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aMzumattantrazaGkhAbhiSekam.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the 29-folio palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 31392.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTAdazakriyA_I00060.title: Aṣṭādaśakriyā (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTAdazakriyA_I00060.summary: An anonymous Śaiva manual on the eighteen ritual operations (aṣṭādaśakriyā) connected with temple consecration (pratiṣṭhā), transcribed from palm-leaf bundle RE31059. The text covers preliminary rites (Pratiṣṭhādhivāsanavidhi), worship of the tattvas (Tattvārcanā), touch-oblations (Sparśāhuti), and partial sections of the installation of Gaurī (Gaurīpratiṣṭhā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTAdazakriyA_I00060.attribution: Anonymous Śaiva paddhati on the eighteen ritual operations (kriyā) of consecration (pratiṣṭhā). No author is named in the surviving text.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTAdazakriyA_I00060.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of the palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 31059 (39 folios, 41.5 × 3.5 cm, 7–8 lines per side), Muktabodha catalog no. I00060, revision 0, 8 May 2026. No printed edition is known.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTAdazakriyA_I00060.coverage: partial — The transcription begins on folio 4a (image 3b) ('oṃ hāṃ bhairavāya namaḥ - anāmikāgraparve'), so folios 1–3 are lost. The text breaks off on the final image in the middle of a list of tattva oblations ('ākāśatatvādhipataye - sūkṣmāya svāhā'), without a final colophon. The Muktabodha description says the final Gaurīpratiṣṭhā section 'appears incomplete'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTamAtRkApUjA_M00540.title: Navapīṭhāṣṭamātṛkāpūjāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTamAtRkApUjA_M00540.summary: The Navapīṭhāṣṭamātṛkāpūjāvidhi is a Nepalese Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) for the worship and bali offerings dedicated to the eight Mother Goddesses (Aṣṭamātṛkā) across the sacred pithas of the Kathmandu Valley, typically performed during life-cycle events such as marriage (vivāha) and ihi. The work consists of Sanskrit mantras, dhyānas, and stotras interspersed with ritual stage directions and recording notations in Classical Newari.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTamAtRkApUjA_M00540.attribution: A traditional Newar ritual handbook combining Sanskrit mantras/stotras with Newari ritual stage directions (paddhati).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTamAtRkApUjA_M00540.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript ms./596 (Reel No. A 436/7).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTamAtRkApUjA_M00540.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual transcribed from manuscript NGMCP 1/596 (Reel No. A 436/7), including introductory rites, pūjā sequences, dhyānas, stotras, and post-colophon Newari records of ceremonies from Nepal Samvat 810 to 848.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTottarazatanAmAni_I00050.title: Aṣṭottaraśatanāmāni
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTottarazatanAmAni_I00050.summary: A liturgical anthology of approximately seventeen aṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalīs (108 names in dative case with namaḥ) preserved in the South Indian palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 31378. Spanning Śaiva, Śākta, Vaiṣṇava, and Saura traditions (including Śiva, Gaṇapati, Subrahmaṇya, Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Narasiṃha, Viṣṇu, Harihara, the Saptarṣis, and Tripurasundarī), the compilation was intended for arcana and daily worship.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTottarazatanAmAni_I00050.attribution: Anonymously compiled liturgical handbook intended for temple arcana, domestic worship, and personal devotional recitation.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTottarazatanAmAni_I00050.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 31378 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), prepared by scholars at IFP under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra; published online by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute in collaboration with IFP (e-text catalog no. I00050).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aSTottarazatanAmAni_I00050.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the 43 folios of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 31378, containing approximately 17 liturgical name collections (nāmāvalīs) with lacunae and scribal corrections noted by the transcriber.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_agastyasaMhitA_M00574.title: Agastyasaṃhitā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_agastyasaMhitA_M00574.summary: The Agastyasaṃhitā is a Vaiṣṇava text framed as a dialogue between the sage Agastya and his disciple Sutīkṣṇa, incorporating teachings revealed by Śiva to Pārvatī. It expounds mantras, dhyānas, yantras, dīkṣā procedures, temple rituals, and worship centering on Rāma alongside Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, and Hanūmān.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_agastyasaMhitA_M00574.attribution: Tradition attributes the revelation to the sage Agastya instructing Sutīkṣṇa, containing an inner dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_agastyasaMhitA_M00574.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS No. 5294 (46 folios), Shri Raghunatha Temple MSS Library, Jammu, selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski; data-entered under the supervision of Anirban Dash for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00574; revision 1: Apr. 4, 2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_agastyasaMhitA_M00574.coverage: complete — Complete in 32 adhyāyas, concluding with 'itiśrīagastisaṃhitāyāṃdvātriṃśodhyāyaḥ' and 'samāptoyaṃgraṃthaḥ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_aghorazivAcArya_mahotsavavi.title: Kriyākramadyotikā (Mahotsavavidhi and Prāyaścittavidhi)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aghorazivAcArya_mahotsavavi.author: Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aghorazivAcArya_mahotsavavi.summary: This text contains two major ritual sections from Aghoraśiva's Śaivasiddhānta paddhati, the Kriyākramadyotikā: the Mahotsavavidhi and the Prāyaścittavidhi. The Mahotsavavidhi provides exhaustive prescriptions for the temple's annual festival (mahotsava), including flag raising (dhvajārohaṇa), yāgaśālā ceremonies, processional rites, and sacred immersion. The Prāyaścittavidhi outlines expiatory rituals, homas, and rededications for ritual flaws, impurities, and structural disruptions in the Śiva temple.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aghorazivAcArya_mahotsavavi.attribution: Aghoraśiva composed the Kriyākramadyotikā (frequently called Aghoraśivapaddhati).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aghorazivAcArya_mahotsavavi.edition: Diplomatic transcript of palm-leaf manuscript IFP MS 30722, Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), prepared under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi, 2023 (Muktabodha catalog no. I00004).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_aghorazivAcArya_mahotsavavi.coverage: partial — Covers two sections of the Kriyākramadyotikā: Mahotsavavidhi (ff. 1a–45a) and Prāyaścittavidhi (ff. 45a–91a).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezatantra_M00504.title: Amṛteśatantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezatantra_M00504.summary: The Amṛteśatantra (commonly known as the Netratantra) is an influential Śaiva tantra dedicated to the worship of Amṛteśa / Mṛtyuñjaya and Amṛtalakṣmī. Across 24 chapters, it presents mantric procedures, yogic visualizations, initiation (dīkṣā), and extensive rites for pacification, healing, royal protection, and liberation. This e-text is a diplomatic transcription of an early dated palm-leaf manuscript from Nepal copied in Nepāla Saṃvat 320 (c. 1101 CE).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezatantra_M00504.attribution: Canonical Śaiva tantra framed as an instruction from Śiva (Bhagavān) to the Devī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezatantra_M00504.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS no. pra-285 (Reel B25/4), palm-leaf manuscript dated Nepāla Saṃvat 320 (c. 1101 CE), copied by Paṇḍita Kīrtidhara.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezatantra_M00504.coverage: complete — Complete across all 24 paṭalas, concluding at chapter 24 (caturviṃśatimaḥ paṭalaḥ) followed by a scribal colophon dated Nepāla Saṃvat 320.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezvaradikSAvidhi_M00539.title: Amṛteśvaradīkṣāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezvaradikSAvidhi_M00539.author: Viśveśvara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezvaradikSAvidhi_M00539.summary: The Amṛteśvaradīkṣāvidhi is a Śaiva ritual manual (paddhati/ṭippaṇaka) detailing the initiation procedures (dīkṣā) according to the Amṛteśvarabhairava (Netratantra) cult, composed by Viśveśvara. It opens with verses emphasizing the rarity and value of human birth and the impermanence of the body, before systematically setting forth the purification of tattvas, kalās, and cosmic realms (bhuvanas) necessary to liberate the disciple.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezvaradikSAvidhi_M00539.attribution: Composed by Viśveśvara on the basis of the Netratantra / Amṛteśvarabhairava tradition and wider Śaiva āgamas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezvaradikSAvidhi_M00539.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of NGMCP MS 5-4867 (Reel No. A 231/17), Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, Catalog No. M00539
SA_MB_ilx_mb_amRtezvaradikSAvidhi_M00539.coverage: partial — Incomplete at the beginning due to manuscript loss: lacks the opening incipit (verses 1–4 missing, text begins in media res with verse 5); preserved through the final colophon at verse 12 of the concluding section.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_anAdivIrazaivasaGgraha_M006.title: Anādivīraśaivasārasaṅgraha (part 1)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anAdivIrazaivasaGgraha_M006.author: Saṃpādanasiddhavīra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anAdivIrazaivasaGgraha_M006.summary: The Anādivīraśaivasārasaṅgraha by Saṃpādanasiddhavīra is a Vīraśaiva theological compendium vindicating the antiquity (anāditva) of the Vīraśaiva tradition. It integrates scriptural citations from Vedic, Āgamic, and Purāṇic literature with expository prose, articulating doctrines of the aṣṭāvaraṇa and ṣaṭsthala. This first volume encompasses chapters 1 through 8, culminating in the Viśvotpattisthala.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anAdivIrazaivasaGgraha_M006.attribution: Composed by the Vīraśaiva scholar-yogi Saṃpādanasiddhavīra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anAdivIrazaivasaGgraha_M006.edition: Anādivīraśaivasārasaṃgraha (bhāga 1). Edited by Maṇūra Maṭhādhyakṣa Mallikārjuna Śāstrī. Solapur: Vīraśaivaliṅgibrāhmaṇadharmagranthamālā (grantha 19), Śake 1827 / CE 1905.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anAdivIrazaivasaGgraha_M006.coverage: partial — Contains Part 1 (bhāga 1), comprising prakaraṇas 1–8, ending with the Viśvotpattisthala.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_anantazambhu_siddhAntasArAv.title: Siddhāntasārāvalī with Siddhāntasārāvalīvyākhyā (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anantazambhu_siddhAntasArAv.author: Trilocanaśivācārya, Anantaśambhu
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anantazambhu_siddhAntasArAv.summary: The Siddhāntasārāvalī of Trilocanaśivācārya (12th c.) is a verse compendium of Śaiva Siddhānta doctrine and ritual, arranged in the four pādas: jñāna, kriyā, yoga and caryā. Anantaśambhu's commentary explains it with extensive quotations from the Siddhāntāgamas and ritual manuals. Its topics include the categories pati, paśu and pāśa, the tattvas, daily and occasional worship, initiation (dīkṣā), yoga, and festivals and pratiṣṭhā (installation). This e-text transcribes a single incomplete and partly disordered IFP palm-leaf manuscript.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anantazambhu_siddhAntasArAv.attribution: Root text by Trilocanaśivācārya (12th c., Tamil Nadu), who is named in the commentator's introduction as resident of the Āmardaka maṭha. Commentary by Anantaśambhu, possibly 14th c. The manuscript also contains, on fols. 7b–9b, unrelated ritual extracts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anantazambhu_siddhAntasArAv.edition: No printed edition; transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf manuscript 30687 (160 fols., 42 × 4 cm), by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra; IFP and Muktabodha, ©2023 (Muktabodha catalog no. I00022; CC BY-NC 4.0), via the ilx_skt TEI corpus.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_anantazambhu_siddhAntasArAv.coverage: partial — IFP palm-leaf manuscript 30687 (160 fols.; incomplete, some folios out of order). Present: the Jñānapāda (colophon '[jñānapādaṃ samāptam]'); the Kriyāpāda, of which according to the IFP description only 90 of 118 verses survive (colophon); and the Yogapāda (8 verses, colophon). The Caryāpāda (41 verses according to the description) breaks off on fol. 159b in the section on liṅga proportions, without a colophon. Fol. 160 is unreadable.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_antyeSTividhi_I00049.title: Antyeṣṭividhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_antyeSTividhi_I00049.summary: A South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta funerary manual for initiates (Viśeṣāntyeṣṭi), transcribed from a single palm-leaf bundle (IFP RE30578). It serves as a guide to Adhvaśuddhi, mapping out the four Kalās (Śānti, Vidyā, Pratiṣṭhā, Nivṛtti) with their constituent Tattvas, Bhuvanas, Varṇas, Padas, and Mantras, and covers the 12-day post-mortuary cycle.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_antyeSTividhi_I00049.attribution: Author field left empty because no author is named in the available evidence for this manuscript bundle.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_antyeSTividhi_I00049.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE30578 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), Muktabodha catalog no. I00049, revision 0, 20 Jan. 2026.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_antyeSTividhi_I00049.coverage: complete — The markers '(p.5b, l.1)' … '(p.88a, l.1)' are pdf image numbers, not folio numbers. The transcriber's notes say 'p = pdf picture'. The text opens with a heading ('antyeṣṭividhiḥ', 'athā adhvaśuddhi vitāntyeṣṭiḥ', image 5b) and ends with 'śubhamastu' (image 88a). The Muktabodha description notes that the codex is in excellent condition, showing no signs of decay or damage, and its listed contents match the text.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bRhattAlavidhi_I00030.title: Kriyākramadyotikā (excerpts: Bṛhattālādiṛkṣotsavāntavidhi, Śāntihomavidhi, Prāyaścittavidhi)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bRhattAlavidhi_I00030.author: Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bRhattAlavidhi_I00030.summary: Excerpts from the Kriyākramadyotikā of Aghoraśiva, transcribed from IFP palm-leaf bundle RE 32406. The sections cover festival rites including bṛhattāla, navasandhi, monthly, fortnightly, and asterism festivals, an extensive portion of prāyaścittavidhi, and an incomplete ending section on śivaliṅgapañcāsanapūjā with citations on Śivarātri from the Kāmika and Lalita Āgamas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bRhattAlavidhi_I00030.attribution: The IFP/Muktabodha header notes that this bundle contains sections from Śrīmadaghōraśivācāryar’s Kriyākramadyōtikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bRhattAlavidhi_I00030.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of the palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32406 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), Muktabodha catalog no. I00030, revision 0, 14 Oct. 2024.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bRhattAlavidhi_I00030.coverage: excerpt — Selected sections from Aghoraśiva's Kriyākramadyotikā: rituals related to utsavapūjāvidhi such as bṛhattāla, navasandhi, māsotsava, pakṣotsava, and ṛkṣotsava, along with prāyaścittavidhi and incomplete sections on śivaliṅgapañcāsanapūjā and Śivarātri citations.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bagalAmukhIpaJcAGgam_M00623.title: Bagalāmukhīpañcāṅga
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bagalAmukhIpaJcAGgam_M00623.summary: The Bagalāmukhīpañcāṅga is a Śākta tantric liturgical compendium comprising traditional liturgical limbs (such as paṭala, kavaca, and stavarāja) for the worship of Bagalāmukhī, one of the ten Mahāvidyās. It details the Brahmāstra mantra formulae, yantra diagrams, nyāsa rites, dhyāna visualizations, and praise-hymns primarily aimed at stambhana (immobilization/paralysis of enemies and obstacles), protection, and spiritual accomplishment.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bagalAmukhIpaJcAGgam_M00623.attribution: A traditional five-limbed liturgical manual (pañcāṅga) dedicated to the Mahāvidyā Bagalāmukhī, with sections ascribed to revelation tantras including the Rudrayāmala.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bagalAmukhIpaJcAGgam_M00623.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Devanagari manuscript no. 6025 (accession no. 1636 ka), Dharmartha Trust Library at Raghunath Temple, Jammu, dated VS 1939 [ CE].
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bagalAmukhIpaJcAGgam_M00623.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript witness, concluding with the scribal colophon dated VS 1939 (1882 CE) executed in Jammu.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAnudIkSitaH_nArAyaNadIkSi.title: Mātṛkārṇanighaṇṭu
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAnudIkSitaH_nArAyaNadIkSi.author: Bhānudīkṣita
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAnudIkSitaH_nArAyaNadIkSi.summary: The Mātṛkārṇanighaṇṭu (or Mātṛkāvarṇasaṃgraha) is a short tantric glossary in 87 verses composed by Bhānudīkṣita, son of Nārāyaṇa Dīkṣita. It systematically catalogues the esoteric names, deities, bodily locations, and symbolic code-words associated with each syllable of the Sanskrit alphabet (mātṛkā)—from oṃkāra and a to kṣa—serving as a key for mantroddhāra (the deciphering and construction of secret mantras encoded in tantric treatises).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAnudIkSitaH_nArAyaNadIkSi.attribution: Identified in verse 4 (śrībhānunā) and the closing colophon as Bhānudīkṣita, son of Nārāyaṇa Dīkṣita (śrīmatsakalavidvānmaṇḍalīmaṇḍana-śrīdīkṣitanārāyaṇa-tanaya-dīkṣitabhānu).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAnudIkSitaH_nArAyaNadIkSi.edition: Diplomatic transcript of MS 4858 (Alm. 22, Shlf. 1, Tantra section, 6 folios), Shri Raghunath Temple Manuscript Library, Dharmartha Trust, Jammu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAnudIkSitaH_nArAyaNadIkSi.coverage: complete — Complete text in 87 verses with opening maṅgala and concluding colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAskararAya_gurukalA_M0068.title: Mālāmantroddhāra with Gurukalā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAskararAya_gurukalA_M0068.author: Bhāskararāya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAskararAya_gurukalA_M0068.summary: The Gurukalā (also known as the Khaḍgamālābhāṣya) is Bhāskararāya's commentary on the Mālāmantroddhāra section of the Lalitāpariśiṣṭatantra. It provides an exegesis of the fifteen Mālāmantras generated from the fifteen-syllabled Kādimata mantra, detailing the deities of the Śrīcakra, their symbolic weapons, and the ritual and meditative practices associated with the Khaḍgamālā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAskararAya_gurukalA_M0068.attribution: Bhāskararāya's authorship is stated in the introductory verses (vv. 2–3: 'bhāratyupākhyo bhārakararatyo gaṃbhīrarāyasunaḥ ... vyākurute') and the closing colophon: 'iti śrīgaṃbhīrādhvaritanujanurbhāskarabudhāgnicinnirdiṣṭāyāmiha gurukalānāmavikṛtau ... caramapaṭalaḥ paryavasitaḥ'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAskararAya_gurukalA_M0068.edition: Manuscript transcription: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (BORI), Pune, MS No. 7439 (Devanāgarī, 28 folios, dated Śaka 1838, copied by Tryambaka Gaṇeśa Pūrakara); transcribed by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00682).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAskararAya_gurukalA_M0068.coverage: complete — Complete text of both paṭalas of the Mālāmantroddhāra from the Lalitāpariśiṣṭatantra along with Bhāskararāya's commentary Gurukalā, ending at folio 28a with scribal colophons.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAvacUDAmaNi_M00575.title: Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAvacUDAmaNi_M00575.author: Vidyākaṇṭha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAvacUDAmaNi_M00575.summary: The Bhāvacūḍāmaṇi is an unedited Kashmirian Śaiva Siddhānta commentary composed by Vidyākaṇṭha (II), disciple of Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha (II). It serves as an extensive commentary on the Mayasaṅgraha, an Āgamic manual treating temple architecture (vāstu), iconography, installation of liṅgas (liṅgapratiṣṭhā), and Śaiva ritual practices. The text is preserved in a single unique manuscript witness held in Jammu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAvacUDAmaNi_M00575.attribution: Composed by Vidyākaṇṭha (II), disciple of Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha (II). The terminal scribal colophon refers to it as 'iti śrīmahāmaheśvareṇakṛtaṃ bhāvacūḍāmaṇīṃ nāma taṃtraṃ samāptam', but the introductory verses confirm Vidyākaṇṭha's authorship of this commentary on the Mayasaṅgraha.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAvacUDAmaNi_M00575.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library (Jammu), MS No. 5291 (codex unicus).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhAvacUDAmaNi_M00575.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the codex unicus, concluding with final benedictory verses and the closing colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhadrakAlipratiSThAvidhi_yA.title: Bhadrakālīpratiṣṭhāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhadrakAlipratiSThAvidhi_yA.summary: The Bhadrakālīpratiṣṭhāvidhi is a Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) for the consecration and installation (pratiṣṭhā/sthāpana) of the fierce goddess Bhadrakālī (identified in the opening verses as Cāmuṇḍā) in villages, towns, or sacred groves. It outlines the ritual calendar, construction and purification of the sacrificial pavilion (yāgaśālā) and fire-pits (kuṇḍa), gatekeeper invocations (toraṇapūjā), vase installations (kalaśasthāpana), nyāsa systems, mantras, and the culminating installation rites.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhadrakAlipratiSThAvidhi_yA.attribution: A paddhati/vidhi detailing the installation and worship of Bhadrakālī (also designated Cāmuṇḍā in the opening verse), attributed in the IFP manuscript record to a Yāmalatantra tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhadrakAlipratiSThAvidhi_yA.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript no. 30604, transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra, IFP / Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhadrakAlipratiSThAvidhi_yA.coverage: unclear — Transcribes ff. 1a–20a of IFP manuscript 30604. A sectional colophon '[iti yāmaḻāgame bhadrakāḻipratiṣṭhāvidhiḥ]' appears on f. 16b, followed on ff. 17a–20a by āvaraṇapūjā mantras and dhyāna verses; lacks a final explicit or closing colophon on f. 20a, where the text breaks off amid lacunae with 'bhadrakāḻīṃ namaste||'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhagavatutpala_spandapradIp.title: Spandapradīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhagavatutpala_spandapradIp.author: Bhagavatutpala
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhagavatutpala_spandapradIp.summary: The Spandapradīpikā is an exegetical commentary on the Spandakārikā composed by Bhagavatutpala (Utpala Vaiṣṇava) of Kashmir, probably active around the tenth century. The commentary is notable for its syncretic perspective, interpreting non-dual Śaiva Spanda concepts through the lens of Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava theology and citing early canonical saṃhitās such as the Jayākhya, Sātvata, Pauṣkara, and Ahirbudhnya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhagavatutpala_spandapradIp.attribution: The commentary is by Bhagavatutpala (Utpala Vaiṣṇava, son of Trivikrama).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhagavatutpala_spandapradIp.edition: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (ed.), Spandapradīpikā: A Commentary on the Spandakārikā by Bhagavadutpalācārya, Varanasi: Indica Books, 2000 (also keyed directly for Muktabodha M00532; the TEI header note referencing SUNY Press 1992 refers to Dyczkowski's accompanying translation volume).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhagavatutpala_spandapradIp.coverage: complete — Complete commentary running through the closing stanza and final colophon: 'ity ācāryabhagavadutpalaviracitā spandapradīpikā samāptā'.
translations: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, The Stanzas on Vibration: The Spandakārikā with Four Commentaries: The Spandasaṃdoha by Kṣemarāja, the Spandavṛtti by Kallaṭabhaṭṭa, the Spandavivṛti by Rājānaka Rāma, the Spandapradīpikā by Bhagavadutpala, Albany: State University of New York Press, 1992. (English)
Lilian Silburn, Spandakārikā: Stances sur la vibration de Vasugupta, PICI 58, Paris: Institut de Civilisation Indienne, 1990. (French)

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktavilAsa_I00013.title: Bhaktavilāsa (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktavilAsa_I00013.summary: The Bhaktavilāsa (Śivabhaktavilāsa), presented as part of the Skandapurāṇa and narrated by Agastya, is a Sanskrit verse text describing the details of Śiva devotees (such as Sundaramūrti, Mucukunda, Nīlakaṇṭha). This witness opens with a Śiva–Devī dialogue (end of adhyāya 2) and is an incomplete South Indian palm-leaf manuscript in the IFP collection.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktavilAsa_I00013.attribution: Ascribed in its colophons to the Skandapurāṇa (Bhaktamāhātmya). Agastya is the narrator. The IFP and Muktabodha records name 'Agastya' as author ('written by Sri Agastyar Maharshi').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktavilAsa_I00013.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of the palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 30846 (43 folios, 32 × 3.5 cm, 9 lines per side), Muktabodha catalog no. I00013, revision 0, 14 Aug. 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktavilAsa_I00013.coverage: partial — The first surviving leaf is folio 2a, which begins at verse 2.26 (Śiva–Devī dialogue). Chapter 1 and the start of chapter 2 are lost (colophon of adhyāya 2). The text breaks off in a damaged passage of the story of the hunter's son.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktotsava_I00044.title: Bhaktotsava
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktotsava_I00044.summary: A late Śaiva Siddhānta ritual compilation preserved in palm-leaf bundle RE30806 of the Institut Français de Pondichéry. It contains liturgical and festival procedures (utsavavidhi) including goddess festivals (śaktyutsava / devyutsava), the veneration of Śaiva saints/devotees (bhaktotsava), periodic festivals (vṛṣotsava / varṣotsava), expiations for ritual faults (utsavaprāyaścitta), marriage rituals (vivāha), and sacrificial fire division (agnivibhajana), drawing upon the Lalitāgama, Uttarakāmikāgama, and Kāraṇāgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktotsava_I00044.attribution: An anonymous South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta ritual compilation (prayoga/paddhati) combining temple festival procedures, domestic/sanskāra rites (marriage), and expiations extracted or adapted from canonical Śaivāgamas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktotsava_I00044.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE30806 (39 folios).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhaktotsava_I00044.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the 39 folios of IFP palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE30806, diplomatically recording scribal orthography, missing/damaged characters, and folio references.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bheritADana_cUrNikA_devatAv.title: Bherītāḍanādividhi (Ekāmranāthālaya)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bheritADana_cUrNikA_devatAv.summary: A Śaiva Āgamic liturgical ritual manual (prayoga) associated with the Ekāmranātha temple in Kanchipuram. It provides the procedural directions, mantras, musical notations, dance specifications, and rhythmic prose recitations (cūrṇikā) for beating the kettle-drum (bherītāḍana) to announce festival rites, invoking the deities (devatāvāhana), and executing musical-dance oblations to the directional guardians (sandhyāvāhana / dikpālasandhi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bheritADana_cUrNikA_devatAv.attribution: A practical Śaiva Āgamic liturgical manual (prayoga/paddhati) containing drum-proclamation rituals and directional offerings formulated for worship at the Ekāmranātha (Ekambareswarar) temple in Kanchipuram.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bheritADana_cUrNikA_devatAv.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 32397, Institut Français de Pondichéry. Unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bheritADana_cUrNikA_devatAv.coverage: complete — Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 32397 preserving the complete liturgical handbook as contained in the codex.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhojadeva_ascribed_to_siddh.title: Siddhāntasārapaddhati (beginning missing)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhojadeva_ascribed_to_siddh.author: Bhojadeva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhojadeva_ascribed_to_siddh.summary: An early Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual (paddhati) ascribed in its colophons to King Bhojadeva (Bhojarāja, 11th c.). Preserved in old Nepalese palm-leaf manuscripts, it details Śaiva ritual procedures (including nityakarman, initiation, consecration, and other rites) and was drawn upon by later authorities including Somaśambhu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhojadeva_ascribed_to_siddh.attribution: The section colophons ascribe the work to Mahārājādhirāja Śrī Bhojadeva. Muktabodha records the author as 'bhojadeva ascribed to'. Sanderson examines manuscripts of the work (identifying it as the Siddhāntasārapaddhati or Bhojadevapaddhati by Bhojadeva / Bhojarāja, r. 1018 to 1060) and demonstrates its influence on later Saiddhāntika ritual literature, including the Somaśambhupaddhati.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhojadeva_ascribed_to_siddh.edition: Unpublished transcription of the Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript NGMCP 5-743/vi (śaivatantra 203, Reel no: B 28/19).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bhojadeva_ascribed_to_siddh.coverage: partial — The e-text begins mid-sentence ('yena saptavāramati dīptāstrābhimantritena …') inside the daily rite (nityakarman), so the opening is missing (colophon at ilx_skt: iti mahārājādhirāja śrībhojadeva viracitāyāṃ siddhāntasārapaddhatau nityakarmavidhissamāptaḥ). The ilx_skt metadata classifies the file as 'incomplete' with the colophon note 'in middle'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_bodhAyanaprayoga_I00017.title: Bodhāyanaprayoga
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bodhAyanaprayoga_I00017.author: Pañcākṣaranātha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bodhAyanaprayoga_I00017.summary: A ritual manual following the Bodhāyana tradition. According to the manuscript description, it contains procedures for pūrvaprayoga and aparaprayoga, including snāna, prāṇāyāma, śrāddhaprayoga, gṛhasthasyaupāsana, vidhuraupāsanavidhi, brahmayajña, bhūtaśuddhi, mahānyāsa, Śiva-saṅkalpa, pañcabrahmanyāsa, aṣṭatriṃśatkalānyāsa, pañcākṣaranyāsa, bhojanavidhi, gṛhasthadharma, tailābhyaṅgavidhi, kṣauravidhi, strīdharma, vidhavādharma, followed by the Bodhāyanamantrapraśna arranged in āśvāsas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bodhAyanaprayoga_I00017.attribution: Associated with Pañcākṣaranātha based on the initial title/colophon heading 'bodhāyana-āhnikam - pañcākṣaranāthaviracitanityakarmaparicchedaḥ - bodhāyanamantrapraśnaḥ'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bodhAyanaprayoga_I00017.edition: Diplomatic transcript of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript RE 30720.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_bodhAyanaprayoga_I00017.coverage: partial — Manuscript transcription is incomplete, lacking explicit and final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrAvalocakana_M00506.title: Candrāvalokana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrAvalocakana_M00506.summary: The Candrāvalokana is a short Haṭhayogic tract framed as a dialogue between Maheśvara (Śiva) and Matsyendranātha. It is best known in yoga historiography as a key early source for the definition of śāmbhavīmudrā and the absorption (laya) of mind and breath, famously cited in chapter 4 of the Haṭhapradīpikā. It interprets esoteric yogic gazes through lunar allegories (amāvāsyā, pratipad, and paurṇamāsī).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrAvalocakana_M00506.attribution: Cast as an esoteric dialogue between Maheśvara and Matsyendranātha; colophon attributes it to Maheśvara ('iti maheśvareṇaviracitaṃ candrāvalokanam').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrAvalocakana_M00506.edition: Manuscript transcription from Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), transcript T00788.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrAvalocakana_M00506.coverage: complete — Complete short tract ending with the colophon 'iti maheśvareṇaviracitaṃ candrāvalokanam sampūrṇaṃ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrajJAna_nityArchanavidh.title: Candrajñāna (Mantravāsa and Nityārcanavidhi, incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrajJAna_nityArchanavidh.summary: Verse sections of the Śaiva Siddhānta scripture Candrajñāna(āgama) on the 'dwelling of mantras' (mantravāsa) and on the daily worship of Śiva (nityārcana), transcribed from a badly damaged South Indian palm-leaf manuscript. The surviving text covers the times of worship, images of wood, pedestals, the worship of Sūrya and Indra, the fruits of worship, the seats and the five purifications (bhūta-, mantra-śuddhi etc.), the lion-throne, the Sadāśiva form, invocation, food offering and bathing, and the bathing of the liṅga with various substances.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrajJAna_nityArchanavidh.attribution: Scriptural (āgamic) text. The colophon 'iti candratajñāne' ascribes the material to the Candrajñāna, associated with the Siddhāntāgama tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrajJAna_nityArchanavidh.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP manuscript 32608 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), Muktabodha catalog no. I00008, revision 0, 14 May 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_candrajJAna_nityArchanavidh.coverage: partial — Transcription of a manuscript in very bad condition (IFP manuscript 32608 / RE32608). It runs from folio 1a to folio 36a, with folio 20 missing and many lacunae. The transcriber lists 24 section headings: mantravāsam (f. 1a), nityārcanam (f. 2a), trikālapūjā, dārumayam, pīṭhalakṣaṇam, pūjākālam, śuddhādipūjābhedam, saurapūjā, indrapūjā, arcanāphalam, āsanavidhi tathā pañcaśuddhi, bhūtaśuddhi, pañcātmā, sthānaśuddhi, mantraśuddhi (f. 24a), siṃhāsanam, vāmabrahmamantraḥ, sadāśivam, āvāhanamantram tathā mantrapūjanam, naivedyam, mahābhiṣekam, naivedyam tathā snapanam, abhiṣekakramam, and phalodakavidhi (f. 36a). The text breaks off within the phalodakavidhi ('gojalairabhiṣekaṃ tu …', '(End of ṛE32608.)'). ilx_skt metadata classifies it as 'incomplete'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_caturvedArthatAtparyasaMgra.title: Caturvedārthatātparyasaṃgraha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_caturvedArthatAtparyasaMgra.author: Haradatta
SA_MB_ilx_mb_caturvedArthatAtparyasaMgra.summary: The Caturvedārthatātparyasaṃgraha is a 150-verse Śaiva philosophical and polemical work. Through an exegesis of Vedic passages, mantras, and Upaniṣadic texts, it demonstrates that Lord Śiva is the supreme Brahman and the ultimate purism (tātparya) of the four Vedas, defending Śaiva theism against rival school interpretations.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_caturvedArthatAtparyasaMgra.edition: Transcript T. 1061 of the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), transcribed from a manuscript belonging to G. Swaminatha Gurukkal; digitized and transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00601).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_caturvedArthatAtparyasaMgra.coverage: complete — Complete root text in 150 verses, ending at verse 150 with 'iti caturvedārthatātparyasaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_cennabasavezvara_attributed.title: Vīraśaivotkarṣapradīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_cennabasavezvara_attributed.author: Cannabasaveśvara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_cennabasavezvara_attributed.summary: The Vīraśaivotkarṣapradīpikā ('Illumination of the Excellence of Vīraśaivism') is a doctrinal treatise composed in mixed prose and verse by Sudhāpurastha Cannabasaveśvarasvāmin, affiliated with the Toṇṭada and Murughā Vīraśaiva lineages. It defends the Vedic status and spiritual supremacy of Vīraśaiva philosophy and practice, drawing upon Upaniṣadic, Purāṇic, and Śaivāgama authorities to elucidate key tenets such as the ṣaṭsthala, aṣṭāvaraṇa, pañcācāra, and atyāśrama. The e-text concludes with a brief excerpt from the thirteenth chapter of the Kriyāsāra concerning qualifications for Śaiva consecration.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_cennabasavezvara_attributed.attribution: Authored by Cannabasaveśvara (Cannabasavārya Deśika) residing in Sudhāpura. As stated in verses 2–5, he traces his teaching lineage through Toṇṭada Siddhamaheśvara, Murughā Śāntavīra Yati, and Gurusiddha Deśika. The TEI header specifies 'attributed to' to distinguish him from the 12th-century Liṅgāyata leader Cannabasava.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_cennabasavezvara_attributed.coverage: complete — Text of the Vīraśaivotkarṣapradīpikā followed by an appendix quoting verses 67–70 of upadeśa 13 from Kriyāsāra.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAmodara_son_of_gaGgAdhara_.title: Yantracintāmaṇi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAmodara_son_of_gaGgAdhara_.author: Dāmodara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAmodara_son_of_gaGgAdhara_.summary: The Yantracintāmaṇi is a widely cited medieval Sanskrit tantric treatise on yantras composed by Dāmodara, son of Gaṅgādhara. Structured as a dialogue between Umā and Maheśvara upon Mount Kailāsa, the work provides detailed instructions for constructing, inscribing, and ritually activating yantras across eight principal sections corresponding to the ṣaṭkarman (vaśya, ākarṣaṇa, stambhana, vidveṣaṇa, māraṇa, uccāṭana) as well as rites for pacification (śānti), protection (rakṣā), and liberation from physical confinement (bandhamokṣa).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAmodara_son_of_gaGgAdhara_.attribution: Dāmodara introduces his lineage in the opening stanzas (vv. 1–6: Mahādeva -> Devadatta -> Gaṅgādhara -> Dāmodara) and states that Śiva inspired him in a dream to compile this yantra treatise based on various Śaiva, Saura, and Śākta texts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAmodara_son_of_gaGgAdhara_.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS 4919, Raghunath Temple Library, Jammu (J&K), unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAmodara_son_of_gaGgAdhara_.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of manuscript 4919, preserving the introductory pīṭhikā and the eight thematic sections (adhikāras) treating the ṣaṭkarmas, śānti, rakṣā, and bandhamokṣa, ending with the concluding colophon: iti śrīdāmodareṇa śivājñākareṇa paṇḍitarājena viracito yantracintāmaṇiḥ samāptaḥ.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAzarathIyatantram_M00521.title: Dāśarathīyatantra (beginning missing)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAzarathIyatantram_M00521.summary: A Vaiṣṇava tantra focused on the worship of Rāma. It is framed as Ṛṣyaśṛṅga's teaching to Śatānanda and other sages and styles itself Vedārthasaṃgraha / Vedasārārthasaṃgraha and Anuttarabrahmatattvarahasya. It incorporates Śrīcakra / Rājarājeśvarī elements.
