SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAzarathIyatantram_M00521.attribution: Anonymous Vaiṣṇava (Rāma-centred) tantra in which Ṛṣyaśṛṅga is the narrator. The final verses are a scribal colophon of Vaṃśīdhara, a devotee of Rāma and of the Śrīcakra (Rājarājeśvarī), with a śaka date.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAzarathIyatantram_M00521.edition: Transcription of MS 4886, Raghunatha Temple Library, Jammu (copied by Vaṃśīdhara).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dAzarathIyatantram_M00521.coverage: partial — Beginning missing: the e-text opens at adhyāya 1, v. 15 ('…rīśīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutaṃ || 15 ||'). The final colophon is 'iti śrīmadanuttarabrahmatatvarahasye dāśarathīye taṃtre vedasārārthasaṃgrahe uttarabhāge saubhāgyavidhodaye rājavidyāmāhātmye śāstrarahasyakathanaṃ nāma paṃcacatvārīṃśodhyāyaḥ', followed by a scribal colophon of Vaṃśīdhara. ilx_skt catalog classifies it as 'incomplete' with the colophon note 'almost at end'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_I00061.title: Kriyākramadyotikā (Dīkṣāvidhi with Maṇipravāḷa commentary)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_I00061.author: Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_I00061.summary: The Dīkṣāvidhi forms the initiation section of the Kriyākramadyotikā by the Śaiva Siddhānta preceptor Aghoraśivācārya. This text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 32578 from the Institut Français de Pondichéry, presenting Sanskrit root formulas and procedures embedded in an extensive Maṇipravāḷam (Tamil-Sanskrit) ritual commentary. It details the preliminary rites, entrance initiation, and final liberating initiation (nirvāṇadīkṣā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_I00061.attribution: Aghoraśivācārya composed the Sanskrit Kriyākramadyotikā. The bilingual Maṇipravāḷam commentary and ritual exposition in Tamil and Sanskrit is an anonymous South Indian liturgical transmission.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_I00061.edition: Pondicherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 32578 (diplomatic transcription prepared by IFP scholars under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra, funded by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_I00061.coverage: partial — Covers the initiation section of the Kriyākramadyotikā, comprising the pavilion preparations, Adhivāsanavidhi, Samayadīkṣāvidhi, and Nirvāṇadīkṣāvidhi, transcribed from palm-leaf folios of IFP MS RE 32578.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_M00543.title: Dīkṣāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_M00543.summary: A Pāśupata ritual handbook transcribed from manuscript NGMCP Reel A 39/12 (pra. 736). The text opens with an invocation of Lakulin and treats ritual consecration (saṃskāravidhi), rules of ascetic conduct, expiations, and concluding rites.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_M00543.attribution: A ritual manual opening with a salutation to Lakulin (v. 1: tasmai lakuline namaḥ).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIkSAvidhi_M00543.coverage: uncertain — ilx_skt catalog lists completeness as uncertain (noting colophon spelling variations: 'pratyaṃ neṣṭavidhiḥ samāptāḥ').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIpayAdavidhi_M00544.title: Dīpayāgavidhi (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIpayAdavidhi_M00544.summary: A Nepalese Śākta ritual manual (paddhati) of the Kulaśāsana / Ūrdhvāmnāya, i.e. Śrīvidyā (Tripurasundarī) tradition with Kubjikā elements, for the worship of the goddess through lamp offerings (dīpayāga): kumbha-, dīpa- and balipūjā with mantras, mudrās, short stotra verses and Newari ritual rubrics. The manuscript appends a Gurustava ascribed to the Tantrarāja, a short caru/dīpa rite, paśuyāga, homa and ārātika rubrics, and a Mahātripurasundarīstotra ascribed to Jagatānanda.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIpayAdavidhi_M00544.attribution: The paddhati is an anonymous ritual compilation from Nepal. An included hymn towards the end (lines 404–408) is attributed in its colophon to Jagatānanda.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIpayAdavidhi_M00544.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription (no printed edition): Kathmandu, National Archives, MS 1-1696/807, NGMPP reel A 239/14.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dIpayAdavidhi_M00544.coverage: partial — Transcription of an incomplete manuscript: the folio sequence starts at fol. 2a (fol. 1 lost; the e-text opens mid-sentence 'cene devitvaṃ ...') and ends at fol. 24a, breaking off in an untitled Tripurasundarī hymn after the Mahātripurasundarīstotra. The Dīpayāgavidhi proper (lines 1–189) lacks only its opening; it is followed by a Gurustava, a short caru/dīpa rite, paśuyāga, homa and ārātika rubrics and hymns.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNAmUrtisaMhitA_M00625.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNAmUrtisaMhitA_M00625.summary: The Dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā is a Śākta Tantric scripture of the Śrīvidyā tradition framed as a dialogue between Īśvara and Devī. Across 33 paṭalas, it expounds the ritual worship, mantras, yantras, and mudrās of Tripurasundarī and various manifestations of Lakṣmī. It details both daily ritual practices (nityapūjā) and periodic or seasonal observances (naimittikapūjā), concluding with the damanakāropaṇa rite.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNAmUrtisaMhitA_M00625.attribution: A Śākta-Śrīvidyā tantric saṃhitā framed as a dialogue between Īśvara (Śiva) and Devī, traditionally associated with the Dakṣiṇāmūrti school of Śrīvidyā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNAmUrtisaMhitA_M00625.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS 1633K (Devanāgarī, paper, 83 folios, dated Saṃvat 1950 Caitra [c. CE]), preserved at the Dharmartha Trust Library, Shri Raghunath Temple, Jammu; transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the direction of Anirban Dash (Catalog no. M00625, June/November 2023).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNAmUrtisaMhitA_M00625.coverage: complete — Complete in 33 paṭalas, concluding with the scribal colophon 'saṃpūrṇaiṣāṃ dakṣiṇāmūrtisaṃhitā ... jamvūmadhye liptā 1950 caitre'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNakAlIpUjApaddhati_M00.title: Dakṣiṇakālīpūjāpaddhati
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNakAlIpUjApaddhati_M00.summary: An anonymous Śākta liturgical manual (paddhati/prayoga) detailing the rites for the ritual worship (pūjā) of the goddess Dakṣiṇakālī (Dakṣiṇakālikā). The text details the practitioner's preparatory purifications (snāna, ācamana, saṃvitsādhana), nyāsa procedures (including sthitimātṛkānyāsa and bījanyāsa), mandala and pātra consecration, āvāhana, standard offerings (upacāra), balidāna, japa, and concluding dismissal rites.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNakAlIpUjApaddhati_M00.attribution: A traditional ritual manual for the worship of Dakṣiṇakālī / Dakṣiṇakālikā preserved in Nepalese manuscript transmission without named authorship.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNakAlIpUjApaddhati_M00.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Kathmandu, National Archives / NGMCP MS 4-2660 (Reel no. B 187/18). E-text prepared by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00541), selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski and data-entered under the supervision of Anirban Dash (Revision 0, 25 Sept 2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dakSiNakAlIpUjApaddhati_M00.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual running from the opening purification rites (prayoga) to the closing colophon (iti śrīmaddakṣiṇakālikāpūjāpaddhati samāptā).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dattAtreyatantra_M00632.title: Dattātreyatantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dattAtreyatantra_M00632.summary: The Dattātreyatantra is a practical tantric handbook devoted to occult rituals and the sixfold magic acts (ṣaṭkarman). Structured as an inquiry by Dattātreya answered by Śiva on Mount Kailāsa, it details incantations, herbal preparations, and yantras for pacification, subjugation (vaśīkaraṇa), eradication (uccāṭana), and lethal destruction (māraṇa), concluding with formulas for warding off wild beasts, serpents, and poisons.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dattAtreyatantra_M00632.attribution: Cast as a revelatory dialogue between Dattātreya and Maheśvara (Śiva) on Mount Kailāsa; an anonymous ritual work belonging to the practical tantric and ṣaṭkarman tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dattAtreyatantra_M00632.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS no. 4913 (15 folios), Shri Raghunatha Temple Manuscripts Library, Jammu (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dattAtreyatantra_M00632.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcript of the 15-folio manuscript ending at paṭala 22 (dvāviṃśatipaṭalaḥ).
translations: Jvālāprasāda (tr.), Dattātreyatantra. (Hindi)

SA_MB_ilx_mb_devIpUjA_M00507.title: Devīpūjā with Mahārājñīstava, Vākyamañjarī and Sarasvatīstuti
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devIpUjA_M00507.author: Kṛṣṇakavi, Rūpa Bhavānī
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devIpUjA_M00507.summary: A Kashmiri Śākta devotional booklet. It opens with a liturgy for the worship of the Goddess (Durgāpūjā) that invokes the Kashmiri goddesses Śārikā, Mahārājñī, Jvālāmukhī and others, with seat purification, nyāsa, invocation and offerings. A Sanskrit hymn to Mahārājñī (Khīr Bhavānī) by Paṇḍita Kṛṣṇa(kavi) follows. Then comes a collection of mystical sayings (vākyamañjarī) of the Kashmiri saint Rūpa Bhavānī (Alakṣyeśvarī), largely in Kashmiri and opening with a 'Nirvāṇadaśaka'. A ten-verse Sarasvatīstuti closes the booklet.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devIpUjA_M00507.attribution: Kashmiri Śākta compilation. The Mahārājñīstava is ascribed to 'Paṇḍita Kṛṣṇakavi' (or Kṛṣṇaka). The third part is ascribed to Rūpa Bhavānī, called Alakṣyeśvarī (Kashmiri Alakhīśvarī). The Durgāpūjā liturgy and the Sarasvatīstuti are anonymous.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devIpUjA_M00507.coverage: complete — Each of the four parts ends with its own colophon ('iti durgāpūjā sampūrṇā', 'iti … mahārājñīstavaḥ sampūrṇaḥ', 'iti … vākyamañjarī sampūrṇā', 'iti sarasvatīstutiḥ'). The first line, 'paropakārāya prākāśyaṃ nītā', is the end of a title-page or publication formula of the printed source.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_devatAdhyAnavacanAni_I00052.title: Devatādhyānavacanāni (beginning missing)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devatAdhyAnavacanAni_I00052.summary: An anonymous South Indian ritual handbook made up mainly of dhyāna verses, which describe the forms, attributes and mounts of deities for visualization in worship. It includes Śaiva forms (Sadāśiva, Dakṣiṇāmūrti), forms of the Goddess (Durgā, the Lakṣmīs), Vaiṣṇava deities and the nine planets with their gotras and directions. It also contains ritual notes such as the examination of coconuts (nālikeralakṣaṇa), the visualization of the yāgaśālā as a divine body, and, towards the end, verses on ancestral offerings (śrāddha, pitṛtarpaṇa).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devatAdhyAnavacanAni_I00052.attribution: Anonymous South Indian compilation of dhyāna verses (Śaiva, Śākta, Vaiṣṇava, Navagraha) and ritual notes. No author and no source colophons.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devatAdhyAnavacanAni_I00052.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of the palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32402 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), Muktabodha catalog no. I00052. No printed edition is known.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_devatAdhyAnavacanAni_I00052.coverage: partial — The '(p.4b …)' markers are pdf image numbers ('p = pdf picture'), not folio numbers. The e-text starts on image 4b in the middle of a dhyāna of the Lakṣmīs ('vaktrāsthe bhāgyalakṣmī …'), followed by a fragmentary nakṣatra list, so the opening is defective. Some images are skipped or out of order (6a, 9b, 29b, 39b, 52b/53a), and many passages are marked as damaged. Image 58a is blank. The text ends on image 58b in the middle of an instruction ('… lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ paścime caiva pūjayet'), followed by the Tamil 'cupam' (śubham). As a compilation it has no defined complete extent.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhvajArohaNavarSavarddhanav.title: Dhvajāvarohaṇavarṣavardhanavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhvajArohaNavarSavarddhanav.summary: A Newar Śākta-Śaiva ritual manual (paddhati) composed in mixed Sanskrit and Classical Newari for religious rituals under King Sumati Jayajitāmitramalla. The text outlines procedures for fire oblations (lakṣāhuti), flag-lowering/raising rituals, and annual anniversary rites (varṣavardhana). It details domestic and lineage deity rituals (deguli) and offerings honoring Siddhilakṣmī, Guhyakālī, Tripurasundarī, and Jayatumbureśvarī alongside Svacchandabhairava.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhvajArohaNavarSavarddhanav.attribution: Anonymous ritual manual composed in mixed Sanskrit and Classical Newari for ceremonial observances sponsored by King Sumati Jayajitāmitramalla, who is invoked as the yajamāna at the beginning of the text.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhvajArohaNavarSavarddhanav.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu MS 1-735 (NGMCP reel A 240/15), transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the supervision of Dr. Anirban Dash; text selected by Dr. Mark S. G. Dyczkowski; Muktabodha Digital Library, M00542 (revised Sept. 25, 2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhvajArohaNavarSavarddhanav.coverage: partial — Incomplete transcription of manuscript NGMCP 1-735 (reel A 240/15); lacks a final scribal colophon and explicit (the title colophon 'iti dhvajāvarohanavarṣavarddhanavidhisamāptaṃ' occurs in the middle of the manuscript, which continues with further rituals and ends after a Svacchandabhairavastuti).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnabindUpaniSat_M00106.title: Dhyānabindūpaniṣad with Dhyānabindūpaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnabindUpaniSat_M00106.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnabindUpaniSat_M00106.summary: The Dhyānabindūpaniṣad is one of the classical Yoga Upaniṣads, focusing on the practice and philosophy of dhyāna (meditation) and nada-yoga. It expounds meditation on the sacred syllable Om (praṇava) along with its constituent mātrās, bindu, and nāda, the sixfold yoga (ṣaḍaṅgayoga), the nature of the jīva, and the awakening of Kuṇḍalinī to achieve non-dual liberation. The Vivaraṇa commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin interprets the yogic terminology and practices from an Advaita Vedānta perspective of pure consciousness (brahmamātra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnabindUpaniSat_M00106.attribution: The root Upaniṣad is an anonymous text of the Yoga Upaniṣad group, traditionally associated with the Kṛṣṇayajurveda. The Vivaraṇa commentary was composed by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, disciple of Vāsudevendra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnabindUpaniSat_M00106.edition: Yoga upaniṣads with the commentary of śrī upaniṣad brahmayogin, ed. Śāstrī Mahādeva, Madras: Adyar library and research centre, 1920.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnabindUpaniSat_M00106.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 106 verses with full Vivaraṇa commentary and concluding colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnazloka_navatriMzatkala.title: Dhyānaśloka, Navatriṃśatkalaśakrama, Nītisāra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnazloka_navatriMzatkala.summary: A composite South Indian Śaiva manuscript codex containing three separate liturgical and gnomic texts: Dhyānaślokas detailing iconographic visualizations of deities; the Navatriṃśatkalaśakrama detailing the snapana ritual using thirty-nine consecrated pots; and a Nītisāra anthology of didactic verses on worldly wisdom and morality.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnazloka_navatriMzatkala.attribution: Anonymous palm-leaf manuscript miscellany containing ritual meditation verses (dhyāna) for Śaiva deities, a paddhati for 39-pot snapana ritual, and a collection of didactic nīti verses.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnazloka_navatriMzatkala.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) bundle RE32583 (29 folios, 35.56 cm × 4.20 cm, 6–9 lines per folio). Unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_dhyAnazloka_navatriMzatkala.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE32583 across 29 folios (image markers 5b through 28b).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_ekAmranAthASTatakam_and_ekA.title: Ekāmranāthāṣṭaka and Ekāmranāthaśataka (Śataka verses 1–42)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_ekAmranAthASTatakam_and_ekA.summary: Two devotional stotras to Śiva as Ekāmranātha, the presiding deity of the Ekāmreśvara (Ekambareswarar) temple at Kanchipuram, the earth (pṛthivī) liṅga among the Pañcabhūtasthalas. The e-text gives the complete eight-verse Ekāmranāthāṣṭaka (refrain ekāmramūlanilayāya namaśśivāya) and verses 1–42 of the Ekāmranāthaśataka, each with a word-by-word Tamil gloss, transcribed from IFP palm-leaf manuscript RE 30753.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_ekAmranAthASTatakam_and_ekA.attribution: Both devotional stotras and their interlinear/word-by-word Tamil glosses (pratipadārtha) are anonymous temple hymns dedicated to Śiva Ekāmranātha at Kanchipuram.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_ekAmranAthASTatakam_and_ekA.edition: Unpublished transcription of palm-leaf manuscript, Institut Français de Pondichéry, RE 30753 (Grantha script, 75 folios); no printed edition traced.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_ekAmranAthASTatakam_and_ekA.coverage: partial — Complete Ekāmranāthāṣṭaka (8 verses) followed by the Ekāmranāthaśataka, which ends with verse 42 (of a nominal 100) at fol. 74a (74b blank, transcriber's note 'completed', i.e. the manuscript itself is defective/unfinished; IFP description: 'Ekāmranāthāṣṭakam is completed and Ekāmranāthaśatakam is not completed'). Each verse is followed by a Tamil pratipadārtha in transliteration. The e-text opens with a few stray verses (on Caṇḍeśvara and nirmālya rules, fol. 5a) before the aṣṭaka.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_gandharvatantra_M00646.title: Gandharvatantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gandharvatantra_M00646.summary: The Gandharvatantra is a Śākta Tantra framed as an instruction delivered by Śiva to Pārvatī, featuring the sage Viśvāmitra. It provides extensive instructions on mantra-japa, internal and external ritual worship, yantras, mudrās, and kuṇḍalinī-yoga synthesized with nondual Śākta philosophy.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gandharvatantra_M00646.attribution: Framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī (pārvatīśvarasaṃvāda).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gandharvatantra_M00646.edition: Gandharvatantra, edited by Ram Chandra Kak and Harabhatta Shastri, Srinigar [Srinagar]: Maharaja Harasinghji Bahadur, 1934.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gandharvatantra_M00646.coverage: complete — Complete in 42 paṭalas (ends with chapter 42: tattvajñānopadeśana).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_gautamatantra_M00647.title: Gautamatantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gautamatantra_M00647.summary: The Gautamatantra (also known as Gautamīyatantra) is a prominent Vaiṣṇava (Kṛṣṇaite) tantric text framed as a dialogue between Gautama and Nārada. It focuses upon the theology, mantra practice, and ritual worship of Kṛṣṇa, especially the ten-syllable Gopālamantra (gopījanavallabhāya svāhā). The text treats initiation (dīkṣā), nyāsa, dhyāna, yantras, and ritual attainment (siddhi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gautamatantra_M00647.attribution: Traditional Vaiṣṇava tantric scripture; Gautama and Nārada appear as dialogue interlocutors.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gautamatantra_M00647.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Devanāgarī paper manuscript no. 2651 ka (80 folios, copied in Jammu in Saṃvat 1944 / CE), preserved at Ragunath Temple, Jammu.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_gosvAmIjanArdanaH_jagannivA.title: Mantracandrikā (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gosvAmIjanArdanaH_jagannivA.author: Janārdanabhaṭṭa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gosvAmIjanArdanaH_jagannivA.summary: A mantra compendium by Janārdanabhaṭṭa, son of Jagannivāsa, providing mantras with ṛṣi, chandas, devatā, nyāsa, and dhyāna for deities including Gaṇapati, forms of the Goddess (such as Tārā), Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa, Rāma, Kārtavīryārjuna, and Śiva (including Nīlakaṇṭha), concluding with instructions on rosary consecration (mālāpratiṣṭhā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gosvAmIjanArdanaH_jagannivA.attribution: The introductory verses and colophons identify the author as Gosvāmi Janārdanabhaṭṭa, son of Gosvāmi Jagannivāsa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gosvAmIjanArdanaH_jagannivA.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS no. 4853, Shri Raghunatha Temple MSS Library, Jammu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_gosvAmIjanArdanaH_jagannivA.coverage: partial — Contains prakāśas including Gaṇapati, Śakti, Vaiṣṇava, Śiva, etc., followed by a closing section on rosary consecration breaking off at 'mūlamantreṇa hutvā'. The manuscript concludes with a note '(maṃtracaṃdrakāsūcisameta patre 85 śloka 2700)'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_hAritAyana_tripurArahasya_j.title: Tripurārahasyajñānakhaṇḍa with Tātparyadīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_hAritAyana_tripurArahasya_j.author: Hāritāyana, Śrīnivāsa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_hAritAyana_tripurArahasya_j.summary: The Tripurārahasya (Jñānakhaṇḍa) is a Śākta non-dualist philosophical text framed as a discourse between Dattātreya and Paraśurāma, recited by the sage Sumedhas Hāritāyana to Nārada. It blends Advaita Vedānta, Pratyabhijñā Śaivism, and Śrīvidyā tantric metaphysics, demonstrating through dialogues and narrative parables that supreme reality is unconditioned pure Consciousness (Cit / Tripurā). The e-text contains all 22 chapters of the Jñānakhaṇḍa along with Śrīnivāsa Bhaṭṭa's classic commentary, the Tātparyadīpikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_hAritAyana_tripurArahasya_j.attribution: The root scripture Tripurārahasya is traditionally attributed to the sage Hāritāyana. The commentary Tātparyadīpikā was written by Śrīnivāsa Bhaṭṭa (son of Vaidyanātha Dīkṣita).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_hAritAyana_tripurArahasya_j.coverage: complete — Text of the Jñānakhaṇḍa accompanied by the Tātparyadīpikā commentary, concluding with chapter 22.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_haradatta_attributed_to_har.title: Hariharatāratamya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_haradatta_attributed_to_har.author: Rāmeśvara Adhvarin
SA_MB_ilx_mb_haradatta_attributed_to_har.summary: The Hariharatāratamya is a Śaiva stotra and polemical work in 94 verses comparing the mythological deeds, forms, and attributes of Viṣṇu (Hari) and Śiva (Hara). The stanzas rhetorical frame poses the constant refrain asking wise elders to judge who is greater ('ko vānayor adhika ityanucintya vṛddhāḥ satyaṃ vadantu tam imaṃ vayam āśrayāmaḥ'), consistently resolving in favor of Śiva's transcendence and non-dual supreme reality.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_haradatta_attributed_to_har.attribution: The Muktabodha metadata notes 'Author : haradatta attributed to' and 'Author source: colophon - but cat.: Haradatta?'. Verse 94 names the author as Rāmeśvara Adhyarasudhāmaṇi, son of Śrīkānta ('śrīkāṃtanāmavibudheṃdratanūbhavena rāmeśvarādhyarasudhāmaṇinā praṇītam').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_haradatta_attributed_to_har.coverage: complete — Complete text in 94 verses with author stanza and final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnapUjAvidhi_from_the_vAt.title: Vātulāgama (Jñānapūjāvidhi)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnapUjAvidhi_from_the_vAt.summary: A liturgical chapter (vidhi) associated with the Vātulāgama detailing the performance of Jñānapūjā ('gnostic worship'). It outlines the ritual qualifications and daily preparatory observances (nityakarma, prāṇāyāma, tarpaṇa, and temple visit), contemplative meditation on Śiva in the bhrūmadhya (eyebrow center), and the internal and external worship directed toward the southern portal (dakṣiṇadvāra / Dakṣiṇāmūrti) leading to liberation.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnapUjAvidhi_from_the_vAt.attribution: A ritual section attributed to the Vātulāgama (one of the 28 canonical Śaiva Siddhānta Mūlāgamas).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnapUjAvidhi_from_the_vAt.edition: Manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) paper manuscript bundle RE 47827, ff. 4b–9a (Deviprasad Mishra, Sambandhan Anandavardhana, and Arul Nandi, eds., IFP / Muktabodha Digital Library, text I00031, 2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnapUjAvidhi_from_the_vAt.coverage: excerpt — A single ritual procedure (ff. 4b–9a of manuscript RE 47827) extracted from the Vātulāgama corpus.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnaprakAza_prAsAdacandrik.title: Prāsādacandrikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnaprakAza_prAsAdacandrik.author: Jñānaprakāśa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnaprakAza_prAsAdacandrik.summary: The Prāsādacandrikā is a Śaiva Siddhānta manual attributed to Jñānaprakāśa of Kamalālaya (Tiruvārūr). Based on Āgamic sources such as the Suprabhedāgama and Svāyambhuva, it details the internal yogic pronunciation (uccāra) of the Prāsādamantra, the seven stages of unification (sāmarasya), internal junctures (viṣuva), and the ascent of consciousness through the cakras and subtle sound centers to Śiva.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnaprakAza_prAsAdacandrik.attribution: The concluding lines record that the work was compiled or recorded by Aruṇadeva based on the teaching of Jyeṣṭhajñānaprakāśācārya residing at Kamalālaya (Tiruvārūr).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnaprakAza_prAsAdacandrik.edition: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T0093 (unpublished manuscript transcript)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jJAnaprakAza_prAsAdacandrik.coverage: incomplete — Text in 108 verses plus concluding colophon, matching IFP transcript T0093, pp. 1–12 (with manuscript lacunae indicated by asterisks in the transcript).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_3_M0.title: Jayadrathayāmala (ṣaṭka 3)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_3_M0.summary: The third ṣaṭka of the Jayadrathayāmala (also designated Śiraccheda), a foundational scripture of the Kaula Vidyāpīṭha and Kālīkrama systems. This section details esoteric mantric theology, complex yoginī hierarchies and mandala rituals (such as those of Matacakreśvarī), and advanced yogic practices culminating in the Mahāmelāpasiddhi.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_3_M0.attribution: A major Śākta-Śaiva scripture belonging to the Vidyāpīṭha division of the Bhairavasrotas and the Kālīkrama tradition, framed as a dialogue between Bhairava and the Devī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_3_M0.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu (NAK) MS 5-1975 (NGMPP reel A 152/9; paper, Newari script, 236 folios, dated Nepāla Saṃvat 807 [1686/ CE]). Transcribed under the supervision of Anirban Dash for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00680).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_3_M0.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the third ṣaṭka (hexad) of the Jayadrathayāmala, preserved across folios 1a–236 in MS NAK 5-1975, ending with the Mahāmelāpasiddhipaṭala colophon and the scribal date Nepāla Saṃvat 807.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_4_M0.title: Jayadrathayāmala (ṣaṭka 4)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_4_M0.summary: The Jayadrathayāmala Ṣaṭka 4 is a scriptural text belonging to the Bhairava Tantras and the Kālīkula/Krama traditions, featuring mudrās, ritual practices, and deities such as Rāviṇī and Mahālakṣmī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_4_M0.attribution: A revealed scripture belonging to the Bhairava Tantras and Kālīkula/Krama traditions.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_4_M0.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of National Archives Nepal MS 1-1468 (NGMPP reel B122/4; paper, Newari script, 237/239 folios, scribed in A.D. 1626/7); digital transcript prepared by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00681).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jayadrathayAmala_SaTka_4_M0.coverage: partial — Text of the fourth ṣaṭka of Jayadrathayāmala, spanning folios 1a–240a including the terminal patra index.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_jirNoddhAraH_I00028.title: Jīrṇoddhāra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jirNoddhAraH_I00028.summary: An extensive Śaivasiddhānta ritual manual detailing the principles and practices of renovation and restoration (jīrṇoddhāra) following the guidelines of the Kāmikāgama. Covering approximately 200 topics in the Pratiṣṭhā sections, it begins with Vighneśvarapūjā and extends through Ācāryavaraṇam and Śuddhanṛttam (ending in the Kāmikāgamoktanṛttavidhi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jirNoddhAraH_I00028.attribution: An anonymous Śaivasiddhānta paddhati/prayoga manual detailing temple renovation and restoration rites according to the Kāmikāgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jirNoddhAraH_I00028.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 30511, transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra; Institut Français de Pondichéry & Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, Pondicherry, 2024.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_jirNoddhAraH_I00028.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of IFP palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 30511 (261 folios), spanning from Vighneśvarapūjā through Kāmikāgamoktanṛttavidhi.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kAmezvarIpUjA_M00546.title: Kāmeśvarīpūjā (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kAmezvarIpUjA_M00546.summary: An anonymous Nepalese Śrīvidyā ritual manual for the worship of the goddess Kāmeśvarī/Tripurasundarī, with Newari rubrics. It contains offering formulas, nyāsa, bali mantras, dhyāna, arghapātra preparation, internal worship (antaryāga), and the worship of the deities of the Śrīcakra enclosures (trailokyamohana-, saṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra), in several separately concluded sections.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kAmezvarIpUjA_M00546.attribution: Anonymous ritual manual (paddhati) preserved in Nepalese manuscripts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kAmezvarIpUjA_M00546.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription (no printed edition): Kathmandu, National Archives, MS 5-397, NGMPP reel A 49/2.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kAmezvarIpUjA_M00546.coverage: partial — Manuscript transcription, fols. 1a–30a with fol. 24 missing. The e-text opens abruptly in the middle of a rite (naivedya, prāṇāhuti) without a maṅgala and breaks off at fol. 30a mid-sentence ('tataḥ saptavidhā (*?) bhagavatī'). Internal closing formulas show it is a compilation of several ritual units (pūjāpaṭala, paddhati, dhyāna, Tripurasundarī cakra worship: trailokyamohana- and saṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaivalyasAra_M00602.title: Kaivalyasāra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaivalyasAra_M00602.author: Maritoṃṭadārya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaivalyasAra_M00602.summary: The Kaivalyasāra is a foundational Sanskrit Vīraśaiva theological and philosophical treatise composed by Maritoṃṭadārya. Structured around the system of 101 progressive spiritual stations (ekottaraśatasthala) divided across six major prakaraṇas, the treatise correlates Upaniṣadic śruti passages with Śaivāgamic doctrines to articulate the Śivādvaita philosophy. It systematically expounds the metaphysical non-dual union (aṅgaliṅgasāmarasya) between the individual practitioner (aṅga) and transcendent-immanent Śiva (liṅga).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaivalyasAra_M00602.attribution: Referred to in the internal colophons as Śrīmatparamaśivayogirāṭparivrājakācārya Śrī-Toṃṭadārya, but specified as Maritoṃṭadārya in the edition's title page and in modern scholarly literature (e.g. Potter EIP).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaivalyasAra_M00602.edition: Kaivalyasāra by Maritoṃṭadārya, Vīraśaivaliṅgibrāhmaṇadharmagranthamālā, grantha 30, Solapur: [s.n.], Śake 1828 [1907 CE].
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaivalyasAra_M00602.coverage: complete — Complete text covering all six prakaraṇas (Bhaktasthala through Mahāliṅgasthala) expounding the 101 sthalas (ekottaraśatasthala), matching the concluding colophon of the sixth prakaraṇa.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaumArasaMhitA_M00661.title: Kaumārasaṃhitā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaumArasaMhitA_M00661.summary: The Kaumārasaṃhitā is a Tāntrika manual framed as a dialogue between Brahmā and Īśvara (Śiva), focusing on the esoteric ritual cult of Vidyāgaṇapati (Gaṇapati integrated with Śrīvidyā). Across seven adhyāyas, it details his iconographic form, dhyāna, mantra-uddhāra, yantra, puraścaraṇa, and specific homas and prayogas for pacification, worldly attainment, and victory over adversaries.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaumArasaMhitA_M00661.attribution: A Śākta/Gāṇapatya tantric text presented as a revelation dialogue between Brahmā and Īśvara (Śiva).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaumArasaMhitA_M00661.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 4078 (Devanāgarī, Alm. 19, Shlf. 3), Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library, Jammu (copied Saṃvat / CE), digitized by eGangotri.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kaumArasaMhitA_M00661.coverage: complete — Complete text in 7 adhyāyas (folios 1a–28b), concluding at adhyāya 7 with scribal dating Saṃvat 1942 jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 10.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kedArakalpa_M00671.title: Kedārakalpa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kedArakalpa_M00671.summary: A Śaiva tantric pilgrimage and ritual manual presented as a dialogue between Īśvara and Kārttikeya. It outlines the sacred pilgrimage along the Himalayan Mahāpatha to Kedāranātha and Mount Kailāsa, ritual preparations, and practices believed to grant liberation while embodied and physical ascent to Kailāsa (sadehakailāsagamana).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kedArakalpa_M00671.attribution: Framed as an instruction from Īśvara (Śiva) to Kārttikeya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kedArakalpa_M00671.edition: Kedārakalpa. Bombay: Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara Steam Press, Saṃvat 1963 [ or 1907 CE].
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kedArakalpa_M00671.coverage: complete — Complete in 44 paṭalas across 200 pages, concluding at paṭala 44 colophon (phalaśrutivarṇana).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kriyoDDIzamahAtantrarAja_M0.title: Kriyoḍḍīśamahātantrarāja
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kriyoDDIzamahAtantrarAja_M0.summary: The Kriyoḍḍīśamahātantrarāja is a Śākta-Śaiva tantric manual focused on practical rituals (prayoga) and the six magical acts (ṣaṭkarman). Framed as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī, the text provides protective incantations (kavacas), bījamantras, yantras, and medicinal and protective rites against diseases, malevolent spirits (grahas), and sorcery.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kriyoDDIzamahAtantrarAja_M0.attribution: The opening rubric gives 'śrīmadindrajitpraṇītaḥ' (traditionally attributed to Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa), but the work is internally framed as a Tantric dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī (śivagaurīsaṃvāda).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kriyoDDIzamahAtantrarAja_M0.coverage: complete — Complete text in 21 paṭalas, concluding with the colophon '[iti kriyoḍḍīśe mahātantrarāje śivagaurīsaṃvāde ekaviṃśatitamaḥ paṭalaḥ] || 29 || [samāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ]'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kuNDasaMskAravidhi_I00051.title: Kuṇḍasaṃskāravidhi (fragment)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kuNDasaMskAravidhi_I00051.summary: A Śaiva Siddhānta ritual handbook (paddhati) setting out the purification/consecration procedures (saṃskāra) and homa offerings performed across directional fire-altars (kuṇḍas: Āgneya, Dakṣiṇa, Nairṛta, Paścima, Vāyu, Uttara) in the context of temple renovation (jīrṇoddhāra) and aṣṭabandhana ceremonies. The present text is an incomplete transcription of IFP palm-leaf manuscript RE 31372.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kuNDasaMskAravidhi_I00051.attribution: Anonymous ritual paddhati belonging to the South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kuNDasaMskAravidhi_I00051.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript bundle RE 31372.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kuNDasaMskAravidhi_I00051.coverage: fragment — Defective at both ends, transcribed from an incomplete palm-leaf manuscript bundle of 12 folios; text begins mid-sentence at image 3b, line 1, and breaks off incomplete at image 12a, line 7 in the Vāyukuṇḍahoma section.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikASTAviMzatikarmArcana.title: Kubjikāṣṭāviṃśatikarmārcana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikASTAviMzatikarmArcana.summary: The Kubjikāṣṭāviṃśatikarmārcana is an esoteric Tantric worship manual (paddhati) belonging to the Western Transmission (Paścimāmnāya / Kubjikā tradition) preserved in Nepal. It details twenty-eight sequential ritual actions (aṣṭāviṃśatikarma) comprising the worship of the goddess Kubjikā and her attendant pantheon, including preparatory purification rites, nyāsas, maṇḍala designs, and mantra recitation, interspersed with ritual directions in classical Newari.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikASTAviMzatikarmArcana.attribution: A ritual manual (paddhati) belonging to the Kubjikā (Paścimāmnāya) tradition, preserved anonymously in Nepal.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikASTAviMzatikarmArcana.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of NGMCP manuscript 5-1891, Reel No. B 181/18; selected by Dr. Mark S.G. Dyczkowski, data-entered by Muktabodha staff supervised by Dr. Anirban Dash (Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, e-text M00551, Sept. 26, 2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikASTAviMzatikarmArcana.coverage: unclear — The core text of the Kubjikāṣṭāviṃśatikarmārcana concludes with an internal colophon ('iti paścimajeṣṭhāmnāya astāviśatikarmmārccanaṃ samāpta'), but the manuscript transcription continues with supplementary rites, instructions, and mantras, terminating without a final codex colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAguhyezvarIpUjApaddha.title: Kubjikāguhyeśvarīpūjāpaddhati
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAguhyezvarIpUjApaddha.summary: The Kubjikāguhyeśvarīpūjāpaddhati is a Nepalese Tantric ritual manual dedicated to Goddess Guhyeśvarī venerated in her Kubjikā aspect. Written in Sanskrit with Newari liturgical directions and ritual glosses, it outlines standard liturgical procedures including bhūtaśuddhi, nyāsa, pātrapūjā, gurumaṇḍala worship, kramārcana, offerings (bali), and animal sacrifice (paśujāga). The surviving witness was written by King Sumati Jayajitāmitramallavarman.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAguhyezvarIpUjApaddha.attribution: The colophon names King Sumati Jayajitāmitramallavarman as the scribe who copied the text with his own hand ('svakarena likhitaṃ').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAguhyezvarIpUjApaddha.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: National Archives, Kathmandu, NGMCP MS 1-1696/2247, Reel B 181/17.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAguhyezvarIpUjApaddha.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual from initial Gaṇeśa and Gurupādukā invocations to the closing verses, colophon, and scribal date formula.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAgurumaNDalapUjA_M005.title: Kubjikāgurumaṇḍalapūjā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAgurumaNDalapUjA_M005.summary: The Kubjikāgurumaṇḍalapūjā is a Śākta tantric ritual manual (paddhati) detailing the rites of the gurumaṇḍala in the Kubjikā lineage. It specifies the preparation of the maṇḍala, offerings, nyāsa, mantras, stotras, and concluding dismissal (visarjana) rites with liturgical rubrics in Newari.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAgurumaNDalapUjA_M005.attribution: A ritual manual (paddhati) belonging to the Kubjikā / Paścimāmnāya tradition of the Kathmandu Valley, incorporating Sanskrit verses, bījamantras, and Newari liturgical rubrics.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAgurumaNDalapUjA_M005.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript 1-1696/1642 (Reel No. A 234/12), selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute staff under the supervision of Anirban Dash (Catalog no. M00548).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAgurumaNDalapUjA_M005.coverage: incomplete — Transcription of manuscript NGMCP A 234/12, including colophon 'iti gurumaṇḍalapūjāvidhi /// samvat 8012 jyeṣṭhaśuklanavami śrīharipatideva na coyājuro śubhā'. Marked as incomplete in the catalog.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikApUjA_M00549.title: Kubjikāpūjā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikApUjA_M00549.summary: An anonymous tantric ritual manual (paddhati) belonging to the Kubjikā (Paścimāmnāya) tradition of Nepal, containing Sanskrit mantras and liturgical directions in classical Newari (Nevārī). It prescribes the daily ritual routine (nityakarma), including saṃdhyāvandana, diverse nyāsas, liṅgārcana, arghapātrapūjā, bhūtaśuddhi, ātmapūjā, and mālāsodhana.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikApUjA_M00549.attribution: A traditional, anonymous ritual manual (paddhati) of the Newar Kubjikā (Paścimāmnāya) cult preserved in the Kathmandu Valley.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikApUjA_M00549.coverage: unclear — Catalogued as incomplete in Muktabodha and ilx_skt because it lacks an explicit and colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAsamayanirvANadIkSAvi.title: Kubjikāsamayanirvāṇadīkṣāvidhi (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAsamayanirvANadIkSAvi.summary: An unpublished Newar ritual manual (paddhati) of the Kubjikā (Paścimāmnāya) Śākta-Śaiva tradition. It sets out the preliminary daily rites (sandhyā, nyāsa, pūjā), guru homage, and the ceremonial procedures for the samayadīkṣā and nirvāṇadīkṣā initiations. Sanskrit mantras and ritual injunctions are interspersed with rubrics in Classical Newari.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAsamayanirvANadIkSAvi.attribution: Anonymous ritual manual (paddhati) belonging to the Newar Kubjikā (Paścimāmnāya) tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAsamayanirvANadIkSAvi.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript 4-132 (Reel No. A 975/2); unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_kubjikAsamayanirvANadIkSAvi.coverage: partial — Incomplete; text breaks off abruptly at segment 1499/1500 during the description of daśamudrāpradāna.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_lalitAgama_M00252.title: Lalitāgama (Saṃprokṣaṇavidhi)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_lalitAgama_M00252.summary: A short ritual extract regarding the temple reconsecration and purification ceremony (saṃprokṣaṇavidhi) attributed to the Lalitāgama, one of the foundational Śaiva Siddhānta Āgamas. It details the worship of guardian deities at the cardinal temple gateways, preparation of the sacrificial pavilion (yāgamaṇḍapa), purification with pañcagavya, establishment of ritual pitchers (kumbhasthāpana), and the recitation of the Pāśupatāstramantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_lalitAgama_M00252.edition: Unpublished transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) / EFEO transcript T0202 (transcribed from a manuscript of Swaminatha Gurukkal Tiruvanadudurai).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_lalitAgama_M00252.coverage: excerpt — Short ritual excerpt of 28 verses plus the Pāśupatāstramantra specifically covering temple reconsecration/purification (saṃprokṣaṇa).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_laugAkSi_nityakarmavidhi_M0.title: Nityakarmavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_laugAkSi_nityakarmavidhi_M0.author: Laugākṣi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_laugAkSi_nityakarmavidhi_M0.summary: The Nityakarmavidhi is a daily ritual paddhati of the Kashmiri Smārta tradition attributed to Laugākṣi. It details daily domestic rites, including snāna, sandhyā, viṣṇupañcāyatanapūjā, and bhojanavidhi. The text concludes with a devotional appendix comprising stotras attributed to Kālidāsa, Kulaśekhara, Śaṅkarācārya, and Abhinavagupta (Śivastuti).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_laugAkSi_nityakarmavidhi_M0.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to the sage Laugākṣi. The compiled paddhati concludes with a devotional anthology containing hymns attributed to Kālidāsa (Sarasvatīstuti), King Kulaśekhara (Mukundamālāstuti), Śaṅkarācārya (Govindāṣṭaka), and Abhinavagupta (Śivastuti).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_laugAkSi_nityakarmavidhi_M0.coverage: complete — Daily ritual manual including snānavidhi, sandhyopāsanā, viṣṇupañcāyatanapūjāvidhi, pañcagavyavidhi, and bhojanavidhi, ending with stotras including Abhinavagupta's Śivastuti.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgArcanatantra_M00514.title: Liṅgārcanatantra (paṭalas 1–12, incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgArcanatantra_M00514.summary: The Liṅgārcanatantra is a Śaiva-Śākta tantric scripture presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Devī (Harapārvatīsaṃvāda). It focuses on the ritual preparation, consecration, and worship of the liṅga—especially the pārthiva (clay/earth) liṅga—detailing required mantras, upacāras, and the esoteric merits of liṅgapūjā. The present transcription terminates abruptly during an exchange concerning the admissibility of ritual remnants (nirmālya) in paṭala 13.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgArcanatantra_M00514.attribution: Revealed tantric text presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Devī (Harapārvatīsaṃvāda).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgArcanatantra_M00514.edition: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00937 (manuscript transcript)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgArcanatantra_M00514.coverage: partial — Contains paṭalas 1–12 complete, breaking off after the opening inquiry of paṭala 13.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgalakSaNam_I00032.title: Liṅgalakṣaṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgalakSaNam_I00032.summary: A diplomatic transcription of manuscript bundle RE 10980 held at the Institut Français de Pondichéry. Despite the traditional library title 'Liṅgalakṣaṇa', the palm-leaf manuscript contains no architectural or iconographic text on the liṅga; it is instead a personal devotional manual (vacana- and śloka-pustaka belonging to Kuppusāmi) containing dhyāna verses for Gaṇeśa, Śiva, Vṛṣabha, Pradoṣanāyaka, Caṇḍeśvara, the Tamil Śaiva saints (Appar/Vāgīśa, Māṇikkavācakar, Sambandar, Sundarar), Somāskanda, Bhogaśakti, and Bālasubrahmaṇya, alongside astrological notes and the hymn Śivapāhyaṣṭaka.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgalakSaNam_I00032.attribution: A personal Śaiva miscellany or manual belonging to one Kuppusāmi ('kuppusāmi vacanapustakaṃ ślokapustakam', fol. 1b). The individual stotras, dhyāna verses, and astrological passages are anonymous.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgalakSaNam_I00032.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 10980 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP). Transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra. Published online by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute in collaboration with the IFP, 2024 (Muktabodha text I00032).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_liGgalakSaNam_I00032.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of IFP palm-leaf manuscript RE 10980 (22 folios; folios 20a–22b blank, ending with 'śivapāhi aṣṭakaṃ saṃpūrṇam').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAnasarAma_svAtantrayadIpik.title: Svātantryadīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAnasarAma_svAtantrayadIpik.author: Mānasarāma
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAnasarAma_svAtantrayadIpik.summary: A compendium of the core tenets of non-dual Kashmir Śaivism composed in four chapters (ullāsa) by Mānasarāma, grand teacher of Swami Lakṣmanjoo. Formulated as concise aphorisms accompanied by the author's own prose commentary, the treatise expounds the doctrine of divine absolute autonomy (svātantrya), the nature of consciousness (saṃvid), and the unfolding of the universal powers (śakti).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAnasarAma_svAtantrayadIpik.attribution: Both the aphorisms (sūtra) and the commentary are composed by Mānasarāma.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAnasarAma_svAtantrayadIpik.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription; data-entered by the staff of Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (catalog no. M00533, revision Sept. 14, 2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAnasarAma_svAtantrayadIpik.coverage: complete — Complete in 4 ullāsas, ending with 'iti śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavarya viracitāyāṃ svātantryadīpikāyāṃ svātantryaśaktyucchalanaṃ nāma caturthollāsaḥ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAtRkAtantra_M00634.title: Mātṛkātantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAtRkAtantra_M00634.summary: The Mātṛkātantra is an unprinted Śākta-Śaiva tantric text framed as a dialogue on Mount Kailāsa between Caṇḍikā and Bhairava/Śaṅkara. It discusses alchemical procedures (dhātuvāda / rasaśāstra) with mercury (pārada) and herbal ingredients to create gold and silver for ritual worship during the Kaliyuga, outlines the recitation manual and benefits of the Caṇḍīpāṭha (Devīmāhātmya / Saptaśatī), and concludes with devotional hymns and protective armors including a Gurukavaca.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAtRkAtantra_M00634.attribution: Revealed tantric scripture presented as a dialogue between Śiva (Bhairava/Śaṅkara) and Caṇḍikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAtRkAtantra_M00634.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of Manuscript 72 (Śāradā script), Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan, Lucknow.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mAtRkAtantra_M00634.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript text, terminating with '[śrīmātṛkātantraṃ sampūrṇam]' and '(amudritam)'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtitatvAnusandhAndarzanam_.title: Bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitā (Mṛtitattvānusmaraṇa)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtitatvAnusandhAndarzanam_.summary: The Mṛtitattvānusmaraṇa is an eschatological and ritual text framed as a dialogue between Śrībhairava and Bhairavī, traditionally transmitted as a section of the Kashmiri Śaiva Bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitā. It provides a detailed account of the post-mortem journey of the soul, the geography and punishments of Yamaloka, the accounting of deeds by Citragupta, and the specific duties of relatives during dying, cremation (śāvasnāna, antyeṣṭi), the ten-day period (daśāha), and the performance of dīpaśrāddha to dispel the darkness of the pretamārga.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtitatvAnusandhAndarzanam_.attribution: Traditionally presented as an exposition by Bhairava to Bhairavī forming part of the Bhṛṅgīśasaṃhitā, an extensive Kashmiri Śaiva text corpus preserved primarily in Śāradā manuscripts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtitatvAnusandhAndarzanam_.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Dogra Art Museum manuscript 436 (paper, Śāradā script), transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the supervision of Anirban Dash (Revision 0, April 4, 2024; catalog number M00644).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtitatvAnusandhAndarzanam_.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the work as preserved in Dogra Art Museum MS 436, beginning with the opening dialogue on Yamaloka and funeral rites (segments 0–5) and ending with the dīpaśrāddha mantras and scribal colophon note '[itimantraṃpaṭhitvācadīpāndadyāthāvidhivividhā itiśubham mṛtisandhāna]' (segments 234–243).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtyuNjayapUjApaddhati_M005.title: Mṛtyuñjayapūjāpaddhati
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtyuNjayapUjApaddhati_M005.summary: A Nepalese ritual manual (paddhati) setting forth the domestic and tantric liturgical procedures for the worship of Mṛtyuñjaya (Śiva). The text combines Sanskrit Vedic and tantric mantras with ritual instructions in Classical Newari, encompassing preliminary purification rites, Sūryapūjā, Viṣṇupūjā, the principal Mṛtyuñjayapūjā, and an appended rite for pacifying Saturn (Śanaiścarapāṭhavidhi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtyuNjayapUjApaddhati_M005.attribution: Anonymous ritual manual composed in mixed Sanskrit mantras and Classical Newari rubrics.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtyuNjayapUjApaddhati_M005.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) reel no. A 455/14 (running no. 1642).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mRtyuNjayapUjApaddhati_M005.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of manuscript NGMCP A 455/14 (running from initial nyāsa through Mṛtyuñjayapūjā to the concluding Śanaiścarapāṭhavidhi and final colophon: 'thvate śanaiścara pāṭhaḥ samāptaḥ || śubhaṃ ||').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAbhairavapUjA_M00524.title: Mahābhairavapūjā (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAbhairavapUjA_M00524.summary: An anonymous Newar ritual manual (paddhati) for the worship of Ākāśamahābhairava, drawn up for a rite (tolanapratiṣṭhā and viśvajātrā) sponsored by King Jayabhūpatīndra Malla. Invoking Kubjikā and Siddhilakṣmī, it gives pādukā and bali mantras, purification of vessels, and navātmapūjā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAbhairavapUjA_M00524.attribution: Anonymous Newar paddhati. The saṅkalpa (lines 2–5) names the yajamāna as King Jayabhūpatīndra Malla (Bhūpatīndra Malla of Bhaktapur, r. c. 1696–1722) and the occasion as a tolanapratiṣṭhā and viśvajātrā for Ākāśamahābhairava; the manuscript was thus prepared for a royal rite in his reign.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAbhairavapUjA_M00524.coverage: partial — Manuscript transcription. Begins with the maṅgala and saṅkalpa; breaks off after navātmapūjā in a sequence of pādukā/bali mantras without a final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahApratyaGgIrA_M00552.title: Mahāpratyaṅgīrā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahApratyaGgIrA_M00552.summary: A Buddhist protective text (dhāraṇī / kalpa) dedicated to Mahāpratyaṅgirā. Opening in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven in the Nandana grove with Śakra, Brahmā, and assemblies of deities and bodhisattvas, the text details protective dhāraṇīs, mantras, śānti rites, and spells for subduing māras and obstacles.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahApratyaGgIrA_M00552.attribution: Scriptural Buddhist protective text (dhāraṇī/kalpa) traditionally set in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahApratyaGgIrA_M00552.edition: Diplomatic transcript of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 4-346, Reel no. B 107/13, selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, data-entered by Muktabodha staff under the supervision of Anirban Dash (2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahApratyaGgIrA_M00552.coverage: uncertain — Manuscript transcript including Newari and Sanskrit scribal verses at the end; ilx_skt completeness listed as uncertain.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahArahasyasaMpradAya_M0067.title: Mahārahasyasaṃpradāya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahArahasyasaMpradAya_M0067.author: Vimalaprabodha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahArahasyasaMpradAya_M0067.summary: The Mahārahasyasaṃpradāya (concluding with the title Śrīkrama) is a medieval ritual manual (paddhati) associated with the Kubjikā (Paścimāmnāya) and Krama esoteric traditions. It details the daily ritual procedure (pūjāvidhi), maṇḍala layout, nyāsa, and mantra worship of Kubjikā, Bhairava, and the lineage gurus. The e-text represents a diplomatic transcript of a palm-leaf manuscript preserved in the Kaiser Library, Kathmandu, dated Nepāla Saṃvat 331 (1211 CE) during the reign of Arimalla.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahArahasyasaMpradAya_M0067.attribution: Attributed to Vimalaprabodha by Muktabodha. The surviving colophon at folio 44a reads 'iti śrīmahārahasye saṃpradāye śrīkramaṃ samāptam' without an explicit author colophon.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahArahasyasaMpradAya_M0067.edition: Kathmandu, Kaiser Library, MS 79 (part 2; NGMPP Reel No. C 6/15), palm leaf, 44 folios, in early Newari script, dated Nepāla Saṃvat 331 (1211 CE) during the reign of King Arimalladeva (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahArahasyasaMpradAya_M0067.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the 44-folio manuscript text, ending with the concluding colophon and scribal dating to NS 331 (1211 CE).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAvAkyopaniSat_M00109.title: Mahāvākyopaniṣad with Mahāvākyopaniṣadvivaraṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAvAkyopaniSat_M00109.author: Upaniṣadbrahmayogin
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAvAkyopaniSat_M00109.summary: The Mahāvākyopaniṣad is a short minor Upaniṣad belonging to the Atharvavedic tradition and counted as the 92nd text in the Muktikā canon of 108 Upaniṣads, classified as one of the twenty Yoga Upaniṣads. It elucidates the distinction between worldly ignorance (avidyā) and spiritual illumination (vidyā), teaching that ultimate liberation is achieved through transcending cosmic darkness and recognizing the supreme solar Self within via contemplation of the Vedic great pronouncements (mahāvākyas). This e-text provides the complete root text accompanied by the Advaitic Vivaraṇa commentary of Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAvAkyopaniSat_M00109.attribution: The Mahāvākyopaniṣad is an Atharvavedic Upaniṣad. The commentary is by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin, disciple of Vāsudevendra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAvAkyopaniSat_M00109.edition: Pandit A. Mahadeva Sastri (ed.), The Yoga Upaniṣads with the Commentary of Śrī Upaniṣad-Brahmayogin, Madras: Adyar Library and Research Centre, 1920.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahAvAkyopaniSat_M00109.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad (all 12 sections/mantras) with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin's commentary.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahezvarAcArya_svAtantryadI.title: Svātantryadīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahezvarAcArya_svAtantryadI.author: Maheśvarācārya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahezvarAcArya_svAtantryadI.summary: The Svātantryadīpikā ('Lamp of Absolute Freedom') is a non-dual Kashmir Shaiva philosophical treatise in four chapters (ullāsas) attributed to Maheśvarācārya. Drawing on Pratyabhijñā and Trika tenets, it elucidates the nature of Paramaśiva's sovereign autonomy (svātantrya), the deployment of the five principal powers (pañcaśakti), the manifestation of cosmos and individual existence (jīva), and the realization of one's intrinsic divine identity.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahezvarAcArya_svAtantryadI.attribution: Colophons consistently attribute the work to Śrī Mahāmāheśvarācāryavarya / Maheśvarācārya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahezvarAcArya_svAtantryadI.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS no. 1127 ka (Mansa Ram Mongha / Alm 5593) preserved in the Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library, Jammu (digitized by eGangotri); transcribed under the supervision of Anirban Dash for Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2024 (Catalog no. M00668).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mahezvarAcArya_svAtantryadI.coverage: complete — Complete in 4 chapters (ullāsas) across 110 folios (pṛ. 1a–110b), ending with the colophon of the fourth chapter (Svātantryaśaktyucchalana).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_makuTottararahasya_M00525.title: Makuṭottararahasya (chapter 3: Mantrayogoddhāra)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_makuTottararahasya_M00525.summary: The third chapter (spanda), titled Mantrayogoddhāra, of the Makuṭottararahasya, an esoteric Śaiva-Śākta scriptural text associated with the Makuṭāgama corpus. In a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī centered on the temple at Cidambaram, it delineates the geometry and ritual installation of the Śrīsabhā-mahāyantra, combining the Śaiva five-syllable (pañcākṣara) and Śākta fifteen-syllable (pañcadaśākṣarī) mantric systems around the cosmic dance of Śiva as Cidambara Naṭarāja.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_makuTottararahasya_M00525.attribution: Esoteric Śaiva-Śākta scripture associated with the Makuṭāgama tradition, focusing on the Cidambaram cult.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_makuTottararahasya_M00525.edition: Unpublished transcript: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00164; transcribed and digitized by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00525), supervised by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (revised Sept. 12, 2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_makuTottararahasya_M00525.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 3 (tṛtīyaspanda), designated 'Mantrayogoddhāra', comprising 106 numbered verses plus unnumbered opening and closing stanzas.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mannAthazyamalApratiSThAvid.title: Mannāthaśyāmalāpratiṣṭhāvidhi and Cāmuṇḍāpūjāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mannAthazyamalApratiSThAvid.summary: This bundle comprises two Śaiva ritual texts transcribed from IFP palm-leaf manuscript RE 32415. The first section gives the installation and consecration rituals (pratiṣṭhā/sthāpana) for Mannātha and Śyāmalā, attributed in the cataloguer's note to the Sakalāgamasaṅgraha tradition. The second section preserves the Cāmuṇḍāpūjāvidhipaṭala, detailing homa, tarpaṇa, and pūjā rites for goddess Cāmuṇḍā, ascribed in its colophon to the Rauravatantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mannAthazyamalApratiSThAvid.attribution: According to the IFP metadata, the first text is drawn from the Sakalāgamasaṅgraha corpus; the second text is ascribed in the colophon to the Rauravākhya Mahātantra (Rauravāgama).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mannAthazyamalApratiSThAvid.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 32415 (Pondicherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry), transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; published digitally as Muktabodha e-text I00034 (2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mannAthazyamalApratiSThAvid.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32415 (ff. 3b–28a).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mantramahAdeva_gaurIkAJcali.title: Gaurīkāñcalikātantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mantramahAdeva_gaurIkAJcali.summary: The Gaurīkāñcalikātantra is a Śaiva-Śākta tantric medical-astrological treatise cast as a dialogue between Śiva and Gaurī. It details pharmacognosy and botanical gathering rules based on seasons and asterisms, prognostic astrology regarding the onset of illness, fatal bodily omens (ariṣṭa / mṛtyucihna), and divination via bodily spasms and twitches (spanda / aṅgasphuraṇa).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mantramahAdeva_gaurIkAJcali.attribution: Cast as a Haragaurīsaṃvāda between Śrīdevī and Śrī-Īśvara. The Muktabodha TEI header erroneously listed 'mantramahādeva' in the author field.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mantramahAdeva_gaurIkAJcali.coverage: complete — Complete text ending with the colophon 'iti śrīharagaurīsaṃvāde gaurīkāñcalikātantraṃ samāptam'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_maritoNTadArya_vIrazaivAnan.title: Vīraśaivānandacandrikā (Vādakāṇḍa)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maritoNTadArya_vIrazaivAnan.author: Maritoṇṭadārya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maritoNTadArya_vIrazaivAnan.summary: The Vādakāṇḍa of the Vīraśaivānandacandrikā by Maritoṇṭadārya, written as instruction for Basava Nāyaka of Keladi as a sequel to the work's Kriyākāṇḍa. In 24 prakaraṇas it sets out the Vīraśaiva siddhānta (ṣaṭsthala, liṅgāṅgasāmarasya, liṅgadhāraṇa, Śiva's supremacy) and refutes rival systems: Cārvāka, the four Buddhist schools, Jainas, Pāśupata divisions, Pāñcarātra (Mādhva and Rāmānuja), Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika, Sāṅkhya, Yoga, Mīmāṃsā and Advaita vivartavāda.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maritoNTadArya_vIrazaivAnan.attribution: Colophons: composed by Maritoṇṭadārya, who received his knowledge through the grace of Toṇṭada Siddheśvara, as instruction (upadeśa) for Basava of the Keladi dynasty (keladisadāśivarāyanāyakavaṃśa…basavavasudhāsaṅkrandana).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maritoNTadArya_vIrazaivAnan.edition: A printed edition of the Vīraśaivānandacandrikā (Vādakāṇḍa) published in Varanasi in 1936. (probable)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maritoNTadArya_vIrazaivAnan.coverage: partial — Complete Vādakāṇḍa: introductory verses 1–5 and prose, through the 24th prakaraṇa (vīraśaivamatotkarṣatanniṣṭhaśivabhaktotkarṣanirūpaṇa) and the final colophon 'vādakāṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ'. The Kriyākāṇḍa of the same work is not contained.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_maunappa_paNDita_vIrazaivAc.title: Vīraśaivācārakaustubha (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maunappa_paNDita_vIrazaivAc.author: Maunappapaṇḍita
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maunappa_paNDita_vIrazaivAc.summary: The Vīraśaivācārakaustubha is a Sanskrit Vīraśaiva (Liṅgāyata) treatise on ritual observance and conduct (ācāra) attributed to Maunappapaṇḍita. It expounds religious principles and daily rituals.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maunappa_paNDita_vIrazaivAc.attribution: Attributed in the Muktabodha catalog metadata to Maunappa-Paṇḍita.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maunappa_paNDita_vIrazaivAc.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Jangamwadi Math Collection (digitized by eGangotri), Devanāgarī paper manuscript (13.5" x 8.4"), 25 folios (398 verses), incomplete.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_maunappa_paNDita_vIrazaivAc.coverage: partial — Incomplete manuscript transcription of 25 folios comprising 398 verses, breaking off without a terminal colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_muNDamAlAtantram_1_M00537.title: Muṇḍamālātantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_muNDamAlAtantram_1_M00537.summary: The Muṇḍamālātantra is a late Śākta Kaula scripture in ten chapters (paṭalas). It is particularly prominent in tantric literature for establishing the explicit doctrinal and symbolic correspondences between the ten Mahāvidyās (Kālī, Tārā, Chinnamastā, etc.) and the ten Avatāras of Viṣṇu. The work also details mantroddhāra, stotras, kavacas, and esoteric ritual practices including śavasādhanā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_muNDamAlAtantram_1_M00537.attribution: Anonymous Śākta Kaula tantra presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_muNDamAlAtantram_1_M00537.coverage: complete — Complete text in 10 paṭalas (concludes at 10.87 followed by 'iti prathamaṃ muṇḍamālātantraṃ samāptam').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_mudrAprakAza_M00627.title: Mudrāprakāśa (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mudrAprakAza_M00627.author: Rāmakiśora
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mudrAprakAza_M00627.summary: The Mudrāprakāśa is a Tantric digest by Rāmakiśora defining and explaining the formation, classification, and ritual application of hand gestures (mudrās) used in worship, nyāsa, and invocation. It systematically cites classical Tantric authorities, including the Mantradarpaṇa, Tantrasāra, Kulārṇavatantra, Gautamīyatantra, and Jñānārṇavatantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mudrAprakAza_M00627.attribution: The opening verses explicitly identify the author as Rāmakiśora: 'natvā gurupadaṃ rāmakiśoreṇeṣṭasiddhidaṃ / sādhakānāṃ mude mudrāprakāśo 'yaṃ viracyate'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mudrAprakAza_M00627.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of MS 1406k (Tantra, 39 folios), Dharmartha Trust Library, Raghunath Temple, Jammu (acc./shelfmark 5866 / 1406 Ka, Almira 26, Shelf 3). Unpublished diplomatic transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_mudrAprakAza_M00627.coverage: partial — Incomplete transcription of MS 1406k (comprising 39 folios), ending abruptly mid-sentence: 'taṃtrasāre aṃtarāṃguṣṭamuṣṭiṃ tukṛtvāvāmakarasyaca madhya'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAdAnusandhAna_M00526.title: Nādānusandhāna
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAdAnusandhAna_M00526.summary: A short Haṭha- and Layayoga tract in 67 verses framed as an instruction delivered by Śiva to Pārvatī. It outlines the practice of absorption in the ten inner unstruck sounds (anāhatanāda)—beginning with ciṇi, ciñciṇī, and bell/conch sounds up to thunder and kettle-drums—along with elemental tattva-dissolution, bodily signs, and mind absorption leading to liberation.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAdAnusandhAna_M00526.attribution: Cast as a revelation spoken by Śiva to Pārvatī: 'iti śrīyogaśāstre śrīpārvatīśvarasaṃvāde nādānusaṃdhānaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAdAnusandhAna_M00526.edition: Manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 5-2714, Reel No. A62/11; unpublished digital transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAdAnusandhAna_M00526.coverage: complete — Complete text in 67 numbered verses with opening invocation and concluding colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAgabhaTTa_tripurAsArasamuc.title: Tripurāsārasamuccaya with Padārthādarśa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAgabhaTTa_tripurAsArasamuc.author: Nāgabhaṭṭa, Govindācārya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAgabhaTTa_tripurAsArasamuc.summary: The Tripurāsārasamuccaya of Nāgabhaṭṭa is an important compendium of the Śākta Śrīvidyā tradition in ten chapters (paṭalas). It details the daily and special ritual worship, mantra extraction and repetition, yantra diagrams, nyāsa procedures, mudrās, and homa (fire offerings) associated with Goddess Tripurasundarī. Govindācārya's commentary Padārthādarśa clarifies technical mantric code-words, ritual injunctions, and traditional Śākta interpretations.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAgabhaTTa_tripurAsArasamuc.attribution: The root work is attributed to Nāgabhaṭṭa. The commentary is titled Padārthādarśa in its final chapter colophon; its author is named as Govindācārya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAgabhaTTa_tripurAsArasamuc.edition: Tripurāsārasamuccayaḥ tantraśāstram śrīnāgabhaṭṭaviracitaḥ śrīgovindācāryyakṛtavyākhyayā samalaṅkṛtaḥ, ed. Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara Bhaṭṭācārya, 2nd ed., Calcutta: Kalikātā Yantra, 1897.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nAgabhaTTa_tripurAsArasamuc.coverage: complete — Complete in 10 paṭalas (prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ to daśamaḥ paṭalaḥ: homavidhāna), including both root text and commentary.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNThaSaTkarmaprayoga_I.title: Nīlakaṇṭhaṣaṭkarmaprayoga
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNThaSaTkarmaprayoga_I.summary: A composite Śaiva-tantric ritual manual and stotra miscellany preserved in South Indian manuscript tradition (IFP MS 31151). The codex encompasses 18 sections of liturgical material combining Sanskrit formulas with Tamil ritual rubrics and mantra diagrams, including procedures for the six sorcery rites (ṣaṭkarma such as uccāṭana and bhedana), snakebite and poison appeasement (viṣaśānti), yantra diagrams (e.g. Bālāyantra), dhyānas, and devotional hymns including the Umāmaheśvarastotra and Gaṅgādharāṣṭaka.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNThaSaTkarmaprayoga_I.attribution: A scribal miscellany (saṅgraha) containing 18 discrete items.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNThaSaTkarmaprayoga_I.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript no. 31151; prepared by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; published digitally by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute in collaboration with the Institut Français de Pondichéry, Puducherry, 2023 (Catalog no. I00014).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNThaSaTkarmaprayoga_I.coverage: unclear — Transcription of manuscript IFP 31151; multiple folios are broken or defective, and completeness is recorded as uncertain.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNTha_kAtyAyanItantraT.title: Kātyāyanītantraṭīkā (chapter 23)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNTha_kAtyAyanItantraT.author: Nīlakaṇṭha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNTha_kAtyAyanItantraT.summary: The Mantravyākhyāprakāśikā (also designated Kātyāyanītantraṭīkā) is a tantric commentary by Nīlakaṇṭha Śaiva on the 23rd chapter (paṭala) of the Kātyāyanītantra. This chapter establishes the authoritative 700-mantra breakdown (saptaśatīmantrasaṅkhyāvibhāga) of the Devīmāhātmya / Durgāsaptaśatī necessary for ritual applications such as homa, japa, and saṃpuṭīkaraṇa. The commentary meticulously accounts for each chapter's verse segments, half-verses, and uvāca-lines to verify the exact tally of seven hundred mantras.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNTha_kAtyAyanItantraT.attribution: The commentator identifies himself in verse 5 ('śaivopanāmako vidvān nīlakaṇṭho 'bhidhānataḥ'), concluding verse 2 ('raṅganāthasūteneyaṃ śrīlakṣmītanayena ca / nīlakaṇṭhena viduṣā mantrasaṃkhyāprakāśikā'), and the final colophon ('iti śrīraṅgabhaṭṭasutalakṣmīgarbhajaśaivopanāmanīlakaṇṭhakṛtāyāṃ...').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNTha_kAtyAyanItantraT.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS 5295 (14 folios), Shri Raghunatha Temple MSS Library, Jammu; transcribed by the staff of Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the direction of Anirban Dash (Catalog no. M00631).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nIlakaNTha_kAtyAyanItantraT.coverage: partial — Contains only the 23rd chapter (trayoviṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ) of the Kātyāyanītantra with Nīlakaṇṭha's commentary, which establishes the 700-mantra division (saptaśatīmantrasaṅkhyāvibhāga) of the Devīmāhātmya. The manuscript transcript comprises 14 folios.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_navagrahadhyAnam_I00026.title: Navagrahadhyānam
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navagrahadhyAnam_I00026.summary: A Śaivāgama liturgical manual for the propitiation and worship of the nine planetary deities (navagraha). It includes iconographical dhyāna stanzas describing the physical appearance, weapons, vehicles, and orientation of Gaṇeśa and the nine planets (Sūrya through Ketu), accompanied by planetary hymns (aṣṭakas), ritual directions for pūjā offerings, and a Mantrāṣṭaka.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navagrahadhyAnam_I00026.attribution: A traditional Śaiva liturgical text for navagraha propitiation preserved in palm-leaf manuscript form without individual authorial attribution.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navagrahadhyAnam_I00026.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 32425 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra, Pondicherry: Muktabodha Indological Research Institute & IFP, 2023–2024.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navagrahadhyAnam_I00026.coverage: partial — Incomplete; diplomatic transcription covering fols. 1a–26b of IFP manuscript RE 32425, lacking an explicit or final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_navakuNDavidhi_I00036.title: Navakuṇḍavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navakuNDavidhi_I00036.summary: A late Śaiva Siddhānta ritual compilation detailing the rites of the sacrificial pavilion (yāgaśālā) during temple consecration (pratiṣṭhā). It describes the layout, geometric forms, presiding deities, mantras, and oblations for the nine fire-pits (navakuṇḍavidhi) and five fire-pits (pañcakuṇḍavidhi), incorporating procedures and citations from the Kāmikāgama, Sahasrāgama, and related Śaivāgama sources, concluding with dhyāna verses for the sixty-three Tamil Śaiva saints (Āṟupattumūṟṟuvar).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navakuNDavidhi_I00036.attribution: A practical Śaiva ritual manual (paddhati/vidhi) drawing on Āgamas such as the Kāmikāgama and Sahasrāgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navakuNDavidhi_I00036.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32408 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), Puducherry.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navakuNDavidhi_I00036.coverage: complete — Transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32408 (images 5b–70b), which contains procedures for nine and five fire-pits (navakuṇḍa, pañcakuṇḍa), aṣṭabandhana, Śivaliṅgapratiṣṭhā, and the dhyāna verses for the sixty-three Śaiva saints (Āṟupattumūṟṟuvar).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_navapIThASTamAtRkArAdhanavi.title: Navapīṭhāṣṭamātṛkārādhanavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navapIThASTamAtRkArAdhanavi.summary: A Newar tantric ritual manual (paddhati) composed in mixed Sanskrit and Newari for the propitiation of the nine sacred seats (navapīṭha) and eight mother goddesses (aṣṭamātṛkā), primarily in the context of the Kubjikā and Śākta traditions (invoking Kubjikā, Siddhilakṣmī, and Ucchiṣṭhanātha). It was commissioned for King Bhūpatīndra Malla for a Durgā temple consecration (durgāprāsādapratiṣṭhā), and contains liturgical instructions, mantras, nyāsas, bali rituals, and embedded devotional hymns including the Mālinīdaṇḍaka and Pīṭhāvatārastotra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navapIThASTamAtRkArAdhanavi.attribution: Composed by an anonymous Newar tantric priest on behalf of King Jayabhūpatīndramallavarman (Bhūpatīndra Malla), explicitly named as the yajamāna in the opening sankalpa-vākya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navapIThASTamAtRkArAdhanavi.edition: Manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 1-764 (Reel no. A 241/5), selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, keyed under the supervision of Anirban Dash, Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (Digital Library Cat. No. M00555).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navapIThASTamAtRkArAdhanavi.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual as transcribed from manuscript NGMCP 1-764, concluding with '[iti pithipūjāvidhi samāptaḥ]'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_navarNacaNDIpaJcaGga_M00670.title: Navārṇacaṇḍīpañcāṅga
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navarNacaNDIpaJcaGga_M00670.summary: A Śākta ritual compilation attributed to the Rudrayāmalatantra focusing on the veneration of Caṇḍī through her nine-syllable formula (Navārṇamantra). The text provides the standard components of a tantric pañcāṅga manual, including mantra analysis (mantroddhāra), yantra diagram construction, preliminary nyāsa rituals, worship manuals (arcanapaddhati), protective armor (kavaca), and laudatory stotras.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navarNacaNDIpaJcaGga_M00670.attribution: Attributed in the text to the Rudrayāmala (Rudrayāmalatantra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navarNacaNDIpaJcaGga_M00670.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library (Jammu) MS No. 4818 gha / 4818 kh, digitized by eGangotri on Internet Archive (NavarnaChandiPanchangam4818GhaAlm21Shlf5DevanagariTantra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_navarNacaNDIpaJcaGga_M00670.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of manuscript folios 1a–60b, ending with the final colophon 'iti śrīrudrayāmale taṃtre navārṇavacaṃḍīpaṃcāgastotraṃ samāptam'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nigamajJAnadeva_varuNapaddh.title: Varuṇapaddhati with Vilocana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nigamajJAnadeva_varuNapaddh.author: Varuṇaśiva, Nigamajñānadeva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nigamajJAnadeva_varuNapaddh.summary: The Varuṇapaddhati is a South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual (paddhati) composed by Varuṇaśiva. This e-text provides the root text along with the Vilocana commentary by Nigamajñānadeva, a Śaiva scholar of Vyāghrapura (Chidambaram). The manual expounds two fundamental aspects ('bījadvaya') of Śaiva ritual practice: initiation (dīkṣā) and consecration or temple installation (pratiṣṭhā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nigamajJAnadeva_varuNapaddh.attribution: Nigamajñānadeva identifies himself in the colophons as the son of Vāmadeva and a resident of Vyāghrapura (Chidambaram). The root manual is attributed to Varuṇaśiva (Varuṇācārya).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nigamajJAnadeva_varuNapaddh.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript no. 30480, transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra (Pondicherry: IFP / Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nigamajJAnadeva_varuNapaddh.coverage: incomplete — Manuscript transcription marked as incomplete (lacking explicit+final colophon in catalog metadata).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nirvANaguhyakAlIpUjA_M00557.title: Nirvāṇaguhyakālīpūjā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nirvANaguhyakAlIpUjA_M00557.summary: The Nirvāṇaguhyakālīpūjā is a ritual manual (paddhati) centered on the worship of Nirvāṇaguhyakālī. The work outlines ritual procedures including purification, āsana, pūjā offerings, nyāsa, and mantra invocations.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nirvANaguhyakAlIpUjA_M00557.attribution: A ritual manual (paddhati) for the worship of Nirvāṇaguhyakālī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nirvANaguhyakAlIpUjA_M00557.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: NGMCP 5-2378, Reel no. B 189/8.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nirvANaguhyakAlIpUjA_M00557.coverage: unclear — Manuscript transcription without an explicit closing colophon naming the end of the text.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nitArcanavidhi_vAsanArcanav.title: Vātulatantra (Nityārcanapaṭala)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nitArcanavidhi_vAsanArcanav.summary: The Nityārcanapaṭala (also termed Vāsanārcanavidhi) from the Vātulatantra (Sahasrasaṃhitā recension) is an āgamic manual of daily Śaiva worship according to Śaivasiddhānta ritual doctrine. It details the classification of liṅgas (śailaja, ratnaja, lohaja, dāruja, mṛṇmaya, kṣaṇika), the distinction between ātmārtha (private) and parārtha (public) worship, preliminary purifications (pañcaśuddhi), āsanas, and the full sequence of Śiva-pūjā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nitArcanavidhi_vAsanArcanav.attribution: A revealed Śaivasiddhānta āgamic text forming part of the Vātula corpus (specifically designated in the colophon as belonging to the Sahasrasaṃhitā recension of the Vātulatantra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nitArcanavidhi_vAsanArcanav.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript RE27521 (Grantha script, 66 folios), prepared by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra, Institut Français de Pondichéry / Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nitArcanavidhi_vAsanArcanav.coverage: partial — Contains the Nityārcanapaṭala (daily worship chapter, also titled/labelled Vāsanārcanavidhi) extracted from the Vātulatantra.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_nityAdisaGgraha_M00673.title: Nityādisaṅgraha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nityAdisaGgraha_M00673.author: Takṣakavarta
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nityAdisaGgraha_M00673.summary: The Nityādisaṅgraha is an extensive Kashmiri Śaiva ritual manual (paddhati) composed by Rājānaka Takṣakavarta. Synthesizing liturgical and mantric traditions from the Bhairavatantras and Śaiva Siddhānta (relying heavily on the Svacchandatantra), it details daily worship (nityapūjā), oblations, initiation obligations, ritual procedures for linga and sthaṇḍila worship, and occasion-specific rites such as the Śivarātri observance.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nityAdisaGgraha_M00673.attribution: The concluding colophon attributes the work to Takṣakavarta: 'samāpteyaṃm nityādisaṅgrahābhidhānapaddhatiḥ kṛtistatrabhavataḥ mahāmāheśvarācāryaśrīmattakṣakavartasyeti śivam'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nityAdisaGgraha_M00673.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS Stein Or. d. 43, Bodleian Library, Oxford (Aurel Stein collection, Śāradā script, 149 fols.), unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_nityAdisaGgraha_M00673.coverage: complete — Transcription concluding with the work's final colophon on fol. 148b.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pAzupatagurukrama_M00679.title: Tantraviṣaye Pūjāstotra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pAzupatagurukrama_M00679.summary: A Śaiva-Śākta liturgical and devotional compendium (stotrasaṅgraha and pūjā manual) diplomatically transcribed from a 48-leaf Newari manuscript preserved in the Kaiser Library, Kathmandu. The compilation includes the Rudrayāmalāntargata Gurūpadeśa (Pādukāpañcakastotra), an eight-verse Pāśupatagurukrama tracing a lineage of masters down to Bhairavānanda, the Jyotirānandastava, the Kullukā from the Rudrayāmala, both the Ānandalaharī and Saundaryalaharī, and an Antaryajana manual with caturliṅgadhyāna instructions.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pAzupatagurukrama_M00679.attribution: A composite Śaiva-Śākta manuscript anthology containing anonymous liturgical procedures, extracts attributed to the Rudrayāmala, and stotras traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya (Ānandalaharī, Saundaryalaharī).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pAzupatagurukrama_M00679.edition: Kathmandu, Kaiser Library, MS 257 (NGMPP reel C 28/3; Newari script, 48 leaves, 20.1 x 6.9 cm).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pAzupatagurukrama_M00679.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of Kathmandu, Kaiser Library MS 257 (48 leaves, up to f. 44b with a displaced leaf transcribed at the end with a Hindi editorial note).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pIThapUjAvidhi_M00559.title: Pīṭhapūjāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pIThapUjAvidhi_M00559.summary: A Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) in Sanskrit mixed with Newari performance instructions, detailing ritual worship of pīṭhas, the Aṣṭamātṛkās, and Bhairava. The colophon mentions King Jayabhūpatīndramalladeva and the date Saṃvat 821, referencing Ākāśamahābhairava and a navagṛhapraveśapratiṣṭhā ceremony.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pIThapUjAvidhi_M00559.attribution: Liturgical paddhati featuring yajamāna-vākya recitations mentioning King Bhūpatīndramalla.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pIThapUjAvidhi_M00559.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcription from manuscript NGMCP 1/1081 Reel No: B 191/12.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pIThapUjAvidhi_M00559.coverage: complete — Diplomatic transcription of the manuscript witness, including the concluding date colophon of Nepāla Saṃvat 821 and an additional yajamāna-vākya.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrNAnanda_zrItattvacintAma.title: Tattvacintāmaṇi with the commentary of Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha (chapters 6–10)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrNAnanda_zrItattvacintAma.author: Pūrṇānanda, Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrNAnanda_zrItattvacintAma.summary: The Śrītattvacintāmaṇi is a Tantric digest composed by Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa.
