This portion comprises prakāśas 6 to 10: it includes verses from chapter 6 (dealing with subtle centres, Kuṇḍalinī, etc.) and continues through ritual and liturgical topics including kuṇḍa construction, homa rituals, and mantroddhāra, accompanied by the commentary of Bhuvanamohana Sāṅkhyatīrtha.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrNAnanda_zrItattvacintAma.attribution: Pūrṇānanda Paramahaṃsa is the author of the root text Śrītattvacintāmaṇi. The commentary was written by Bhuvanmohan Saṃkhyatirtha with notes by Chintamani Bhattacharya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrNAnanda_zrItattvacintAma.edition: Critically edited from original manuscripts with original commentary by Bhuvanmohan Saṃkhyatirtha and with notes by Chintamani Bhattacharya, Calcutta, 1936.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrNAnanda_zrItattvacintAma.coverage: partial — Covers chapters (prakāśas) 6 through 10 of the work. Prakāśa 6 starts at verse 21 and the text runs through to the end of prakāśa 10.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrvAmnAyanityadevArcanavid.title: Pūrvāmnāyanityadevārcanavidhi with Navātmāpūjāvidhi (fragments)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrvAmnAyanityadevArcanavid.summary: Portions of a Śākta ritual manual containing daily worship and bali rites of the Pūrvāmnāya and Caturāmnāya traditions, with pādukā mantras for goddesses including Bhagamālinī, Tripurasundarī, and Kubjikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrvAmnAyanityadevArcanavid.attribution: A Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) associated with the Caturāmnāya and Kubjikā traditions.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrvAmnAyanityadevArcanavid.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: NGMCP 1-1696/142, Reel no: B 191/22.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pUrvAmnAyanityadevArcanavid.coverage: incomplete — Acephalous and incomplete manuscript transcription; opens with pādukā mantras and includes the colophon 'iti pūrvvāmnāya nityakarmmadevārccanabalyārccanavidhi samāpta' in the middle, breaking off during a Kubjikā sequence.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_paJcaratnavyAkhyA_M00603.title: Pañcaratnavyākhyācatuṣṭaya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paJcaratnavyAkhyA_M00603.author: Vīraṇārādhya, Revaṇārādhya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paJcaratnavyAkhyA_M00603.summary: The Pañcaratnavyākhyācatuṣṭaya is a compilation of four Sanskrit Vīraśaiva exegetical works by Revaṇārādhya commenting on four five-verse hymns (Pañcaratnas) composed by his father, Sosale Vīraṇārādhya. The four commentaries—Tantrasāraprakāśikā, Tārakadīpikā, Śivatattvaprakāśikā, and Śrutyarthaprakāśikā—elucidate Śaiva ontology (pati, paśu, pāśa, and the ṣaḍadhvan) and synthesize Upanisadic and Śaivāgama teachings from a Vīraśaiva / Śivādvaita perspective.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paJcaratnavyAkhyA_M00603.attribution: Sosale Vīraṇārādhya composed the root verses of the four Pañcaratna hymns; his son Revaṇārādhya (Revaṇasiddheśvarātmaja) composed the four commentaries.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paJcaratnavyAkhyA_M00603.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00658 (pp. 1–66), copied from Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (GOML) Madras manuscripts D. 5087, D. 5088, D. 5089, and D. 5090.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paJcaratnavyAkhyA_M00603.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the four commentaries found in IFP transcript T00658 (pp. 1–66): Tantrasāraprakāśikā (pp. 1–21), Tārakadīpikā (pp. 22–28), Śivatattvaprakāśikā (pp. 29–36), and Śrutyarthaprakāśikā (pp. 37–66).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_padyavAhinI_M00676.title: Padyavāhinī
SA_MB_ilx_mb_padyavAhinI_M00676.author: Śaṅkara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_padyavAhinI_M00676.summary: The Padyavāhinī is a Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) in verse composed by Śaṅkara, synthesizing ritual traditions of the five currents (pañcasrotas). Incorporating Śāmbhava, Trika, Śrīvidyā, and Krama elements, it covers daily morning rites, nyāsa, pūjā, mantra extraction, and pavitrāropaṇa rituals.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_padyavAhinI_M00676.attribution: Attributed to Śaṅkara in the metadata headers. The text opening mentions Vyutpala as an earlier guru and refers to standing in the position of his praśiṣya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_padyavAhinI_M00676.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcription of Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (GOML), Chennai, MS No. R. 3203(a) (paper, Devanāgarī).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_padyavAhinI_M00676.coverage: complete — Transcribes the text from GOML Chennai MS R. 3203(a) (pp. 1–73).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_parAmbArcanacandrikA_M00629.title: Parāmbārcanacandrikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parAmbArcanacandrikA_M00629.summary: The Parāmbārcanacandrikā is a comprehensive Śrīvidyā ritual manual (paddhati) detailing the worship (arcana) of the supreme Goddess Parāmbā (Tripurasundarī). It begins with an esoteric analysis of the Śrīvidyā mantras (kādividyā and hādividyā) citing the Tantrarājatantra and Saundaryalaharī, and systematically guides the practitioner through morning rites, gurupādukā worship, nyāsas, external and internal offering sequences, and final expiatory prayers.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parAmbArcanacandrikA_M00629.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 1322 (kramāṅka 144, 74 folios), Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan (UPSS), Lucknow.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parAmbArcanacandrikA_M00629.coverage: partial — Lacks an explicit and final work colophon, ending abruptly after '...kṣamāyya||' on fol. 74, despite the manuscript cover notation 'patra - 74 pūrṇa'. An internal chapter colophon (itiśrīparāṃbārcanacaṃdrikāyāṃdvitīyaprakāśaḥ) occurs in the text.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_parArthapUjA_I00058.title: Parārthapūjā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parArthapUjA_I00058.summary: An unpublished late South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta temple liturgical manual (paddhati) written in Sanskrit with Tamil scribal notes, outlining the rites of public worship (parārthapūjā) for Lord Śiva and secondary deities. The manual details procedures starting from obtaining permission from Kṣetrapāla and opening the shrine doors, through purification rites (sthānaśuddhi, dravyaśuddhi), establishment of the five seats (pañcāsana), liṅga bathing (snapana), to the concluding worship of Manonmanī and Caṇḍeśvara.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parArthapUjA_I00058.attribution: A late South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta temple ritual manual. Scribal notations at the opening and colophon mention Kośapeṭṭai Subrahmaṇya Gurukkal and Cirukuṉṟam Subrahmaṇyan.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parArthapUjA_I00058.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE31011 in the collection of the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), prepared under the IFP-Muktabodha transcription project directed by Dr. Deviprasad Mishra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_parArthapUjA_I00058.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE31011 (pp. 5b–43b), opening with prārambha and concluding with parisamāptam.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_paramahaMsapaddati_M00664.title: Paramahaṃsapaddhati
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paramahaMsapaddati_M00664.summary: A short ritual manual (paddhati) ascribed to the Rudrayāmalatantra detailing the daily rites and contemplative practices of a Paramahaṃsa ascetic. It encompasses rules for purificatory cleansing (śauca, snāna, danta-dhāvana), prāṇāyāma, kara- and aṅga-nyāsa, dhyāna on the guru and supreme self, recitation of the Haṃsa mantra, and Vedāntic meditation upon the Upaniṣadic Mahāvākyas leading to non-dual absorption (samādhi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paramahaMsapaddati_M00664.attribution: Ascribed in the opening heading and closing colophon to the Rudrayāmalatantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paramahaMsapaddati_M00664.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple MSS Library (Jammu) MS No. 1065-gha (8 folios), digitized via eGangotri.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_paramahaMsapaddati_M00664.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of an 8-folio manuscript, concluding with 'itiśrīrudrayāmalataṃtreparamahaṃsapaddhatisapūrṇaṃ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyASTAviMzatikramA.title: Paścimāmnāyāṣṭāviṃśatikramārcana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyASTAviMzatikramA.summary: This is a Newar ritual manual (paddhati) of the Kubjikā cult (Paścimāmnāya, the 'Western Transmission'), mixing Sanskrit mantras with Newari ritual instructions. It sets out the worship of the goddess Kubjikā and her retinue in 28 sequences (aṣṭāviṃśatikrama): guru veneration, purification of the hands and of the vessels for water and arghya, bhūtaśuddhi, extensive nyāsas, meditation on the kramas, and worship of the lineages of Siddhas/Nāthas (navanātha, the 'ānanda' teachers). The manuscript then gives supplementary rites, chiefly bali offerings to Vaṭuka, the 64 yoginīs and other deities, and closing formulas for dakṣiṇā and gifts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyASTAviMzatikramA.edition: Unedited manuscript: National Archives Kathmandu (NAK) 8/961, microfilmed by the NGMCP (Nepal-German Manuscript Cataloguing/Preservation Project) as reel B 190/38. The text is a transcription of this manuscript, not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyASTAviMzatikramA.coverage: unclear — The e-text is a transcription of a single Nepalese manuscript. The main krama-worship runs from the gurupādukā invocation, nyāsas (aghora-, granthi-, dvādaśāṅga-, ṣaḍdūtī-, rudrakhaṇḍa-, mātṛkhaṇḍa-, trikhaṇḍā-nyāsa), kramadhyāna and vimalapañcaka through 'iti aṣṭāviṃśatikramma || 28 ||' to the colophon '[iti śrīpaścimajeṣṭhānjeṣṭhe āmnāya aṣṭāviṃśati krammārccaṇaṃ samāpta]'. After this come further rites: trikhaṇḍāpūjana, mūlasthāna devārcana, the catuḥṣaṣṭiyoginī-, mahā-, samaya- and śānti-bali, and gift/dakṣiṇā formulas with Newari rubrics ending '... upadohanārthaṃ || śubha ||'. The ilx_skt Muktabodha metadata marks the transcription as 'incomplete, lacking final colophon', with the colophon located 'in middle'. It could not be checked whether folios are missing, because the NGMCP description of the manuscript was not accessible.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyasamayadIkSAvidh.title: Paścimāmnāyasamayadīkṣāvidhi (fragment)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyasamayadIkSAvidh.summary: An incomplete Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) transcribed from Nepalese manuscript NGMCP 4/204 (Reel A 243/11), associated with the Paścimāmnāya (Kubjikā) tradition. The extant fragment preserves preliminary ritual prescriptions concerning the selection of auspicious seasons, lunar days, and lunar asterisms for magical rites (ṣaṭkarman), herbal-gathering protocols (auṣadhagrahaṇa) with Newari vernacular procedural rubrics, and auxiliary mantras of Sudarśana and Garuḍa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyasamayadIkSAvidh.attribution: Anonymous ritual paddhati belonging to the Newar Paścimāmnāya (Kubjikā) manuscript corpus.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyasamayadIkSAvidh.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript MS 4/204 (Reel no. A 243/11), transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00560, Rev. 0, Sept. 26, 2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimAmnAyasamayadIkSAvidh.coverage: fragment — Incomplete transcription of NGMCP MS 4/204 (Reel A 243/11). The surviving 169 lines consist of astrological timing rules for ṣaṭkarman rites (ṛtu-, tithi-, nakṣatranirṇaya), medicinal plant collection rites (auṣadhagrahaṇavidhi) with Classical Newari vernacular rubrics, and protective mantras (Sudarśana, Garuḍa), breaking off abruptly at line 168.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimArcanapaddhati_M00678.title: Paścimārcanapaddhati (vidhis 1–2 and beginning of 3)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimArcanapaddhati_M00678.author: Vimalaprabodha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimArcanapaddhati_M00678.summary: A Kubjikā ritual manual by Vimalaprabodha, disciple of Sahadeva, dedicated to the worship of Navātman. The manuscript breaks off at fol. 92b.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimArcanapaddhati_M00678.attribution: Composed by Vimalaprabodha, disciple of Sahadeva.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimArcanapaddhati_M00678.edition: Manuscript transcription: Kathmandu, Kaiser Library ms # 79 (NGMPP reel C 6/15), palm leaf; NGMPP card gives 'ने.सं. 331'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimArcanapaddhati_M00678.coverage: partial — Text breaks off at fol. 92b.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimajyeSThAmnAyakarmArca.title: Paścimajyeṣṭhāmnāyakarmārcanapaddhati
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimajyeSThAmnAyakarmArca.summary: An unpublished Nepalese Kaula ritual manual (paddhati) of the Western / elder transmission (Paścimajyeṣṭhāmnāya) focusing on the worship of the goddess Kubjikā and her retinue. It details sequences of nyāsa (kara-, vaktra-, aṅga-, and ṣaḍdūtīnyāsa), jar- and seat-installation, oblation (bali), the worship of the six transmissions (ṣaḍāmnāyapūjā), Yoginī groups, and concluding mantra transmission (upadeśa) regulations.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimajyeSThAmnAyakarmArca.attribution: Anonymous ritual handbook preserved in Nepalese Newar tantric collections.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimajyeSThAmnAyakarmArca.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) Reel no. B 190/39.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pazcimajyeSThAmnAyakarmArca.coverage: partial — Lacking a formal final colophon for the codex as a whole; the work's title colophon ('iti śrīśrīśrīpaścimajeṣṭhāmnāya krammārccana paddhatiḥ samāptaṃ') occurs internally/in the middle, followed by additional sections on dīkṣā rules, tithiphala, and upadeśa, concluding abruptly with 'śubhaḥ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_I000.title: Prāsādaṣaṭślokīvyākhyā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_I000.summary: An anonymous commentary (vyākhyā) on the Prāsādaṣaṭślokī, a Śaiva Siddhānta text consisting of six verses analyzing the Prāsādamantra (hauṃ). It explains the internal esoteric structure, kalās (specifically the twelve kalās), associated devatās, sonic micro-divisions (mātrā), and bodily locations from the mūlādhāra up to the brahmarandhra according to Śaivāgama teachings.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_I000.attribution: The work opens with an invocatory sentence attributing the effort to the grace of Gaṇādhīśa ('yathā mūrttigaṇādhīśa kṛpāleśānmayādhunā śrī matprāsāda ṣaṭślokyavyākhyānaṃ likhyate'), but leaves the author unnamed.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_I000.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 30592 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), Puducherry (18 folios).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_I000.coverage: complete — Transcribes the extant manuscript bundle IFP RE 30592 (18 folios), commenting on all six verses expounding the 12-kalā Prāsādamantra, and ending with closing Tamil notes.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_M005.title: Prāsādaṣaṭślokī with Vyākhyā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_M005.summary: The Prāsādaṣaṭślokī is a six-verse Śaiva esoteric text detailing the phonic, spatial, and yogic ascent of the Prāsādamantra (the bījamantra of Paramaśiva, hauṃ) from the mūlādhāra through bodily and cranial centers up to unmanā. The accompanying anonymous prose Vyākhyā explicates the twelvefold and sixteenfold divisions (kalā) of the mantra, its anatomical measurements (aṅgula), phonic stages, and internal absorption (laya). The transcript concludes with supplementary passages detailing the Kalāprāsāda and the yogic viṣuvats.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_M005.attribution: The root verses and the prose commentary are transmitted anonymously in the South Indian Śaiva manuscript tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_M005.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00469, prepared by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. M00529).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prAsAdaSaTzlokIvyAkhyA_M005.coverage: complete — Contains all 6 root verses, the complete prose vyākhyā, and an appended exposition on the kalāprāsāda and viṣuvats as preserved in IFP transcript T00469.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_prabhuliGgalila_M00621.title: Prabhuliṅgalīlā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prabhuliGgalila_M00621.summary: The Prabhuliṅgalīlā is a Sanskrit Vīraśaiva hagiographical text presented as part of the Bhaviṣyatpurāṇa, narrating the life, deeds, and teachings of the 12th-century saint Allama Prabhu. Closely related to Cāmarasa's Kannada work Prabhuliṅgalīle, it depicts Allama Prabhu's conquest of Māyā and his spiritual dialogues with prominent Vīraśaiva figures such as Gorakṣanātha, Muktāyakkā, and Basava, elucidating Vīraśaiva philosophical principles including the Ṣaṭsthala system.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prabhuliGgalila_M00621.attribution: Framed within the Bhaviṣyatpurāṇa ('bhaviṣyatpurāṇe prabhuliṃgalīlāprāraṃbhaḥ', 'ityārṣaśrībhaviṣyatpurāṇakathāviśālāyāṃ ... prabhuliṅgalīlāyāṃ'). It is related to Cāmarasa's Kannada text Prabhuliṅgalīle.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_prabhuliGgalila_M00621.coverage: complete — Complete in 25 adhyāyas, ending with the colophon of the 25th chapter ('paṃcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_pratyaMgirApUjAvidhi_M00561.title: Pratyaṃgirāpūjāvidhi (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pratyaMgirApUjAvidhi_M00561.summary: An anonymous Nepalese ritual manual for the worship of the fierce goddess Pratyaṅgirā, chiefly to destroy enemies. It prescribes a saṅkalpa for having a brahmin recite the Pratyaṅgirā mālāmantra framed by nine Atharvavedic verses (śūdras omit them), nyāsa, the yantra, the dhyāna of the goddess, upacāras and āvaraṇapūjā, then a phalaśruti and a list of auxiliary mantras.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pratyaMgirApUjAvidhi_M00561.attribution: Anonymous ritual compilation (paddhati/vidhi) dedicated to the cult of Goddess Pratyaṅgirā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pratyaMgirApUjAvidhi_M00561.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription (no printed edition): NGMCP pra 1696/1735 Reel No: 192/2 (as given in the Muktabodha header).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_pratyaMgirApUjAvidhi_M00561.coverage: partial — Short manuscript transcription, fols. 1a, 2a–7b (fol. 1b missing). Saṅkalpa, nyāsa, yantra, dhyāna, upacāras and āvaraṇapūjā are followed by a phalaśruti whose last verse is left unfinished ('paṭhitā pāṭhitā devī sarvasiddhi karī'), then a list of miscellaneous mantras (Kāmadeva, Navadurgā, śivāstra, piṅgalāstra) ending without a colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_revantapUjA_M00563.title: Daśakarmapaddhati (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_revantapUjA_M00563.summary: An anonymous Newar manual (paddhati) of the domestic life-cycle rites (daśakarma), giving Sanskrit mantras with procedural rubrics in Newari. It covers the prenatal rites (garbhādhāna, puṃsavana, sīmantonnayana), birth and childhood rites (jātakarma, nāmakaraṇa, annaprāśana, cūḍākaraṇa), vratabandha, vedārambha and samāvartana, and the marriage rites up to caturthīkarma. An appended section gives the names of Agni for the various rites.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_revantapUjA_M00563.attribution: Anonymous Newar paddhati of the Brahmanical (Vājasaneyi-type) life-cycle rites, with Newari rubrics.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_revantapUjA_M00563.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription (no printed edition): Kathmandu, National Archives, MS 1-1696/2214, NGMPP reel A 456/46 (catalogued as Revantapūjā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_revantapUjA_M00563.coverage: partial — Manuscript transcription, fols. 1b–74a with fols. 1a, 6a, 38 and 72 missing. Contains yavodakavidhi, garbhādhāna, puṃsavana, sīmantonnayana, māsapūrṇa, jātakarma, sūtikāgni, ṣaṣṭhījāgara, niṣkramaṇa, nāmakaraṇa, annaprāśana, kaṇṭhasūtra, cūḍākaraṇa, vratabandha, vedārambha, śrāvaṇīkarma, samāvartana, vivāha, bhramaṇayātrā and caturthīkarma, then an appended 'eighth paṭala' on the names of Agni and verses on thread measures. It ends at fol. 74a without a final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAhib_kaul_kalpavRkSa_M0005.title: Kalpavṛkṣa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAhib_kaul_kalpavRkSa_M0005.author: Sāhiba Kaula
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAhib_kaul_kalpavRkSa_M0005.summary: The Kalpavṛkṣa (or Kalpavṛkṣabandha) is an unpublished non-dual Śaiva philosophical treatise by the Kashmiri master Sāhiba Kaula. Written at the behest of Mahārāja Jayavantsiṃha of Maruvāṭa for the instruction of beginners (bālabodha), it synthesizes the viewpoints of Brahmādvaita, Śivādvaita, and Mahādvaita, articulating Pratyabhijñā and Spanda philosophy in accessible terms.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAhib_kaul_kalpavRkSa_M0005.attribution: Composed by the Kashmiri Śaiva author Sāhiba Kaula (fl. 19th century according to the Muktabodha header note, author of the Devīnāmavilāsa). The text explicitly names the author in the opening and final colophon and mentions that it was composed upon the request of King Jayavantsiṃha of Maruvāṭa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAhib_kaul_kalpavRkSa_M0005.edition: Diplomatic transcription from manuscript MS No. 1353, Oriental Research Library (ORL), University Campus, Hazratbal, Srinagar (paper, Śāradā script, 37 folios / 74 pages, 25 x 17.3 cm, bad condition); unpublished.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAhib_kaul_kalpavRkSa_M0005.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript (ORL MS 1353, 37 folios), preserving the work from its opening verse through the final colophon and praśasti.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAvaratantramantrasaMgraha_.title: Sāvaratantramantrasaṃgraha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAvaratantramantrasaMgraha_.author: Rāmasiṃha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAvaratantramantrasaMgraha_.summary: A compendium of Śābara (vernacular folk-tantric) incantations, protective mantras, and healing rituals attributed to Rāmasiṃha. The text interweaves early modern vernacular North Indian formulas invoking deities (Śiva, Pārvatī, Hanumān), Nātha siddhas (Gorakhnāth), and Muslim pīrs (Sulaimān) to treat physical ailments, fevers, and encounters with wild animals.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAvaratantramantrasaMgraha_.attribution: Only the final colophon (6th prakāśa) names the compiler: "iti śrīsāvaratantre mantrasaṃgrahe durge rāmasiṃhakṛte ...". The colophons of prakāśas 1–5 name sections or sub-collections (Bhānumatī-carita, Sonā ciraiyā, Kavūtarakalā, Durgomadanā-vicitrakalā) but no author.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAvaratantramantrasaMgraha_.edition: Manuscript transcription of Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan (UPSS), Lucknow, MS 5144 (diplomatic transcription).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sAvaratantramantrasaMgraha_.coverage: complete — Six prakāśas, each closed by a colophon: (1) pretādi-agni-upaśamana; (2) śarīraja-ādi-upaśamana; (3) bandhamokṣa, uccāṭana, garbharakṣā, bālarakṣā; (4) sthāvara-jaṅgama viṣa; (5) māraṇa, mohana, vidveṣaṇa; (6) dvārācakra etc., ending with jvara mantras. A scribal colophon follows ("yādṛśaṃ pustakaṃ ... saṃvat phālguṇa saptamī ..."), so the copy in UPSS MS 5144 is complete as transmitted. The work's extent outside this manuscript is unknown. The language is mostly early modern Hindi with Sanskrit mantra and colophon material.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_sUtradhAramaNDana_prAsAdama.title: Prāsādamaṇḍana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sUtradhAramaNDana_prAsAdama.author: Maṇḍana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sUtradhAramaNDana_prAsAdama.summary: The Prāsādamaṇḍana is a Sanskrit manual on Hindu temple architecture (vāstuśāstra) composed by Sūtradhāra Maṇḍana. In eight chapters, it covers site preparation, ground layout, proportional measurements, styles of temples (including Nāgara, Drāviḍa, and Bhūmija), doorframe and śikhara designs, maṇḍapa construction, image installation, and temple renovation (jīrṇoddhāra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sUtradhAramaNDana_prAsAdama.attribution: The colophons attribute the work to Sūtradhāra Maṇḍana (śrīsūtradhāramaṇḍanaviracite vāstuśāstre prāsādamaṇḍane).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sUtradhAramaNDana_prAsAdama.edition: Jagaddhara Jāḍū Śāstrī (Jagaddhar Zadoo), ed., Prāsādamaṇḍanaṃ śrīsūtradhāramaṇḍanaviracitam, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies (KSTS) 72, Srinagar: Durgā Press / Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir State, 1947 (Saṃvat 2004).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sUtradhAramaNDana_prAsAdama.coverage: complete — Complete in 8 adhyāyas, preceded by the editor's table of contents (viṣayānukramaṇī).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahasrAgama_I00042.title: Sahasrāgama (Karṣaṇādipratiṣṭhānta section)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahasrAgama_I00042.summary: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of the Karṣaṇādipratiṣṭhāntabhāga of the Sahasrāgama (also titled Sahasratantram in the manuscript). Topics include the eightfold binding paste (aṣṭabandhana), repeated consecration (punarāvarta), sacrificial pavilion layout (yāgaśālā), and preliminary sacrificial offerings.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahasrAgama_I00042.attribution: Identified as a text of the Sahasrāgama (Mūlāgama) in the manuscript metadata, preserved under the manuscript bundle title Śaivāgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahasrAgama_I00042.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcription of French Institute of Pondicherry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE15540 (titled 'Śaivāgama', identified as Sahasrāgama, 88 folios). Transcribed by the IFP Indology team under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. I00042), 2024.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahasrAgama_I00042.coverage: partial — Preserves the Karṣaṇādipratiṣṭhānta portion of the Mūlāgama, covering rituals from soil-preparation to consecration/installation (including Aṣṭabandhanavidhi, Punarāvartapratiṣṭhāvidhi, Padanyāsavidhi, and Yāgaśālānirmāṇavidhi), transcribed from folios 4b–86a of IFP bundle RE15540.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahib_kaul_zrIvidyAnityapad.title: Śrīvidyānityapaddhati (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahib_kaul_zrIvidyAnityapad.author: Sāhib Kaul
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahib_kaul_zrIvidyAnityapad.summary: The Śrīvidyānityapaddhati attributed to Sāhib Kaul is a ritual manual detailing daily worship (nityapaddhati) in the Śrīvidyā tradition. The text prescribes morning rites, guru contemplation, nyāsa sequences, ghaṭapūjā, and pātrapūjā. This e-text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of an incomplete manuscript preserving only the earlier portions of the rite.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahib_kaul_zrIvidyAnityapad.attribution: Attributed in the Muktabodha catalog record to Sāhib Kaul.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahib_kaul_zrIvidyAnityapad.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of Jammu, Raghunath Temple Library MS 1673k (unpublished).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sahib_kaul_zrIvidyAnityapad.coverage: partial — Diplomatic transcription of Jammu, Raghunath Temple MS 1673k. The text runs from the morning rites (prātaḥkṛtya, guru-dhyāna, nyāsa) through ghaṭasthāpana and ghaṭapūjā into the śrīpātrapūjā / viśeṣārghya-sthāpana, and breaks off mid-word at the last segment ("śaṃvi..."). There is no final colophon. ilx_skt metadata: "Completeness: incomplete".

SA_MB_ilx_mb_sakalAgamasArasaGgraha_I000.title: Sakalāgamasārasaṅgraha (incomplete: bundle images 1–91b)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sakalAgamasArasaGgraha_I000.summary: The Sakalāgamasārasaṅgraha is an unpublished South Indian Śaiva ritual compendium preserved in palm-leaf manuscripts. It gathers ritual prescriptions, temple consecration (pratiṣṭhā), renovation (jīrṇoddhāraṇa), festival timing, and expiatory rites from canonical Śaivāgamas such as the Kāraṇa, Svāyambhuva, and Ajita, interspersing Sanskrit verses with practical Tamil notes and material recipes (such as aṣṭabandhana binding agent).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sakalAgamasArasaGgraha_I000.attribution: A South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta ritual digest (saṅgraha / prayoga manual) assembling instructions, mantras, and quotations from various Āgamas (e.g., Kāraṇa, Svāyambhuva, Ajita, Suprabheda).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sakalAgamasArasaGgraha_I000.edition: Diplomatic transcription of the palm-leaf bundle IFP RE 22716 (Institut Français de Pondichéry; 298 folios / images; 350 × 25 mm). Prepared by the IFP Indology team under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra and published online by IFP and the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. I00039; publication year 2024; Revision 0: Feb. 7, 2025, Revision 1: June 4, 2025). Unpublished in print.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_sakalAgamasArasaGgraha_I000.coverage: partial — Diplomatic transcription of IFP bundle RE 22716. The e-text runs from the title and index images (p.1–6, a topic list of ca. 70–75 items from kṣetreśasthāpana to bhūtaśuddhi) through Tamil aṣṭabandhana recipes, pratiṣṭhā sections, a Gaṅgāstotra and Kālīpratiṣṭhā. It ends at image p.91b with quotations from the Kāraṇa and Svāyambhuva on pūjāmāsa and ayana, with no closing colophon. The bundle has 298 images, so roughly two thirds of the bundle is not in the e-text.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_samayadIkSAdhivAsanavidhi_M.title: Samayadīkṣādhivāsanavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_samayadIkSAdhivAsanavidhi_M.summary: An anonymous Śaiva ritual manual (paddhati) describing the preliminary rites of initiation (samayadīkṣā) and preliminary consecration (adhivāsana). The manual outlines the worship of the four entrance gateways and arches (toraṇapūjā, dvārapūjā), invocation of kalaśas and guardians, preparation and worship of the sacrificial fire (kuṇḍa, garbhāgni), oblations, psychic channel union (nāḍīsaṃdhāna), and conferral of the sacred thread (yajñopavīta) upon the disciple.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_samayadIkSAdhivAsanavidhi_M.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu MS 1-1078 (NGMCP Reel No. A 48/23).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_samayadIkSAdhivAsanavidhi_M.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript text, concluding with 'samānyasamaya dīkṣāmiti'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_saravatIstotram_mantrabhAsy.title: Sarasvatīstotra, Mantrabhāṣya, Aṣṭādaśajātinirṇaya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saravatIstotram_mantrabhAsy.summary: A composite transcription of three short Sanskrit works preserved across consecutive manuscripts in the Shri Raghunatha Temple Library in Jammu. It opens with the Sarasvatīstotra, a hymn attributed to the sage Āśvalāyana invoking Sarasvatī as the supreme Brahman and power of speech, complete with nyāsa/viniyoga formulas. This is followed by a prose Mantrabhāṣya dealing with Vedic/mantric exposition, and concludes with the Aṣṭādaśajātinirṇaya, a brief verse enumeration of the four varṇas and fourteen mixed/derivative castes (upavarṇas).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saravatIstotram_mantrabhAsy.attribution: The initial stotra is framed as uttered by the sage Āśvalāyana ('śrī āśvalāyana uvāca', colophon: 'oṃ asya śrīsarasvatīstotramaṃtrasya āśvalāyana ṛṣiḥ'). The Mantrabhāṣya and Aṣṭādaśajātinirṇaya are anonymous/traditional works.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saravatIstotram_mantrabhAsy.edition: Manuscript transcriptions from Shri Ragunatha Temple MSS Library Jammu, nos. 2674 k, 2675 kh, and 2676 g.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saravatIstotram_mantrabhAsy.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of three consecutive manuscript codices: Sarasvatīstotra, Mantrabhāṣya, and Aṣṭādaśajātinirṇaya.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyakalpadrUma_M00648.title: Saubhāgyakalpadruma (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyakalpadrUma_M00648.summary: The Saubhāgyakalpadruma is a Śākta Śrīvidyā ritual paddhati detailing the daily worship (nityapūjā) of Tripurasundarī. It outlines preliminary morning observances (snāna, sandhyopāsanā, tarpana, nyāsa) followed by the elaborate sequence of worship for each circuit (āvaraṇa) of the Śrīcakra. In this manuscript witness, the text breaks off unfinished in the seventh circuit (Sarvarogaharacakra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyakalpadrUma_M00648.attribution: Anonymous Śrīvidyā paddhati. The author refers to his guru as Śrīpādavānanda (or Pādavānanda). Rāmacandra Pāṭhaka noted in line 0 is the owner of the physical manuscript.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyakalpadrUma_M00648.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Jammu, Raghunath Temple Library MS 4896. Transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute staff under the supervision of Anirban Dash (Revision 0, 6 April 2024; Catalog no. M00648).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyakalpadrUma_M00648.coverage: partial — Incomplete. Covers morning rituals (prātaḥsmṛti, snāna, sandhyā, nyāsa) and the stepwise āvaraṇapūjā of the Śrīcakra through the sixth āvaraṇa (Nigarbhayoginīs) and into the seventh āvaraṇa (Sarvarogaharacakra), where it breaks off abruptly at line 625 during the invocation of the Vaśinī vāgdevatās.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyaratnAkara_M00577.title: Saubhāgyaratnākara (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyaratnAkara_M00577.author: Vidyānandanātha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyaratnAkara_M00577.summary: The Saubhāgyaratnākara is an extensive Tantric ritual digest (paddhati) of the Śrīvidyā Śākta tradition composed in mixed verse and prose by Vidyānandanātha, a disciple of Saccidānandanātha. It systematically details initiation (dīkṣā), daily and occasional worship (nitya-naimittika-pūjā), complex nyāsas (including the mahāṣoḍhānyāsa), mantra-puraścaraṇa, and internal meditative rituals (ātmapūjā) centered on Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī and the Śrīcakra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyaratnAkara_M00577.attribution: Identified in opening verse 5 ('śrīvidyānaṃdanāthohaṃ vītarāgo viviktadhīḥ') and colophons as Vidyānandanātha, disciple of Saccidānandanātha.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyaratnAkara_M00577.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Shri Ragunatha Temple MSS Library Jammu, no. 4892.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyaratnAkara_M00577.coverage: partial — Incomplete manuscript transcription; contains the opening taraṅgas and subsequent ritual procedures covering nyāsa up to ātmapūjā, lacking the explicit and final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyatantra_M00649.title: Saubhāgyatantra (Pārāyaṇavidhi, chapters 1–11)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyatantra_M00649.summary: The Pārāyaṇavidhi section of the Saubhāgyatantra is a Śākta tantric manual detailing the astronomical, calendrical, and liturgical calculations (ahargaṇa) necessary for the systematic continuous recitation (pārāyaṇa) of Śrīvidyā mantras. It integrates chronological reckoning (yuga, maṇḍala, ahargaṇa) with the esoteric worship of the Nityā deities and the traditional transmission lineages (āmnāya) culminating in Rājarājeśvarī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyatantra_M00649.attribution: A Śākta tantric scripture belonging to the Śrīvidyā tradition, framed as revealed āgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyatantra_M00649.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 1042gh (1042gha) preserved at the Raghunath Temple Library, Jammu (J&K), prepared under the supervision of Anirban Dash, Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (revision 0, April 6, 2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_saubhAgyatantra_M00649.coverage: partial — Comprises chapters 1 to 11 of the Pārāyaṇavidhi section of the Saubhāgyatantra.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhAntalezasaMgrahaTIkA_M.title: Siddhāntaleśasaṃgrahavyākhyā Śrīkṛṣṇālaṃkāra (paricchedas 1–3)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhAntalezasaMgrahaTIkA_M.author: Acyutakṛṣṇānandatīrtha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhAntalezasaMgrahaTIkA_M.summary: The Śrīkṛṣṇālaṃkāra (or Kṛṣṇālaṅkāra) is a commentary by Acyutakṛṣṇānandatīrtha on Appaya Dīkṣita's Siddhāntaleśasaṃgraha, the classic Advaita Vedānta doxography compiling diverse views within the post-Śaṅkara tradition. This e-text is a transcription of a manuscript from Jammu containing paricchedas 1–3.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhAntalezasaMgrahaTIkA_M.attribution: Acyutakṛṣṇānandatīrtha is described in the colophon as a disciple of Svayaṃprakāśānanda Sarasvatī ('śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājikācāryaśrīmatsvayaṃprakāśānaṃdasarasvatīdivyaśrīcaraṇāraviṃdasaṃlagnarajobhūtasya').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhAntalezasaMgrahaTIkA_M.edition: Manuscript transcription of Shri Raghunath Temple Manuscript Library, Jammu, MS no. 5388 gh
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhAntalezasaMgrahaTIkA_M.coverage: partial — Paricchedas 1 to 3 only (concluding with the colophon of tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ). Pariccheda 4 is absent.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkavaca_M00567.title: Siddhilakṣmīkavaca
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkavaca_M00567.summary: A Śākta-Tāntrika protective hymn (kavaca) and mālāmantra dedicated to the goddess Siddhilakṣmī, identified closely in the text with Pratyaṅgirā and connected to the Trailokyaḍāmara tradition. It provides dhyāna descriptions, a viniyoga invoking Nārāyaṇa ṛṣi and the Gāyatrī metre, and systematic protective invocations of various forms of Lakṣmī, Mātṛkās, and Bhairavas for every limb and organ of the practitioner.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkavaca_M00567.attribution: Scriptural Śākta text attributed to the Trailokyaḍāmara (colophon reads: iti śrītrailokyaḍāre [= trailokyaḍāmare] śrīsiddhilakṣmīkavaca samāptaḥ).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkavaca_M00567.edition: Manuscript transcription from Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP), MS no. E 2663, Reel no. E 158/8 (unpublished manuscript transcription).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkavaca_M00567.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript text comprising an opening mālāmantra, introductory dialogue, dhyāna, viniyoga, and 58 verses of kavaca and phalaśruti ending with the colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramArcanA_M005.title: Siddhilakṣmīkramārcana
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramArcanA_M005.summary: A Nepalese Śākta ritual manual (paddhati) for the sequential worship (kramārcana) of Siddhilakṣmī, a major goddess closely associated with Guhyakālī and the lineage of the Newar kings. The text details purification rites, nyāsa (specifically vajrakavacagranthinyāsa), fire sacrifice preparations (kuṇḍasaṃskāra), homa, and festival rites (navamī and daśamī pūjā), featuring Sanskrit mantras interspersed with ritual instructions in Classical Newari.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramArcanA_M005.attribution: Anonymous liturgical ritual manual (paddhati) from the Nepalese Śākta/Newar tantric tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramArcanA_M005.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) reel no. H 337/5.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramArcanA_M005.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual transcribed from manuscript NGMCP Reel no: H 337/5; catalogued with colophon 'iti śrīsiddhilakṣmīkramārcanaṃ samāpta + additional text'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramasthaNDilAr.title: Siddhilakṣmīkramasthaṇḍilārcanavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramasthaNDilAr.summary: A Nepalese Śākta ritual manual (paddhati) detailing the worship (arcana) of the tantric goddess Siddhilakṣmī on a prepared ritual ground or altar (sthaṇḍila). The work incorporates complex nyāsa sequences, kalāyudha visualizations, bali offerings, and embedded devotional compositions such as the Mālinīdaṇḍaka and Siddhilakṣmītrikhaṇḍadaṇḍaka, accompanied by practical ritual directions in Newari.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramasthaNDilAr.attribution: A traditional liturgical manual (paddhati) containing Sanskrit mantras and verses with Newari ritual rubrics, preserved in the Kathmandu Valley.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramasthaNDilAr.edition: Manuscript transcription based on Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 1-624, Reel A 249/6; selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski, transcribed under the supervision of Anirban Dash for Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2021 (catalogue no. M00569).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIkramasthaNDilAr.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript text, concluding with the thaṇḍilārcanavidhi and adhivāsanavidhi colophons.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmImantroddhara_M0.title: Siddhilakṣmīmantroddhāra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmImantroddhara_M0.summary: A short Tantric ritual manual and hymn dedicated to the goddess Siddhilakṣmī (also referred to as Trottalā), a prominent esoteric form of the Goddess in the Krama, Jayadrathayāmala, and Newar traditions. The text outlines daily purifications (snāna), esoteric mantra extraction (mantroddhāra) involving the five praṇavas (pañcapraṇava), the fruits of caru offerings, and concludes with three laudatory verses (stotra) extolling Siddhilakṣmī as the supreme liberative reality.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmImantroddhara_M0.attribution: Scriptural/traditional manual belonging to the cult of Siddhilakṣmī (Trottalā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmImantroddhara_M0.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of National Archives, Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript (reel B 28/23).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmImantroddhara_M0.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript, ending with '[śrīśiddhilakṣmīmantrodhārastotra samāpta]'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmInityapUjApaddha.title: Siddhilakṣmīnityapūjāpaddhati (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmInityapUjApaddha.summary: An incomplete Śākta-Tāntrika ritual manual (paddhati) setting out daily worship (nityapūjā) associated with Siddhilakṣmī in the Kubjikā / Paścimāmnāya tradition. The text details preliminary purification rites, guru-maṇḍala adoration, nyāsa sequences (including kara-, vaktra-, and aṅganyāsa), vessel sanctification (jalapātra and arghyapātra), mantras, and offering sequences up to the concluding nirmālya rites.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmInityapUjApaddha.attribution: Anonymous liturgical ritual manual belonging to the Kubjikā / Paścimāmnāya tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmInityapUjApaddha.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: NGMCP Reel no: H 377/7.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmInityapUjApaddha.coverage: partial — Incomplete; explicitly marked as '(ūncomplete)' at the opening, and breaks off mid-word at segment 651 with 'devī nirmā'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIvidhAna_M00572.title: Siddhilakṣmīvidhāna
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIvidhAna_M00572.summary: A Śākta-Tāntrika ritual manual detailing the mantras, prastāra extraction, visualization, and magical rites (prayoga) dedicated to the goddess Siddhilakṣmī (also addressed as Trailokyavijayā). The text constitutes chapter 36 of the second ṣaṭka of the 24,000-verse Jayadrathayāmala (Śiraccheda / Vidyāpīṭha division of the Bhairava corpus).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIvidhAna_M00572.attribution: Scriptural dialogue between Devī and Bhairava canonical within the Śiraccheda / Vidyāpīṭha stream of the Jayadrathayāmala.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIvidhAna_M00572.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription of Nepal-German Manuscript Conservation Project (NGMCP) MS 4/304 (Reel no. A 59/14). Keyed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute staff under the supervision of Anirban Dash; text selected by Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (catalog no. M00572).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmIvidhAna_M00572.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the chapter as preserved in NGMCP manuscript 4/304, concluding with the colophon of the 36th paṭala of the second ṣaṭka of the Jayadrathayāmala.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmyadhivAsanasthaN.title: Siddhilakṣmyadhivāsanasthaṇḍilārcanavidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmyadhivAsanasthaN.summary: A Tantric ritual manual (paddhati) in hybrid Sanskrit with Newari liturgical directions prescribing the ground-altar worship (sthaṇḍilārcana) for the preliminary habitation or consecration rite (adhivāsana) of the goddess Siddhilakṣmī. Stemming from the Nepalese royal Śākta-Tantric traditions, it provides detailed procedures for purificatory baths, nyāsa, kalaśapūjā, bali offerings, and worship of kula and lineage deities (deguli).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmyadhivAsanasthaN.attribution: Anonymous ritual paddhati in hybrid Sanskrit and Newari preserved in the Kathmandu Valley.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmyadhivAsanasthaN.edition: Diplomatic e-text transcription based directly on Nepalese manuscript NGMCP MS 1/727 (Reel B 198/21).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_siddhilakSmyadhivAsanasthaN.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript from opening invocation to final colophon (adhivāsanakarmaṇi thaṇḍilārcanavidhiḥ samāptaḥ).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_somanAtha_ajJAnadhvAntadIpi.title: Ajñānadhvāntadīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_somanAtha_ajJAnadhvAntadIpi.author: Somanātha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_somanAtha_ajJAnadhvAntadIpi.summary: The Ajñānadhvāntadīpikā is a tantric manual (mantrapaddhati) attributed to Somanātha, son of Maheśabhaṭṭa. It treats the qualifications of guru and śiṣya, astrologically auspicious timings for dīkṣā, mantra examination and purification (siddhādisādhana), nyāsa, and various practical rituals (prayogas) and yantras accompanied by vernacular Hindi commentary.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_somanAtha_ajJAnadhvAntadIpi.attribution: The author identifies himself in verse 1 as 'somanātho maheśajaḥ'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_somanAtha_ajJAnadhvAntadIpi.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Devanāgarī manuscript MS 4966 (38 folios; Alm. 22, Shlf. 4), Dharmartha Trust Library at Raghunath Temple, Jammu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_somanAtha_ajJAnadhvAntadIpi.coverage: incomplete — Lacking explicit and final colophon according to catalog metadata. The e-text ends on fol. 38 with vernacular-annotated mantras, a yantra drawing, and a blank folio.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_stotrasaGgraha_I00057.title: Stotrasaṅgraha (incomplete: Ātmārthapūjā section and Mahāgaṇeśapañcaratna)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_stotrasaGgraha_I00057.summary: A Śaiva palm-leaf bundle (IFP RE 31139). The transcribed part is a manual for personal worship (ātmārthapūjā), including astrasandhi, Śivasandhi and Śivasūryapūjā, in Sanskrit with Tamil instructions. Its saṅkalpa is addressed to Mīnākṣīsundareśvara. It ends with the Mahāgaṇeśapañcaratna. The bundle's larger section of Śiva stotras is not transcribed.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_stotrasaGgraha_I00057.attribution: A composite Śaiva/Smārta ritual and stotra collection combining Sanskrit verses with Tamil rubrics.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_stotrasaGgraha_I00057.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 31139 (also labelled RE-31193), Institut Français de Pondichéry, transcribed under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra, published online by the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. I00057).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_stotrasaGgraha_I00057.coverage: partial — IFP bundle RE 31139 has 55 images. The e-text covers images p.5b–17b: dhyānas of the sandhyā goddesses, astrasandhi, Śivasandhi, ātmārthapūjā (with a saṅkalpa for Mīnākṣīsundareśvara), pañcāsana and āvaraṇa worship, and then the Mahāgaṇeśapañcaratna (vv. 1–5 and phalaśruti), with the beginning of the first section damaged. It ends with "(remaining position blank), (p.18a blank, f.ई, उ is missing)". The second section described by IFP (Sadāśivāṣṭaka, Hālāsyanāthāṣṭaka, Liṅgāṣṭaka, Bhairavāṣṭaka, Śrīsthalīśvarāṣṭaka, Śivapañcākṣarastotra, Bhujaṅgapriyākalpaka, Kṣetrapālavāṣṭaka, etc.) is not in the e-text.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_svAtmArAma_AcArasAratantra_.title: Haṭhapradīpikā and Ācārasāratantra (with other texts)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_svAtmArAma_AcArasAratantra_.author: Svātmārāma
SA_MB_ilx_mb_svAtmArAma_AcArasAratantra_.summary: This e-text presents a diplomatic transcription of a composite Nepalese codex (NGMCP MS 3-325) combining Haṭhayoga and Kaula tantric ritual. It opens with an incomplete copy of Svātmārāma's Haṭhapradīpikā (beginning at 1.15 and concluding chapter 4), followed by the unedited Ācārasāratantra expounding transgressive Cīnācāra ritual and yoginī-vidhis. The codex concludes with the Samayācāra tract, the Pātravandanastotra from the Rudrayāmala praising the ritual wine cup, and the Ulūkakalpa detailing owl-based sorcery.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_svAtmArAma_AcArasAratantra_.attribution: The Haṭhapradīpikā is explicitly attributed in the colophons to Svātmārāmayogīndra. The Ācārasāratantra, Samayācāra, and Ulūkakalpa are anonymous Kaula/Tantric treatises. The Pātravandanastotra is attributed to the Rudrayāmalatantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_svAtmArAma_AcArasAratantra_.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (NGMCP) MS 3-325, Reel B 116/8
SA_MB_ilx_mb_svAtmArAma_AcArasAratantra_.coverage: partial — Transcription of composite manuscript NGMCP 3-325. Haṭhapradīpikā lacks 1.1–1.14 (starts abruptly at 1.15) but carries through chapter 4 (line 679). The remaining works (Ācārasāratantra, Samayācāra, Pātravandanastotra, Ulūkakalpa) are transcribed in full as preserved in this manuscript.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_tArAsahasranAmavyAkhyAbhidh.title: Tārāsahasranāmavyākhyābhidhārthacintāmaṇi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tArAsahasranAmavyAkhyAbhidh.author: Viśveśvara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tArAsahasranAmavyAkhyAbhidh.summary: A commentary by Viśveśvara, son of Lakṣmīdhara, on the Tārāsahasranāma (the thousand names of Tārā, beginning "kailāsaśikharāsīnam"). In its colophons it is called Girijābhidhārthacintāmaṇi and its final section is marked as the 12th mayūkha (ravimita). Each name is explained grammatically and etymologically, with citations from lexica, Purāṇas, tantras and śāstra works. The e-text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of a Jammu manuscript dated saṃvat 1942 (1885/86 CE).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tArAsahasranAmavyAkhyAbhidh.attribution: Viśveśvara, son of Lakṣmīdhara, names himself in the second maṅgala verse and in mayūkha colophons ("... budhasya tanūdbhavena viśveśvareṇa vihite girijābhidhārthacintāmaṇau ravimito 'yam agān mayūkhaḥ"). The closing verses say he wrote it while King Vājacandra ruled. Muktabodha's title "Tārāsahasranāmavyākhyābhidhārthacintāmaṇi" comes from the manuscript label. The author's own title is Girijābhidhārthacintāmaṇi.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tArAsahasranAmavyAkhyAbhidh.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 4972, Shri Raghunatha Temple Library, Jammu (121 folios, dated saṃvat 1942).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tArAsahasranAmavyAkhyAbhidh.coverage: complete — The 12th mayūkha colophon ("ravimito 'yam agān mayūkhaḥ") is present at the end, followed by three closing verses of the author and a scribal colophon dated saṃvat 1942, caitra kṛṣṇa caturdaśī (the title label has saṃ. 1941), on 121 folios. A final note calls it the "tārāsahasranāmaṭīkā".

SA_MB_ilx_mb_tatvazodhanam_M00655.title: Tattvaśodhanam
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tatvazodhanam_M00655.summary: Tattvaśodhanam is a short Śākta Tantric ritual manual outlining the procedures for ritual purification of both substances (dravyaśodhana) and cosmic principles (tattvaśodhana). It covers the veneration of the lineage of gurus, Gaṇapati, and Bhairava, the consecration of the water pot (kalaśapūjā), the invocation of solar, lunar, and fire energies into ritual vessels, and kuṇḍalinī meditation ascending from the mūlādhāra to the brahmarandhra. The manuscript concludes with a scribal colophon dated Saṃvat 1727 from Mallāragaḍha, followed by an opening fragment of a Dīpanāthaprakaraṇa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tatvazodhanam_M00655.attribution: A manual of ritual purification (tattvaśodhana and dravyaśodhana) within the Śākta/Tantric tradition; no author is mentioned in the manuscript.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tatvazodhanam_M00655.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript UPSS 2042 (Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan, Lucknow, 6 folios, dated [Vikrama] 1727), prepared by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute under the supervision of Anirban Dash (2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tatvazodhanam_M00655.coverage: complete — Complete text of Tattvaśodhanam across 6 folios, concluded by the scribal colophon dated Saṃvat 1727, followed by a brief incipit of an attached Dīpanāthaprakaraṇa.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_totakaula_kaulArcanadIpikA_.title: Kaulārcanadīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_totakaula_kaulArcanadIpikA_.summary: The Kaulārcanadīpikā is an anonymous Kaula Śākta ritual compendium (paddhati/nibandha) outlining the rites, principles, and obligations of the Kaula path (kulācāra, vīrācāra). It compiles scriptural citations from tantras including the Nirvāṇatantra, detailing esoteric worship, cakra rituals, and pañcatattva sādhana. At the close of the manuscript, a brief scribal appendix preserves selected verses on jñānayoga from the second paṭala of the Jñānatantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_totakaula_kaulArcanadIpikA_.attribution: The cataloguer mistook the scribe Tota Kaula ('likhitaṃ totakaulāni') for the author, an error reproduced in the Muktabodha digital library metadata. The text is an anonymous Kaula digest.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_totakaula_kaulArcanadIpikA_.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 5605gh (5605gha), Shri Raghunatha Temple Manuscripts Library, Jammu (dated Saṃvat 1947, copied by Tota Kaula).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_totakaula_kaulArcanadIpikA_.coverage: complete — Transcription of Jammu Raghunatha Temple MS 5605gha (104 folios), containing the complete Kaulārcanadīpikā followed by an appendix of several verses copied from paṭala 2 of the Jñānatantra.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_troTalottara_M00534.title: Troṭalottara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_troTalottara_M00534.summary: A scripture belonging to the Gāruḍa Tantra stream focused on the goddess Tvaritā and her nine-syllabled vidyā (navākṣarī). It details healing and anti-venom prayogas against snakebites and poisons, accompanied by magical operations, a twelve-verse hymn (Tvaritāstotra) in Śārdūlavikrīḍita metre, and a dhyānasūtra on the internal bodily nyāsa of the mantra syllables across the nine cakras.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_troTalottara_M00534.attribution: Revealed Śaiva/Gāruḍa tantric scripture ascribed to Śiva through Suparṇa (Garuḍa/Tārkṣya).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_troTalottara_M00534.edition: Manuscript transcription from National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript ms. 5-4844 (Reel B 126/15).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_troTalottara_M00534.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of manuscript witness NGMCP 5-4844 (Reel B 126/15), comprising the Troṭalottara/Tvaritājñānakalpa proper and its appended Tvaritāstotra and Sārdhanavākṣaryāsthānavinyāsadhyānasūtra.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_tyAgarAyaguru_parArthapUjAv.title: Parārthapūjāvidhi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tyAgarAyaguru_parArthapUjAv.author: Tyāgarāyaguru
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tyAgarAyaguru_parArthapUjAv.summary: The Parārthapūjāvidhi (also titled Nityapūjāvidhi on fol. 1a) is a Śaivasiddhānta ritual manual (paddhati) specifying daily communal temple worship (parārthapūjā). It details rites such as Kṣetrapālapūjā, dvārapūjā, awakening and procession of the mūrti, preliminary purification (sthalaśuddhi), Sūryapūjā, Vighneśvarapūjā, liṅga bathing (snapana), and bali offerings.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tyAgarAyaguru_parArthapUjAv.attribution: Folio 1a notes that the text is written in the author's own hand: 'araśūrī tyāgarāyaguru sva hastalukhitam' (sva-hastalikhitam), indicating Araśūrī Tyāgarāyaguru as either the compiler/author or the scribe.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tyAgarAyaguru_parArthapUjAv.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), MS 30482. Transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra. Pondicherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry and Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_tyAgarAyaguru_parArthapUjAv.coverage: partial — Lacks a concluding colophon or explicit for the work as a whole. The transcription covers the text on ff. 1a–42a of IFP manuscript 30482 (ff. 42b–43b are blank), ending on f. 42a without a final puṣpikā.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAJchAkalpalatA_M00641.title: Vāñchākalpalatā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAJchAkalpalatA_M00641.author: Buddhirāja
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAJchAkalpalatA_M00641.summary: The Vāñchākalpalatā is a Śākta-Gāṇapatya ritual manual compiled by Buddhirāja. It outlines the upasthāna, nyāsa, and recitation procedures for the Vāñchākalpalatā-Gaṇapati mantra (a syncretic Śrīvidyā-Gaṇapati rite), drawing on Atharvavedic mantras, the Kaumārīsaṃhitā, and the Prayogapārijāta. The transcript concludes with the short Saṃkaṣṭanāśanagaṇeśastotra appended from the Nāradapurāṇa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAJchAkalpalatA_M00641.attribution: Authored by Buddhirāja as stated in verse 1. The work incorporates mantras and rites associated with the Atharvaveda, Kaumārīsaṃhitā, and Prayogapārijāta.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAJchAkalpalatA_M00641.edition: Diplomatic transcription of MS 1309, Shri Raghunatha Temple MSS Library, Jammu (transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, transcript M00641, 2023, unpublished).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAJchAkalpalatA_M00641.coverage: complete — Text of the ritual manual as preserved in Jammu MS 1309, followed by the Saṃkaṣṭanāśanagaṇeśastotra from the Nāradapurāṇa.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAtulAgama_I00012.title: Vātulāgama (selected chapters)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAtulAgama_I00012.summary: The Vātulāgama is one of the twenty-eight Siddhānta Śaiva mūlāgamas. This e-text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of IFP palm-leaf manuscript RE 26381, preserving sections on temple ritual, primarily the Nityārcanavidhipaṭala, liṅga worship, festival rites (utsava), and expiatory rites (prāyaścitta). It concludes with a Tamil scribal colophon recording its completion by Ṣaṇmukha Gurukkal.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAtulAgama_I00012.attribution: Revealed scriptural text traditionally enumerated as one of the 28 Siddhānta Śaiva mūlāgamas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAtulAgama_I00012.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) palm-leaf manuscript RE 26381 (63 folios), prepared by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. I00012), 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vAtulAgama_I00012.coverage: partial — Transcribes 63 folios of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 26381, containing sections on śivaliṅgārcana, the Nityārcanavidhipaṭala, utsava, and prāyaścitta.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIracUDAmaNi_M00656.title: Vīracūḍāmaṇi with Muṇḍamālātantra (Muṇḍamālātantra: paṭalas 1–3 and beginning of 4)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIracUDAmaNi_M00656.summary: A manuscript with two Śākta tantras. The Vīracūḍāmaṇi (11 paṭalas) gives the vīrācāra worship of Mahānīlasarasvatī/Tārā: morning rites, haṃsa-sādhana, offering japa to the deities of the cakras, dīkṣā, pūjā, mantroddhāra, homa and kāmya rites. It is followed by the first three and a half paṭalas of a Muṇḍamālātantra, on the mahāvidyās, the akṣamālā, the four great pīṭhas and balidāna, which breaks off.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIracUDAmaNi_M00656.attribution: Both are anonymous Śākta tantras in Śiva–Devī dialogue. The Vīracūḍāmaṇi deals with the krama of Mahānīla(sarasvatī)/Tārā/Ekajaṭā in vīrācāra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIracUDAmaNi_M00656.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of MS 4865, Raghunath Temple Library, Jammu.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIracUDAmaNi_M00656.coverage: partial — Jammu, Raghunath Temple MS 4865. The Vīracūḍāmaṇi has paṭala colophons 1–11. The 11th ("iti °cūḍāmaṇau kāmyanitya° ekādaśaḥ paṭalaḥ") has no explicit samāpti, so whether the work is complete cannot be established. The Muṇḍamālātantra follows with paṭala 1 (mahāvidyās), paṭala 2 (akṣamālā), paṭala 3 (pīṭhas, abbreviated colophon "i° mu° tṛ° pa°") and the beginning of paṭala 4 (balidāna). It breaks off mid-sentence ("surādānena deveśi mahā..."). ilx_skt: "Completeness: incomplete".

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIratantra_M00613.title: Vīratantra (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIratantra_M00613.author: Vīracannabasava
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIratantra_M00613.summary: A late Vīraśaiva theological and polemical treatise composed in mixed verse and prose by Vīracannabasava of Sudhāpurī, writing within the lineage of the 15th–16th century saint Tōṭada Siddhēśvara and Murigā Śāntavīra. The work expounds classical Vīraśaiva doctrine, focusing on the eight protective shields (aṣṭāvaraṇa), five conducts (pañcācāra), six stages (ṣaṭsthala), and the superiority of personal liṅga worship (iṣṭaliṅga) over temple idols (sthiraliṅga). It supports its positions by citing extensive passages from Purāṇic and Tantric/Āgamic texts such as the Śāṅkarasaṃhitā, Pārameśvara, Kūrmapurāṇa, and Sūtasaṃhitā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIratantra_M00613.attribution: The frame verses (vv. 3–7) praise Toṭada Siddheśvara and Murigā Śāntavīra Yati, and present the guru Vīracannabasava(ārya) ("vīracaṃna basavāya edhate", v. 5) answering the paṇḍita Muragaya. The author is therefore Vīracannabasava or a pupil recording his teaching. The attribution rests only on these verses.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIratantra_M00613.coverage: partial — The e-text begins with the maṅgala and frame verses and the thesis on the supremacy of the Vīraśaiva, supported by quotations from Śāṅkarasaṃhitā, Pārameśvara, Kūrma and Sūtasaṃhitā. It continues through arguments on aṣṭāvaraṇa, pañcācāra and ṣaṭsthala, and on iṣṭaliṅga versus sthiraliṅga worship. It breaks off mid-sentence ("tathā ca jaṅgamatattvasya sarvābhya..."). ilx_skt: "Completeness: incomplete".

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAcArapradIpikA_M006.title: Vīraśaivācārapradīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAcArapradIpikA_M006.author: Gurudeva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAcArapradIpikA_M006.summary: The Vīraśaivācārapradīpikā is a 38-chapter ritual and doctrinal compendium of the Vīraśaiva tradition composed by Gurudeva.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAcArapradIpikA_M006.coverage: complete — Complete in 38 chapters; ends with the colophon of chapter 38 (aṣṭatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAgama_M00610.title: Vīraśaivāgama (incomplete: paṭalas 1–12 and beginning of 13)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAgama_M00610.summary: An anonymous Vīraśaiva scripture cast as a dialogue between Devī and Śiva, whose colophons assign it to a 'Sahasrakoṭisaṃhitā'. It opens with a classification of Śaiva and other sectarian traditions and declares Vīraśaivism superior to them. Its chapters set out the stages (sthala) of Vīraśaiva devotion and the doctrine and worship of the prāṇaliṅga and its six petals (ṣaḍdala). The surviving part of the last chapter deals with the preparation and wearing of sacred ash (bhasma).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAgama_M00610.attribution: Anonymous revealed Vīraśaiva scripture, cast as a dialogue between Devī and Īśvara. The chapter colophons place it in a 'Sahasrakoṭisaṃhitā' (e.g. seg. 190–191: 'iti vīraśaivāgame sahasrakoṭisaṃhitāyāṃ prāṇaliṅgasaṃbandhānāṃ bhaktistalaṃ nāma prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAgama_M00610.edition: Unpublished: transcript T00195 of the Institut Français de Pondichéry, copied from Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Madras, MS D. 5497. Not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivAgama_M00610.coverage: partial — Paṭalas 1–12 complete with colophons (1 bhaktisthala, 2 māheśvarasthala, 3 prasādasthala, 4 prāṇaliṅgadala, 5 śaraṇasthala, 6 śivaliṅgaikya/ṣaḍdala, 7 niṣkala prāṇaliṅga, 8 vīrāgamarahasya, 9 niṣkalaprāṇaliṅganirṇaya, 10 jñānaliṅgavidhi, 11 [title damaged], 12 darśaviśeṣamahimāvidhi); the 13th, on sacred ash, breaks off without colophon (seg. 1039–1183), followed by the transcriber's note '[asamāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ asaṃpūrṇaśca]' (seg. 1184). The full extent of the work is unknown.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.title: Vīraśaivasiddhāntottarakaumudī (incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.author: Vīrabhadrārādhya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.summary: The Vīraśaivasiddhāntottarakaumudī is a Vīraśaiva theological and ritual manual (paddhati) composed by Vīrabhadrārādhya. Drawing on Śaiva scriptures and āgamic traditions, it details the descent and role of the Gaṇendras, the path of bhakti, initiation (ṣaḍadhvadīkṣā), the bearing of the liṅga (liṅgadhāraṇa), and daily ritual observances (dinakarma) including sandhyopāsanā, bhasmasnāna, and agnikārya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.attribution: The author Vīrabhadrārādhya identifies himself in vv. 14–17 as the son of Candraśekhara and Annapūrṇā, of the Bhāradvāja gotra and the lineage of Udbhavārādhya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00342 (copied from Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Madras, MS D. 5495)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.coverage: partial — Incomplete; covers gaṇendravibhava, initiation, sandhyā, and morning homa up to śivāgni meditation, ending with '|| [asaṃpūrṇo'yaṃ gnanthaḥ] ||'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.title: Vīraśaivasiddhāntottarakaumudī (Śivapūjāvidhi)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.summary: The Vīraśaivasiddhāntottarakaumudī is a Vīraśaiva ritual and theological manual. This section, the Śivapūjāvidhi, details the liturgical sequence and inner significance of worshipping Śiva through the Guru, Liṅga, and Jaṅgama. It explains the reception and spiritual efficacy of pādodaka (sacred foot-wash) and prasāda, and expounds the performance of the ritual upacāras in association with the Pañcabrahma mantras.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.attribution: A passage cites Somānārya ('iti somānāryeṇa bahudhā praṇītaṃ miśrārpaṇāyām'), but the text as a whole is cataloged anonymously in manuscript repositories such as GOML MS D5496.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) transcript T00343 (copied from Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Madras, MS D5496).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vIrazaivasiddhAntottarakaum.coverage: partial — Complete text of the Śivapūjāvidhi section (final colophon: 'iti śrīvīraśaivasiddhāntottarakomudyāṃ śivapūjāvidhiḥ samāptaḥ').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vedAntasAravIrazaivacintAma.title: Vedāntasāravīraśaivacintāmaṇi (Uttarakhaṇḍa)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vedAntasAravIrazaivacintAma.author: Niṣṭhūra Nañjaṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vedAntasAravIrazaivacintAma.summary: The Vedāntasāravīraśaivacintāmaṇi is an influential late medieval/early modern scholastic compendium of Vīraśaiva doctrine, philosophy, and orthopraxy by Niṣṭhūra Nañjaṇa. Drawing on Upaniṣads, Śaivāgamas, Purāṇas, and earlier authorities like the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi, the Uttarakhaṇḍa expounds Vīraśaiva theological principles (liṅgāṅgasāmarasya, ṣaṭsthala), daily conduct, initiation, and funerary rituals (anteṣṭi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vedAntasAravIrazaivacintAma.attribution: Colophons uniformly attribute the text to Niṣṭhūra Nañjaṇācārya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vedAntasAravIrazaivacintAma.edition: Vedāntasāravīraśaivacintāmaṇi of Niṣṭhūra Nañjaṇācārya, Solapur: Vīraśaivaliṅgibrāhmaṇagranthamālā, 1905.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vedAntasAravIrazaivacintAma.coverage: partial — Uttarakhaṇḍa only (prakaraṇas 1–21); the Pūrvakhaṇḍa is not contained in this file.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vighnezvaramUlamantra_I0004.title: Vighneśvaramūlamantra
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vighnezvaramUlamantra_I0004.summary: A South Indian ritual and liturgical compendium (arcanā-saṅgraha) transcribed directly from IFP palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 32409. Opening with the Vighneśvaramūlamantra and Vighneśvarasahasranāma, it includes sahasranāmas, triśatīs, and aṣṭottaraśatanāmastotras/nāmāvalis for Gaṇeśa, Subrahmaṇya, Devī, Lalitā, Śrīvidyā, Sabhāpati, Vīrabhadra, and Bhairava.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vighnezvaramUlamantra_I0004.attribution: An anonymous liturgical compilation of mantras, sahasranāmas, and nāmāvalis for Śaiva and Śākta temple/domestic worship.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vighnezvaramUlamantra_I0004.edition: Manuscript RE 32409, Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), Pondicherry. Diplomatic e-text prepared by the IFP Indology team under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; published digitally by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. I00040), 2024.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vighnezvaramUlamantra_I0004.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32409 (digital frames p. 1 to p. 220b).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vimalAnanda_tArAbhaktitaraG.title: Tārābhaktitaraṅgiṇī (taraṅga 13: Saptaśatikāvidhāna)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vimalAnanda_tArAbhaktitaraG.author: Vimalānanda
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vimalAnanda_tArAbhaktitaraG.summary: The Tārābhaktitaraṅgiṇī is a Śākta tantric ritual work composed by Vimalānanda. This e-text transcribes the Saptaśatikāvidhāna section, which treats ritual procedures, mantras (such as the Navārṇavamantra), and diagrams (including the Ghaṭārgalāyantra) associated with the Saptaśatī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vimalAnanda_tArAbhaktitaraG.attribution: Attributed to Vimalānanda in the colophon.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vimalAnanda_tArAbhaktitaraG.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Manuscript no. 4930, Shri Raghunatha Temple MSS Library, Jammu (107 folios).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vimalAnanda_tArAbhaktitaraG.coverage: partial — Preserves the Saptaśatikāvidhāna portion of the Tārābhaktitaraṅgiṇī, copied in a 107-folio manuscript; concluding with the colophon 'itivimalānaṃdaviracitāṃtārābhaktitaraṃgīṇīsthasaptaśatikāvidhānaṃsamāptam'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_virUpAkSapaNcazikA_M00535.title: Virūpākṣapañcāśikā with Vivṛti
SA_MB_ilx_mb_virUpAkSapaNcazikA_M00535.author: Virūpākṣanātha, Vidyācakravartin
SA_MB_ilx_mb_virUpAkSapaNcazikA_M00535.summary: The Virūpākṣapañcāśikā is a concise South Indian non-dual Śaiva treatise attributed to Virūpākṣanātha, deeply rooted in Pratyabhijñā and Trika philosophy. Arranged in four sections (skandhas), the work expounds that the objective universe constitutes the body of supreme consciousness (viśvaśarīratva), the ultimate unity of consciousness and manifest reality (prakāśaikātmya), reflexive awareness (pratyavamarśa), and mystical attainments (vibhūti/siddhi). This e-text features the root verses embedded within the authoritative Vivṛti commentary composed by Vidyācakravartin.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_virUpAkSapaNcazikA_M00535.attribution: The root kārikās are attributed to Virūpākṣanātha (Śrīvirūpākṣa). The Vivṛti commentary is by Mahāmāheśvara Vidyācakravartin.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_virUpAkSapaNcazikA_M00535.edition: Trivandrum: Travancore Government Press, 1910, ed. T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_virUpAkSapaNcazikA_M00535.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all four skandhas of the Virūpākṣapañcāśikā, and Vidyācakravartin's Vivṛti commentary up to the concluding benedictory verses.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_viraktotpattikriyAlakSaNa_M.title: Viraktotpattikriyālakṣaṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_viraktotpattikriyAlakSaNa_M.summary: A Vīraśaiva theological and ritual compendium expounding the origins, characteristics, and rites of the virakta (renunciant) and nirābhāri ascetics. Drawing upon Śaivāgamic sources alongside traditional accounts of Prabhu Deva (Allama Prabhu), Basaveśvara, and Cannabasava, it sets forth ascetic conduct within the ṣaṭsthala schema, culminating in rules for dīkṣā and the veneration of Guru and Jaṅgama.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_viraktotpattikriyAlakSaNa_M.attribution: Traditional Vīraśaiva compendium citing Āgamic scriptures regarding ascetic initiation and conduct.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_viraktotpattikriyAlakSaNa_M.coverage: unclear — The catalog label in ilx_skt indicates 'fragments' (completeness notes: 'excerpt').

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vivekacintAmaNi_M00620.title: Vivekacintāmaṇi (pariccheda 1 and fragment of pariccheda 2)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vivekacintAmaNi_M00620.author: Liṅgarāja
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vivekacintAmaNi_M00620.summary: The Vivekacintāmaṇi (or Śrīliṅgarājīya) is an encyclopedic Sanskrit prose and verse adaptation of Nijaguṇa Śivayogī's Kannaḍa classic. Produced under King Liṅgarāja, it synthesizes Vīraśaiva thought with orthodox and heterodox philosophical doxography, Āgamic and Vedic taxonomies, cosmology, cosmography, ritual categories, and yoga.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vivekacintAmaNi_M00620.attribution: A Sanskrit adaptation of the Kannaḍa Vīraśaiva encyclopedic work of the same title by Nijaguṇa Śivayogī. The colophon attributes the work to Liṅgarāja.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vivekacintAmaNi_M00620.edition: Vivekacintāmaṇi of Liṅgarāja. Solapur: Vīraśaiva Liṅgī-Brāhmaṇa Granthamālā, 1906.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vivekacintAmaNi_M00620.coverage: partial — Contains the complete pariccheda 1 (lines 1–2276) and an opening portion of pariccheda 2, breaking off at line 2434 with '[apūrṇa]'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSAntyeSTi_I00048.title: Viśeṣāntyeṣṭi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSAntyeSTi_I00048.summary: The Viśeṣāntyeṣṭi is an anonymous South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual (prayoga/paddhati) detailing post-mortem rites (antyeṣṭi) and purification of the cosmic paths (adhvaśuddhi) for deceased initiates holding the viśeṣadīkṣā level of initiation. It details the preparation of the corpse, transport to the cremation ground, configuration of the fire pit (kuṇḍa) and sthaṇḍila, nyāsa procedures, and liberation rituals according to Śaivāgamic practice.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSAntyeSTi_I00048.attribution: Anonymous manual of Śaiva funeral rites based on Śaivāgama traditions.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSAntyeSTi_I00048.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript bundle RE30586, transcribed by the IFP Indology team under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra; published online by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog I00048).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSAntyeSTi_I00048.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the Viśeṣāntyeṣṭi text from IFP MS RE30586 (pp. 4b–40b), followed by concluding mantra and nyāsa formulas through p. 42a.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSArthaprakAzikA_M00614.title: Viśeṣārthaprakāśikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSArthaprakAzikA_M00614.author: Māyideva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSArthaprakAzikA_M00614.summary: The Viśeṣārthaprakāśikā is a Vīraśaiva theological and ritual manual in verse composed by Māyideva. Structured in five chapters (adhikaraṇas) as a dialogue between guru and disciple, it covers initiation (ṣaṭsthalabrahmopadeśa), the ritual procedure for Liṅga worship (śivaliṅgārcana), the nature of prasāda, spiritual cultivation and mantra repetition (puraścaraṇa), and final liberation/bodily exit (dehāvasāna).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSArthaprakAzikA_M00614.attribution: Attributed in colophons to Māyideva (author of the Śivānubhavasūtra).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_vizeSArthaprakAzikA_M00614.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all five adhikaraṇas as enumerated in opening verses 5–7: 1. Brahmopadeśavidhi, 2. Śivaliṅgārcanakrama, 3. Prasādasadbhāva, 4. Ṣaṭsthalabrahmapuraścaraṇa, and 5. Dehāvasāna.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_yatidharmabodhinIvyAkhyA_I0.title: Yatidharmabodhinīvyākhyā (fragment)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yatidharmabodhinIvyAkhyA_I0.author: Nīlakaṇṭha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yatidharmabodhinIvyAkhyA_I0.summary: The Yatidharmabodhinīvyākhyā is an ascetic manual detailing the rules, observances, and ritual obligations of renunciants (yatidharma). It addresses qualifications for saṃnyāsa, guru worship, the characteristics and handling of the ascetic staff (daṇḍa) and mudrās, and the transfer of sacred fires for an āhitāgni renunciant. This transcript comprises an incomplete fragment spanning folios 3b to 14a of IFP manuscript RE 31344.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yatidharmabodhinIvyAkhyA_I0.attribution: According to the TEI header description, the work is authored by Nīlakaṇṭhayati.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yatidharmabodhinIvyAkhyA_I0.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript bundle RE 31344 (unpublished manuscript transcript, 14 folios).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yatidharmabodhinIvyAkhyA_I0.coverage: fragment — Preserves folios 3b–14a of manuscript IFP RE 31344; breaks off incompletely on f. 14a, line 7 in the section discussing the rites of an āhitāgni entering saṃnyāsa.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogajAgama_I00015.title: Yogajāgama (selected paṭalas)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogajAgama_I00015.summary: The Yogajāgama is traditionally enumerated as the second of the twenty-eight Mūlāgamas of the Śaivasiddhānta canon, categorized as one of the ten Śivabhedas. The text deals primarily with kriyā and caryā aspects of Śaiva temple ritual and architecture, including temple planning (prāsādalakṣaṇa), iconometry (pratimālakṣaṇa), the installation of attendant deities (parivārasthāpana), liṅga installation (liṅgasthāpana), fire rituals (agnikārya), and initiation rites (dīkṣā). This e-text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of an incomplete palm-leaf manuscript preserved at the French Institute of Pondicherry (IFP MS 39691).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogajAgama_I00015.attribution: Canonical Śaivasiddhānta scripture traditionally classified as the second of the 28 Mūlāgamas (specifically one of the ten Śivabhedas), revealed by Śiva (Paraśiva) to Sudhākhya, Vibhu, and Bhasma.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogajAgama_I00015.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP MS 39691, preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry; transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra (Pondicherry: IFP & Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023, catalog no. I00015; unpublished digital transcript).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogajAgama_I00015.coverage: partial — Incomplete manuscript bundle containing selected paṭalas/sections from IFP MS 39691 (ff. 1a–62a), treating parivārasthāpanavidhi, ācāryalakṣaṇa, vighneśasthāpana, liṅgasthāpana, ratnaliṅgasthāpana, pratimālakṣaṇa, tālasaṅkhyā, śūlalakṣaṇa, dhvajārohaṇa/pavitrārohaṇa, maṇḍalavidhāna, phalapākavidhi, pañcākṣara, vibhavaniścaya, naivedyavidhi, agnikārya, kuṇḍalakṣaṇa, śāntihoma, dīkṣālakṣaṇa, and prāsādalakṣaṇa.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogasArasamuccaya_M00503.title: Yogasārasamuccaya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogasArasamuccaya_M00503.summary: The Yogasārasamuccaya is an unpublished Śaiva/Tantric yoga treatise in nine chapters (paṭalas) preserved in Nepalese manuscripts, transmitted as part of the Akulāgama tradition. Structured as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī, it describes ṣaḍaṅgayoga, prāṇāyāma, subtle anatomy, mantras, and the duties of life stages (caturāśrama).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogasArasamuccaya_M00503.attribution: Framed as an īśvarapārvatīsaṃvāda belonging to the Akulāgama tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogasArasamuccaya_M00503.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives, Kathmandu / NGMCP MS 1-9 (Reel no. B 115/6), dated NS 791 (1671 CE); transcribed by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute staff under the supervision of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski (2021).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_yogasArasamuccaya_M00503.coverage: complete — Complete in 9 paṭalas, concluding with the chapter 9 colophon (caturāśramādikathana) and a scribal colophon dated Nepāla Saṃvat 791 (1671 CE).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zabdArthacintAmaNi_M00645.title: Śabdārthacintāmaṇi (incomplete: breaks off in the closing verses)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zabdArthacintAmaNi_M00645.author: Premanidhi Pantha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zabdArthacintAmaNi_M00645.summary: The Śabdārthacintāmaṇi is a commentary by Premanidhi Pantha on the Śāradātilaka, a compendium of mantraśāstra. It provides explanations, ritual procedures, mantras, and citations from tantric texts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zabdArthacintAmaNi_M00645.attribution: The colophon verses give the author's family and origin: 'yasyodyotamatī satī guṇavatī mātā pitomāpattir nāma premanidhīti pathakulabhūḥ kūrmmācalo janmabhūḥ ... vārāṇasīvāsabhūḥ' (colophon in catalog metadata). He is Premanidhi of the Pantha family, son of Umāpati, born in Kūrmācala and resident in Vārāṇasī. He names himself in the opening ('premanidher dvijāddhi', seg. 7) and closing verses, and worships Kārtavīryārjuna ('kṛtavīryātmajatanuṃ', 'kṛtavīryanaṃdana').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zabdArthacintAmaNi_M00645.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Raghunath Temple Library, Jammu, manuscript 1480k.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zabdArthacintAmaNi_M00645.coverage: partial — The e-text comments on the Śāradātilaka and breaks off mid-word in the author's concluding verses (ending 'kvāpi premanidhir jaḍādhipatiko ... prodūṣaṇā thaṃ spṛ'). Muktabodha notes it as 'incomplete' lacking explicit and final colophon.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivabhuSaNam_I00033.title: Śaivabhūṣaṇa with Tamil commentary
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivabhuSaNam_I00033.summary: The Śaivabhūṣaṇa is a South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta ritual handbook (paddhati) consisting of 355 Sanskrit verses accompanied by an extensive bilingual Tamil prose commentary. It synthesizes prescriptions from the Kriyāpāda of the Śaivāgamas on topics including initiation (dīkṣā), the seven classes of Śaivas, qualifications of guru and disciple, daily rites (nityakarma), sūryapūjā, snapanavidhi, homa, temple festivals (utsava), and funerary rites (antyeṣṭi).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivabhuSaNam_I00033.attribution: Both root text and Tamil prose commentary are anonymous.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivabhuSaNam_I00033.edition: Pondicherry: Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) and Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2024. Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 30704 (137 folios).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivabhuSaNam_I00033.coverage: complete — Text of 355 verses with continuous Tamil commentary transcribed from all 137 folios of IFP MS RE 30704.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivarahasyam_I00045.title: Śaivarahasya (selected stotras and rituals)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivarahasyam_I00045.summary: A liturgical and devotional compilation transcribed from damaged palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 32601 at the Institut Français de Pondichéry. Written in Grantha and Telugu scripts, it brings together Śaiva, Śākta, and Saura devotional stotras and ritual sequences, including the Lalitāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī, an Umāmaheśvara stotra from the Śivarahasya, Vighneśvarastotra, Indrākṣīstotra, Ādityahṛdaya, Mārgasahāyāṣṭaka, Mīnākṣyaṣṭaka, Śivakavaca, and Rudrapūjā rites. The manuscript bundle reflects South Indian personal and domestic worship collections.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivarahasyam_I00045.attribution: A devotional compendium preserved in a multi-text South Indian palm-leaf manuscript bundle.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivarahasyam_I00045.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript bundle RE 32601 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), transcribed by the IFP Indology team under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra, digital publication by Muktabodha Indological Research Institute (catalog no. I00045, released 2023/2025).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaivarahasyam_I00045.coverage: partial — Diplomatic transcription of damaged palm-leaf manuscript bundle IFP RE 32601 (55 folios, Grantha and Telugu scripts), containing extensive lacunae, illegible passages, and blank leaves.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaktimaNTapapUjA_I00037.title: Śaktimaṇṭapapūjā with appended nyāsas (incomplete at end)
