SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaktimaNTapapUjA_I00037.summary: An anonymous South Indian ritual manual of the late Śaiva Siddhānta for worship of the Goddess in the sacrificial pavilion (śaktimaṇṭapa / śaktiyāga). It prescribes the preparation of the pavilion and vessels (vardhanī), the worship of the four doorways and their toraṇas (caturdvārapūjā), the altar (vedikārcana) and the āvaraṇa deities, and the invocation of Gaurī. Appended are several nyāsa procedures: Dūtikānyāsa, Devīśrīkaṇṭhanyāsa, Devīṣaḍadhvanyāsa, kalānyāsa and Śrīkaṇṭhamātṛkānyāsa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaktimaNTapapUjA_I00037.attribution: An anonymous South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta ritual compilation preserved in manuscript form.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaktimaNTapapUjA_I00037.edition: Unpublished: transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry manuscript bundle RE10781 (62 folios, 5 lines per folio). Not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zaktimaNTapapUjA_I00037.coverage: partial — The main text, the Śaktimaṇṭapapūjāvidhi, is complete (colophon at seg. 622). The appended Dūtikānyāsa, Devīśrīkaṇṭhanyāsa and Devīṣaḍadhvanyāsa also end with closing formulas; the last ends at seg. 810 with 'ṣaḍoddhvā [= ṣaḍadhvā] samāptaḥ'. The manuscript then gives the vaktra- and kalānyāsas and a Śrīkaṇṭhamātṛkānyāsa (seg. 843ff.), which breaks off mid-formula on p. 59b / f. 55a (seg. 879). The rest of the bundle (pp. 59b–62b) is blank. The IFP description calls the Devīṣaḍadhvanyāsa the incomplete section. The e-text shows that it is the following mātṛkānyāsa that is cut off.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNaya_M00674.title: Śambhunirṇaya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNaya_M00674.summary: The Śambhunirṇaya (also known as the Śambhunirṇayatantra) is an influential Śāmbhava Kaula tantric ritual work divided into 26 avacchedas. It expounds initiation, maṇḍala layout, mantra pīṭhas, and the ritual framework of the Śāmbhava tradition, mentioning lineages and teachers such as Lakuleśin and Kroḍamuni. It circulated widely in South India, inspiring commentaries such as Śivānandamuni's Śambhunirṇayadīpikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNaya_M00674.attribution: Scriptural Śāmbhava Kaula treatise, framed as a dialogue between Śambhu and the Devī (Himātmajā).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNaya_M00674.edition: Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (GOML), Chennai, MS No. R. 3203(c) (paper, Devanāgarī script). Unpublished manuscript transcription.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNaya_M00674.coverage: complete — Complete text in 26 avacchedas, matching pages 77–131 of GOML MS R. 3203(c).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNayadIpaka_M00675.title: Śambhunirṇayadīpikā (avacchedas 1–8)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNayadIpaka_M00675.author: Śivānandanātha
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNayadIpaka_M00675.summary: The Śambhunirṇayadīpikā is a Tantric commentary by Śivānandanātha on the Śambhunirṇaya (also known as the Sahasrārdhaśāsana or Mateśamata), an esoteric ritual work framed in 26 avacchedas. The surviving commentary covers maṇḍala construction, ritual procedures, the worship of naveśvaras and dūtīs, homa, therapeutic rituals, and contemplative yogic practices (dhyāna), breaking off incomplete during the discussion of śaktidhyāna in the eighth section.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNayadIpaka_M00675.attribution: In the opening verses and colophons, the author Śivānandanātha identifies himself as disciple of Vidyānandanātha, son/disciple of Pratiṣṭhānanda, and in the lineage/grandson of Ajeśa.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNayadIpaka_M00675.edition: Unpublished transcript: Government Oriental Manuscripts Library (GOML), Madras, MS R. 3203(c), pp. 132–165. Transcribed in 1919–1920 from a manuscript belonging to M. R. Ry. Tippan Nambūripād of Ponnurekottamana, Perumbavoor, Travancore state.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zambhunirNayadIpaka_M00675.coverage: partial — Contains introductory verses outlining the 26 avacchedas of the root work and breaks off incomplete in the text (around p. 165, discussing śaktidhyāna).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zatarudriyabhASya_I00016.title: Śatarudriyabhāṣya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zatarudriyabhASya_I00016.author: Abhinavaśaṅkara
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zatarudriyabhASya_I00016.summary: A commentary on the Śatarudriya (Rudrādhyāya, Taittirīyasaṃhitā 4.5) attributed to Abhinavaśaṅkara. The work interprets the Vedic mantras in accordance with Advaita Vedānta and Śaiva traditions, quoting from Upaniṣads, Purāṇas, and Śaiva literature, and provides the ritual context, dhyāna, and application for each mantra.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zatarudriyabhASya_I00016.attribution: The colophon explicitly attributes the text to Paramahaṃsaparivrājakasārvabhauma Advaitavidyāpratiṣṭhāpana Abhinavaśaṅkara (advaitavidyāpratiṣṭhāpanābhinavaśaṅkarabhagavadbhiḥ kṛtaṃ śrī rudrabhāṣyaṃ sampūrṇam).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zatarudriyabhASya_I00016.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription from palm-leaf manuscript IFP 12684 (Institut Français de Pondichéry, 102 folios), transcribed by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra, Pondicherry, 2023.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zatarudriyabhASya_I00016.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on the eleven anuvākas of the Śatarudriya / Rudrādhyāya (Taittirīyasaṃhitā 4.5), spanning folios 1 to 100/102 in the manuscript.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitadarpaNa_M00606.title: Śivādvaitadarpaṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitadarpaNa_M00606.author: Śivānubhava Śivācārya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitadarpaNa_M00606.summary: The Śivādvaitadarpaṇa is a Vīraśaiva / Śivādvaita treatise by Śivānubhava Śivācārya. It expounds Śaktiviśiṣṭādvaita and Śivādvaita doctrines in connection with the Brahmasūtras and Upaniṣads, referencing concepts such as the jīva, ānandamaya, dīkṣā, liṅga, and mahāvākyas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitadarpaNa_M00606.attribution: Author: Śivānubhava Śivācārya, disciple of Ciddhana (Cidghana) Śivācārya, connected with the Pūvvallī Pañcavarṇa Mahāmaṭha (final colophon).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitadarpaNa_M00606.coverage: complete — Work ends with 'iti caturthaparicchedaḥ' and the final colophon 'śrīśivānubhavaśivācāryaviracitaśrīśivādvaitadarpaṇaḥ sampūrṇaḥ'. Seg. 0 begins with 'atha dvitīyaparicchedasthaviṣayāḥ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitimaJjarI_M00607.title: Śivādvaitamañjarī and Śaivasiddhāntadīpikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitimaJjarI_M00607.author: Svaprabhānanda, Śaṃbhudeva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitimaJjarI_M00607.summary: A composite e-text containing two Vīraśaiva/Śaiva philosophical treatises. The first, Svaprabhānanda's Śivādvaitamañjarī, defends Vīraśaiva Śivādvaita against Kevalādvaita Vedānta, opening with an examination and refutation of Śaṅkara's Adhyāsabhāṣya. The second, Śaṃbhudeva's Śaivasiddhāntadīpikā (also designated Pāśupatamataprakaraṇa), provides an exposition of Śaiva and Pāśupata doctrine, explaining the five bonds (pāśapañcaka), the attributes of released souls, and Śiva's fivefold cosmic activity (pañcakṛtya).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitimaJjarI_M00607.attribution: The first treatise concludes with the colophon attributing it to Svaprabhānanda (segment 1366: '...svaprabhānandaviraciteyaṃ śivādvaitamañjarī'). The second treatise concludes with colophons naming Sarvārthaśaṃbhudeva (segments 1846–1848).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAdvaitimaJjarI_M00607.coverage: complete — Contains both treatises complete: Svaprabhānanda's Śivādvaitamañjarī (segments 1–1366) and Śaṃbhudeva's Śaivasiddhāntadīpikā (Pāśupatamataprakaraṇa, segments 1367–1848).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAgrayogin_kriyAdIpikA_I0.title: Kriyādīpikā (paṭalas 1–6) with extracts from the Varuṇapaddhati, Kriyākramadyotikā and other ritual texts
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAgrayogin_kriyAdIpikA_I0.author: Śivāgrayogin, Varuṇaśiva, Aghoraśiva
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAgrayogin_kriyAdIpikA_I0.summary: A Śaiva Siddhānta ritual manual attributed to Śivāgrayogin, along with other ritual texts and extracts.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAgrayogin_kriyAdIpikA_I0.attribution: Colophon: 'iti varṇāśramamācāryavaryaśaivaparipālakaśivāgrayogiviracitāyāṃ kriyādīpikāyāṃ śaucācamanasnānasai(śai)vasandhyānuṣṭhānavidhirnāma prathamaḥ paṭalaḥ /// iti vātulākhye mahātantre jñānapāde jñānapūjāvidhipaṭalaḥ samāptaḥ /// iti śārā(ra)dātilake trayodaśaḥ paṭalaḥ'.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAgrayogin_kriyAdIpikA_I0.edition: Unpublished: transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf manuscript RE 15527. Not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAgrayogin_kriyAdIpikA_I0.coverage: partial — Marked incomplete/fragments in ilx_skt catalog metadata. Transcription ends with '(end of re 15527)'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAnanda_yogacintAmaNi_M00.title: Yogacintāmaṇi
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAnanda_yogacintAmaNi_M00.author: Śivānandasarasvatī
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAnanda_yogacintAmaNi_M00.summary: The Yogacintāmaṇi by Śivānandasarasvatī is a massive four-chapter compendium harmonizing classical Pātañjala Yoga, Advaita Vedānta, and Haṭhayoga traditions. It is an encyclopedic compilation of citations from works on yoga (including Yogasūtra, Purāṇas, Upaniṣads, and Haṭhayoga treatises), on which the author comments.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAnanda_yogacintAmaNi_M00.attribution: Colophons identify the author as Śivānandasarasvatī, disciple of Rāmacandra Sadānanda Sarasvatī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAnanda_yogacintAmaNi_M00.edition: Transcription of National Archives Kathmandu / NGMCP manuscript 1-1337 (reel no. B 39/5).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivAnanda_yogacintAmaNi_M00.coverage: complete — Complete in 4 paricchedas; line records: 'yogacintāmaṇau caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptaścāyaṃ yogacintāmaṇirgranthaḥ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivagaNapatisubrahmaNyaprat.title: Śivasubrahmaṇyagaṇapatipratiṣṭhā (incomplete: Śiva section and opening of the Subrahmaṇya section)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivagaNapatisubrahmaNyaprat.summary: An anonymous late Śaiva Siddhānta ritual compilation for installing (pratiṣṭhā) images of Śiva, Subrahmaṇya and Gaṇapati, preserved in an IFP palm-leaf bundle. The transcribed part covers Śiva rites and starts Subrahmaṇya rites, drawing extracts from texts such as the Aṃśumat and Śivālayanirmāṇadīpikā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivagaNapatisubrahmaNyaprat.attribution: An anonymous South Indian compilation of pratiṣṭhā rites for Śiva, Subrahmaṇya and Gaṇapati. It combines rubrics with extracts named in colophons from the Aṃśumat, Śivālayanirmāṇadīpikā, Kumāratantra, Candrajñānāgama, and quotations from the Kāraṇa, Dīpta and others. Rubrics are partly in Tamil.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivagaNapatisubrahmaNyaprat.edition: Unpublished: transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf bundle RE30970 (109 folios, 390 × 33 mm). Not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivagaNapatisubrahmaNyaprat.coverage: partial — The bundle RE30970 contains 109 folios covering consecration rituals for Śiva, Subrahmaṇya, and Gaṇapati. The e-text breaks off at p. 52a (f. 76a) during the Subrahmaṇyamaṇṭapapūjā, leaving the Subrahmaṇya and Gaṇapati sections incomplete/untranscribed.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivajJAnasiddhisvapakSadRST.title: Śivajñānasiddhisvapakṣadṛṣṭāntasaṅgraha, Saptalakṣaṇa treatises (last treatise incomplete)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivajJAnasiddhisvapakSadRST.author: Vedajñāna, Mallayārya
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivajJAnasiddhisvapakSadRST.summary: A transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE 30494 containing the Śivajñānasiddhisvapakṣadṛṣṭāntasaṅgraha, an anthology quoting Āgamas and related Śaiva scriptures (including Svāyambhuva, Ajita, Cintya, Suprabheda, Niśvāsa, etc.), followed by Saptalakṣaṇa grammatical/phonetic treatises, including Mallayārya's Samānasandhivyākhyāna (Padadarpaṇa), Vilaṅghyavyākhyāna, Hrasvasaṃgraha / Avarṇi, Avarṇyāvarṇayorvyākhyāna, and Aniṅgyaparibhāṣā.

Vedajñāna is tentatively associated with the text in the catalog record ('Vedajñāna?').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivajJAnasiddhisvapakSadRST.edition: Unpublished: transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf manuscript RE 30494.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivanirvANa_M00651.title: Śivanirvāṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivanirvANa_M00651.summary: An elaborate Kashmiri Śaiva liturgical handbook (paddhati) detailing cremation and post-mortem liberation rituals (antyeṣṭi / nirvāṇavidhi) for deceased initiates (samayin, ācārya, etc.). It describes bījākṣara mantras, the preliminary purification of ground and ritual implements, prāṇāyāma, internal deconstruction of the subtle and gross bodies (sūkṣma- and sthūladehaśuddhi), invocations of Bahurūpabhairava, and concluding bone-gathering rites (asthisañcaya).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivanirvANa_M00651.attribution: A ritual manual of the Kashmirian Śaiva funerary and post-cremation tradition (śivanirvāṇavidhi/antyeṣṭi), preserved anonymously in paddhati form.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivanirvANa_M00651.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of Jammu, Dogra Art Museum manuscript 476 (dated Saptarṣi/Laukika Saṃvat 5010 [ CE], Bhādrapada śukla navamī).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivanirvANa_M00651.coverage: complete — The primary Nirvāṇapaddhati ritual manual concludes with a scribal colophon; it is followed by an appended supplementary rite for collecting bones on the fourth day (athacaturthadivase asthisañcayaśmaśānavidhiḥ).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivarahasya_part_1_M00666.title: Śivarahasya (aṃśa 1)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivarahasya_part_1_M00666.summary: The Śivarahasya is a massive Śaiva compendium structured as an itihāsa in twelve books (aṃśas), expounding the supremacy of Śiva, mythological narratives, and ritual and devotional observances. This first volume, the Māheśvarāṃśa, details the transmission of secret Śaiva doctrine to the sage Jaigīṣavya, praises of Śiva and Devī by Skanda and other divinities, the religious merit of liṅga worship and temple building, and theological arguments asserting Śiva's transcendence over all other deities.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivarahasya_part_1_M00666.attribution: Ascribed in tradition to divine revelation (imparted by Śiva/Skanda to Jaigīṣavya and recounted by Sūta). Within the text (e.g. adhyāya 6), Vyāsa is portrayed as an auditor rather than author.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivarahasya_part_1_M00666.edition: Śrīśivarahasyākhyaḥ mahetihāsaḥ: māheśvarākhyaḥ prathamāṃśaḥ, ed. Marūvūr Gaṇeśa Śāstrī and Varahūr Sundareśvara Śāstrī, Madras: Vāṇīnilaya Mudrākṣaraśālā, 1913.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivarahasya_part_1_M00666.coverage: partial — Contains the complete first aṃśa (Prathamāṃśa / Māheśvarāṃśa) of the twelve aṃśas of the Śivarahasya, preceded by the publisher's front matter, contents (viṣayānukramaṇikā), and followed by the printed errata list (śuddhipatra).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasUtravRtti_M00667.title: Śivasūtra with Śivasūtravṛtti
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasUtravRtti_M00667.summary: The Śivasūtra is the foundational scriptural text of non-dual Kashmir Shaivism (Trika/Pratyabhijñā), traditionally revealed to Vasugupta on Mount Mahādeva. It expounds the nature of ultimate consciousness and liberation through three sequential stages: Śāmbhavopāya, Śāktopāya, and Āṇavopāya. The Śivasūtravṛtti is a concise anonymous commentary explicating each sūtra with glosses and scriptural citations from texts such as the Mālinīvijayottaratantra and Ucchuṣmabhairava.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasUtravRtti_M00667.attribution: The root Śivasūtras are traditionally held to have been revealed by Śiva to the Kashmiri master Vasugupta. The accompanying Śivasūtravṛtti is an anonymous concise gloss.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasUtravRtti_M00667.edition: Diplomatic transcription of manuscript no. 1672 ka (shelfmark Alm. 27, shelf 2, accession no. 6052; 13 folios; Devanagari script), Shri Raghunath Temple Manuscript Library, Jammu; corrected by Sāhibakaula Śivanāthaka for General Mahārāja Rāma Siṃha of Kashmir.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasUtravRtti_M00667.coverage: complete — Complete in three unmeṣas (concluding at: 'ity āṇavopāyaprakāśanaṃ tṛtīyunmeṣaḥ 3 samāpteyaṃ śivasūtravṛttiḥ'), corresponding to all 13 folios of manuscript no. 1672 ka.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasahasranAmastotra_uttar.title: Śivasahasranāmastotra (Ādityapurāṇa)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasahasranAmastotra_uttar.summary: The Śivasahasranāmastotra from the Ādityapurāṇa (also termed Mṛtyuñjayasahasranāmastotra) is a stotra of one thousand epithets addressed to Śiva. It is framed by a dialogue narrating how Viṣṇu, seeking to defeat the Daityas, installed a liṅga on Mount Himavat and propitiated Śiva with one thousand names and one thousand lotus blossoms to receive the Sudarśanacakra. This e-text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription of IFP manuscript 32407 prepared for the Muktabodha Indological Research Institute.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasahasranAmastotra_uttar.attribution: Ascribed to the Ādityapurāṇa in the introductory narrative dialogue and manuscript tradition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasahasranAmastotra_uttar.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP) manuscript no. 32407 (unpublished transcript).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasahasranAmastotra_uttar.coverage: partial — Contains the introductory narrative frame (Viṣṇu's worship of Śiva to obtain the Sudarśanacakra), viniyoga, dhyāna, and the 1,000 names; ends abruptly after line 1438 without an uttarapīṭhikā or closing phalaśruti.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasiddhAntacandrikA_M0061.title: Śivasiddhāntacandrikā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasiddhAntacandrikA_M0061.author: Siddhanañjeśa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasiddhAntacandrikA_M0061.summary: The Śivasiddhāntacandrikā is a Vīraśaiva (Śivādvaita) verse treatise by Siddhanañjeśa Śivācārya of Pūvallī. It contains an introductory chapter and dialogue instruction involving guru Cidghana and a king, expounding Śivādvaita doctrine, liṅga and aṅga, and concluding with the king achieving jīvanmukti.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasiddhAntacandrikA_M0061.attribution: Siddhanañjeśa Śivācārya of the Pūvallī Pañcavaṇṇigī tradition. The work contains a dialogue between a king and the guru Cidghana. The final verse 80 states the Candrikā was taught for Cannavīrā Mahādevī and Cikkanañjeśvara ('cannavīrāmahādevyai cikkanaṃjeśvarāya ca / śivajñānaikasiddhyarthaṃ proktā siddhāṃtacaṃdrikā').
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivasiddhAntacandrikA_M0061.coverage: complete — Includes Upodghātapariccheda and concluding verse 80 with '[samāptā]'. Muktabodha notes 'Verses only without commentary'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavacaNDotsavabhaktots.title: Śivotsavacaṇḍotsavabhaktotsavasahita
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavacaNDotsavabhaktots.summary: A South Indian Śaivasiddhānta temple festival ritual manual (utsavapaddhati) transcribed from palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE32412. It prescribes procedures for grand festivals dedicated to Śiva (Śivamahotsava), Caṇḍeśa (Caṇḍotsava), and the Śaiva devotees/nāyaṉmārs (Bhaktotsava), covering preparatory rites such as bherītāḍana, dhvajārohaṇa, vṛṣayāga, rathotsava, cūrṇotsava, ghaṭābhiṣeka, and kṣetrapālapūjā.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavacaNDotsavabhaktots.attribution: A South Indian Śaivasiddhānta paddhati compilation based on Śaivāgamic codes; cites sections from sources including the Rauravāgama kriyāpāda.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavacaNDotsavabhaktots.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript RE 32412 preserved at the Institut Français de Pondichéry (IFP), Grantha script, 102 folios.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavacaNDotsavabhaktots.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the 102 folios of palm-leaf manuscript IFP RE32412, concluding with the Kṣetrapālapratiṣṭhāvidhipaṭala (iti raurave kriyāpāde kṣetrapālapriṣṭhāvidhipaṭalaḥ).

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavavidhi_I00021.title: Śivotsavavidhi (composite manuscript; breaks off at the end)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavavidhi_I00021.summary: A composite South Indian Śaiva Siddhānta manuscript on temple festivals (utsava) and seasonal observances. It contains short tracts on the Dhanurmāsa worship, the Kṛttikā lamp festival, Dīpāvali and Navarātri, as well as rakṣoghnahoma, mudrās, the sixteen upacāras and dravyāhuti homa. Its core is a series of festival chapters from the Cintya (Pratiṣṭhātantra), covering sprouting, flag-hoisting, drum-beating, bali processions, vehicle and chariot processions, tīrtha and cūrṇotsava, with the corresponding expiations (prāyaścitta). It also has utsava chapters of the Sūkṣma, Makuṭa and Kāraṇa Āgamas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavavidhi_I00021.attribution: Anonymous compilation. The colophon at seg. 2327 names one Kālīśvaraguru as the writer or copyist of the Cintya śivotsava section ('kālīśvaraguruṇā likhite'). A note at seg. 1083 records the dravyāhuti section as written in the owner's own hand ('(அப்பா/அய்யா) svahastalikhitam'). One colophon attributes a Sakalāgamasaṅgraha to Aghoraśivācārya; that attribution is reported, not verified.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavavidhi_I00021.edition: Unpublished: transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf manuscript RE 27544 (200 folios/pictures). Not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zivotsavavidhi_I00021.coverage: partial — The transcription runs from picture P5b to P200a of the 200-picture bundle; 'P' numbers are photograph numbers, and the folio numbering restarts within sections. It starts with a section heading on P5b, so the first pictures probably contain only covers or blank leaves; this was not verified. It ends mid-sentence on P200a (seg. 5838) in the rites after the utsavavidhi that ends at seg. 5733, without a colophon. The material on the following leaves is therefore lost or not photographed. Individual Āgama chapters are mostly complete with paṭala colophons. Muktabodha marks completeness as 'uncertain'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrAdhakArikA_I00006.title: Śrāddhakārikā (damaged, with lacunae)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrAdhakArikA_I00006.summary: An anonymous Śrīvaiṣṇava manual of domestic (gṛhya) rites in Sanskrit with Tamil rubrics, preserved in IFP manuscript 31231. Its main subject is the annual śrāddha for the father (pratyābdikaśrāddha), performed both by the pārvaṇa procedure with homa and in the shortened saṅkalpa form, with Mahāviṣṇu as protector of the rite. It also gives procedures for rekindling the domestic fire (agnisandhāna), aupāsana, the student's aupāsana and pañcagavya. It ends with a cosmographic saṅkalpa formula and fragmentary Tamil–Maṇipravāḷa notes.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrAdhakArikA_I00006.attribution: An anonymous Śrīvaiṣṇava domestic ritual manual. It salutes 'sarvebhyaḥ śrīvaiṣṇavebhyaḥ', uses the 'śrībhagavadājñākaiṅkarya' saṅkalpa and the 'śrāddhasaṃrakṣaka śrīmahāviṣṇu', and the appended Tamil notes mention Deśika, the Tirumantra and Dvaya.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrAdhakArikA_I00006.edition: Unpublished: transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf manuscript RE 31231. Not a printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrAdhakArikA_I00006.coverage: partial — Sections run from agnisandhāna (from about P004b; the first picture marker is P005a at seg. 7) to the closing rubric 'śrāddhakārikai' on P42a (seg. 484). All sections listed in the IFP description are present. Leaf damage causes frequent lacunae, marked '(........)'. The cosmographic saṅkalpa (P39–40) and the Tamil notes on P40b–41a are fragmentary. Muktabodha marks the text 'incomplete'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIbAdarAyanamahaRSi_attrib.title: Basavapurāṇa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIbAdarAyanamahaRSi_attrib.author: Vyāsa
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIbAdarAyanamahaRSi_attrib.summary: The Sanskrit Basavapurāṇa (Basaveśvarapurāṇa) is a Vīraśaiva (Liṅgāyat) purāṇa in 43 adhyāyas, framed as a dialogue in which Skanda answers Agastya's questions. It narrates the birth of Basava (Basaveśvara) as a partial incarnation of Nandin, his marriage, his service at the court of Bijjala and his miracles. It also tells the legends of many Śaiva and Vīraśaiva devotees (e.g. Kannappa, Dīpada Kaliya, Moligemāra, Śivanāgadeva) and argues for Vīraśaiva doctrine and practice against Vedic ritualism and rival sects. It closes with a scene in which Viśvakarman weighs the work against Vyāsa's other compositions and finds it the best of all purāṇas.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIbAdarAyanamahaRSi_attrib.attribution: The ascription to Bādarāyaṇa/Vyāsa is pseudepigraphic. Colophons present the work as a 'svarūpagrantha' and 'paramarahasya' in the form of a dialogue between Skanda (Kumāra) and Agastya. It is a Sanskrit Vīraśaiva work and should not be confused with the Telugu Basavapurāṇamu of Pālkuriki Somanātha.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIbAdarAyanamahaRSi_attrib.coverage: complete — The text begins '[śrīvyāsoktabasavapurāṇaṃ prārabhyate] [prathamo'dhyāyaḥ] agastyapraśnaḥ' and ends with the colophon of the 43rd adhyāya: 'iti śrībādarāyaṇamaharṣipraṇīte śrībasaveśvarapurāṇe svarūpagraṃthe paramarahasye skaṃdāgastyasaṃvāde tricatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ śrībasaveśvarapurāṇaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ'.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIcakranavAvaraNapUjA_I000.title: Śrīcakranavāvaraṇapūjā
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIcakranavAvaraNapUjA_I000.summary: An unpublished Śrīvidyā ritual manual (paddhati) detailing the worship of Mahātripurasundarī through the Śrīcakra. The text opens with preliminary rites including Dīpapūjākalpa, sets out the nyāsas and dhyāna for the Ṣoḍaśākṣarī and Pañcadaśākṣarī mantras, details guru-pūjā, and systematically covers the worship of the deities presiding over the nine enclosures (navāvaraṇa) of the Śrīcakra from Trailokyamohana to Sarvānandamaya, concluding with Vedic recitations including Pavamānasūkta and Puruṣasūkta.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIcakranavAvaraNapUjA_I000.edition: Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf manuscript IFP 31226 (Institut Français de Pondichéry), prepared by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Dr. Deviprasad Mishra (Pondicherry/New Delhi: Muktabodha Indological Research Institute & IFP, 2023–2024).
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIcakranavAvaraNapUjA_I000.coverage: partial — Incomplete manuscript copy; the ritual text breaks off abruptly mid-verse during the recitation of the Puruṣasūkta on fol. 48a without an explicit or concluding colophon, leaving folios 48b–50a blank.

SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIvidyApUjAkramaH_and_devI.title: Śrīvidyāpūjākrama and Devīdhyāna (incomplete manuscript)
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIvidyApUjAkramaH_and_devI.summary: A Śrīvidyā ritual manual (pūjākrama) for the worship of Lalitā Tripurasundarī in the Śrīcakra, with dhyāna verses for the deities of the successive āvaraṇas, nyāsa, the installation of the ritual vessels (śaṅkha-, śuddhipātra- and mahārghya-sthāpana), and a long numbered nāmāvali of the Goddess whose names match the Lalitāsahasranāma (e.g. nityayauvanā, taruṇādityapāṭalā, bindutarpaṇasantuṣṭā). Transcribed from a damaged, incomplete palm-leaf bundle in the IFP collection.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIvidyApUjAkramaH_and_devI.attribution: Traditional anonymous Śrīvidyā ritual texts preserving paddhati and dhyāna procedures for the worship of Lalitā Tripurasundarī.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIvidyApUjAkramaH_and_devI.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription of Institut Français de Pondichéry palm-leaf bundle RE 31062 (16 x 3 cm, 57 images), by Sambandhan Anandavardhana and Arul Nandi under the supervision of Deviprasad Mishra; IFP and Muktabodha Indological Research Institute, 2023/2024 (Muktabodha catalog no. I00027, revision 0: 2024/08/18). No printed edition.
SA_MB_ilx_mb_zrIvidyApUjAkramaH_and_devI.coverage: partial — Diplomatic transcription of palm-leaf bundle IFP RE 31062 (57 images). Folio 1 is missing (transcriber: "f.0 heading only, f1 missing"), so the text begins in the middle of the fifth āvaraṇa ("|| pañcamā(mam) ||"); leaves are damaged with many lacunae, the numbered nāmāvali has gaps, and the last leaves (pp. 54-56) contain damaged fragments before a closing mantra; pp. 57a-b are blank/bundle photo.

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranaratnamala.title: Adhikaraṇaratnamālā
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranaratnamala.author: Vedāntadeśika
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranaratnamala.summary: A Viśiṣṭādvaita versified manual summarizing the 185 adhikaraṇas (topical sections) of the Brahmasūtras based on Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya, attributed to Vedānta Deśika. Composed predominantly in Āryā/Gīti meters, each stanza epitomizes the final doctrinal conclusion (siddhānta) of an adhikaraṇa, concluding with the refrain dedicating the realization to the supreme Brahman manifest as Lord Śrīnivāsa (Veṅkaṭeśvara).
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranaratnamala.attribution: The colophon verse explicitly mentions 'Śrīdeśikārya' as the author, traditionally identifying Vedānta Deśika (Veṅkaṭanātha). Note: Not to be confused with the Adhikaraṇaratnamālā of Sukhaprakāśa.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranaratnamala.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 185 numbered verses summarizing all 185 adhikaraṇas of the Brahmasūtras according to Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya, preceded by a taniyan and invocation and ending with the colophon verse.

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranasaravalih.title: Adhikaraṇasārāvalī
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranasaravalih.author: Veṅkaṭanātha
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranasaravalih.summary: The Adhikaraṇasārāvalī is a philosophical poem in Sragdharā metre composed by the Viśiṣṭādvaita master Veṅkaṭanātha (Vedānta Deśika). It systematically encapsulates each adhikaraṇa (topical section) of the Brahmasūtras according to Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya. Covering all four adhyāyas, each stanza formulates the pūrvapakṣa objections and establishes the Viśiṣṭādvaita siddhānta.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranasaravalih.attribution: Authored by Veṅkaṭanātha (also known as Vedānta Deśika), who is invoked and named in the introductory verses.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_adhikaranasaravalih.coverage: complete — Complete text of the root verses across all four adhyāyas of the Brahmasūtra (ending with verse concluding the fourth adhyāya, vājivaktras saha mama gurubhir...).

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitamakaranda.title: Advaitamakaranda
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitamakaranda.author: Lakṣmīdhara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitamakaranda.summary: The Advaitamakaranda is a celebrated short Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa in 28 anuṣṭubh verses by Lakṣmīdhara Kavi. Through succinct introspective and dialectical reasoning, the work demonstrates the identity of the conscious self (ātman) with unconditioned existence, consciousness, and bliss (saccidānanda brahman), dismissing bodily, mental, and waking/dream/sleep states as illusory superimpositions (adhyāsa).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitamakaranda.attribution: Authored by Lakṣmīdhara Kavi (also referred to as Lakṣmīdharakavi).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitamakaranda.coverage: complete — Complete short prakaraṇa text consisting of all 28 kārikās, ending with verse 28 mentioning Lakṣmīdharakavi.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitapancaratnam.title: Advaitapañcaratna
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitapancaratnam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitapancaratnam.summary: The Advaitapañcaratna (also known as Ātmapañcaka) is a concise philosophical stotra of five verses attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. Employing standard Advaita analogies such as the rope and the snake, the dream state, and reflections in a mirror, each verse refutes identity with the body, senses, intellect, or external possessions and concludes with the refrain 'śivo'ham' ('I am Śiva/pure consciousness').
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitapancaratnam.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya in the closing colophon.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitapancaratnam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 5 verses with the traditional closing colophon.
translations: Potter, Karl H. (ed.), Encyclopedia of Indian Philosophies, Vol. 3: Advaita Vedānta up to Śaṃkara and His Pupils, Princeton: Princeton University Press, p. 343 (summary by K. Raghavan Pillai under the title Advaitapañcaratna, or Ātmapañcaka). (English)

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitarasamanjari.title: Advaitarasamañjarī
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitarasamanjari.author: Sadāśiva Brahmendra
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitarasamanjari.summary: The Advaitarasamañjarī is a short Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa text by Sadāśiva Brahmendra. Across 44 main verses (preceded by seven introductory verses honoring Lalitā, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, Gaṇeśa, and the lineage of preceptors), it expounds non-dual metaphysics, rejecting phenomenal diversity as illusory superimposition using classical similes (rope-snake, city of Gandharvas, firebrand circle) and asserting one's true nature as pure, unconditioned Brahman.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitarasamanjari.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Sadāśiva Brahmendra (also known as Sadāśivendra Sarasvatī).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitarasamanjari.coverage: complete — Complete work with 7 introductory/mangalācaraṇa stanzas and 44 main thematic stanzas followed by the closing colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitasiddhih.title: Advaitasiddhi
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitasiddhih.author: Madhusūdanasarasvatī
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitasiddhih.summary: The Advaitasiddhi is a monumental 16th-century polemical treatise of Advaita Vedānta by Madhusūdanasarasvatī, composed primarily in response to Vyāsatīrtha's Dvaita masterwork Nyāyāmṛta. Formulated using the rigorous technical terminology of Navya-Nyāya, the work systematically refutes Dvaita critiques across four paricchedas. It is celebrated for its intricate dialectical defense of the five classical definitions of the world's falsity (mithyātva), non-dual scriptural hermeneutics, and the Advaitic conception of mokṣa.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitasiddhih.attribution: The author names himself in introductory verse 4 ('muninā madhusūdanena') and the pariccheda colophons identify the work as composed by Madhusūdanasarasvatī, pupil of Viśveśvarasarasvatī.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitasiddhih.coverage: complete — Complete across all four paricchedas (prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ at [0], concluding colophon of caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ at [3455]).

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitanubhutih.title: Advaitānubhūti
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitanubhutih.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitanubhutih.summary: Advaitānubhūti is a short Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa in 84 anuṣṭubh verses expounding non-dualism. Employing classic Vedāntic analogies (the single moon appearing double to defective vision, space enclosed within diverse pots, water turning to hail, and mirages), it teaches that the pure conscious Self is immutable, ever-free, and distinct from the three bodies (sthūla, sūkṣma, kāraṇa) and the three states of experience (jāgrat, svapna, suṣupti).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitanubhutih.attribution: Traditionally ascribed in colophons to Śaṅkarācārya, pupil of Govinda Bhagavatpāda. In some early printed catalogues (e.g., Cecil Bendall), the author was misidentified as Govinda Parivrājaka Paramahaṃsa due to a misreading of the standard colophon formula śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_advaitanubhutih.coverage: complete — Complete in 84 verses (numbered 1.1–1.84), concluding with the complete colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_anatmasrivigarhanaprakar.title: Anātmaśrīvigarhaṇaprakaraṇa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_anatmasrivigarhanaprakar.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_anatmasrivigarhanaprakar.summary: The Anātmaśrīvigarhaṇaprakaraṇa is an 18-verse Advaita Vedānta didactic poem traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. Through the recurring question and refrain 'tataḥ kiṃ ... yena svātmā naiva sākṣātkṛto 'bhūt' ('what then of it, if one has not directly realized one's own Self?'), the text systematically dismisses secular learning, wealth, physical pleasures, social honors, austerities, yogic powers, and celestial realms as worthless in the absence of direct Self-realization (ātmasākṣātkāra).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_anatmasrivigarhanaprakar.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkara (śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṃkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_anatmasrivigarhanaprakar.coverage: complete — Complete text of 18 verses (16 verses featuring the refrain 'tataḥ kiṃ ... yena svātmā naiva sākṣātkṛto 'bhūt' and two phalaśruti/concluding verses) followed by the closing colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhagavadbhaktirasayanam.title: Bhagavadbhaktirasāyana with Svopajñaṭīkā
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhagavadbhaktirasayanam.author: Madhusūdanasarasvatī
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhagavadbhaktirasayanam.summary: The Bhagavadbhaktirasāyana is a prominent 16th-century treatise by the Advaita master Madhusūdana Sarasvatī synthesizing Advaita Vedānta philosophy with devotional aesthetics (rasaśāstra). Over three ullāsas, the work formulates bhakti (devotion to Kṛṣṇa) as an autonomous aesthetic rasa and the ultimate puruṣārtha, adapting classical Nāṭyaśāstra categories (vibhāva, anubhāva, vyabhicāribhāva, sthāyibhāva) into a theological framework. An extensive autocommentary (ṭīkāmatallikā) accompanies the first ullāsa.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhagavadbhaktirasayanam.attribution: Composed by Madhusūdana Sarasvatī across three ullāsas, together with his own prose commentary (ṭīkāmatallikā) on the first ullāsa.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhagavadbhaktirasayanam.coverage: complete — Complete text of all three ullāsas (ullāsa 1 with 32 verses and autocommentary; ullāsa 2 with 78 verses; ullāsa 3 with 30 verses). The autocommentary was only ever written for the first ullāsa.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhedojjivanam.title: Bhedojjīvana with the commentaries of Bhagavantarāya, Ānandatīrtha, Vāsudevācārya, Śrīnātha, Kāśī Timmaṇṇācārya and Śarkarā Śrīnivāsa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhedojjivanam.author: Vyāsatīrtha, Bhagavantarāya, Ānandatīrtha, Vāsudevācārya, Śrīnātha, Kāśī Timmaṇṇācārya, Śarkarā Śrīnivāsa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhedojjivanam.summary: The Bhedojjīvana ('Reviving Difference') is a short polemical treatise by the Dvaita scholar Vyāsatīrtha. It defends the reality of difference (bheda) against Advaita. In this e-text each passage of the root text is followed by six later Mādhva commentaries and glosses, by Bhagavantarāya, Ānandatīrtha (son of Mudgalārya), Kumbhārī Vāsudevācārya, Hulagī Śrīnātha, Kāśī Timmaṇṇācārya and Śarkarā Śrīnivāsa.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhedojjivanam.attribution: The root text is by Vyāsatīrtha (Vyāsarāja, 1478–1539; also given as c. 1460–1539); the root colophon reads 'brahmaṇyatīrthapūjyapādaśiṣyeṇa vyāsayatinā kṛtaṃ bhedojjīvanaṃ samāptam'. The commentators as identified in the e-text: (1) Bhagavantarāya, 'bhagavannāmnā', a pupil of Bhāskarī Veṅkaṭavarāhācārya (seg. 4 and 8661). (2) Ānandatīrtha, son of Mudgalārya, of Janārdanapura (seg. 66 and 8706–8710); he is not Madhva. (3) Vāsudevācārya, son of Kumbhārī Nārāyaṇācārya (seg. 91 and 8725). (4) Śrīnātha, called Hulagī Śrīnāthācārya in the heading, of Vyāghrapurī and son of Vāsudevārya (seg. 156 and 8740–8744). (5) Kāśī Timmaṇṇācārya, called Kāśī Tirumalācārya in the colophon (seg. 173 and 8748). (6) Śarkarā Śrīnivāsācārya (seg. 192 and 8788–8792). None of the commentators is dated here.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhedojjivanam.coverage: complete — Complete. The root text runs to its colophon (seg. 8585–8586), and each of the six commentaries ends with its own colophon (segs. 8586–8792).

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasika.title: Bhāvaprakāśikā
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasika.author: Raṅgarāmānuja
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasika.summary: The Bhāvaprakāśikā by Raṅgarāmānuja Muni is a commentary on the Śrutaprakāśikā on the Śrībhāṣya.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasika.attribution: Author: Raṅgarāmānuja Muni, called Daśopaniṣadbhāṣyakāra in the colophon. The work is a commentary on the Śrutaprakāśikā (itself on the Śrībhāṣya).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasika.coverage: complete — Ends with the colophon of adhyāya 4, pāda 4 (jagadvayāpāravarjādhikaraṇa), 'samāptaccādhyāyaḥ', and the totals 'samuditadhikaraṇasaṅkhyā 156 samuditasūtraṣṭadṛlvā 544'.

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_bhattarahasyam_khandadev.title: Bhāṭṭarahasya (partial)
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_bhattarahasyam_khandadev.author: Khaṇḍadeva
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_bhattarahasyam_khandadev.summary: The Bhāṭṭarahasya (also called Bhāṭṭatantrarahasya) is a treatise by Khaṇḍadeva on the semantics of verbal cognition (śābdabodha) according to the Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsā school. Formulated in the precise terminology of Navya-Nyāya, it examines the definitions of dharma and adharma, the semantic import of injunctive endings (vidhi) and productive agency (bhāvanā), verbal roots (dhātu), verbal suffixes (ākhyāta), and case terminations (vibhakti). This incomplete e-text ends with the discussion of the nominative case.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_bhattarahasyam_khandadev.coverage: partial — Contains introductory discussions on dharma, vidhivāda, bhāvanāvāda, dhātvartha, ākhyātārtha, and concludes at the end of the nominative case analysis (kātyāyanamatena prathamāvibhakyarthanirūpaṇaṃ samāptam, line 626). The treatments of subsequent cases (dvitīyā through saptamī) are missing.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahmanucintanam.title: Brahmānucintana
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahmanucintanam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahmanucintanam.summary: The Brahmānucintana is a short Advaita Vedānta contemplative text consisting of 29 verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. It guides the practitioner through meditative affirmations of identity with Brahman ('ahaṃ brahmāsmi') and the negation of the physical body, senses, and elements.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahmanucintanam.coverage: complete — Complete text in 29 verses with concluding colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahrsutrarthapadyamalik.title: Brahmasūtrārthapadyamālikā (adhyāyas 1–2)
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahrsutrarthapadyamalik.author: Rājagopāla
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahrsutrarthapadyamalik.summary: A Viśiṣṭādvaita verse summary of Bādarāyaṇa's Brahmasūtras in anuṣṭubh meter according to Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya. Composed by the 44th pontiff of Ahobila Maṭha (Śrīvaṇ Śaṭhakopa Śrī Vedānta Deśika Yatīndra Mahādeśika / Rājagopāla), the work summarizes the purports and adhikaraṇas of the sūtras. This e-text contains the first two adhyāyas (Samanvaya and Avirodha).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahrsutrarthapadyamalik.attribution: Composed by Śrīvaṇ Śaṭhakopa Śrī Vedānta Deśika Yatīndra Mahādeśika (identified in the colophon as the 44th pontiff of Ahobila Maṭha, who calls himself Rājagopāla in the opening verses).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_brahrsutrarthapadyamalik.coverage: partial — Covers adhyāya 1 (pādas 1–4) and adhyāya 2 (pādas 1–4), concluding with the colophon of the second adhyāya.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_cidgaganacandrika.title: Cidgaganacandrikā with Divyacakorikā (vimarśas 1–2)
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_cidgaganacandrika.author: Kālidāsa, Karrā Agnihotra Śāstrin
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_cidgaganacandrika.summary: The Cidgaganacandrikā is an esoteric hymn associated with the Krama system. This e-text provides the first two vimarśas accompanied by Karrā Agnihotra Śāstrin's Sanskrit commentary Divyacakorikā.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_cidgaganacandrika.attribution: The root text is traditionally ascribed to Kālidāsa. The commentary Divyacakorikā is by Karrā Agnihotra Śāstrin (dīkṣā name: Dhanadānandanātha).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_cidgaganacandrika.coverage: partial — Contains vimarśas 1 and 2 only (concluding at the end with the colophon of the dvitīya vimarśa).

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dasaslokistutih_brhatsto.title: Daśaślokīstuti
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dasaslokistutih_brhatsto.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dasaslokistutih_brhatsto.summary: The Daśaślokīstuti is a ten-verse devotional hymn (stotra) dedicated to Śiva accompanied by Ambā (Sāmba), traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. Verse 1 invokes Sāmba across grammatical cases, while the subsequent verses praise his cosmic supremacy and purāṇic exploits—such as the burning of Tripura, the drinking of the ocean poison, and his superiority over Brahmā and Viṣṇu—each concluding with the refrain 'tasmin me hṛdayaṃ sukhena ramatāṃ sāmbe parabrahmaṇi'.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dasaslokistutih_brhatsto.attribution: The colophon attributes it to Śaṅkarācārya ('iti śrīmacchaṅkarācāryaviracitā daśaślokīstutiḥ sampūrṇā').
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dasaslokistutih_brhatsto.coverage: complete — Complete: 10 verses, all ending in the refrain 'tasmin me hṛdayaṃ sukhena ramatāṃ sāmbe parabrahmaṇi', which is abbreviated 'tasmin me ...' from verse 3 on, followed by the colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvaitadyumaniparisistam.title: Dvaitadyumaṇipariśiṣṭa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvaitadyumaniparisistam.summary: The Dvaitadyumaṇipariśiṣṭa is a Dvaita Vedānta polemical treatise functioning as a supplement (pariśiṣṭa) to the Dvaitadyumaṇi. It critiques Advaita Vedānta epistemology and ontology, focusing on the reality of difference (bheda) between jīva and Brahman even in liberation (mukti), the analysis of the supreme human end (parameṣṭa / puruṣārtha), and theories of error and non-existence (such as anirvacanīyakhyāti, asatkhyāti, and shell-silver illusion).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvaitadyumaniparisistam.attribution: A Dvaita Vedānta polemical supplement (pariśiṣṭa) associated with the Dvaitadyumaṇi; the author is not stated in the e-text.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvaitadyumaniparisistam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the pariśiṣṭa from the opening discussion on puruṣārtha/parameṣṭa to the concluding colophon (iti dvaitadyumaṇipariśiṣṭaṃ sampūrṇam).

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvadasastotrani.title: Dvādaśastotra with Kandukastuti
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvadasastotrani.author: Madhva
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvadasastotrani.summary: The Dvādaśastotra is a collection of twelve devotional hymns composed by Madhva (Ānandatīrtha), the founder of Dvaita Vedānta. Addressed to Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa, the hymns combine personal devotion and iconographic meditation with Dvaita theological doctrines, emphasizing the absolute sovereignty and independence of Viṣṇu. Appended to the text is the Kandukastuti, a short praise poem describing Kṛṣṇa playing with a ball.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvadasastotrani.attribution: The texts are traditionally attributed to Madhvācārya under his ascetic ordination name Śrīmad-Ānandatīrtha Bhagavatpāda.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_dvadasastotrani.coverage: complete — Contains the Dvādaśastotra followed by the Kandukastuti and the editor's concluding dedication.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_drgdrsyavivekah.title: Dṛgdṛśyaviveka
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_drgdrsyavivekah.author: Bhāratītīrtha
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_drgdrsyavivekah.summary: The Dṛgdṛśyaviveka is a concise 46-verse Advaita Vedānta introductory treatise analyzing the fundamental distinction between the unchanging subject/seer (dṛś, sākṣin) and the changing objective realm/seen (dṛśya). It outlines the powers of avidyā/māyā, the threefold definition of the individual soul (jīva: pāramārthika, vyāvahārika, and prātibhāsika), and describes kinds of samādhi (savikalpa and nirvikalpa, internal and external) as practical means for realizing non-dual Brahman.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_drgdrsyavivekah.attribution: The concluding colophon explicitly names Bhāratītīrtha Svāmin. Tradition and scholarship also associate or ascribe the text to Śaṅkara or Vidyāraṇya.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_drgdrsyavivekah.coverage: complete — Complete text of 46 verses ending with colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gurorgunamanimala.title: Gurorguṇamaṇimālā
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gurorgunamanimala.author: Giridharācārya
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gurorgunamanimala.summary: A 20th-century biographical eulogy (carita) in verse composed by Kadalīkanda Giridharācārya celebrating the Dvaita Vedānta and Vyākaraṇa scholar Mahāmahopādhyāya Śrīmuṣṇaṃ Subbarāyācārya. It narrates his lineage, early Vedic education, śāstric training across South and Central India, and his scholarly disputations.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gurorgunamanimala.attribution: Colophon explicitly reads: 'iti śrīpadapurī(tirupati)virājamāna śrīveṅkaṭeśvarasaṃskṛtamahākalāśālāyāṃ sāhityapradhānādhyāpakena dvaitavedāntaniṣṇātena kadalīkandānvayajena śrīnivāsācāryaputreṇa giridharācāryeṇa raciteyaṃ gurorguṇamaṇimālā'.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gurorgunamanimala.coverage: complete — Complete text of the biographical poem, concluding with author verses and formal colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitabhasyatatparyacandri.title: Gītābhāṣyatātparyacandrikā (up to 18.58)
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitabhasyatatparyacandri.author: Veṅkaṭanātha
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitabhasyatatparyacandri.summary: The Gītābhāṣyatātparyacandrikā is an extensive sub-commentary composed by Veṅkaṭanātha on Rāmānuja's Gītābhāṣya. In this Wikisource transcription, the commentary covers chapters 1 up to 18.58.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitabhasyatatparyacandri.attribution: Veṅkaṭanātha (also titled Vedāntācārya / Kavitārkikakesarin) composed this sub-commentary on Rāmānuja's Bhagavadgītābhāṣya.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitabhasyatatparyacandri.coverage: partial — Covers chapter 1 through chapter 18, verse 58; verses 18.59–18.78 and the closing colophon/maṅgala are missing in this e-text.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyanirnayah.title: Gītātātparyanirṇaya
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyanirnayah.author: Madhva
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyanirnayah.summary: The Gītātātparyanirṇaya is one of two treatises on the Bhagavadgītā composed by Madhvācārya (the other being the Gītābhāṣya). It is a topical, theological commentary organized across 18 adhyāyas that synthesizes the philosophical import of the Gītā from the Dvaita Vedānta perspective, focusing on the supreme sovereignty and transcendence of Nārāyaṇa, the hierarchical dependence of jīvas, and the role of selfless duty and bhakti as means to liberation.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyanirnayah.coverage: complete — Complete in 18 adhyāyas matching the Bhagavadgītā, ending with the colophon to adhyāya 18.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyatikabhavadip.title: Gītātātparyaṭīkābhāvadīpa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyatikabhavadip.author: Rāghavendratīrtha
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyatikabhavadip.summary: The Gītātātparyaṭīkābhāvadīpa is a Dvaita Vedānta sub-commentary (ṭippaṇī) authored by Rāghavendratīrtha on Jayatīrtha's Nyāyadīpikā, which is itself an exposition of Madhvācārya's Bhagavadgītātātparyanirṇaya. The text resolves difficult syntactic constructions and clarifies the theological and exegetical polemics of Jayatīrtha across all eighteen chapters of the Gītā.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyatikabhavadip.attribution: A super-commentary (ṭippaṇī / bhāvadīpa) by Rāghavendratīrtha on Jayatīrtha's Gītātātparyaṭīkā (also known as Nyāyadīpikā), which in turn comments on Madhvācārya's Bhagavadgītātātparyanirṇaya.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_gitatatparyatikabhavadip.coverage: complete — Complete in 18 adhyāyas matching the 18 chapters of the Bhagavadgītā, concluding at adhyāya 18.

SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jayantikalpah.title: Jayantīkalpa
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jayantikalpah.author: Madhva
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jayantikalpah.summary: The Jayantīkalpa is a short ritual manual in sixteen verses composed by Madhva (Ānandatīrtha, 13th century), founder of the Dvaita Vedānta school. It outlines the observances for the Kṛṣṇajayantī festival (when Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī coincides with the Rohiṇī nakṣatra), detailing fasting rules (upavāsa), ritual purification, and the specific mantras for presenting arghya offerings to Kṛṣṇa and the Moon (Candra).
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jayantikalpah.attribution: Attributed in the text heading and colophon to Ānandatīrtha (śrīmadānandatīrthabhagavatpabādapraṇītasarvamūlagranthāḥ; śrīmadānandatīrthabhagavatpādācāryaviracito jayantīkalpaḥ samāptaḥ).
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jayantikalpah.coverage: complete — Complete text in 16 verses with closing colophon.

SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jinendragunasamstutih.title: Jinendraguṇasaṃstuti
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jinendragunasamstutih.summary: The Jinendraguṇasaṃstuti is a Jain philosophical stotra of 50 verses celebrating the qualities of the Jina. Alongside devotion to the Tīrthaṅkara, the verses systematically defend foundational Jain tenets—including omniscience (kevalajñāna), syādvāda/anekāntavāda, and the nature of liberation—while critiquing opposing viewpoints regarding consciousness, verbal testimony, and causality.
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_jinendragunasamstutih.attribution: No author name appears in the e-text or its colophons.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_jivanmuktanandalahari.title: Jīvanmuktānandalaharī
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_jivanmuktanandalahari.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_jivanmuktanandalahari.summary: The Jīvanmuktānandalaharī ('Wave of Bliss of the Living-Liberated') is an Advaita Vedānta poetic work comprising 17 verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. It depicts the detached, unconditioned lifestyle and mental equanimity of a jīvanmukta (one liberated while living), who moves through varied settings, company, and dualities of experience without delusion due to spiritual knowledge received through the guru's initiation.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_jivanmuktanandalahari.coverage: complete — Complete in 17 verses (16 descriptive verses ending with the refrain 'munir na vyāmohaṃ bhajati gurudīkṣākṣatatamāḥ' followed by a concluding verse 17) plus colophon.

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_karmanirnayah.title: Karmanirṇaya
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_karmanirnayah.author: Madhva
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_karmanirnayah.summary: The Karmanirṇaya ('Determination of Ritual Action') is one of the ten philosophical treatises (Daśaprakaraṇa) composed by Madhva (Ānandatīrtha), the founder of Dvaita Vedānta. In this work, Madhva interprets the Mahānāmnī verses and Vedic ritual injunctions of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, arguing against Advaitin views of ritual non-efficacy and an unqualified (nirguṇa) Brahman. He demonstrates the principle of sarvaśabdavācyatva—that all Vedic texts and rituals ultimately signify and extol Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_karmanirnayah.attribution: Authored by Madhvācārya (Ānandatīrtha, c. 1230 A.D.); one of his ten philosophical monographs known collectively as the Daśaprakaraṇas within the Sarvamūlagrantha.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_karmanirnayah.coverage: complete — Complete root text, ending with the closing benediction and final colophon ('iti śrīmadānandatīrthabhavagatpādācāryaviracitaḥ karmanirṇayaḥ samāptaḥ').

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_kenopanisadbhasyam.title: Kenopaniṣad with Kenopaniṣadbhāṣya
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_kenopanisadbhasyam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_kenopanisadbhasyam.summary: The Kenopaniṣadbhāṣya (specifically the Padabhāṣya) is Śaṅkara's definitive word-by-word commentary on the Kenopaniṣad (belonging to the Jaiminīya/Talavakāra school of the Sāmaveda). In this work, Śaṅkara establishes that Brahman, as pure consciousness and the inner Self (pratyagātman), transcends all sensory and mental cognition and cannot be grasped as an object of knowledge. He argues against the necessity of ritual actions (karma) for ultimate liberation, showing that final freedom (amṛtatva) arises exclusively from unmediated Self-knowledge.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_kenopanisadbhasyam.attribution: Śaṅkara is traditionally credited with two separate commentaries on the Kenopaniṣad: the Padabhāṣya (a literal, word-for-word commentary) and the Vākyabhāṣya (a sentence-by-sentence exposition). The text here is the widely accepted Padabhāṣya.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_kenopanisadbhasyam.coverage: complete — Complete text of all four khaṇḍas of the Kenopaniṣad accompanied by Śaṅkara's Padabhāṣya, ending at khaṇḍa 4, verse 9.
translations: Swami Gambhirananda, Eight Upanisads: with the Commentary of Sankaracarya, vol. 1, Calcutta: Advaita Ashrama, 1957. (English)

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_laghuvakyavrttih.title: Laghuvākyavṛtti
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_laghuvakyavrttih.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_laghuvakyavrttih.summary: The Laghuvākyavṛtti is a concise Advaita Vedānta tract in 18 anuṣṭubh verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. It presents a contemplative method for discriminating between pure witness-consciousness (śuddhabodha) and changing mental modifications (vṛtti) or the reflected ego (cidābhāsa). By recognizing the pure consciousness persisting in the silent interval between mental thoughts, the seeker is led to verify the non-dual import of the mahāvākya 'ahaṃ brahma'.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_laghuvakyavrttih.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya, though like many short Advaita prakaraṇas, its authentic authorship by the historical Ādi Śaṅkara remains uncertain in modern scholarship.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_laghuvakyavrttih.coverage: complete — Complete 18-verse text with concluding colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_manisapancakam.title: Manīṣāpañcaka
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_manisapancakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_manisapancakam.summary: The Manīṣāpañcaka is a short Advaita Vedānta work in five verses (framed by introductory verses and a concluding devotion) traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. Originating according to tradition in Śaṅkara's encounter with Lord Śiva disguised as an outcaste (caṇḍāla) in Vārāṇasī, the text asserts that anyone who has realized pure non-dual consciousness—whether a caṇḍāla or a brāhmaṇa—is truly one's guru.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_manisapancakam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising two introductory verses (the dialogue between the ascetic and the caṇḍāla/Śiva), the five central verses with the refrain 'gururityeṣā manīṣā mama', and one concluding verse ('dāsaste'haṃ...').
translations: Translated in P. Sankaranarayana, What is Advaita?. (English)
Translated, with Śamkara's Māyāpañcaka and Upadeśasāhasrī, by R. Krishnaswamy Aiyar. Srirangam 1964. (English)

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mundakopanisadbhasyam.title: Muṇḍakopaniṣad with Muṇḍakopaniṣadbhāṣya
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mundakopanisadbhasyam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mundakopanisadbhasyam.summary: The Muṇḍakopaniṣadbhāṣya is Śaṅkara's classic Advaita Vedānta commentary on the Muṇḍakopaniṣad of the Atharvaveda. In his commentary, Śaṅkara elucidates the fundamental distinction between lower knowledge (aparā vidyā), comprising ritual works and external learning, and higher knowledge (parā vidyā), which leads directly to the imperishable Brahman (akṣara). He emphasizes renunciation (saṃnyāsa) as a prerequisite for liberating knowledge and interprets key allegories, including the archery metaphor of Om and the famous image of the two birds perched on the same tree.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mundakopanisadbhasyam.attribution: The Muṇḍakopaniṣad is an Atharvaṇa Vedic text. Its commentary is attributed to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mundakopanisadbhasyam.coverage: complete — Complete in 3 muṇḍakas (each divided into 2 khaṇḍas), including the initial śāntipāṭha, introductory sambandhabhāṣya, root mantras, and full commentary ending at 3.2.11.
translations: Gupta, Som Raj (trans.). The Word Speaks to the Faustian Man. (English)

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_manameyodayah_narayanabh.title: Mānameyodaya (Pramāṇapariccheda)
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_manameyodayah_narayanabh.author: Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_manameyodayah_narayanabh.summary: The Mānameyodaya is an introductory primer of the Bhāṭṭa school of Pūrvamīmāṃsā written in alternating kārikās and prose. This first division, the Pramāṇapariccheda, composed by Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa, systematizes Kumārila Bhaṭṭa's epistemology, expounding valid knowledge and establishing the six Bhāṭṭa pramāṇas (pratyakṣa, anumāna, upamāna, śabda, arthāpatti, and abhāva) while rebutting rival Prābhākara, Buddhist, and Nyāya doctrines.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_manameyodayah_narayanabh.attribution: A Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsā treatise on epistemology (Pramāṇapariccheda) composed by Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa in the seventeenth century.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_manameyodayah_narayanabh.coverage: partial — Contains only the first division (Pramāṇapariccheda), consisting of 186 kārikās interspersed with prose commentary treating the six Bhāṭṭa pramāṇas (pratyakṣa, anumāna, upamāna, śabda, arthāpatti, abhāva). The Meyapariccheda is not present.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mayapancakam.title: Māyāpañcaka
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mayapancakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mayapancakam.summary: A short Advaita Vedānta text in five verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya, describing the illusory power of māyā. Each verse ends with the refrain celebrating māyā as expert in producing the impossible ('aghaṭitaghaṭanāpaṭīyasī māyā'), illustrating how the undifferentiated, non-dual consciousness is made to appear divided into jīva, īśvara, social hierarchy, and cosmic forms.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mayapancakam.attribution: Traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya (pupil of Govinda Bhagavatpāda), as explicitly stated in the colophon.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_mayapancakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 5 verses with concluding colophon.
translations: Translated, with Śamkara's Manīṣāpañcaka and Upadeśasāhasrī, by R. Krishnaswamy Aiyar. Srirangam 1964. (English)

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_mimamsaparibhasa_krsnaya.title: Mīmāṃsāparibhāṣā
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_mimamsaparibhasa_krsnaya.author: Kṛṣṇayajvan
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_mimamsaparibhasa_krsnaya.summary: The Mīmāṃsāparibhāṣā of Kṛṣṇayajvan is an elementary manual (prakaraṇa) of Pūrvamīmāṃsā. Composed in clear introductory prose for students (bālānām), it systematizes the essential categories of ritual hermeneutics, including the definition of dharma, the classification of Vedic injunctions, the means of subsidiary application, and the principles governing ritual sequence (krama).
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_mimamsaparibhasa_krsnaya.attribution: Authorship is explicitly confirmed both in verse 2 (kriyate kṛṣṇayajvanā) and in the final colophon (iti śrīkṛṣṇayajvakṛtā mīmāṃsāparibhāṣā samāptā).
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_mimamsaparibhasa_krsnaya.coverage: complete — Complete text, containing the opening maṅgala verses through the concluding discussion of ritual sequence (krama) and final colophon.
translations: Swami Madhavananda, Mīmāṃsāparibhāṣā of Kṛṣṇa Yajvan. (English)

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_naiskarmyasiddhih.title: Naiṣkarmyasiddhi
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_naiskarmyasiddhih.author: Sureśvara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_naiskarmyasiddhih.summary: The Naiṣkarmyasiddhi ('Establishment of Actionlessness') is an independent prakaraṇa work in four adhyāyas composed in mixed verse and prose by Sureśvara, a direct disciple of Śaṅkarācārya. The text provides a systematic philosophical defense of Advaita Vedānta soteriology, arguing that liberation (mokṣa) is achieved solely through knowledge (jñāna) of the non-dual Self and rejecting the necessity of ritual action (karma) or the combination of knowledge and action (jñānakarmasamuccaya). It examines nescience (avidyā), the method of superimposition and rescission (adhyāropāpavāda), and the direct liberating knowledge generated by Upaniṣadic mahāvākyas.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_naiskarmyasiddhih.attribution: Consists of kārikās interlinked with prose connective explanations (sambandhokti / vṛtti) written by Sureśvara himself, as noted in the concluding verse 4.78.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_naiskarmyasiddhih.coverage: complete — Complete in four adhyāyas (chapters 1–4), containing both verse kārikās and authorial connective prose.
translations: Balasubramanian, R., trans. and ed. 1988. The Naiṣkarmyasiddhi of Sureśvara. Madras: University of Madras. (English)
Alston, A. J., trans. 1959. (English)

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayamayukhamalika.title: Nayamayūkhamālikā
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayamayukhamalika.author: Appayya Dīkṣita
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayamayukhamalika.summary: The Nayamayūkhamālikā constitutes the second section (dvitīyapariccheda) of the Caturmatasāra by Appayya Dīkṣita. In this work, the author summarises the adhikaraṇas of Bādarāyaṇa's Brahmasūtras strictly from the perspective of Rāmānuja's Viśiṣṭādvaita Vedānta (explicitly referenced in verse 2 as lakṣmaṇāryahṛdayānusāriṇī). It illustrates Appayya Dīkṣita's doxographical method of systematically expounding each school of Vedānta strictly on its own terms.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayamayukhamalika.attribution: The colophon explicitly attributes the text to Appayya Dīkṣita, son of Raṅgarājādhvarin, forming the second section (dvitīyapariccheda) of his fourfold Vedāntic summary Caturmatasāra.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayamayukhamalika.coverage: complete — Complete across all four adhyāyas of the Brahmasūtra according to Rāmānuja's Viśiṣṭādvaita system, concluding with adhyāya 4, pāda 4 (jagadvyāpāravarjādhikaraṇa) and the final work colophon.

SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayasangatimalika.title: Nayasaṅgatimālikā
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayasangatimalika.author: Lakṣmīpuram Śrīnivāsācārya
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayasangatimalika.summary: The Nayasaṅgatimālikā is a metrical Viśiṣṭādvaita treatise in 216 verses by Lakṣmīpuram Śrīnivāsācārya. Following Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya on the Brahmasūtra, it defines the technical forms of connection (saṅgati, such as upodghāta, apavāda, pratyudāhṛti, etc.) and delineates the precise logical linkage between each of the 156 adhikaraṇas across the four adhyāyas.
SA_GSP28_ilx_ws_nayasangatimalika.coverage: complete — Complete in 216 verses detailing the saṅgatis across all 156 adhikaraṇas of the Brahmasūtra.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirgunamanasapuja.title: Nirguṇamānasapūjā
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirgunamanasapuja.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirgunamanasapuja.summary: The Nirguṇamānasapūjā ('Mental Worship of the Attributeless Self') is an Advaita Vedānta devotional and philosophical poem in 33 verses framed as an inquiry between pupil and preceptor. It reinterprets standard ritual offerings of pūjā (such as invocation, seat, water, bath, garments, incense, light, and food offering) as modes of non-dual contemplative realization of the inner ātman beyond name, form, and ritual activity.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirgunamanasapuja.attribution: Colophon attributes authorship to Śaṅkara (pupil of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirgunamanasapuja.coverage: complete — Complete text in 33 verses plus pupil/guru dialogue markers and closing colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirvanamanjari.title: Nirvāṇamañjarī
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirvanamanjari.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirvanamanjari.summary: The Nirvāṇamañjarī is a short Advaita Vedānta hymn of 12 verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. It expounds the nature of the supreme Self through radical apophatic negations of empirical categories, bodily identity, castes, and life stages, alternately concluding stanzas with the refrains 'śivo 'ham' ('I am Śiva') and 'tad evāham asmi' ('That alone am I').
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirvanamanjari.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara in the closing colophon.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_nirvanamanjari.coverage: complete — Complete text in 12 verses plus concluding colophon.
translations: Translated, with Samkara's Nirvanasatka and Svarupasamdhana, by R. Krishnaswamy Aiyar. Srirangam 1965. (English)

SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayadipika.title: Nyāyadīpikā
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayadipika.author: Jayatīrtha
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayadipika.summary: The Nyāyadīpikā is Jayatīrtha's sub-commentary on Madhvācārya's Bhagavadgītātātparyanirṇaya in the Dvaita Vedānta tradition. The work elucidates Madhva's interpretation of the Bhagavadgītā, defending Dvaita tenets such as the absolute supremacy of Viṣṇu, the reality of the cosmos, and the fundamental ontological difference (bheda) between the individual soul (jīva) and Brahman.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayadipika.attribution: Composed by Jayatīrtha, prominent commentator in the Dvaita Vedānta school of Madhvācārya (Ānandatīrtha). Distinct from Dharmabhūṣaṇa's Jaina work of the same title.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayadipika.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on all 18 chapters of Madhva's Gītātātparyanirṇaya, terminating with the final verse and colophon of chapter 18.

SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayakalapasangrahah.title: Nyāyakalāpasaṅgraha
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayakalapasangrahah.summary: The Nyāyakalāpasaṅgraha (or Śārīrakanyāyakalāpasaṅgraha) is an anonymous versified summary of the Brahmasūtra adhikaraṇas composed by an adherent of the Viśiṣṭādvaita tradition. Following the interpretation of Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya, the work systematically condenses the prima facie views (pūrvapakṣa) and definitive conclusions (siddhānta) of each topic across all four adhyāyas.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayakalapasangrahah.attribution: A preliminary editorial header reads 'śrībhagavadrāmānujaviracite nyāyakalāpasaṅgrahaḥ', but the opening verse clearly shows that the author is a disciple or follower venerating Rāmānuja ('praṇamya rāmānuja saṃyamīśvaraṃ prabodhahetuṃ hṛdayāmbujanmanaḥ | karomi taddarśanamārgagocaraṃ śārīrakanyāyakalāpasaṃgraham || 1 ||').
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayakalapasangrahah.coverage: complete — Complete summary across all four adhyāyas (sixteen pādas) of the Brahmasūtra according to Rāmānuja's Śrībhāṣya, ending at 4.4.43.

SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayamuktavali.title: Nyāyamuktāvalī
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayamuktavali.author: Rāghavendratīrtha
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayamuktavali.summary: The Nyāyamuktāvalī is an adhikaraṇa-by-adhikaraṇa manual on Bādarāyaṇa's Brahmasūtras composed by the Dvaita Vedānta master Rāghavendra Tīrtha. Following the interpretations of Madhvācārya and Jayatīrtha, it analyzes each adhikaraṇa through five traditional members (viṣaya, saṃśaya, pūrvapakṣa, siddhānta, and prayojana) along with logical transitions (saṅgati). It provides a concise digest for studying the Dvaita exegesis of the Brahmasūtras.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayamuktavali.attribution: Authored by Rāghavendrayati, disciple of Sudhīndratīrtha. Opening line reads 'śrīrāghavendrayatikṛtaśrīnyāyamuktāvaliḥ' and the colophon to adhyāya 4 pāda 4 reads: 'śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācārya śrīmatsudhīndragurupādaśiṣyarāghavendrayatikṛtāyāṃ nyāyamuktāvalyāṃ caturthādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ'.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayamuktavali.coverage: complete — Complete in four adhyāyas (all 16 pādas), covering the Brahmasūtras from 1.1.1 to 4.4.11.

SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayasiddhantamuktavali.title: Kārikāvalī with Nyāyasiddhāntamuktāvalī
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayasiddhantamuktavali.author: Viśvanāthapañcānana
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayasiddhantamuktavali.summary: The Kārikāvalī (also known as Bhāṣāpariccheda) together with its auto-commentary, the Nyāyasiddhāntamuktāvalī, is a standard 17th-century manual of the syncretic Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika system composed by Viśvanātha Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya. Spanning 168 metric kārikās and accompanying prose, the work systematically explains the seven ontological categories (dravya, guṇa, karma, sāmānya, viśeṣa, samavāya, and abhāva) alongside the four Nyāya means of valid cognition (pratyakṣa, anumāna, upamāna, and śabda). Due to its precision and accessible pedagogical organization, it became one of the standard foundational textbooks of Navya-Nyāya philosophy across traditional pandit schools.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayasiddhantamuktavali.attribution: Both the 168 kārikās and the Muktāvalī commentary are traditionally attributed in the text's opening stanzas (vv. 2–3) and final colophon to Viśvanātha Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya, son of Vidyānivāsa Bhaṭṭācārya (fl. early 17th century).
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_nyayasiddhantamuktavali.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all 168 kārikās of the Kārikāvalī and the full Muktāvalī commentary, concluding with the guṇanirūpaṇa and final colophons.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancadasi.title: Pañcadaśī
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancadasi.author: Vidyāraṇya
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancadasi.summary: The Pañcadaśī ('Fifteen Chapters') is an influential 14th-century manual of Advaita Vedānta traditionally attributed to Vidyāraṇya (and in part to Bhāratītīrtha). It is divided into three pentads corresponding to the tripartite nature of Brahman: Viveka-pañcaka (discrimination of existence, sat), Dīpa-pañcaka (illumination of consciousness, cit), and Ānanda-pañcaka (nature of bliss, ānanda). Through pedagogical metaphors—such as the picture-canvas (citradīpa) and the stage lamp (nāṭakadīpa)—the work systematically expounds non-dual ontology, epistemology, and liberation (jīvanmukti).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancadasi.coverage: complete — Complete root text comprising all fifteen prakaraṇas across the three pentads (viveka-, dīpa-, and ānanda-pañcaka), ending at chapter 15 (Viṣayānanda) verse 35 and the final colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancapadikavivaranam.title: Pañcapādikāvivaraṇa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancapadikavivaranam.author: Prakāśātman
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancapadikavivaranam.summary: The Pañcapādikāvivaraṇa by Prakāśātman is a celebrated sub-commentary on Padmapāda's Pañcapādikā (which comments on Śaṅkara's Brahmasūtrabhāṣya on the Catussūtrī). It established the Vivaraṇa school of Advaita Vedānta, defending the doctrine of ignorance (avidyā/ajñāna) as a positive entity (bhāvarūpa) located in Brahman as both locus and object, and advocating the reflection theory (pratibimbavāda) of the individual self (jīva).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancapadikavivaranam.attribution: Chapter colophons style him 'Śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakānanyānubhavapūjyapādaśiṣyasvaprakāśānubhavabhagavat' (i.e. Svaprakāśānubhava / Prakāśātman, pupil of Ananyānubhava).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancapadikavivaranam.coverage: complete — Complete text across all nine varṇakas, terminating with the final colophon of the 9th varṇaka: 'iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakānanyānubhavapūjyapādaśiṣyasvaprakāśānubhavabhagavataḥ kṛtau pañcapādikāvivaraṇe samanvayādhikaraṇaṃ nāma navamaṃ varṇakaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancikaranam.title: Pañcīkaraṇa
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancikaranam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancikaranam.summary: A very concise Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa text outlining the quintuplication (pañcīkaraṇa) of the five subtle elements to form the gross universe. It details the correspondences between the three bodies (sthūla, sūkṣma, kāraṇa), the three states of consciousness (jāgrat, svapna, suṣupti), the cosmic manifestations (Virāj, Hiraṇyagarbha, Avyākṛta), and the phonetic components of Oṃ (A-U-M), culminating in meditative samādhi on the non-dual Self through the mahāvākyas.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancikaranam.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to Śaṅkarācārya (disciple of Govinda Bhagavatpāda). An early Vārttika attributed to Sureśvara attests to its traditional acceptance in early Advaita circles.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pancikaranam.coverage: complete — Complete short prose prakaraṇa text from the opening line (athātaḥ paramahaṃsānāṃ samādhividhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ) to the colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prabodhasudhakarah.title: Prabodhasudhākara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prabodhasudhakarah.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prabodhasudhakarah.summary: The Prabodhasudhākara ('Nectar-Ocean of Awakening') is an Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa treatise in 257 verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. Written primarily in āryā metre, the text expounds the stages of spiritual awakening starting from dispassion (vairāgya) through the contemplation of bodily transience and suffering, discernment between Self and non-Self (ātmabodha), control of the mind and senses, and culminates in intense devotion (bhakti) to Kṛṣṇa as integral to liberation.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prabodhasudhakarah.attribution: Traditional attribution to Ādi Śaṅkara is asserted in the concluding colophon ('śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau').
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prabodhasudhakarah.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all 257 verses and the final colophon.
translations: Samvid (transl.), Prabodhasudhākara. (English)

SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_pramanalaksanam.title: Pramāṇalakṣaṇa
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_pramanalaksanam.author: Madhva
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_pramanalaksanam.summary: The Pramāṇalakṣaṇa is one of the ten short philosophical treatises (Daśaprakaraṇa) authored by Madhva (Ānandatīrtha, 13th c.), the founder of Dvaita Vedānta. Presenting epistemology in accordance with the Brahmatarka, Madhva defines valid knowledge (yathārthaṃ pramāṇam) and divides pramāṇa into kevalapramāṇa (veridical cognition) and anupramāṇa (means of knowledge: perception, inference, and scriptural testimony). The treatise systematically analyzes definitions, scopes, and fallacies, defending Dvaita realism against Advaita and other rivals.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_pramanalaksanam.attribution: Madhva is commonly referenced as Ānandatīrtha in traditional colophons.
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_pramanalaksanam.coverage: complete — Complete mūla text consisting of opening mangala verse, prose philosophical sutras/vṛtti, closing verses, and final colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pramanapaddhatih.title: Pramāṇapaddhati
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pramanapaddhatih.author: Jayatīrtha
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pramanapaddhatih.summary: The Pramāṇapaddhati is an influential primer of Dvaita epistemology and logic composed by Jayatīrtha. Systematizing the epistemological doctrine set forth in Madhvācārya's Pramāṇalakṣaṇa, the treatise is divided into three sections corresponding to the three valid means of knowledge accepted in Dvaita: perception (pratyakṣa), inference (anumāna), and verbal testimony (āgama). It provides clear definitions of pramāṇa, discusses truth and error, expounds syllogistic reasoning and fallacies (hetvābhāsas), and defends the authoritativeness and intrinsic validity (svataḥprāmāṇya) of Vedic scripture.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pramanapaddhatih.attribution: Manual of epistemology in the Dvaita Vedānta school, authored by Jayatīrtha.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_pramanapaddhatih.coverage: complete — Complete text ending with granthaścāyaṃ saṃpūrṇaḥ.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih.title: Prauḍhānubhūti
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih.summary: The Prauḍhānubhūti ('Mature Direct Realization') is an Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa in 17 verses attributed to Śaṅkara. It articulates the practitioner's non-dual realization of pure consciousness (cit), negating identification with the physical body, vital breath, mind, and intellect, and asserting the non-existence of dualistic phenomena from the paramārtha standpoint.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih.attribution: Attributed to Śaṅkara in the concluding colophon.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih.coverage: complete — Complete text in 17 verses with concluding colophon.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih_samulam.title: Prauḍhānubhūti
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih_samulam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih_samulam.summary: The Prauḍhānubhūti is a short Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa in 17 verses attributed to Śaṅkara. It celebrates direct non-dual realization (anubhūti), asserting that the true self is pure consciousness, unattached, and identical with Brahman, while phenomenal duality is merely an illusion superimposed on it.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih_samulam.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya and catalogued among his works (e.g. Potter entry 379.48).
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_praudhanubhutih_samulam.coverage: complete — Complete in 17 verses, ending with the colophon 'iti prauḍhānubhūtiḥ samāptā'.

SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prasnottararatnamalika.title: Praśnottararatnamālikā
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prasnottararatnamalika.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prasnottararatnamalika.summary: The Praśnottararatnamālikā ('Garland of Jewels of Questions and Answers') is a didactic gnomic poem of 67 verses in āryā metre structured as a series of moral and philosophical catechisms. It addresses virtues such as truthfulness, discernment (viveka), charity, guru devotion, and liberation from worldly suffering. Widely esteemed for its concise practical wisdom, it was preserved in distinct versions across Hindu, Jain, and Buddhist lineages.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prasnottararatnamalika.attribution: Attributed in this Brahmanical Advaita recension to Śaṅkarācārya. The gnomic text exists in multiple recensions: the Jain tradition attributes it to the Rāṣṭrakūṭa king Amoghavarṣa I or Vimalacandra, while a Tibetan translation in the Tanjur attributes it to a Buddhist tradition.
SA_GSP33_ilx_ws_prasnottararatnamalika.coverage: complete — Complete 67-verse text of the Brahmanical recension including opening and concluding verses and colophon.

SA_GS26_ilx_ws_pranavakalpah.title: Praṇavakalpa
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_pranavakalpah.author: Madhva
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_pranavakalpah.summary: The Praṇavakalpa is a short liturgical and initiation tract attributed to Madhva (Ānandatīrtha) on the recitation and meditation of the sacred syllable Om (Praṇava) according to Dvaita Vedānta. It sets out the preceptor's instruction to a renunciant disciple, prescribing the visualization (dhyāna) of Nārāyaṇa within the heart, an oath renouncing monism (advaita) and affirming the eternal ontological distinction between Viṣṇu and souls, and rules for daily japa and scriptural study.
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_pranavakalpah.attribution: Attributed to Ānandatīrtha (Madhva) in the heading ('śrīmadānandātīrthabhagavatpādapraṇītasarvamūlagranthāḥ') and in the closing colophon of the e-text. Not to be confused with other works called Praṇavakalpa (e.g. the Skandapurāṇa-affiliated Praṇavakalpa, or the excerpt from the Mantraprastāva of the Vaiṣṇavasaṃhitā listed by Bendall).
SA_GS26_ilx_ws_pranavakalpah.coverage: complete — 28 numbered verses followed by the author colophon ('iti śrīmadānandatīrthabhagavatpādācāryaviracitaḥ praṇavakalpaḥ samāptaḥ') and a closing 'iti praṇavakalpaḥ / śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇamastu'.

SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_purvapaksiyavyaptih.title: Pūrvapakṣīyavyāptilakṣaṇa
SA_GSP29_ilx_ws_purvapaksiyavyaptih.summary: A brief Navya-Nyāya pedagogical manual (*kroḍapatra*) explicating the first prima facie definition (*pūrvapakṣa-lakṣaṇa*) of invariable concomitance (*vyāpti*) from Gaṅgeśa's *Vyāptipañcaka*, formulated as *sādhyābhāvavadavṛttitvam* ('non-occurrence in that which possesses the absence of the probandum').
