SA_GK19_ilx_ws_alankarasangrahah.title: Alaṅkārasaṅgraha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_alankarasangrahah.author: Amṛtānandayogin
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_alankarasangrahah.summary: The Alaṅkārasaṅgraha is a treatise on Sanskrit poetics (alaṅkāraśāstra) and dramaturgy (nāṭyaśāstra) composed in 11 paricchedas by Amṛtānandayogin under the patronage of King Manma. It integrates poetic theory with theatrical rules, discussing auspicious syllabic patterns (varṇagaṇa), word and meaning (śabdārtha), aesthetic sentiment (rasa), heroes and heroines (netṛbheda), figures of speech (alaṅkāra), poetic faults and virtues (doṣa and guṇa), dramatic junctures and plots (sandhyaṅga), major dramatic genres (rūpaka), theatrical embellishments (nāṭyālaṅkāra), and court panegyric compositions (cāṭuprabandha).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_alankarasangrahah.attribution: Authored by Amṛtānandayogin (also named Amṛtānandayogīndra in colophons) at the request of King Manma (Manmabhūpati), son of Bhaktibhūmipati.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_alankarasangrahah.coverage: complete — Complete text in 11 paricchedas (chapters 1–11), concluding with the colophon of the 11th pariccheda on cāṭuprabandhalakṣaṇa and 'alaṅkārasaṅgrahaḥ sampūrṇaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ambastotram_svami_vivekan.title: Ambāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ambastotram_svami_vivekan.author: Vivekānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ambastotram_svami_vivekan.summary: The Ambāstotra is a seven-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn dedicated to the Mother Goddess, composed by Swami Vivekananda. Composed in the vasantatilakā metre, the hymn contemplates the Divine Mother as the ruler of both joy and sorrow, life and death, concluding with an expression of self-surrender (śaraṇāgati).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ambastotram_svami_vivekan.attribution: A modern Sanskrit stotra composed by Swami Vivekananda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ambastotram_svami_vivekan.coverage: complete — Complete text in 7 verses in vasantatilakā metre.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_annapurnastotram.title: Annapūrṇāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_annapurnastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_annapurnastotram.summary: The Annapūrṇāstotra is a devotional hymn dedicated to Goddess Annapūrṇā as the presiding deity of nourishment and benevolence in Vārāṇasī (Kāśī). The primary section consists of ten verses characterized by internal rhyming epithets ending in the refrain requesting spiritual and material alms (bhikṣā). The concluding verses implore the goddess for knowledge and dispassion (jñānavairāgyasiddhi), declaring Pārvatī and Maheśvara to be the universal parents.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_annapurnastotram.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya, as reflected in the colophon (iti śrīmacchaṃkarācāryaviracitamannapūrṇāstotraṃ saṃpūrṇam).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_annapurnastotram.coverage: complete — Complete in 15 verses (a 10-verse refrain hymn followed by 3 supplementary devotional verses and 2 widely cited closing ślokas).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparadhaksamapanastotra.title: Aparādhakṣamāpanastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparadhaksamapanastotra.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparadhaksamapanastotra.summary: The Aparādhakṣamāpanastotra is a 10-verse devotional hymn addressed to Lord Dattātreya by Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī. In each verse, the poet laments failing to recite the divine name during successive stages of life—from previous births and intrauterine existence to infancy, youth, and decrepitude—ending each stanza with a fervent plea for compassionate pardon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparadhaksamapanastotra.attribution: Attributed in verse 10 ('dattaśiṣyeṇa') and the final colophon to Vāsudevānandasarasvatī Svāmī Mahārāja.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparadhaksamapanastotra.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra in 10 verses with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparajitastotram.title: Aparājitāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparajitastotram.summary: A popular protective hymn and ritual formula (vidyā/kavaca) dedicated to Goddess Aparājitā in her Vaiṣṇavī aspect, presented as a teaching imparted by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya. It combines stotra verses with prose dhāraṇī-like mantra invocations of Viṣṇu, his incarnations, and the goddess to ward off malevolent spirits, diseases, sorcery, and other dangers.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparajitastotram.attribution: Internal framing attributes the teaching of the vidyā to the sage Mārkaṇḍeya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aparajitastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of the stotra in 46 verses/sections including introductory viniyoga, dhyāna, prose mantra passages, and concluding kṣamāpanā verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarinatesvarastotram.title: Ardhanārīnaṭeśvarastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarinatesvarastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarinatesvarastotram.summary: The Ardhanārīnaṭeśvarastotra (or Ardhanārīnaṭeśvarāṣṭaka) is an eight-verse hymn dedicated to the androgynous composite form of Śiva and Pārvatī (Ardhanārīśvara). In each stanza, the poet pairs and contrasts the feminine half (Pārvatī) and the masculine half (Śiva) in appearance, ornaments, and cosmic roles (such as creation through lāsya and cosmic dissolution through tāṇḍava), closing each verse with the dual refrain 'namaḥ śivāyai ca namaḥ śivāya'. Traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya, the poem concludes with a phalaśruti verse promising auspiciousness and longevity.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarinatesvarastotram.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkara, pupil of Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda (śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryaśrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavatpraṇītam).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarinatesvarastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 verses plus 1 phalaśruti verse (9 verses total) and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastaka.title: Ardhanārīśvarāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastaka.author: Upamanyu
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastaka.summary: The Ardhanārīśvarāṣṭaka is an eight-verse devotional hymn celebrating the combined androgynous manifestation of Śiva and Pārvatī (Ardhanārīśvara). In each stanza, the dual attributes, ornaments, and cosmic roles of the goddess (Śivā) and the god (Śiva) are contrasted before culminating in the refrain 'namaḥ śivāyai ca namaḥ śivāya'. It is traditionally attributed to the sage Upamanyu.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastaka.attribution: Ascribed in verse 9 ('ardhanārīśvarastotraṃ upamanyukṛtaṃ tvidam') and the colophon to the puranic sage Upamanyu.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastaka.coverage: complete — Complete text containing 8 stanzas in Upajāti metre contrasting Śivā and Śiva, with the refrain 'namaḥ śivāyai ca namaḥ śivāya', plus 1 concluding phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastottarasat.title: Ardhanārīśvarāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastottarasat.summary: The Ardhanārīśvarāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra is a devotional hymn of 108 paired names honoring Ardhanārīśvara, the composite form of Śiva and Devī. Across 39 ślokas, each name for the Śakti aspect (e.g. Cāmuṇḍīkāmbā, Pārvatī) is balanced by a corresponding title for the Śiva aspect (e.g. Śrīkaṇṭha, Parameśvara), presenting parallel iconographic traits, epithets, and mythological exploits. The closing colophon traces the stotra to the Skandapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastottarasat.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to the Skandapurāṇa (iti śrīskānde ardhanārīśvarāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotram).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ardhanarisvarastottarasat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 40 verses (39 verses enumerating 108 complementary name pairs for the feminine and masculine halves of the composite deity, concluding with 1 phalaśruti verse) and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aucityavicaracarca.title: Aucityavicāracarcā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aucityavicaracarca.author: Kṣemendra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aucityavicaracarca.summary: The Aucityavicāracarcā is an 11th-century treatise on poetic theory by the Kashmiri polymath Kṣemendra. Formulating the Aucitya doctrine of alaṅkāraśāstra, Kṣemendra establishes appropriateness or propriety (aucitya) as the vital essence (jīvita) of poetic art, arguing that poetic ornaments (alaṅkāra) and qualities (guṇa) fail without it. The treatise defines and analyzes distinct loci of propriety, examining each through classical quotations illustrative of poetic excellence or flaw.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aucityavicaracarca.attribution: Composed by Kṣemendra (also known by his title Vyāsadāsa), son of Prakāśendra, during the reign of King Ananta of Kashmir, as recorded in the concluding verses and colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aucityavicaracarca.coverage: complete — Complete work containing introductory verses, kārikās with autovṛtti and illustrative citations across the varieties of aucitya, and all closing verses through the final colophon.
translations: Suryakanta, Kṣemendra Studies: Together with an English Translation of His Kavikaṇṭhābharaṇa, Aucityavicāracarcā and Suvṛttatilaka, Poona: Oriental Book Agency, 1954. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutagita.title: Avadhūtagītā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutagita.author: Dattātreya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutagita.summary: The Avadhūtagītā is a classical text of radical non-dualism (Advaita) traditionally ascribed to the sage Dattātreya. Across eight chapters, it expounds the true nature of the Self (ātman) as all-pervasive, immutable consciousness entirely free from superimposition, ritual action, bondage, and release. The closing chapter gives an esoteric acrostic etymology defining the characteristics of an avadhūta through the four syllables a, va, dhū, and ta.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutagita.attribution: Ascribed to Dattātreya, explicitly confirmed in colophon verse 8.10 ('dattātreyāvadhūtena nirmitānandarūpiṇā').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutastakam.title: Avadhūtāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutastakam.summary: A 15-verse non-dual Vedāntic hymn of praise (stuti) eulogizing the avadhūta (identified in the opening rubric with Śukadeva) as an embodiment of the unconditioned Ātman. Each verse extols his freedom from mental conditioning, grief, and dualities, concluding with the regular refrain 'hy avadhūtaṃ namāmy aham'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutastakam.attribution: The introductory line designates the text as a stuti of Śukadeva ('atha paramahaṃsa śiromaṇyavadhūtaśrīsvāmīśukadevastutiḥ'), but no individual author is attributed in the text or colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avadhutastakam.coverage: complete — Complete as transmitted in 15 verses, concluded by the colophon 'iti avadhūtāṣṭakaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avimarakam.title: Avimāraka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avimarakam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avimarakam.summary: Avimāraka is a six-act Sanskrit drama traditionally attributed to Bhāsa, dramatizing a romantic tale likely drawn from the Bṛhatkathā cycle. The narrative follows Prince Viṣṇusena, who lives incognito in the outcast community under the name Avimāraka due to a sage's curse, and falls in love with Princess Kuraṅgī after rescuing her from an elephant attack. Aided by magical elements—most notably an invisibility-granting ring given by a vidyādhara—the lovers secretly unite before his noble lineage is revealed by the sage Nārada, culminating in their formal marriage.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_avimarakam.coverage: complete — Complete drama in six acts (aṅkas 1–6), including dramatis personae prefix, interspersed Sanskrit chāyā for Prākrit speeches, and the final bharatavākya.
translations: A. C. Woolner and L. Sarup (transl.). (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjanasailanathastotram.title: Añjanaśailanāthastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjanasailanathastotram.author: Vādibhītikarārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjanasailanathastotram.summary: A 14-verse Śrīvaiṣṇava hymn of praise addressed to Lord Veṅkaṭeśvara of Añjanaśaila (Tirupati). Verses 2–13 describe the divine form, compassion, and miraculous boons granted to devotees, ending with the recurring refrain 'ārādhayāmi harimañjanaśailanātham'. The concluding verse attributes the composition to Vādibhītikarārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjanasailanathastotram.attribution: Attributed in verse 14 to Vādibhītikarārya ('vādibhītikarāryeṇa racitā').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjanasailanathastotram.coverage: complete — Complete stotra in 14 verses (13 praise verses plus 1 phalaśruti/signature verse).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asvatthastotram.title: Aśvatthastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asvatthastotram.summary: A devotional hymn praising the sacred Aśvattha tree (Ficus religiosa), cast as an exposition by Brahmā to Nārada. The text identifies the tree with various deities and details ritual circumambulation (pradakṣiṇa) along with rewards such as the alleviation of diseases, eradication of sins, and attainment of longevity and prosperity.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asvatthastotram.attribution: Traditional hymn framed as a dialogue between Nārada and Brahmā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asvatthastotram.coverage: complete — Complete short hymn with introductory dialogue, phalaśruti, and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastotram.title: Aṅgārakastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastotram.summary: A short devotional hymn of seven verses dedicated to Aṅgāraka (Mars/Bhauma), traditionally ascribed to the Skandapurāṇa. It enumerates epithets of Mars and details the phala (benefits) of recitation, particularly the alleviation of debt, poverty, and planetary afflictions.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastotram.attribution: The introductory viniyoga formula attributes the hymn to Virūpāṅgiras as ṛṣi, while the concluding colophon assigns it to the Skandapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastotram.coverage: complete — Complete 7-verse stotra with introductory viniyoga and concluding Skandapurāṇa colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastottarasatanamav.title: Aṅgārakāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastottarasatanamav.summary: A litany of devotional names (aṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī) formulated for the liturgical worship and propitiation of Aṅgāraka (Maṅgala / Mars), one of the nine planetary deities (navagraha). Each name is recited in the dative case framed by 'oṃ' and 'namaḥ', invoking the deity's astrological roles (ruler of Aries and Scorpio), mythological lineage (son of the Earth, born in Bharadvāja gotra), iconography (four-armed, ram-mounted, spear-bearing), and protective virtues.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_angarakastottarasatanamav.coverage: complete — Complete 108-name ritual litany (nāmāvalī) with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astalaksmistotram.title: Aṣṭalakṣmīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astalaksmistotram.summary: An eight-verse devotional hymn invoking the eight forms of the goddess Lakṣmī (Aṣṭalakṣmī): Ādilakṣmī, Dhānyalakṣmī, Dhairyalakṣmī, Gajalakṣmī, Santānalakṣmī, Vijayalakṣmī, Vidyālakṣmī, and Dhanalakṣmī. Each verse praises the attributes of one manifestation and closes with a petition for protection addressed to the consort of Madhusūdana (Viṣṇu).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astalaksmistotram.attribution: A popular devotional hymn of indeterminate late traditional authorship. Verse 6 explicitly refers to Śaṅkarācārya and his Kanakadhārāstotra ('kanakadharāstuti vaibhava vandita śaṅkara deśikamānya pade'), demonstrating that the stotra postdates Śaṅkara.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astalaksmistotram.coverage: complete — Complete in 8 verses, addressing the eight standard aspects of Lakṣmī: Ādilakṣmī, Dhānyalakṣmī, Dhairyalakṣmī, Gajalakṣmī, Santānalakṣmī, Vijayalakṣmī, Vidyālakṣmī, and Dhanalakṣmī.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astadasasaktipithastotram.title: Aṣṭādaśaśaktipīṭhastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astadasasaktipithastotram.summary: A short Śākta devotional hymn of six verses enumerating the traditional eighteen primary sacred seats of the Goddess (Aṣṭādaśa Mahāśaktipīṭha) and their tutelary deities across South Asia (including Śāṅkarī in Laṅkā, Kāmākṣī in Kāñcī, and Sarasvatī in Kaśmīra). It concludes with a brief phalaśruti promising removal of disease and destruction of enemies upon twilight recitation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_astadasasaktipithastotram.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 6 anuṣṭubh verses followed by the concluding formula 'iti aṣṭādaśaśaktipīṭhastutiḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_attalasundarastakam.title: Aṭṭālasundarāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_attalasundarastakam.summary: The Aṭṭālasundarāṣṭaka is a short Śaiva devotional hymn in eight verses (with a concluding phalaśruti) addressed to Śiva as Sundareśvara of Madurai (Aṭṭālasundara). Excerpted from the Hālāsyamāhātmya, the stotra is spoken by the legendary king Vikrama Pāṇḍya, praising Śiva as the creator and protector of the universe and the tutelary deity (kuladaivata) of the Pāṇḍya dynasty, with each stanza ending in the refrain 'kalaye'ṭṭālasundaram'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_attalasundarastakam.attribution: Colophon states 'iti śrīhālāsyamāhātmye vikramapāṇḍyakṛtaṃ aṭṭālasundarāṣṭakam', presenting it as a hymn uttered by King Vikrama Pāṇḍya within the Hālāsyamāhātmya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_attalasundarastakam.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 8 verses plus a phalaśruti verse (9 verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhajagovindam.title: Bhajagovindastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhajagovindam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhajagovindam.summary: The Bhajagovindastotra is a didactic hymn traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. The poem warns of the futility of worldly vanity, scholastic grammar, wealth, and sensual pleasure, urging devotion to Govinda and detachment from the cycle of rebirth (saṃsāra). In this recension of 33 verses, verse 32 references Śaṅkara's disciples instructing a grammarian.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhajagovindam.coverage: complete — Complete 33-verse composite recension, preceded by a prefixed Hare Kṛṣṇa mahāmantra in lines [0]–[3].

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bharatakavacam.title: Bharatakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bharatakavacam.summary: A protective hymn (kavaca) dedicated to Bharata, the younger brother of Rāma, excerpted from the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa. Spoken by the sage Agastya, it contains standard ritual preliminaries (nyāsa, dhyāna) followed by protective anatomical invocations invoking Bharata under various devotional and mythological epithets, and concludes with a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bharatakavacam.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vālmīki as an excerpt from the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa; Agastya serves as the speaker in the frame narrative.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bharatakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete stotra as extracted from the Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Manoharakāṇḍa), comprising ṛṣyādinyāsa, aṅganyāsa, dhyāna, the kavaca verses, and concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavanyastakam.title: Bhavānyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavanyastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavanyastakam.summary: The Bhavānyaṣṭaka is a devotional hymn of eight stanzas in the bhujaṅgaprayāta metre addressed to the goddess Bhavānī, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. Each verse concludes with the refrain 'gatistvaṃ gatistvaṃ tvamekā bhavāni' ('You alone are my refuge, my sole refuge, O Bhavānī!'), expressing complete surrender (śaraṇāgati / prapatti), confession of human frailty, and renunciation of worldly reliance.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavanyastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 8 verses with final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhojaprabandhah.title: Bhojaprabandha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhojaprabandhah.author: Ballāla
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhojaprabandhah.summary: The Bhojaprabandha is a popular collection of biographical anecdotes composed by Ballāla. Set at the court of the Paramāra ruler Bhoja of Dhārā, it gathers prominent classical Sanskrit poets—such as Kālidāsa—into a literary circle, emphasizing courtly wit, verse exchanges, and the king's boundless generosity.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhojaprabandhah.coverage: complete — Complete text in mixed prose and verse, concluding with verse 328 and the colophon 'śrīmanmahārājādhirājasya dhārānagarādhīśasya bhojarājasya prabandhaḥ samāptimaphāṇīt'.
translations: Louis H. Gray, trans. The Narrative of Bhoja by Ballala of Benares. American Oriental Series 34. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasah_saradatanay.title: Bhāvaprakāśa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasah_saradatanay.author: Bhāvamiśra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasah_saradatanay.summary: The Bhāvaprakāśa of Bhāvamiśra is an Āyurvedic treatise structured into three parts (Pūrvakhaṇḍa, Madhyakhaṇḍa, and Uttarakhaṇḍa), providing a synthesis of classical Indian medicine, therapeutics, and rasāyana.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasah_saradatanay.attribution: Attributed to Bhāvamiśra in the e-text opening and scholarly literature.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bhavaprakasah_saradatanay.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all three divisions: Pūrvakhaṇḍa, Madhyakhaṇḍa, and Uttarakhaṇḍa (ending at line [21093] 'iti trisaptatitamo rasāyanādhikāraḥ samāptaḥ 73', followed by the author's closing benedictions and line [21102] 'samāptaścāyaṃ granthaḥ').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bilvastakam.title: Bilvāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bilvastakam.summary: The Bilvāṣṭaka is a popular devotional hymn consisting of eight verses in praise of offering trifoliate bilva (bael) leaves in the worship of Śiva. Each verse highlights the religious merit and expiation of sins earned through offering a single bilva leaf, followed here by an additional ninth verse listing the eight leaves regarded as bilva substitutes (aṣṭabilvāni).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_bilvastakam.coverage: complete — Complete 8 verses of the hymn plus an additional verse (verse 9) enumerating the eight plants considered equivalent to bilva (aṣṭabilvāni).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmadevakrtaramastutih.title: Brahmadevakṛtarāmastuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmadevakrtaramastutih.summary: A 9-verse devotional hymn praising Rāma uttered by Brahmā, extracted from the Yuddhakāṇḍa of the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa. Extols Rāma, identifying him with non-dual supreme consciousness (sattāmātra, dṛśirūpa) who assumed human form, ending with a phalaśruti verse.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmadevakrtaramastutih.coverage: complete — Complete standalone hymn of 9 verses (8 verses of stuti plus 1 phalaśruti verse).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmajnanavali.title: Brahmajñānāvalīmālā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmajnanavali.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmajnanavali.summary: The Brahmajñānāvalīmālā is a short Advaita Vedānta prakaraṇa of 21 verses traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. It summarizes non-dual metaphysics and the nature of the self through rhythmic, meditative declarations of identity with unattached, non-dual consciousness (Brahman). Verse 20 contains the celebrated summary maxim of Advaita: 'brahma satyaṃ jaganmithyā jīvo brahmaiva nāparaḥ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_brahmajnanavali.coverage: complete — Complete text of 21 verses with closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balacaritam.title: Bālacarita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balacaritam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balacaritam.summary: The Bālacarita ('The Deeds of the Boy') is a five-act Sanskrit drama dramatizing the early life of Kṛṣṇa. The narrative follows his birth in Mathurā, his transfer to Gokula, the subduing of the serpent Kāliya, the slaying of various demons (such as Dhenuka, Ariṣṭa, and Keśin), and his eventual overthrow of King Kaṃsa in the wrestling arena. A distinctive dramaturgical feature of the play is the stage personification of Viṣṇu's divine weapons and an appearance by the goddess Kātyāyanī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balacaritam.coverage: complete — Complete drama in five acts (aṅkas 1–5), including prologue (sthāpanā), Prakrit passages with inline Sanskrit chāyā, and the concluding bharatavākya (ending: 'pañcamo'ṅkaḥ | avasitaṃ bālacaritam |').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balamukundastakam.title: Bālamukundāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balamukundastakam.author: Bilvamaṅgala
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balamukundastakam.summary: The Bālamukundāṣṭaka is a short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn in eight verses addressed to baby Kṛṣṇa (Bālamukunda). The verses celebrate iconic episodes and forms of Kṛṣṇa's early childhood, opening with the famous depiction of the infant lying upon a banyan leaf (vaṭapatraśāyī) sucking his lotus-foot, followed by scenes of butter-stealing, the subduing of the serpent Kāliya, and the breaking of the Yamalārjuna trees.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_balamukundastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 8 verses with final colophon line.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campakastakam.title: Campakāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campakastakam.author: Kambham Cokkaṇṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campakastakam.summary: The Campakāṣṭaka is an eight-verse devotional hymn (stotra) composed in praise of Viṣṇu worshipped at Campakāpurī. Each stanza concludes with the refrain 'campakāpurīnivāsamānivāsamāśraye' and praises the deity's celestial iconography, sacred ornaments, and mythological deeds.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campakastakam.attribution: Attributed in Sanskrit Wikisource and ilx_skt metadata to Kambham-cokkaṇṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campakastakam.coverage: complete — Complete eight-verse devotional hymn (aṣṭaka) with the refrain 'campakāpurīnivāsamānivāsamāśraye'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campubharatam.title: Campūbhārata (fragment)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campubharatam.author: Anantabhaṭṭa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campubharatam.summary: The Campūbhārata (or Bhāratacampū) of Anantabhaṭṭa is a Sanskrit campūkāvya (mixed verse and prose) that narrates the events of the Mahābhārata. This e-text is an abandoned digital fragment containing only the opening section of the first stabaka followed by isolated verses.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campubharatam.attribution: The Campūbhārata (or Bhāratacampū) is attributed to Anantabhaṭṭa (also styled Anantakavi).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campubharatam.coverage: fragment — Contains only the opening portion of Stabaka 1 (verses 1–26 with intervening prose) followed by three isolated verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campuramayanam.title: Campūrāmāyaṇa (incomplete)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campuramayanam.author: Bhoja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campuramayanam.summary: The Campūrāmāyaṇa (also known as Rāmāyaṇacampū) is a Sanskrit campū work retelling the Rāmāyaṇa narrative, attributed to Bhoja (with continuation by Lakṣmaṇasūri). This online transcription is incomplete, containing only Bālakāṇḍa, Ayodhyākāṇḍa, and an unfinished Sundarakāṇḍa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campuramayanam.attribution: Attributed to Bhoja, with a continuation by Lakṣmaṇakavi / Lakṣmaṇasūri.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_campuramayanam.coverage: partial — Incomplete. Contains Bālakāṇḍa, Ayodhyākāṇḍa, and part of Sundarakāṇḍa (ending at v. 68 in the Madhuvana episode).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candramaulisvarabhujangas.title: Candramaulīśvarabhujaṅgastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candramaulisvarabhujangas.author: Śaṅkarānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candramaulisvarabhujangas.summary: A 13-verse Śaiva devotional hymn composed in the bhujaṅgaprayāta meter in praise of Śiva Candramaulīśvara, attributed to Śaṅkarānandācārya. The verses extol Śiva's cosmic form, his mythic attributes, and his ascetic iconography, typically concluding with an abbreviated refrain invoking Śiva, Ambā, and Candramauli.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candramaulisvarabhujangas.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkarānandācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candramaulisvarabhujangas.coverage: complete — Complete text of 13 stanzas with introductory heading and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_caturvimsatinamapratipada.title: Caturviṃśatināmapratipādakacūrṇikā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_caturvimsatinamapratipada.author: Bhadrācala Rāmadāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_caturvimsatinamapratipada.summary: The Caturviṃśatināmapratipādakacūrṇikā is a rhythmic Sanskrit devotional prose hymn (cūrṇikā) attributed to Bhadrācala Rāmadāsa. It recounts the narrative of the Rāmāyaṇa by correlating successive episodes of Rāma's life with the twenty-four sacred names of Viṣṇu (Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, etc.), concluding with praises of Rāma at Bhadrāchalam.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_caturvimsatinamapratipada.attribution: Traditional attribution to Bhadrācala Rāmadāsa, as stated in the opening and closing lines of the e-text.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_caturvimsatinamapratipada.coverage: complete — Complete text of the stotra in prose (cūrṇikā), running through the twenty-four canonical names of Viṣṇu from Mukunda/Keśava to Kṛṣṇa and concluding with the colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candikastakam.title: Caṇḍikāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candikastakam.author: Umāpatidvivedin
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candikastakam.summary: The Caṇḍikāṣṭaka is a 20th-century Śākta devotional stotra addressed to the goddess Caṇḍikā (Durgā/Umā), written in ornate, highly alliterative Sanskrit verse (including yamaka and anuprāsa). It was composed by Umāpatidvivedin ('Kavipati') and presented to the Śākta scholar Jagadānandaśarman on Mahāṣṭamī in VS 1983 (1926 CE).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candikastakam.attribution: The author is specified as Umāpatidvivedin with the byname/title Kavipati ('kavipatyupanāmaka-'). Verse 10 supplies a chronogram date for the presentation of the work to Jagadānandaśarman: 'rāmāṣṭāṅkaśaśāṅke'bde' (Vikrama Saṃvat 1983 = 1926 CE), on Thursday during the Śukla Aṣṭamī of Āśvina.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_candikastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 10 verses (8 stanzas of the hymn proper plus 2 closing stanzas of phalaśruti, dedication, and date).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_cidambaram_srinatarajastu.title: Sabhāpatistuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_cidambaram_srinatarajastu.summary: A 15-verse hymn praising Śiva as Sabhāpati (Naṭarāja at Cidambaram), excerpted from the Muktikāṇḍa of the Sūtasaṃhitā. The stotra adapts formulas from the Vedic Śatarudrīya into anuṣṭubh verses, celebrating Śiva as cosmic dancer, presiding deity of the Assembly, and supreme reality.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_cidambaram_srinatarajastu.attribution: A devotional hymn occurring within the Muktikāṇḍa of the Sūtasaṃhitā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_cidambaram_srinatarajastu.coverage: complete — Complete 15-verse stotra as excerpted from the Muktikāṇḍa of the Sūtasaṃhitā.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_citramimamsa.title: Citramīmāṃsā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_citramimamsa.author: Appayya Dīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_citramimamsa.summary: The Citramīmāṃsā is a treatise on Sanskrit alaṅkāraśāstra by Appayya Dīkṣita. The work breaks off during the treatment of atiśayokti, and prompted Paṇḍitarāja Jagannātha's critique, the Citramīmāṃsākhaṇḍana.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_citramimamsa.attribution: Authored by Appayya Dīkṣita. The work breaks off during the discussion of atiśayokti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_citramimamsa.coverage: complete — The e-text contains the whole extant text of the work: introduction of the three kinds of kāvya, then the arthālaṅkāras up to atiśayokti, breaking off in the atiśayokti section, followed by the verse 'apy ardhacitramīmāṃsā na mude kasya māṃsalā...' and the editorial note 'samāptaś cāyaṃ samupalabhyamāno granthaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_carudattam.title: Cārudatta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_carudattam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_carudattam.summary: Cārudatta (also known as Daridracārudatta) is a classical Sanskrit-Prakrit play in four acts attributed to Bhāsa. It relates the romance between Cārudatta, an impoverished and noble merchant of Ujjayinī, and the wealthy courtesan Vasantasenā, intertwined with scenes involving the thief Sajjalaka (Śarvilaka) and the thief's burglary of Cārudatta's house. The surviving text breaks off at the end of the fourth act without a formal conclusion or bharatavākya, paralleling the first four acts of Śūdraka's ten-act Mṛcchakaṭikā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_carudattam.attribution: Ascribed to Bhāsa, though scholarship debates whether it is an earlier drama by Bhāsa / Śūdraka or an adaptation related to the Mṛcchakaṭikā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_carudattam.coverage: complete — Complete as extant; covers Acts 1 to 4 with interlinear/bracketed Sanskrit chāyā. The play survives only in this four-act form, breaking off at the end of Act 4.
translations: A. C. Woolner and L. Sarup, in PAB / Thirteen Trivandrum Plays. (English)
Anna Aurelia Esposito, Cārudatta, ein indisches Schauspiel: kritische Edition und Übersetzung mit einer Studie des Prakrits der “Trivandrum-Dramen”, Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz, 2004. (German)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitidarpanah.title: Cāṇakyanītidarpaṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitidarpanah.author: Cāṇakya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitidarpanah.summary: The Cāṇakyanītidarpaṇa is a gnomic anthology in seventeen adhyāyas traditionally attributed to Cāṇakya. It comprises aphorisms and practical guidance on social conduct, statecraft, character evaluation, friendship, and moral prudence.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitidarpanah.attribution: A gnomic collection traditionally attributed to Cāṇakya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitidarpanah.coverage: complete — Text in 17 adhyāyas (final verse numbered 5131 in digital transcription).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitih.title: Cāṇakyanīti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitih.author: Cāṇakya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitih.summary: The Cāṇakyanīti is a famous didactic anthology in 17 chapters containing maxims on worldly wisdom (nīti), ethical conduct, social relations, statecraft, and household life. Traditionally ascribed to Cāṇakya, it draws widely on Sanskrit gnomic and subhāṣita literature and represents one of the most popular nīti compilations in India.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitih.attribution: Traditionally ascribed to Cāṇakya. Modern scholarship notes that maxims under Cāṇakya's name circulated in various collections.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_canakyanitih.coverage: complete — Complete text of the 17-chapter recension, ending at chapter 17, verse 19.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dakaradidattasahasranamas.title: Dakārādidattasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dakaradidattasahasranamas.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dakaradidattasahasranamas.summary: The Dakārādidattasahasranāmastotra is a devotional hymn enumerating one thousand names of the deity Dattātreya, all composed alliteratively to begin with the consonant 'da' (dakārādi). It is attributed in the colophon to Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dakaradidattasahasranamas.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī Yativareṇya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dakaradidattasahasranamas.coverage: complete — Complete stotra consisting of opening dhyāna verses, 158 name-verses (epithets beginning with 'da-'), and a concluding phalaśruti verse (v. 159) with colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurticaturvimsativ.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrticaturviṃśativarṇamālāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurticaturvimsativ.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurticaturvimsativ.summary: The Dakṣiṇāmūrticaturviṃśativarṇamālāstotra is a 25-verse devotional and philosophical hymn praising Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti. The first 24 verses are composed in the Mattamayūra metre, each beginning successively with one of the twenty-four syllables of the Dakṣiṇāmūrti mantra, weaving together meditational iconography with Advaita Vedānta themes.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurticaturvimsativ.coverage: complete — Complete in 25 verses: 24 acrostic verses based on the Dakṣiṇāmūrti mantra, followed by one concluding phalaśruti/saṅgraha verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtimanasikapujas.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtimānasikapūjāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtimanasikapujas.author: Vijñānendra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtimanasikapujas.summary: A 27-verse devotional stotra dedicated to the mental worship (mānasikapūjā) of Śiva in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti. The hymn systematically visualizes the traditional ritual sequence (upacāras), from invocation (āvāhana) and pañcāmṛta bathing to garments, incense, light, food offerings, and circumambulation, culminating in surrender to Dakṣiṇāmūrti as the supreme guru.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtimanasikapujas.attribution: Attributed directly to Vijñānendra in the closing line.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtimanasikapujas.coverage: complete — Complete text of 27 numbered verses and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamali.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtinavaratnamālikāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamali.author: Navanāthasiddha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamali.summary: A ten-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the primordial guru seated under the banyan tree. The stanzas meditate on his yogic and iconographic attributes, his trampling of the demon Apasmāra (personified ignorance), and his manifestation as supreme consciousness (citkalā), concluding with a benedictory phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamali.attribution: Ascribed to 'Navanāthasiddha' in the final colophon line. Whether this designates a specific Nātha author or a collective lineage tradition is uncertain.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamali.coverage: complete — Complete text of 10 stanzas (9 root verses forming the 'navaratna' followed by a phalaśruti verse and colophon).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamala.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtinavaratnamālāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamala.summary: A devotional hymn of nine verses (navaratnamālā) praising Śiva in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the supreme teacher seated at the foot of the banyan tree. The stanzas depict diverse iconographical and meditative forms (dhyānas) of Dakṣiṇāmūrti—holding the cinmudrā, vīṇā, manuscript, and rosary—and supplicate him as the primordial guru who bestows liberating knowledge.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtinavaratnamala.attribution: Anonymous stotra; no author is indicated in the colophon or source edition.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.attribution: Ascribed in the closing colophon to Sadāśivabrahmendra: 'iti śrīmatparamahaṃsa parivrājakācāryavarya śrīsadāśiva brahmendraviracitaṃ śrīdakṣiṇāmūrtistotram'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.coverage: complete — Complete hymn as presented in the e-text: opening dhyāna verse 'mandasmitasphurita...', a long series of 'jaya ...' invocations, verses numbered up to 47, closing verses and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.author: Śaṅkarabhāratī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.summary: A 19-verse devotional hymn addressed to Śiva in his form as Dakṣiṇāmūrti, depicted as the primal teacher seated beneath the banyan tree expounding spiritual truth through silence and the cinmudrā. In the closing colophon, the hymn is attributed to Śaṅkarabhāratī Svāmin.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtistotram_brhat.coverage: complete — Complete 19-stanza hymn ending with the colophon naming Śaṅkarabhāratī.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyastakam_brhat.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyastakam_brhat.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyastakam_brhat.summary: The Dakṣiṇāmūrtyaṣṭaka (Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra) is an Advaita hymn ascribed to Śaṅkara, praising Śiva as Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the guru who reveals the Self, using images such as the city seen in a mirror, the seed and sprout, and the lamp in a pot with holes. This e-text gives the form preserved in the Bṛhatstotraratnākara, framed by dhyāna verses and a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyastakam_brhat.coverage: complete — Complete as represented in the e-text: includes the opening dhyāna verse, the core stanzas of the Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra (refrain abbreviated 'tasmai ...'), the phalaśruti, and subsequent devotional verses numbered through 17 with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattamalamantram.title: Dattamālāmantra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattamalamantram.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattamalamantram.summary: The Dattamālāmantra is a devotional mantra-stotra dedicated to Dattātreya by Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī (Ṭeṃbe Svāmī). Structured as an incantatory mālāmantra, it invokes Dattātreya with various bījas and epithets to counteract affliction, illnesses, adverse planetary influences, and hostile sorcery (paramantra, parayantra, paratantra).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattamalamantram.attribution: Attributed in the opening title heading ('śrī| pa| pa| vāsudevānaṃdasarasvatī ṭeṃbe svāmimahārāja kṛta') to Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī (Ṭeṃbe Svāmī Mahārāja).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattamalamantram.coverage: complete — Complete short mālāmantra text ending with 'oṃ namo mahāsiddhāya svāhā |'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattastavastrotram.title: Dattastavastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattastavastrotram.author: Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattastavastrotram.summary: The Dattastavastotra is a nine-verse Sanskrit hymn in praise of Dattātreya attributed to Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī. Verses 1–8 invoke Dattātreya with the refrain 'dattātreyaṃ namāmi taṃ' for protection against malignant spirits (bhūtas, pretas, piśācas), physical afflictions, epidemic diseases, and poison, concluding with a phalaśruti promising divine favor.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattastavastrotram.attribution: Attributed to Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī in the colophon (iti śrīvāsudevānandasarasvatīviracitaṃ dattastavastotraṃ saṃpūrṇama).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattastavastrotram.coverage: complete — Complete 9-verse hymn (8 stanzas with the refrain 'dattātreyaṃ namāmi taṃ' and 1 concluding phalaśruti verse) with colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattaparadhaksamapanastot.title: Dattāparādhakṣamāpanastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattaparadhaksamapanastot.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattaparadhaksamapanastot.summary: An eight-verse Sanskrit hymn addressed to Dattātreya by Vāsudevānandasarasvatī. The hymn offers supplication for the forgiveness of conscious and unconscious sins, requests firm devotion and mental clarity, and concludes with peace invocations adapted from Vedic formulas.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattaparadhaksamapanastot.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Vāsudevānandasarasvatī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattaparadhaksamapanastot.coverage: complete — Complete 8-verse hymn concluding with final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatharvasirsam.title: Dattātharvaśīrṣa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatharvasirsam.summary: The Dattātharvaśīrṣa is a short modern devotional prose stotra composed in the Atharvaśīrṣa litany style, dedicated to Dattātreya. It extols the deity as the pervasive witness of existence, the cosmic director (viśvanāṭakasūtradhāra), and saccidānanda. It explicitly assimilates Dattātreya into the historical lineage of the Marathi Datta Sampradāya, invoking Śrīpāda Śrīvallabha, Nṛsiṃha Sarasvatī of Ganagapur, Svāmī Samartha of Akkalkot, and Kṛṣṇa Sarasvatī of Kolhapur.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatharvasirsam.coverage: complete — Complete 7-section prose litany concluding with a Datta-gāyatrī verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyadvadasah_nama_s.title: Dattātreyadvādaśanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyadvadasah_nama_s.summary: A short devotional hymn (stotra) enumerating twelve sacred names of Dattātreya (Mahāyogin, Prabhurīśvara, Trimūrti, Jñānasāgara, Jñānavijñāna, Sarvamaṅgala, Puṇḍarīkākṣa, Devavallabha, Nandadeveśa, Nandadāyaka, Mahārudra, and Karuṇākara). The hymn begins with a liturgical viniyoga formula and concludes with a phalaśruti extolling its curative, protective, and spiritually liberating virtues.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyadvadasah_nama_s.attribution: No historical author is attributed in the text.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyadvadasah_nama_s.coverage: complete — Complete hymn consisting of the introductory viniyoga, the enumeration of the twelve names of Dattātreya, the phalaśruti, and the concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyasahasranamavali.title: Dattātreyasahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyasahasranamavali.summary: The Dattātreyasahasranāmāvalī is a devotional liturgical text comprising one thousand names of Dattātreya, the divine incarnation of the Hindu Trimūrti revered especially in the Avadhūta and Nātha traditions. Each name is cast in the dative case accompanied by 'oṃ' and 'namaḥ' for use in ceremonial worship (arcana) and japa recitation, celebrating his attributes as ascetic, guru, and supreme reality.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyasahasranamavali.attribution: A traditional liturgical formulation derived from a Dattātreyasahasranāmastotra, arranged for ritual arcana with 1,000 dative names preceded by 'oṃ' and followed by 'namaḥ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyasahasranamavali.coverage: complete — Complete enumeration of 1,000 names (1–1000) followed by the closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastotram_naradap.title: Dattātreyastotra (Nāradapurāṇa)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastotram_naradap.summary: This is a short devotional hymn to Dattātreya, ascribed in its colophon to the sage Nārada and to the Nāradapurāṇa. After a dhyāna verse and a viniyoga, its anuṣṭubh verses with the refrain 'dattātreya namo'stu te' praise Dattātreya as the embodiment of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, as the naked (digambara) avadhūta and supreme brahman, and as the god who lives at Mātāpura (Mahur). The closing verses promise destruction of enemies and sins and a direct vision of Datta. It is a popular hymn of the Dattātreya cult.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastotram_naradap.attribution: The colophon reads 'iti śrīnāradapurāṇe nāradaviracitaṃ dattātreyastotraṃ susaṃpūrṇam', and the viniyoga names Nārada as ṛṣi.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastotram_naradap.coverage: complete — The full hymn: dhyāna verse 'jaṭādharaṃ pāṇḍurāṅgaṃ ...', viniyoga (ṛṣi Nārada, anuṣṭubh, deity Śrīdatta), 18 verses with the refrain 'dattātreya namo'stu te' (vv. 17–18 are phalaśruti), and the closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyavajrakavacam.title: Dattātreyavajrakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyavajrakavacam.summary: The Dattātreyavajrakavaca is a protective hymn (kavaca) to Dattātreya traditionally extracted from the Rudrayāmala. Set as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī following a frame involving Dalādana Muni and a hunter, it provides standard ritual elements (viniyoga, nyāsa), an anatomical protection sequence invoking aspects of Dattātreya, and a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyavajrakavacam.attribution: Colophon attributes the work to the Rudrayāmala (Himavatkhaṇḍa, Umāmaheśvarasaṃvāda).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyavajrakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 78 verses with introductory prose viniyoga and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastacakrabijasto.title: Dattātreyāṣṭacakrabījastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastacakrabijasto.summary: The Dattātreyāṣṭacakrabījastotra is a short devotional hymn of nine verses venerating Dattātreya as the supreme guru residing within the subtle body. Each verse visualizes Dattātreya in one of the psychic centers (cakras)—from Mūlādhāra through Svādhiṣṭhāna, Maṇipūra, Anāhata, Viśuddha, Ājñā, and the Sahasrāra lotus—associating him with the corresponding petals, seed syllables (bījas), and presiding deities.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dattatreyastacakrabijasto.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra in 9 verses comprising an introductory dhyāna verse, seven chakra-bīja meditation verses (Mūlādhāra through Sahasrāra), and a concluding verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastotram.title: Daśāvatārastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastotram.author: Vādirāja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastotram.summary: A short nine-verse devotional hymn (stotra) composed by Vādirāja. The poem salutes Viṣṇu's ten classical avataras (Matsya, Kūrma, Varāha, Nṛsiṃha, Vāmana, Paraśurāma, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa/Yādava, Buddha, and Kalki) before concentrating its praise and iconography on Lord Hayagrīva (Hayānana) as the grantor of wisdom and divine scriptures.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastotram.attribution: Attributed to Vādirāja in verse 8 and the final colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastotram.coverage: complete — Complete short hymn in 9 verses with closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastuti.title: Daśāvatārastuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastuti.author: Vādirāja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastuti.summary: The Daśāvatārastuti is a Sanskrit hymn by Vādirāja praising the incarnations of Viṣṇu. Renowned for its intricate anuprāsa and rhyming cadence, it traverses the avatāras (including Matsya, Hayagrīva, Kūrma, Dhanvantari, Mohinī, Varāha, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Paraśurāma, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Buddha, and Kalki), concluding with a phalaśruti containing the author's signature.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastuti.attribution: Composed by Vādirāja, as embedded directly in verse 34 ('dhīvādirājayatibhūvāgvilāsanilayam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasavatarastuti.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 34 verses in a complex alliterative meter, ending with the author's signature and phalaśruti in verse 34.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_devibhujangam.title: Devībhujaṅgastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_devibhujangam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_devibhujangam.summary: The Devībhujaṅgastotra is a 28-verse hymn composed in the bhujaṅgaprayāta metre praising the supreme Goddess (Tripurasundarī/Bhavānī). It synthesizes Advaita Vedāntic non-dualism with Śākta and Śrīvidyā theology, referencing the pañcakośas, bindutraya, kuṇḍalinī yoga, and the unity of Śiva and Śakti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_devibhujangam.attribution: Attributed to Śaṅkarācārya in printed editions (e.g. VVP, WS 17).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_devibhujangam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 28 verses concluding with the colophon 'iti devībhujaṅgastotraṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhanalaksmistotram.title: Dhanalakṣmīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhanalaksmistotram.summary: A short devotional hymn addressed to Dhanalakṣmī (or Dhanadā) beseeching relief from poverty and the bestowal of wealth and auspiciousness. The text opens with Pārvatī asking Śiva for a reliable means to dispel indigence for householders, followed by Śiva's teaching of the hymn and its phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhanalaksmistotram.attribution: Traditional stotra without historical author attribution; presented within a dialogue frame where Śiva responds to Pārvatī's query on removing poverty.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhanalaksmistotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of the stotra ending with '|| iti śrī dhanalakṣmī stotraṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhvanitatvasamiksa.title: Dhvanitattvasamīkṣā (fragment: opening of chapter 1)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhvanitatvasamiksa.summary: Opening of a Sanskrit study of dhvani, arguing that all śabda, meaningful or not, can be called dhvani. It cites Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya (Paspaśāhnika: 'pratītapadārthako loke dhvaniḥ śabdaḥ'), Bhartṛhari's Vākyapadīya (Brahmakāṇḍa), a Śaiva verse identifying dhvani with mantravīrya and parā vāc, and the Yogacūḍāmaṇi Upaniṣad on praṇava. It also refers in passing to modern acoustics.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhvanitatvasamiksa.attribution: Author not named on Wikisource or in file metadata.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhvanitatvasamiksa.coverage: fragment — Short text fragment breaking off after a Mahābhāṣya quotation.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhurtasamagamah.title: Dhūrtasamāgama
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhurtasamagamah.author: Jyotirīśvara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dhurtasamagamah.summary: The Dhūrtasamāgama is a prahasana composed by Jyotirīśvara Kaviśekhara under King Narasiṃhadeva. The play mocks religious ascetics and legal figures, depicting Viśvanagara, a courtesan (Anaṅgasenā), and Asajjātimiśra.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_durgastutih.title: Durgāstuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_durgastutih.summary: A short devotional hymn (stotra) of eight verses praising the goddess Durgā, focusing on her manifestation as Śūlinī Durgā (Mahāśūlinī). The verses describe her iconography, multiple weapons, lion mount, and protective power to dispel sins, inner obstacles, and adversaries.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_durgastutih.attribution: Anonymous stotra dedicated to the goddess Durgā in her Śūlinī / Mahāśūlinī form.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_durgastutih.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 8 verses (aṣṭaka).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvadasajyotirlingastotram.title: Dvādaśajyotirliṅgastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvadasajyotirlingastotram.summary: The Dvādaśajyotirliṅgastotra is a popular Śaiva hymn celebrating the twelve sacred Jyotirliṅga shrines across India (Somanātha, Mallikārjuna, Mahākāla, Oṃkāra, Vaidyanātha, Nāganātha, Kedāranātha, Tryambakeśvara, Rāmeśvara, Bhīmaśaṅkara, Viśvanātha, and Ghṛṣṇeśvara). Each verse identifies a liṅga, its sacred geographical locale, and Śiva's saving grace, concluding with a verse declaring the spiritual fruit (phalaśruti) of reciting the hymn.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvadasajyotirlingastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 13 verses (12 verses eulogizing each of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas and 1 concluding phalaśruti verse).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvatrimsatputtalikasimhas.title: Siṃhāsanadvātriṃśikā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvatrimsatputtalikasimhas.summary: A narrative frame-story cycle also referred to in the text as Vikramārkacarita. The narrative opens with an invocation, an avataraṇikā set on Mount Kailāsa with Parameśvara and Pārvatī, followed by Bhartṛhari's vairāgyakathā in Ujjayinī involving Anaṅgasenā and King Vikramāditya, and proceeds with the tales related by the puttalikās before concluding with an epilogue describing the curse liberation (śāpamocana) on Kailāsa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvatrimsatputtalikasimhas.attribution: Contains sections associated with Vararuci in scholarship on recensions; the e-text itself has no author attribution.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dvatrimsatputtalikasimhas.coverage: partial — Substantially complete narrative containing the introductory frame story (avataraṇikā, Bhartṛhari's vairāgyakathā) and puttalikā stories (including tale 32 colophon), ending abruptly mid-sentence in the epilogue (upasaṃhāraḥ) with 'tathom'.
translations: Franklin Edgerton (trans.), Vikrama's Adventures or The Thirty-Two Tales of the Throne, Harvard Oriental Series, Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press, 1926. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daridryadahanasivastotram.title: Dāridryadahanaśivastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daridryadahanasivastotram.author: Vasiṣṭha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daridryadahanasivastotram.summary: The Dāridryadahanaśivastotra is a short devotional hymn of eight verses (aṣṭaka) and a phalaśruti addressed to Śiva. Traditionally attributed to the sage Vasiṣṭha, each stanza praises Śiva's cosmic, ascetic, and benign attributes while concluding with a refrain invoking him as the destroyer of poverty, grief, and suffering.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_daridryadahanasivastotram.attribution: Attributed in the text and colophon to Vasiṣṭha.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasabodhah.title: Dāsabodha (Sanskrit translation, excerpts)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasabodhah.author: Rāmadāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dasabodhah.summary: A Sanskrit prose translation (chāyā) of selected verses and chapters from the Dāsabodha, the Marathi spiritual work by Saint Rāmadāsa. Structured as an exposition between guru and disciple, the text integrates philosophy with devotion (bhakti), moral discernment, and guidance on righteous living in society. This digital text preserves an incomplete selection of verses translated into simple Sanskrit prose.
