SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dutaghatotkacam.title: Dūtaghaṭotkaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dutaghatotkacam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dutaghatotkacam.summary: The Dūtaghaṭotkaca is a short one-act Sanskrit play (an utsṛṣṭikāṅka or vyāyoga) set during the Mahābhārata war immediately following the slaughter of Abhimanyu. Kṛṣṇa dispatches Ghaṭotkaca as an emissary to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's court with a final peace warning. While Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī receive him with sorrow and respect, Duryodhana and his allies insult his demonic lineage and reject peace, prompting Ghaṭotkaca to deliver Kṛṣṇa's message foretelling their total destruction.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_dutaghatotkacam.coverage: complete — Complete one-act play in 52 verses (though verse 51 is misnumbered as 41 in this e-text). The text includes a modern introductory dramatis personae list (pātrāṇi) and inline Sanskrit chāyā in parentheses for the Prākrit speeches.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ekadasamukhahanumatkavaca.title: Ekātmatāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ekadasamukhahanumatkavaca.summary: The Ekātmatāstotra is a 33-verse Sanskrit hymn. It enumerates India's sacred geography (mountains, rivers, tirthas), philosophical and religious literatures across Indian traditions, and historical figures spanning Vedic ṛṣis, ancient and medieval rulers, Bhakti poets, modern scientists, freedom fighters, and leaders.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ekadasamukhahanumatkavaca.coverage: complete — Complete hymn in 33 verses plus the closing slogan 'vande bhāratamātaram'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauraganoddesa_dipika.title: Gauragaṇoddeśadīpikā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauraganoddesa_dipika.author: Kavikarṇapūra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauraganoddesa_dipika.summary: The Gauragaṇoddeśadīpikā is a sixteenth-century Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava hagiographical and theological catalogue composed by Kavikarṇapūra in 1576 CE (Śaka 1498). It systematically identifies Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Pañcatattva, the Dvādaśa Gopālas, and other close associates with their divine counterparts and eternal roles in Kṛṣṇa's Vraja-līlā and puranic avatāra traditions.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauraganoddesa_dipika.attribution: Paramānanda Sena, known by the epithet Kavikarṇapūra, was the son of Caitanya's associate Śivānanda Sena.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauraganoddesa_dipika.coverage: complete — Complete text in 215 verses, concluding with the chronogram verse dating the composition to Śaka 1498 (vasu-graha-manu = 1498 Śaka / 1576 CE).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamaval.title: Gauryaṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamaval.summary: The Gauryaṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī is a devotional litany of 108 sacred names addressed to the goddess Gaurī, formulated in the dative case (oṃ ... namaḥ) for pūjā recitations and arcana rituals. The names praise Gaurī both as Śiva's consort and as the supreme Śakti, identifying her with various forms of Devī such as Tripurasundarī, Annapūrṇā, and Mahākālī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamaval.coverage: complete — Complete litany containing the 108 dative names with praṇava and namaḥ.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamasto.title: Gauryāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamasto.summary: A 25-verse Śākta hymn praising Goddess Gaurī through 108 epithets. Set within an interlocutory frame where the sage Dattātreya instructs Paraśurāma, the text includes meditative visualization (dhyāna), the catalog of divine names, and a phalaśruti promising deliverance from misfortune and the attainment of liberation (kaivalya).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamasto.attribution: Traditional stotra framed as a dialogue between Dattātreya and Paraśurāma (Bhārgava/Jāmadagnya), recounting the names originally imparted by Bṛhaspati (Dhiṣaṇa) to Śacī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauryastottarasatanamasto.coverage: complete — Complete 25-verse text comprising introductory dialogue, dhyāna, stotra of 108 names, and phalaśruti.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauridasakam.title: Gaurīdaśaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauridasakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauridasakam.summary: The Gaurīdaśaka is a devotional hymn (stotra) of ten verses addressed to the goddess Gaurī, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. It lauds the goddess as the ultimate cosmic reality, transcendent yet immanent, embodying sat-cit-ānanda and Śabdabrahman, while delineating yogic contemplation of her form ascending from the mūlādhāra through the spinal channel to the brahma-randhra.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauridasakam.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya, pupil of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gauridasakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 10 stanzas plus 1 phalaśruti verse and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gamgastakam.title: Gaṅgāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gamgastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gamgastakam.summary: The Gaṅgāṣṭaka is a classical Sanskrit hymn of praise (stotra) addressed to the sacred river Gaṅgā, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. Composed primarily in classical metres such as Śārdūlavikrīḍita and Sragdharā, the work praises the divine origin, purificatory efficacy, and liberating power of the Ganges, concluding with a prayer for release on her banks.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gamgastakam.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkarabhagavat, styled as pupil of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gamgastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn comprising 8 core verses followed by 1 prayer verse, 1 phalaśruti verse, and the closing colophon (10 verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastotra.title: Gaṅgāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastotra.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastotra.summary: The Gaṅgāstotra is a popular devotional hymn of fourteen verses composed in the rhythmic pajjhaṭikā metre in praise of the sacred river goddess Gaṅgā. Traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara, the stotra extols Gaṅgā's divine descent upon Śiva's locks, her purification of the three worlds, and her ability to grant liberation to all who revere or bathe in her waters.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastotra.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya (Śaṅkara) based on the signature 'śaṃkarasevakaśaṃkararacitaṃ' in verse 14.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastotra.coverage: complete — Complete in 14 verses, opening 'devi sureśvari bhagavati gaṃge' and closing with the signature line in verse 14 ('śaṃkarasevakaśaṃkararacitaṃ... iti ca samāptaḥ').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_kalidasakrtam.title: Gaṅgāṣṭaka (two hymns)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_kalidasakrtam.author: Kālidāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_kalidasakrtam.summary: Two short devotional hymns (aṣṭaka) to the river goddess Gaṅgā, both ascribed to Kālidāsa. The first praises life on the Gaṅgā's banks above royal splendour and the saving power of a drop of her water; the second praises her descent through Śiva's matted hair and her purifying waves.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_kalidasakrtam.attribution: Ascribed to Kālidāsa in the text (phalaśruti 'kṛtaṃ kālidāsena ramyam' and colophons).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_valmikikrtam.title: Gaṅgāṣṭakam
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_valmikikrtam.author: Vālmīki
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_valmikikrtam.summary: The Gaṅgāṣṭakam is an eight-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to the river goddess Gaṅgā, traditionally ascribed to Maharṣi Vālmīki. Opening with the verse 'mātaḥ śailasutāsapatni...', the poet longs to spend his life and face death on the banks of the sacred Ganges rather than enjoy temporal sovereignty, concluding with a phalaśruti verse promising deliverance from samsara.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_valmikikrtam.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to Vālmīki in verse 9 ('vālmīkinā viracitaṃ śubhadaṃ manuṣyaḥ') and the opening/closing colophons.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gangastakam_valmikikrtam.coverage: complete — Complete in 8 verses plus 1 concluding phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesabhujamgam.title: Gaṇeśabhujaṃgastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesabhujamgam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesabhujamgam.summary: The Gaṇeśabhujaṃga is a nine-verse devotional hymn addressed to Gaṇeśa, composed in the rhythmic bhujaṅgaprayāta metre. It celebrates the elephant-headed deity by invoking both his iconic visual forms (dancing posture, bells, tusk, trunk, and crescent ornament) and his transcendent nature as the non-dual supreme absolute (paramoṃkāra, kaivalyabhās). The hymn concludes with a phalaśruti verse extolling the spiritual and worldly merits attained through daily morning recitation.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesapancaratnam.title: Gaṇeśapañcaratna
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesapancaratnam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesapancaratnam.summary: The Gaṇeśapañcaratna is a popular devotional hymn comprising five stanzas in praise of Gaṇeśa followed by a concluding phalaśruti stanza, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. It extols Gaṇeśa as Vināyaka, son of Śiva, destroyer of obstacles, and an object of continuous meditation for yogins.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesapancaratnam.coverage: complete — Complete in 5 verses plus 1 phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastotram.title: Saṃkaṭanāśanagaṇeśastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastotram.summary: The Saṃkaṭanāśanagaṇeśastotra is a well-known eight-verse Sanskrit hymn addressed to Gaṇeśa, attributed to the Nāradapurāṇa and framed as an utterance of Nārada. It enumerates twelve names of Gaṇeśa (including Vakratuṇḍa, Ekadanta, Lambodara, and Gajānana) alongside a phalaśruti promising removal of obstacles, acquisition of wisdom and wealth, and fulfillment of desires.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastotram.attribution: Ascribed to the Nāradapurāṇa, framed as spoken by the sage Nārada ('nārada uvāca').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastotram.coverage: complete — Complete 8-verse hymn with framing speech prefix and concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastakam.title: Gaṇeśāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastakam.summary: An eight-verse devotional hymn (aṣṭaka) dedicated to Gaṇeśa (Mahāgaṇapati) for the removal of afflictions and obstacles (saṅkaṣṭaharaṇa). The verses systematically incorporate tantric bījamantras (oṃ, gaṃ, vaṃ, kraṃ, klīṃ, hrīṃ, śrīṃ, huṃ, etc.), outline Gaṇapati's visual iconography, describe his six-cornered and eight-petaled yantra, and conclude with the worldly and spiritual rewards of recitation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastakam.attribution: A traditional, anonymous tantric-inflected devotional hymn invoking Gaṇapati with bījamantras.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ganesastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising a short introductory viniyoga, 8 verses in Sragdharā metre with bījamantras and yantra meditation, and a concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_godavaristotram.title: Godāvarīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_godavaristotram.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_godavaristotram.summary: A 10-verse hymn in praise of the sacred river Godāvarī (Gautamī). The hymn extols its divine origin from Tryambakeśvara, compares its merit favorably to the Gaṅgā, Revā (Narmadā), and Kurukṣetra, and highlights the sanctity of pilgrimage and bathing during the Siṃhastha period.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_godavaristotram.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to pa. pa. Śrīvāsudevānandasarasvatī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_godavaristotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn in 10 verses concluding with the author's colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalahrdayastotram.title: Gopālahṛdayastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalahrdayastotram.summary: A short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn and ritual text addressed to Gopāla (Vāsudeva). It features an opening viniyoga citing Saṅkarṣaṇa as the seer, followed by verses invoking protective presence and cosmic form (virāṭ-rūpa), a series of prose namaskāra salutations to Puruṣa-Vāsudeva in his varied manifestations, and a concluding phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalahrdayastotram.attribution: The introductory viniyoga names Bhagavān Saṅkarṣaṇa as the ṛṣi and Gopāla/Vāsudeva as the devatā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalahrdayastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text containing viniyoga, 8 metric verses, 39 prose namaskāra formulas, and concluding phalaśruti ending with 'iti gopālahṛdayastotraṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalaksayakavacam.title: Gopālākṣayakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalaksayakavacam.summary: A short Vaiṣṇava protective hymn (kavaca) in 15 verses framed as an instruction given by Brahmā to Nārada, purporting to belong to the Brahmasaṃhitā. It assigns various divine names of Viṣṇu and Kṛṣṇa (Govinda, Keśava, Dāmodara, Vāsudeva, etc.) to protect different limbs of the body, times of day, and directions of space. The phalaśruti asserts victory in battle, release from disease, and attainment of Viṣṇuloka.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalaksayakavacam.attribution: A traditional Vaiṣṇava protective hymn attributed in its colophon to the Brahmasaṃhitā (brahmasaṃhitokta).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalaksayakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete text in 15 verses with preliminary dialogue, viniyoga, and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalastakam_paramahamsas.title: Gopālāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalastakam_paramahamsas.author: Brahmānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalastakam_paramahamsas.summary: The Gopālāṣṭaka is a nine-verse devotional hymn (eight thematic stanzas in vasantatilakā metre followed by a phalaśruti) attributed to Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda. Each stanza praises Gopāla (Kṛṣṇa) as the supreme cosmic ground and inner ruler (antaryāmin), integrating Upaniṣadic theology with devotion.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalastakam_paramahamsas.attribution: Attributed to Paramahaṃsasvāmī Brahmānanda in the colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gopalastakam_paramahamsas.coverage: complete — Complete text containing 8 stanzas with refrain and 1 phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindadamodarastotra.title: Govindadāmodarastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindadamodarastotra.author: Bilvamaṅgala
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindadamodarastotra.summary: The Govindadāmodarastotra is a Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn of 71 stanzas traditionally ascribed to Bilvamaṅgala. Each verse concludes with the refrain 'govinda dāmodara mādhaveti', depicting episodes in Kṛṣṇa's life (such as Draupadī's rescue, Yaśodā binding Kṛṣṇa, and the gopīs churning butter) or urging the senses to chant these holy names.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindadamodarastotra.attribution: Attributed to Bilvamaṅgalācārya in the colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindadamodarastotra.coverage: complete — Complete devotional poem of 71 verses featuring the refrain 'govinda dāmodara mādhaveti', ending with a colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastotram.title: Govindastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastotram.author: Kalyāṇīdevī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastotram.summary: A short four-verse Vaiṣṇava hymn praising Govinda (Bālakṛṣṇa) by Kalyāṇīdevī. Each verse praises the divine infant form and acts of Kṛṣṇa, culminating in the recurring refrain 'kuntalasantatirājitasanmukha devakinandana govinda vande'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastotram.attribution: Attributed in the opening heading and colophon to Kalyāṇīdevī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastotram.coverage: complete — Complete 4-verse stotra with opening heading and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastakam.title: Govindāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastakam.summary: A devotional hymn (stotra) of eight verses plus a phalaśruti celebrating Kṛṣṇa under the name Govinda. Each of the eight stanzas juxtaposes Kṛṣṇa's pastoral līlās in Gokula and Vṛndāvana with non-dual philosophical attributes of the supreme reality (brahman), concluding with the uniform refrain 'praṇamata govindaṃ paramānandam'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastakam.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_govindastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 verses plus 1 concluding phalaśruti stanza and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gurugita.title: Gurugītā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gurugita.summary: The Gurugītā ('Song of the Guru') is a devotional dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī, traditionally presented as part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the Skandapurāṇa. The text establishes the essential identity of the guru with supreme Brahman and Śiva, delineating the merits of guru devotion, contemplation, and esoteric mantric practice. It is recited in traditions such as the Dattātreya sampradāya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gurugita.attribution: Traditionally presented as a dialogue between Śiva and Pārvatī narrated by Sūta to the ṛṣis, claiming provenance from the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the Skandapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gurugita.coverage: complete — Complete text of the extended recension (designated as 'vṛhada rūpa' in the opening), with verse-by-verse modern Hindi prose translation.
translations: Muktananda, Swami. 1972. Śrī Gurugītā. Transliteration and English Translation. Ganeshpuri, Maharashtra: Gurudev Siddha Peeth. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatryastakam.title: Gāyatryaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatryastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatryastakam.summary: A short devotional hymn consisting of eight stanzas and a concluding phalaśruti verse addressed to the goddess Gāyatrī. Each of the eight main stanzas ends with the refrain meditating on her as the beloved of Hari, three-eyed, and five-faced ('gāyatrīṃ harivallabhāṃ triṇayanāṃ dhyāyāmi pañcānanām'). The work is traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatryastakam.attribution: Attributed to Śaṅkarācārya in the closing colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatryastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn comprising 8 main verses with a concluding phalaśruti verse (verse 9) and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatrisahasranamavali.title: Gāyatrīsahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatrisahasranamavali.summary: A liturgical recitation list (nāmāvalī) consisting of 1,008 names of goddess Gāyatrī framed in the ritual dative formula with 'oṃ' and 'namaḥ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatrisahasranamavali.coverage: complete — Complete liturgical recitation list of 1,008 invocations (numbered 1–1008), beginning with 'oṃ acintyalakṣaṇāyai namaḥ' and concluding with 'oṃ parāṃvikāyai namaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatristotram.title: Gāyatryaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatristotram.summary: The Gāyatryaṣṭaka is an anonymous devotional hymn (stotra) comprising eight rhymed stanzas addressed to the goddess Gāyatrī as the Mother of the Vedas and the embodiment of cosmic energy. Each stanza concludes with a shared refrain praising Mother Gāyatrī, followed by a ninth concluding verse stating the spiritual merit (phalaśruti) of reciting the aṣṭaka.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatristotram.attribution: Traditional anonymous stotra dedicated to the goddess Gāyatrī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_gayatristotram.coverage: complete — Complete eight-stanza hymn with the refrain 'bhaje 'mbāṃ gāyatrīṃ parama subhagā naṃdajananīm' followed by a one-verse phalaśruti (9 stanzas total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hammiramahakavyam.title: Hammīramahākāvya (cantos 1–9 and canto 10 fragment)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hammiramahakavyam.author: Nayacandrasūri
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hammiramahakavyam.summary: The Hammīramahākāvya is a 15th-century historical Sanskrit epic (mahākāvya) composed by the Jain monk Nayacandrasūri. It celebrates the lineage and heroic reign of the Cāhamāna (Chauhan) ruler Hammīradeva of Raṇastambhapura (Ranthambore), culminating in his celebrated defence and ultimate fall against the Delhi Sultan Alauddin Khalji in 1301 CE. The work combines classical court-poetic conventions with historical and regional bardic narratives.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hammiramahakavyam.attribution: Hammīramahākāvya is attributed to Nayacandrasūri and dated to the 15th century CE.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hammiramahakavyam.coverage: partial — Transcribed text ends at verse 26 of an incomplete section/canto.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hanumatkrtasitaramastotra.title: Hanūmatkṛtasītārāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hanumatkrtasitaramastotra.summary: A short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn of eleven verses honoring Sītā and Rāma as a divine couple, traditionally attributed to Hanumat. Each line balances parallel epithets praising Rāma and Sītā in tandem, concluding with two benedictory verses detailing the spiritual fruits (phalaśruti) of daily morning recitation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hanumatkrtasitaramastotra.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Hanūmat (Hanumān), as stated in verse 11 (kṛtaṃ hanūmatā puṇyaṃ stotram) and the concluding colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hanumatkrtasitaramastotra.coverage: complete — Complete text of 11 verses with colophon (9 praise verses followed by 2 phalaśruti verses).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_haristotram.title: Haristotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_haristotram.author: Brahmānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_haristotram.summary: The Haristotra (also designated Haryaṣṭaka) is a devotional hymn of nine verses in praise of Viṣṇu/Hari attributed to Paramahaṃsa Brahmānanda. Verses 1–8 describe the divine form, attributes, and cosmic deeds of Hari, each concluding with the refrain 'bhaje 'haṃ bhaje 'ham', followed by a concluding ninth phalaśruti stanza.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_haristotram.attribution: The hymn is attributed in the colophon to Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_haristotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 stanzas with the refrain 'bhaje 'haṃ bhaje 'ham' plus 1 phalaśruti verse (9 verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hemakamaksidandakam.title: Hemakāmākṣīdaṇḍaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hemakamaksidandakam.summary: A modern Sanskrit stotra in daṇḍaka meter celebrating Hemakāmākṣī (Baṅgāru Kāmākṣī), the golden goddess originally of Kanchipuram and currently enshrined in Thanjavur. The text traces the historical migration of the murti from Kanchipuram through Gingee and Udayarpalayam to Thanjavur, praising the royal patronage of the Thanjavur Marathas and prominent devotees including the Carnatic composer Śyāma Śāstrī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_hemakamaksidandakam.coverage: complete — Short daṇḍaka hymn including initial ślokas and concluding phrases.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambastotram_gaurikrtam.title: Herambastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambastotram_gaurikrtam.summary: A 14-verse devotional hymn to Gaṇeśa in his form as Heramba, excerpted from the Mudgalapurāṇa. Spoken by Gaurī (Pārvatī) when beset by a demon, it implores Heramba for divine protection, prompting Gaṇeśa to appear in response to her prayer.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambastotram_gaurikrtam.attribution: A devotional hymn traditionally spoken by Gaurī (Pārvatī) within the narrative of the Mudgalapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambastotram_gaurikrtam.coverage: complete — Complete 14-verse stotra with narrative setting and closing colophon as excerpted from the Mudgalapurāṇa.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambopasthanam.title: Herambopasthāna
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambopasthanam.author: Gaṇapati Muni
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambopasthanam.summary: The Herambopasthāna is a 40-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) dedicated to Gaṇeśa (Heramba) by Vāsiṣṭha Gaṇapati Muni. Structured into four sections of ten verses each in distinct meters (Śaśivadanā, Madalekhā, Indravajrā, and Vasantatilakā), the hymn integrates devotional praise with esoteric yogic symbolism (mūlādhāracakra, kundalinī, and prāṇa) and Vedic identifications (such as Brahmaṇaspati and Indra).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambopasthanam.attribution: Identified in the closing colophon as the composition of Gaṇapati (son of Narasiṃha, of the Vāsiṣṭha gotra), disciple of Bhagavān Maharṣi Ramaṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_herambopasthanam.coverage: complete — Complete in 4 khaṇḍas comprising 40 verses (10 verses each in Śaśivadanā, Madalekhā, Indravajrā, and Vasantatilakā meters).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrakrtasriramastotram.title: Indrakṛtaśrīrāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrakrtasriramastotram.summary: The Indrakṛtaśrīrāmastotra is a nine-verse hymn of praise to Rāma recited by Indra, extracted from the thirteenth sarga of the Yuddhakāṇḍa in the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa. Uttered after the slaying of Rāvaṇa, the stotra extols Rāma as the transcendent reality (nirākāra, parānandarūpa) who has manifested in human guise to relieve the burden of the earth. Indra expresses devotion, acknowledging the destruction of his own cosmic pride (trilokādhipatyābhimāna) through the grace of Rāma's lotus feet.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrakrtasriramastotram.attribution: The hymn occurs in the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa (Yuddhakāṇḍa, sarga 13).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrakrtasriramastotram.coverage: complete — Complete 9-verse hymn as extracted from the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, Yuddhakāṇḍa, sarga 13.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrasahasranamastotram.title: Indrasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrasahasranamastotram.author: Gaṇapati Muni
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrasahasranamastotram.summary: A thousand-name hymn (sahasranāma) dedicated to Indra, composed by Gaṇapati Muni. The epithets are systematically compiled from Ṛgvedic mantras and structured into ten centuries (śatakas), followed by a seven-verse epilogue explaining the Vedic provenance and ritual usage of the names.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrasahasranamastotram.attribution: Colophon explicitly reads: 'iti śrībhagavanmaharṣiramaṇāntevāsino vāsiṣṭhasya narasiṃhasūnorgaṇapateḥ kṛtiḥ indrasahasranāmastotraṃ sampūrṇam'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_indrasahasranamastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text containing ten hundred-name centuries (nāmaśatakas) followed by a 7-verse phalaśruti/epilogue.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jagannathasahasranamastot.title: Jagannāthasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jagannathasahasranamastot.summary: A Vaishnava devotional hymn listing one thousand names of Lord Jagannātha of Puri, framed as a dialogue between Bhīṣma and Yudhiṣṭhira ascribed to the Brahmapurāṇa. It opens with an invocation, viniyoga, and a dhyāna describing the wooden icon (brahmadāru) on the ratnasiṃhāsana of Nīlācala alongside Balabhadra and Subhadrā, continues with 1,000 epithets celebrating Jagannātha's cosmic and avataric forms, and concludes with a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jagannathasahasranamastot.attribution: Traditional Purāṇic text framed as a dialogue between Bhīṣma and Yudhiṣṭhira from the Brahmapurāṇa (iti śrībrahmapurāṇe bhīṣmayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jagannathasahasranamastot.coverage: complete — Complete stotra, including introductory prārthanā, viniyoga, dhyāna, the sahasranāma proper, and concluding phalaśruti.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jatayukrtaramastotram.title: Jaṭāyukṛtarāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jatayukrtaramastotram.summary: The Jaṭāyukṛtarāmastotra is a 13-verse hymn from the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa (Araṇyakāṇḍa, chapter 8), voiced by the dying vulture king Jaṭāyu to Rāma. Blending Advaita Vedānta ontology with fervent bhakti, the stotra extols Rāma as the unconditioned supreme reality beyond the three guṇas, and concludes with Rāma conferring liberation (sārūpya) upon Jaṭāyu.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jatayukrtaramastotram.attribution: Spoken by the vulture king Jaṭāyu in the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa (Araṇyakāṇḍa, sarga 8).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_jatayukrtaramastotram.coverage: complete — Complete 13-verse devotional hymn (10 toṭaka stotra verses plus 3 narrative/phalaśruti verses), corresponding to Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, Araṇyakāṇḍa 8.44–56.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kamalapatyastakam.title: Kamalāpatyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kamalapatyastakam.author: Brahmānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kamalapatyastakam.summary: The Kamalāpatyaṣṭaka is a short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn of eight stanzas with a concluding phalaśruti verse attributed to Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda. Each stanza exhorts humanity with the refrain 'bhajata re manujāḥ kamalāpatim' to turn towards Viṣṇu, emphasizing the transience of life, youth, family, and physical health, and urging the utilization of a rare human birth for spiritual liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kamalapatyastakam.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda. Verse 9 refers to the author generically as 'paramahaṃsajana'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kamalapatyastakam.coverage: complete — Complete 9-verse devotional hymn (8 principal verses with the refrain 'bhajata re manujāḥ kamalāpatim' plus 1 phalaśruti verse and colophon).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kanakadharastotra.title: Kanakadhārāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kanakadharastotra.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kanakadharastotra.summary: The Kanakadhārāstotra is a celebrated 22-verse devotional hymn to Lakṣmī, the consort of Viṣṇu. According to traditional hagiographies, Śaṅkara composed this hymn in an act of compassion for an impoverished woman who offered him an āmalaka fruit as alms, resulting in a miraculous shower of gold. The text praises the merciful glances (apāṅga) of the goddess and invokes her blessings for spiritual and temporal welfare.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kanakadharastotra.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 22 verses including concluding phalaśruti and final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kapinamupavasah.title: Kapīnāmupavāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kapinamupavasah.author: D. T. Tātācārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kapinamupavasah.summary: Kapīnāmupavāsa ('The Fasting of the Monkeys') is a satirical poem by ḍi ṭi tātācāriyar. It humorously describes a troop of monkeys who decide to prove their moral equality with humans by observing an Ekādaśī fast, only to rationalize collecting and storing jambu fruits in their cheek pouches to 'save effort' for the next morning, promptly eating them instead.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kapinamupavasah.coverage: complete — Complete short poem in 31 verses (the last verse is numbered 35 in the e-text following verse 30).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_karnabharam.title: Karṇabhāra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_karnabharam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_karnabharam.summary: The Karṇabhāra ('The Burden of Karṇa') is a one-act heroic play (vyāyoga or utsṛṣṭikāṅka) traditionally attributed to Bhāsa, based on the Mahābhārata. Set on the battlefield of Kurukṣetra, it portrays Karṇa's psychological sorrow and impending sense of doom as he prepares for his final duel with Arjuna, recalling the curse of his preceptor Paraśurāma and illustrating his supreme magnanimity in surrendering his divine armor (kavaca) and earrings (kuṇḍala) to Indra disguised as a brahmin.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_karnabharam.coverage: complete — Complete one-act play of 25 verses, beginning with the opening stage direction (nāndyante tataḥ praviśati sūtradhāraḥ) and ending with the Bharatavākya (v. 25) and colophon 'karṇabhāramavasitam'. Lines [79]–[91] in the e-text are an accidental duplicated copy of lines [49]–[61].

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kaupinapancakam.title: Kaupīnapañcaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kaupinapancakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kaupinapancakam.summary: A short five-verse Advaita hymn praising the spiritual detachment and inner bliss of the renouncer (saṃnyāsin). Each verse celebrates the ascetic who meditates on the Upanisadic mahāvākyas and abides in non-dual Brahman, concluding with the refrain 'kaupīnavantaḥ khalu bhāgyavantaḥ' ('blessed indeed are they who wear only a loincloth').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kaupinapancakam.attribution: Attributed in the text to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kaupinapancakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 5 verses followed by the concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_keralodayah.title: Keralodaya (canto 1, incomplete)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_keralodayah.author: K. N. Eḻuttacchan
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_keralodayah.summary: Keralodaya is a modern Sanskrit mahākāvya in 21 cantos containing nearly 2500 verses dealing with the history of Kerala. This e-text contains part of the first sarga (svapnamañjarī): the repentant Paraśurāma, tormented by his violence, approaches Brahmā / Viriñca, who teaches him non-violence and instructs him to abandon his axe.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_keralodayah.attribution: Modern Sanskrit mahākāvya composed by K. N. Eḷuthachan. Divided into twenty-one cantos, it contains nearly 2500 verses dealing with the entire history of Kerala, political, social and cultural against the background of South Indian history.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_keralodayah.coverage: partial — Only sarga 1: verses 1–9 and 27–65 (vv. 10–26 missing in the e-text).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ketvastottarasatanamavali.title: Ketvaṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ketvastottarasatanamavali.summary: The Ketvaṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī is a devotional and astrological litany comprising 108 names of Ketu, the descending lunar node in Indian Jyotiṣa. Formulated as liturgical dative salutations ('oṃ ... namaḥ'), the names enumerate mythological qualities, astrological planetary positions, and iconographic attributes associated with Ketu.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ketvastottarasatanamavali.attribution: Traditional liturgical recitation list of the 108 names of Ketu, commonly chanted in Navagraha pūjā and japa rituals.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ketvastottarasatanamavali.coverage: complete — Complete litany comprising an opening bījamantra followed by 108 dative invocations (namaḥ formulas) and a closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kiratastakam.title: Kirātāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kiratastakam.summary: The Kirātāṣṭaka is a ten-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Kirātaśāstā (Dharmaśāstā in his form as a forest hunter). The suppliant calls upon the armed deity to destroy hostile enemies, robbers, malevolent occult practices (vaśya, stambhana, māraṇa), and evil spirits or planetary afflictions (grahas), concluding with a phalaśruti verse promising victory over kings, relief from fears, and spiritual liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kiratastakam.attribution: Traditional devotional hymn without an ascribed author; the deity addressed is Dharmaśāstā / Kirātaśāstā as the son of Śiva.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kiratastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text in 10 verses (9 hymn stanzas plus 1 phalaśruti verse) ending with 'iti kirātāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayananda.title: Kuvalayānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayananda.author: Appayadīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayananda.summary: The Kuvalayānanda is an influential manual of Sanskrit poetics (alaṅkāraśāstra) composed by the 16th-century polymath Appayadīkṣita under the patronage of King Veṅkaṭapati. Taking the fifth chapter of Jayadeva's Candrāloka as its structural baseline, it organizes and elaborates upon over one hundred figures of sense (arthālaṅkāra), providing definition verses (lakṣaṇa), illustrative examples (lakṣya), and explanatory prose comments.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayananda.attribution: Composed by Appayadīkṣita (c. 16th century) under King Veṅkaṭapati. The work adopts and supplements the alaṅkāra stanzas from Jayadeva's Candrāloka along with Appayadīkṣita's own prose commentary (vṛtti).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayananda.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Kuvalayānanda in 172 verses with prose commentary (vṛtti), running from the maṅgala verses to the concluding verse 172 and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayanandah_sodaharana.title: Kuvalayānanda (incomplete)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayanandah_sodaharana.author: Appayya Dīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayanandah_sodaharana.summary: The Kuvalayānanda is an influential manual of Sanskrit rhetoric (alaṅkāraśāstra) composed by Appayya Dīkṣita (16th–17th c.). Expanding upon the fifth chapter of Jayadeva's Candrāloka, the author systematically defines, illustrates, and analyzes over one hundred figures of speech (arthālaṅkāras). This e-text is an incomplete transcription containing only the opening portion through the nidarśanālaṅkāra.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayanandah_sodaharana.attribution: The Kuvalayānanda incorporates the kārikā definitions from Jayadeva's Candrāloka (as Appayya explicitly notes in verse 5: 'yeṣāṃ candrālike [candrāloke] dṛśyante...') and adds Appayya Dīkṣita's own definitions, examples, and vṛtti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kuvalayanandah_sodaharana.coverage: partial — Incomplete. The text ends abruptly at verses 55–56 under nidarśanālaṅkāra; the complete text covers over one hundred figures of speech and around 170 verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam.title: Kālabhairavāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam.summary: The Kālabhairavāṣṭaka is an eight-stanza devotional hymn (with an appended phalaśruti verse) eulogizing Kālabhairava, the fierce manifestation of Śiva acting as the guardian protector of the sacred city of Vārāṇasī (Kāśī). Each stanza ends with the refrain 'kāśikāpurādhinātha-kālabhairavaṃ bhaje', celebrating the deity's awe-inspiring iconography, dread cosmic sovereignty, and mercy in purging sins and bestowing liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam.attribution: Ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya in the source headers and TEI header; the e-text itself has no colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam.coverage: complete — Eight stanzas with refrain plus phalaśruti (refrain repeated after it); no verse numbers and no colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam_brhats.title: Kālabhairavāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam_brhats.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam_brhats.summary: The Kālabhairavāṣṭaka is a popular devotional hymn consisting of eight stanzas dedicated to Kālabhairava, the wrathful manifestation of Śiva regarded as the guardian and ruler of Kāśī (Vārāṇasī). Each stanza describes aspects of Bhairava's cosmic form and attributes and concludes with the refrain 'kāśikāpurādhināthakālabhairavaṃ bhaje'. A ninth verse provides the phalaśruti promising spiritual release and protection from delusion, grief, and sins.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam_brhats.attribution: Ascribed to Śaṅkara in the colophon ('iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau'); the ascription is traditional, as for most stotras attributed to Śaṅkara.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kalabhairavastakam_brhats.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 verses featuring the refrain 'kāśikāpurādhināthakālabhairavaṃ bhaje', followed by 1 phalaśruti stanza and standard colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kartikeyastotram.title: Kārtikeyastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kartikeyastotram.summary: A short devotional hymn of six verses praising Kārtikeya (Skanda), listing twenty-eight sacred epithets (aṣṭāviṃśati nāmāni) of the deity. Traditionally extracted from the Rudrayāmalatantra, it is recited as a prajñāvivardhana (intellect-enhancing) stotra believed to confer eloquence and sharp intelligence.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kartikeyastotram.attribution: Traditionally regarded as an excerpt from the Rudrayāmala (Rudrayāmalatantra), framed as spoken directly by Skanda (śrīskanda uvāca).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kartikeyastotram.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 6 verses containing the 28 names of Kārtikeya with phalaśruti and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_katyayanyastakam.title: Kātyāyanyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_katyayanyastakam.summary: The Kātyāyanyaṣṭaka is a nine-verse Sanskrit stotra dedicated to the goddess Kātyāyanī, specifically associated with the temple tradition at Aversa/Chatrapuri. The text praises her attributes as the slayer of Mahiṣāsura, invokes her attendant deities and kulagotra lineages, and concludes with a phalaśruti verse attributed to or mentioning Kumṭhācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_katyayanyastakam.attribution: Verse 9 designates the hymn as 'kumaṭhācāryaja' (originating from/composed by Kumṭhācārya), composed for Goddess Kātyāyanī of the Kātyāyanī Bāṇeśvara shrine (associated with Aversa/Chatrapuri).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_katyayanyastakam.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 8 verses plus 1 phalaśruti verse (9 verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kavyadarsavyakhya_hrdayan.title: Kāvyādarśavivṛti (chapters 1 and 3)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kavyadarsavyakhya_hrdayan.author: Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kavyadarsavyakhya_hrdayan.summary: Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara's Sanskrit commentary (Vivṛti) on Daṇḍin's Kāvyādarśa. The e-text covers chapters 1 and 3 (up to verse 187).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kavyadarsavyakhya_hrdayan.attribution: A commentary on Daṇḍin's Kāvyādarśa composed by Jīvānanda Vidyāsāgara Bhaṭṭācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_kavyadarsavyakhya_hrdayan.coverage: partial — Commentary on pariccheda 1 (ending at verse 105 in sample context) and pariccheda 3 (ending at verse 187 with colophon). Pariccheda 2 is not present.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_krsnasahasranamastotram.title: Kṛṣṇasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_krsnasahasranamastotram.author: Harihara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_krsnasahasranamastotram.summary: A Vaishnava devotional hymn (stotra) enumerating one thousand names of Kṛṣṇa. Set in a narrative frame where Kṛṣṇa manifests before King Harihara and requests a thousand-name praise celebrating his deeds, the text includes formal ritual preliminaries (viniyoga, nyāsa, and dhyāna), a continuous catalogue of epithets covering Kṛṣṇa's cosmic attributes and pastoral and heroic deeds in Gokula, Mathurā, and Dvārakā, and a concluding phalaśruti detailing the spiritual benefits of recitation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_krsnasahasranamastotram.attribution: The opening verses (1–10) state that King Harihara (described as an ornament of the Rukmi dynasty: rukmimahīpālavaṃśarakṣāmaṇiḥ) had propitiated Rāma with a thousand names, prompting Kṛṣṇa to appear and ask him to praise him with a sahasranāma based on his līlās. In the mantra ritual framework, Parāśara is named as the ṛṣi.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_krsnasahasranamastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising the 13 introductory verses, viniyoga, nyāsa, 3 dhyāna verses, the stotra of 1,000 names, and the concluding phalaśruti (ending at v. 211).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarasimhasuprabhata.title: Yādagirilakṣmīnarasiṃhasuprabhāta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarasimhasuprabhata.author: Vaṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarasimhasuprabhata.summary: The Yādagirilakṣmīnarasiṃhasuprabhāta is a morning awakening hymn (suprabhāta) in 33 verses composed by Vaṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya. Following traditional suprabhāta conventions, it opens with the standard Rāmāyaṇa verse ('kausalyā suprajā rāma...'), depicts the arrival of dawn, deities, and devotees at the sanctum, and calls upon the deity to awaken.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarasimhasuprabhata.attribution: Directly ascribed in the text rubric to Vaṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarasimhasuprabhata.coverage: complete — Complete text in 33 verses, concluding with the phalaśruti verse (v. 33) and closing rubric 'iti śrī lakṣmī narasiṃha suprabhātam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarayanastotram.title: Lakṣmīnārāyaṇastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarayanastotram.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarayanastotram.summary: An eight-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa by Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī. The first seven verses repeat the refrain 'trāhi māṃ bhavasāgarāt' ('save me from the ocean of worldly existence'), concluding with a verse of self-surrender (śaraṇāgati).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarayanastotram.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Vāsudevānandasarasvatī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminarayanastotram.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 8 verses plus a colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhakarunarasast.title: Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhakaruṇārasastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhakarunarasast.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhakarunarasast.summary: The Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhakaruṇārasastotra is a devotional hymn in 17 verses addressed to Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. The verses employ vivid metaphors of existential distress (saṃsāra as a forest fire, a deep well, ocean monsters, and venomous serpents), with each verse ending in the refrain requesting a saving hand ('mama dehi karāvalambam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhakarunarasast.attribution: Attributed in verse 17 and the colophon to Śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavat, pupil of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhakarunarasast.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 17 verses with parenthetical variant readings (pāṭhabheda) and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhamangalasasan.title: Yādagirilakṣmīnṛsiṃhamaṅgalāśāsana
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhamangalasasan.author: Vāṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhamangalasasan.summary: A 14-verse Śrīvaiṣṇava devotional hymn (maṅgalāśāsana) composed by Vāṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya praising Lord Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha enshrined at Yadagiri (Yādādri / Yadagirigutta, Telangana). Each verse extols the deity's divine grace, cosmic sovereignty, and cave residence, concluding with an auspicious invocation (maṅgalam).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhamangalasasan.attribution: Attributed to Vāṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya according to the text's closing colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhamangalasasan.coverage: complete — Complete text of 14 verses with closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhapancaratna.title: Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhapañcaratna
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhapancaratna.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhapancaratna.summary: The Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhapañcaratna is a five-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. Utilizing the recurring refrain 'bhaja bhaja lakṣmīnarasiṃhānaghapadasarasijamakarandam', each verse addresses the human mind as a wandering bee (cetobhṛṅga), urging it to abandon the illusory and suffering-filled wasteland of mundane existence (saṃsāra) and take shelter at the lotus feet of the deity.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhapancaratna.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkara, disciple of Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhapancaratna.coverage: complete — Complete 5-verse stotra with traditional concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhaprapatti.title: Yādagirilakṣmīnṛsiṃhaprapatti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhaprapatti.author: Vaṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhaprapatti.summary: A short six-verse devotional surrender hymn (prapatti) dedicated to Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha at the sacred hill of Yādagiri, composed by Vaṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya. The first verse pays homage to Lakṣmī as the intercessor, followed by five verses surrendering at the divine feet of Narasiṃha with the recurring refrain 'lakṣmīnṛsiṃha caraṇau śaraṇam prapadye'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhaprapatti.attribution: Colophon explicitly credits authorship to Vaṅgīpuram Narasiṃhācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhaprapatti.coverage: complete — Complete 6-verse stotra followed by the concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhasahasranamav.title: Lakṣmīnṛsiṃhasahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhasahasranamav.summary: A Vaiṣṇava liturgical collection of 1,000+ devotional names dedicated to Viṣṇu in his half-man, half-lion incarnation (Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha). Each epithet is structured as an individual dative mantra (oṃ [name] namaḥ) designed for arcanā, pūjā recitation, and ritual flower offerings.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhasahasranamav.attribution: A traditional liturgical formulation (nāmāvalī) reciting the one thousand names of Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha in the dative case with oṃ and namaḥ for ritual worship (arcanā).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_laksminrsimhasahasranamav.coverage: complete — Complete ritual nāmāvalī containing an initial bīja invocation, 1,006 dative mantras (oṃ ... namaḥ), and a concluding closing formula (śrī lakṣmīnṛsiṃha sahasranāmāvaliḥ samāptaḥ).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_lalitapancaratnam.title: Lalitāpañcaratna
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_lalitapancaratnam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_lalitapancaratnam.summary: The Lalitāpañcaratna is a brief five-verse morning hymn (prātaḥsmaraṇa) addressed to the goddess Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī, followed by a phalaśruti verse. Each verse begins with a morning invocation ('prātaḥ smarāmi...', 'prātar bhajāmi...', etc.), meditating in turn on the goddess's face, hands, lotus feet, transcendent nature as Paraśivā, and holy names. Attributed to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_lalitapancaratnam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 5 core stanzas plus 1 phalaśruti verse (total 6 verses).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhurastakam.title: Madhurāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhurastakam.author: Vallabhācārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhurastakam.summary: The Madhurāṣṭaka is an eight-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) composed by Vallabhācārya, the founding teacher of the Puṣṭimārga tradition. Structured with the recurring refrain 'madhurādhipater akhilaṃ madhuram' ('all is sweet regarding the Lord of Sweetness'), the hymn describes the divine sweetness of Kṛṣṇa's form, attire, actions, companions, and pastoral activities in Vraja.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhurastakam.attribution: Consistently and traditionally attributed to Vallabhācārya, founder of the Puṣṭimārga (Śuddhādvaita) tradition.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhurastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 8 stanzas with the closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhusudanastotram.title: Madhusūdanastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhusudanastotram.author: Śukadeva
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhusudanastotram.summary: A 16-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Viṣṇu under the name Madhusūdana, traditionally attributed to Śukadeva. Verses 1–12 beseech deliverance from the sufferings of worldly existence (saṃsāra), old age, and rebirth using the refrain 'trāhi māṃ madhusūdana', while verses 13–16 praise the supreme salvific power of the twelve-syllable Vāsudeva mantra (oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhusudanastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 16 verses followed by a concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhyamavyayogah.title: Madhyamavyāyoga
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhyamavyayogah.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhyamavyayogah.summary: The Madhyamavyāyoga ('The Middle One') is a one-act Sanskrit drama belonging to the vyāyoga genre, traditionally attributed to Bhāsa. Drawing on characters from the Mahābhārata, the play depicts Ghaṭotkaca demanding the sacrifice of the middle son of a wandering Brahmin family as food for his mother Hiḍimbā. Bhīma, the middle Pāṇḍava, intervenes by offering himself as the substitute victim, leading to a trial of strength and the joyful reunion of Bhīma with his demon-born son and wife.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_madhyamavyayogah.coverage: complete — Complete one-act play in 52 verses, opening with the stage directions and nāndī and ending with the bharatavākya (verse 52) and the final colophon 'madhyamavyāyogaṃ nāma nāṭakaṃ samāptam'.
translations: Ernest Paxton Janvier, The Madhyamavyāyoga: A Drama Composed by the Poet Bhāsa, Translated from the Original Sanskrit with Introduction and Notes, Mysore: Wesleyan Mission Press (Diss. Univ. of Pennsylvania 1922). (English)
A. C. Woolner and L. Sarup, translation cited in Mahāsubhāṣitasaṃgraha. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahamahimanvitam_adityast.title: Ādityastotraratna
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahamahimanvitam_adityast.author: Appayyadīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahamahimanvitam_adityast.summary: A 14-verse hymn in Sragdharā metre praising the Sun god (Āditya) attributed to Appayyadīkṣita. Combining Purāṇic cosmology with Upaniṣadic theology, it delineates the solar chariot, rays, and months, identifying the deity within the solar orb as Paraśiva and the Udgītha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahamahimanvitam_adityast.attribution: Attributed to Appayyadīkṣita in the opening heading and concluding colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahamahimanvitam_adityast.coverage: complete — Complete hymn in 14 Sragdharā verses (12 descriptive stanzas, 1 structural summary stanza, 1 phalaśruti stanza).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahanandisvarasujangastot.title: Mahānandīśvarabhujaṅgastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mahanandisvarasujangastot.summary: A short six-verse devotional hymn (stotra) composed in the bhujaṅgaprayāta meter praising Śiva as Mahānandīśvara or the Mahānandiliṅga (associated with the sacred site of Mahanandi). Each verse describes Śiva's cosmic attributes and concludes with a devotional refrain saluting the Mahānandi liṅga.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_malharikavacam.title: Mallārīkavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_malharikavacam.summary: The Mallārīkavaca is a short protective stotra dedicated to Mallāri (Khaṇḍobā / Mārtaṇḍa Bhairava, consort of Mhālasā), an avatar of Śiva particularly venerated in Maharashtra and Karnataka. Attributed to the Mallārīmāhātmya section of the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa, the text invokes the deity seated on Maṇiratnagiri for deliverance from enemies, wild beasts, diseases, and planetary afflictions.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_malharikavacam.attribution: Spoken by Sanatkumāra; attributed in the colophon to the Kṣetrakhaṇḍa, Mallārīmāhātmya of the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_malharikavacam.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra/kavaca including initial viniyoga, stotra verses, phalaśruti, and concluding colophon formula.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manobodhah.title: Manobodha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manobodhah.author: Rāmadāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manobodhah.summary: The Manobodha (widely known in Marathi as Manāce Śloka) is a devotional and philosophical poem by Samartha Rāmadāsa. Addressed to the human mind (manas), the work instructs it to renounce worldly infatuations, transcend bodily identification, and cultivate ethical righteousness and surrender to Rāma. This e-text preserves an anonymous metrical Sanskrit translation composed on the banks of the Tapti river.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manobodhah.attribution: Original Marathi composition by Samartha Rāmadāsa. This Sanskrit verse translation was composed by an unnamed devotee ('śrīrāmadāsānudāsaḥ') residing on the banks of the Tapatī (Tapti) river.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manobodhah.coverage: complete — Complete Sanskrit translation corresponding to the Marathi text, followed by concluding stanzas and the closing prayer 'āpadāmapahartāraṃ...'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mantragarbhasridattatreya.title: Mantragarbhadattātreyāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mantragarbhasridattatreya.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mantragarbhasridattatreya.summary: A 24-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) enumerating 108 names and epithets of deity Dattātreya. The verses are interwoven ('manusyūta') with auspicious bījamantras and sacred syllables (such as oṃ, hrīṃ, klīṃ, drāṃ) associated with the worship of Dattātreya.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_medhadaksinamurtimantrava.title: Medhādakṣiṇāmūrtimantravarṇapadastuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_medhadaksinamurtimantrava.summary: A 24-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn praising Śiva in his form as Medhā-Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the granter of intellect and wisdom. Each verse is an acrostic reflection meditating on one successive syllable of the 24-syllable Medhādakṣiṇāmūrti mantra ('oṃ namo bhagavate dakṣiṇāmūrtaye mahyaṃ medhāṃ prajñāṃ prayaccha svāhā').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_medhadaksinamurtimantrava.attribution: No author mentioned in the text or closing colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_medhadaksinamurtimantrava.coverage: complete — Complete text in 24 verses matching the 24 syllables of the Medhādakṣiṇāmūrti mantra.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_murukastakam.title: Murukāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_murukastakam.author: Somaśekharayajvan
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_murukastakam.summary: The Murukāṣṭaka is a short Sanskrit devotional hymn dedicated to Murukan (Subrahmaṇya/Skanda) by Somaśekharayajvan. Designed as a vibhakti-stotra, verses 2–9 decline the deity's name across the Sanskrit cases, flanked by an opening invocation to Gaṇeśa and a concluding phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_murukastakam.attribution: Verse 10 attributes the composition to Somaśekharayajvan (digital text has the typo 'somaśekharayajvamiḥ').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_murukastakam.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 10 verses: mangala to Gaṇeśa (v. 1), 8 vibhakti verses addressing Murukan (vv. 2–9), and phalaśruti (v. 10).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manasollasah.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra with Mānasollāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manasollasah.author: Śaṅkara, Sureśvara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manasollasah.summary: The Mānasollāsa is an influential metrical exposition (vārttika) in ten chapters (ullāsas) expounding Śaṅkara's celebrated ten-verse hymn, the Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra. Traditionally ascribed to Sureśvara, the text systematically develops the hymn's pithy Advaita Vedānta doctrines, treating themes such as the illusory nature of phenomenal diversity (māyā/vivarta), the mirror-like reflection of the world in pure consciousness, the critiques of rival philosophical views (including Buddhist Śūnyavāda and Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika), and the ultimate identity of the individual soul (jīva) with Parameśvara (Śiva-Dakṣiṇāmūrti).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manasollasah.attribution: The root hymn Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra is traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya, and the metrical commentary Mānasollāsa is traditionally ascribed to Sureśvarācārya. Scholars note doctrinal differences between the Mānasollāsa and Sureśvara's undisputed vārttikas.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_manasollasah.coverage: complete — Complete text of both works: the 10 stanzas of the Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra followed by all 10 ullāsas (chapters) of the Mānasollāsa (ending with daśamollāsasaṅgrahaḥ and final colophon).
translations: A. Mahadeva Sastri, The Vedanta Doctrine of Sri Sankaracharya: Comprising the Dakshinamurti-Stotra and Sureshwaracharya's Manasollasa. (English)
Harshananda, Dakshinamurti Stotra with Manasollasa of Suresvaracharya, Bangalore, 1992. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_markandeyasivastakam.title: Mārkaṇḍeyaśivāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_markandeyasivastakam.author: Yajñeśa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_markandeyasivastakam.summary: The Mārkaṇḍeyaśivāṣṭaka is a short eight-verse Sanskrit hymn praising Śiva residing on the banks of the Godāvarī River, commemorating his protection of the young devotee Mārkaṇḍeya from Yama. A ninth concluding verse credits the composition to Yajñeśa of the Kolācala lineage.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_markandeyasivastakam.attribution: Composed by a brāhmaṇa named Yajñeśa of the Kolācala family. The hymn is addressed to Śiva on the bank of the Godāvarī, referencing the legend of Śiva rescuing Mārkaṇḍeya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_markandeyasivastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text containing 8 stanzas of the hymn plus 1 signature/concluding verse (9 verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mamgalyastavah.title: Māṅgalyastava
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mamgalyastavah.summary: The Māṅgalyastava is a 50-verse Vaiṣṇava hymn embedded in the Viṣṇudharmottarapurāṇa, presented as a dialogue between Pulastya and Dālbhya. The hymn praises Hari across his cosmic and avataric forms—specifically highlighting Varāha and Nṛsiṃha—and functions as an apotropaic chant to dispel bad dreams, counteract inauspicious omens, and ensure success and auspiciousness (māṅgalya) at the start of any endeavor.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mamgalyastavah.attribution: A Vaiṣṇava stotra framed as a dialogue between the sage Pulastya and Dālbhya, preserved within the Viṣṇudharmottarapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mamgalyastavah.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 50 verses including introductory narrative frame, stuti, and concluding phalaśruti with colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_minaksistrotram.title: Mīnākṣīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_minaksistrotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_minaksistrotram.summary: A five-verse devotional hymn (pañcaratna) addressed to Goddess Mīnākṣī of Madurai, praising her divine form, her identity as Śrīvidyā residing in the Śrīcakra, and her status as the consort of Sundareśvara. Each verse concludes with the refrain 'mīnākṣīṃ praṇato 'smi saṃtatam ahaṃ kāruṇyavārāṃ nidhim'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_minaksistrotram.coverage: complete — Complete 5 verses (pañcaratna) with the refrain 'mīnākṣīṃ praṇato 'smi saṃtatam ahaṃ kāruṇyavārāṃ nidhim'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mrtyunjayamanasikapujasto.title: Mṛtyuñjayamānasikapūjāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mrtyunjayamanasikapujasto.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mrtyunjayamanasikapujasto.summary: The Mṛtyuñjayamānasikapūjāstotra is a 46-verse devotional hymn attributed to Śaṅkara providing an elaborate mental worship (mānasapūjā) directed to Śiva as Mṛtyuñjaya. Devotees mentally visualize Śiva seated on Mount Kailāsa and present the traditional sequence of devotional offerings (upacāras)—ranging from ceremonial seating, bath, and fine garments to fragrant unguents and multi-course food offerings—concluding with a three-verse phalaśruti detailing the rewards of daily worship across the three junctures of the day.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mrtyunjayamanasikapujasto.attribution: Traditionally attributed in the closing colophon to Śaṅkara (Govindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣya).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_mrtyunjayamanasikapujasto.coverage: complete — Complete text in 46 verses, ending with the full colophon and phalaśruti.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naisadhiyacaritam.title: Naiṣadhīyacarita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naisadhiyacaritam.author: Śrīharṣa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naisadhiyacaritam.summary: The Naiṣadhīyacarita (or Naiṣadha) by the philosopher-poet Śrīharṣa (12th century CE) is one of the five celebrated mahākāvyas ('great court epics') of classical Sanskrit literature. Across 22 cantos, it narrates the story of King Nala and Princess Damayantī up to their wedding and honeymoon, elaborating on the Nalopākhyāna from the Mahābhārata. Famed for its intricate linguistic craftsmanship, double entendres (śleṣa), and profound philosophical references, the work is traditionally regarded as the ultimate test of scholarship ('naiṣadhaṃ vidvad-auṣadham').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naisadhiyacaritam.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 22 sargas (cantos 1–22) without commentary, ending at 22.155.
translations: Translated by K. K. Handiqui in Naiṣadhacarita of Śrīharṣa, Deccan College Building Centenary and Silver Jubilee Series 33, Poona 1965. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nakhastutih.title: Nakhastuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nakhastutih.author: Ānandatīrtha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nakhastutih.summary: The Nakhastuti is a two-verse Sanskrit hymn (stotra) attributed to Ānandatīrtha. It glorifies the divine power of the claws (nakha) of Viṣṇu in his Narasiṃha incarnation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nakhastutih.attribution: Attributed in colophons to Śrīmadānandatīrtha Bhagavatpādācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nakhastutih.coverage: complete — Complete in 2 verses, followed by a colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narmadastakam.title: Narmadāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narmadastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narmadastakam.summary: The Narmadāṣṭaka is a devotional hymn of eight stanzas (plus a concluding phalaśruti verse) eulogizing the river goddess Narmadā, traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya. Composed in a rhythmic meter featuring complex assonance, each verse praises the river's sanctity, mythic associations with sages such as Mṛkaṇḍu and Pippalāda, and her power to destroy sins and grant liberation, ending with the recurring refrain 'tvadīyapādapaṅkajaṃ namāmi devi narmade'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narmadastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 stanzas with the refrain 'tvadīyapādapaṅkajaṃ namāmi devi narmade', followed by one concluding phalaśruti verse (9 verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_navagrahastotram.title: Navagrahastotra with Navagrahapīḍāharastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_navagrahastotram.author: Vyāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_navagrahastotram.summary: A collation of two popular Sanskrit devotional hymns dedicated to the propitiation of the nine planetary deities (Navagraha: Sūrya/Ravi, Candra/Soma, Maṅgala, Budha, Bṛhaspati/Guru, Śukra, Śani, Rāhu, and Ketu). The first hymn, ascribed to Vyāsa, describes the iconography, attributes, and genealogy of each deity in nine anuṣṭubh stanzas followed by a three-stanza phalaśruti. The second hymn, attributed to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa, invokes each planet in turn to dispel distress arising from unfavorable astrological placements (viṣamasthānasambhūtāṃ pīḍām).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_navagrahastotram.attribution: The first stotra ('japākusumasaṅkāśaṃ...') is traditionally attributed to Vyāsa. The second stotra ('grahāṇāmādirādityo...') is attributed in its colophon to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_navagrahastotram.coverage: complete — Contains the complete 9 planetary verses plus 3-verse phalaśruti of the Vyāsa-Navagrahastotra, followed immediately by the complete 9 verses and closing colophon of the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇokta Navagrahapīḍāharastotra.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_natesasahasranamastotram.title: Naṭeśasahasranāmastotra with Naṭeśapañcaratna (Pañcaratna: verses 1–2 only)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_natesasahasranamastotram.summary: The Naṭeśasahasranāmastotra is a thousand-name hymn to Śiva as Naṭeśa, framed as Śiva's answer to Parameśvarī and recounting its earlier revelation to Viṣṇu. It is followed in the e-text by stanzas of the Naṭeśapañcaratna.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_natesasahasranamastotram.attribution: Framed as Śiva's teaching to Parameśvarī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_natesasahasranamastotram.coverage: complete — Includes pūrvapīṭhikā, sahasranāma stanzas, and the opening of Naṭeśapañcaratna.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naradabhaktisutram.title: Nāradabhaktisūtra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naradabhaktisutram.summary: The Nāradabhaktisūtra is a classic Sanskrit treatise of 84 sūtras outlining the philosophy and practice of devotion (bhakti). It defines bhakti as supreme love (paramaprema) and surrender to the divine, contrasts it with ritual action (karman) and philosophical knowledge (jñāna), and details its eleven affective manifestations (ekādaśadhā bhakti) along with the requisite disciplines for spiritual aspirants.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naradabhaktisutram.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Nārada, who is cited in the third person within the sūtras (sūtras 19, 84).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_naradabhaktisutram.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all 84 sūtras.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastotram.title: Nārāyaṇastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastotram.summary: A devotional hymn of thirty rhyming couplets praising Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa across his various avatāric deeds (notably Kṛṣṇa and Rāma), featuring the recurring refrain 'nārāyaṇa nārāyaṇa jaya govinda hare'. It is traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastotram.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya (cf. verse 30 and colophon).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text consisting of the opening dhruvapada (refrain), 30 couplets, and the closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastakam.title: Nārāyaṇāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastakam.author: Kūreśa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastakam.summary: The Nārāyaṇāṣṭaka is a short eight-verse devotional hymn (stotra) attributed to Kūreśa. Commemorating Nārāyaṇa as the supreme refuge of the distressed (ārtatrāṇaparāyaṇa), the verses recount canonical instances of divine protection—including Prahlāda, Vibhīṣaṇa, Gajendra, Draupadī, Ahalyā, and Dhruva—culminating in a phalaśruti verse on the efficacy of chanting the name Nārāyaṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayanastakam.coverage: complete — Complete eight-verse stotra with introductory verse, exempla verses, and closing phalaśruti with colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayaniyam_bhaktapriyavy.title: Nārāyaṇīya with Bhaktapriyā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayaniyam_bhaktapriyavy.author: Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa, Deśamaṅgalavārya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayaniyam_bhaktapriyavy.summary: The Nārāyaṇīya is a devotional poem composed by Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭatiri, which condenses the Bhāgavatapurāṇa into 100 daśakas addressed directly to Kṛṣṇa at Guruvayur. This e-text contains the root work accompanied by the Bhaktapriyā commentary of Deśamaṅgalavārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayaniyam_bhaktapriyavy.attribution: The root devotional kāvya was composed by Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa (Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭatiri). The Sanskrit commentary Bhaktapriyā is authored by Deśamaṅgalavārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_narayaniyam_bhaktapriyavy.coverage: complete — Complete in 100 daśakas along with the Bhaktapriyā commentary through daśaka 100.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nilakanthanamassivayastak.title: Nīlakaṇṭhanamaśśivāyāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nilakanthanamassivayastak.summary: The Nīlakaṇṭhanamaśśivāyāṣṭaka is a short devotional hymn of eight verses addressed to Śiva as Nīlakaṇṭha, each verse closing with the refrain 'śrī nīlakaṇṭhāya namaśśivāya'. It is preserved within the Garalapurīnāthamāhātmyam of the Skandapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nilakanthanamassivayastak.attribution: Colophon attributes the stotra to the Garalapurīnāthamāhātmyam of the Skandapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nilakanthanamassivayastak.coverage: complete — Complete stotra consisting of 8 stanzas with the refrain 'śrī nīlakaṇṭhāya namaśśivāya' and 1 concluding narrative verse (9 verses total) followed by the colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nitiprakasika.title: Nītiprakāśikā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nitiprakasika.author: Vaiśampāyana
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nitiprakasika.summary: The Nītiprakāśikā is a Sanskrit treatise on statecraft (nītiśāstra) and the science of warfare (dhanurveda), framed as a dialogue between the sage Vaiśampāyana and King Janamejaya. It provides detailed classifications and descriptions of traditional weapons (mukta, amukta, muktāmukta, yantramukta), battle formations (vyūha), military tactics, and the ethical and administrative duties of kings (rājavyāpāra).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nitiprakasika.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the epic sage Vaiśampāyana (a pupil of Vyāsa), who recites political and military doctrine to King Janamejaya at Takṣaśilā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nitiprakasika.coverage: complete — 8 adhyāyas, ending with the colophon of adhyāya 8 (rājavyāpārakathana, 100 vv.) and 'nītiprakāśikā samāptā'; mūla only, no commentary.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nrsimhasarasvatyastakam.title: Nṛsiṃhasarasvatyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nrsimhasarasvatyastakam.author: Sarasvatī Gaṅgādhara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nrsimhasarasvatyastakam.summary: The Nṛsiṃhasarasvatyaṣṭaka is an eight-verse devotional stotra dedicated to Nṛsiṃha Sarasvatī. Found within the Gurucarita, each verse concludes with the refrain 'vandayāmi nārasiṃha sarasvatīśa pāhi mām'. It praises the guru's spiritual attributes, ascetic discipline, and holy presence at the confluence of the rivers (kṛṣṇāveṇītīravāsa pañcanadīsevanam).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nrsimhasarasvatyastakam.attribution: Verse 8 identifies the composer as the son of Gaṅgādhara ('gaṃgādharāātmajam'), known in tradition as Sarasvatī Gaṅgādhara, author of the Gurucarita (as noted in the colophon 'iti śrī gurucaritrāṃtargata śrīnarasiṃhasarasvatīaṣṭakasaṃpūrṇam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_nrsimhasarasvatyastakam.coverage: complete — Complete 8 stanzas plus concluding phalaśruti verses, though verse 3 has an untranscribed/dotted half-line in line [5].

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_padminiparinayah.title: Padminīpariṇaya with Padminīpariṇayakathāsaṅgraha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_padminiparinayah.author: Elattūr Sundararāja Bhaṭṭācārya, Varadarāja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_padminiparinayah.summary: The Padminīpariṇaya is a ten-act Sanskrit drama by Elattūr Sundararāja Bhaṭṭācārya. Under the story of prince Bhāskara winning princess Padminī, with a sub-plot of Kumudākara and Kaumudī and the guidance of the yogin Śāradānanda, it allegorically retells the Rāmāyaṇa (Bhāskara = Rāma, Padminī = Sītā/Lakṣmī, Jīmūta = Rāvaṇa), as the prefatory Kathāsaṅgraha explains.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_padminiparinayah.attribution: Play ends with bharatavākya mentioning 'bhaktissundararājasūrihṛdaye rāmasya saṃvardhatām'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_padminiparinayah.coverage: complete — Play ends with 'iti padminīpariṇaye daśamo'ṅkaḥ', preceded by the Kathāsaṅgraha.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parasuramastotram.title: Paraśurāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parasuramastotram.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parasuramastotram.summary: A short seven-verse devotional stotra addressed to Paraśurāma, the Bhārgava avatāra of Viṣṇu. The verses extol his iconography (wielding the axe and bow), his vanquishing of Kārtavīryārjuna and the corrupt Kṣatriyas, and his descent as the son of Jamadagni and Reṇukā. Verse 6 highlights him as the recipient of the grace of Dattātreya (śrīdattakaruṇābhājana), reflecting the author's Dattātreya-sampradāya affiliation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parasuramastotram.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to pa. pa. Śrīvāsudevānandasarasvatī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parasuramastotram.coverage: complete — Complete 7-verse hymn concluded by a full colophon marked 'saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancamukhihanumatkavacam.title: Pañcamukhihanumatkavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancamukhihanumatkavacam.summary: A devotional and apotropaic ritual kavaca addressed to Pañcamukha Hanumān, representing five divine aspects (Hanumān, Narasiṃha, Garuḍa, Varāha, and Hayagrīva). The text opens with viniyoga, nyāsa, and dhyāna describing the five faces and ten weapons of the deity, followed by bīja-mantras, exorcistic incantations against diseases, evil spirits, and poisons, and concludes with a phalaśruti claiming provenance from the Sudarśanasaṃhitā and Rudrayāmala.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancamukhihanumatkavacam.attribution: Colophon attributes the text to the Sudarśanasaṃhitā, Rudrayāmala, or Atharvaṇarahasya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancamukhihanumatkavacam.coverage: complete — Complete ritual kavaca text comprising viniyoga, nyāsa, digbandha, dhyāna, prayogamantra, protective prose/mantra invocations, and phalaśruti with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancaratram.title: Pañcarātra (Act 2 end and Act 3)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancaratram.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancaratram.summary: The Pañcarātra is a Sanskrit play attributed to Bhāsa dramatizing an episode related to Duryodhana, Droṇa, and the Pāṇḍavas around the Virāṭa cattle raid. The present file is defective, containing only the finale of Act 2 (from verse 71) and all of Act 3.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pancaratram.coverage: partial — Incomplete: covers only the end of Act 2 (from verse 71 to character exit) and the entire Act 3 (verses 1–26 and closing colophon 'avasitaṃ pañcarātram'). Act 1 and verses 1–70 of Act 2 are missing.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prajnavivardhanastotra.title: Prajñāvivardhanastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prajnavivardhanastotra.summary: The Prajñāvivardhanastotra is a short devotional hymn (stotra) of six verses addressed to Kārttikeya/Skanda. It enumerates twenty-eight epithets of the deity (including Mahāsena, Gāṅgeya, Krauñcāri, and Guha) recommended for morning recitation to attain wisdom, eloquence, and success in learning.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prajnavivardhanastotra.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra of 6 anuṣṭubh verses preceded by a viniyoga formula and concluding with a colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prameyaratnavali.title: Prameyaratnāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prameyaratnavali.author: Baladevavidyābhūṣaṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prameyaratnavali.summary: The Prameyaratnāvalī is an 18th-century philosophical and theological manual composed by the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava thinker Baladevavidyābhūṣaṇa. Structured around nine core philosophical propositions (prameyas) derived from the Mādhva tradition—including the supreme reality of Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa, the ontological reality of the created world, the real distinction between souls and God, and the three means of valid knowledge (pratyakṣa, anumāna, and śabda)—the work validates Gauḍīya theology through extensive śruti, smṛti, and Purāṇic citations.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prameyaratnavali.attribution: Baladevavidyābhūṣaṇa authored the Govindabhāṣya on the Brahmasūtra.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_prameyaratnavali.coverage: complete — Complete text covering all nine prameya sections, concluding with segment 215–216: 'iti śrībhagavatkṛṣṇacaitanyasampradāyācāryaśrīmadbaladevavidyābhūṣaṇakṛtā prameyaratnāvalī pūrtimagāta / samāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ'.
translations: The Brahmasūtras with Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa's Govindabhāṣya and Prameyaratnāvalī, trans. S. C. Vasu. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratijnayaugandharayanam.title: Pratijñāyaugandharāyaṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratijnayaugandharayanam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratijnayaugandharayanam.summary: A four-act drama attributed to Bhāsa. It focuses on Yaugandharāyaṇa, the minister of King Udayana of Vatsa, who acts after Udayana is captured by King Mahāsena of Ujjayinī via an artificial elephant.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratijnayaugandharayanam.coverage: complete — Complete drama in four acts (aṅkas 1–4), preceded by a character list (kathāpātrāṇi) and including inline Sanskrit chāyā in parentheses alongside Prākrit passages.
translations: A. C. Woolner and L. Sarup (trans.), translated verses from Pratijñāyaugandharāyaṇa. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratimanatakam.title: Pratimānāṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratimanatakam.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratimanatakam.summary: The Pratimānāṭaka is a seven-act drama attributed to Bhāsa, dramatizing the Rāmāyaṇa story.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratimanatakam.attribution: The play is attributed to Bhāsa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pratimanatakam.coverage: complete — Complete drama in seven acts (prathamo 'ṅkaḥ through saptamo 'ṅkaḥ), ending with the standard Bharatavākya (7.15) and 'pratimānāṭakaṃ samāptam'. Interlinear Sanskrit chāyā is provided in parentheses following Prakrit passages.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parvatisankaravalambastot.title: Pārvatīśakarāvalambastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parvatisankaravalambastot.author: Śaṅkarabhāratīsvāmī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parvatisankaravalambastot.summary: The Pārvatīśakarāvalambastotra is a 26-verse Śaiva devotional hymn addressed to Śiva as Pārvatīśa (Lord of Pārvatī). Conforming to the karāvalamba genre, each stanza depicts human vulnerability across life stages—childhood ignorance, youthful passion, worldly entanglements, disease, and the horrors of dying—imploring Śiva to extend a sustaining hand (mama dehi karāvalambam) for final refuge.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parvatisankaravalambastot.attribution: Attributed in the final colophon to Śrīmat Paramahaṃsa Parivrājaka Śaṅkarabhāratīsvāmī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_parvatisankaravalambastot.coverage: complete — Complete stotra consisting of 26 verses with phalaśruti and concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pamduramgastakam.title: Pāṇḍuraṅgāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pamduramgastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pamduramgastakam.summary: A short devotional hymn (stotra) of eight verses (and a phalaśruti) dedicated to Viṣṇu in the form of Pāṇḍuraṅga (Viṭṭhala) at Pandharpur on the banks of the Bhīmarathī river. Each stanza describes the iconographic form of the deity standing on a brick to grace his devotee Puṇḍarīka and concludes with the refrain 'parabrahma-liṅgaṃ bhaje pāṇḍuraṅgam'. It is traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pamduramgastakam.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkara (śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_pamduramgastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 stanzas plus 1 concluding phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghuviragadyam.title: Raghuvīragadya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghuviragadyam.author: Vedāntadeśika
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghuviragadyam.summary: The Raghuvīragadya (also known as the Mahāvīravaibhava) is an ornate rhythmic prose hymn (gadya-stotra) composed by Vedāntadeśika in praise of Rāma. Structured as an uninterrupted series of elaborate, alliterative compound epithets in the vocative case, the work narrates the events of Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa sequentially through the seven kāṇḍas.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghuviragadyam.attribution: Attributed to Vedāntadeśika; the concluding verse refers to 'kavikathaka siṃha' (kavikathaka siṃhakathitaṃ) and names the work 'mahāvīra vaibhavaṃ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghuviragadyam.coverage: complete — Complete text, containing the introductory verse, continuous prose vocative epithets tracing the narrative of the Rāmāyaṇa, and the concluding ślokas.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rudrastakam.title: Rudrāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rudrastakam.author: Tulasīdāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rudrastakam.summary: The Rudrāṣṭaka is an eight-stanza Sanskrit hymn (plus a concluding phalaśruti verse) in praise of Śiva. The stotra extols Śiva both as the nirguṇa, transcendental reality beyond name and form, and as the compassionate, iconic saguṇa deity.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rudrastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 8 verses in bhujaṅgaprayāta metre (here split into 16 half-verses) followed by one anuṣṭubh phalaśruti verse (lines 17–18).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavayadaviyam.title: Rāghavayādavīya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavayadaviyam.author: Veṅkaṭādhvarin
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavayadaviyam.summary: The Rāghavayādavīya is an anuloma-viloma citrakāvya in 30 verses composed by the 17th-century South Indian poet Veṅkaṭādhvarin. Read in the standard forward order (anuloma), each verse narrates an episode from the Rāmāyaṇa; read in reverse letter-by-letter order (viloma), each verse depicts the life and deeds of Kṛṣṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavayadaviyam.attribution: Veṅkaṭādhvarin (also known as Veṅkaṭārya Yajvan, 17th century), South Indian poet and author of the Viśvaguṇādarśacampū.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavayadaviyam.coverage: complete — Complete work of 30 verses, each printed with its direct reading (anuloma, for Rāma) followed by its exact reverse reading (viloma, for Kṛṣṇa).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavastakam.title: Rāghavāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavastakam.summary: The Rāghavāṣṭaka is an anonymous Sanskrit devotional poem (stotra) dedicated to Rāma. Across eight verses marked by the refrain 'praṇamāmi rāghavakuñjaram', it eulogizes episodes from the Rāmāyaṇa along with Rāma's divine qualities, concluding with a phalaśruti and a salutation verse.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavastakam.attribution: The hymn is anonymous, with no author indicated in the e-text or headers.
