SA_GK19_ilx_ws_raghavastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 8 verses with the refrain 'praṇamāmi rāghavakuñjaram', followed by 1 phalaśruti verse and 1 concluding namaskāra verse (10 verses total), ending with 'iti śrīrāghavāṣṭakaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rajendrakarnapurah.title: Rājendrakarṇapūra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rajendrakarnapurah.author: Śambhu
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rajendrakarnapurah.summary: The Rājendrakarṇapūra is a short panegyrical poem in 75 verses composed by the 11th-century Kashmiri poet Śambhu in honor of King Harṣadeva of Kashmir. Written in various classical metres including Śārdūlavikrīḍita and Mandākrāntā, the poem praises the king.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rajendrakarnapurah.attribution: Śambhu, a Kashmiri poet ('kāśmīradeśodbhava' in the colophon), addressed the poem to King Harṣadeva of Kashmir; he also wrote the Anyoktimuktālatā (Aufrecht; Mahāsubhāṣitasaṃgraha).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rajendrakarnapurah.edition: Probably the Kāvyamālā printing: Rājendrakarṇapūra of Śambhu, in Kāvyamālā Gucchaka 1, pp. 22–34. (probable)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rajendrakarnapurah.coverage: complete — 75 verses with final colophon 'iti kāśmīradeśodbhavamahākaviśrīśaṃbhuviracito rājendrakarṇapūraḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramakavacam.title: Rāmakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramakavacam.summary: The Rāmakavaca (also termed Vajrakavaca) is an apotropaic prayer (kavaca) addressed to Rāma, presented as an instruction given by the sage Agastya to his disciple Sutīkṣṇa. Embedded in the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa, the hymn comprises liturgical framing formulas (viniyoga, dhyāna), sequential invocations of Rāma's divine names and epithets to safeguard each limb and organ of the practitioner, and an efficacy statement (phalaśruti) promising protection against hazards, sins, and malevolent entities.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramakavacam.attribution: The colophon refers to the text as part of the Vālmīkīya Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Manoharakāṇḍa). In tradition, the work is attributed to Vālmīki.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the stotra (viniyoga, dhyāna, kavaca, and phalaśruti; 28 verses plus prologue/dhyāna), from the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramasatpadi.title: Rāmaṣaṭpadī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramasatpadi.author: Mathurānātha Śukla
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramasatpadi.summary: The Rāmaṣaṭpadī is a seven-verse devotional hymn (stotra) to Rāma composed by Mathurānātha Śukla. It features intricate verbal play and alliteration (yamaka/anuprāsa) across six eulogistic stanzas celebrating Rāma's divine form and virtues, followed by a concluding dedicatory verse.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramasatpadi.attribution: The colophon explicitly names Mālavīya Śukla Mathurānātha as the author.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramasatpadi.coverage: complete — Complete short stotra in 7 verses (6 descriptive/praise verses comprising the ṣaṭpadī plus a concluding phalaśruti/dedicatory stanza) with full closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramastakam.title: Rāmāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramastakam.summary: An eight-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (aṣṭaka) in praise of Rāma. Each verse extols his divine attributes, virtues, and heroic deeds from the Rāmāyaṇa narrative, concluding with the refrain 'śrīrāmacandraṃ satataṃ namāmi'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramastakam.attribution: Circulates anonymously; neither colophon nor traditional attribution is provided in the e-text.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_ramastakam.coverage: complete — Complete in 8 verses with the refrain 'śrīrāmacandraṃ satataṃ namāmi'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samanvaya_vyakhya.title: Kuvalayānanda with Samanvayā (verses 1–104)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samanvaya_vyakhya.author: Appayya Dīkṣita, T. K. Rāmacandra Ayyar
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samanvaya_vyakhya.summary: A Sanskrit commentary (vyākhyā) explaining definition-and-example kārikās on poetic figures (alaṃkāra) including Upamā, Rūpaka, Apahnuti, Tulyayogitā, Nidarśanā, Vibhāvanā, Sama, Svabhāvokti, Bhāvika, and Udātta, glossing vocabulary, clarifying syntax, and providing illustrative verses.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samanvaya_vyakhya.coverage: partial — Kārikās numbered up to 104 with commentary, concluding after an example of Udātta.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sampradayamimamsapatram.title: Sampradāyamīmāṃsāpātra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sampradayamimamsapatram.summary: A short Sanskrit tract of 24 anuṣṭubh verses arguing that the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas belong to the Mādhva sampradāya: sampradāya is defined by dīkṣā-mantra lineage, Caitanya took initiation from Īśvara Purī of the Mādhva line, and doctrinal differences make only a sub-branch (śākhā), as with Rāmānandīs among Rāmānujīyas or Harivyāsīs among Nimbārkīs. It compares Mādhva and Gauḍīya views on mukti, sādhana, pramāṇa and causation and appeals to Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa's Govindabhāṣya and Prameyaratnāvalī.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sampradayamimamsapatram.attribution: No author named. The closing line 'iti śrīśrīgauḍīyavaiṣṇavasāhitye śrīharidāsadāsamahodayena dhṛtam' says the verses were recorded/cited by Haridāsa Dāsa in his Śrīśrīgauḍīyavaiṣṇavasāhitya; it does not make him the author.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sampradayamimamsapatram.coverage: complete — 24 numbered verses (v. 11 and v. 22 have three pādas-pairs) followed by the citation line; complete as transmitted.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santanagopalastotram.title: Santānagopālastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santanagopalastotram.summary: The Santānagopālastotra (referred to in verse 100 as the Putraśataka) is a Vaiṣṇava hymn of 101 verses addressed to Kṛṣṇa in his infant/child form (Gopāla). Preceded by a short mūlamantra, the stotra consists of repeated invocations and petitions seeking the boon of offspring (putralābha / santāna), concluding with a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santanagopalastotram.attribution: A traditional stotra commonly found in devotional stotra compendia; verse 100 identifies it as a 'putraśataka' spoken by Śrīvāsudeva (śrīvāsudevakathita).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santanagopalastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 101 verses preceded by the santānagopāla-mūlamantra.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanatanadevisuktam.title: Sanātanadevīsūkta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanatanadevisuktam.summary: The Sanātanadevīsūkta is a short hymn of 25 verses dedicated to the Goddess. It consists largely of adaptations of celebrated stuti passages from the Devīmāhātmya (specifically the 'yā devī sarvabhūteṣu' refrains of chapter 5 and closing prayers from chapter 11), supplemented with verses eulogizing Devī as the supreme Tripurā and eighteen-armed Mahālakṣmī/Durgā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanatanadevisuktam.attribution: A devotional hymn incorporating and adapting famous verses from the Devīmāhātmya (such as the Aparājitāstuti of chapter 5 and the Nārāyaṇīstuti of chapter 11) alongside verses eulogizing Tripurā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanatanadevisuktam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 25 verses as presented on Sanskrit Wikisource.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasvatistotram.title: Sarasvatīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasvatistotram.summary: The Sarasvatīstotra is a short devotional hymn of ten verses praising Sarasvatī, the goddess of learning and speech. The first eight verses extol her virtues, each ending with the refrain 'tava naumi sarasvati pādayugam' ('I bow, O Sarasvatī, to your pair of feet'), followed by two phalaśruti verses promising wisdom and eloquence to those who recite it.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasvatistotram.attribution: According to verse 10 (idaṃ stavaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ brahmaṇā ca prakirtitam), the stotra is traditionally attributed to Brahmā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasvatistotram.coverage: complete — Complete 10-verse stotra comprising eight verses with the refrain 'tava naumi sarasvati pādayugam' followed by two phalaśruti verses and the concluding colophon 'śrīsarasvatīstutiḥ samāptā'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_siddhamamgalastotra.title: Siddhamaṅgalastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_siddhamamgalastotra.summary: The Siddhamaṅgalastotra is a nine-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn dedicated to Śrīpāda Śrīvallabha, revered in the Datta tradition as the first avatāra of Dattātreya in the Kali Yuga. Originating from chapter 17 of the Śrīpāda Śrīvallabha Caritāmṛta, the hymn invokes the deity through references to his parents, maternal grandfather, lineage, and sacred seat at Pīṭhikāpuram (Pithapuram). Each verse ends with the auspicious refrain 'jaya vijayībhava, digvijayībhava, śrīmadakhaṇḍa śrī vijayībhava'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_siddhamamgalastotra.coverage: complete — Complete 9-verse devotional stotra with its characteristic refrain in each stanza.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_siddhamangalastotram.title: Siddhamaṅgalastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_siddhamangalastotram.summary: The Siddhamaṅgalastotra is a nine-verse devotional hymn dedicated to Śrīpāda Śrīvallabha. The hymn praises his parentage, ancestry, and holy nature, concluding each stanza with a shared benedictory refrain.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_siddhamangalastotram.coverage: complete — Complete in 9 verses with the characteristic victory refrain 'jaya vijayībhava digvijayībhava śrīmadakhaṇḍa śrīvijayībhava'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_suvarnamalastutih_brhatst.title: Suvarṇamālāstuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_suvarnamalastutih_brhatst.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_suvarnamalastutih_brhatst.summary: The Suvarṇamālāstuti is an alphabetical devotional hymn addressed to Śiva as Sāmba Sadāśiva, traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkara. Each stanza begins with a sequential letter of the Sanskrit varṇamālā and incorporates the refrain 'sāmba sadāśiva śambho śaṅkara śaraṇaṃ me tava caraṇayugam'. The text blends Vedāntic philosophical references (such as śruti citations and upādhi terminology) with Śaiva devotional praise.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_suvarnamalastutih_brhatst.attribution: The closing colophon ascribes the hymn to Śaṅkarabhagavat, pupil of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda (śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau). Source headers list the author as Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_suvarnamalastutih_brhatst.coverage: complete — An alphabetical hymn with an opening verse ('atha kathamapi …') and verses covering letters from a to kṣa with the refrain 'sāmba sadāśiva …'. It ends with the colophon 'suvarṇamālāstutiḥ sampūrṇā'. The e-text's verse numbering is erratic: many numbers are omitted, and the second-last verse is numbered 41.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasamuccayah.title: Sārasamuccaya (Sanskrit stanzas only)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasamuccayah.author: Vararuci
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasamuccayah.summary: The Sārasamuccaya is an ethical anthology associated with the Old Javanese tradition containing 511 numbered Sanskrit stanzas (plus 6 introductory verses). In this e-text, the Sanskrit stanzas alone are preserved.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sarasamuccayah.coverage: partial — All Sanskrit stanzas (6 introductory, then 511, ending 'iti sārasamuccayaḥ samāptaḥ'); the Old Javanese text is omitted.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitaramastakam.title: Sītārāmāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitaramastakam.author: Acyutayati
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitaramastakam.summary: The Sītārāmāṣṭaka is a Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) of eight stanzas with a concluding phalaśruti verse composed by Acyutayati, disciple of Madhusūdanāśrama. Addressed to Rāma, each verse praises his divine attributes and deeds while repeating the refrain imploring for devotional service at his lotus feet ('tvāṃ bhajato raghunandana dehi dayāghana me svapadāmbujadāsyam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitaramastakam.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Acyutayati, a pupil of Madhusūdanāśrama; the author's name is also woven as a mudrā / śleṣa into the ninth verse ('labhate'cyutarāmapadāmbujadāsyam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitaramastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 8 stanzas with refrain and 1 phalaśruti stanza, ending with the full colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitastottarasatanamavalih.title: Sītāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitastottarasatanamavalih.summary: The Sītāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī is an anonymous devotional litany comprising 108 names of Sītā framed in the dative case with 'oṃ' and 'namaḥ' for liturgical arcanā. The names praise her divine status as an incarnation of Lakṣmī and recount episodes from the Rāmāyaṇa narrative.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitastottarasatanamavalih.attribution: Traditional devotional nāmāvalī (liturgical list of 108 names); anonymous.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sitastottarasatanamavalih.coverage: complete — Complete ritual litany of 108 dative names with praṇava and namaḥ, concluded by the colophon 'iti sītāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvaliḥ saṃpūrṇā'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundaryastakam.title: Tripurasundaryaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundaryastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundaryastakam.summary: An eight-verse Śākta devotional hymn (aṣṭaka) celebrating the goddess Tripurasundarī (the paramount form of the Divine Mother in the Śrīvidyā tradition). The verses describe her dwelling in the Kadamba forest, her radiant form, compassionate nature, and supreme cosmic power. The text is traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundaryastakam.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya, as stated in the concluding colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundaryastakam.coverage: complete — Complete 8-verse devotional aṣṭaka with colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundarimanasapujas.title: Tripurasundarīmānasapūjāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundarimanasapujas.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundarimanasapujas.summary: The Tripurasundarīmānasapūjāstotra is a 127-verse liturgical hymn belonging to the Śrīvidyā tradition, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. It guides the practitioner through an elaborate internal worship (mānasapūjā) of the goddess Tripurasundarī, visualizing the ocean of nectar (amṛtasindhu), the island of gems (Cintāmaṇidvīpa), the jeweled palace, and the nine circuits (āvaraṇas) of the Śrīcakra, followed by the mental offering of traditional upacāras.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundarimanasapujas.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to Śaṅkara in the closing colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tripurasundarimanasapujas.coverage: complete — Complete text of 127 verses plus the final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tulajastakam.title: Tulajāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tulajastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tulajastakam.summary: The Tulajāṣṭaka is a short Śākta devotional stotra addressed to the goddess Tulajā Bhavānī. Composed of eight descriptive verses each ending with the refrain 'vande 'ham ādyāṃ tulajābhavānīm', it extols the divine mother's beauty, adorned attire, weapons, and cosmic worship by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, followed by a two-verse phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tulajastakam.attribution: Attributed in the text heading and colophon to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tulajastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn consisting of 8 stanzas with the refrain 'vande 'ham ādyāṃ tulajābhavānīm' followed by 2 concluding phalaśruti verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tvamevabruhistotram.title: Tvamevabrūhistotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tvamevabruhistotram.author: Rājamaṇiśarman
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tvamevabruhistotram.summary: A six-verse devotional and patriotic Sanskrit poem addressed to Rāma, composed by Rājamaṇiśarman. The poet laments the contemporary decline of India (Bhārata) and Ayodhyā, asking Rāma why he no longer intervenes against oppressors as he did against Rāvaṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tvamevabruhistotram.attribution: Attributed to Rājamaṇiśarman in the concluding colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tvamevabruhistotram.coverage: complete — Complete short poem in 6 verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tam_vidyamiha_labhemahi.title: Tāṃ Vidyāmiha Labhemahi
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tam_vidyamiha_labhemahi.summary: A six-verse modern Sanskrit prayer song (prārthanā-gīta) honoring true learning and spiritual knowledge (vidyā). Each stanza articulates an essential virtue or fruit of genuine education—dispelling ignorance, alleviating misery, recognizing unity in diversity, fostering altruism, and finding joy—concluding with the refrain 'tāṃ vidyāmiha labhemahi' ('May we attain that knowledge here').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tam_vidyamiha_labhemahi.coverage: complete — Complete text of 6 verses with recurrent refrain.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tandavastakam.title: Tāṇḍavāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tandavastakam.author: Patañjali
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tandavastakam.summary: The Tāṇḍavāṣṭaka is a Sanskrit hymn of nine verses plus a phalaśruti celebrating Śiva Naṭarāja dancing at Chidambaram. Written with the recurring refrain 'paracidambaranaṭaṃ hṛdi bhaja', it avoids sounds with descenders/tails (caraṇa-śṛṅga-rahita) and is traditionally attributed to the serpent-sage Patañjali.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tandavastakam.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Patañjali (iti śrīpatañjalikṛtaṃ tāṃḍavāṣṭakam) and in verse 10 referred to as bhujagapuṅgavakṛta.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_tandavastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn comprising 9 praise verses with the refrain 'paracidambaranaṭaṃ hṛdi bhaja' plus 1 concluding phalaśruti verse (total 10 verses).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uddhavagita.title: Uddhavagītā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uddhavagita.summary: The Uddhavagītā is a philosophical and devotional dialogue contained within the eleventh book (Skandha 11) of the Bhāgavatapurāṇa. Prior to his departure from the earthly realm, Kṛṣṇa imparts instructions to Uddhava, synthesizing metaphysics, cosmology, and devotional theism (bhakti-yoga). Notable sub-episodes within the instruction include the dialogue of the Avadhūta recounting his teachers drawn from nature, the Haṃsagītā, and the Bhikṣugītā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uddhavagita.coverage: complete — Complete text of the eleventh book (Skandha 11) of the Bhāgavatapurāṇa across all 31 adhyāyas (adhyāyas 1–31, ending with the Mausalopākhyāna). The dialogue between Kṛṣṇa and Uddhava itself occupies adhyāyas 6–29.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_udara_jagadadhara.title: Udāra Jagadādhāra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_udara_jagadadhara.summary: A brief eight-verse devotional stotra addressed to Viṣṇu/Hari as Jagadādhāra ('support of the universe'). The speaker prays for non-attachment to family and wealth, constant chanting of the 'Rāma Kṛṣṇa Hare' mantra, liberation from worldly delusion, and the realization of non-dual devotion (advaita-bhakti) where differences of self and other dissolve.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_udara_jagadadhara.attribution: No authorial colophon or external attribution is recorded. The text features the phrase 'rāma kṛṣṇa hare' mantra in verse 6, characteristic of late or modern devotional prayer compositions.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umamahesvarastotram.title: Umāmaheśvarastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umamahesvarastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umamahesvarastotram.summary: The Umāmaheśvarastotra is a short devotional hymn comprising twelve dual-case praise verses and a final benefit-verse (phalaśruti), traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. Each stanza celebrates the joint divine forms of Śiva and Pārvatī and concludes with the recurrent refrain 'namo namaḥ śaṅkarapārvatībhyām'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umamahesvarastotram.coverage: complete — Complete in 12 praise stanzas (dvādaśaka) addressed in dual grammatical case to Śiva and Pārvatī, followed by 1 phalaśruti verse and final colophon 'iti umāmaheśvarastotraṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umasahasranamastotram.title: Umāsahasra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umasahasranamastotram.author: Gaṇapati Muni
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umasahasranamastotram.summary: The Umāsahasra is a 1,000-verse devotional and philosophical mahākāvya in praise of the goddess Umā (Mahāśakti) by Kāvyakaṇṭha Vāsiṣṭha Gaṇapati Muni. Composed in 40 stabakas divided into 10 śatakas across a wide variety of classical meters, the work synthesizes Vedic symbolism, Śākta Tantra, and Advaita metaphysics, culminating in verses honoring the author's guru, Sri Ramana Maharshi.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umasahasranamastotram.attribution: Authored by Vāsiṣṭha Gaṇapati, disciple of Sri Ramana Maharshi and son of Narasiṃha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_umasahasranamastotram.coverage: complete — Complete in 40 stabakas grouped into 10 śatakas, ending with verse 40.25 (cumulative verse 1000) and the final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uttararamacaritam.title: Uttararāmacarita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uttararamacaritam.author: Bhavabhūti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uttararamacaritam.summary: The Uttararāmacarita ('The Later Deeds of Rāma') is a celebrated Sanskrit drama in seven acts composed by Bhavabhūti (8th century CE), dramatizing the later life of Rāma after his return to Ayodhyā, particularly the abandonment of Sītā due to civic suspicion, Rāma's sorrow in the Daṇḍaka forest, and their reunion. Celebrated as a prominent dramatic expression of the pathetic sentiment (karuṇarasa), the play concludes with their full reconciliation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uttararamacaritam.attribution: Attributed to Bhavabhūti, an 8th-century playwright under the patronage of Yaśovarman.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_uttararamacaritam.coverage: complete — Complete drama in seven acts (aṅkas 1–7) with inline Sanskrit chāyā following Prakrit dialogue, closing with the bharatavākya and a brief maṅgala verse from an unnamed commentator (ṭīkākāra).
translations: Coulson, Michael. Three Sanskrit Plays. (English)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vairagyapancakam.title: Vairāgyapañcaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vairagyapancakam.author: Vedāntadeśika
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vairagyapancakam.summary: The Vairāgyapañcaka is a short philosophical hymn on detachment (vairāgya) by the Viśiṣṭādvaita theologian Vedāntadeśika (14th century). Composed in refusal of court patronage, it expresses indifference to worldly wealth and human rulers, asserting that the only true and eternal treasure is Lord Varadarāja on Hastiśaila (Kāñcīpuram).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vairagyapancakam.coverage: complete — Complete text containing all 5 stanzas plus the standard concluding 6th verse (hastiśailāgre vastu paitāmahaṃ dhanam) and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_varahapancaka.title: Varāhapañcaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_varahapancaka.author: Vādirājatīrtha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_varahapancaka.summary: The Varāhapañcaka is a short five-verse devotional stotra addressed to Viṣṇu in his Varāha (boar) avatāra, opening with an invocatory homage to Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_varahapancaka.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Vādirājayatin ('iti śrīvādirājayatikṛtaṃ varāhapañcakaṃ saṃpūrṇam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_varahapancaka.coverage: complete — Complete text of 5 verses followed by the concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vatukabhairavasahasranama.title: Vaṭukabhairavasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vatukabhairavasahasranama.summary: A Śaiva-Śākta devotional hymn of a thousand epithets praising Vaṭukabhairava, the youthful manifestation of Bhairava. Styled as a Devī-Hara dialogue from the Bhairavatantra, it features ritual framing (viniyoga, nyāsa), an alphabetical litany of protective and auspicious names, and a closing phalaśruti on the benefits of recitation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vatukabhairavasahasranama.attribution: Colophon attributes the stotra to the Bhairavatantra, set as a dialogue between Devī and Śiva (Devīharasaṃvāda).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vatukabhairavasahasranama.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 145 verses along with introductory dialogue, viniyoga prose, and closing phalaśruti ending at verse 145 and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedapadastavah.title: Vedapādastava
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedapadastavah.author: Jaimini
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedapadastavah.summary: The Vedapādastava is a 136-verse Śaiva hymn traditionally ascribed to the sage Jaimini. Set within a Purāṇic narrative frame at Puṇḍarīkapura featuring a dialogue between the ṛṣis and Sūta, the stotra praises Śiva dancing in the assembly together with the goddess. It is structured such that Vedic pādas (from the Ṛgveda, Śatarudrīya, and related Vedic mantras) are woven into the metrical lines of the praise.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedapadastavah.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Jaimini (Jaiminimaharṣi), who in the frame narrative encounters Śiva dancing in Puṇḍarīkapura and composes this stotra.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedapadastavah.coverage: complete — Complete in 136 verses, including the introductory frame dialogue (vv. 1–11), the stotra integrating Vedic pādas (vv. 12–133), and the phalaśruti (vv. 134–136), concluding with 'iti śrījaiminimaharṣiṇā praṇīto vedapādastavassampūrṇaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedasarasivastotram.title: Vedasāraśivastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedasarasivastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedasarasivastotram.summary: The Vedasāraśivastotra ('Hymn to Śiva, the Essence of the Veda') is an 11-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. It addresses Śiva both under his iconic aspects (Paśupati, blue-throated, five-faced, consort of Bhavānī) and as the transcendent, formless (nirākāra), non-dual (dvaitahīna) supreme principle described in Vedic and Upaniṣadic thought.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vedasarasivastotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 11 verses with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesastotram.title: Veṅkaṭeśastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesastotram.author: Prativādibhayaṅkara Aṇṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesastotram.summary: An 11-verse hymn to Veṅkaṭeśa (lord of Veṅkaṭa / Vṛṣaśaila), asking for protection and forgiveness, and declaring devotion to him in his Kṛṣṇa and Rāma forms (vv. 4–8).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesastotram.coverage: complete — 11 verses, numbered 1–11, ending 'iti śrī veṅkaṭeśa stotram sampūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesvarasahasranamava.title: Veṅkaṭeśvarasahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesvarasahasranamava.summary: A Vaiṣṇava devotional litany containing 991 formulaic dative invocations ('oṃ [name] namaḥ') addressed to Lord Veṅkaṭeśvara (Śrīnivāsa) of Tirumala-Tirupati. Derived from the versified Veṅkaṭeśvarasahasranāma found in regional Purāṇic māhātmyas, the epithets celebrate the deity's cosmic form, Purāṇic avatāras, and local sacred topography. It is widely used in daily temple archana rituals.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_venkatesvarasahasranamava.coverage: complete — Complete litany of 991 numbered liturgical invocations (from 'oṃ śrī veṅkaṭeśāya namaḥ 1' to 'oṃ veṅkaṭādrigadādharāya namaḥ 991'), concluding with the closing line 'śrī veṅkaṭeśvara sahasranāmāvaliḥ samāptaṃ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vidyaranyastottarasatanam.title: Vidyāraṇyāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vidyaranyastottarasatanam.summary: A 29-verse devotional hymn (stotra) presenting 108 epithets honoring Vidyāraṇya, the 14th-century pontiff of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham. The verses recount traditional biographical and historical accomplishments, including the founding of Vidyānagara (Vijayanagara), the coronation of King Bukka, his commentaries on Vedic and Vedāntic texts, and his ascetic life.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vidyaranyastottarasatanam.attribution: Traditional anonymous stotra reciting 108 names and epithets in praise of Vidyāraṇya Svāmin.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vidyaranyastottarasatanam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 29 verses (28 verses of epithets followed by 1 phalaśruti verse) concluding with ॥ iti śrīvidyāraṇyāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotram ॥.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vilomaksararamakrsnakavya.title: Vilomākṣararāmakṛṣṇakāvya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vilomaksararamakrsnakavya.author: Sūryakavi
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vilomaksararamakrsnakavya.summary: The Vilomākṣararāmakṛṣṇakāvya is a 36-stanza Sanskrit citrakāvya composed by Sūryakavi. In this palindromic work (anulomapratiloma), reading the first half of each stanza forward tells the story of Rāma, while reading the second half in reverse syllable order yields the story of Kṛṣṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vilomaksararamakrsnakavya.attribution: Composed by Sūryakavi, confirmed by the closing colophon: 'iti śrīdaivajñapaṇḍita sūryakavi viracitaṃ vilomākṣararāmakṛṣṇakāvyaṃ samāptam'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vilomaksararamakrsnakavya.coverage: complete — Complete in 36 stanzas, terminating with verse 36 and the author's concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vinayakastotra.title: Vināyakastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vinayakastotra.summary: A devotional hymn to Gaṇeśa (Vināyaka) framed in the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa as spoken by Skanda. It describes the physical iconography, virtues, and divine epithets of Gaṇeśa, and concludes with a four-verse phalaśruti stating the worldly and spiritual benefits of reciting or hearing it.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vinayakastotra.attribution: Colophon attributes the hymn to Skanda within the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa ('iti śrībrahmāṇḍapurāṇe skandaprokta vināyakastotraṃ sampūrṇam'). Per cataloguing conventions, Purāṇic author fields remain empty.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vinayakastotra.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising an introductory dhyāna verse, 16 numbered stotra verses, and 4 phalaśruti verses with final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visvesvarastakam.title: Viśveśvarāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visvesvarastakam.summary: The Viśveśvarāṣṭaka is a devotional stotra comprising eight verses dedicated to Shiva as Viśvanātha / Viśveśvara, the presiding deity of Vārāṇasī (Kāśī). Each verse praises his attributes, iconography, and nature as supreme lord, concluding with the refrain 'vārāṇasīpurapatiṃ bhaja viśvanātham'. A ninth concluding verse describes the spiritual and worldly merits (phalaśruti) of reciting the hymn.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visvesvarastakam.coverage: complete — Contains all 8 main stanzas in Vasantatilakā metre with the refrain 'vārāṇasīpurapatiṃ bhaja viśvanātham', followed by 1 phalaśruti stanza.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnumahimnastotram.title: Viṣṇumahimnastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnumahimnastotram.author: Brahmānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnumahimnastotram.summary: The Viṣṇumahimnastotra is a devotional Sanskrit hymn in 35 verses composed by Paramahaṃsa Brahmānanda in praise of Viṣṇu. Patterned after the devotional 'mahimnaḥ' genre (best known from the Śivamahimnastotra), it extols Viṣṇu as the supreme deity transcending sectarian divisions, recounts the ten avatāras (daśāvatāra), and celebrates his rescue of devotees such as Gajendra.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnumahimnastotram.attribution: Attributed in verse 33 (paramahaṃsajanena samīritam) and the final colophon to Paramahaṃsa Svāmin Brahmānanda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnumahimnastotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn consisting of 35 numbered verses and introductory/closing colophons.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusahasranamavalih.title: Viṣṇusahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusahasranamavalih.summary: The Viṣṇusahasranāmāvalī is a devotional liturgical work comprising the one thousand names of Viṣṇu adapted from the Viṣṇusahasranāmastotra (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsanaparvan). Each epithet is structured as an individual dative formula ('oṃ [name] namaḥ') intended for recitation during ritual worship.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusahasranamavalih.attribution: The thousand names are derived from the Viṣṇusahasranāmastotra in the Anuśāsanaparvan of the Mahābhārata, arranged into dative liturgical formulas with oṃ and namaḥ for ritual worship.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusahasranamavalih.coverage: complete — Contains the complete sequence of liturgical dative invocations (from oṃ viśvasmai namaḥ to oṃ sarvapraharaṇāyudhāya namaḥ).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusatanamastotram.title: Viṣṇuśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusatanamastotram.summary: A short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn enumerating one hundred sacred epithets of Viṣṇu (including Vāsudeva, Hṛṣīkeśa, Jalaśāyin, Govinda, and Puruṣottama). It concludes with a brief phalaśruti stating that recitation delivers the spiritual merit of numerous sacrifices and grants liberation (viṣṇusāyujya).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusatanamastotram.attribution: The phalaśruti attributes the recitation traditionally to Vyāsa ('vyāsena kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_visnusatanamastotram.coverage: complete — Complete short hymn of anuṣṭubh verses (epithets plus phalaśruti) followed by a final mantra formula.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vyaktivivekah.title: Vyaktiviveka (chapter 1)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vyaktivivekah.author: Mahimabhaṭṭa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vyaktivivekah.summary: The Vyaktiviveka is an 11th-century treatise on Sanskrit poetics (alaṅkāraśāstra) by Rājānaka Mahimabhaṭṭa of Kashmir. It was written to refute the theory of suggestion (dhvani/vyañjanā) formulated by Ānandavardhana, arguing that all implied aesthetic meanings are fully explainable by logical inference (anumāna). This first chapter (vimarśa 1) mounts an epistemological critique of Ānandavardhana's definition and main divisions of dhvani.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vyaktivivekah.attribution: Rājānaka Mahimabhaṭṭa was an 11th-century Kashmiri rhetorician. The text consists of mixed prose (vṛtti) and summary verses (saṅgrahaśloka). Ruyyaka's commentary (Vyākhyāna) is not included in this e-text.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vyaktivivekah.coverage: partial — Contains only the first vimarśa (Dhvanilakṣaṇākṣepa), comprising 105 saṅgrahaślokas with intervening prose explanations, terminating at segment [411]. Chapters 2 and 3 are absent.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vasudevastakam.title: Vāsudevāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vasudevastakam.author: Nārāyaṇaguru
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vasudevastakam.summary: The Vāsudevāṣṭaka is an eight-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Vāsudeva (Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa) attributed to Śrī Nārāyaṇaguru. Each stanza celebrates the divine forms, deeds, and attributes of the deity, concluding with the refrain 'śrībhūpate hara hare sakalāmayaṃ me' praying for the removal of all illness and afflictions.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vasudevastakam.attribution: Attributed to Śrī Nārāyaṇaguru in the colophon ('iti śrī nārāyaṇaguruviracitaṃ vāsudevāṣṭakaṃ saṃpūrṇam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_vasudevastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 verses with final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adityanamavalih.title: Ādityanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adityanamavalih.summary: The Ādityanāmāvalī (or Ādityahṛdayanāmāvalī) is a liturgical litany comprising 138 names of the solar deity Āditya/Sūrya, cast in the dative case with initial Praṇava and terminal namaḥ (oṃ ... namaḥ).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adityanamavalih.coverage: complete — Complete sequence of 138 dative ritual salutations (oṃ ... namaḥ) addressed to the solar deity Āditya.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adyastotram.title: Ādyāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adyastotram.summary: The Ādyāstotra is a short Śākta stotra of 20 verses celebrating the primordial Goddess Ādyā (Ādyākālī), framed as a dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada from the Brahmayāmala. It enumerates the various forms of the Goddess worshipped across holy sites (pīṭhas and kṣetras such as Kāmākhyā, Setubandha, Puruṣottama, Gayā, and Vārāṇasī), her puranic manifestations and demon-slaying exploits, and concludes with a protective formula (kavaca) and verses on the religious benefits (phalaśruti) of recitation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adyastotram.attribution: Colophon states: 'iti brahmayāmale brahmanāradasaṃvāde ādyā stotraṃ samāptam'. Traditional tantric attribution to the Brahmayāmala.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_adyastotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 20 verses (the final verse is misnumbered 10 in the e-text) with closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_amnayastotram.title: Āmnāyastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_amnayastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_amnayastotram.summary: The Āmnāyastotra is a 22-verse metrical manual outlining the four cardinal monastic seats (maṭhas): Dvārakā (west), Govardhana/Purī (east), Badarikāśrama (north), and Śṛṅgerī (south). For each maṭha, it systematically details the associated Veda, Mahāvākya, founding disciple (Padmapāda, Hastāmalaka, Toṭaka, Sureśvara), presiding deity, Śakti, tīrtha, sampradāya, and Daśanāmī ascetic titles.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandalahari.title: Ānandalaharī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandalahari.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandalahari.summary: The Ānandalaharī is a devotional hymn of 20 verses addressed to Goddess Bhavānī (Pārvatī), traditionally attributed to Śaṅkarācārya. The work praises the supreme beauty, compassionate maternal grace, and salvific power of the Goddess.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandalahari.attribution: Ascribed by tradition to Śaṅkarācārya, though scholars consider it not to have been composed by the historical Advaita philosopher Śaṅkara.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandasagarastavah.title: Ānandasāgarastava
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandasagarastavah.author: Nīlakaṇṭhadīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandasagarastavah.summary: The Ānandasāgarastava is a devotional hymn (stotra) of 108 verses composed by Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita in praise of the goddess Mīnākṣī at Madurai. It blends ardent Śaiva-Śākta prapatti (self-surrender) with philosophical reflections criticizing dry scholastic intellectualism and complex ritual requirements in favor of devotional refuge.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandasagarastavah.attribution: Colophon explicitly attributes the work to Nīlakaṇṭhadīkṣita.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anandasagarastavah.coverage: complete — Complete stotra in 108 verses with opening and closing verses and colophon intact.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anamdaramayanaramaraksa.title: Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Janmakāṇḍa, sarga 5: Rāmarakṣākathana)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anamdaramayanaramaraksa.summary: The fifth sarga of the Janmakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa recounts the recitation and efficacy of the Rāmarakṣā hymn. Framed as a dialogue between Rāmadāsa and Viṣṇudāsa, it narrates how Śiva revealed this protective kavaca to Pārvatī to empower Skanda to defeat Tārakāsura, and how Vālmīki later employed it to protect Sītā's son Kuśa from baleful planetary spirits. The chapter incorporates the celebrated Rāmarakṣāstotra traditionally attributed to the seer Budhakauśika as its core litany.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anamdaramayanaramaraksa.attribution: The Ānandarāmāyaṇa claims authorship by Vālmīki in its chapter colophons (vālmīkīye janmakāṇḍe). Within the chapter, the incorporated kavaca hymn is explicitly attributed to the ṛṣi Budhakauśika.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anamdaramayanaramaraksa.coverage: partial — One complete chapter of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Janmakāṇḍa, sarga 5, verses 1–51, with colophon). The other sargas and kāṇḍas of the work are not included.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_arttatranastotram.title: Ārttatrāṇastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_arttatranastotram.author: Appayadīkṣita
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_arttatranastotram.summary: An eight-verse devotional stotra addressed to Śiva Gaṅgādhara, attributed to Appayadīkṣita. Each stanza recalls an episode in which Śiva rescued his devotees from danger or suffering—such as drinking the hālāhala poison to save the gods, bestowing the ocean of milk upon Upamanyu, rescuing Mārkaṇḍeya from death, assisting Arjuna, and holding the celestial Gaṅgā for Bhagīratha—concluding with the refrain 'ārttatrāṇaparāyaṇaḥ sa bhagavān gaṅgādharo me gatiḥ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_arttatranastotram.attribution: Attributed in the concluding colophon to Appayadīkṣita.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_arttatranastotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 8 Śārdūlavikrīḍita stanzas with the closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aryapancadasistotram.title: Āryāpañcadaśīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aryapancadasistotram.author: Tyāgarāja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aryapancadasistotram.summary: The Āryāpañcadaśīstotra is a Śākta hymn composed in the āryā metre by Tyāgarāja, an initiate of the guru Ānandanātha. Its 15 verses form an acrostic structured around the 15 syllables of the Śrīvidyā Pañcadaśākṣarī mantra addressed to the Goddess Lalitā / Kāmākṣī, concluding with a benedictory verse.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aryapancadasistotram.attribution: The colophon specifies the author as an Andhra scholar from the Kāśyapa gotra named Tyāgarāja, who was a disciple of Ānandanātha ('ity ānandanāthapādapadmopajīvinā kāśyapagotrotpannenāndhreṇa tyāgarājanāmnā viracitam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_aryapancadasistotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn containing 15 stanzas forming an acrostic on the 15 syllables of the Śrīvidyā Pañcadaśākṣarī mantra (ka-e-ī-la-hrīṃ, ha-sa-ka-ha-la-hrīṃ, sa-ka-la-hrīṃ), followed by a 16th concluding phalaśruti verse and colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamastotra.title: Āñjaneyasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamastotra.summary: The Āñjaneyasahasranāmastotra is a devotional hymn presenting one thousand epithets of Hanumān (Āñjaneya). Framed as a discourse spoken by Vālmīki to assembly sages, the text includes liturgical nyāsa and dhyāna sections followed by names celebrating Hanumān's exploits, cosmic forms, and role as servant and messenger of Rāma, concluding with a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamastotra.attribution: The frame narrative introduces the thousand names of Hanumān via an inquiry by the sages to Vālmīki.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamastotra.coverage: complete — Complete stotra with pūrvapīṭhikā, nyāsa, dhyāna, 1000 names, and phalaśruti (ending at verse 134) with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamavalih.title: Āñjaneyasahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamavalih.summary: The Āñjaneyasahasranāmāvalī is a devotional litany of names addressed to Hanumān (Āñjaneya) formatted for arcana ritual practice (in the dative case flanked by 'oṃ' and 'namaḥ'). The epithets glorify his valor, wisdom, deeds from the Rāmāyaṇa, cosmic attributes, and supreme devotion to Sītā and Rāma.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_anjaneyasahasranamavalih.attribution: Devotional / liturgical name litany (nāmāvalī) for Hanumān (Āñjaneya).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asrayastakam.title: Āśrayāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asrayastakam.summary: The Āśrayāṣṭaka is an eight-verse devotional stotra dedicated to Hariharaputra (Śāstā / Ayyappa). Each stanza concludes with the refrain 'hariharātmajam īśvaram āśraye' ('I take refuge in the Lord, the son of Hari and Hara'), praising the deity's compassionate nature, weapons, forest dwelling, and role as protector of his devotees.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_asrayastakam.coverage: complete — Complete 8 verses with the refrain 'hariharātmajamīśvaramāśraye', terminating with '|| āśrayāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam ||'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanistotram.title: Śanistotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanistotram.summary: A short devotional hymn of 11 verses addressed to the planetary deity Śanaiścara (Saturn). Mythologically placed in the mouth of King Daśaratha, it invokes Saturn by various traditional epithets (such as Koṇa, Antaka, Babhru, Piṅgala, Manda, and Sauri) to avert planetary afflictions, concluding with phalaśruti verses promising protection and welfare.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanistotram.attribution: The stotra frames King Daśaratha as the speaker and seer (daśaratha ṛṣiḥ, daśaratha uvāca) propitiating Saturn (Śanaiścara).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanistotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 11 verses with initial viniyoga formula and concluding colophon (iti śrīdaśarathaproktaṃ śanaiścarastotraṃ saṃpūrṇam).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanivajrapamjarakavacam.title: Śanivajrapaṃjarakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanivajrapamjarakavacam.summary: A short protective hymn (kavaca) of twelve verses addressed to Śani (Saturn), framed as a teaching of Brahmā to the sages (traditionally located in the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa). It invokes various names of Saturn to protect each part of the body and concludes with a phalaśruti offering protection from afflictions caused by adverse astrological transits of Saturn.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanivajrapamjarakavacam.attribution: Colophon attributes the text to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa (brahmanāradasaṃvāde).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sanivajrapamjarakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete 12-verse stotra preceded by an invocation/dhyāna verse and followed by a colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saranagatigadyam.title: Śaraṇāgatigadya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saranagatigadyam.author: Rāmānuja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saranagatigadyam.summary: The Śaraṇāgatigadya is a seminal devotional prose work (gadya) in the Viśiṣṭādvaita Vedānta tradition attributed to Rāmānuja, forming the first component of his Gadyatraya. It takes the form of an imaginary dialogic prayer wherein the aspirant first surrenders to Śrī (Lakṣmī) as mediatrix (puruṣakāra) at Śrīraṅgam, and then through her intercession performs total self-surrender (prapatti / śaraṇāgati) to Nārāyaṇa (Śrīraṅganātha), seeking eternal service (kaiṅkarya).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saranagatigadyam.attribution: Traditionally regarded as the first and primary work of the Gadyatraya prose devotional trilogy composed by Rāmānuja.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saranagatigadyam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Śaraṇāgatigadya, concluding with the colophon attributing it as part of the Gadyatrayaprabandha.
translations: K. Bhashyam, Śaraṇāgatigadya with Sudarśana Sūri's commentary translated into English, Madras: Visishtadvaita Pracharini Sabha, 1958. (English)
Shokei Matsumoto, 『シャラナーガティガディヤ』 [Śaraṇāgatigadyam], Naritasan Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Kiyō (1984). (Japanese)

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samkarastotram.title: Śaṃkarastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samkarastotram.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samkarastotram.summary: A devotional hymn of nine verses addressed to Śiva (Śaṃkara) attributed to Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī. The hymn praises Śiva as the supreme lord who quaffed the hālāhala poison, acknowledges the poet's lack of ritual expertise, and prays for divine grace, steady devotion, and freedom from distress.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samkarastotram.attribution: The colophon attributes the text to 'pa. pa. śrīvāsudevānandasarasvatī'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_samkarastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 9 verses followed by the concluding colophon ('iti śrī pa. pa. śrīvāsudevānandasarasvatīviracitaṃ śaṃkarastotraṃ saṃpūrṇam').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarabhagavaccaranastut.title: Śaṅkarabhagavaccaraṇastutyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarabhagavaccaranastut.author: Vidyāraṇya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarabhagavaccaranastut.summary: An eight-verse hymn (aṣṭaka) in praise of Ādi Śaṅkarācārya, traditionally attributed to Vidyāraṇya Muni. The poem lauds Śaṅkara as an incarnation of the Supreme Reality (Śiva/Brahman) and compares him to a royal swan (paramahaṃsa) that separates the milk of Vedic non-dual truth from the water of worldly confusion.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarabhagavaccaranastut.attribution: Attributed in the concluding colophon to Vidyāraṇya Muni.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarabhagavaccaranastut.coverage: complete — Complete 8-verse hymn (aṣṭaka) with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasahas.title: Śaṅkarācāryāṣṭottarasahasranāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasahas.summary: The Śaṅkarācāryāṣṭottarasahasranāmāvalī is a devotional litany of 1,008 names dedicated to Ādi Śaṅkarācārya. Arranged in dative case with initial 'oṃ' and terminal 'namaḥ', the epithets systematically trace the traditional biography of the philosopher-saint as recounted in the Śaṅkaravijaya literature, from his incarnation in Kālaṭī, education, and renunciation, through his philosophical debates, composition of commentaries, and founding of institutions, to his ascension of the Sarvajñapīṭha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasahas.attribution: Traditional Advaita devotional litany eulogizing Ādi Śaṅkarācārya, heavily drawing upon the narrative tradition of the Śaṅkaravijayas (such as the Mādhavīya Śaṅkaradigvijaya). The closing lines contain formulas characteristic of the South Indian Śaṅkarācārya maṭhas (notably Kāñcī Kāmakoṭi Pīṭha).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasahas.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising four introductory verses, a sequential series of 1,008 dative names (namaḥ litany) recounting the life and accomplishments of Ādi Śaṅkara, and concluding benedictory verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasatan.title: Śaṅkarācāryāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasatan.summary: A 24-verse devotional hymn enumerating 108 laudatory names and deeds of Ādi Śaṅkarācārya. The verses celebrate his role in refuting rival philosophical systems (ṣanmatasthāpanācārya, durvādimatakhaṇḍana), his composition of commentaries and hymns, his encounter with Maṇḍanamiśra, and his disciples including Padmapāda, Sureśvara, Hastāmalaka, and Toṭaka.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankaracaryastottarasatan.coverage: complete — Complete hymn consisting of 24 anuṣṭubh verses followed by a concluding phalaśruti distich.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarastakam.title: Śaṅkarāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarastakam.author: Brahmānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarastakam.summary: The Śaṅkarāṣṭaka is a devotional hymn of eight rhyming verses composed in praise of Lord Śiva by Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda. Each stanza celebrates attributes and mythological deeds of Śiva (such as destroying Kāma, wearing snakes, defeating Tripura, and bearing the Gaṅgā) and concludes with the refrain 'vande'. A concluding phalaśruti verse promises attainment of the Śaiva realm to the dedicated practitioner.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarastakam.attribution: Attributed in the phalaśruti verse (v. 9) and the colophon to Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sankarastakam.coverage: complete — Contains all 8 stanzas praising Śiva, followed by a phalaśruti verse and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivabhujangam.title: Śivabhujaṅga
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivabhujangam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivabhujangam.summary: The Śivabhujaṅga is a devotional hymn to Śiva in 40 verses in the bhujaṅgaprayāta metre, traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkara. It opens with a verse to Gaṇeśa and praises Śiva as the transcendent fourth (turīya), as the five-faced god and in his Ardhanārīśvara form. The poet confesses his unworthiness and prays for protection when the messengers of Death arrive. The last verses give a phalaśruti and name the metre.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivabhujangam.attribution: Traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkara (Potter, EIP vol. 1, Bibliography no. 53).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivabhujangam.coverage: complete — 40 numbered verses in bhujaṅgaprayāta, from the opening verse to Gaṇeśa (Vakratuṇḍa, v. 1) to the signature verse naming the metre (v. 40), followed by the closing line 'śivabhujaṅgaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivakesadipadantavarnanas.title: Śivakeśādipādāntavarṇanastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivakesadipadantavarnanas.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivakesadipadantavarnanas.summary: A hymn of 29 sragdharā verses ascribed to Śaṅkara, describing Śiva's body from head to foot (keśādipādānta). It moves from the matted locks, the tripuṇḍra mark and the third eye through the face, the five faces (Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, Īśāna), the throat, the arms and the torso, down to the toenails and the dust of his feet. Each part is invoked to bless or protect the listeners, and the hymn closes with a verse on Śiva's supreme, attributeless splendour.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivakesadipadantavarnanas.attribution: The colophon ascribes the hymn to Śaṅkara: 'iti śrīmatparamahaṃsa parivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivakesadipadantavarnanas.coverage: complete — 29 verses in sragdharā metre, describing Śiva from his matted locks down to his feet and ending with a summarising v. 29. The closing colophon is present.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamangalastakam.title: Śivamaṅgalāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamangalastakam.summary: The Śivamaṅgalāṣṭaka is an eight-verse Śaiva devotional hymn with a concluding phalaśruti verse. Each stanza praises Śiva in various iconic, theological, and cosmic forms—including the five faces (Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa, and Īśāna)—ending with the auspicious refrain 'maṅgalam'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamangalastakam.attribution: Traditional anonymous stotra; verse 9 states that the hymn was composed upon inspiration from Goddess Cāmuṇḍā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamangalastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 maṅgala verses followed by 1 concluding phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasapuja.title: Śivamānasapūjā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasapuja.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasapuja.summary: The Śivamānasapūjā ('Mental Worship of Śiva') is a short devotional hymn. In four primary Śārdūlavikrīḍita stanzas, the devotee mentally visualizes and presents all ritual offerings (upacāras) to Śiva in the heart, concluding with a non-dual meditation that identifies the devotee's own self with Śiva and every daily action as an act of worship.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasapuja.coverage: complete — Contains the 4 core stanzas of the mānasa-pūjā in Śārdūlavikrīḍita metre, followed by a phalaśruti verse and the well-known kṣamāpanā verse ('karacaraṇakṛtaṃ...').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasikapujastotram.title: Śivamānasikapūjāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasikapujastotram.author: Śivānandāvadhūta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasikapujastotram.summary: A 30-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Śiva composed by Śivānandāvadhūta. Structured around the theme of mental worship (mānasikapūjā), the hymn poetically contrasts standard ritual upacāras (such as āsana, snāna, vastra, dīpa, and gīta) with Śiva's infinite, transcendent nature, concluding with surrender and prayer for non-dual bliss.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasikapujastotram.attribution: The colophon explicitly attributes this 30-verse hymn to Śivānandāvadhūta (iti śivānandāvadhūtaracita śivamānasikapūjāstotram).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamanasikapujastotram.coverage: complete — Complete in 30 verses with introductory title and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamatrkavarnamalastotra.title: Śivamātṛkāvarṇamālāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamatrkavarnamalastotra.summary: The Śivamātṛkāvarṇamālāstotra is an alphabetical Śaiva hymn (mātṛkāstotra) attributed to the Skandapurāṇa. Set in a narrative frame where Viṣṇu performs austerities on Mount Kailāsa, each verse systematically praises Śiva using the successive letters of the Sanskrit alphabet (vowels, bindu, visarjanīya, and consonants), blending devotional epithets with non-dualistic philosophical attributes.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamatrkavarnamalastotra.attribution: Colophon explicitly identifies the hymn as an excerpt from the Skandapurāṇa: 'iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe viṣṇukṛtaśivamātṛkāvarṇamālāstotram'. Spoken by Viṣṇu (Nārāyaṇa) in the framing narrative by Sūta.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivamatrkavarnamalastotra.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 69 verses, including narrative prologue (vv. 1–6), the alphabetical mātṛkā hymn (vv. 7–65), and epilogue/phalaśruti (vv. 66–69).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanaksatramalikastotram.title: Śivanakṣatramālikāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanaksatramalikastotram.author: Kṛṣṇarāja Woḍeyar III
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanaksatramalikastotram.summary: A 27-stanza devotional hymn (nakṣatramālikā) in praise of Śiva, composed by Kṛṣṇarāja (Kṛṣṇabhūpa / Śrīkṛṣṇendra). Each of the 27 stanzas praises an aspect or mythological feat of Śiva, ending with the common refrain 'śiva eva gatirmama', accompanied by three concluding stanzas providing the dedication, phalaśruti, and metric/chronogram details.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanaksatramalikastotram.attribution: Attributed in verses 28–30 to Kṛṣṇabhūpa / Śrīkṛṣṇendra, who is described as filled with the grace of goddess Cāmuṇḍā ('śrīcāmuṇḍākṛpāpūrṇa'). Verse 30 contains a Śaka date beginning 'ratnaśailanagāvanī'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanaksatramalikastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 30 verses: 27 verses corresponding to the nakṣatras with the refrain 'śiva eva gatirmama', followed by three concluding verses (verses 28–30) with authorial dedication, phalaśruti, and chronogram.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanavaratnastavah.title: Śivanavaratnastava
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanavaratnastavah.summary: The Śivanavaratnastava ('Nine-Gem Praise of Śiva') is a short devotional hymn extracted from the Sūtasaṃhitā of the Skandapurāṇa. Consisting of nine verses in praise of Śiva spoken by Bṛhaspati followed by three verses of phalaśruti narrated by Sūta, it extols Śiva through metaphysical and yogic epithets (including references to the mūlādhāra and nābhikanda) as the supreme Brahman and granter of liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanavaratnastavah.attribution: In the colophon (iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe sūtasaṃhitāyāṃ bṛhaspatikṛtaḥ śivanavaratnastavaḥ), the hymn is framed as spoken by Bṛhaspati to Śiva, narrated by Sūta in the Sūtasaṃhitā section of the Skandapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanavaratnastavah.coverage: complete — Complete 12-verse hymn (9 verses of praise spoken by Bṛhaspati plus 3 verses of phalaśruti spoken by Sūta) extracted from the Sūtasaṃhitā of the Skandapurāṇa.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanamavalyastakam_brhat.title: Śivanāmāvalyaṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanamavalyastakam_brhat.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanamavalyastakam_brhat.summary: A short hymn to Śiva ascribed to Śaṅkara. Its eight vasantatilakā verses string together vocative names of Śiva (Candracūḍa, Girīśa, Nīlakaṇṭha, Viśvanātha, the lord of Vārāṇasī and Maṇikarṇikā, and others), each closing with the plea 'O lord of the world, save me from the dense thicket of saṃsāric suffering'. A ninth verse of homage, which also appears in the Dāridryadahanaśivastotra, concludes the text.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanamavalyastakam_brhat.attribution: The colophon ascribes the hymn to Śaṅkara ('iti śrīmatparamahaṃsa parivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau'). The attribution is traditional, not historically established.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanamavalyastakam_brhat.coverage: complete — Eight vasantatilakā verses with the refrain 'saṃsāraduḥkhagahanāj jagadīśa rakṣa' (abbreviated 'saṃsāra ...' after v. 1), a ninth verse 'gaurīvilāsabhavanāya maheśvarāya ...' with the refrain 'dāridryaduḥkhadahanāya namaḥ śivāya', and the colophon. The ninth verse is also a verse of the popular Dāridryadahanaśivastotra.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapancaksaristotram_brh.title: Śivapañcākṣarīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapancaksaristotram_brh.summary: A short Śaiva devotional hymn of seven verses praising Lord Śiva. The hymn meditates upon the Praṇava (Oṃ) followed by the syllables of the Pañcākṣaramantra (na-ma-śi-vā-ya), with each successive verse dedicated to an individual syllable, and finishes with a closing verse of dual homage to Śivā and Śiva.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapancaksaristotram_brh.attribution: Anonymous: the colophon ('iti śivapañcākṣarīstotram') names no author. It is distinct from the well-known Śivapañcākṣarastotra ascribed to Śaṅkara ('nāgendrahārāya trilocanāya ...'), being constructed upon oṃ and the syllables na-ma-śi-vā-ya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapancaksaristotram_brh.coverage: complete — 7 verses, with the refrain abbreviated as '...' in vv. 2–6: one on oṃ, one on each of the five syllables na-ma-śi-vā-ya, and a closing verse of homage to Śivā and Śiva. The colophon follows.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapratipadanastotram.title: Śivapratipādanastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapratipadanastotram.summary: The Śivapratipādanastotra is a short devotional hymn of 21 verses praising Śiva, extracted from the Skandapurāṇa in the context of a dialogue between Nandīśvara and Viṣṇu. Using repetitive anaphoric salutations ('namas te'), the hymn glorifies Śiva as the ultimate ground of creation and dissolution, manifesting as the elements, bodily and sensory faculties, and epistemic categories (mātṛ, māna, meya, miti).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapratipadanastotram.attribution: Traditional Purāṇic hymn, stated in the concluding colophon to be from the Skandapurāṇa (Nandīśvaraviṣṇusaṃvāda).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapratipadanastotram.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 21 verses plus colophon (segment [22]), as preserved in the source.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapadadikesantastutih.title: Śivapādādikeśāntastuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapadadikesantastutih.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapadadikesantastutih.summary: A 41-verse devotional stotra in the sragdharā metre praising Śiva. The hymn opens with descriptions of Kailāsa, Śiva's weapons, and his entourage (including Gaṇeśa, Skanda, and Nandin), followed by a systematic devotional description of the deity's physical form from feet to head (pādādikeśānta) concluded by a phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapadadikesantastutih.attribution: Attributed to Śaṅkarācārya (pupil of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda) in the concluding colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivapadadikesantastutih.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 41 verses in sragdharā metre with closing phalaśruti and concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivaraksastotram.title: Śivarakṣāstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivaraksastotram.author: Yājñavalkya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivaraksastotram.summary: The Śivarakṣāstotra is a protective hymn (kavaca/rakṣā) of twelve verses dedicated to Sadāśiva/Śiva. Closely modeled in structure and phrasing on the popular Rāmarakṣāstotra of Budhakauśika, it invokes different epithets and aspects of Śiva to protect every part of the reciter's body, and concludes with a phalaśruti attesting to protection from supernatural harm and final liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivaraksastotram.attribution: Traditional attribution to the sage Yājñavalkya, stated explicitly in verse 12 (stating that Yājñavalkya wrote down what Nārāyaṇa revealed to him in a dream) and in the introductory viniyoga and colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivaraksastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising introductory viniyoga, dhyāna, kavaca/rakṣā verses, and phalaśruti (12 numbered verses total).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasahasranamastotram.title: Śivasahasranāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasahasranamastotram.summary: The Śivasahasranāmastotra ('Hymn of the Thousand Names of Śiva') is a major Śaiva devotional hymn extracted from the Anuśāsanaparvan of the Mahābhārata (adhyāya 17). Narrated by Upamanyu to Kṛṣṇa, who in turn recounts it to Yudhiṣṭhira, the hymn contains the one thousand epithets of Śiva originally revealed to the sage Taṇḍi. It synthesizes Vedic, cosmogonic, and philosophical aspects of Śiva and forms one of the standard liturgical sahasranāmas of the Hindu tradition.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasahasranamastotram.attribution: Within the Mahābhārata frame, Kṛṣṇa narrates to Yudhiṣṭhira the stotra as taught by Upamanyu, who received it from the sage Taṇḍi.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasahasranamastotram.coverage: complete — Complete stotra as extracted from Mahābhārata Anuśāsanaparvan 17 (vulgate numbering), comprising an invocatory dhyāna verse, 182 numbered ślokas (introductory narrative, 1,000 names, and phalaśruti), and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivastotram.title: Śivastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivastotram.author: Upamanyu
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivastotram.summary: A 20-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Śiva, traditionally attributed to the sage Upamanyu. The verses praise Śiva's paradoxical attributes (such as bearing virulent poison yet being ambrosial, carrying skulls yet conferring supreme purity), express humble surrender, and plead for liberation from worldly suffering and the clutches of death, concluding with two benedictory phalaśruti stanzas.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivastotram.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 20 verses (numbered 1–16, then repeating numbers 14–17 due to an internal numbering error in the source), concluded with phalaśruti verses and final colophon 'ityupamanyukṛtaṃ śivastotraṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram.title: Śivatāṇḍavastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram.author: Rāvaṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram.summary: The Śivatāṇḍavastotra is a well-known ecstatic hymn dedicated to Śiva's cosmic dance (tāṇḍava). Composed largely in the rhythmic Pañcacāmara meter, it celebrates Śiva's cosmic form and ascetic beauty before closing with devotional phalaśruti verses.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the mythical king of Laṅkā, Rāvaṇa; historical authorship and date are undetermined.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 17 verses (15 descriptive verses in pañcacāmara meter followed by 2 concluding phalaśruti verses) with closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram_brhats.title: Śivatāṇḍavastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram_brhats.author: Rāvaṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram_brhats.summary: The Śivatāṇḍavastotra is a hymn ascribed to Rāvaṇa, in the pañcacāmara metre except for the last verse. With heavy alliteration and onomatopoeia ('dhagad-dhagad-dhagaj-jvalal-…'), it celebrates Śiva's fierce tāṇḍava dance, the Gaṅgā in his matted locks, his serpent ornaments and the fire of his forehead eye. The poet longs for equanimity and for devotion to Śiva. The last two verses give a phalaśruti for daily recitation and for recitation after pūjā on pradoṣa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram_brhats.attribution: The opening title ('rāvaṇakṛtaśivatāṇḍavastotram') and the colophon ('iti śrīrāvaṇaviracitaṃ śivatāṇḍavastotraṃ sampūrṇam') ascribe the hymn to Rāvaṇa, and v. 14 calls it 'daśavaktragītam'. Rāvaṇa is kept because the source names him.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivatandavastotram_brhats.coverage: complete — 14 verses: 13 in pañcacāmara metre (vv. 1–12 praising Śiva's dance and v. 13 a phalaśruti) and v. 14 in vasantatilakā (daśavaktragītam, for recitation at the end of pūjā on pradoṣa). The colophon follows. A stray line 'rāvaṇakṛtaśivatāṇḍavastotram' inside v. 12 appears in the e-text.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasankarastakam.title: Śivaśaṅkarāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasankarastakam.summary: A devotional hymn (stotra) of eleven stanzas addressed to Śiva. The poet laments mortal frailty, the fear of death, and the torment of Yama's messengers, concluding each verse with the refrain 'śivaśaṅkara śivaśaṅkara hara me hara duritam' seeking deliverance from sins and suffering.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasankarastakam.attribution: An anonymous devotional stotra addressed to Śiva.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivasankarastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 11 verses ending with 'iti śrī śivaśaṅkarāṣṭakam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanandalahari_brhatstot.title: Śivānandalaharī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanandalahari_brhatstot.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sivanandalahari_brhatstot.summary: The Śivānandalaharī ('Wave of the bliss of Śiva') is a hymn of 100 verses to Śiva in various metres, traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkara. It joins Advaita themes to fervent bhakti, using extended images for the devotee's mind: an elephant to be bound with the chain of devotion, a monkey, a bride. It also uses images of devotion itself, such as the hunter Kaṇṇappa's offering. The closing verses offer the poem to Śiva as a bride and assert his supremacy over Brahmā and Viṣṇu.

It petitions the deity and the holy city to awaken and bestow auspiciousness, praising the sacred tīrthas of Kāśī including the river Gaṅgā, Maṇikarṇikā, Dhuṇḍirāja Gaṇeśa, and Annapūrṇā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikasivisvanathasuprabha.attribution: Traditional devotional morning hymn associated with the Kāśī Viśvanātha temple in Varanasi, incorporating several well-known traditional verses (e.g., v. 3 'brahmā murāris tripurāntakārī', v. 26 'sānandam ānandavane vasantam').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnakarnamrtam.title: Śrīkṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnakarnamrtam.author: Līlāśuka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnakarnamrtam.summary: The Śrīkṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta (or Kṛṣṇakarṇāmṛta) is an influential Sanskrit devotional lyric celebrating the beauty, sweetness (mādhurya), and sports of Kṛṣṇa in Vraja. In the southern recension, the work consists of three cantos (āśvāsas) of approximately one hundred verses each; the eastern (Bengal) tradition preserves primarily the first canto, famously brought to Bengal by Caitanya Mahāprabhu, where it became a cornerstone of Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava aesthetics and devotion.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnavilasam.title: Kṛṣṇavilāsa (cantos 1–4)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnavilasam.author: Sukumāra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnavilasam.summary: The Kṛṣṇavilāsa is a Sanskrit mahākāvya by Sukumāra on the life of Kṛṣṇa. This e-text contains sargas 1–4. They begin with the description of Mount Meru and the gods' appeal to Viṣṇu over the burden of the Earth, and go on to Kṛṣṇa's birth and his childhood in Gokula, ending with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma tending the herds in Vraja.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnavilasam.attribution: Ascribed to the poet Sukumāra (Sukumārakavi) in the heading and the colophons.

It celebrates Kṛṣṇa's divine deeds from his childhood in Vraja to the Mahābhārata war, closing with a ninth verse promising liberation from rebirth.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnastaka.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Paramahaṃsa Brahmānanda ('iti śrīparamahaṃsabrahmānandaviracitaṃ śrīkṛṣṇāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam'). The source header and URL attribute it to Śaṅkara / Śrīmacchaṅkarācārya.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnastakam.summary: The Śrīkṛṣṇāṣṭaka is an eight-stanza devotional hymn (stotra) dedicated to Kṛṣṇa. Each verse praises aspects of Kṛṣṇa's iconography, attributes, and divine actions, ending with the recurring refrain 'kṛṣṇaṃ vande jagadgurum' ('I revere Kṛṣṇa, teacher of the universe'), followed by a single concluding phalaśruti verse.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srikrsnastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text consisting of the 8 stanzas with the refrain 'kṛṣṇaṃ vande jagadgurum' plus one closing phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilaksmanakavacam.title: Lakṣmaṇakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilaksmanakavacam.summary: The Lakṣmaṇakavaca is a protective devotional hymn (kavaca) dedicated to Lakṣmaṇa, extracted from the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa. Narrated by Agastya, it comprises initial ritual procedures (viniyoga, nyāsa), a visualization meditation (dhyāna, vv. 1–4), and an apotropaic sequence (vv. 5–15) invoking Lakṣmaṇa's various epithets to protect directions and parts of the body.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilaksmanakavacam.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vālmīki as part of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Manoharakāṇḍa); framed as spoken by the sage Agastya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilaksmanakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the stotra as found in Ānandarāmāyaṇa, Manoharakāṇḍa, containing viniyoga, nyāsa, dhyāna (verses 1–4), protective kavaca (verses 5–15), and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilingastakam.title: Liṅgāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilingastakam.summary: The Liṅgāṣṭaka is an eight-verse Śaiva devotional hymn (aṣṭaka) in praise of the Liṅga form of Sadāśiva. Each verse highlights divine attributes and deeds associated with the Liṅga and closes with the refrain 'tatpraṇamāmi sadāśivaliṅgam'. A ninth concluding verse conveys the phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srilingastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of eight stanzas ending with the refrain 'tatpraṇamāmi sadāśivaliṅgam', followed by a concluding phalaśruti verse.

It is excerpted from the Ānandarāmāyaṇa, a popular late medieval Sanskrit retelling of the Rāma story emphasizing devotional rituals, stotras, and pilgrimages.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimadanjaneyastottarasat.title: Śrīmadāñjaneyāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimadanjaneyastottarasat.summary: The Śrīmadāñjaneyāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra is a 22-verse devotional hymn enumerating 108 epithets and deeds of Hanumān (Āñjaneya). SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimahadevakrtaramastotra.title: Mahādevakṛtarāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimahadevakrtaramastotra.summary: The Mahādevakṛtarāmastotra is a 13-verse stotra excerpted from the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa. In it, Śiva (Mahādeva) praises Rāma as the non-dual supreme reality (Brahman) transcending the three guṇas and cycle of creation. Śiva famously notes that he resides in Kāśī with Pārvatī and imparts the saving mantra of Rāma's name (tāraka-mantra) to those dying there.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimahadevakrtaramastotra.attribution: A 13-verse devotional stotra addressed by Mahādeva (Śiva) to Rāma, excerpted from the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimahadevakrtaramastotra.coverage: complete — Complete 13-verse stotra plus framing colophon as extracted from the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srimahalaksmyastakam.title: Śrīmahālakṣmyaṣṭaka

It concludes with a three-verse phalaśruti detailing the spiritual and material rewards of reciting the text once, twice, or thrice daily.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinandakumarastakam.summary: An eight-verse devotional hymn (aṣṭaka) celebrating Kṛṣṇa as Nandakumāra ('the son of Nanda'). Set in a rhythmic rhyming metre, each verse praises Kṛṣṇa's physical beauty, divine sports in Vraja/Vṛndāvana, and role as the ultimate refuge, while incorporating the poet's signature name 'vallabha'. The text is a popular devotional recitation in the Puṣṭimārga tradition.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinandakumarastakam.attribution: Attributed by colophon to Vallabhācārya. Each stanza embeds the signature 'vallabha'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinrsimhasarasvatiprarth.title: Śrīnṛsiṃhasarasvatīprārthanāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinrsimhasarasvatiprarth.author: Vāsudevānandasarasvatī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinrsimhasarasvatiprarth.summary: The Śrīnṛsiṃhasarasvatīprārthanāṣṭaka is an eight-verse hymn (aṣṭaka) composed by Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī in praise of the saint Nṛsiṃha Sarasvatī, regarded in the Dattātreya sampradāya as an incarnation of Dattātreya. The verses enumerate prominent miracles associated with him in the Guru Caritra tradition—such as reviving a dead Brahmin's son, making a barren buffalo yield milk, and curing leprosy—with each verse concluding with the refrain 'sa nṛsiṃhasarasvatī yatir bhagavān me'sti parā varā gatiḥ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinrsimhasarasvatiprarth.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to 'śrī pa. pa. śrīvāsudevānandasarasvatī'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srinrsimhasarasvatiprarth.coverage: complete — Complete eight-verse devotional stotra (aṣṭaka) with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriraghunathastakam.title: Raghunāthāṣṭaka

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriraghunathastakam.summary: The Raghunāthāṣṭaka is a short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn (stotra) dedicated to Rāma. In eight verses featuring a recurrent refrain ('sasītaṃ sānandaṃ praṇata raghunāthaṃ suranutam'), it outlines major milestones of the Rāmāyaṇa narrative—including the birth in the solar lineage, breaking of Śiva's bow, forest exile, monkey alliance, destruction of demons, and righteous rule in Ayodhyā—concluding with a phalaśruti verse.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriraghunathastakam.attribution: Colophon explicitly credits the hymn to Paṇḍita Śivadatta Miśra Śāstrī ('iti paṇḍita śrīśivadattamiśraśāstri viracitaṃ śrīraghunāthāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam'). Verse 9 states 'raghunāthena nirmitam', which functions either as a punning dedication to Raghunātha (Rāma) or as an alternate authorial moniker.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriraghunathastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 stanzas with the refrain 'sasītaṃ sānandaṃ praṇata raghunāthaṃ suranutam', followed by a concluding ninth phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srirangastotra.summary: A short Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn of ten verses addressed to Lord Raṅganātha (Viṣṇu reclining at Srirangam), followed by a concluding phalaśruti verse. SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srirangastotra.coverage: complete — Complete 10-verse stotra plus one concluding phalaśruti verse (total 11 verses), terminating with 'iti śrīraṅgastotram'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramabhujangaprayatasto.title: Śrīrāmabhujaṅgaprayātastotra

The text celebrates Rāma's grace, his deliverance of devotees, and the liberating potency of his holy name in Kāśī, concluding with earnest supplications for protection from death and worldly fear.

The eight principal stanzas praise Rāma's divine forms, deeds, and epithets, each concluding with the refrain 'ramānātho rāmo ramatu mama citte tu satatam', followed by a final verse on the fruits of recitation (phalaśruti).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramacandrastakam.attribution: The poet Amaradāsa identifies himself in the colophon as a disciple of Haṃsadāsa, who was in turn a disciple of Rāmadāsa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramacandrastakam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 8 stanzas with recurring refrain plus 1 phalaśruti stanza and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramagita.title: Rāmagītā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramagita.summary: The Rāmagītā is an Advaita Vedānta philosophical dialogue forming the fifth chapter of the Uttarakāṇḍa of the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa. In response to questions posed by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma teaches that release from saṃsāra is attained not by ritual works (karma) or a combination of knowledge and action (jñānakarmasamuccaya), but solely through direct knowledge (jñāna) of the non-dual Self (ātman). The work systematically synthesizes classical Upaniṣadic Advaita epistemology with devotion to Rāma.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramagita.attribution: Embedded in the Uttarakāṇḍa (chapter 5) of the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, which is framed as an Umā-Maheśvara dialogue.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramagita.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Rāmagītā from the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa (Uttarakāṇḍa, sarga 5), comprising all 62 verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramahrdayam.title: Rāmahṛdaya
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramahrdayam.summary: The Rāmahṛdaya ('Heart of Rāma') is a nine-verse Advaita teaching from the Bālakāṇḍa of the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, which circulates on its own as a stotra. Narrated by Śiva, it gives Rāma's instruction to Hanumān on the self, the non-self and the supreme self. It uses the analogy of threefold space (total space, space enclosed in a pond, and space reflected in its water) for brahman, consciousness delimited by the intellect, and its reflection (ābhāsa). Liberation comes through knowing identity by the mahāvākyas, combined with devotion to Rāma.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramahrdayam.attribution: The colophon reads 'śrīmadadhyātmarāmāyaṇe bālakāṇḍe śrīrāmahṛdayaṃ sampūrṇam'. The passage is spoken by Śiva ('śrī mahādeva uvāca'), who reports Rāma's teaching to Hanumān.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramahrdayam.coverage: complete — The complete Rāmahṛdaya as it circulates on its own: 9 verses ('tato rāmaḥ svayaṃ prāha …' to 'idaṃ rahasyaṃ hṛdayaṃ …'), from Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, Bālakāṇḍa. It is an excerpt only relative to the Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, and the title already names just the Rāmahṛdaya. The e-text gives the passage twice in a row, which is a Wikisource duplication, not additional text.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramanamasamkirtanam.title: Śrīrāmanāmasaṃkīrtana
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramanamasamkirtanam.summary: The Śrīrāmanāmasaṃkīrtana (popularly known as the Nāmarāmāyaṇa or Aṣṭottaraśatanāmarāmāyaṇa) is a devotional chanting litany that recounts the narrative of the Rāmāyaṇa through 108 epithets and invocations of Rāma arranged sequentially across all seven kāṇḍas. In this compilation, the hymn is prefaced by traditional dhyānaślokas—notably the Sanskrit maṅgalācaraṇa verses from Tulsīdāsa's Rāmacaritamānasa—and concludes with seven well-known devotional verses dedicated to Hanumān.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramanamasamkirtanam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the liturgical chanting compilation as presented, consisting of introductory verses and a prayer, the 108 names of the Nāmarāmāyaṇa across the seven kāṇḍas, and concluding Hanūmatstotra verses ending with 'iti aṣṭottaraśatanāmarāmāyaṇaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramapratahsmaranam.title: Śrīrāmaprātaḥsmaraṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramapratahsmaranam.summary: The Śrīrāmaprātaḥsmaraṇa is a short devotional stotra consisting of five verses and a phalaśruti verse intended for morning recitation. Each verse sequentially directs contemplation to Rāma's lotus-like face, hands, feet, holy name, and divine form, recounting mythic events such as the breaking of Śiva's bow and the liberation of Ahalyā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramapratahsmaranam.coverage: complete — Complete hymn comprising 5 devotional kārikās plus 1 phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastakam.title: Śrīrāmāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastakam.author: Brahmānanda
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastakam.summary: A short devotional hymn consisting of eight verses in praise of Rāma with the refrain 'namāmi rāmamīśvaram', followed by a concluding phalaśruti verse. The stanzas recount key episodes of the Rāmāyaṇa narrative, including the protection of Viśvāmitra's sacrifice, the release of Ahalyā from her stone curse, the breaking of Śiva's bow, the chasing of the golden deer, the salvation of Jaṭāyu, the bridging of the ocean, and the slaying of Rāvaṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastakam.attribution: Attributed to Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda in the closing colophon ('iti śrīparamahaṃsasvāmibrahmānandaviracitaṃ śrīrāmāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam'). In verse 9 it is termed Raghūttamāṣṭaka.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastakam.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 8 octet verses ending with the refrain 'namāmi rāmamīśvaram' and a 9th phalaśruti stanza.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastottarasatanamava.title: Śrīrāmāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastottarasatanamava.summary: The Śrīrāmāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī is a devotional litany of 108 names of Rāma recited during ritual worship (arcana) and daily prayer. The names invoke his physical beauty, epic feats from the Rāmāyaṇa (such as slaying Tāṭakā, Khara, and Rāvaṇa, and breaking the bow of Śiva), his virtues, and his supreme theological identity as Parabrahman and the source of liberation.
