SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastottarasatanamava.attribution: A traditional liturgical recitation consisting of 108 names of Rāma in the dative case accompanied by Praṇava and namaḥ, widely found in Vaiṣṇava pūjā paddhatis and stotra collections.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sriramastottarasatanamava.coverage: complete — Complete litany containing all 108 dative names with closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisadasivendrastavah.title: Śrīsadāśivendrastava
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisadasivendrastavah.author: Saccidānandaśivābhinavanṛsiṃhabhāratī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisadasivendrastavah.summary: A devotional hymn (stotra) of 45 verses composed by Jagadguru Saccidānanda Śivābhinava Nṛsiṃha Bhāratī praising the Advaita master and avadhūta Sadāśiva Brahmendra Sarasvatī. The verses describe his strict asceticism, his literary works such as the Siddhāntakalpavallī, and well-known hagiographical legends including his undisturbed equanimity when attacked and dismembered by an ascetic-hostile passerby.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisadasivendrastavah.attribution: Composed by Śṛṅgagiri Jagadguru Saccidānandaśivābhinavanṛsiṃhabhāratī Mahāsvāmin, as stated in the colophon.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisadasivendrastavah.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 45 verses with concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakanamavali.title: Śrīsiddhivināyakāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakanamavali.summary: The Śrīsiddhivināyakanāmāvalī is a liturgical recitation consisting of names of Gaṇeśa (Siddhivināyaka) in the dative case accompanied by 'namaḥ'. The names invoke his attributes, form, and status as the remover of impediments and grantor of spiritual and worldly success.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakanamavali.attribution: Traditional devotional recitation of names (nāmāvalī) of Siddhivināyaka.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakanamavali.coverage: complete — Litany of names in dative form with 'namaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakastotram.title: Śrīsiddhivināyakastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakastotram.author: Divākara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakastotram.summary: A 20-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (stotra) dedicated to Gaṇeśa as Siddhivināyaka. It comprises prayers for wisdom, protection against obstacles, descriptions of Gaṇeśa's iconographic forms and divine epithets, and concludes with a phalaśruti and signature by the devotee Divākara.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakastotram.attribution: Internally attributed to the devotee Divākara in verse 20.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisiddhivinayakastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 20 verses including phalaśruti and bhanitā.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyapancaratnam.title: Subrahmaṇyapañcaratna
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyapancaratnam.summary: A short five-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (pañcaratna) with an appended phalaśruti verse praising Subrahmaṇya (Kārttikeya/Murugan). The stotra specifically honors the deity enshrined along the banks of the Kumāradhārā river, describing him as a six-faced, twelve-eyed form of Śeṣa bearing the śakti spear, concluding each stanza with the refrain 'brahmaṇyadevaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyapancaratnam.attribution: Traditional anonymous stotra popular in South Indian devotional practice, explicitly celebrating the deity at Kukke Subrahmaṇya on the banks of the Kumāradhārā river ('kumāra dhārātaṭa mandirastham').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyapancaratnam.coverage: complete — Complete text containing 5 stanzas, 1 phalaśruti verse, and the final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyasahasranama.title: Subrahmaṇyabhujaṅgastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyasahasranama.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyasahasranama.summary: The Subrahmaṇyabhujaṅgastotra is a 33-stanza devotional hymn in the bhujaṅgaprayāta metre addressed to the deity Subrahmaṇya (Kārttikeya/Murugan). The stotra describes the divine form of the six-faced god seated on his peacock mount, praises his victory over demon forces, and supplicates him for relief from physical and mental afflictions, spiritual surrender, and ultimate liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyasahasranama.attribution: Attributed to Śaṅkara Bhagavān in the colophon (iti śrīmacchkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau śrīsubrahmaṇyabhujaṅgaṃ saṃpūrṇam).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisubrahmanyasahasranama.coverage: complete — Complete in 33 verses in the bhujaṅgaprayāta metre with introductory invocation to Gaṇeśa and final phalaśruti.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisvamisamarthastottaras.title: Śrīsvāmīsamarthāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisvamisamarthastottaras.summary: The Śrīsvāmīsamarthāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvalī is a devotional litany of 108 names (nāmāvalī) dedicated to Svāmī Samartha of Akkalkot. The names invoke his identity as an incarnation of Dattātreya and Śrīpāda Śrīvallabha, praising his divine qualities and protective grace, and concluding with reverence to Akkalkot Svāmī Samartha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisvamisamarthastottaras.attribution: A devotional nāmāvalī dedicated to Svāmī Samartha of Akkalkot. Names 106–107 pay homage to 'matpriyapitāmahasadgurubhyāṃ namaḥ' and 'pavitratamatātyāsāhebacaraṇāraviṃdābhyāṃ namaḥ'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisvamisamarthastottaras.coverage: complete — Complete litany of 108 devotional names in standard dative formula ('oṃ ... namaḥ') numbered 1–108, preceded by an incipit line.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitakavacam.title: Sītākavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitakavacam.summary: The Sītākavaca is a protective devotional hymn (kavaca) addressed to Sītā, extracted from the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa. Framed as a dialogue in which the sage Agastya instructs his disciple, it features nyāsa, dhyāna, directional and anatomical protective verses invoking diverse aspects of Sītā, and closes with a phalaśruti recommending the recitation of the four kavacas of Hanumān, Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā, and Rāma.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitakavacam.attribution: The kavaca forms part of the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa, traditionally attributed to Vālmīki. The hymn is framed as a teaching given by the sage Agastya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the stotra/kavaca including nyāsa, dhyāna, protective verses, and phalaśruti (20 verses in the main metre/phalaśruti section), closing with the colophon from the Ānandarāmāyaṇa Manoharakāṇḍa.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitaramagitam.title: Sītārāmagīta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitaramagitam.summary: A short Vaiṣṇava devotional song (gīta/stotra) consisting of 18 verses in praise of Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa. The first 16 verses comprise rhyming stanzas celebrating their virtues, deeds, and divine attributes, each concluding with the refrain 'rahasi naumi tau sītārāmalakṣmaṇau'. The final two verses consist of rhythmic nāmasaṅkīrtana repetitions of the divine names of Rāma, Sītā, Kṛṣṇa, and Rādhā.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitaramagitam.coverage: complete — Complete in 18 verses as presented on Sanskrit Wikisource (16 rhyming stanzas with the refrain 'rahasi naumi tau sītārāmalakṣmaṇau' followed by 2 kīrtana/nāmajapa verses).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitastottarasatanamast.title: Sītāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitastottarasatanamast.summary: The Sītāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra is a 108-name devotional hymn dedicated to Sītā, embedded in the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa. Framed as a dialogue between Sage Agastya and Sutīkṣṇa, the hymn extols Sītā through epithets celebrating her divine identity with Lakṣmī, her virtues, and her role in the subdual of Mūlakāsura. It includes full ritual prescriptions (nyāsa, dhyāna) and a concluding phalaśruti.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitastottarasatanamast.attribution: The stotra forms an excerpt from the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa, framed as an instruction delivered by Agastya to Sutīkṣṇa. The Ānandarāmāyaṇa as a whole is traditionally ascribed to Vālmīki.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisitastottarasatanamast.coverage: complete — Complete stotra as extracted from the Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Manoharakāṇḍa), including preliminary verses, nyāsa, dhyāna, the 17 verses containing the 108 names, and the concluding phalaśruti (vv. 18–22) with final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivaisnavavandana.title: Śrīvaiṣṇavavandanā
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivaisnavavandana.author: Jīva Gosvāmin
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivaisnavavandana.summary: The Śrīvaiṣṇavavandanā is a Sanskrit hymn of praise attributed to Jīva Gosvāmin. It systematically enumerates and reveres Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Nityānanda, Advaita Ācārya, and their circle of followers, framing the Gauḍīya lineage within the broader Mādhva sampradāya.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivaisnavavandana.attribution: Ascribed in the colophon and closing verses to Jīva Gosvāmin, referencing his elder kin Sanātana Gosvāmin and Rūpa Gosvāmin.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivaisnavavandana.coverage: complete — Complete text of verses from the maṅgalācaraṇa to the concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesakaravalambast.title: Śrīveṅkaṭeśakarāvalambastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesakaravalambast.author: Nṛsiṃhabhāratī
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesakaravalambast.summary: A 14-verse devotional hymn (stotra) addressed to Lord Veṅkaṭeśa (Viṣṇu) of Śeṣaśaila (Tirupati), beseeching his protective hand (karāvalamba) to rescue the devotee from worldly suffering. Composed by Śrī Nṛsiṃhabhāratī of the Śṛṅgeri tradition, each stanza concludes with the recurring refrain 'śrī veṅkaṭeśa mama dehi karāvalambam'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesakaravalambast.attribution: Attributed in verse 14 to Nṛsiṃhayatin and in the final colophon specifically to the Śṛṅgeri Jagadguru Nṛsiṃhabhāratī Svāmin.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesakaravalambast.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 14 verses with concluding phalaśruti and closing colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesasuprabhatam.title: Śrīveṅkaṭeśasuprabhāta
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesasuprabhatam.author: Prativādibhayaṅkara Aṇṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesasuprabhatam.summary: A 29-verse dawn hymn (suprabhāta) addressed to Lord Veṅkaṭeśvara (Vṛṣācalapati), opening with 'kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā sandhyā pravartate' and concluding with a phalaśruti verse in praise of those who recite the morning prayer daily.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivemkatesasuprabhatam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Suprabhāta hymn proper (verses 1–29 ending with '|| iti veṅkaṭeśa suprabhātam ||').

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesamangalasasana.title: Śrīveṅkaṭeśamaṅgalaśāsana
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesamangalasasana.author: Prativādibhayaṅkara Aṇṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesamangalasasana.summary: A 14-verse Sanskrit devotional hymn (maṅgalaśāsana) invoking eternal auspiciousness upon Lord Veṅkaṭeśvara (Śrīnivāsa) of Tirumala.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesamangalasasana.coverage: complete — Complete text containing 14 verses of the devotional hymn.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesaprapatti.title: Śrīveṅkaṭeśaprapatti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesaprapatti.author: Prativādibhayaṅkaram Aṇṇa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesaprapatti.summary: The Śrīveṅkaṭeśaprapatti is a 16-verse hymn of ritual self-surrender (śaraṇāgati/prapatti) addressed to Lord Veṅkaṭeśvara. The opening verse invokes Śrī (Lakṣmī), followed by verses praising the Lord's lotus feet, and concluding with a declaration of service.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivenkatesaprapatti.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 16 stanzas (verses 1–16 and concluding colophon).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivighnesvarastottarasat.title: Vighneśvarāṣṭottaraśatanāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivighnesvarastottarasat.summary: A 17-verse devotional hymn enumerating 108 epithets of Gaṇeśa / Vighneśvara in verse form. Verses 15–17 provide the mythological narrative frame and phalaśruti, recounting that Śaṅkara praised Gaṇeśa before setting out to destroy Tripura, and promising freedom from obstacles and fulfillment of desires to devotees who recite the hymn with offerings of dūrvā grass and bilva leaves.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivighnesvarastottarasat.attribution: Within the framing verses (vv. 15–16), the hymn is traditionally attributed as a praise spoken by Śiva (Śaṅkara) prior to attacking Tripura.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivighnesvarastottarasat.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 17 verses (14.5 verses of 108 names followed by 2.5 verses of phalaśruti).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivindhyavasinistotram.title: Vindhyavāsinīstotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivindhyavasinistotram.summary: A short devotional hymn consisting of an introductory dhyāna verse and eight rhyming stanzas praising the goddess Vindhyavāsinī (a form of Durgā enshrined in the Vindhya hills). Each stanza celebrates her mythic exploits, such as slaying Śumbha and Niśumbha, and closes with the refrain 'bhajāmi vindhyavāsinīm'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srivindhyavasinistotram.coverage: complete — Complete eight-verse hymn (aṣṭaka) preceded by an introductory dhyāna verse citing the Devīmāhātmya / Bhāgavata tradition (Nandagopa-gṛhe jātā...).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisatrughnakavacam.title: Śatrughnakavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisatrughnakavacam.summary: A protective hymn (kavaca) dedicated to Śatrughna, the youngest brother of Rāma, embedded in the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa. Framed as an exposition delivered by sage Agastya to Sutīkṣṇa, it contains ritual nyāsa procedures, a dhyāna verse visualizing Śatrughna reverently fanning Rāma and Sītā, anatomical protective stanzas invoking Śatrughna under various epithets for bodily protection, and closing phalaśruti verses promising progeny and worldly fulfillment.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisatrughnakavacam.attribution: A devotional kavaca occurring within the Manoharakāṇḍa of the Ānandarāmāyaṇa, structured as a dialogue where sage Agastya instructs Sutīkṣṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisatrughnakavacam.coverage: complete — Complete kavaca text as embedded in the Ānandarāmāyaṇa (Manoharakāṇḍa), comprising viniyoga, nyāsa, dhyāna, kavaca proper, and phalaśruti (ending colophon: iti śrī śatakoṭirāmacaritāṃtargata śrīmadānandarāmāyaṇe vālmikīye manoharakāṇḍe śrī śatrughnakavacaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivapancaksarastotram.title: Śivapañcākṣarastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivapancaksarastotram.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivapancaksarastotram.summary: The Śivapañcākṣarastotra is a six-verse hymn praising Śiva, traditionally attributed to Śaṅkara. The first five verses sequentially honor Śiva while acrostically dedicating each stanza to one syllable of the five-syllable mantra namaḥ śivāya (na, ma, śi, vā, ya). A sixth verse (phalaśruti) promises attainment of Śiva's realm (Śivaloka) to those who recite the hymn.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivapancaksarastotram.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkarācārya ('iti śrīmad śankarācāryaviracitaṃ śivapañcākṣarastotraṃ sampurṇam').
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivapancaksarastotram.coverage: complete — Complete text of 6 verses (5 stanzas for each syllable of na-maḥ-śi-vā-ya plus 1 phalaśruti verse) and concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivasatakam.title: Śivāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivasatakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivasatakam.summary: Devotional hymn in praise of Śiva consisting of eight stanzas concluding with the refrain 'śivaṃ śaṅkaraṃ śambhumīśānamīḍe', followed by a concluding phalaśruti stanza.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivasatakam.coverage: complete — Complete 8 verses of the hymn followed by verse 9 as phalaśruti.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivastakam.title: Śivāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivastakam.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivastakam.summary: An eight-verse hymn of praise (aṣṭaka) to Lord Śiva, characterized by the refrain 'śivaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaṃbhumīśānamīḍe' terminating each stanza, followed by a concluding phalaśruti. The stotra extols Śiva's cosmic supremacy alongside his ascetic and fierce attributes, celebrating him as the destroyer of ignorance and lord of liberation.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srisivastakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 8 stanzas plus 1 closing phalaśruti verse.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sabarikavacam.title: Śābarīkavaca
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sabarikavacam.summary: A protective incantation (kavaca) stemming from the folk-tantric and Nātha-oriented Śābara tradition, addressed to Śābarī devī alongside Vīrabhadra, Baṭukabhairava, and Kṣetrapāla. It incorporates dhyāna verses to the Nātha guru-maṇḍala, purāṇic and tantric bījamantras, apotropaic formulas for warding off grahas and piśācas, and a standard phalaśruti promising health, protection, and success.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sabarikavacam.attribution: Anonymous ritual text of the Śābara / Nātha tantric sphere. The attribution to Vedavyāsa in Sanskrit Wikisource is unverified.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_sabarikavacam.coverage: complete — Complete ritual text containing dhyāna, prārthanā, viniyoga, prose and verse protective formulas, and phalaśruti.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saligramastotra.title: Śāligrāmastotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saligramastotra.summary: A Vaiṣṇava devotional hymn of 32 verses praising the worship of the sacred Śāligrāma stone, framed as a dialogue between Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira in the Bhaviṣyottarapurāṇa. It describes the sacred origin of Śāligrāma stones near the Gaṇḍakī river, the spiritual efficacy of drinking the bath-water (pādodaka) poured over the stone, and the various auspicious and inauspicious physical markings (cakra, colors, shapes) identifying manifestations of Viṣṇu such as Nṛsiṃha, Varāha, and Vāsudeva.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saligramastotra.attribution: Colophon attributes the text to the Bhaviṣyottarapurāṇa as a dialogue between Śrīkṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saligramastotra.coverage: complete — Complete stotra of 32 verses with introductory viniyoga and concluding colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santavilasah.title: Śāntavilāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santavilasah.author: Jagannātha
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santavilasah.summary: The Śāntavilāsa is a devotional and reflective lyric collection of 44 verses praising Mukunda/Kṛṣṇa, renunciation of worldly pursuits, and detachment.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_santavilasah.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Jagannātha Paṇḍita (iti śrīmajjagannāthapaṇḍitaviracito śāntavilāsaḥ).

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradabhujangaprayatastak.title: Śāradābhujaṅgaprayātāṣṭaka
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradabhujangaprayatastak.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradabhujangaprayatastak.summary: An eight-verse hymn (aṣṭaka) composed in the bhujaṅgaprayāta meter praising Goddess Śāradā (traditionally Śāradāmbā of Śṛṅgeri). Each stanza extols her physical beauty, maternal compassion, and role as the source of wisdom and learning, concluding with the refrain 'bhaje śāradāmbām ajasraṃ madambām'.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradabhujangaprayatastak.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Śaṅkarācārya (śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradabhujangaprayatastak.coverage: complete — Complete 8 verses (aṣṭaka) with the colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradapancaratnastutih.title: Śāradāpañcaratnastuti
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradapancaratnastutih.summary: The Śāradāpañcaratnastuti is a short Sanskrit devotional hymn comprising one dhyāna-śloka and five verses praising Goddess Śāradāmbā at Sringeri on the banks of the Tuṅgā river. The verses extol her as the grantor of wisdom and spiritual liberation, venerated by Ādi Śaṅkara and the pontiffs of the Sringeri pīṭha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradapancaratnastutih.attribution: The hymn addresses Goddess Śāradā of Sringeri (installed on the Tuṅgā river) and references Vidyātīrtha.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_saradapancaratnastutih.coverage: complete — Complete text consisting of one introductory dhyāna verse and five stotra verses.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srngaraprakasah.title: Śṛṅgāraprakāśa (chapters 1–12)
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srngaraprakasah.author: Bhoja
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srngaraprakasah.summary: The Śṛṅgāraprakāśa is an encyclopedic masterwork of Sanskrit poetics (alaṅkāraśāstra) and dramaturgy (nāṭyaśāstra) in 36 chapters (prakāśas) composed by King Bhoja of Dhārā (11th century). Chapters 1 to 12 form the foundational half of the work, treating grammatical and semantic theory (śabdārtha, padārtha, vākyārtha, vṛtti), literary flaws (doṣa), excellences (guṇa), ornamentation (alaṅkāra), and dramatic and poetic genres (prabandha). The remainder of the work (chapters 13–36, omitted here) develops Bhoja's famous aesthetic theory that śṛṅgāra (identified with ego/self-awareness, ahaṃkāra/abhimāna) is the single supreme and all-encompassing rasa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srngaraprakasah.attribution: Ascribed to Bhojadeva (composed in the 11th century).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_srngaraprakasah.coverage: partial — Contains only Prakāśas 1–12 out of 36. The text breaks off with the colophon: 'iti śrī mahārājānadhirāja śrī bhojadevavicite śṛṅgāraprakāśe prabandhāṅgacatuṣṣaṣṭicatuṣṭayaprakāśo nāma dvādaśaḥ prakāśaḥ'.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_urubhangah.title: Ūrubhaṅga
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_urubhangah.author: Bhāsa
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_urubhangah.summary: The Ūrubhaṅga ('The Shattering of the Thighs') is a one-act Sanskrit drama (often classified as an utsṛṣṭikāṅka) attributed to Bhāsa, based on the final mace duel between Duryodhana and Bhīma in the Mahābhārata. Uniquely in classical Sanskrit drama, which traditionally avoids tragic conclusions, the play focuses on the dying Duryodhana, portraying him as a heroic, remorseful, and dignified figure who accepts his fate and counsels peace. It culminates in his vision of heaven and death on stage, followed by Aśvatthāman's vow of nocturnal vengeance.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_urubhangah.coverage: complete — Complete one-act drama consisting of introductory dramatis personae list, prologue (sthāpanā), and all 66 verses concluding with the bharatavākya and final colophon.

SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rnamocanamahaganapatistot.title: Ṛṇamocanamahāgaṇapatistotra
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rnamocanamahaganapatistot.summary: The Ṛṇamocanamahāgaṇapatistotra is a devotional hymn of ten verses addressed to Gaṇapati, traditionally attributed to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa. The stotra petitions Gaṇeśa through various iconographical and color forms (red, black, yellow, smoky, and all-colored vestments) to release the worshipper from worldly and karmic debts (ṛṇa).
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rnamocanamahaganapatistot.attribution: The viniyoga names Śukrācārya as the traditional seer (ṛṣi), and the colophon attributes the hymn to the Brahmāṇḍapurāṇa.
SA_GK19_ilx_ws_rnamocanamahaganapatistot.coverage: complete — Complete text of 10 verses preceded by a viniyoga formula and followed by a phalaśruti (v. 10) and colophon.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_aksamalikopanisat.title: Akṣamālikopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_aksamalikopanisat.summary: The Akṣamālikopaniṣad is a Śaiva Upaniṣad formatted as an instructional dialogue between Prajāpati and Guha on the rosary (akṣamālā), describing its materials, construction, stringing, and the consecration of the beads with letters from 'a' to 'kṣa', concluding with the fruits of practice.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_aksamalikopanisat.attribution: Traditionally classified as a Śaiva Upaniṣad.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_aksamalikopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad, beginning with the opening verse ('akārādikṣakārānta...'), the śāntipāṭha ('vāṅ me manasi pratiṣṭhitā...'), the dialogue between Prajāpati and Guha on the rosary, and concluding with the phala and final śāntipāṭha.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atharvasikhaupanisad.title: Atharvaśikhopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atharvasikhaupanisad.summary: The Atharvaśikhopaniṣad is a minor Śaiva text associated with the Atharvaveda, listed among the fourteen Śaiva Upaniṣads in the Muktikā canon. Framed as a discourse delivered by the sage Atharvan to Pippalāda, Aṅgiras, and Sanatkumāra, it expounds meditation upon the sacred syllable Om (Praṇava). The text identifies the constituent mātrās of Om with Vedic fires, deities, worlds, and states of consciousness, establishing the fourth transcendental quarter (turīya) as Śiva (Īśāna, Śaṃbhu), who is the ultimate reality and sole cause to be meditated upon.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atharvasikhaupanisad.attribution: A text traditionally attached to the Atharvaveda.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atharvasikhaupanisad.coverage: complete — Complete in 3 sections, preceded by the opening maṅgala verse and the Atharvavedic śāntipāṭha ('bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...'), and concluding with the final śānti and colophon.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_avyaktopanisat.title: Avyaktopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_avyaktopanisat.summary: The Avyaktopaniṣad is a minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad traditionally affiliated with the Sāmaveda. It presents a cosmogonic narrative in which Prajāpati (Brahmā) emerges from the primordial golden egg and seeks the unmanifest source of creation (Avyakta), revealed to him as Nṛsiṃha (Narasimha). Through the contemplation and ritual-philosophical repetition of the Nṛsiṃhānuṣṭubha-mantra ('ugraṃ vīraṃ mahāviṣṇum...'), Prajāpati gains the knowledge and capacity required to create the world.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_avyaktopanisat.attribution: A minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad traditionally attached to the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_avyaktopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in prose and verse across its traditional sections, preceded by an invocatory verse ('svājñānāsurarāḍgrāsasvajñānanarakesarī...') and the śāntipāṭha ('āpyāyantu mamāṅgāni...'), ending with 'ityavyaktopaniṣatsamāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_bhasmajabalopanisat.title: Bhasmajābālopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_bhasmajabalopanisat.summary: The Bhasmajābālopaniṣad is a sectarian Śaiva Upaniṣad affiliated with the Atharvaveda. Cast as an exposition imparted on Mount Kailāsa by Mahādeva (Śiva) to Bhusuṇḍa Jābāla, it establishes the ritual gathering, purification, and preparation of cow-dung sacred ash (bhasma) and prescribes the precise Vedic mantras for marking the body with the tripuṇḍra. The second chapter focuses on the sacred geography and liberative power of Kāśī (Varanasi) as an embodiment of the liṅga, detailing the strict behavioral observances demanded of residents therein.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_bhasmajabalopanisat.attribution: A sectarian Śaiva Upaniṣad affiliated with the Atharvaveda. Commented on by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_bhasmajabalopanisat.coverage: complete — Text framed by the Atharvaveda śāntipāṭha ('bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...').

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyupanisat.title: Dakṣiṇāmūrtyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyupanisat.summary: The Dakṣiṇāmūrtyupaniṣad is a minor Śaiva Upaniṣad framed as an inquiry by Śaunaka and other ṛṣis to the sage Mārkaṇḍeya at the Mahābhāṇḍīra fig tree in Brahmāvarta regarding the secret of immortality. Mārkaṇḍeya reveals the knowledge of Śiva in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti, providing multiple mantra formulas (including 24-, 9-, 18-, and 12-syllable mantras and the anuṣṭubh mantrarāja) along with their corresponding dhyāna verses, mudrās, and nyāsa rituals. The work synthesizes ritual tantric upāsanā with Advaita Vedānta by identifying Dakṣiṇāmūrti with ultimate non-dual consciousness (śemuṣī).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_daksinamurtyupanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 33 numbered prose sections and verses, enclosed by the opening and closing śāntipāṭha (saha nāvavatu).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_dattatreyopanisad.title: Dattātreyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_dattatreyopanisad.summary: The Dattātreyopaniṣad is a sectarian Upaniṣad belonging to the Vaiṣṇava group and traditionally affiliated with the Atharvaveda. Structured as an instruction given by Nārāyaṇa to Brahmā on the supreme liberating principle (tāraka), the text details the meditation and sacred mantras of Dattātreya. It teaches the one-syllable (dāṃ), six-syllable, eight-syllable, twelve-syllable, sixteen-syllable, and anuṣṭubh mantras, providing their corresponding ṛṣi, meter, devatā, bīja, śakti, kīlaka, nyāsa applications, and the spiritual fruits of recitation.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_dattatreyopanisad.attribution: Upaniṣad text with an opening verse associated with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_dattatreyopanisad.coverage: complete — Complete: maṅgala verse, śāntipāṭha, text down to the final śāntipāṭha and colophon 'iti dattātreyopaniṣatsamāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ekaksaropanisat.title: Ekākṣaropaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ekaksaropanisat.summary: The Ekākṣaropaniṣad is a minor Upaniṣad consisting of thirteen verses and a concluding prose formula. It praises the supreme non-dual principle (identified with the single syllable / Brahman) as both the transcendent origin and cosmic creator manifesting as Rudra, Viṣṇu, Hiraṇyagarbha, and all beings. The text asserts that meditative realization of this ancient lord within the heart cave leads beyond ordinary intellect to the supreme state.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ekaksaropanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text containing 13 verses followed by a concluding prose formula, opening and closing śāntipāṭhas, and an opening invocatory maṅgala verse.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_garudopanisat.title: Garuḍopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_garudopanisat.summary: The Garuḍopaniṣad (or Gāruḍopaniṣad) is a minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad affiliated with the Atharvaveda. Set as an esoteric transmission from Brahmā to Nārada and subsequently to Indra and Bharadvāja, the work expounds the Gāruḍī Brahmavidyā. It consists of nyāsas, dhyāna verses describing the multi-serpent-adorned cosmic form of Garuḍa, and incantations intended to neutralize snakebites and all forms of poison.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_garudopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad with opening and closing Atharvaveda śāntipāṭha ('bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...'), as well as the introductory maṅgala verse by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_gopalatapinyupanisat.title: Gopālatāpinyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_gopalatapinyupanisat.summary: The Gopālatāpinyupaniṣad is a sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad affiliated with the Atharvaveda (no. 95 in the Muktikā canon) and a foundational canonical text for Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava theology. The work is split into two halves: the Gopālapūrvatāpinī expounds the eighteen-syllable Gopāla mantra, the yantra, and the meditational identification of Gopāla Kṛṣṇa with the supreme non-dual Brahman; the Gopālottaratāpinī presents a dialogue between the gopīs led by Gāndharvī (Rādhā) and the sage Durvāsas, resolving the paradox of Kṛṣṇa as an eternal, non-attached ascetic despite his romantic sports in Vṛndāvana.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_gopalatapinyupanisat.attribution: Traditionally classified as one of the minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣads belonging to the Atharvaveda (Muktikā no. 95).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_gopalatapinyupanisat.coverage: complete — Includes Gopālapūrvatāpinī and Gopālottaratāpinī, ending with 'iti gopālottaratāpinyupaniṣatsamāptā', preceded by an opening maṅgala verse, the Atharvavedic śāntipāṭha, and a Muktikā-list verse.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_hayagrivopanisat.title: Hayagrīvopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_hayagrivopanisat.summary: The Hayagrīvopaniṣad is a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad. Structured as a teaching given by Brahmā to Nārada, it expounds the worship, dhyāna, and esoteric mantras of Hayagrīva, the horse-necked form of Viṣṇu. It focuses on the attainment of sacred wisdom, eloquence (vāksiddhi), destruction of sins, and spiritual liberation.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_hayagrivopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text including opening śāntipāṭha (bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...), dialogue between Brahmā and Nārada, Hayagrīva mantras and vidyā, and closing benedictions.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_itihasopanisat.title: Itihāsopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_itihasopanisat.summary: The Itihāsopaniṣad is an un-canonical minor Upaniṣad associated with the Kāṇva recension. It begins with the narrative of King Vṛṣādarvi of the Śibi dynasty receiving this lore from a sun deity, prescribing its study and recitation for Vedic proficiency and ancestor propitiation during śrāddha rituals. The remainder of the text contains diverse gnomic, moral, and Vedāntic verses treating truth, self-restraint, tapo-vidyā, and the mystery of Brahman.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_itihasopanisat.attribution: A rare minor Upaniṣad outside the standard Muktikā canon of 108 Upaniṣads, explicitly affiliating itself at segment 203 with the Kāṇva recension of the Śukla Yajurveda ('kāṇvaśākhe pārayeti').
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_itihasopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad, concluding with the explicit colophon 'iti itihāsopaniṣat saṃpūrṇā' at segment 204, followed by closing śrāddha and suparṇa verses (segments 205–209).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_kalisantaranopanisat.title: Kalisantaraṇopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_kalisantaranopanisat.summary: The Kalisantaraṇopaniṣad is structured as a dialogue between the sage Nārada and Brahmā at the end of the Dvāparayuga, addressing how beings can cross the ocean of cyclic existence during the Kaliyuga. Brahmā prescribes the repetition of the sixteen divine names of Nārāyaṇa (starting with 'hare rāma...'), declaring that this requires no restrictive injunctions and purifies the chanter of sins.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_kalisantaranopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all three short sections (khaṇḍas), including the introductory śāntipāṭha (saha nāvavatu), the maṅgala verse, and the concluding formula.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_krsnopanisat.title: Kṛṣṇopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_krsnopanisat.summary: The Kṛṣṇopaniṣad is a minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad in two sections (khaṇḍas) that presents an allegorical and metaphysical interpretation of the Kṛṣṇa avatāra. It begins with the forest ascetics encountering Rāma and wishing to embrace him; Rāma instructs them to become gopīs in his future incarnation as Kṛṣṇa. The subsequent text allegorizes the actors, weapons, and adversaries of the Kṛṣṇa mythos, equating Kṛṣṇa with the supreme non-dual Brahman, his associates with divine and scriptural principles, and his foes with negative mental states.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_krsnopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in two khaṇḍas with opening and closing Atharvaveda śāntipāṭha ('bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...').

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mahavakyopanisat.title: Mahāvākyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mahavakyopanisat.summary: The Mahāvākyopaniṣad is a short Vedāntic text expounding direct realization (aparokṣānubhava) of Brahman, distinguishing the light of spiritual knowledge from the darkness of ignorance and bodily identification. Contemplating the inner identity between the solar deity (Āditya) and the self through the mantra 'so'ham' and the haṃsa, it incorporates Puruṣasūkta verses and concludes with a phalaśruti promising absolution from sins and absorption into Mahāviṣṇu (viṣṇusāyujya).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mahavakyopanisat.attribution: Upaniṣad featuring a commentary by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mahavakyopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short Upaniṣad, preceded by an invocatory maṅgala verse and the śāntipāṭha ('bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...').

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maithilimahopasat.title: Maithilīmahopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maithilimahopasat.summary: The Maithilīmahopaniṣad is a short Rāmaite Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣadic text framed in its colophon as part of the fifth adhyāya of the Vālmīkisaṃhitā. In the dialogue, seven sage-inquirers (Lāṭyāyana, Kauñjāyana, Khāḍāyana, Bhalandana, Vilva, Ailākya, and Tālukṣya) approach the enthroned goddess Maithilī (Sītā) seeking instruction on what ought to be recited, attained, meditated upon, and known for liberation. Sītā teaches the supreme efficacy of Rāma's name and the six-syllable mantra, concluding with a lineage of transmission passing from Rāma to herself, Hanumān, Brahmā, Vasiṣṭha, Parāśara, Vyāsa, and Śuka.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maithilimahopasat.attribution: A sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad centered on Sītā (Maithilī) and Rāma; according to its concluding colophon, it forms the fifth chapter of the Vālmīkisaṃhitā.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maithilimahopasat.coverage: complete — Complete text in five sections (prathamopaniṣad through pañcamyupaniṣad), ending with the concluding colophon: 'iti vālmīki saṃhitā pañcama adhyāya antargata maithilīmahopaniṣad samāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maitrayanyupanisat.title: Maitrāyaṇyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maitrayanyupanisat.summary: The Maitrāyaṇyupaniṣad (or Maitrī Upaniṣad) is a late classical Vedic Upaniṣad traditionally attached to the Maitrāyaṇīya śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Framed as an exposition by the ascetic sage Śākāyanya to King Bṛhadratha, it integrates early Vedānta with concepts from early Sāṃkhya and Yoga, notably presenting one of the earliest systematic descriptions of a sixfold yoga (ṣaḍaṅgayoga). The text addresses existential suffering, the distinction between the elemental self (bhūtātman) and the transcendent immortal self, and meditation on Om, the sun, and prāṇa.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maitrayanyupanisat.attribution: A classical Upaniṣad traditionally associated with the Maitrāyaṇīya śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, framed as teachings given by the sage Śākāyanya to King Bṛhadratha, citing Maitreya and the Vālakhilyas.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_maitrayanyupanisat.coverage: complete — Complete in 7 prapāṭhakas. Note that the etext repeats the full text three times consecutively due to an ingestion/concatenation error on Sanskrit Wikisource.
translations: Olivelle, Patrick. Upaniṣads. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1996. (English)
Hume, Robert Ernest. The Thirteen Principal Upanishads. Oxford, 1921. (English)
Deussen, Paul. Sixty Upaniṣads of the Veda. German edition 1897. (German)

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mudgalopanisat.title: Mudgalopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mudgalopanisat.summary: The Mudgalopaniṣad is a minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad affiliated with the Ṛgveda. Composed in four sections (khaṇḍas), it gives a theological and allegorical reinterpretation of the Puruṣasūkta (Ṛgveda 10.90) in light of Pañcarātra theology (identifying Puruṣa with Nārāyaṇa/Vāsudeva and teaching the Caturvyūha doctrine) and Vedāntic cosmology, including the doctrine of the five sheaths (pañcakośa).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mudgalopanisat.attribution: A minor Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad traditionally affiliated with the Ṛgveda.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mudgalopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising four khaṇḍas, opening with the Ṛgvedic śāntimantra (vāṅ me manasi pratiṣṭhitā...) and ending with the final śāntipāṭha and colophon (iti mudgalopaniṣatsamāptā).
translations: Jan Gonda, 'The Mudgalopaniṣad', Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Südasiens 12–13 (1968–69), pp. 101–113 [Festschrift Erich Frauwallner]. (English)

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_muktikopanisat.title: Muktikopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_muktikopanisat.summary: The Muktikopaniṣad is a late Vedāntic text framed as a dialogue between Śrī Rāma and Hanūmān in Ayodhyā. It is famous for formulating the canonical catalog of 108 Upaniṣads mapped to the four Vedic Saṃhitās and describing four graduated forms of liberation (sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sāyujya) leading to kaivalya. The second adhyāya draws heavily on philosophical formulations related to the Mokṣopāya/Yogavāsiṣṭha tradition, focusing on the destruction of latent impressions (vāsanākṣaya), the dissolution of the mind (manonāśa), and the attainment of jīvanmukti and videhamukti.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_muktikopanisat.attribution: Traditional scriptural text classified as the 108th Upaniṣad and attributed to the Śukla Yajurveda. It takes the form of a dialogue between Śrī Rāma and Hanūmān in Ayodhyā.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_muktikopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete in two adhyāyas (adhyāya 1 ending at line 154, and adhyāya 2 ending at line 337 with 'iti muktikopaniṣatsamāptā').

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mantrikopanisat.title: Mantrikopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mantrikopanisat.summary: The Mantrikopaniṣad harmonizes Sāṅkhya categories—including the eightfold unmanifest Prakṛti and principles—into a Vedāntic framework, discussing the twenty-sixth principle (ṣaḍviṃśaka puruṣa) transcending cosmic modifications.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_mantrikopanisat.coverage: complete — Text of 19 numbered verses plus unnumbered closing verse/prose, framed by the śāntipāṭha ('oṃ pūrṇamadaḥ...') and an opening invocatory maṅgalaśloka.
translations: Paul Deussen, Sechzig Upanishad's des Veda, Leipzig 1897 (Engl. transl. V. M. Bedekar and G. B. Palsule, Sixty Upaniṣads of the Veda, Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1980). (German/English)

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_niruktopanisat.title: Niruktopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_niruktopanisat.summary: The Niruktopaniṣad is a minor Upaniṣadic text dealing with human embryology, physical anatomy, and transmigration, closely related in contents and style to the Garbhopaniṣad. It outlines conception, the sequential formation of the embryo and fetus month by month, constitutional bodily components (such as bones, joints, and vital points / marmans), the fetus's prenatal reflections on past rebirths, and the loss of prenatal memory upon birth.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_niruktopanisat.attribution: A minor anatomical and embryological Upaniṣad of traditional Vedic affiliation, structured in two chapters numbered adhyāyas 20 and 21 in the colophons.
translations: K. Kaladhar and. V. Prasad, 'Niruktopaniṣad and Garbhopaniṣad: The Vedic Sources of Studies on Human Embryology', Bulletin of the Indian Institute of History of Medicine: Hyderabad 24. (English)

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_niralambopanisat.title: Nirālambopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_niralambopanisat.summary: The Nirālambopaniṣad ('Upaniṣad of the Supportless') is a minor Upaniṣad arranged as an Advaita catechism, posing and systematically defining over thirty core ontological, cosmological, and soteriological terms—including Brahman, Īśvara, Jīva, Prakṛti, Karma, Jñāna, Ajñāna, Bandha, Mokṣa, and Saṃnyāsa. It concludes that ultimate reality is non-dual consciousness devoid of worldly support (nirālamba), accessible through experiential realization of the mahāvākyas.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_niralambopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 40 prose/verse sections with opening and closing śāntipāṭha (pūrṇamadaḥ) and concluding colophon.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanapurvatapiniyopani.title: Nārāyaṇapūrvatāpinīyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanapurvatapiniyopani.summary: The Nārāyaṇapūrvatāpinīyopaniṣad is a late Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad framed within the Ātharvaṇarahasya. Structured as a dialogue where Brahmā instructs Sanatkumāra across six khaṇḍas, it expounds the theological significance and ritual use of the Nārāyaṇa eight-syllable formula (oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya). Topics treated include the correlation of the mantra's syllables with cosmic elements (aṣṭamūrti), the veneration of Mahālakṣmī as supreme Prakṛti, and the design and deity layout (āvaraṇadevatā) of the Nārāyaṇa-yantra.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanapurvatapiniyopani.attribution: Scriptural text traditionally affiliated with the Atharvaveda (specifically designated in the colophons as belonging to the Ātharvaṇarahasya); author treated as anonymous.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanapurvatapiniyopani.coverage: complete — Complete text in 6 khaṇḍas, concluding with the final colophon 'iti nārāyaṇapūrvatāpinīyopaniṣat samāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanottaratapiniyopani.title: Nārāyaṇottaratāpinīyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanottaratapiniyopani.summary: The Nārāyaṇottaratāpinīyopaniṣad is a sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad presented as an instruction by Brahmā proclaiming Nārāyaṇa to be the supreme Brahman and ground of existence. Across three short khaṇḍas, it integrates classical Upaniṣadic citations (such as the two birds motif, the cosmogonic evolution from ākāśa to puruṣa, and the subtle flame within the heart) with Vaiṣṇava devotional formulae centered on Vāsudeva and Nārāyaṇa. It concludes with an extensive phalaśruti detailing the expiation of grave sins (mahāpātakas) and the attainment of liberation in Vaikuṇṭha.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanottaratapiniyopani.attribution: A sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad presenting itself as part of the Atharvaṇarahasya tradition.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_narayanottaratapiniyopani.coverage: complete — Complete in three khaṇḍas, concluding with 'iti nārāyaṇottaratāpinīyopaniṣat samāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhapurvatapaniyopanis.title: Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣad with Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣadbhāṣya
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhapurvatapaniyopanis.author: Śaṅkara
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhapurvatapaniyopanis.summary: The Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣad is an Atharvavedic Upaniṣad dedicated to Narasiṃha and centered on the meditation and esoteric power of the Nārasiṃha-mantrarāja in anuṣṭubh meter. The commentary attributed to Śaṅkara interprets the text from an Advaitic standpoint while integrating tantric, mantra-śāstric, and Pāñcarātra elements.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhapurvatapaniyopanis.attribution: Colophon attributes the work to Śaṅkarabhagavat, disciple of Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda (śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṃkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhapurvatapaniyopanis.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on the Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣad, ending with 'iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrīmacchaṃkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣadbhāṣyaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhatapanyupanisad_1.title: Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhatapanyupanisad_1.summary: The Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīyopaniṣad is a late Vedic Vaiṣṇava scripture associated with the Atharvaveda, forming the first part of the two-part Nṛsiṃhatāpanīya Upaniṣad. In five chapters, it describes Prajāpati's creation of the cosmos through ascetic heat (tapas) and the vision of the 32-syllabled Anuṣṭubh Mantrarāja dedicated to Nṛsiṃha (ugraṃ vīraṃ mahāviṣṇum...). The work elaborates the mystical syllables, liturgical application, diagrammatic meditation (yantra), and the ontological identification of Nṛsiṃha with all Vedic deities, cosmic states, and supreme non-dual Brahman.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhatapanyupanisad_1.attribution: Canonical Upaniṣad belonging to the Atharvaveda and classified among the Vaiṣṇava and Tāpanīya Upaniṣads.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhatapanyupanisad_1.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Pūrvatāpanīya section in five chapters (prathamopaniṣad through pañcamopaniṣad), concluding with 'iti nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpinyupaniṣatsamāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhottaratapaniyopanis.title: Nṛsiṃhottaratāpanīyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhottaratapaniyopanis.summary: The Nṛsiṃhottaratāpanīyopaniṣad is a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad belonging to the Atharvaveda tradition, forming the second part of the composite Nṛsiṃhatāpanīyopaniṣad. In nine khaṇḍas, it develops an Advaitic metaphysical synthesis of the Oṃkāra and the four quarters/states of the Ātman (jāgrat, svapna, suṣupta, turīya) closely adapted from the Māṇḍūkyopaniṣad, identifying the supreme non-dual Brahman with Lord Nṛsiṃha.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhottaratapaniyopanis.attribution: A traditional Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad associated with the Atharvaveda tradition; traditionally regarded as śruti (revelation).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_nrsimhottaratapaniyopanis.coverage: complete — Complete in 9 khaṇḍas, concluding at segment 66 ('iti navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ||9||') and followed by the Atharvavedic śāntipāṭha ('oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...').

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_paingalopanisat.title: Paiṅgalopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_paingalopanisat.summary: The Paiṅgalopaniṣad is a Sāmānya Vedānta Upaniṣad affiliated with the Śukla Yajurveda, framed as an esoteric dialogue between the sage Paiṅgala and his teacher Yājñavalkya. Across four adhyāyas, it expounds an Advaita Vedāntic synthesis covering cosmology and quintuplication (pañcīkaraṇa), the three bodies (śarīratraya) and states of consciousness, an exegesis of the Mahāvākyas (especially 'tat tvam asi'), and the path to jīvanmukti and final release.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_paingalopanisat.attribution: A dialogic Upaniṣad presented as instruction imparted by Yājñavalkya to his pupil Paiṅgala; classified as a Sāmānya Upaniṣad belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_paingalopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in four adhyāyas with introductory and concluding śāntipāṭhas.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pindopanisat.title: Piṇḍopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pindopanisat.summary: The Piṇḍopaniṣad is a short minor ritual Upaniṣad affiliated with the Atharvavedic tradition that treats the post-mortem mechanics of funerary rice-ball offerings (piṇḍadāna). In the form of a dialogue between deities/ṛṣis and Brahmā, it outlines how the departed spirit (haṃsa), disembodied immediately after cremation, progressively reconstructs an intermediate subtle body limb by limb across the ten daily piṇḍa offerings during the antyeṣṭi funerary rites.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pindopanisat.attribution: A late minor Upaniṣad traditionally affiliated with the Atharvaveda.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pindopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 18 verses/segments concluding with 'iti piṇḍopaniṣat samāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pranagnihotropanisat.title: Prāṇāgnihotropaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pranagnihotropanisat.summary: The Prāṇāgnihotropaniṣad internalizes the Vedic Agnihotra sacrifice as the bodily sacrifice (śārīrayajña), identifying food consumption and the vital breaths (prāṇas) with ritual offerings, and establishing parts of the body and mental faculties with ritual sacrificial elements to teach liberation (mokṣa).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_pranagnihotropanisat.coverage: complete — Text with khaṇḍas, preceded by an invocation and followed by closing śāntipāṭha.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_rudrahrdayopanisat.title: Rudrahṛdayopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_rudrahrdayopanisat.summary: The Rudrahṛdayopaniṣad is framed as an exchange between Śuka and Vyāsa on the ultimate identity of the gods, propounding non-difference between Rudra and Viṣṇu, asserting that worship or enmity toward one is directed at the other. It analyzes divine reality across male and female dualities and culminates in an Advaitic exposition of Brahman as transcendent consciousness (saccidānanda) accessible via higher knowledge (parā vidyā).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_rudrahrdayopanisat.attribution: Framed as a dialogue between Śuka and his father Vyāsa.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_rudrahrdayopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad in 52 metrical verses, flanked by opening and closing śāntipāṭhas ('oṃ saha nāvavatu...').

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramarahasyopanisat.title: Rāmarahasyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramarahasyopanisat.summary: The Rāmarahasyopaniṣad is an Upaniṣadic text of unknown date. Structured around a dialogue where Hanūmat instructs Sanaka and other sages, the text proclaims Rāma as the supreme Tāraka Brahman. It sets forth the esoteric meaning, constituent syllables (aṅgas), yantras, and ritual recitations (puraścaraṇa) of various Rāma mantras.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramarahasyopanisat.attribution: A text of unknown date, commented upon by Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramarahasyopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text including the opening Atharvavedic śāntipāṭha (bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...) and concluding colophon (iti śrīramarahasyopaniṣatsamāptā).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramatapinyupanisat.title: Rāmatāpinyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramatapinyupanisat.summary: The Rāmatāpinyupaniṣad is divided into the Pūrvatāpinī and Uttarātāpinī sections. The Pūrvatāpinī expounds the theological identity of Rāma as the supreme non-dual Brahman, establishing the iconography, the six-syllable Rāma mantra, and yantric ritual worship. The Uttarātāpinī identifies Rāma with the saving Tāraka mantra and correlates his forms with states of consciousness and the praṇava.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_ramatapinyupanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising both major divisions: the Pūrvatāpinī (5 upaniṣads/adhyāyas) and the Uttarātāpinī (5 khaṇḍas).
translations: Paul Deussen, Sixty Upaniṣads of the Veda, translated from German by V. M. Bedekar and G. B. Palsule, parts 1 and 2, Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1980. (English)

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarasvatirahasyopanisat.title: Sarasvatīrahasyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarasvatirahasyopanisat.summary: The Sarasvatīrahasyopaniṣad is an Upaniṣad structured as a dialogue between inquiring ṛṣis and the sage Āśvalāyana, presenting devotion and mantras to goddess Sarasvatī alongside an Advaita Vedānta exposition of māyā, īśvara, and savikalpaka/nirvikalpa samādhi.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarasvatirahasyopanisat.attribution: Śākta Upaniṣad, opens with Ṛgvedic śāntipāṭha (vāṅ me manasi…). The opening verse is an invocatory maṅgala verse to Rāmacandra.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarasvatirahasyopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete: maṅgala verse, Ṛgvedic śāntipāṭha (vāṅ me manasi…), dialogue of the ṛṣis with Āśvalāyana, Sarasvatī mantras and Advaita closing section, ending with śāntipāṭha and colophon 'iti sarasvatīrahasyopaniṣatsamāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarvasaropanisat.title: Sarvasāropaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarvasaropanisat.summary: The Sarvasāropaniṣad is a short Sāmānya-Vedānta Upaniṣad structured as a catechistic glossary of Advaita metaphysics. In twenty-one prose passages and concluding verses, it poses and answers questions defining fundamental concepts: bondage (bandha), liberation (mokṣa), avidyā, vidyā, the four states of consciousness (jāgrat, svapna, suṣupti, turīya), the five sheaths (pañcakośa), the soul and witness consciousness (kartṛ, jīva, kṣetrajña, sākṣin, kūṭastha, antaryāmin), concluding with the identification of the innermost self (pratyagātman) with unconditioned Brahman.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarvasaropanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising opening and closing śāntimantras ('saha nāvavatu...') and 21 numbered sections (prose definitions in §§ 1–15, concluding philosophical verses in §§ 16–21).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_saubhagyalaksmyupanisat.title: Saubhāgyalakṣmyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_saubhagyalaksmyupanisat.summary: The Saubhāgyalakṣmyupaniṣad is a Śākta Upaniṣad synthesizing devotional ritualism with yoga philosophy, beginning with the yantra, nyāsa, and mantra-vidyā of Goddess Mahālakṣmī anchored in the Ṛgvedic Śrīsūkta, and progressing into teachings on prāṇāyāma, internal cakras, nāḍīs, and meditative absorption culminating in kaivalya.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_saubhagyalaksmyupanisat.coverage: complete — Complete: maṅgala verse, Ṛgvedic śāntipāṭha, the khaṇḍas (first ends at seg. 66 '|| 1||'), closing śāntipāṭha and colophon 'iti śrīsaubhāgyalakṣmyupaniṣatsamāptā' (seg. 150).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_skandopanisad.title: Skandopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_skandopanisad.summary: The Skandopaniṣad is an Upanishad associated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Opening with a speaker's declaration to Mahādeva of his identity with Acyuta and Śiva, the text teaches radical non-difference between the individual soul (jīva) and Śiva, as well as the ultimate identity of Śiva and Viṣṇu ('śivāya viṣṇurūpāya śivarūpāya viṣṇave'). It synthesizes Śaiva and Vaiṣṇava devotional motifs into Advaita Vedānta, concluding with the Vedic refrain 'tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam'.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_skandopanisad.attribution: Attached to the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda according to the text colophon.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_skandopanisad.coverage: complete — Complete text in 15 verses, preceded by an invocatory maṅgala verse and the śāntipāṭha (saha nāvavatu).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_subalopanisat.title: Subālopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_subalopanisat.summary: The Subālopaniṣad is framed as an inquiry into cosmic origins and dissolution. It details cosmogony from primal darkness (tamas) through the cosmic egg and the cosmic Puruṣa, followed by dissolution (pralaya) of elements back into the supreme deity Nārāyaṇa. It also elaborates subtle heart anatomy, the nature of the inner ruler (antaryāmin), and conditions for liberation.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_subalopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 16 khaṇḍas, opening with the śāntipāṭha 'oṃ pūrṇamadaḥ...' and closing with '|| iti subālopaniṣatsamāptā ||'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_samarahasyopanisat.title: Sāmarahasyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_samarahasyopanisat.summary: The Sāmarahasyopaniṣad is a sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad presenting esoteric Braj devotional theology framed as an inquiry by Brahmā's sons (Sanaka and others) into the eternal līlā of Vaikuṇṭha and Vraja, followed by a dialogue between Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī. The text exalts Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa (Puruṣottama, Rasikānanda) as the supreme transcendent non-dual reality beyond the kṣara and akṣara realms. It details the nature of jīvas, the subtle body (liṅgaśarīra), and the transformation of worldly passions into sādhanā through the esoteric path of aesthetic devotion (rasamārga / snehamārga).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_samarahasyopanisat.attribution: A sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad purporting to belong to the Sāmavedic tradition, reflecting the Rādhā-centric theology and devotional terminology (snehamārga, rasikānanda, rasamārga, nikuñjadevī) of Braj Vaiṣṇavism.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_samarahasyopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text concluding with the scribal/closing verse and colophon: 'yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ ca yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ rādhe prasīda harivallabhe || iti sāmarahasyopaniṣat samāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_savitryupanisat.title: Sāvitryupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_savitryupanisat.summary: The Sāvitryupaniṣad elaborates nine cosmic and microcosmic generative pairs (mithuna) representing Savitṛ and Sāvitrī—such as fire and earth, wind and ether, mind and speech, and man and woman. It connects this duality to the three pādas of the Gāyatrī mantra and concludes with the Balā and Atibalā vidyā formulas.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_savitryupanisat.attribution: Upaniṣadic text. The e-text opens with an invocatory maṅgala verse to Rāmacandra and an Upaniṣad-listing verse.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_savitryupanisat.coverage: complete — Complete: maṅgala verse and Upaniṣad-list verse, Sāmavedic śāntipāṭha (āpyāyantu…), the Savitṛ–Sāvitrī mithuna sections, Gāyatrī and Balā/Atibalā sections, and closing śāntipāṭha.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sitopanisat.title: Sītopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sitopanisat.summary: The Sītopaniṣad is a Vaiṣṇava-Śākta minor Upaniṣad affiliated with the Atharvaveda. In a dialogue between Prajāpati and the gods, Sītā is identified as Mūlaprakṛti and the praṇava, acting as the dynamic cosmic power of Rāma. She is expounded in three functional aspects as Icchāśakti, Kriyāśakti, and Sākṣācchakti (represented respectively by Śrī, Bhū, and Nīlā), culminating in the description of Vīralakṣmī.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sitopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 37 sections/verses, opening and concluding with the Atharvaveda śāntipāṭha (bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...).

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_suryopanisat.title: Sūryopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_suryopanisat.summary: The Sūryopaniṣad (also referred to in the text as Sūryātharvāṅgirasa) is an Upaniṣad classified as an Atharvavedīya sāmānyopaniṣad. It extols Sūryanārāyaṇa / Āditya as the supreme reality, identifying him with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, the Vedas, and the cosmic principles, and includes the Sūrya-gāyatrī and an eight-syllable solar mantra alongside phalaśruti declarations detailing purification from sins and liberation from death.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_suryopanisat.attribution: Traditionally designated as an Atharvavedic sāmānyopaniṣad. Incorporates an introductory maṅgala-śloka associated with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_suryopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad, including Atharvaveda śāntipāṭha and opening maṅgala verse.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_tripuratapinyupanisat.title: Tripurātāpinyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_tripuratapinyupanisat.summary: The Tripurātāpinyupaniṣad is a Śākta Upaniṣad belonging to the Śrīvidyā tradition and traditionally affiliated with the Atharvaveda. Arranged into five sections (upaniṣads), it presents an esoteric synthesis identifying Vedic mantras (Gāyatrī, Jātavedas, and Mṛtyuñjaya) with the Śrīvidyā mantra syllables, details the geometry and esoteric worship of the Śrīcakra along with mudrās, and expounds the ultimate identity between the goddess Tripurasundarī and non-dual consciousness (Brahman).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_tripuratapinyupanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in five sections (prathamā through pañcamā upaniṣat), followed by the Atharvaveda śāntipāṭha and final colophon.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_tarasaropanisat.title: Tārasāropaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_tarasaropanisat.summary: The Tārasāropaniṣad is a Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad formulated as dialogues between Bṛhaspati, Bharadvāja, and Yājñavalkya. It identifies the ultimate liberating mantra (tāraka) imparted at Avimukta as the eight-syllabled Nārāyaṇa mantra and Praṇava (oṃ). The text correlates the component morphemes and phonemes of the mantra with deities and figures of the Rāmāyaṇa—equating them with Jāmbavān, Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā, and Rāma as the supreme Puruṣottama.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_tarasaropanisat.coverage: complete — Text with opening maṅgala, śāntipāṭha, and concluding colophon.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vajrasucyupanisat.title: Vajrasūcyupaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vajrasucyupanisat.summary: The Vajrasūcyupaniṣad examines the defining criteria of a Brāhmaṇa. Through sequential refutations, it denies that brāhmaṇahood consists in the individual self (jīva), the physical body (deha), caste or lineage by birth (jāti), scriptural learning (jñāna), ritual action (karma), or religious merit (dhārmika). It concludes that a true Brāhmaṇa is defined by realization of the non-dual Brahman (sat-cit-ānanda) coupled with self-mastery and absence of egotism.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vajrasucyupanisat.attribution: A minor Upaniṣad structurally similar to Aśvaghoṣa's Vajrasūcī, sometimes attributed to Śaṅkara / a Vedānta scholar named Śaṅkara.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vajrasucyupanisat.coverage: complete — Comprising 9 sections flanked by śāntipāṭha and closing line.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_visvambharopanisat.title: Viśvaṃbharopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_visvambharopanisat.summary: The Viśvaṃbharopaniṣad is a sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad styled as an Atharvavedic dialogue between sage Śāṇḍilya and Mahāśambhu (Śiva). It glorifies Śrī Rāma as the ultimate reality beyond saguṇa and nirguṇa, from whom all avatāras (including Kṛṣṇa and Nārāyaṇa) manifest. The text instructs the practitioner in principal Rāma mantras (ṣaḍakṣara, aṣṭākṣara, and dvayamantra), diagrammatic yantra preparation, nyāsa rituals, and daily pūjā offerings.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_visvambharopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short Upaniṣad, concluding with 'ityatharvaṇe viśvambharopaniṣat samāptaḥ'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vasudevopanisat.title: Vāsudevopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vasudevopanisat.summary: The Vāsudevopaniṣad is a minor sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad, traditionally attached to the Sāmaveda. Structured as a dialogue between Bhagavān Vāsudeva and the sage Nārada, it outlines the ritual requirements and sacred mantras for applying the vertical sectarian forehead mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) using sacred clay (gopīcandana). It interprets the puṇḍra mystically through the syllables of Oṃ (A-U-M) and the manifestations of Viṣṇu, concluding with the spiritual rewards of unswerving devotion to Vāsudeva.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vasudevopanisat.attribution: A minor sectarian Vaiṣṇava Upaniṣad canonically affiliated with the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_vasudevopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete root text, preceded by an opening maṅgala śloka ('yatsarvahṛdayāgāraṃ...'), the standard Sāmaveda śāntipāṭha ('āpyāyantu mamāṅgāni...'), and concluded with the final colophon.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_arseyopanisat.title: Ārṣeyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_arseyopanisat.summary: The Ārṣeyopaniṣad is an archaic prose Upaniṣad written in Vedic Brāhmaṇa-like style. It records a theological dispute (brahmodya) among five ancient sages—Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Gautama, and Vasiṣṭha—who successively critique each other's conceptions of Brahman (intermediate space, the cosmic egg/water, the solar light, and the golden person) as perishable (ārta), culminating in Vasiṣṭha's exposition of Brahman as the all-encompassing, imperishable inner Ātman approached through neti neti.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_arseyopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short prose Upaniṣad (segments 0–23), concluding with the verses and final colophon 'ityārṣeyopaniṣat samāptā'.
translations: Belvalkar, S. K. (tr.), 'Four Unpublished Upanishadic Texts', 1925. (English)

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atmabodhopanisat.title: Ātmabodhopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atmabodhopanisat.summary: The Ātmabodhopaniṣad (also referred to at its conclusion as the Ātmaprabodhopaniṣad) is an Upaniṣadic text. Adhyāya 1 delineates meditation on Nārāyaṇa via the aṣṭākṣaramantra, the inner luminosity of Brahman in the heart lotus, and liberation. Adhyāya 2 forms an extended monistic hymn of Self-knowledge, declaring the transcendent Self to be unattached, beyond the three bodies (sthūla, liṅga, kāraṇa), and identical with pure, non-dual consciousness.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_atmabodhopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in two adhyāyas (adhyāya 1 with 8 sections/mantras and adhyāya 2 with 31 verses), preceded by an opening maṅgalaśloka and the śāntipāṭha (oṃ vāṅme manasi), and concluding with the phalaśruti formula.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarabhopanisat.title: Śarabhopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarabhopanisat.summary: The Śarabhopaniṣad is a sectarian Śaiva Upaniṣad formulated as a dialogue where Brahmā instructs the sage Paippalāda on the supremacy of Śiva among the Trimūrti, recounting how Śiva assumed the form of the Śarabha to overpower Viṣṇu/Narasiṃha and extols Śiva/Rudra as the supreme Brahman.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarabhopanisat.coverage: complete — Text of the Upaniṣad including the opening verse, opening and closing śāntipāṭha (Bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ...), and the dialogue between Paippalāda and Brahmā.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sukarahasyopanisat.title: Śukarahasyopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sukarahasyopanisat.summary: The Śukarahasyopaniṣad (also known as the Rahasyopaniṣad) is framed as an initiation given by Śiva to Vyāsa's son Śuka during his upanayana, detailing the ritual and esoteric exposition of the four Vedic Mahāvākyas together with their nyāsa, dhyāna, and viniyoga. Upon receiving this instruction, Śuka attains jīvanmukti and renounces the worldly life.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sukarahasyopanisat.attribution: Presented as a dialogue wherein Śiva imparts the secret doctrine of the Mahāvākyas to Śuka at Vyāsa's request.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sukarahasyopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 53 sections bounded by the śāntimantra and the colophon 'iti śukarahasyopaniṣatsamāptā'.

SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarirakopanisat.title: Śārīrakopaniṣad
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarirakopanisat.summary: The Śārīrakopaniṣad is a minor Sāmānya Vedānta Upaniṣad affiliated with the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It provides an anatomical and psychological exposition of the human embodiment (śarīra) integrating Sāṅkhya cosmology and Vedāntic metaphysics. It details the five gross elements (mahābhūtas) and their bodily constituents, the sensory and motor faculties (indriyas), the fourfold internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa), the three guṇas, and the four states of consciousness (jāgrat, svapna, suṣupti, turīya), concluding with the identification of the seventeenfold subtle body (liṅgaśarīra) and the supreme Self transcending the embodied soul (jīva/kṣetrajña).
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarirakopanisat.attribution: A traditional Upaniṣad classified under the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. The opening verse ('tattvagrāmopāyasiddhaṃ ... śrīrāmabrahma me gatiḥ') is an invocatory maṅgala śloka associated with Upaniṣadbrahmayogin.
SA_GV05_ilx_ws_sarirakopanisat.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Upaniṣad, preceded by an invocatory couplet and the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda śāntimantra ('saha nāvavatu'), containing the prose sections, 8 numbered kārikās, closing śāntimantra, and final colophon.

SA_GV04_ilx_ws_aitareyaranyakam.title: Aitareyāraṇyaka
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_aitareyaranyakam.summary: The Aitareyāraṇyaka is an Āraṇyaka text belonging to the Śākala recension of the Ṛgveda. Arranged in five books (āraṇyakas), it expounds the ritual and theological symbolism of the Mahāvrata ceremony (Books 1 and 5), early Upaniṣadic speculations on prāṇa and the Self including the core Aitareya Upaniṣad (Book 2), esoteric phonological and recitational doctrines of the saṃhitāpāṭha (Book 3), and the Mahānāmnī verses (Book 4).
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_aitareyaranyakam.attribution: Āśvalāyana is traditionally credited with some chapters in the Aitareyāraṇyaka.
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_aitareyaranyakam.coverage: complete — Complete text of all five books (āraṇyakas) of the Aitareyāraṇyaka, including the embedded Aitareya Upaniṣad (Book II, adhyāyas 4–6), concluding with the closing śāntimantra of Book 5.
translations: Arthur Berriedale Keith, The Aitareya Āraṇyaka, Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1909. (English)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atharvapratisakhyam.title: Atharvaprātiśākhya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atharvapratisakhyam.summary: The Atharvaprātiśākhya is a phonetico-grammatical treatise belonging to the Atharvaveda, distinct from the Śaunakīyā Caturādhyāyikā. Structured in three prapāṭhakas subdivided into pādas, the work codifies euphonic combination (sandhi), accentuation (svara), lengthening, and the systematic conversion between the Padapāṭha and Saṃhitāpāṭha.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atharvapratisakhyam.attribution: Preserved within the Atharvaveda tradition. Distinct from the Śaunakīyā Caturādhyāyikā (published by W. D. Whitney).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atharvapratisakhyam.coverage: complete — Complete sūtrapāṭha in 3 prapāṭhakas (Prapāṭhaka 1 in 3 pādas, Prapāṭhaka 2 in 4 pādas, Prapāṭhaka 3 in 4 pādas), concluding with 'ātharvaṇe sahitālakṣaṇagranthe prātiśākhyamūlasūtraṃ samāptam'.

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_bhaisajyaratnavali.title: Bhaiṣajyaratnāvalī (chapters 90–106 and Pariśiṣṭa)
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_bhaisajyaratnavali.author: Govindadāsa, Brahmaśaṅkara Miśra
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_bhaisajyaratnavali.summary: This e-text contains an excerpt of the Bhaiṣajyaratnāvalī revised by Brahmaśaṅkara Miśra, including the Pariśiṣṭa (addressing disorders such as pittaroga) and concluding chapters (including viśiṣṭarogādhikāra chapters such as śīrṣāmburoga, mastiṣkavepana, and apamumūrṣucikitsā up to chapter 106).
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_bhaisajyaratnavali.attribution: The Bhaiṣajyaratnāvalī is traditionally ascribed to Govindadāsa. The text here represents a revision by Brahmaśaṅkara Miśra ('saṃskṛtā brahnaśaṅkareṇādhikāśikam') who also dedicated/opened the Pariśiṣṭa honoring Satyanārāyaṇa Śāstrī.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_bhaisajyaratnavali.coverage: excerpt — Contains the Pariśiṣṭa (beginning with pittarogacikitsāprakaraṇam) followed by chapters of the main text viśiṣṭarogādhikāra up to chapter 106 (apamumūrṣucikitsāprakaraṇam). Early chapters of the Bhaiṣajyaratnāvalī are absent.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bhasikasutrani.title: Bhāṣikasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bhasikasutrani.author: Kātyāyana
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bhasikasutrani.summary: The Bhāṣikasūtra (or Bhāṣikapariśiṣṭasūtra), traditionally attributed to Kātyāyana, is a short phonetic treatise (pariśiṣṭa) setting forth the rules of accentuation (bhāṣikasvara) in Brāhmaṇa prose, particularly describing the two-accent system (udātta and anudātta) in contrast to tripartite mantra accentuation, verbal accent shifts, and recitation tones.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bhasikasutrani.attribution: Ascribed to Kātyāyana in the concluding colophon.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bhasikasutrani.coverage: complete — Complete root text in three adhyāyas (adhyāya 1: 23 sūtras; adhyāya 2: 22 sūtras; adhyāya 3: 29 sūtras), ending with the final colophon.

SA_GV02_ilx_ws_chandogyabrahmanam.title: Chāndogyabrāhmaṇa
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_chandogyabrahmanam.summary: The Chāndogyabrāhmaṇa (widely known as the Mantrabrāhmaṇa) is a Vedic ritual text of the Kauthuma śākhā of the Sāmaveda comprising two prapāṭhakas of eight khaṇḍas each. It compiles liturgical verses and formulas for domestic (gṛhya) ceremonies, including marriage, garbhādhāna, upanayana, and funeral rites, functioning as the mantra collection corresponding to the Gobhilagṛhyasūtra. In the larger ten-chapter Chāndogya corpus, these two chapters immediately precede the eight chapters constituting the Chāndogyopaniṣad.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_chandogyabrahmanam.attribution: A Vedic Brāhmaṇa text belonging to the Kauthuma recension of the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_chandogyabrahmanam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the two prapāṭhakas (each containing 8 khaṇḍas) constituting the Chāndogyabrāhmaṇa proper (Mantrabrāhmaṇa), ending at 2.8.14 ('iti dvitīyo bhāgaḥ'). Prapāṭhakas 3–10 of the traditional ten-chapter Chāndogya collection form the Chāndogyopaniṣad.

SA_GV02_ilx_ws_devatadhyayabrahmanam.title: Devatādhyāyabrāhmaṇa
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_devatadhyayabrahmanam.summary: The Devatādhyāyabrāhmaṇa is traditionally counted as the fifth of the eight Brāhmaṇas of the Sāmaveda (Kauthuma and Rāṇāyanīya schools). In four short khaṇḍas, it enumerates the presiding deities associated with various Sāman melodies and endings, describes the colors and deities of Vedic meters, presents etymological analyses (nirvacana) of metrical terms, and concludes with an esoteric correspondence between the limbs of the cosmic deity and the Sāvitrī verse.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_devatadhyayabrahmanam.attribution: A scriptural Vedic Brāhmaṇa belonging to the Kauthuma-Rāṇāyanīya school of the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_devatadhyayabrahmanam.coverage: complete — Complete mūla text in 4 khaṇḍas (including the final Sāvitryaṅga section). The colophons preserve the commentary colophon formula of Sāyaṇa's Vedārthaprakāśa, but the commentary text itself is omitted.

SA_GS38_ilx_ws_dhanurvedah.title: Sadāśivadhanurveda
SA_GS38_ilx_ws_dhanurvedah.summary: The Sadāśivadhanurveda is a classical Sanskrit treatise on the martial arts and archery traditionally framed as revealed by Sadāśiva (Śiva). It covers social eligibility and ritual initiation into weaponry, astrological timing for training, protective aṅganyāsa formulas, weapon dimensions and classifications, bowmanship techniques, target practice (vedha), omenology on the battlefield, and army deployment (vyūha).
SA_GS38_ilx_ws_dhanurvedah.attribution: The treatise frames its instruction on archery and warfare as divine revelation from Sadāśiva (Śiva).
SA_GS38_ilx_ws_dhanurvedah.coverage: complete — Closing with the final colophon 'iti śrīmatsadāśivaprokto dhanurvedaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ekagnikandam.title: Ekāgnikāṇḍa with Ekāgnikāṇḍavyākhyāna
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ekagnikandam.author: Haradatta
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ekagnikandam.summary: The Ekāgnikāṇḍa (also known as the Mantraprapāṭhaka) is a collection of Vedic mantras belonging to the Taittirīya recension of the Yajurveda, arranged for domestic rituals (gṛhyakarmasu) of the Āpastamba school. Divided into two prapāṭhakas, this e-text preserves the root mantra text accompanied by the Ekāgnikāṇḍavyākhyāna of Haradatta.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ekagnikandam.attribution: The root mantra collection belongs to the Taittirīya recension of the Yajurveda, functioning in the Āpastamba school as the Mantraprapāṭhaka / Ekāgnikāṇḍa. The commentary is by Haradatta.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ekagnikandam.coverage: complete — Complete text of both prapāṭhakas of the Ekāgnikāṇḍa together with Haradatta's vyākhyāna, the introductory Upoddhāta, and the concluding Mantrapratīkasūcī.

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_haritasamhita.title: Hārītasaṃhitā
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_haritasamhita.author: Hārīta
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_haritasamhita.summary: The Hārītasaṃhitā is a Sanskrit Āyurvedic treatise presented as an instructional dialogue between the sage Ātreya and his pupil Hārīta. Divided into six divisions (sthānas)—including Prathama- (Prakīrṇa- / Sūtra-), Dvitīya- (Doṣadhātu-), Tṛtīya- (Cikitsā-), Kalpa-, and Śārīrasthāna, followed by a pariśiṣṭa—it treats nosology, clinical therapy, pharmacology, and dietetics.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_haritasamhita.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Hārīta, one of the six pupils of Ātreya.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_haritasamhita.coverage: complete — Text ending with the pariśiṣṭādhyāya and final colophon ('ityātreyabhāṣite hārītottare pariśiṣṭādhyāyaḥ 1 / iti hārītasaṃhitā samāptā').
translations: Alix Raison, La Hārītasamhitā: texte médical sanskrit avec un glossaire / index, Pondichéry: Institut Français d'Indologie, 1974. (French)

SA_GV02_ilx_ws_jaiminiyopanisadbrahmanam.title: Jaiminīyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇa
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_jaiminiyopanisadbrahmanam.summary: The Jaiminīyopaniṣadbrāhmaṇa is a Vedic prose text of the Jaiminīya (Talavakāra) school of the Sāmaveda, functioning as its Āraṇyaka. In four adhyāyas it gives esoteric interpretations of the sāman chant (especially the gāyatra-sāman and the udgītha), the syllable om, prāṇa and the correspondences between ritual, cosmos and person. The fourth adhyāya contains the Kena Upaniṣad (4.18–21), and the text ends with an exposition of the Sāvitrī verse (4.27–28).
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_jaiminiyopanisadbrahmanam.attribution: Anonymous Vedic prose text of the Jaiminīya (Talavakāra) śākhā of the Sāmaveda, functioning as the Āraṇyaka of that school. It contains the Kena (Talavakāra) Upaniṣad at JUB 4.18–21 (= adhyāya 4, anuvāka 10).
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_jaiminiyopanisadbrahmanam.coverage: complete — Complete: four adhyāyas divided into anuvākas and khaṇḍas, with khaṇḍas numbered continuously within each adhyāya as in Oertel (opening JUB 1.1.1 "prajāpatir vā idaṃ trayeṇa vedena…", closing with the Sāvitrī section 4.28 and the colophon "ityupaniṣadbrāhmaṇaṃ samāptam").
translations: Hanns Oertel, 'The Jaiminīya or Talavakāra Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa: Text, Translation, and Notes', Journal of the American Oriental Society 16 (1896). (English)

SA_GV04_ilx_ws_katharanyakam.title: Kaṭhāraṇyaka
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_katharanyakam.summary: The Kaṭhāraṇyaka is the Āraṇyaka of the Kaṭha (Caraka-Kaṭha) śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It survives in fragmentary form, chiefly in a Śāradā birch-bark manuscript from Kashmir kept at Tübingen. It is a brāhmaṇa-style exposition of the Pravargya (the hot-milk offering in the Mahāvīra pot) and its prāyaścittas, and ends with the Gharmājaṭhara and Śukriya brāhmaṇas.
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_katharanyakam.coverage: complete — The text as preserved: 240 numbered sections beginning 'yuñjate brāhmaṇa' (yuñjate mana ity āhavanīye juhoti …) and ending with the colophons 'iti gharmājaṭharābrāhmaṇaṃ samāptam / iti śukriyabrāhmaṇaṃ samāptam 240'. Lacunae of the manuscript tradition are marked '---', and there are sub-sections 235-1, 239-1. The whole of what survives is present; the work itself is fragmentary.

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_kasyapasamhita.title: Kāśyapasaṃhitā (incomplete)
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_kasyapasamhita.summary: The Kāśyapasaṃhitā (also known as Vṛddhajīvakīyatantra) is an Āyurvedic treatise on kaumārabhṛtya (pediatrics, care of pregnant women and infants). It discusses lehana (electuaries), infant development, milk, and various disorders.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_kasyapasamhita.attribution: Colophon notes name the text 'kāśyapasaṃhitā vṛddhajīvakīyatantraṃ ca'. Associated in tradition with Vṛddhajīvaka and Vātsya.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_kasyapasamhita.coverage: partial — The e-text breaks off in the Khilasthāna with 'dakṣiṇāṃ diśamāśritya deśā vi---' followed by the note 'khilasthānasyaitāvāneva bhāga upalabdhaḥ kāśyapasaṃhitā vṛddhajīvakīyatantraṃ ca etāvatyevopalabdhabhāge viśrāmyati'.

SA_GV02_ilx_ws_kathakabrahmanam.title: Kāṭhakabrāhmaṇa (fragments)
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_kathakabrahmanam.summary: Brāhmaṇa text containing prose ritual explanations including agnyādheya, śrāddha, and mekhalā.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_kathakabrahmanam.coverage: fragment — Text contains sections including agnyādheyabrāhmaṇam, śrāddhabrāhmaṇam, and mekhalābrāhmaṇam.

SA_GV00_ilx_ws_kathakasamhita_visvarah.title: Kāṭhakasaṃhitā
SA_GV00_ilx_ws_kathakasamhita_visvarah.summary: The Kāṭhakasaṃhitā (or Kaṭhasaṃhitā) is the Saṃhitā of the Kaṭha śākhā belonging to the Kṛṣṇa (Black) Yajurveda. Combining metrical yajus mantras with archaic brāhmaṇa-style ritual and mythological expositions, it provides the liturgical foundation for Vedic ceremonies such as the Darśapūrṇamāsa, Agnyādheya, Agnicayana, and Aśvamedha.
SA_GV00_ilx_ws_kathakasamhita_visvarah.attribution: Canonical Saṃhitā of the Kaṭha (Caraka) school of the Kṛṣṇa (Black) Yajurveda.
SA_GV00_ilx_ws_kathakasamhita_visvarah.coverage: complete — Complete. It has all 40 sthānakas, in the three granthas iṭhimikā (1–18), madhyamikā (19–30) and orimikā (31–40), and the fifth grantha (Aśvamedha) with its 13 vacanas, each closed by a colophon. The text ends 'ityekottaraśatādhvaryuśākhāprabhedabhinne ... aśvamedho nāma pañcamo granthaḥ saṃpūrṇaḥ || saṃpūrṇā ca carakaśākhā'. It has no accents (visvara).

SA_GV00_ilx_ws_krsnayajurvedakandah_5_7.title: Taittirīyasaṃhitā (kāṇḍas 5–7)
SA_GV00_ilx_ws_krsnayajurvedakandah_5_7.summary: The Taittirīya Saṃhitā is the primary saṃhitā of the Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa (Black) Yajurveda, interspersing liturgical mantras (yajus) with prose theological and ritual explanations (brāhmaṇa). Kāṇḍa 5 deals with the Agnicayana (piling of the fire altar), Kāṇḍa 6 with the Soma sacrifice, and Kāṇḍa 7 with the Gavāmayana sattra and the Aśvamedha (horse sacrifice).
