SA_GV00_ilx_ws_krsnayajurvedakandah_5_7.attribution: Canonical text of the Taittirīya śākhā of the Black (Kṛṣṇa) Yajurveda.
SA_GV00_ilx_ws_krsnayajurvedakandah_5_7.coverage: partial — Contains Kāṇḍas 5, 6, and 7 (from 5.1.1 to 7.5.25), completing the second half of the seven-kāṇḍa Taittirīya Saṃhitā; unaccented text.
translations: Arthur Berriedale Keith (trans.), The Veda of the Black Yajus School entitled Taittiriya Sanhita, Harvard University Press, 1914. (English)

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_madhavanidanam.title: Mādhavanidāna
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_madhavanidanam.author: Mādhavakara
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_madhavanidanam.summary: The Mādhavanidāna (originally titled Rogaviniścaya) is a foundational 7th–8th-century Ayurvedic treatise devoted to pathology and clinical diagnosis (nidāna). Composed by Mādhavakara, the text systematizes the five diagnostic factors (pañcanidāna: nidāna, pūrvarūpa, rūpa, upaśaya, and saṃprāpti) across sixty-nine disease classifications, forming part of Ayurveda's 'shorter triad' (laghutrayī).
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_madhavanidanam.attribution: Authored by Mādhavakara (son of Indukara), dated by scholarship to circa the 7th–8th century CE.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_madhavanidanam.coverage: complete — Complete root text (mūla) in 69 thematic sections, from Pañcanidānalakṣaṇa and Jvara down to Viṣaroga, ending with the standard concluding verses and final colophon (iti śrīmādhavakaraviracitaṃ mādhavanidānaṃ samāptam).
translations: G. J. Meulenbeld, The Mādhavanidāna and its Chief Commentary, Leiden: E. J. Brill, 1974. (English)

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_nadipariksa.title: Nāḍīparīkṣā
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_nadipariksa.author: Kaṇāda
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_nadipariksa.summary: The Nāḍīparīkṣā ('Examination of the Pulse') is an Āyurvedic manual of pulse diagnosis. It describes the palpation of the radial pulse (jīvanāḍī) at the wrist with fingers, interpreting rhythm, speed, and volume corresponding to vāta, pitta, kapha, and their combinations. It further details diagnostic pulse variations across various morbid states and fatal prognostic signs.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_nadipariksa.attribution: The opening verses (segments 2–3) were composed by Śaṅkara (styled 'Brahmānvita-Śaṅkara'), who composed the commentary 'Vaidyapriyā' at the request of Jayakṛṣṇadāsa.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_nadipariksa.coverage: complete — Root text preceded by introductory verses mentioning the commentary Vaidyapriyā.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedarseyadipah.title: Sāmavedārṣeyadīpa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedarseyadipah.author: Bhaṭṭabhāskara
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedarseyadipah.summary: The Sāmavedārṣeyadīpa is an anukramaṇī-style guide to the Sāmaveda composed by Bhaṭṭabhāskara (Bhāskarayajvan) of the Kāśyapa gotra. Drawing on the Ārṣeyabrāhmaṇa, Nidānasūtra, and Kalpasūtra traditions, it systematically records the seer (ṛṣi), meter (chandas), and deity (devatā) for the chants (sāman) and root verses (ṛc) of the Āgneya, Aindra, Pāvamāna, and Āraṇyaka portions of the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedarseyadipah.attribution: The author identifies himself as Bhāskarayajvan (Bhaṭṭabhāskarādhvarīndra) of the Kāśyapa gotra.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedarseyadipah.coverage: complete — Complete work across divisions including Āgneya, Aindra, Āraṇyaka, Śukriya, and Śakvarī, concluding with final colophon: iti śrīmadbhaṭṭabhāskarādhvarīndraviracitaḥ sāmavedārṣeyadīpaḥ samāptaḥ.

SA_GV02_ilx_ws_taittiriyabrahmanam_visva.title: Taittirīyabrāhmaṇa
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_taittiriyabrahmanam_visva.summary: The Taittirīyabrāhmaṇa is the principal Brāhmaṇa prose text of the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa (Black) Yajurveda. Structured into three kāṇḍas, it expounds the theological rationale, liturgical formulas, and rituals of major śrauta rites including the Agnyādhāna, Gavāmayana, Vājapeya, Soma sacrifices, Nakṣatreṣṭis, Sautrāmaṇī, Aśvamedha, and Agnicayana. The third kāṇḍa also preserves significant theological and cosmological narratives, notably an archaic version of the Naciketas story (3.11.8).
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_taittiriyabrahmanam_visva.attribution: A Vedic Śruti prose text belonging to the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda; traditional revelation without individual human authorship.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_taittiriyabrahmanam_visva.coverage: complete — All three kāṇḍas, from 1.1.1.1 to the end of 3.12.9 (Viśvasṛj-cayana, '… yebhyaś cainat prāhuḥ'); accents removed (viśvarapāṭha). The Kāṭhaka sections (3.10–3.12) are included.

SA_GV04_ilx_ws_taittiriyaranyakam_visvar.title: Taittirīyāraṇyaka (prapāṭhakas 1–8)
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_taittiriyaranyakam_visvar.summary: The Taittirīyāraṇyaka is the Āraṇyaka associated with the Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It contains liturgical and theological material for rites such as the Āruṇaketuka fire-altar (prapāṭhaka 1), svādhyāya and the Brahmayajña (prapāṭhaka 2), Pravargya (prapāṭhakas 4–5), Pitṛmedha (prapāṭhaka 6), and the Śīkṣāvallī and Ānandavallī of the Taittirīyopaniṣad (prapāṭhakas 7–8). This e-text provides an unaccented transcription of prapāṭhakas 1 to 8.
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_taittiriyaranyakam_visvar.attribution: Traditional Vedic liturgical and theological text belonging to the Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda; anonymous.
SA_GV04_ilx_ws_taittiriyaranyakam_visvar.coverage: partial — Contains prapāṭhakas 1 through 8 only (out of 10). Prapāṭhakas 9 (Bhṛguvallī of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad) and 10 (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad) are omitted. The text is unaccented (visvara).
translations: Charles Malamoud, Le svādhyāya. Récitation personelle du Veda. Taittirīya-Āranyaka livre II. Paris: Institut de civilisation indienne, 1977. (French)
Patrick Olivelle, ed. and trans., Upaniṣads, World's Classic Series, Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1996. (English)

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_tantrayuktih.title: Tantrayukti (anthology of Āyurvedic passages on tantrayukti)
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_tantrayuktih.summary: An anthology of Sanskrit passages on tantrayukti, the devices used to compose and interpret technical treatises, as discussed in Āyurvedic classics including the Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha, Carakasaṃhitā, and Suśrutasaṃhitā Uttaratantra 65.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_tantrayuktih.attribution: Composite Wikisource compilation including passages from the tantrayukti sections of the Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha (with Indu), Carakasaṃhitā (with Cakrapāṇidatta), and Suśrutasaṃhitā Uttaratantra 65 with Ḍalhaṇa's commentary.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_tantrayuktih.coverage: excerpt — Anthology of excerpts treating the tantrayuktis across different Āyurvedic treatises, including Suśrutasaṃhitā Uttaratantra 65 with commentary.

SA_GV02_ilx_ws_vamsabrahmanam.title: Vaṃśabrāhmaṇa
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_vamsabrahmanam.summary: The Vaṃśabrāhmaṇa is traditionally reckoned as the eighth of the minor Brāhmaṇas belonging to the Kauthuma school of the Sāmaveda. In three short khaṇḍas, it preserves the genealogical list of teachers and disciples (vaṃśa) responsible for the preservation and transmission of Sāmavedic ritual chants and teachings. The teacher lineages trace back from historical teachers through ancient ṛṣis to divine figures and ultimately to Brahman Svayambhū.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_vamsabrahmanam.attribution: A Vedic prose text traditionally classified as the eighth of the minor Brāhmaṇas belonging to the Kauthuma recension of the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV02_ilx_ws_vamsabrahmanam.coverage: complete — Complete text in three khaṇḍas (khaṇḍa 1: 27 sentences; khaṇḍa 2: 35 sentences; khaṇḍa 3: 15 sentences, ending with 'samānaṃ paraṃ samānaṃ param').

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_visavaidyasarasamuccayam.title: Viṣavaidyasārasamuccaya
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_visavaidyasarasamuccayam.summary: The Viṣavaidyasārasamuccaya is a Sanskrit compendium on toxicology (agadatantra / viṣavaidya). It details the examination of astrological factors, messengers (dūta), and omens (śakuna) at the time of snakebites, anatomical vulnerability based on vital spots (marman), and therapeutic treatments including antidotes, medicated ghees, and supportive rituals.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_visavaidyasarasamuccayam.attribution: The author pays homage to his preceptor Vāsudeva (1.1–1.2) but remains anonymous.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_visavaidyasarasamuccayam.coverage: complete — Text complete in three parts/adhyāyas, closing with the Garuḍa benediction and authorial kṣamāpanā verse (3.72).

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedaprakasah.title: Āyurvedaprakāśa
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedaprakasah.author: Mādhava
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedaprakasah.summary: The Āyurvedaprakāśa of Upādhyāya Mādhava is a rasaśāstra treatise on preparing and using mercury, minerals, metals, gems and poisons in medicine. The first chapter covers the processing (saṃskāra) of mercury and related alchemical procedures, and the later chapters cover the uparasas, metals, gems and poisons. It quotes many earlier rasa authorities (Rasārṇava, Rasendracintāmaṇi, Rasaratnasamuccaya and others).
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedaprakasah.coverage: complete — Complete treatise including chapter 1 on mercurial procedures (sūtasādhana/saṃskāra) and subsequent treatments of minerals, metals, etc., ending with errata (pāṭhasaṃśodhana) and variant readings.

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedasutram_yoganandan.title: Āyurvedasūtra with the commentary of Yogānandanātha
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedasutram_yoganandan.author: Yogānandanātha
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedasutram_yoganandan.summary: The Āyurvedasūtra is a syncretic Sanskrit treatise that synthesizes classical Āyurvedic medicine (the tridoṣa doctrine, dhātus, dietetics, and pathology) with Yogic physiology (nāḍīs, cakras, prāṇa, and samādhi). Arranged in 16 praśnas, the root aphorisms are accompanied by the prose Bhāṣya of Yogānandanātha, which explains bodily health, humoral balance, and dietary discipline as prerequisites for spiritual realization.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedasutram_yoganandan.attribution: The root aphorisms are traditional/anonymous. The prose commentary (Bhāṣya) is attributed to Yogānandanātha.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_ayurvedasutram_yoganandan.coverage: complete — Ending with 'ityāyurvedasya ṣoḍaśaḥ praśnaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_GS40_ilx_ws_sarngadharasamhita.title: Śārṅgadharasaṃhitā
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_sarngadharasamhita.author: Śārṅgadhara
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_sarngadharasamhita.summary: The Śārṅgadharasaṃhitā is an Āyurvedic medical compendium composed by Śārṅgadhara. Divided into three divisions (Pūrvakhaṇḍa, Madhyamakhaṇḍa, and Uttarakhaṇḍa), it deals with pharmaceutical preparations, disease diagnosis, and treatment.
SA_GS40_ilx_ws_sarngadharasamhita.coverage: complete — Text of all three sections (Pūrvakhaṇḍa, Madhyamakhaṇḍa, Uttarakhaṇḍa) followed by editorial appendices (including Pathyāpathyavivecana).

SA_GV01_ilx_ws_rgbhasyam_srimadanandatir.title: Ṛgbhāṣya
SA_GV01_ilx_ws_rgbhasyam_srimadanandatir.author: Madhva
SA_GV01_ilx_ws_rgbhasyam_srimadanandatir.summary: The Ṛgbhāṣya is a theological commentary on the first 40 sūktas of the Ṛgveda (the first adhyāya of the first aṣṭaka) composed by Madhvācārya (Ānandatīrtha). In this work, Madhva applies a threefold hermeneutical framework (adhiyajña, adhidaiva, and adhyātma/parabrahma) to demonstrate that the Vedic hymns fundamentally refer to and praise Viṣṇu-Nārāyaṇa as the supreme divinity.
SA_GV01_ilx_ws_rgbhasyam_srimadanandatir.coverage: complete — Madhva's Ṛgbhāṣya covers the first 40 sūktas (the first adhyāya of the first aṣṭaka) of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā. The e-text concludes with 'iti śrīmadānandatīrthabhagavatpādācāryaviracitaṃ ṛgbhāṣyaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvedapratisakhyam.title: Ṛgvedaprātiśākhya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvedapratisakhyam.author: Śaunaka
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvedapratisakhyam.summary: The Ṛgvedaprātiśākhya is the oldest surviving phonological and metric treatise (prātiśākhya) of the Vedic literature, affiliated with the Śākala recension of the Ṛgveda and traditionally attributed to Śaunaka. Organized into three adhyāyas comprising eighteen paṭalas, it systematically describes Vedic phonetics, sandhi rules, accentuation (svara), syllable length, meter (chandas), and the phonetic modifications required to derive the continuous saṃhitāpāṭha from the word-by-word padapāṭha. It forms an indispensable source for the history of Vedic phonology and early Indian grammatical thought.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvedapratisakhyam.coverage: complete — Contains all 3 adhyāyas (18 paṭalas) of the root metrical/sūtra text; ends with paṭala 18 and adhyāya 3 colophon (though with OCR/transcription corruption in the colophon strings).
translations: Mangal Deva Shastri (tr.), Ṛgvedaprātiśākhya, Punjab Oriental Series, Lahore. (English)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_amoghanandini_siksa.title: Amoghānandinīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_amoghanandini_siksa.summary: The Amoghānandinīśikṣā is a phonetic manual (śikṣā) of the Vājasaneyi tradition. It lists Saṃhitā words to be pronounced with labial versus dental/labio-dental sounds, treats nāda, nasalisation (anunāsika), pluti, and syllable-counts of recitation units, closing with verses on correct recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_amoghanandini_siksa.attribution: Traditional Mādhyandina (Vājasaneyi) śikṣā. The main text opens 'atha śikṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi hyamoghānandakāriṇīm'. Its closing verses call it 'amoghānandasaṃjñā … kṛtā vājasaneyinām'.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_amoghanandini_siksa.coverage: complete — Main text contains verses and prose example lists, closing with verse 57 (amoghānandasaṃjñā ... kṛtā vājasaneyinām) and colophon 'iti amaghānandinī śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_antanirdesam.title: Antanirdeśa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_antanirdesam.summary: The Antanirdeśa is an anonymous Vedalakṣaṇa index text belonging to the Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It lists the opening words and concluding boundary markers of the anuvākas of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, classifying them by length according to the number of constituent pada/daśatī units (from 1 up to 59).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_antanirdesam.attribution: Anonymous Vedalakṣaṇa treatise preserved in the South Indian recitation tradition of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_antanirdesam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short tract in 46 lines/segments, enumerating ending points and groups from 1 to 59, concluding with 'antanirdeśassamāptaḥ'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arunasamanam.title: Aruṇasamāna
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arunasamanam.summary: An ancillary mnemonic text listing word forms and endings, concluding with 'aruṇaśamānaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arunasamanam.coverage: complete — Complete short mnemonic text listing words alphabetically from 'a' to 'h' followed by groups with shared endings (-īr, -ūr, -aiḥ, -yoḥ), concluding with 'aruṇaśamānaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_avasananirnayasiksa.title: Avasānanirṇayaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_avasananirnayasiksa.author: Anantadeva
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_avasananirnayasiksa.summary: The Avasānanirṇayaśikṣā is a short phonetico-liturgical manual (śikṣā) belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda tradition, attributed to Anantadeva. It systematically classifies and enumerates the caesuras/pauses (avasāna) across the 40 adhyāyas (1,975 kaṇḍikās) of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, categorizing verses according to their number of avasānas (dvyavasāna, tryavasāna, etc.) to ensure accurate Vedic recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_avasananirnayasiksa.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Anantadeva.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_avasananirnayasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved, from the initial mangala/pratijñā through section 14, the concluding statistical summary tallying 1,975 kaṇḍikā-avasānas in 40 adhyāyas, and the final colophon.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_dhatupathah.title: Dhātupāṭha
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_dhatupathah.author: Pāṇini
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_dhatupathah.summary: The Dhātupāṭha is the canonical verbal inventory of the Pāṇinian grammatical tradition (Vyākaraṇa), serving as the foundational auxiliary text to the Aṣṭādhyāyī. It arranges approximately two thousand verbal roots into ten conjugation classes (gaṇas), starting from bhvādi and ending with curādi. Each entry provides the root's base form with diacritical markers (anubandhas) denoting accent, voice (parasmaipada, ātmanepada, or ubhayapada), and morphophonological traits, alongside traditional semantic glosses.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_dhatupathah.attribution: The Dhātupāṭha is an essential ancillary text of the Pāṇinian grammatical tradition.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_dhatupathah.coverage: complete — Complete enumeration across all ten verbal classes (gaṇas), opening with the bhvādigaṇa (bhū sattāyām) and concluding with the curādigaṇa ending (pucchādiṣu dhātvartha ityeva siddham).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_siksaparibhasa.title: Aṣṭādhyāyī with Pāṇinīyaśikṣā, Gaṇapāṭha, Dhātupāṭha, and Liṅgānuśāsana
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_siksaparibhasa.author: Pāṇini
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_siksaparibhasa.summary: The Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini (c. 350 BCE) is the foundational text of Sanskrit grammar, formulating nearly 4,000 aphoristic rules across eight chapters. This e-text reproduces a traditional compendium presenting the core sūtrapāṭha together with auxiliary treatises: the Pāṇinīyaśikṣā, the Gaṇapāṭha, the Dhātupāṭha, and the Liṅgānuśāsana.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_siksaparibhasa.attribution: Traditional Indian grammatical lineage attributes the ancillary texts to Pāṇini.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_siksaparibhasa.edition: Aṣṭādhyāyī (śikṣāparibhāṣādisahitā). Mumbaī: Khemarāja Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa, "Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara" Chāpākhānā, n.d.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_astadhyayi_siksaparibhasa.coverage: complete — Contains the complete Pāṇinīyaśikṣā (opening segments 1–32), the eight adhyāyas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī sūtrapāṭha, the Gaṇapāṭha, the Dhātupāṭha, and the Liṅgānuśāsana in full.
translations: Sumitra M. Katre, Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini. Austin: University of Texas Press, 1987. (English)
Otto Böhtlingk, Pâṇini's Grammatik. Leipzig: H. Haessel, 1887. (German)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanagrhyasutram.title: Baudhāyanagṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanagrhyasutram.summary: The Baudhāyanagṛhyasūtra is a principal domestic ritual manual of the Baudhāyana school of the Black Yajurveda (Kṛṣṇayajurveda, Taittirīya śākhā). Structured in four praśnas, it covers the seven standard pākayajña archetypes and life-cycle rites (saṃskāras) from marriage (vivāha) through pregnancy, birth, childhood ceremonies, Vedic initiation (upanayana), study vows, ancestral offerings, house construction, and domestic prāyaścittas. It constitutes the gṛhya component of the comprehensive Baudhāyana Kalpasūtra.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanagrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Praśnas 1–4 of the Baudhāyanagṛhyasūtra, with colophons for each praśna, ending with the double pratīka list of 4.12, 'iti bodhāyanīye gṛhyasūtre caturthapraśnaḥ | iti bodhāyanīyagṛhyasūtraṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasrautasutram.title: Baudhāyanaśrautasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasrautasutram.summary: The Baudhāyanaśrautasūtra, of the Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, is generally regarded as the oldest extant Śrautasūtra. It prescribes, largely from the Adhvaryu's standpoint, the solemn rites from the Darśapūrṇamāsa, Agnyādheya, Agnihotra, Paśubandha and Cāturmāsya through the Agniṣṭoma, Agnicayana, Vājapeya, Rājasūya, Aśvamedha and sattras. Distinctive are its discursive Dvaidha sections recording differing opinions of Baudhāyana, Śālīki, Aupamanyava and other teachers, followed by Karmānta and Prāyaścitta sections.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasrautasutram.attribution: Traditionally ascribed to the sage Baudhāyana (Bodhāyana) of the Taittirīya śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasrautasutram.coverage: complete — No praśna colophons or numbering survive in the e-text, so completeness was checked by content: it runs from the Darśapūrṇamāsa ('āmāvāsyena vā paurṇamāsena vā haviṣā yakṣyamāṇo bhavati') through ritual sections, Dvaidha sections recording views of Baudhāyana, Śālīki, Aupamanyava, and ends 'sarvānityācāryaḥ sarvānityācāryaḥ'.
translations: C. G. Kashikar, trans., Baudhāyanaśrautasūtram, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts / Motilal Banarsidass. (English)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasulbasutram.title: Baudhāyanaśulbasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasulbasutram.summary: The Baudhāyanaśulbasūtra contains detailed geometric rules and measurement techniques for the construction of Vedic sacrificial altars (agnicayana), including the geometric statement of the Pythagorean theorem, methods for squaring the circle and circling the square, and precise fractional approximations of the square root of two.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_baudhayanasulbasutram.coverage: complete — Root text opening with 'atheme 'gnicayāḥ' and ending with 'prākṛto vā triguṇaḥ... iti baudhāyanaśulbasūtram'.
translations: Thibaut, G., trans. In Baudhāyanaśulbasūtram, ed. Satyaprakash and R. S. Sharma. Dr. Ratna Kumari Publications Series 4, 1968 (first published. (English)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajagrhyasutram.title: Bhāradvājagṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajagrhyasutram.summary: The Bhāradvājagṛhyasūtra is a Vedic manual of domestic ritual affiliated with the Bhāradvāja school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Arranged in three praśnas, the work systematically describes lifecycle rites (saṃskāras) such as upanayana (vedic initiation), vivāha (marriage), and simantonnayana/childbirth ceremonies, followed by domestic oblations (pākayajñas), ancestral offerings, and prāyaścitta expiations.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajagrhyasutram.attribution: Belongs to the domestic ritual tradition of the Bhāradvāja school.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajagrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Complete in 3 praśnas: colophons 'iti bhāradvājasūtre prathamaḥ praśnaḥ', '… dvitīyaḥ praśnaḥ', '… tṛtīyaḥ praśnaḥ samāptaḥ | bhāradvājīyaṃ gṛhyasūtraṃ samāptam'; praśna 3 ends with khaṇḍa 21 ('nama ācāryebhyo nama ācāryebhyaḥ 21').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasiksa.title: Bhāradvājaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasiksa.summary: The Bhāradvājaśikṣā is a Vedāṅga phonetic treatise belonging to the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, traditionally ascribed to the sage Bharadvāja. In 134 anuṣṭubh verses, it provides orthoepic and phonological rules for the proper recitation and chanting of Vedic passages, covering topics such as accentuation (svara, pracaya), vowel insertion (svarabhakti), consonant gemination (dvitva), and phonetic transitions between padapāṭha and saṃhitāpāṭha.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Bharadvāja. It functions as an orthoepic and phonetic manual (śikṣā) for the Taittirīya branch of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 134 metrical verses (kārikās 1–134).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasrautasutram.title: Bhāradvājaśrautasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasrautasutram.summary: The Bhāradvājaśrautasūtra is the Śrautasūtra of the Bhāradvāja school of the Taittirīya Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, close in content and wording to the Āpastamba and Hiraṇyakeśin sūtras. Its 15 praśnas give the Adhvaryu's procedures for the Darśapūrṇamāsa, Agnyādheya, Agnihotra, Cāturmāsya, Paśubandha and the Agniṣṭoma Soma sacrifice, ending with the brahman priest's duties in the Soma rite.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasrautasutram.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Bhāradvāja, representing the Bhāradvāja carana of the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bharadvajasrautasutram.coverage: complete — Praśnas 1–15 with opening and closing colophons for each; kaṇḍikā markers in praśna.kaṇḍikā form (e.g. '14.26', '15.4'). Praśna 15 is short (kaṇḍikās 15.1–15.5, on the brahman priest in the Soma rite, ending 'etenottarayoḥ savanayoḥ 1 | iti pañcadaśaḥ praśnaḥ'). The Paitṛmedhikasūtra and Pariśeṣasūtra printed with it by Kashikar are not included.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_bhasavrttih.title: Bhāṣāvṛtti
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_bhasavrttih.author: Puruṣottamadeva
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_bhasavrttih.summary: The Bhāṣāvṛtti is a concise 12th-century commentary on Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī by the Buddhist grammarian Puruṣottamadeva of Bengal. It systematically treats only the sūtras applicable to classical Sanskrit (bhāṣā), deliberately omitting rules restricted to Vedic usage (chāndasa) and Vedic accentuation (svara).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_bhasavrttih.attribution: Author names himself in the opening maṅgalācaraṇa (segment 2–3): 'namo buddhāya, bhāṣāyāṃ yathātrimunilakṣaṇam / puruṣottamadevena ladhvī vṛttir vidhīyate'.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_bhasavrttih.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Bhāṣāvṛtti covering all eight adhyāyas (1.1 to 8.4, omitting exclusively Vedic rules as designed by the author, concluding with 'a a || iti ||').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyaparibhasasu.title: Bodhāyanagṛhyaparibhāṣāsūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyaparibhasasu.summary: The Bodhāyanagṛhyaparibhāṣāsūtra is an auxiliary ritual text belonging to the Baudhāyana tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (Taittirīya śākhā). In two praśnas, it formulates general rules of interpretation (paribhāṣā), clarifying domestic offering procedures, ritual qualifications, mantras, purifications, and the performance of life-cycle ceremonies (saṃskāra) taught across the Bodhāyana domestic ritual corpus.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyaparibhasasu.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Bodhāyana (Baudhāyana) of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (Taittirīya śākhā).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyaparibhasasu.coverage: complete — Complete in 2 praśnas: opens 'atha bodhāyanagṛhyasūtre paribhāṣāprārambhaḥ | atha prathamapraśnaḥ'; colophons 'iti bodhāyanīye gṛhyaparibhāṣāsūtre prathamaḥ praśnaḥ samāptaḥ', '… dvitīyaḥ praśnaḥ samāptaḥ', 'iti bodhāyanīyagṛhyaparibhāṣā samāptā'; final adhyāya closes with a pratīka list.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyasesasutram.title: Bodhāyanagṛhyaśeṣasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyasesasutram.summary: The Bodhāyanagṛhyaśeṣasūtra is a supplementary ritual text (śeṣasūtra) belonging to the Baudhāyana school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (Taittirīya recension). Comprising five praśnas, it provides instructions for domestic and ancillary rituals omitted or only briefly mentioned in the base Gṛhyasūtra, including expiations (prāyaścitta), apotropaic ceremonies (śānti, notably the ugrarathaśānti for the sixtieth birthday), house building, and temple-like daily devotional worship (paricaryā/pūjā) of deities such as Mahādeva, Viṣṇu, Vighneśvara, and Durgā.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyasesasutram.attribution: Associated with the tradition of Bodhāyana / Baudhāyana of the Taittirīya recension.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_bodhayanagrhyasesasutram.coverage: complete — Complete in five praśnas (praśnas 1–5), concluding at 5.8 with the ugrarathaśāntividhi and the colophon 'iti bodhāyanīyagṛhyaśeṣasūtraṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_brhaddevata.title: Bṛhaddevatā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_brhaddevata.author: Śaunaka
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_brhaddevata.summary: The Bṛhaddevatā ('Great [Index of] Deities') is an extensive metrical treatise in eight adhyāyas belonging to the Vedāṅga and Anukramaṇī literature of the Ṛgveda, traditionally attributed to Śaunaka. Composed predominantly in anuṣṭubh verses, it systematically catalogs the deities presiding over every hymn, verse, hemistich, and quarter-verse of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in sequential order. In addition to ritual classification and etymological remarks reflecting Nirukta traditions, the work is especially renowned for preserving early narrative legends (ākhyānas) explaining the mythical contexts of the hymns.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_brhaddevata.attribution: The Bṛhaddevatā is traditionally ascribed to the ancient teacher Śaunaka, though scholarship views it as belonging to the Śaunaka school.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_brhaddevata.coverage: complete — Complete text in 8 adhyāyas, extending from Adhyāya 1, verse 1 to Adhyāya 8, verse 140 (concluding with the traditional final verse 'sa brahyāmṛtamatyantaṃ... viśati jyotiruttamam || 140||').
translations: Macdonell, Arthur Anthony, The Bṛhad-devatā Attributed to Śaunaka, Harvard Oriental Series, Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press, 1904. (English)

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_brhatsamudrikasastra.title: Bṛhatsāmudrikāśāstra
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_brhatsamudrikasastra.author: Śobhanātha
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_brhatsamudrikasastra.summary: The Bṛhatsāmudrikaśāstra is a treatise on sāmudrika (physiognomy and physical marks) dealing with the bodily characteristics of men and women (strīpuruṣalakṣaṇa). This e-text contains the Sanskrit verses accompanied by a Hindi commentary (Bhāṣāṭīkā) by Nārāyaṇaprasāda Miśra.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_brhatsamudrikasastra.attribution: The accompanying Hindi commentary (Bhāṣāṭīkā) was authored by Jyotirvid Paṇḍita Nārāyaṇaprasāda Miśra of Lakhimpur Kheri (Awadh).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_brhatsamudrikasastra.edition: Bṛhatsāmudrikaśāstra (strīpuruṣalakṣaṇa), with Hindi commentary by Jyotirvid Paṇḍita Nārāyaṇaprasāda Miśra. Kalyāṇa-Mumbaī: Gaṅgāviṣṇu Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa, Lakṣmīveṅkaṭeśvara Press, Saṃvat 1963, Śake 1828 [ CE].
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_brhatsamudrikasastra.coverage: complete — Text of the treatise with introductory bhūmikā and Hindi commentary, concluding with publisher notices and advertisements.

SA_GK17_ilx_ws_chandomanjari.title: Chandomañjarī with Prabhā (stabakas 1–3)
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_chandomanjari.author: Gaṅgādāsa, Haridatta Śāstrī, Śaṅkaradeva Śāstrī
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_chandomanjari.summary: The Chandomañjarī of Gaṅgādāsa is a popular classical manual on Sanskrit metrics (chandaḥśāstra), known for providing illustrative verses devoted primarily to Kṛṣṇa. This e-text contains the first three stabakas accompanied by the modern Sanskrit Prabhā commentary by Haridatta Śāstrī and Śaṅkaradeva Śāstrī.
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_chandomanjari.attribution: Gaṅgādāsa identifies himself in opening verse 1 as the son of Gopāladāsa and Santoṣā (vaidyagopāladāsajaḥ santoṣātanayaḥ). Commentators Haridatta Śāstrī and Śaṅkaradeva Śāstrī introduce themselves explicitly in opening verse 2 of the Prabhā commentary.
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_chandomanjari.coverage: partial — Contains stabakas 1 to 3 up to the 26-syllable metre class (Utkṛti), breaking off incomplete at the end in the gloss on apavāhā.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_carayaniyasiksa.title: Cārāyaṇīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_carayaniyasiksa.summary: The Cārāyaṇīyaśikṣā is a metrical Vedāṅga phonetic treatise (śikṣā) belonging to the Cārāyaṇīya branch of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Arranged in ten adhyāyas totaling approximately 344 verses, it systematically expounds Vedic phonetic and recitation principles, including sthāna (points of articulation), karaṇa (manner/organs of articulation), accents (udātta, anudātta, svarita, pracaya), vowel length and morae (mātrā), consonant doubling, yama consonants, and phonetic modifications in recitation (sandhi, vikāra).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_carayaniyasiksa.attribution: Associated with the Cārāyaṇīya śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (traditionally named after Cārāyaṇa).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_carayaniyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text in 10 adhyāyas (chapters), matching the self-stated extent of 340+ verses in adhyāya 10 (vv. 41-42: ekatraiva tu vikhyātaṃ ślokānāṃ tu śatatrayam catvāriṃśadadhikaṃ vai) and concluding with 'iti cārāyaṇīyaśikṣāyāṃ daśamo'dhyāyaḥ'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatukarika.title: Dhātukārikā
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatukarika.author: Śrīkaṇṭha
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatukarika.summary: The Dhātukārikā (subtitled Bālarañjanī) by Śrīkaṇṭha is a versified grammatical mnemonic handbook on Sanskrit verbal roots according to the Pāṇinian system. Composed as a pedagogical aid complementary to Dharmādhikāri Cakravarti Ayyaṅgār's Śabdakārikā, it systematically covers the verbal roots across all ten classes (bhvādi to curādi), classifying their meanings, voice (parasmaipada, ātmanepada, ubhayapada), augment iṭ behaviors (seṭ, aniṭ, veṭ), and marker letters (anubandhas).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatukarika.attribution: In the prologue (vv. 1–6), the author states that after students study the Śabdakārikā on nominal forms composed by Dharmādhikāri Cakravarty Ayyaṅgār, he composed this Dhātukārikā (subtitled Bālarañjanī) in accessible verse to help students master verbal roots without struggling through the ancient Dhātupāṭha.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatukarika.coverage: complete — Complete text treating roots across all ten gaṇas (bhvādi through curādi) and concluding with anubandha rules; ends with 'iti dhātukārikā samāptā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatvarthanirupanam.title: Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntalaghumañjūṣākuñjikā (part 2: Dhātvarthanirūpaṇa to Nipātārthanirūpaṇa)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatvarthanirupanam.author: Durbalācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatvarthanirupanam.summary: A grammatical treatise or commentary running from the discussion of the meaning of roots (dhātvarthanirūpaṇa) to the conclusion of the determination of the meaning of particles (dhātvarthanipātārthanirṇaya). It discusses views of Prabhākara Mīmāṃsakas, Maṇḍana Miśra's followers, and others.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_dhatvarthanirupanam.coverage: partial — Text opens with dhātvarthanirūpaṇam and concludes with iti dhātvarthanipātārthanirṇayaḥ.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_drahyayanasrautasutram.title: Drāhyāyaṇaśrautasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_drahyayanasrautasutram.summary: The Drāhyāyaṇaśrautasūtra is the principal Śrauta manual of the Rāṇāyanīya recension of the Sāmaveda. In 31 paṭalas, it prescribes the ritual duties, recitations, and chants (sāmans) of the Udgātṛ and his assisting priests (Prastotṛ, Pratihartṛ, Subrahmaṇya) across the full spectrum of Śrauta sacrifices, closely paralleling the Lāṭyāyanaśrautasūtra of the Kauthuma school.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_drahyayanasrautasutram.attribution: Ascribed to the Vedic sage Drāhyāyaṇa, representing the Rāṇāyanīya śākhā of the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_drahyayanasrautasutram.coverage: complete — Complete sūtra text in 31 paṭalas; ending at segment 3381 with 'iti drāhyāyaṇaśrautasūtre ekatriṃśe paṭale caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ 4' followed by 'samāpto'yaṃ granthaḥ'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_dvitvalaksanam.title: Dvitvalakṣaṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_dvitvalaksanam.summary: The Dvitvalakṣaṇa is a short anonymous Vedic phonetic text (lakṣaṇagrantha) consisting of 11 verses that formulate rules and prohibitions regarding consonant gemination (dvitva) and consonant-vowel interactions in recitation, with explicit reference to the Kāṭhaka tradition.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_dvitvalaksanam.attribution: Traditional anonymous phonetic text belonging to the ancillary Vedic literature (Lakṣaṇagrantha / Śikṣā literature).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_dvitvalaksanam.coverage: complete — Complete text of 11 verses concluding with 'iti dvitvalakṣaṇaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_galadrksiksa.title: Galadṛkśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_galadrksiksa.summary: The Galadṛkśikṣā (also titled Luptarksaṅkhyātmikā Śikṣā) is a concise Vedic ancillary manual (śikṣā/pariśiṣṭa) belonging to the Śuklayajurveda (Mādhyandina Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā). It systematically tracks and counts omitted (galita/lupta) and inserted or additional (praviṣṭa/adhika) ṛc verses across the forty adhyāyas, functioning as an orthological and mnemonic control for traditional oral chanting and textual transmission.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_galadrksiksa.attribution: A traditional Śikṣā/pariśiṣṭa text attached to the Śuklayajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, Mādhyandina recension), preserved anonymously in the manuscript tradition.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_galadrksiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text covering all forty adhyāyas of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā through Īśāvāsya (adhyāya 40) and concluding with the verse count and colophon 'iti luptarksaṅkhyātmikā śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gautamisiksa.title: Gautamīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gautamisiksa.summary: The Gautamīśikṣā is a short Vedic phonetic treatise (śikṣā) belonging to the Sāmaveda tradition. It specifically analyzes complex consonant clusters (saṃyogaśṛṅkhalā), consonant gemination (dvirbhāva), transitional nasal sounds (yamas), and the combinations of up to seven consonants appearing in Sāmavedic recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gautamisiksa.attribution: The treatise belongs to the Gautama tradition of the Sāmaveda and is traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Gautama (cf. segment 119: 'gautamenoktaṃ na saptākṣarātparaḥ saṃyogo bhavati...').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gautamisiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in two prapāṭhakas, concluding with 'iti dvitīyaprapāṭhakaḥ' and 'iti sāmavedīyagautamīśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gobhilagrhyasutram.title: Gobhilagṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gobhilagrhyasutram.summary: The Gobhilagṛhyasūtra is the principal domestic ritual manual (gṛhyasūtra) of the Kauthuma and Rāṇāyanīya schools of the Sāmaveda. Arranged in four prapāṭhakas, it details the domestic fire rites (gṛhyāgni, sthālīpāka), the full cycle of life-cycle sacraments (saṃskāras including marriage, pregnancy rites, tonsure, and upanayana), regular domestic observances, ancestral rites (piṇḍapitṛyajña, aṣṭakā, śrāddha), and formal guest reception (arghya).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gobhilagrhyasutram.attribution: Traditionally ascribed to the sage Gobhila and belonging to the Kauthuma and Rāṇāyanīya recensions of the Sāmaveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_gobhilagrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Complete text in 4 prapāṭhakas ending at 4.10.26 with final colophon: 'iti caturthaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ / iti sāmavedasya gobhilīyagṛhyasūtraṃ samāptam'.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_goladhyayah.title: Golādhyāya with Vāsanābhāṣya and Marīci (part 1: up to the Golabandhādhikāra)
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_goladhyayah.author: Bhāskara, Munīśvara
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_goladhyayah.summary: The Golādhyāya is the astronomical/cosmological division of Bhāskara's Siddhāntaśiromaṇi. This e-text contains the first part up to the Golabandhādhikāra, accompanied by commentary including Munīśvara's Marīci.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_goladhyayah.attribution: Bhāskarācārya completed the Siddhāntaśiromaṇi in Śaka 1072. The Golādhyāya is its fourth division. Munīśvara, also known as Viśvarūpa, son of Raṅganātha, was born in Śaka 1525. He completed the pūrvārdha of the Marīci in Śaka 1557 and the uttarārdha in Śaka 1560.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_goladhyayah.coverage: partial — Part 1 of the Golādhyāya ('Siddhāntaśiromaṇeḥ prathamo bhāgaḥ' in the Wikisource link title). It runs up to the end of the Golabandhādhikāra, chapter 27 ('iti saptaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ || 27 ||').
translations: Translation by L. Wilkinson, edited by Pandita Bapu Deva Sastri, of Benares, Calcutta, 1861. (English)

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_harinamamrtavyakaranam.title: Harināmāmṛtavyākaraṇa (prakaraṇas 1–2)
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_harinamamrtavyakaranam.author: Jīvagosvāmī
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_harinamamrtavyakaranam.summary: The Harināmāmṛtavyākaraṇa is a Sanskrit grammar attributed to Jīva Gosvāmī. In this grammar, traditional technical grammatical designations are replaced with names of Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, and related figures (e.g., sarveśvara for vowels). This e-text preserves the root sūtras and commentary for the first two prakaraṇas (ending with the Viṣṇupada-/Kṛṣṇanāmaprakaraṇa).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_harinamamrtavyakaranam.attribution: A grammatical treatise composed by Jīvagosvāmī, containing sūtras and commentary (vṛtti).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_harinamamrtavyakaranam.coverage: partial — Contains only the first two prakaraṇas: Saṃjñāsandhiprakaraṇa and Viṣṇupadaprakaraṇa / Nāmaprakaraṇa (ends at sūtra 218: 'iti śrīśrīharināmāmṛtākhye vaiṣṇavavyākaraṇe nāma viṣṇupadaprakaraṇaṃ dvitīyaṃ samāptaṃ').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hayagrivisiksa.title: Hayagrīvīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hayagrivisiksa.summary: The Hayagrīvīśikṣā is a concise Vedāṅga phonetic treatise dedicated to the rules of jaṭāpāṭha (one of the eight traditional vikṛtipāṭha recitation modifications of Vedic saṃhitās). In eleven ślokas distributed across two vargas (designated as a jaṭāpaṭala), it expounds the mechanics of forward and reverse word pairing, elision and preservation of medial accents (madhyasvara), and sandhi treatment in modified recitations.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hayagrivisiksa.attribution: No human author is named in the text. The tract calls itself a jaṭāpaṭala and ends "mūlaśikṣā samāptā".
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hayagrivisiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text of the mūlaśikṣā in two vargas comprising 11 verses on jaṭāpāṭha (closing: 'mūlaśikṣā samāptā').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hiranyakesisrautasutram.title: Hiraṇyakeśiśrautasūtra with the commentaries Vaijayantī and Jyotsnā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hiranyakesisrautasutram.author: Satyāṣāḍha, Mahādeva, Gopīnātha Dīkṣita
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hiranyakesisrautasutram.summary: The Hiraṇyakeśiśrautasūtra (also designated Satyāṣāḍhaśrautasūtra) is an extensive manual of Vedic ritual. It extends to 29 praśnas and concludes with a pariśiṣṭa, covering Śrauta sacrifices and concluding with Pitṛmedha. The digital text includes the root sūtras along with commentary (including the Vaijayantī by Mahādeva).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hiranyakesisrautasutram.attribution: The sūtra is attributed to Satyāṣāḍha (Hiraṇyakeśin). Commentary portions include the Vaijayantī by Mahādeva.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_hiranyakesisrautasutram.coverage: complete — Extends through the 29th praśna (ekonatriṃśapraśna) and includes the concluding pariśiṣṭa.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatalaksanam.title: Jaṭālakṣaṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatalaksanam.summary: The Jaṭālakṣaṇa is a short metrical manual (lakṣaṇagrantha) detailing the rules governing jaṭāpāṭha, one of the eight traditional modified modes of Vedic recitation (aṣṭavikṛti). It explains the principles of forward and reverse coupling of pairs of words (padadvayam anukramya vyutkramya...) and details phonological and accentual phenomena such as sandhi, svara, kampa, and elongation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatalaksanam.coverage: complete — Complete short tract in 35 metrical verses with brief prose glosses; concludes at verse 35 with 'iti jaṭālakṣaṇaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanivyakhyanam.title: Jaṭāmaṇivyākhyāna
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanivyakhyanam.summary: The Jaṭāmaṇivyākhyāna (or Jaṭāmaṇitātparya) is an ancillary Vedic phonetic-recitational treatise (vikṛti-lakṣaṇa) explaining the rules and sandhi adjustments required for reciting the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in the jaṭāpāṭha ('braided') modification. Referring to the Taittirīya Prātiśākhya and related grammatical rules, it treats standard two-word combinations as well as complex three-word sequences (trikrama), illustrating the permutations (anuloma and viloma) through sacrificial mantra citations.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanivyakhyanam.attribution: The root treatise Jaṭāmaṇi and its commentary (indicated as 'jaṭāmaṇitā[tp]aryam' at segment [101]) are anonymous pedagogical works of the South Indian Taittirīya recitational tradition.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanivyakhyanam.coverage: complete — Commentary on all 76 verses of the Jaṭāmaṇi (section numbers = Jaṭāmaṇi verse numbers), ending with the colophon "jaṭāmaṇitā aparyaṃ saṃpūrṇam" (probably for jaṭāmaṇitātparyaṃ saṃpūrṇam).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanih.title: Jaṭāmaṇi
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanih.author: Nemānabhairava
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanih.summary: The Jaṭāmaṇi is a metrical Vedāṅga treatise (lakṣaṇagrantha) on the mechanics of Vedic recitation (vikṛtipāṭha), specifically jaṭāpāṭha and trikrama in the Taittirīya recension. It establishes phonological and sandhi rules for word permutations, dividing sandhi into ārṣa (natural/canonical) and pauruṣa (artificial/recitational), and details euphonic alterations, vowel quantity changes, and elisions.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanih.attribution: Attributed to Nemānabhairava in opening verse 2, who invokes Gaṇapati, his guru Sarvāvadhānin, Veṅkaṭeśa, and Śaṅkara.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatamanih.coverage: complete — Complete mūla text consisting of 4 mangala verses and 97 numbered kārikās, concluding with 'jaṭāmaṇimūlaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatapatalakarika.title: Jaṭāpaṭalakārikā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatapatalakarika.author: Vyāḍi
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatapatalakarika.summary: The Jaṭāpaṭalakārikā (or Jaṭāpaṭala), attributed to Vyāḍi, is a short 16-verse Vedāṅga manual belonging to the Śaiśirīya recension of the Ṛgveda. It provides the technical rules for the modified recitation modes (vikṛtipāṭha) of Vedic chanting, focusing specifically on the formation, sandhi adjustments, and accentual patterns of jaṭāpāṭha.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatapatalakarika.attribution: Traditional attribution to the ancient phonetician and grammarian Vyāḍi is stated directly in the opening verse.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatapatalakarika.coverage: complete — Complete text of 16 kārikās ending with the standard colophon 'iti jaṭāpaṭalakārikā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatavalli.title: Jaṭāvallī
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatavalli.summary: The Jaṭāvallī is a short metrical treatise in 56 verses belonging to the Taittirīya lakṣaṇa literature of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It formulates phonological and sandhi rules for the jaṭāpāṭha mode of Vedic chanting, detailing euphonic modifications, vowel changes, and retroflexion during both direct (anuloma) and reverse (viloma) word sequences.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatavalli.attribution: The Jaṭāvallī is an anonymous versified lakṣaṇa work transmitted in the Taittirīya recitational tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_jatavalli.coverage: complete — Complete text in 56 anuṣṭubh verses, ending with 'iti jaṭāvallī samāptā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahaparisistam.title: Jñāpakasaṃgrahapariśiṣṭa with Vivṛti
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahaparisistam.summary: The Jñāpakasaṃgrahapariśiṣṭa supplements Nāgeśabhaṭṭa's Jñāpakasaṃgraha. It collects further rules that the Mahābhāṣya derives by jñāpaka (inference from the wording of Pāṇini's sūtras) and that Nāgeśa did not include. The statements are arranged in the order of the eight adhyāyas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, and each is explained in a Sanskrit Vivṛti that sets out the Mahābhāṣya discussion and the forms the jñāpaka justifies.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahaparisistam.attribution: The opening states the purpose: 'jñāpakasaṃgrahe nāgeśena asaṃgṛhītāni bhāṣyārūḍhāni vacanāni saṃkalayya atra vyākhyāyante'. The work supplements Nāgeśa's Jñāpakasaṃgraha with Mahābhāṣya-based jñāpaka statements that Nāgeśa left out.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahaparisistam.coverage: complete — The first pariśiṣṭa in full: it opens with '|| prathamo'dhyāyaḥ ||', covers sūtras through adhyāya 8, and ends with 'iti prathamaṃ jñāpakasaṃgrahapariśiṣṭam'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahah.title: Jñāpakasaṃgraha with Vivṛti
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahah.author: Nāgeśabhaṭṭa, N. S. Rāmānuja Tātācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahah.summary: The Jñāpakasaṃgraha is a Vyākaraṇa treatise attributed to Nāgeśabhaṭṭa. It systematically compiles principles and implicit rules (jñāpaka) deduced from Pāṇini's formulation of the sūtras as discussed in Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya, specifically focusing on those not covered by traditional collections of paribhāṣās. This e-text covers all eight adhyāyas alongside the commentary Vivṛti by Rāmānujācārya, son of Kṛṣṇatāta.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahah.attribution: Root text: Nāgeśabhaṭṭa's collection of jñāpaka-based statements from the Mahābhāṣya that are not among the paribhāṣās, arranged by Aṣṭādhyāyī order. Commentary: the Vivṛti of Rāmānujācārya, son of Kṛṣṇatāta, born in Nāvalpākkam agrahāra. Introductory verse 3 notes that the root text had earlier been published in Telugu script by Pārthasārathi.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_jnapakasamgrahah.coverage: complete — Covers all 8 adhyāyas following the structure of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, concluding with the colophon of the 8th adhyāya ('ityaṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ') and the final verses of the Vivṛti.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_karanapaddhatih.title: Karaṇapaddhati
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_karanapaddhatih.author: Putumana Somayājin
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_karanapaddhatih.summary: The Karaṇapaddhati is an astronomical and mathematical manual (karaṇa) composed around 1730 CE by Putumana Somayājin of the Kerala school. Across ten adhyāyas, the treatise presents practical algorithms for planetary longitudes, eclipses, gnomon shadow reckoning, and spherical astronomy. In Chapter 6, it notably formulates infinite series expansions for π, sine, and cosine functions derived from the lineage of Mādhava of Saṅgamagrāma.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_karanapaddhatih.attribution: Author identifies himself in verse 10.12 as a yajvan born in Śivapura (Malayalam Putumana, fl. c. 1730 CE).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_karanapaddhatih.coverage: complete — Complete in 10 adhyāyas (adhyāya 1 verse 1 through adhyāya 10 verse 12 and closing benediction).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_karmapradipah.title: Karmapradīpa with Pariśiṣṭaprakāśa and Prabhā (prapāṭhaka 1 and part of prapāṭhaka 2)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_karmapradipah.author: Kātyāyana, Nārāyaṇopādhyāya, Candrakānta Tarkālaṅkāra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_karmapradipah.summary: The Karmapradīpa with the commentary Pariśiṣṭaprakāśa and the sub-commentary Prabhā, treating Vedic domestic rituals, offerings, and related rites.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_karmapradipah.attribution: The root text Karmapradīpa is accompanied by the commentary Pariśiṣṭaprakāśa of Nārāyaṇa and a sub-commentary called Prabhā.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_karmapradipah.coverage: partial — Contains prapāṭhaka 1 and part of prapāṭhaka 2 with commentary and sub-commentary.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kauhaliyasiksa.title: Kauhalīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kauhaliyasiksa.summary: The Kauhalīyaśikṣā is a Vedic phonetic manual (śikṣā) expounding phonetic and accentual doctrines following sage Kohala / Kauhala. Composed in 81 anuṣṭubh verses, it treats the Vedic accents (udātta, anudātta, svarita, and pracaya), the varieties of svarita, kampa (tremolo modulation), vikrama transitions, sandhi changes, and vocalic quantities.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kauhaliyasiksa.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to the teachings of sage Kohala / Kauhala (verse 1: 'kauhalīyamatānugām').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kauhaliyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 81 verses, ending with the colophon 'kauhalīyaśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesavipadyatmikasiksa.title: Keśavīpadyātmikāśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesavipadyatmikasiksa.author: Keśava
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesavipadyatmikasiksa.summary: A concise metrical treatise (21 verses) belonging to the Śuklayajurveda (Vājasaneyi/Mādhyandina) tradition, composed by Keśava, son of Gokula. It sets forth rules for Vedic recitation according to the school of Kātyāyana, covering hand and body placement (svaranyāsa) for accents (udātta, anudātta, and svarita), phonetic rules for semivowels, the pronunciation of the retroflex sibilant 'ṣ' as 'kh', and the proper duration of anusvāra.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesavipadyatmikasiksa.attribution: The concluding stanzas (vv. 20–21) state that this kārikā manual was composed by Keśava, son of the astrologer Gokula (Daivajña Gokula), in the lineage of the sage Āstika, expounding the teachings of the sage Kātyāyana.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesavipadyatmikasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text of 21 verses, ending with the authorial concluding stanza.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesaviyasiksa.title: Keśavīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesaviyasiksa.author: Keśava
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesaviyasiksa.summary: The Keśavīyaśikṣā (or Keśavīśikṣā) is a concise phonetic manual (śikṣā) belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda tradition, attributed to Daivajña Keśava and based on the Pratijñāsūtra. It consists of nine short sūtras followed by mnemonic kārikās dealing with vowel lengthening, consonant gemination, anusvāra pronunciation, and the coordination of hand gestures (hastasvara) with Vedic accents during recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesaviyasiksa.attribution: Attributed to Daivajña Keśava, composing within the tradition of the Śukla Yajurveda (Mādhyandina school / Pratijñāsūtra).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kesaviyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved in 13 segments (9 prose sūtras followed by explanatory kārikās) ending with the completion colophon.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_khadiragrhyasutram.title: Khādiragṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_khadiragrhyasutram.summary: The Khādiragṛhyasūtra (also known as the Drāhyāyaṇagṛhyasūtra) is an aphoristic Kalpasūtra manual of domestic ritual belonging to the Sāmaveda, closely related to the Gobhilagṛhyasūtra of which it represents an abridged and systematized recension. Structured across four paṭalas, it prescribes domestic sacrifices (pākayajña), life-cycle ceremonies (saṃskāras) such as marriage, pregnancy rites, tonsure (caula), and Vedic initiation (upanayana), as well as seasonal, ancestral (aṣṭakā, śrāddha), and hospitality rituals (argha).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_khadiragrhyasutram.attribution: A Kalpasūtra manual belonging to the Khādira / Drāhyāyaṇa śākhā of the Sāmaveda; essentially an abridged recension based on the Gobhilagṛhyasūtra.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_khadiragrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Complete text in 4 paṭalas (divided into khaṇḍas), concluding with 'iti caturthaḥ paṭalaḥ / samāptaṃ khādiraṃ gṛhyasūtram'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramakarikasiksa.title: Kramakārikāśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramakarikasiksa.author: Śambhumiśra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramakarikasiksa.summary: A metrical śikṣā text belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā) composed by Śambhu Miśra. In 94 verses, it provides rules and mnemonic indices for the types of pauses and recitative repetition markers (veṣṭana, dviveṣṭya, triveṣṭya, etc.) required during kramapāṭha recitation across the saṃhitā.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramakarikasiksa.attribution: Verse 7 names Śambhu Miśra ('śrīśambhumiśravinirmitā'). Homage is paid in v. 1 to Sūrya (dinamaṇi), Yājñavalkya, and his pupil Kātyāyana.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramakarikasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 94 verses specifying kramapāṭha veṣṭana rules across the 40 adhyāyas of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, concluding with chapter 40 (Īśāvāsyopaniṣad) in verse 94.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramasamdhanasiksa.title: Kramasaṃdhānaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramasamdhanasiksa.summary: The Kramasaṃdhānaśikṣā is a short ancillary phonetico-recitational text (śikṣā) affiliated with the Śukla Yajurveda (Mādhyandina school). It lists and clarifies 115 specific juncture points (saṃdhāna / saṅkrama) across the 40 adhyāyas of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā where distinctive phonetic or sandhi treatments arise during the recitation of the Kramapāṭha.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kramasamdhanasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text detailing the 115 kramasaṃdhānas across the 40 adhyāyas of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, concluding with line 'iti kramasandhānaśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasrautasutram.title: Kātyāyanaśrautasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasrautasutram.author: Kātyāyana
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasrautasutram.summary: The Kātyāyanaśrautasūtra is a Śrautasūtra associated with the Śukla Yajurveda (the Vājasaneyi recension and Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa). It expounds the procedures for solemn Vedic rituals, including royal sacrifices such as the Aśvamedha.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasrautasutram.attribution: Associated with the Śukla Yajurveda tradition and Kātyāyana.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasrautasutram.coverage: complete — Complete text ending at adhyāya 26 sūtras 41–42 ('śāntikaraṇamādyantayoḥ | svādhyāyadarśanāt | iti kātyāyanaśrautasūtram').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasulbasutram.title: Kātyāyanaśulbasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasulbasutram.summary: The Kātyāyanaśulbasūtra is a Śulbasūtra laying down geometrical principles and procedural rules for constructing sacrificial altars (vedis and agnis). The text treats rajjusamāsa, measurement units, rectangular and circular conversions, and geometrical properties.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_katyayanasulbasutram.coverage: complete — Text concluding at verse 39: 'samāpteyaṃ kriyā śaulbī kātyāyanamahātmanaḥ 39 || iti kātyāyanaśulbasūtram'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_kasika_padamanjarivyakhya.title: Padamañjarī
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_kasika_padamanjarivyakhya.author: Haradatta
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_kasika_padamanjarivyakhya.summary: The Padamañjarī of Haradatta Miśra is an indispensable sub-commentary (vyākhyā) on the Kāśikāvṛtti, which is the foundational commentary on Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī by Jayāditya and Vāmana. Haradatta draws deeply from Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya and Kaiyaṭa's Pradīpa to analyze and refine the grammatical derivations, technical terms, and vārttikas treated in the Kāśikā. This e-text preserves the full eight books (adhyāyas) of Haradatta's commentary.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_kasika_padamanjarivyakhya.attribution: Haradatta authored the Padamañjarī, a sub-commentary on the Kāśikāvṛtti of Vāmana and Jayāditya.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_kasika_padamanjarivyakhya.coverage: complete — Complete commentary running from Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.1 through 8.4.68, concluding with the final pāda colophon: 'iti śrībhaṭṭaharadattamiśraviracitāyāṃ padamañjaryāmaṣṭamasyādhyāyasya caturthaḥ pādaḥ'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kathakagrhyasutram.title: Kāṭhakagṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kathakagrhyasutram.summary: The Kāṭhakagṛhyasūtra (also called Laugākṣigṛhyasūtra) is the domestic ritual manual of the Kāṭhaka school of the Black Yajurveda, transmitted in Kashmir. In 73 kaṇḍikās it treats studentship and its vows, the concluding bath, house building, marriage and the rites of pregnancy and childhood, funeral and ancestral rites, and expiatory and propitiatory rites.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kathakagrhyasutram.attribution: The text belongs to the Kāṭhaka recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda and is traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Laugākṣi.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_kathakagrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Ends 73.5 "... dhuraś copadhuraś ca", followed by the colophon "iti laugākṣisūtre gṛhyapañcikāyāṃ pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ".

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ksudrakalpasutram.title: Kṣudrakalpasūtra with Kṣudrakalpasūtrabhāṣya (adhyāyas 4–6)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ksudrakalpasutram.author: Maśaka, Śrīnivāsācārya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ksudrakalpasutram.summary: The Kṣudrakalpasūtra, ascribed to Maśaka Gārgya, is an auxiliary ritual manual belonging to the Sāmaveda (Kauthuma-Rāṇāyanīya tradition) providing detailed prescriptive modifications for Sāman chant arrangements (such as pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍaha variations) within Śrauta liturgies. This e-text covers chapters 4 through 6 accompanied by the continuous Sanskrit commentary (bhāṣya) of the Viśiṣṭādvaita scholar Śatakratu Caturvedi Śrīnivāsācārya.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ksudrakalpasutram.attribution: The root Sāmavedic ritual text is ascribed to the sage Maśaka Gārgya. The commentary is by Śrīmadrāmānujasiddhāntasthāpanācārya Śatakratu Caturvedi Śrīnivāsadīkṣita / Śrīnivāsācārya.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_ksudrakalpasutram.coverage: partial — Contains adhyāyas 4–6 only (from prapāṭhaka 2 khaṇḍa 10 through prapāṭhaka 3 khaṇḍa 16, concluding with the end of the text). Adhyāyas 1–3 are not present in this file.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghubhusanakantih.title: Laghubhūṣaṇakānti
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghubhusanakantih.author: Gopāladeva
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghubhusanakantih.summary: The Laghubhūṣaṇakānti (or Kānti) is a detailed Sanskrit commentary by Gopāladeva on Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra, an influential 17th-century work on the philosophy and semantics of Pāṇinian vyākaraṇa. Reflecting the late traditional Varanasi school of Bālambhaṭṭa Pāyaguṇḍa, it elucidates root semantics (dhātvartha), case and nominal meanings (subartha, kāraka), compounding (samāsa), and the ontological theory of speech (sphoṭa), systematically defending grammarian semantics against Mīmāṃsā and Navya-Nyāya critiques.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghubhusanakantih.attribution: Gopāladeva (alias Manudvapa), son of Śambhudeva and Durgā, grandson of Anantadeva, and younger brother of Kṛṣṇadeva, was a pupil of Bālambhaṭṭa Pāyaguṇḍa.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghubhusanakantih.coverage: complete — Complete text of the commentary from the opening maṅgala through to the end of the Sphoṭanirṇaya section.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghumadhyandiniyasiksa.title: Laghumādhyandinīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghumadhyandiniyasiksa.summary: The Laghumādhyandinīyaśikṣā is a short metrical phonetic treatise (śikṣā) of 28 verses outlining the characteristic pronunciation and recitation conventions of the Mādhyandina recension of the Śukla Yajurveda. It sets out rules for phonetic substitutions, including the realization of uncombined word-initial y- as j-, intervocalic ṣ- as kh-, light versus heavy v-, phonetic coloring of the visarga, and accompanying hand and finger gestures (mocana) used during recitational chanting.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghumadhyandiniyasiksa.attribution: A traditional school-specific phonetic manual (śikṣā) belonging to the Mādhyandina recension of the Śukla Yajurveda, transmitted anonymously.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghumadhyandiniyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 28 verses with concluding colophon (iti laghumādhyandinīyā śikṣā samāptā).

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghusabdendusekharah.title: Laghuśabdenduśekhara (Saṃjñāprakaraṇa only)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghusabdendusekharah.author: Nāgeśabhaṭṭa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghusabdendusekharah.summary: The Laghuśabdenduśekhara is Nāgeśabhaṭṭa's commentary on Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita's Siddhāntakaumudī (related to his Bṛhacchabdenduśekhara). This e-text contains solely the initial Saṃjñāprakaraṇa, ending with 'iti saṃjñāprakaraṇam'.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghusabdendusekharah.attribution: A commentary by Nāgeśabhaṭṭa, son of Śivabhaṭṭa and Satīdevī, under the patronage of King Rāmasiṃha of Śṛṅgaverapura, explicitly attested in the opening verses [1]–[2].
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_laghusabdendusekharah.coverage: partial — Only the Saṃjñāprakaraṇa (opening verses 1–2 and the maṅgala 'natvā phaṇīśaṃ...' to 'iti saṃjñāprakaraṇam'). This is a portion of the commentary on Siddhāntakaumudī. Running heads of the printed edition ('guruprasādasahite laghuśabdenduśekhare') appear in the text.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghvamoghanandinisiksa.title: Laghvamoghānandinīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghvamoghanandinisiksa.summary: A concise Vedic phonetic tract (śikṣā) consisting of 17 verses, belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda tradition. It treats rules for the pronunciation of semivowels (ya and va, their semi-vocalic versus plosive realization, and slight contact / īṣatspṛṣṭatva), reduplication, and the duration (mātrā) of anusvāra.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laghvamoghanandinisiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 17 verses, ending with 'iti śrīlaghvamoghānandinī śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laksmikantasiksa.title: Lakṣmīkāntaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laksmikantasiksa.summary: The Lakṣmīkāntaśikṣā (Varṇakramacatuḥślokī) is a very short Taittirīya śikṣā. In four verses it states the rules of varṇakrama (gemination of consonants, abhinidhāna, insertion of yamas and other transition sounds, nasal treatment), drawing on the Taittirīya Prātiśākhya. On Wikisource, and so in this e-text, it is followed by a second, anonymous text under the same heading: a verse list of Taittirīya words sorted alphabetically by accent type (antodātta and ādyudātta).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laksmikantasiksa.attribution: The first part, a Taittirīya (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) śikṣā on varṇakrama, is known as Lakṣmīkāntaśikṣā or Varṇakramacatuḥślokī. The name comes from its first verse, which presents the 'catuḥślokī' as a gift of Lakṣmī's consort (Lakṣmīkānta, i.e. Viṣṇu). Some reference works treat Lakṣmīkānta as an author's name, but the text does not support that. The second part opens with a homage to Nārāyaṇa and an anonymous author's statement ('nirūpya coccasvaranirṇayo mayā'). It lists Taittirīya words alphabetically by accent type (antodātta first, then ādyudātta).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laksmikantasiksa.coverage: complete — The first part is the complete four-verse text plus its concluding verse. The second part ends with a closing colophon, but its list breaks off rather abruptly in the va- words (segment 85, 'vāco viṃśastu vi'). That is probably a defect in the source, and its completeness cannot be checked.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksigrhyasutrani.title: Laugākṣigṛhyasūtra with Devapālabhāṣya (kaṇḍikās 1–43)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksigrhyasutrani.author: Laugākṣi, Devapāla
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksigrhyasutrani.summary: The Laugākṣigṛhyasūtra (also known as Kāṭhakagṛhyasūtra or Cārāyaṇīyagṛhyasūtra) is the domestic ritual manual of the Kāṭhaka/Caraka śākhā of the Black Yajurveda. It details domestic ceremonies, offerings, and vows. This e-text provides kaṇḍikās 1–43 of the sūtra text together with the bhāṣya of Devapāla, son of Haripāla.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksigrhyasutrani.attribution: Devapāla names himself in the opening mangala (v. 3) as the son of Śrī Haripāla (pituḥ śrīharipālasya nutvā pādau nibandhanam | samantrakāṭhagṛhyasya devapālo'bhidhāsyate).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksigrhyasutrani.edition: Madhusūdan Kaul Śāstrī (ed.), The Laugākṣi-Gṛhya-Sūtras, with the Bhāṣyam of Devapāla, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies 49 (Vol. 1, Srinagar: Research Department, Jammu and Kashmir Government, 1928) and (Vol. 2).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksigrhyasutrani.coverage: partial — Kaṇḍikās 1–43 (ending 'ityāraṇyatratāni saṃpūrṇāni || iti trayaścatvāriṃśī kāṇḍikā || 43 ||').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksisiksa.title: Laugākṣiśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksisiksa.summary: The Laugākṣiśikṣā is a late Vedic phonetic and ancillary treatise associated with the Cārāyaṇīya / Kaṭha tradition of the Yajurveda. In 185 verses and concluding notes, it covers metres (chandas), accents (svara), ṛṣis, deities, and phonetic rules applicable to ritual recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksisiksa.attribution: The text states its affiliation with the Cārāyaṇīya tradition in verse 4: 'pravakṣyāmy anupūrveṇa kṛtsnaṃ cārāyaṇīyake'.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_laugaksisiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text ending at verse 185 with subsequent prose commentary/remarks and final colophon ('iti laugākṣi śikṣā samāptā').

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_linganusasanam.title: Liṅgānuśāsana
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_linganusasanam.author: Pāṇini
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_linganusasanam.summary: The Liṅgānuśāsana is a classical grammatical work on Sanskrit nominal gender (liṅga) attributed to Pāṇini. Spanning 191 sūtras, it systematically organizes nominal stems into feminine, masculine, neuter, and variable genders based on derivational affixes (pratyayas) and semantic categories.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_linganusasanam.attribution: The Liṅgānuśāsana is traditionally ascribed to Pāṇini.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_linganusasanam.coverage: complete — Complete text across 191 sūtras arranged in thematic sections: stryadhikāra, pulliṅgādhikāra, napuṃsakādhikāra, strīpuṃsādhikāra, puṃnapuṃsakādhikāra, and avaśiṣṭaliṅga.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manahsvarasiksa.title: Manaḥsvāraśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manahsvarasiksa.summary: The Manaḥsvāraśikṣā is a short Vedāṅga treatise on the phonetic and accentual recitation (svara and avasāna) of the Śuklayajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā Mādhyandina school). In 64 thematic sections, it groups Vedic mantra incipits (pratīkas) according to accent patterns (udātta, anudātta, kampa, jātya) and metrical pause distribution (tripadā, niravasāna, caturavasāna). Traditionally attributed to Yājñavalkya, it serves as a mnemonic and phonological manual for Vedic chanters.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manahsvarasiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed in its opening verse and colophon to the sage Yājñavalkya (maharṣiyogiyājñavalkyakṛtā).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manahsvarasiksa.coverage: complete — Opening verse, 64 numbered sections and the final colophon.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_muhurtadipakah.title: Muhūrtadīpaka with the commentary of Mahādevabhaṭṭa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_muhurtadipakah.author: Mahādevabhaṭṭa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_muhurtadipakah.summary: The Muhūrtadīpaka is an astrological manual on electional astrology (muhūrta) written by Mahādevabhaṭṭa in Śaka 1583 (1661 CE). In metrical verses accompanied by his own Sanskrit commentary, the work outlines auspicious and inauspicious temporal configurations (tithi, vāra, nakṣatra, and lagna) for domestic saṃskāras, journeys, construction, and daily tasks.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_muhurtadipakah.attribution: In the final verse and commentary (verses 57–58), the author names himself as Mahādeva, son of Kānhajit Vāḍava (patronized by the ruler of Mount Raivata / Girnar), and gives the date of composition as Śaka 1583 (1661 CE).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_muhurtadipakah.edition: Śrīmahādevabhaṭṭaviracitaḥ Muhūrtadīpakaḥ: śrīmanmahādevakaviviracitayā saṃskṛta-ṭīkayā samalaṃkṛtaḥ. Kalyāṇa-Baṃbaī: Gaṅgāviṣṇu Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa (Lakṣmīveṅkaṭeśvara Steam Press), Saṃvat 1994, Śake 1859 [ CE].
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_muhurtadipakah.coverage: complete — Complete in 58 verses with full Sanskrit commentary.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_madhyandiniyasiksa.title: Mādhyandinīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_madhyandiniyasiksa.summary: The Mādhyandinīyaśikṣā is a short phonetic and recitational manual (vedāṅga / śikṣā) belonging to the Mādhyandina recension of the Śukla Yajurveda. It sets out phonological rules on consonantal gemination (dvitva), lists specific instances of the guttural aspirate kha in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, and provides a chapter-by-chapter tally of omitted or elided mantras (galita-ṛc) across its forty adhyāyas.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_madhyandiniyasiksa.attribution: The opening line reads 'mādhyandinamaharṣipraṇītā śikṣā', reflecting traditional attribution to the sage Mādhyandina.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_madhyandiniyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text in 57 segments with opening phonological rules, kavargīya-kha occurrences, chapter-by-chapter enumeration of galitarcas up to adhyāya 40, and final colophon ('mādhyandinīyaśikṣā samāptā').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manavasrautasutram.title: Mānavaśrautasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manavasrautasutram.summary: The Mānavaśrautasūtra is the śrauta ritual manual of the Mānava school of the Maitrāyaṇīya branch of the Black Yajurveda, written mainly from the Adhvaryu's perspective. It covers the new- and full-moon sacrifices and the other prakṛti rites, the Agniṣṭoma, expiations, the Pravargya, the iṣṭis, the Agnicayana, the Vājapeya and Rājasūya. This e-text also contains the Mānava Śulbasūtra and a series of appendices (pratigraha, Rudrajapa, pravara lists, śrāddha rules).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manavasrautasutram.attribution: Traditionally belonging to the Mānava caraṇa of the Maitrāyaṇīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_manavasrautasutram.coverage: complete — 13 books on Wikisource/ilx (Wikisource lists kalpas 1–14 as sub-pages and 15 as a red link). Books 1–9 are the śrauta ritual. 10–12 are the Śulbasūtra (incl. the 'vaiṣṇava' section). 13 holds pratigraha, rudrajapa, pravarādhyāya, śrāddhakalpa and śrāddhapariśiṣṭa, ending 'iti śrāddhapariśiṣṭaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_mandukisiksa.title: Māṇḍūkīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_mandukisiksa.summary: The Māṇḍūkīśikṣā is the metrical śikṣā of the Atharvaveda, ascribed to Maṇḍūka. In 181 verses it treats the three speeds of recitation (druta, madhyama, vilambita), the seven musical notes and how they relate to the Vedic accents, the hand movements that accompany accented recitation and their faults, defects of pronunciation, and rules on sandhi, consonant doubling and other points of phonetics.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_mandukisiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Maṇḍūka (as recorded in concluding verse 181: 'maṇḍūkena kṛtāṃ śikṣāṃ...').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_mandukisiksa.coverage: complete — 181 continuously numbered verses with the colophon 'ityatharvaṇavedīyā māṇḍūkīśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_niruktam.title: Nighaṇṭu with Nirukta
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_niruktam.author: Yāska
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_niruktam.summary: The Nighaṇṭu is the oldest surviving Vedic word-list. It has three parts: synonym lists (naighaṇṭuka-kāṇḍa, adhyāyas 1–3), difficult and homonymous words (naigama, 4) and names of deities (daivata, 5). Yāska's Nirukta is the Vedāṅga treatise on etymology and Vedic exegesis and is built as a commentary on the Nighaṇṭu. It sets out the four word classes (nāman, ākhyāta, upasarga, nipāta), defends the derivation of nouns from verbal roots, and explains the Vedic words and deities with citations of the mantras. The e-text adds the later Pariśiṣṭa (adhyāyas 13–14).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_niruktam.attribution: The Nighaṇṭu is an anonymous Vedic wordlist. The Nirukta is Yāska's foundational commentary and treatise on Vedic etymology and semantics (c. 5th century BCE).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_niruktam.coverage: complete — Nighaṇṭu, Nirukta, and the Pariśiṣṭa.
translations: Sarup (1921) (English)

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradabaitparibhasa.title: Nāradabaiṭparibhāṣā with Bhāvaprakāśikā and the Nāradabaiṭ
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradabaitparibhasa.author: Cakra
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradabaitparibhasa.summary: A short Vedic lakṣaṇa (śikṣā) tract from the Taittirīya tradition. It explains the Nāradabaiṭ, a mnemonic syllable code ascribed to Nārada that encodes the counts of anuvākas and vākyas in the Taittirīyasaṃhitā. Seven paribhāṣā verses set out the rules (which vowels count, how conjunct consonants count in kaṭapayādi fashion, and the bindu-marked syllables ma, da, ga, ta, sa standing for tens). The author's prose commentary, Bhāvaprakāśikā, follows, and then the code strings for all seven kāṇḍas.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradabaitparibhasa.attribution: The author of the paribhāṣā verses and the Bhāvaprakāśikā calls himself Cakra, son of Śrīrāma (v. 7 'cakranāmnā mayā'; colophon 'tena cakreṇa kṛtaṃ śrīrāmasūnunā'). He cannot be identified further. The mnemonic code he explains (baiṭ/baiṭi/baiḍ) is attributed to the muni Nārada. It records the anuvākas and vākyas of the Taittirīyasaṃhitā in a kaṭapayādi-type syllable notation.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradabaitparibhasa.coverage: complete — The text is complete: all seven paribhāṣā verses, the commentary to its colophon, and the baiṭ strings for all seven kāṇḍas, ending 'iti saptamakāṇḍaṃ samāptam | śrībhaktavatsalaparabrahmaṇe namaḥ'. Some praśnas have no entries, and the text says so explicitly (e.g. 'tṛtīyacaturtthayoḥ praśnayo lakṣyāni na bhavanti').

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradasamhita.title: Nāradasaṃhitā with Saralā
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradasamhita.author: Vasatirāma
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradasamhita.summary: The Nāradasaṃhitā is a Sanskrit astrological treatise belonging to the saṃhitā branch of jyotiṣa, traditionally ascribed to the sage Nārada. It treats planetary motions, calendar cycles, muhūrta for domestic rituals (saṃskāras) and everyday activities, portents (utpāta), weather signs, and related topics. This e-text includes the root verses alongside the Hindi commentary Saralā by Vasatirāma Śarman.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradasamhita.attribution: The root saṃhitā text on jyotiṣa is traditionally attributed to Nārada. The Hindi commentary (bhāṣāṭīkā) named Saralā was written by Paṇḍita Vasatirāma Śarman.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradasamhita.edition: Nāradasaṃhitā (jyotiṣaganthaḥ), berīnivāsi-paṇḍita-vasatirāmaśarmanirmita-bhāṣaṭīkāpetā. Mumbayyāṃ: Khemarāja Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa, Śrīveṅkaṭeśvara (Steam) Mudraṇālaya, Māgha Saṃvat 1963 [/ CE].
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_naradasamhita.coverage: not determined — Root Sanskrit verses and Vasatirāma's Hindi bhāṣāṭīkā, accompanied by publisher advertisements.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padacandrika.title: Padacandrikā
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padacandrika.summary: The Padacandrikā is a metrical Vedāṅga grammatical and phonological handbook belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā) tradition of Yājñavalkya. It explains Vedic accentuation (svara, including the eight svarita types), euphonic combination (sandhi), augment rules, vowel lengthening, and phonological features critical to the recitation and analysis of the Vedic Pada text.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padacandrika.attribution: The opening verse salutes Gaṇeśa (Umāputra), Yājñavalkya, and traditional preceptors, but names no author.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padacandrika.coverage: complete — Complete in 562 lines across multiple topical sections (svara, ākhyātopasarga, visarga, lopāgama, dīrgha, anusvāra, nakāravikārābhāva, halsaṃdhi, svarasaṃdhi), concluding with 'iti grantha samāptā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padakarikaratnamala.title: Padakārikāratnamālā
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padakarikaratnamala.author: Śaṅkarācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padakarikaratnamala.summary: The Padakārikāratnamālā is a technical metrical manual (lakṣaṇagrantha) of the Śukla Yajurveda tradition, dealing with the Kāṇva recension of the Vājasaneyisaṃhitā. Structured in 41 adhyāyas, it provides mnemonic verse rules and counts for padapāṭha characteristics, avagraha and boundary markers (veṣṭana), visarga sandhi, and nasal endings (nānta). The work is traditionally ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_padakarikaratnamala.attribution: Ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya in the opening and chapter colophons; this represents a traditional or pseudepigraphic attribution for a technical lakṣaṇagrantha on Śukla Yajurveda recitation.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_paramalaghumanjusa.title: Paramalaghumañjūṣā (Śaktinirūpaṇa to Tātparyavicāra)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_paramalaghumanjusa.author: Nāgeśabhaṭṭa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_paramalaghumanjusa.summary: The Paramalaghumañjūṣā is Nāgeśabhaṭṭa's briefest handbook summarizing the linguistic and semantic theories developed in his Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntamañjūṣā. This partial text covers the nature of linguistic power (śakti, lakṣaṇā, vyañjanā), the sphoṭa doctrine, and the four traditional requisites for sentential comprehension: mutual expectancy (ākāṅkṣā), semantic fitness (yogyatā), contiguity (āsatti), and speaker intention (tātparya).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_paramalaghumanjusa.attribution: Ascribed to Nāgeśabhaṭṭa, confirmed by the opening verse of the text itself.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_paramalaghumanjusa.coverage: partial — Starts with the maṅgala (verse 1) and ends with 'iti tātparyavicāraḥ'. Section colophons: śaktinirūpaṇa, lakṣaṇā, vyañjanā, sphoṭa, ākāṅkṣā, yogyatā, āsatti, tātparya. The Kiraṇāvalī commentary named in the heading is not included.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_pariskaradarpanah.title: Pariṣkāradarpaṇa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_pariskaradarpanah.author: Veṇīmādhava Śukla
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_pariskaradarpanah.summary: The Pariṣkāradarpaṇa ('Mirror of Refinements') by Veṇīmādhava Śukla is a pedagogical manual of Navya-Nyāya and Navya-Vyākaraṇa analytical techniques (pariṣkāra), written specifically for students of grammar (śābdika). The text provides precise definitions and dialectical distinctions for technical scholastic concepts including viṣayatā, pratiyogitā, anuyogitā, avacchedakatā, paryāpti, kāraṇatā, and the semantic analysis of sentence meaning (śābdabodha).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_pariskaradarpanah.attribution: The author introduces himself in introductory verses 5–6 as a Sarayūpārīṇa brāhmaṇa named Veṇīmādhava Śukla, resident between Kāśī and Prayāga.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_pariskaradarpanah.coverage: unclear — Runs from the opening maṅgalācaraṇa to line 608: 'iti pāribhāṣikaprakaraṇam'. It is unclear whether this constitutes the entire work or only the first section (Pāribhāṣikaprakaraṇa).

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_phitsutrani.title: Phiṭsūtra
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_phitsutrani.author: Śāntanava
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_phitsutrani.summary: The Phiṭsūtra is an auxiliary grammatical treatise comprising 87 sūtras divided across four pādas formulating accentual rules (svara) directly governing nominal stems (phiṭ).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_phitsutrani.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all 4 pādas and 87 sūtras (Pāda 1: 23 sūtras; Pāda 2: 26 sūtras; Pāda 3: 19 sūtras; Pāda 4: 19 sūtras).

SA_GK17_ilx_ws_pingalachandahsutram.title: Chandaḥsūtra
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_pingalachandahsutram.author: Piṅgala
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_pingalachandahsutram.summary: The Chandaḥsūtra of Piṅgala is the foundational classical treatise on Sanskrit metrics (chandas), traditionally classified as the primary surviving manual of the Chandas Vedāṅga. Spanning eight adhyāyas, it systematically treats both Vedic meters (chapters 1–4) and classical meters (laukika chandas, chapters 4–8), covering both syllabic (varṇa) and moraic (mātrā) structures. The concluding section of the eighth adhyāya is renowned for introducing early combinatorial algorithms, binary representation, and prastāra methods.
SA_GK17_ilx_ws_pingalachandahsutram.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 8 adhyāyas (concluding at 8.17: 'parepūrṇaṃ pare pūrṇamiti'), preceded by mnemonic introductory verses on gaṇas.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pindalaksanam.title: Piṇḍalakṣaṇa (fragment)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pindalaksanam.summary: The Piṇḍalakṣaṇa is a short Vedic phonetic treatise (Lakṣaṇa/Śikṣā) examining the pronunciation and tightness of cohesion in consonant clusters (varṇapiṇḍa). It classifies clusters into analogical categories such as ayaḥpiṇḍa (compact like an iron ball), dārupiṇḍa (moderately bound like wood), and tūlapiṇḍa (loosely bound like cotton), depending on whether stops, semivowels, sibilants, or nasals are conjoined. It also details the articulation of clusters containing hakāra, citing traditional Śikṣā rules on chest (urasya) versus guttural (kaṇṭhya) voicing.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pindalaksanam.attribution: Anonymous. The examples ('brahmavādinaḥ', 'caturhotṛṇām', 'prajananaṃ jyotiḥ') and the reference to Gautama's rule ('gautamokteḥ') point to the Taittirīya (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) lakṣaṇa tradition.
