The numbered segments mix rule statements with explanatory prose ('ityarthaḥ', 'atra … viśeṣaḥ'), so the text may be a short lakṣaṇa with an embedded explanation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pindalaksanam.coverage: fragment — 37 short numbered sections. The source itself notes 'mātṛkāyāmapyasaṃpūrṇam' ('also incomplete in the exemplar'). The original extent is unknown.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_plutasiksa.title: Plutaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_plutasiksa.summary: The Plutaśikṣā is a brief phonetic tract (Śikṣā) cataloguing occurrences of protracted vowels (pluta) and nasalized protracted vowels (raṅgapluta), providing mnemonic lists and counts.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_plutasiksa.attribution: A traditional phonetic tract (Śikṣā) transmitted anonymously.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_plutasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete short tract concluding with 'iti pluta śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_prathamatrtiyavarnavibhag.title: Prathamatṛtīyavarṇavibhāgalakṣaṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_prathamatrtiyavarnavibhag.summary: The Prathamatṛtīyavarṇavibhāgalakṣaṇa is a concise five-verse Vedic phonetic tract (lakṣaṇagrantha) designed for oral recitation. It sets out mnemonic rules to distinguish whether a first (voiceless unaspirated, prathama) or third (voiced unaspirated, tṛtīya) consonant within a varga is articulated when conjoined with nasals (vargottama) in specific Vedic mantra occurrences.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_prathamatrtiyavarnavibhag.attribution: A short anonymous phonetic manual (lakṣaṇagrantha) belonging to the auxiliary Vedic phonetic/śikṣā literature, codifying the distinction between first and third stop consonants in nasal clusters.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_prathamatrtiyavarnavibhag.coverage: complete — Complete short text consisting of five verses with an opening heading and concluding colophon.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratijnasutram.title: Pratijñāsūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratijnasutram.author: Kātyāyana
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratijnasutram.summary: The Pratijñāsūtra is a concise phonetical and orthoepic treatise preserved as one of the Pariśiṣṭas attributed to Kātyāyana for the Śukla Yajurveda (Mādhyandina recension). In three brief prose sections, it formulates the core rules governing Vedic accentuation (udātta, anudātta, svarita, and the bhāṣika tone of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa) as well as Mādhyandina-specific pronunciation practices, including the realization of semivowels (such as y as j), retroflex sibilants (ṣ as kh), and anusvāra.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratijnasutram.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short 3-section tract on Vedic accentuation and pronunciation rules for the Mādhyandina school, concluding with 'iti kātyāyanapariśiṣṭapratijñāsūtraṃ samāptam'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_praudhamanorama.title: Prauḍhamanoramā (Saṃjñā- to Avyayībhāvaprakaraṇa)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_praudhamanorama.author: Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_praudhamanorama.summary: The Prauḍhamanoramā is Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita's autocommentary on his Siddhāntakaumudī. This partial digital text comprises the beginning sections up to the conclusion of the Avyayībhāva compounds.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_praudhamanorama.attribution: Autocommentary (svopajñavyākhyā) by Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita on his own Siddhāntakaumudī.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_praudhamanorama.coverage: partial — Contains the text from the opening verse through the Saṃjñā-, Sandhi-, Subanta-, Strīpratyaya-, and Avyayībhāvasamāsa sections (ending at line 1555); Tatpuruṣa, Bahuvrīhi, Dvandva, Taddhita, Tiṅanta, and later sections are absent.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratisakhyapradipasiksa.title: Prātiśākhyapradīpaśikṣā (up to the visargasandhi section)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratisakhyapradipasiksa.author: Bālakṛṣṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratisakhyapradipasiksa.summary: The Prātiśākhyapradīpaśikṣā by Bālakṛṣṇa, son of Sadāśiva, is a Śukla Yajurveda manual of recitation. It brings together rules on Vedic recitation, hand movements, accents (udātta, anudātta, svarita), and sandhi rules up to visarga sandhi.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_pratisakhyapradipasiksa.coverage: partial — The e-text covers the introductory verses, rules on accents, hand movements, and sandhi rules up to visargasandhi, ending with 'iti visargasandhikāryam' (sūtra 54) and 'iti prātiśākhyapradīpa śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paraskaragrhyasutram.title: Pāraskaragṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paraskaragrhyasutram.summary: The Pāraskaragṛhyasūtra is the sole surviving domestic ritual manual (gṛhyasūtra) of the White Yajurveda school. Arranged in three kāṇḍas, it prescribes the full cycle of domestic rites and life-cycle sacraments (saṃskāras)—such as marriage, pregnancy rites, tonsure, upanayana, and samāvartana—as well as domestic daily and seasonal oblations (pākayajñas, śrāddha, and seasonal offerings). The text forms an essential witness to late Vedic domestic ritual and social life.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paraskaragrhyasutram.attribution: Belonging to the White Yajurveda tradition.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paraskaragrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Complete text of the sūtra across 3 kāṇḍas, followed by a brief 3-verse devotional stotra to Yājñavalkya titled Yogīśvaradvādaśanāmāni.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parisiksa.title: Pāriśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parisiksa.summary: The Pāriśikṣā is an anonymous metrical Vedāṅga phonetic treatise associated with the Yajurvedic tradition. Structured across 24 concise chapters containing 146 verses, it details the Yajurvedic phonetic inventory (varṇasamāmnāya, varṇasāra), the places and articulatory efforts (sthāna, karaṇa, prayatna), mora values (mātrā), and esoteric associations such as deities and castes linked to each sound.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parisiksa.attribution: A Yajurvedic phonetic manual transmitted anonymously.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parisiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 24 short adhyāyas comprising 146 verses, ending with 'iti caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ / pāri śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parasarisiksa.title: Pārāśarīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parasarisiksa.summary: The Pārāśarīśikṣā is a metrical Vedāṅga phonetic treatise affiliated with the Śukla Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā). Comprising 160 anuṣṭubh verses, it provides rules for the correct pronunciation and accentuation of Vedic mantras, discussing moraic timing (mātrā), accents (svara), anusvāra, visarga, and euphonic combinations, illustrated by citations from the Mādhyandina school.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parasarisiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Parāśara (cf. verse 1 'pārāśaramataṃ yathā' and verse 160 'iti pārāśareṇoktam').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_parasarisiksa.coverage: complete — 160 verses with the colophon 'iti pārāśarīśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paniniyasiksa.title: Pāṇinīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paniniyasiksa.summary: The Pāṇinīyaśikṣā is the principal Vedāṅga treatise on phonetics and pronunciation associated with the Pāṇinian grammatical tradition. It systematically describes the inventory of 63 or 64 speech sounds (varṇa), the physiology of speech production, places of articulation (sthāna), internal and external effort (prayatna), pitch accents (udātta, anudātta, svarita) and their correlation with musical notes, as well as rules and faults in Vedic recitation. This e-text contains the widely cited vulgate metrical recension in 61 verses.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_paniniyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text of the recension in 61 verses.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaith.title: Rāvaṇabaiṭha
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaith.summary: The Rāvaṇabaiṭha is a concise Vedic auxiliary mnemonic treatise (lakṣaṇa) belonging to the Śukla Yajurveda tradition. It employs coded syllables (kūṭākṣaras) correlated with adhyāya pratīkas (such as 'iṣe tvā', 'āpa undantu', 'devasya tvā') to resolve sixteen types of recitational ambiguities (ṣoḍaśavidhasandehanivartaka) in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā. Verse 7 attributes its compilation to a Vedic scholar named Rāma from Ūruhuḍya.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaith.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to Rāvaṇa by title, but verse 7 mentions composition by a Vedic scholar named Rāma from the settlement Ūruhuḍya (śrīrāmavedaviduṣasganayena tena ... baiṇṇāmalakṣaṇamidaṃ racitaṃ samagram).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaith.coverage: complete — Complete short lakṣaṇa text containing the mnemonic code sequences, concluding with 'iti rāvaṇabaiṇmūlaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaitparibhasa.title: Rāvaṇabaiṭparibhāṣā
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaitparibhasa.summary: The Rāvaṇabaiṭparibhāṣā is a concise 24-verse Lakṣaṇa work from the Taittirīya tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It outlines the technical rules and mnemonic codes (paribhāṣā) for the Rāvaṇabaiṭ system, which catalogs phonetic features, gaṇas, and structural characteristics across the pañcāśats of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā to ensure precise oral recitation and preservation.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_ravanabaitparibhasa.coverage: complete — Complete text of 24 verses and the closing colophon.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samasalaksanam.title: Samāsalakṣaṇa with commentary
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samasalaksanam.author: Ratnamaṇḍanasūri
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samasalaksanam.summary: A concise pedagogical handbook on Sanskrit nominal composition (samāsa) attributed to Ratnamaṇḍanasūri. In six verses accompanied by prose commentary, the treatise defines and illustrates the six traditional varieties of compounds: dvaṃdva, karmadhāraya, bahuvrīhi, tatpuruṣa, avyayībhāva, and dvigu, with practical rules governing case-endings, gender, and number agreement.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samasalaksanam.attribution: Both the kārikās and the brief explanatory commentary are attributed to Ratnamaṇḍanasūri in the colophons.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samasalaksanam.coverage: complete — Complete short treatise of 6 mnemonic kārikās and accompanying prose glosses defining the six classical compound classes (dvaṃdva, karmadhāraya, bahuvrīhi, tatpuruṣa, avyayībhāva, and dvigu), concluding with 'iti ṣaṭsamāsaprakriyā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sarvasammatasiksa.title: Sarvasammataśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sarvasammatasiksa.author: Keśavārya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sarvasammatasiksa.summary: The Sarvasammataśikṣā is a Vedic phonetic manual (śikṣā) affiliated with the Taittirīya tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, authored by Keśavārya, son of Sūryadeva. In 98 kārikās, it synthesizes widely accepted phonological doctrines on consonant gemination (dvitva), euphonic augments (āgama), vowel intrusion (svarabhakti), accents, and the ritual hand movements (hasta) accompanying recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sarvasammatasiksa.attribution: The root treatise is authored by Keśavārya, son of Sūryadeva.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sarvasammatasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 98 verses, ending at verse 98 followed by 'iti sarvasaṃmataśikṣā saṃpūrṇā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_samskararatnamala.title: Saṃskāraratnamālā (part 1)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_samskararatnamala.author: Bhaṭṭagopīnāthadīkṣita
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_samskararatnamala.summary: The Saṃskāraratnamālā by Bhaṭṭagopīnāthadīkṣita Oka is an encyclopedic Dharmaśāstra paddhati detailing the domestic rituals (gṛhyakarmāṇi) and life-cycle rites (saṃskāras) of the Satyāṣāḍha-Hiraṇyakeśi school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It synthesizes earlier sūtras, smṛtis, and paddhatis (notably those of Mahādeva, Maheśa, and Mātṛdatta), supplying extensive ritual directions, mantroha, and legal deliberations. This first volume (pūrvārdha, prakaraṇas 1–17) covers the saṃskāras from garbhādhāna, upanayana, and vivāha through house construction and entry (vāstupraveśa).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_samskararatnamala.attribution: Bhaṭṭagopīnāthadīkṣita Oka, son of Gaṇeśadīkṣita Oka, composed this comprehensive paddhati on the Satyāṣāḍha/Hiraṇyakeśi Gṛhyasūtra.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_samskararatnamala.coverage: partial — Pūrvārdha only (prakaraṇas 1–17), treating the sacraments and household rituals according to the first praśna of the Satyāṣāḍha Gṛhyasūtra, closing with vāstupraveśa.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_siddhantatattvavivekah.title: Siddhāntatattvaviveka with Śeṣavāsanā
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_siddhantatattvavivekah.author: Kamalākara
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_siddhantatattvavivekah.summary: The Siddhāntatattvaviveka is an astronomical treatise completed in 1658 CE (Śaka 1580) by Kamalākara, son of Nṛsiṃha Daivajña. Written partly in opposition to Munīśvara, the treatise discusses astronomical mathematics, spheres, and planetary theory while engaging with Yavanamata (Persian/Arabic astronomy). The appended Śeṣavāsanā is the author's own supplementary exposition.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_siddhantatattvavivekah.attribution: Kamalākara composed the treatise in Śaka 1580 (1658 CE) and also composed the Śeṣavāsanā.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_siddhantatattvavivekah.edition: Siddhāntatattvaviveka, Kamalākara Bhaṭṭa, with Śeṣavāsanā, edited by Sudhākara Dvivedī (Sudhākara Dube), Benares Sanskrit Series (BSS), 1885.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_siddhantatattvavivekah.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Siddhāntatattvaviveka across all adhikāras, followed by the complete Śeṣavāsanā.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_siddhantasiksa.title: Siddhāntaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_siddhantasiksa.author: Śrīnivāsamakhin
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_siddhantasiksa.summary: The Siddhāntaśikṣā is a versified phonetical and orthoepic manual (śikṣā) associated with the Vedic tradition, authored by Śrīnivāsamakhin in 74 verses.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_siddhantasiksa.attribution: The introductory and concluding verses explicitly name Śrīnivāsamakhin (Śrīnivāsādhvarin) as the author of the 74 kārikās.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_siddhantasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 74 numbered verses, matching verse 74 (ślokāḥ siddhāntaśikṣāyāṃ catuḥsaptatirīritāḥ) and the closing colophon iti siddhāntaśikṣā samāptā.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarabhaktilaksanaparisis.title: Svarabhaktilakṣaṇapariśiṣṭaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarabhaktilaksanaparisis.summary: The Svarabhaktilakṣaṇapariśiṣṭaśikṣā is a brief Vedic phonetic manual (śikṣā/pariśiṣṭa) in 42 anuṣṭubh stanzas associated with the Śukla Yajurveda (Mādhyandina school). It systematically describes the eight varieties of Vedic accents and hiatus (vivṛtti), consonant recitation rules and gemination, and classifies the varieties of anaptyxis/epenthesis (svarabhakti) when liquids (r, l) are followed by spirants.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarabhaktilaksanaparisis.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Kātyāyana, as stated in verse 42 ('iti kāttyāyanenaiva pariśiṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ mudā') and in the concluding colophon.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarabhaktilaksanaparisis.coverage: complete — Complete in 42 anuṣṭubh verses and the final closing colophon.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarapancasat.title: Svarapañcāśat
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarapancasat.summary: The Svarapañcāśat is a concise versified manual (52 kārikās) outlining the rules of Vedic accentuation (svaralakṣaṇa) for the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It systematically details the conditions for udātta, anudātta, and svarita accents, covering cases of multiple udāttas in compounds, verb accentuation (tiṅanta), enclitics, avagraha, and specific accents in texts such as the Āruṇopaniṣad.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarapancasat.attribution: A traditional anonymous metrical manual (svaralakṣaṇa) summarizing accentuation rules for the Taittirīya tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarapancasat.coverage: complete — Complete text in 52 verses with section headings and final colophon 'iti svarapañcāśat'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svaravyanjanasiksa.title: Svaravyañjanaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svaravyanjanasiksa.summary: The Svaravyañjanaśikṣā is a short anonymous śikṣā in six vargas on distinguishing vocalic ṛ (svara) from consonantal r + i (vyañjana, e.g. ri-, krimi-, tri-) and related repha phenomena in Vedic recitation, listing the words concerned (riśādas-, ripu-, krimi-, triṣṭubh- etc.) and the conditions (accent, sandhi, svarabhakti) under which each is pronounced.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svaravyanjanasiksa.attribution: Traditional anonymous Śikṣā treatise dealing with Vedic phonetics.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svaravyanjanasiksa.coverage: complete — Six vargas (colophons iti prathamo … ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ) ending with 'svaravyañjanaśikṣā samāptā'; the 5th and 6th vargas are partly prose-like and textually corrupt.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarasiksa.title: Svaraśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarasiksa.summary: The Svaraśikṣā is a short Vedic phonetic treatise (śikṣā) in 35 verses dedicated to accentuation (svara). It defines the primary accents—udātta, anudātta, svarita, and pracaya—along with their physiological correlates, deity associations, hand-gesture markers (hastasvara), and the classical varieties of the svarita accent (jātya, kṣaipra, abhinihita, praśliṣṭa, etc.). It emphasizes the grave consequences of faulty recitation and the ritual merit of accurate accentuation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarasiksa.attribution: Anonymous. The opening verse announces a 'svarasaṃgraha' ('praṇamya vedapuruṣaṃ vakṣyāmi svarasaṃgṛhaḥ' [svarasaṃgraham]); the colophon names it 'svaraśikṣā'.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete in 35 metrical verses (stanzas 1–35) with opening line and closing colophon (iti svaraśikṣā samāptā).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarankusasiksa.title: Svarāṅkuśaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarankusasiksa.author: Jayantasvāmin
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarankusasiksa.summary: The Svarāṅkuśaśikṣā is a short Vedāṅga phonetic treatise attributed to Jayantasvāmin, designed for the use of reciters of the Ṛgveda (Bahvṛc). In 22 verses, it details the classification of Vedic pitch accents (svara), focusing extensively on varieties of the circumflex accent (svarita)—such as jātya, abhinihita, kṣaipra, praśliṣṭa, tairovyañjana, tairovirāma, and pādavṛtta—as well as rules concerning accentual tremor (kampa).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarankusasiksa.attribution: Ascribed to Jayantasvāmin in verse 22 and the final colophon; designated specifically for the recitation tradition of the Ṛgveda (Bahvṛc).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarankusasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete: maṅgala (heramba caṇḍikāṃ dhyātvā …) to v. 22, which states that Jayantasvāmin taught 21 ślokas named Svarāṅkuśā for the Bahvṛcas, followed by the colophon 'iti śrī jayantasvāmiproktā svarāṅkuśā śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakam.title: Svarāṣṭaka
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakam.summary: The Svarāṣṭaka is a short metrical Vedāṅga (śikṣā) tract consisting of eight instructional verses on the mechanics of Vedic pitch accentuation and a final phalaśruti. It defines the occurrence of udātta, nihata (anudātta), and svāra (svarita) in single words and compounds, distinguishes prākṛta from aprākṛta svarita, and describes pracaya and kampita tone variations.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakam.coverage: complete — Complete in 9 verses (8 instructional verses plus 1 phalaśruti verse), concluded by 'iti svarāṣṭakaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakasiksa.title: Svarāṣṭakaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakasiksa.summary: The Svarāṣṭakaśikṣā is a short phonetic manual (śikṣā) preserved in the tradition of the Śukla Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā). In eight brief sections, it outlines vocalic sandhi (acsandhi), Vedic accentuation (udātta, anudātta, svarita, pracaya) along with hand/body positions for recitation, consonantal and visarga sandhi rules, and concludes with the fourteen Śivasūtras.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakasiksa.attribution: A compendium of eight phonetic and sandhi sections associated with the Śukla Yajurveda tradition. A colophon attributes a section to Ananta (ityanantakṛto halsandhiḥ).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_svarastakasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text across eight short sections, ending with the colophon 'iti svarāṣṭakaṃ sampūrṇam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedapratisakhyam.title: Puṣpasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedapratisakhyam.summary: The Puṣpasūtra (also known as the Sāmavedaprātiśākhya / Sāmaprātiśākhya) is a phonological and melodic treatise associated with the Sāmaveda in ten prapāṭhakas.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedapratisakhyam.attribution: Ascribed in the opening to Puṣparṣi ('puṣparṣipraṇītam').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedapratisakhyam.coverage: complete — Complete in 10 prapāṭhakas, concluding with 'iti puṣpasūtredaśamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ / puṣpasūtraṃ samāptam / iti sāmaveda prātiśākhyaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedasaptalaksanam.title: Sāmavedasaptalakṣaṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedasaptalaksanam.summary: The Sāmavedasaptalakṣaṇa ('Saptalakṣaṇa') is a metrical collection of seven lakṣaṇa treatises auxiliary to the Sāmaveda padapāṭha, cataloguing words subject to particular sandhi phenomena: visarga elision (Śamāna, with notes on visarga retention and the nasal raṅga), e/ai-final words (Viliṅghya), n-final words before n- (Napara), t-final words (Tapara), shortened vowels (Hrasvasaṃgrahaṇa), word-initial a-vowels (Avarṇi) and words without avagraha (Anavagrahalakṣaṇa). Each rule is illustrated by mnemonic lists of Sāmaveda word forms with counts of the sūtras covered.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedasaptalaksanam.attribution: Anonymous compilation of Sāmavedic padapāṭha/saṃhitā lakṣaṇas.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samavedasaptalaksanam.coverage: complete — Seven treatises with continuous verse numbering 1–138, each closed by its own colophon, ending with the collection colophon 'saptalakṣaṇanāmāyaṃ granthaḥ samāptimagamat'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_saradipikavya.title: Sāramañjarī with Sāradīpikā
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_saradipikavya.author: Jayakṛṣṇa, Kālīpada Tarkācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_saradipikavya.summary: Sāramañjarī is a grammatical treatise elucidated by the Sāradīpikā commentary of Kālīpada Tarkācārya, discussing grammatical semantics, verbal cognition (śābdabodha), compound meaning (samāsa), and case syntax.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_saradipikavya.attribution: The commentary Sāradīpikā on the Sāramañjarī was authored by Kālīpada Tarkācārya (Śrīkālīpadaśarman), son of Haridāsa of Koṭālipāra.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_saradipikavya.coverage: complete — Complete e-text of the commentary ending with the closing colophon.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_asubodhavidya.title: Sāramañjarīvyākhyā
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_asubodhavidya.author: Āśubodha Vidyābhūṣaṇa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_asubodhavidya.summary: A Sanskrit commentary by Āśubodha Vidyābhūṣaṇa on Jayakṛṣṇa Tarkālaṅkāra's Sāramañjarī. The commentary explains the root text's definitions of time (kāla) and the meanings of the lakāras, the kārakas (e.g. adhikaraṇa), the types of compounds (tatpuruṣa, karmadhāraya, dvigu, bahuvrīhi, dvandva) and the functions of words. It cites the Mahābhāṣya, Hari (Bhartṛhari), Durga and lexicographical statements.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_asubodhavidya.attribution: Root text: the Sāramañjarī of Jayakṛṣṇa Tarkālaṅkāra. The commentator gives the author's name as 'tarkālaṅkāropādhikena jayakṛṣṇaśarmmaṇā'. Commentary: Āśubodha Vidyābhūṣaṇa.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_saramanjari_asubodhavidya.coverage: complete — The full commentary, from the opening verses (1–4) to the colophon 'iti śrī āśubodhavidyābhūṣaṇaviracitā sāramañjarīvyākhyā samāptā'. Topics run from kāla and lakāra through kāraka and samāsa to śabdavṛtti and saṅkhyā. The root Sāramañjarī itself is not included (lemmata only).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_taittariyapratisakhyam.title: Taittirīyaprātiśākhya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_taittariyapratisakhyam.summary: The Taittirīyaprātiśākhya is the phonological and phonetic treatise belonging to the Taittirīya recension. In 24 adhyāyas, it provides detailed rules on phonetic inventory, euphonic combination (sandhi), accentuation (svara), moric quantity, and pronunciation necessary to transition between the continuous saṃhitāpāṭha and the uncombined padapāṭha. It cites numerous early phoneticians, including Pauṣkarasādi, Plākṣi, and Vālmīki.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_taittariyapratisakhyam.attribution: Ascribed to the Taittirīya śākhā; no individual author is preserved by tradition, though early phoneticians are cited throughout the text.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_taittariyapratisakhyam.coverage: complete — Complete root text in 24 adhyāyas (sūtras only, without commentary).

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_tattvaprabhavali.title: Tattvaprabhāvalī (Pramāṇakhaṇḍa: Śabdapramāṇa)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_tattvaprabhavali.author: Śrīkṛṣṇavallabhācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_tattvaprabhavali.summary: A philosophical treatise in verse and auto-commentary expounding epistemology and ontology from a Navya-Nyāya standpoint. This excerpt from the Pramāṇakhaṇḍa covers verbal testimony (śabdapramāṇa), discussing the nature of sound, semantic power (śakti), metaphor (lakṣaṇā), divine will (īśvarecchā), affixes, particles, and syntactic-semantic cognition (śābdabodha).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_tattvaprabhavali.coverage: excerpt — Contains only the Śabdapramāṇa section of the Pramāṇakhaṇḍa, consisting of verses 472–485 and intervening prose commentary discussing Navya-Nyāya semantics, grammar, and epistemology.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_uccodarki.title: Uccodarki
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_uccodarki.author: Keśavācārya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_uccodarki.summary: The Uccodarki (also referred to as Uccodarkidaśaślokī) is a short metrical treatise (lakṣaṇagrantha) belonging to the phonetic and accentual tradition of the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Attributed to Keśavācārya, it provides mnemonic rules for identifying instances where an udātta (ucca) tone follows a svarita and outlines the corresponding hand positions (hastavinyāsa) used in traditional recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_uccodarki.attribution: The colophon states: 'iti śrī keśavācāryaviracitamuccodarki saṃpūrṇam'. Verse 12 names the work as Uccodarkidaśaślokī in connection with Keśavācārya.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_uccodarki.coverage: complete — Complete short metrical lakṣaṇa tract of 12 verses with introductory line and closing colophon.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_upasargavrttih.title: Upasargavṛtti
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_upasargavrttih.author: Candragomin
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_upasargavrttih.summary: The Upasargavṛtti (also known as Viṃśatyupasargavṛtti) is an accessory grammatical treatise belonging to the Cāndravyākaraṇa tradition of Candragomin. It opens with an introductory verse cataloguing twenty verbal prefixes (upasarga) and methodically enumerates the semantic functions and shades of meaning associated with each prefix, providing concise illustrative examples for each usage.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_upasargavrttih.attribution: Ascribed to the Buddhist scholar-grammarian Candragomin as an auxiliary treatise to the Cāndravyākaraṇa. The work was translated into Tibetan (Toh 4270 / Otani 5768) by Jetakarṇa and Ñi ma rgyal mtshan.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_upasargavrttih.coverage: complete — Complete text covering all twenty verbal prefixes (upasarga) in 20 numbered sections from pra to upa, ending with the colophon 'iti upasargavṛttiḥ samāptā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_unadikosah.title: Uṇādisūtra with Uṇādikośa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_unadikosah.author: Dayānanda Sarasvatī
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_unadikosah.summary: The Uṇādikośa of Svāmī Dayānanda Sarasvatī is a Sanskrit commentary on the Pañcapādī recension of the Uṇādisūtras. It explains the morphological derivation of irregular primary nominal stems from verbal roots using uṇādi suffixes, referencing relevant Aṣṭādhyāyī rules and providing grammatical, semantic, and Vedic vs. classical glosses.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_unadikosah.attribution: The root Pañcapādī Uṇādisūtras belong to the classical Pāṇinian auxiliary corpus. The commentary, entitled Uṇādikośa or Uṇādivyākhyā (Vaidikalaukikakoṣa), was composed by Svāmī Dayānanda Sarasvatī.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_unadikosah.coverage: complete — Complete across all 5 pādas of the Pañcapādī recension of the Uṇādisūtras, ending with pāda 5, sūtra 70 ('maṅgeralac' / 'maṅgalam') and closing verse/colophon.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaidyanathabaith.title: Lakṣaṇaratna
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaidyanathabaith.author: Vaidyanātha Bhaṭṭa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaidyanathabaith.summary: The Lakṣaṇaratna of Vaidyanātha Bhaṭṭa is a Vedic lakṣaṇa treatise of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā tradition (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda). It establishes mnemonic varṇa sequences encoding structural, phonological, and orthographical features across each anuvāka and pañcāśat, including pragrahavyavasthā, visarga counts, and padapāṭha characteristics.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaidyanathabaith.attribution: Attributed to Vaidyanātha Bhaṭṭa in the introductory paribhāṣā and concluding colophons.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaidyanathabaith.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising the introductory Paribhāṣā (segments 1–13) and mnemonic code tables for the Taittirīya Saṃhitā through to the final colophon (segment 59).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vaikhanasasrautasutram.title: Vaikhānasaśrautasūtra (praśna 13: Pravargya)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vaikhanasasrautasutram.summary: The Vaikhānasaśrautasūtra is a ritual manual belonging to the Vaikhānasa school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. This e-text comprises Praśna 13, which is devoted to the Pravargya ceremony, detailing the preparation and baking of the Mahāvīra vessel, the heating of the milk offering (gharma), and the concluding udvāsana disposal rites.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vaikhanasasrautasutram.edition: W. Caland (ed.), Vaikhānasa-Śrautasūtram: The Description of the Vedic Rites according to the Vaikhānasa School belonging to the Black Yajurveda, Calcutta: Royal Asiatic Society of Bengal, 1941 (Bibliotheca Indica 265). (probable)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vaikhanasasrautasutram.coverage: partial — Contains only the 13th praśna (sections 1–18) of the Vaikhānasaśrautasūtra.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vaiyakaramasiddhantalaghu.title: Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntalaghumañjūṣākuñjikā (part 1)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vaiyakaramasiddhantalaghu.author: Durbalācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vaiyakaramasiddhantalaghu.summary: The Kuñjikā is a Sanskrit commentary on Nāgeśabhaṭṭa's Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntalaghumañjūṣā. This first part explains discussions of the sentence (vākya), signification, sphoṭa, and related grammatical and ontological doctrines.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vaiyakaramasiddhantalaghu.attribution: A commentary (Kuñjikā / dīkā) on the Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntalaghumañjūṣā.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vaiyakaramasiddhantalaghu.coverage: partial — First part of the Kuñjikā: from the opening maṅgala through the discussions of vākya, śakti, lakṣaṇā, vyañjanā, sphoṭa and related topics up to guṇa and dravya. It ends without a colophon.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah.title: Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā with Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah.author: Bhaṭṭojīdīkṣita, Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah.summary: The Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra is an influential 17th-century treatise on semantic theory and linguistic philosophy in the Pāṇinian school by Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa. It serves as an abridgement of his larger Bṛhadvaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa, commenting on the 74 kārikās of the Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā composed by his uncle Bhaṭṭojīdīkṣita. The work systematically articulates and defends the grammarians' semantic doctrines regarding the meaning of verbal roots (dhātvartha), suffixes (tiṅartha, kṛdartha), nominal cases (subartha), compounds (samāsa), and sphoṭa against the opposing positions of the Nyāya and Mīmāṃsā traditions.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah.attribution: The 74 root verses were composed by Bhaṭṭojīdīkṣita (early 17th century). The explanatory commentary was authored by his nephew Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa, son of Raṅgoji Bhaṭṭa, as an abridgement of his own larger Bṛhadvaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 74 kārikās of the Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā and Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's commentary thereon, ending with the Sphoṭavāda section.
translations: Joshi, Shivaram Dattatray. 'Kauṇḍa Bhaṭṭa on the Meaning of Sanskrit Verbs (1).' Saṃbhāṣā: Nagoya Studies in Indian Culture and Buddhism. (English)

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_d.title: Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra with Darpaṇa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_d.author: Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa, Harivallabha
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_d.summary: The Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra is Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's (17th century) condensation of his larger commentary, the Bṛhadvaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa, expounding the 74 grammatical-philosophical kārikās (Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā) of his uncle Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita. It constitutes a foundational treatise of the Navya-Vyākaraṇa school of linguistic philosophy, systematically articulating semantic theories regarding verbal roots, affixes, case endings, compounds, and the doctrine of sphoṭa in vigorous polemic with Nyāya and Mīmāṃsā. This digital edition presents Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's treatise accompanied throughout by Harivallabha's Darpaṇa commentary.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_d.attribution: Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra is Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's own abridgment of his Bṛhadvaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇa (commenting on Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita's 74 Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikās). The Darpaṇa commentary is by Harivallabha, son of Śrīvallabha of Kūrmācala (Kumaon).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_d.coverage: complete — Complete text encompassing all 14 sections from Dhātvarthanirūpaṇa through to Sphoṭavāda, concluding with Harivallabha's concluding verses and the colophon 'iti śrīmatkūrmacalābhijanotprabhātīyopanāmakaśrīvallabhā''tmajaharivallabhaviracite bhūṣaṇasāradarppaṇe sphoṭavādaḥ samāptaḥ'.
translations: Shivaram Dattatray Joshi, 'Kauṇḍa Bhaṭṭa on the Meaning of Sanskrit Verbs (1)', in Nagoya Studies in Indian Culture and Buddhism: Saṃbhāṣā. (English)

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_k.title: Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra with Kāśikā
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_k.author: Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa, Harirāma
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_k.summary: The Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra is Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's (17th c.) auto-abridgment and concise commentary on the 74 verses (Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā) of his uncle Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita. It provides a foundational exposition of Pāṇinian philosophy of language, analyzing the semantic roles of verbal roots, affixes, nominal inflections, and compounds, alongside discussions on sentence cognition and sphoṭa in debate with Naiyāyika and Mīmāṃsaka positions. This e-text also contains the Kāśikā sub-commentary composed by Harirāma Kāla in 1797 CE.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_k.attribution: The Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra was written by Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa (17th c.) expounding the 74 kārikās of his uncle Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita. The Kāśikā commentary was composed by Harirāma Kāla (son of Keśava Dīkṣita and Sakhīdevī) in Vikrama Saṃvat 1854 (1797 CE) in Vārāṇasī.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_k.coverage: complete — Complete text across the 74 kārikā discussions with Harirāma's commentary Kāśikā, ending with the commentator's praśasti and chronogram verses indicating completion in VS 1854.
translations: S. D. Joshi, 'Kauṇḍa Bhaṭṭa on the Meaning of Sanskrit Verbs (1)', Saṃbhāṣā (Nagoya Studies in Indian Culture and Buddhism). (English)

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_s.title: Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā with Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra and Śāṅkarī
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_s.author: Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita, Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa, Śaṅkara Śāstrin
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_s.summary: The Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra is Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa's seventeenth-century treatise commenting on Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita's Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā. It provides an exposition of Pāṇinian philosophy of language, discussing verbal roots (dhātvartha), case relations, and sphoṭa, engaging with Naiyāyika and Mīmāṃsaka positions. This text is accompanied by the Śāṅkarī sub-commentary of Śaṅkara Śāstrin and appends the Sphoṭacandrikā by Śrīkṛṣṇa Bhaṭṭa Mauni.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_s.attribution: Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita authored the root kārikās (Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakārikā). Raṅgojībhaṭṭa's son Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa composed the commentary Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra. The Śāṅkarī commentary is by Śaṅkara Śāstrin (son of Raṅgabhaṭṭa). The terminal treatise Sphoṭacandrikā is by Śrīkṛṣṇa Bhaṭṭa Mauni (son of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa).
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_s.edition: Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra of Kauṇḍabhaṭṭa, with Sphoṭacandrikā by Śrīkṛṣṇa Bhaṭṭa, edited by Vindhyeśvarīprasāda Dvivedin and Gaṇapati Śāstrī Mokāte.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranabhusanasarah_s.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Vaiyākaraṇabhūṣaṇasāra with Śāṅkarīvyākhyā, concluding with the complete Sphoṭacandrikā.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranasiddhantamanju.title: Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntamañjūṣā
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranasiddhantamanju.author: Nāgeśabhaṭṭa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranasiddhantamanju.summary: The Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntamañjūṣā (commonly referred to as Bṛhanmañjūṣā to distinguish it from the Laghu- and Paramalaghu-mañjūṣā) is Nāgeśabhaṭṭa's masterwork on the philosophy of language and semantic theory in the Pāṇinian tradition. It systematically investigates word meaning, communicative functions (śakti, lakṣaṇā, vyañjanā), verbal roots, morphemes, case relations, and sentential comprehension, critically engaging the positions of Nyāya and Mīmāṃsā. The treatise concludes with a rigorous exposition of the sphoṭa doctrine as the ontological core of meaningful language.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranasiddhantamanju.attribution: Composed by Nāgeśabhaṭṭa (18th century CE), son of Śivabhaṭṭa. He explicitly identifies himself and his father in the final colophon and verses.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_vaiyakaranasiddhantamanju.coverage: complete — Complete text of the work (Bṛhanmañjūṣā), preceded by a detailed table of contents (anukramaṇikā, segments 0–185); printed footnotes and manuscript variant readings (e.g., 'kha. pustake') are incorporated inline into the e-text.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vararucisiksa.title: Vararuciśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vararucisiksa.author: Vararuci
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vararucisiksa.summary: The Vararuciśikṣā is a metrical Vedāṅga treatise on Vedic phonetics and orthoepy comprising 129 verses, traditionally attributed to Vararuci. It discusses moraic quantities (mātrā), rules of svarabhakti (anaptyxis), sandhi, phonetic effort, and accentuation (svara), with specific citations of recitation practices across Vedic traditions such as the Kāṭhaka.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vararucisiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text in 129 verses, concluding with 'iti vararuciśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_varnasiksa.title: Varṇaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_varnasiksa.summary: The Varṇaśikṣā is a short Sanskrit treatise of 48 verses cataloguing the esoteric and symbolic dimensions of the Sanskrit alphabet (varṇas). It systematically classifies vowels and consonants according to grammatical gender (masculine, feminine, neuter), the three guṇas (sattva, rajas, tamas), symbolic colors, and presiding deities or tantric bījas.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_varnasiksa.attribution: Traditional anonymous phonetico-esoteric treatise classified under the Śikṣā (Vedāṅga) / mātṛkā literature.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_varnasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text in 48 verses, ending with the colophon 'iti varṇaśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vedaparibhasakarikasiksa.title: Vedaparibhāṣākārikāśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vedaparibhasakarikasiksa.author: Rāmacandra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vedaparibhasakarikasiksa.summary: The Vedaparibhāṣākārikāśikṣā is a brief 11-verse manual belonging to the Mādhyandina branch of the Śukla Yajurveda. Composed by Rāmacandra, son of Siddheśvara, it sets forth mnemonics and paribhāṣā rules for counting words (padas), identifying avagraha, and classifying final consonants and visarga across the anuvākas of the Mādhyandina Saṃhitā.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vedaparibhasakarikasiksa.attribution: Attributed in the concluding colophon to Rāmacandra, son of Siddheśvara (paṇḍitasiddheśvarasūnu paṇḍitarāmacandra).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vedaparibhasakarikasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete 11-verse manual including introductory statement and final colophon.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_visargangulipradarsanapra.title: Visargāṅgulipradarśanaprakāra (excerpt)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_visargangulipradarsanapra.summary: A short anonymous śikṣā/prayoga tract on Vedic recitation, apparently on how the visarga is pronounced and shown with finger gestures (aṅguli-pradarśana) during recitation, including in the ghana mode. The e-text gives only the opening passage (the visarga before a vowel is not to be pronounced like h) and the closing passage (the definition of ghanapāṭha) with the colophon, so the full content of the work cannot be judged from it.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_visargangulipradarsanapra.coverage: excerpt — The e-text gives only two short passages, headed 'prathamaḥ ślokaḥ' (opening: on pronouncing the visarga before a vowel, not as h) and 'antimaḥ ślokaḥ' (closing: the definition of ghanapāṭha, illustrated with 'dasrā yuvākavaḥ sutāḥ'), followed by the colophon 'iti visargāṅgulipradarśanaprakāraḥ samāptaḥ'. The phrase 'ityādiśeṣaṃ jyotsnā viśujjñeyam' shows that the rest is omitted. The body of the work is not reproduced, and its full extent is unknown.

SA_GSD36_ilx_ws_visvamitrasmrtih.title: Viśvāmitrasmṛti
SA_GSD36_ilx_ws_visvamitrasmrtih.summary: The Viśvāmitrasmṛti is a metrical Dharmaśāstra text in eight chapters attributed to the Vedic sage Viśvāmitra. It functions primarily as an āhnika manual focusing on daily domestic rites and duties for twice-born householders, including purification, morning and evening sandhyopāsanā, gāyatrī japa, devapūjā, and vaiśvadeva offerings.
SA_GSD36_ilx_ws_visvamitrasmrtih.attribution: Attributed traditionally to the sage Viśvāmitra.
SA_GSD36_ilx_ws_visvamitrasmrtih.coverage: complete — Complete in 8 adhyāyas (vaiśvadevaprakaraṇa ending at chapter 8).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalasiksa.title: Vyālaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalasiksa.summary: The Vyālaśikṣā is a concise Vedāṅga metrical manual of 12 verses setting forth rules for Vedic modification chants (vikṛtipāṭha) in accordance with the tradition of sage Vyāla. It defines the order, repetition, and reversal of words in recitation patterns including jaṭā, mālā, daṇḍa, ratha, and ghana.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalasiksa.attribution: Traditional attribution to sage Vyāla; verse 1 explicitly frames the treatise as following the view of muni Vyāla ('atha śikṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi vyālamaunimatānugām').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete 12-verse tract defining vikṛti recitation modes, concluding with 'iti vyālaśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalisiksa.title: Vyāliśikṣā with Aṣṭavikṛtivivṛti
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalisiksa.author: Vyāḍi, Madhusūdana
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalisiksa.summary: The e-text contains metrical instruction on Vedic recitation (vikṛtipāṭha). The opening Vyāliśikṣā deals with ghana recitation (number of sandhis and padas), followed by verses detailing rules on vikṛtis, reverse order (vyutkrama), pragṛhya vowels, and sandhi, concluding with descriptions of the eight vikṛtis and a colophon attributing the treatise (Aṣṭauvikṛtivivaraṇa) to Madhusūdana.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalisiksa.attribution: The Vyāliśikṣā's attribution to Vyāḍi (Vyāli) is based on the title; the text states: 'vyāliśikṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi brahmaṇānumataḥ purā sahasravadanenāhaṃ'. The second work is by Madhusūdana according to its colophon ('iti śrīmadhusūdanaviracitāṣṭauvikṛtivivaraṇaṃ samāptam').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyalisiksa.coverage: complete — Vyāliśikṣā vv. 1–8 with continuation, concluding with Madhusūdana's treatise through v. 54 and colophon.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyasasiksa.title: Vyāsaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyasasiksa.summary: The Vyāsaśikṣā is a prominent phonetic manual (śikṣā) belonging to the Taittirīya śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Arranged in 28 sections (prakaraṇas) comprising 525 verses, it details rules of accentuation (svara), sandhi, consonant gemination (dvitva), and recitation modes (pada, krama, and jaṭā) characteristic of the Taittirīya textual tradition. It shares a deep structural relationship with the Taittirīya Prātiśākhya.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyasasiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Vyāsa (cf. closing verse 525: śrīvyāsakaṇṭhaprasṛtāñca śikṣām).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vyasasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete root text in 28 prakaraṇas and 525 numbered verses, concluding with the uccāraṇaphalaprakaraṇam.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vadarthasamgrahah_dvitiya.title: Vādārthasaṃgraha (part 2: Sphoṭatattvanirūpaṇa, Sphoṭacandrikā, Prātipadikasaṃjñāvāda, Vākyavāda with Vākyadīpikā)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vadarthasamgrahah_dvitiya.author: Śeṣakṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa Mauni, Nārāyaṇa Goḍabole, Hariyaśomiśra
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vadarthasamgrahah_dvitiya.summary: The second volume of M. G. Bākre's anthology of short Vyākaraṇa treatises (vāda). It contains Śeṣakṛṣṇa's Sphoṭatattvanirūpaṇa, which defends the indivisible sentence-sphoṭa in kārikās with prose explanation, and Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa Mauni's Sphoṭacandrikā. It also contains Nārāyaṇa Goḍabole's Prātipadikasaṃjñāvāda on the definition of the nominal stem, and a Vākyavāda on the definition of the sentence with Hariyaśomiśra's commentary Vākyadīpikā, which discusses verbal cognition, negation and number.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vadarthasamgrahah_dvitiya.attribution: Anthology edited by Mahādeva Gaṅgādhara Bākre. The colophons name: Śeṣakṛṣṇa; Śrīkṛṣṇa (Kṛṣṇabhaṭṭa Mauni); Nārāyaṇa of the Goḍabole family; and Hariyaśomiśra, associated with king Udayasiṃha. The Vākyadīpikā was written by Hariyaśomiśra.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vadarthasamgrahah_dvitiya.edition: Vādārthasaṃgrahaḥ, dvitīyo bhāgaḥ, ed. Mahādeva Gaṅgādhara Bākre, Bombay, 1913. (probable)
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vadarthasamgrahah_dvitiya.coverage: complete — Texts of volume 2 as transcribed, ending with Hariyaśomiśra's Vākyadīpikā colophon. The text has heavy keying corruption.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vakyapadiyam_savrtti.title: Vākyapadīya with Vṛtti, Puṇyarāja's commentary, and Helarāja's Prakīrṇakaprakāśa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vakyapadiyam_savrtti.author: Bhartṛhari, Puṇyarāja, Helarāja
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vakyapadiyam_savrtti.summary: The Vākyapadīya by Bhartṛhari is the foundational treatise of the philosophy of grammar (Vyākaraṇadarśana) and classical Indian semantic theory. Comprising three books—Brahmakāṇḍa (on Śabdabrahman and the metaphysics of language), Vākyakāṇḍa (on sentence-meaning wholism and the sphoṭa doctrine), and Padakāṇḍa or Prakīrṇaka (fourteen specialized treatises exploring universals, particulars, relations, time, action, and case-roles)—it articulates a non-dualist linguistic philosophy that shaped subsequent debates across Buddhist, Mīmāṃsā, and Nyāya traditions. This e-text contains the complete kārikās across all three books together with their principal classical Sanskrit commentaries.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vakyapadiyam_savrtti.attribution: The root kārikās are by Bhartṛhari. The ancient Vṛtti is traditionally ascribed either to Bhartṛhari himself (svopajñā vṛtti) or to Harivṛṣabha. The commentary on Kāṇḍa 3 is by Helarāja (son of Bhūtirāja).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_vakyapadiyam_savrtti.coverage: complete — Complete across all three kāṇḍas: Kāṇḍa 1 (Brahmakāṇḍa / Āgamasamuccaya), Kāṇḍa 2 (Vākyakāṇḍa), and Kāṇḍa 3 (Padakāṇḍa / Prakīrṇaka, 14 samuddeśas, ending at the colophon of the Vṛttisamuddeśa).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vasisthisiksa.title: Vāsiṣṭhīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vasisthisiksa.summary: The Vāsiṣṭhīśikṣā is an ancillary text of the Śukla Yajurveda (Mādhyandina) that, 'according to the view of Vasiṣṭha', classifies the mantras of each of the forty adhyāyas of the Vājasaneyisaṃhitā as ṛc (metrical) or yajus (prose), giving counts per adhyāya and final totals of 1467 ṛcs and 2823 yajus.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vasisthisiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Vasiṣṭha or representing his school's doctrine ('vāsiṣṭhasya mataṃ yathā').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_vasisthisiksa.coverage: complete — Adhyāya-by-adhyāya classification of ṛc and yajus mantras for all 40 adhyāyas of the Vājasaneyisaṃhitā, closing with the totals (1467 ṛcs, 2823 yajus) and the colophon 'iti ṛgyajuḥvibhāgātmikā vāsiṣṭhī śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GS38_ilx_ws_vastuvidya.title: Vāstuvidyā
SA_GS38_ilx_ws_vastuvidya.summary: The Vāstuvidyā is a classical Sanskrit manual on domestic architecture and civil construction representing the regional architectural tradition of Kerala. In sixteen chapters, it covers units of measurement, requirements for craftsmen and architects (sthapati, sūtragrāhin, takṣaka, vardhakin), site selection and soil examination (bhūmiparīkṣā), the vāstupuruṣamaṇḍala, orientation of residences, layout of hall houses (śālā), joinery and timber examination, and the fabrication and firing of roofing tiles and clay elements (mṛlloṣṭalakṣaṇa).
SA_GS38_ilx_ws_vastuvidya.attribution: The work opens with salutations to Ganeśa, Sarasvatī, and Viśvakarman (vv. 1.1–2); no individual author attribution is recorded in the text or colophons.
SA_GS38_ilx_ws_vastuvidya.coverage: complete — Complete in 16 adhyāyas, terminating at chapter 16 colophon: 'iti vāstuvidyāyāṃ mṛloṭalakṣaṇaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ | vāstuvidyā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajurvedasaptalaksanam.title: Yajurvedasaptalakṣaṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajurvedasaptalaksanam.summary: The Saptalakṣaṇa is a set of seven mnemonic treatises for the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. They list the words that need special treatment when the padapāṭha is converted into saṃhitā, and the reverse. The parts cover the elision of visarjanīya after ā (śamāna), words that resist the usual sandhi (vilaṅghya), words followed by n- or t- (napara, tapara), groups of words with a- and ā- (avarṇi, āvarṇi), and words that are not divided by avagraha in the padapāṭha (aniṅgya). Recitation students use it as a reference aid.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajurvedasaptalaksanam.attribution: A collection of seven lakṣaṇa treatises for the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The e-text's section headings and colophons give their names as Śamāna, Vilaṅghya, Napara, Tapara, Avarṇi, Āvarṇi and Aniṅgya. Only the Aniṅgyaprakaraṇa names an author: Śrīvatsāṅka, son of Devīmanīṣin (v. 77). The other parts are anonymous in the e-text.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajurvedasaptalaksanam.coverage: complete — All seven prakaraṇas are present, each with a closing colophon numbered 1–7 (e.g. 'iti vilaṅghyaprakaraṇaṃ samāptam 2', 'iti aniṅgyaprakaraṇam 7'). The text ends with 'saptalakṣaṇaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohibhasyam.title: Yohibhāṣya
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohibhasyam.author: Sūrabhaṭṭa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohibhasyam.summary: A Taittirīya-school lakṣaṇa treatise in 23 kārikās by Sūrabhaṭṭa, with a prose bhāṣya. It deals with the accent of finite verbs (kriyāpada) in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: it lists the contexts in which a verb that is normally unaccented in a main clause takes the udātta, for example after particular preceding words or in clauses with yad and hi. Each rule is illustrated with Taittirīya passages and counter-examples ('... iti kim').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohibhasyam.attribution: The kārikās are by Sūrabhaṭṭa of Homakanyāpura (v. 1). Whether he also wrote the prose bhāṣya is not stated. The name 'Yohi' probably comes from the particles yad and hi, which condition verbal accent and are listed in vv. 22–23 ('na hi sa taṃ hi te tāṃ hi ... yo yakṣye yasyaivaṃ ...'); this explanation is not confirmed in the literature.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohibhasyam.coverage: complete — Kārikās 1–23, each with a prose bhāṣya, from the maṅgala 'śrī gaṇādhipataye namaḥ' to the colophon 'yohibhāṣyaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohipraptisiksa.title: Yohiprāptiśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohipraptisiksa.summary: This is a short Vedalakṣaṇa/śikṣā manual in 23 verses (anuṣṭubh, after a maṅgala verse in upajāti) on the accentuation of finite verbs (kriyāsvara) in the Taittirīya (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) texts. It lists the verbs and contexts in which the verb keeps its udātta, especially after relative and causal words such as yaḥ, yat, yadi, yathā and hi (hence the name 'yo-hi-prāpti'). It also names the exceptions. In its final verse the text says it was composed to show these accents to learners (bālānām).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohipraptisiksa.attribution: Verse 1: 'śrīmadgaṇeśaṃ praṇipatya devān śrīsūryanārāyaṇasuprasādāt / vakṣye kriyāyā svaralakṣaṇaṃ tad yad dhomakanyāpurasūribhaṭṭaḥ'. This points to a Sūribhaṭṭa of Homakanyāpura as author or source.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yohipraptisiksa.coverage: complete — 23 verses, from the maṅgala verse to v. 23 ('tatsvarasūcanārthaṃ hi bālānām iti varṇitaḥ'), with the colophon 'iti yohiprāptimūlaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_yajusajyotisam.title: Yājuṣajyotiṣa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_yajusajyotisam.author: Lagadha
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_yajusajyotisam.summary: The Yājuṣajyotiṣa is the Yajurvedic recension of the Vedāṅgajyotiṣa, the earliest extant Indian astronomical text, traditionally attributed to the sage Lagadha. Designed to determine the correct seasons and calendar dates for Vedic sacrifices, it describes a five-year luni-solar yuga cycle, the computation of solstices, tithis, parvans, and the positions of the sun and moon relative to the twenty-seven nakṣatras.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_yajusajyotisam.attribution: Traditional attribution to Lagadha, named explicitly in the concluding verse of the recension: 'ityetanmāsavarṣāṇāṃ muhūrtodayaparvaṇām | dinartvayanamāsāṅgaṃ vyākhyānaṃ lagadho'bravīt'.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_yajusajyotisam.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Yājuṣajyotiṣa in 43 numbered verses plus 2 unnumbered/zero-numbered verses (total 45 verses), closing with 'iti yājuṣajyotiṣaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajnavalkyasiksa.title: Yājñavalkyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajnavalkyasiksa.summary: The Yājñavalkyaśikṣā is an authoritative Vedāṅga phonetic treatise affiliated with the Śukla Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi) tradition. Traditionally attributed to Yājñavalkya, it systematizes Vedic accentuation (traisvarya: udātta, anudātta, and svarita), duration (mātrā), recitation faults (pāṭhadoṣa), manual mudrās accompanying recitation, and specific euphonic sandhi rules.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajnavalkyasiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Yājñavalkya; belongs to the phonetical treatise tradition (Śikṣā) of the Śukla Yajurveda (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_yajnavalkyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text of the treatise ending with segment: '|| iti śrīyājñavalkyaśikṣā samāptā ||'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_agnivesyagrhyasutram.title: Āgniveśyagṛhyasūtra
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_agnivesyagrhyasutram.summary: The Āgniveśyagṛhyasūtra is a domestic ritual manual. Structured across three praśnas, it details domestic sacraments (saṃskāras) such as upanayana and vivāha, domestic offerings, śrāddha and antyeṣṭi (funerary) ceremonies, and extensive prāyaścitta (expiatory) rituals.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_agnivesyagrhyasutram.attribution: Tradition attributes the sūtra to the sage Agniveśya (cited as bhagavān āgniveśyaḥ in the text at 3.12).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_agnivesyagrhyasutram.coverage: complete — Complete in three praśnas, ending at praśna 3, adhyāya 12 (tṛtīyapraśne dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ; samāptaṃ cāgniveśyagṛhyasūtram).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambasrautasutram.title: Āpastambaśrautasūtra (lacking kaṇḍikās 1.1–1.3)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambasrautasutram.summary: The Āpastambaśrautasūtra constitutes the Śrauta manual (Praśnas 1–24) of the larger Āpastamba Kalpasūtra belonging to the Taittirīya recension of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It provides exhaustive procedural directions from the standpoint of the Adhvaryu priest for major Vedic rituals, including the Darśapūrṇamāsa, Agnyādheya, Paśubandha, Agniṣṭoma, Agnicayana, Vājapeya, Rājasūya, and Sattra, concluding with general interpretive principles (paribhāṣā), expiations (prāyaścitta), and Pravaras.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambasrautasutram.coverage: partial — Praśnas 1–24 (last colophon 'iti caturdaśī kaṇḍikā | iti caturviṃśaḥ praśnaḥ'). Missing: kaṇḍikās 1.1–1.3; the e-text starts with 'pṛthivyāḥ saṃpṛcaḥ pāhītyanadho nidadhāti 1' (= 1.4.1).
translations: Willem Caland (tr.), Das Śrautasūtra des Āpastamba, 3 vols. (Bd. 1: Göttingen-Leipzig 1921; Bd. 2–3: Amsterdam 1924–. (German)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambiyam_srautasutram.title: Āpastambaśrautasūtra with Dhūrtasvāmibhāṣya and Rāmāgnicidvṛtti (Praśnas 1–5, incomplete)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambiyam_srautasutram.author: Āpastamba, Dhūrtasvāmin, Rāmāgnicit
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambiyam_srautasutram.summary: The Āpastambaśrautasūtra is a Vedic ritual text. This e-text comprises an introductory study (Āpastambakalpasūtraparicaya) along with sūtras accompanied by Dhūrtasvāmin's Bhāṣya and Rāmāgnicit's Vṛtti, terminating incompletely in Praśna 5.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambiyam_srautasutram.attribution: Dhūrtasvāmin authored the Bhāṣya, on which Rāmāgnicit composed a Vṛtti.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apastambiyam_srautasutram.coverage: partial — Contains an introductory treatise (Āpastambakalpasūtraparicaya) and text with commentary breaking off abruptly in Praśna 5.
translations: Willem Caland, Das Śrautasūtra des Āpastamba: Aus dem Sanskrit übersetzt, 3 vols., Göttingen / Amsterdam, 1921, 1924. (German)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apisalasiksa.title: Āpiśalaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apisalasiksa.author: Āpiśali
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apisalasiksa.summary: The Āpiśalaśikṣā is a Sanskrit phonetic treatise (śikṣā). Composed predominantly in brief prose sūtras framed by introductory and concluding verses, it provides an analysis of Sanskrit sound production across sthāna (articulatory place), karaṇa (active articulator), internal and external effort, articulatory pressure, and phonation/accentuation processes (prakrama).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_apisalasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising opening verses and sūtra sections: sthānakaraṇaprakaraṇa, karaṇaprakaraṇa, antaḥprayatnaprakaraṇa, bāhyaprayatnaprakaraṇa, sthānapīḍaprakaraṇa, vṛttikāraprakaraṇa, and the prakramaprakaraṇa with the final summary verses (vv. 25–27).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_aranyakasiksa.title: Āraṇyakaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_aranyakasiksa.summary: The Āraṇyakaśikṣā (or Āraṇyaśikṣā) is an accentological and phonetic treatise belonging to the Taittirīya tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. It provides metrical rules for initial udātta, svarita, anudātta, and ekaśruti accents, as well as sandhi and raṅga rules, across the five praśnas of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (including the Āruṇaketuka and Mahānārāyaṇa sections).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_aranyakasiksa.attribution: Anonymous metrical śikṣā text transmitted within the Taittirīya tradition of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda (one of the traditional Navaśikṣās).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_aranyakasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text of 129 numbered verses followed by concluding unnumbered ślokas, ending with the colophon 'iti āraṇyaśikṣā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arseyakalpah.title: Ārṣeyakalpa with Ārṣeyakalpavyākhyā (without the Upodghāta)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arseyakalpah.author: Maśaka, Varadarāja
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arseyakalpah.summary: The Ārṣeyakalpa (or Maśakakalpa) is a Sāmavedic ritual work attributed to Maśaka. This e-text includes the Sanskrit commentary (Ārṣeyakalpavyākhyā) by Varadarāja, son of Vāmānārya, concluding with adhyāya 11.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arseyakalpah.attribution: The kalpa text is associated with Maśaka (Maśakakalpa). The commentary was composed by Varadarāja, son of Vāmānārya.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_arseyakalpah.coverage: partial — Text with commentary ending 'iti viśvasṛjāmayanaṃ samāptam ... iti śrīvāmānāryasutavaradarājena viracitāyāmārṣeyakalpavyākhyāyāṃ satreṣu tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ ādita ekādaśaḥ || ārṣeyakalpaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_atharvanajyotisam.title: Ātharvaṇajyotiṣa
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_atharvanajyotisam.summary: The Ātharvaṇajyotiṣa is a short astrological text framed as Brahmā's (Pitāmaha's) instruction to Kāśyapa. It deals with electional astrology: activities suited to various muhūrtas, karaṇas, tithis, weekdays, and groups of nakṣatras.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_atharvanajyotisam.attribution: Framed as Pitāmaha's answer to Kāśyapa.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_atharvanajyotisam.coverage: unclear — The e-text contains numbered sections covering muhūrtas, karaṇas, tithis, weekdays, and nakṣatra groups.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksa.title: Ātreyaśikṣā (aniṅgya verses, with opening and closing verses of part 3)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksa.summary: A phonetic text transmitted under the name of Ātreya. The first part versifies, in 27 anuṣṭubh verses, the list of aniṅgya words 'according to the sūtras taught by Ātreya'. Appended are two opening verses and the final verse of a third part on the rules of jaṭāpāṭha recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksa.attribution: Verse 1 explicitly notes that an anonymous author composed these verses based on the Ātreyasūtras.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksa.coverage: partial — Segs. 0–54: 27 verses on aniṅgya words, complete (colophon 'ātreya śikṣā saṃpūrṇam'). Segs. 56–65: 'tṛtīyo bhāgaḥ' on jaṭāpāṭha — only 'prathamau ślokau' (vv. 1–2) and 'antimaḥ ślokaḥ' given, final colophon 'ityātreyaśikṣā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksakarika.title: Ātreyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksakarika.summary: The Ātreyaśikṣā is a metrical Vedāṅga treatise on phonetics and recitation practice affiliated with the Taittirīya śākhā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda. Beginning with an 18-verse anukramaṇikā and paribhāṣā, the text spans 14 chapters covering vowel length, places and efforts of articulation (sthāna, prayatna), accents (udātta, anudātta, svarita, kampa), and the phonetic mechanics of the Vedic recitation modifications (vikṛtipāṭha such as pada, krama, and jaṭā).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksakarika.attribution: Attributed by colophon to Ātreya (ityātreyaśikṣāmūlaṃ saṃpūrṇam).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_atreyasiksakarika.coverage: complete — Complete root text, ending with chapter 14 (iti caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ) and the final colophon 'ityātreyaśikṣāmūlaṃ saṃpūrṇam' at verse 293.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyakarikah.title: Āśvalāyanagṛhyakārikā (chapter 2 excerpt)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyakarikah.author: Kumārila Bhaṭṭa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyakarikah.summary: The Āśvalāyanagṛhyakārikā is a versified ritual manual (prayogakārikā) systematizing domestic rites for practitioners of the Ṛgvedic Āśvalāyana tradition, traditionally attributed to Kumārila Bhaṭṭa. This brief Wikisource excerpt contains only the start of adhyāya 2, laying down the manual procedure and mantras for the Śravaṇākarma and Sarpabali offerings performed during the full moon of Śrāvaṇa.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyakarikah.attribution: Ascribed in the text to Bhaṭṭa Kumārilasvāmin ('bhaṭṭakumārilasvāmipraṇītāḥ').
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyakarikah.coverage: excerpt — Excerpt of only 24 verses from adhyāya 2, covering the Śravaṇākarma (15 verses) and Sarpabali (9 verses).

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyaparisistam.title: Āśvalāyanagṛhyapariśiṣṭa (fragment)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyaparisistam.summary: The Āśvalāyanagṛhyapariśiṣṭa is a late Vedic supplementary ritual text (pariśiṣṭa) belonging to the Āśvalāyana tradition of the Ṛgveda, providing domestic rites and expiations supplementary to the Āśvalāyanagṛhyasūtra. This brief fragment preserves the final four khaṇḍas of adhyāya 3, detailing the rituals of nārāyaṇabali (expiatory obsequies), nāgabali (rites for snake-bite deaths), and vṛṣotsarga (ritual release of a bull).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyaparisistam.attribution: Ascribed traditionally to Āśvalāyana or scholars of his school, but catalogued as an anonymous Vedic ritual supplement (pariśiṣṭa).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_asvalayanagrhyaparisistam.coverage: fragment — Fragment containing only adhyāya 3, khaṇḍas 15–18 (nārāyaṇabali, nāgabali, vṛṣotsarga) and the bare opening heading 'atha caturtho'dhyāyaḥ'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdakaustubhah.title: Śabdakaustubha
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdakaustubhah.author: Bhaṭṭojidīkṣita
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdakaustubhah.summary: The Śabdakaustubha is an extensive commentary on Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī composed in the 17th century by Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita. In contrast to his thematic Siddhāntakaumudī, this treatise comments on the sūtras in their sequential order, providing deep grammatical, hermeneutical, and philosophical analyses drawing heavily on Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya and Kaiyaṭa's Pradīpa. The author left the commentary unfinished, terminating at the conclusion of the first pāda of adhyāya 3 (sūtra 3.1.150).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdakaustubhah.attribution: A major grammatical commentary by Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita (17th century), son of Lakṣmīdhara.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdakaustubhah.coverage: complete — Contains the text from Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.1 up to 3.1.150 (ending 'iti śrīśabdakaustubhe tṛtīyādhyāyasya prathame pāde ṣaṣṭhamānhikam || pādaśca samāptaḥ ||').

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saisiriyasiksa.title: Śaiśirīyaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saisiriyasiksa.summary: The Śaiśirīyaśikṣā is a phonetic manual (śikṣā) belonging to the Ṛgvedic tradition, associated with the Śaiśira branch of the Śākala recension. Written in anuṣṭubh verse with illustrative examples (nidarśanas), it describes the inventory of 63 or 64 speech sounds, the articulatory organs (sthāna and karaṇa), mora timing (mātrā), accents (udātta, anudātta, svarita, pracaya), and phonetic sandhi modifications occurring during Ṛgvedic chant recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saisiriyasiksa.attribution: The text presents itself as Śaiśira's teaching for his śākhā (v. 'śaiśiro 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi śākhāyā lakṣaṇaṃ vidhim'), after listing Mudgala, Gālava, Gārgya, Śākalya and Śaiśira as founders of śākhā divisions; it belongs to the Śaiśirīya branch of the Śākala Ṛgveda. No historical author is known; author field left empty.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saisiriyasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text terminating with the colophon 'iti śaiśirīyaśikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sambhusiksa.title: Śambhuśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sambhusiksa.summary: The Śambhuśikṣā ('Śāṅkarī Śikṣā') is a short metrical lakṣaṇa/śikṣā text of the Taittirīya (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) tradition. It names the sections (kāṇḍas, praśnas, anuvāka groups) of the Taittirīya corpus, and gives rules for jaṭāpāṭha (elision and non-elision), svarabhakti, kampa varieties (pipīlikā, madhyamā etc.), mora values of anusvāra, visarga and pluta, yama, and the finger gestures (aṅgulīsvara) used to show accents.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sambhusiksa.attribution: The opening verse announces 'śikṣāṃ vakṣyāmi śāṅkarīm' after homage to Lakṣmī, Kālikā, Sarasvatī, Gaṇeśa and Śambhu; the title refers to Śambhu/Śaṅkara (Śiva). No human author is named; author field left empty.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sambhusiksa.coverage: complete — Metrical text from the maṅgala (praṇamya śirasā lakṣmīṃ ...) to the colophon 'śambhuśikṣāsamāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samanasiksa.title: Śamānaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samanasiksa.summary: The Śamānaśikṣā is a short Vedāṅga phonetic manual intended for reciters of the Ṛgveda (Bahvṛcas). It sets forth the sandhi rules concerning the elision of visarjanīya preceded by ā when followed by voiced consonants (ghoṣavat) in the Saṃhitā text, illustrating the rules with an alphabetical list of Ṛgvedic words and pratīkas.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_samanasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete root text (mūla) in 32 sections preceded by an introductory paribhāṣā section; ends with 'iti śamānaśikṣāmūlaṃ samāptam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakasiksa.title: Śaunakaśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakasiksa.summary: The Śaunakaśikṣā is a Vedāṅga phonetic treatise (śikṣā) in 67 verses associated with the tradition of Śaunaka, focusing on orthoepic rules for the recitation of the Ṛgveda. It outlines the inventory of sounds, points and articulatory efforts (sthāna and karaṇa), moraic durations (mātrā), accents, sandhi modifications, nasalization (raṅga), and concludes with an analysis of praṇava (oṃkāra) and the merits of correct recitation.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakasiksa.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Vedic sage Śaunaka, closely associated with the phonetic and orthoepic traditions of the Ṛgveda and Atharvaveda.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakasiksa.coverage: complete — Complete text in 67 metrical verses (anuṣṭubh), ending with 'iti śaunaka śikṣā samāptā'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakiya_caturadhyayika.title: Śaunakīyā Caturādhyāyikā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakiya_caturadhyayika.summary: The Śaunakīyā Caturādhyāyīkā (also known as the Atharvavedaprātiśākhya) is a prātiśākhya text of the Atharvaveda, presenting phonological and grammatical rules including sandhi, accents, and recitation. It was edited and translated into English by W. D. Whitney in JAOS 7 (1862).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakiya_caturadhyayika.attribution: Belongs to the Śaunakīya tradition of the Atharvaveda. Śaunaka is cited by name within the text in sūtra 1.8 (śaunakasya pratijñānaṃ na vṛttiḥ).
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_saunakiya_caturadhyayika.coverage: complete — Text ending with iti śaunakīye caturādhyāyike caturthaḥ pādaḥ.
translations: Whitney, W. D. JAOS 7 (1862). (English)

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_srautapadarthanirvacanam.title: Śrautapadārthanirvacana (excerpts)
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_srautapadarthanirvacanam.summary: The Śrautapadārthanirvacana is a Sanskrit prose explanation of śrauta ritual terms, giving procedural definitions and explanations (such as sānnāyya, upaveṣa, śākhāpavitra, prastara, paridhi, caturavatta, pradhānayāga, vasatīvarī). The e-text preserves excerpts dealing with rites including the Darśapūrṇamāsa and animal/soma preparation rituals.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_srautapadarthanirvacanam.attribution: Anonymous/undetermined author; a prose explanatory handbook of śrauta terms in the Taittirīya ritual tradition.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_srautapadarthanirvacanam.coverage: excerpt — Wikisource text contains excerpts on ritual procedures including Darśapūrṇamāsa, Agnīṣomīya, and preparations for the sutyā day, breaking off mid-word ('udagudvāsyāta').

SA_GS41_ilx_ws_srisiddhantasudhanidhih.title: Vyākaraṇasiddhāntasudhānidhi
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_srisiddhantasudhanidhih.author: Viśveśvara
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_srisiddhantasudhanidhih.summary: A commentary by Viśveśvara, pupil of Lakṣmīdhara, on the sūtras of Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī, covering adhyāyas 1–3.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_srisiddhantasudhanidhih.attribution: Viśveśvara was a pupil of Lakṣmīdhara, whom he praises in the maṅgala verse 1.1.4 and in the closing verse.
SA_GS41_ilx_ws_srisiddhantasudhanidhih.coverage: complete — The text runs from opening maṅgala verses to Aṣṭādhyāyī 3.4.117. It ends 'iti śiddhāntasudhānidhau tṛtīyasya caturthapāde prathamāhnikam| pādo'dhyāyaścāyaṃ samāptaḥ', followed by the author's closing verse.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_srivyasapaninibhavanirnay.title: Vyāsapāṇinibhāvanirṇaya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_srivyasapaninibhavanirnay.author: Setumādhavācārya
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_srivyasapaninibhavanirnay.summary: A grammatical and philosophical treatise composed by Vyākaraṇa Setumādhavācārya from the perspective of Dvaita (Mādhva) Vedānta. The work argues that the true intent (bhāva) of both Bādarāyaṇa Vyāsa and Pāṇini supports ontological realism and the supreme reality of Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva, mounting an extensive critique of non-dualist views and later grammarians such as Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_srivyasapaninibhavanirnay.attribution: The author identifies himself as an adherent of the Dvaita/Mādhva school (Śrīmatpūrṇaprajñīyasiddhāntānuyāyin), of the Ātreya gotra, and the son of Mahāmahopādhyāya Śrīmuṣṇaṃ Vyākaraṇa Subbarāyācārya.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_srivyasapaninibhavanirnay.coverage: complete — Complete text from the initial maṅgala through to the final authorial verses and concluding colophon.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdikabharanam.title: Śābdikābharaṇa
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdikabharanam.author: Hariyogin
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdikabharanam.summary: The Śābdikābharaṇa is a Pāṇinian grammatical work on verbal morphology composed by Hariyogin. The treatise begins with an epistemological and philosophical preface (bhūmikā) evaluating the eternity (nityatva) versus non-eternity (anityatva) of phonemes (varṇa) and recognitive cognition (pratyabhijñā), before providing a systematic grammatical commentary on verbal roots according to Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_sabdikabharanam.coverage: complete — Text containing introductory philosophical discourse (bhūmikā) and verbal root treatments concluding with the colophon 'iti hariyoginā viracitaṃ śābdikābharaṇaṃ saṃpūrṇam'.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvarnakramalaksanam.title: Ṛgvarṇakramalakṣaṇa with Vyākhyā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvarnakramalaksanam.author: Narasiṃha
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvarnakramalaksanam.summary: The Ṛgvarṇakramalakṣaṇa is a short Vedāṅga treatise in 44 kārikās by Narasiṃha (Narasiṃhasūri), accompanied by the author's own commentary (Vyākhyā). Drawing on the Śikṣā and Prātiśākhya traditions, it describes the phonetic, phonological, and euphonic rules (varṇakrama) required for correct Ṛgvedic recitation, including consonant doubling (dvitva), abhinidhāna, aspiration, transition sounds (yamas), svarabhakti, nasalization, visarga, and vowel shortening.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvarnakramalaksanam.attribution: Narasiṃha (Narasiṃhasūri) is explicitly named in the opening verses of both the root kārikā text and the commentary.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_rgvarnakramalaksanam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 44 kārikās alongside Narasiṃha's vyākhyā, concluding with the colophons 'iti ṛgvarṇakramalakṣaṇaṃ samāptam' and 'iti vyākhyā samāptā'.

SA_GS24_ilx_ws_satkarakam.title: Ṣaṭkāraka with Saṃbandhodyota
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_satkarakam.author: Rabhasanandin
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_satkarakam.summary: The Ṣaṭkāraka with its commentary Saṃbandhodyota is a concise Buddhist Sanskrit grammatical treatise on kāraka syntax and case relations by Rabhasanandin. Opening with homage to the Buddha, the treatise analyzes the six kārakas, syntactic relations (saṃbandha), and case inflection through the framework of whether an argument is expressed (ukta) or unexpressed (anukta) by verbal, kṛt, or taddhita affixes. The commentary illustrates syntactic principles with distinctively Buddhist examples alongside standard grammatical patterns.
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_satkarakam.attribution: Both the 15 kārikās and the accompanying prose commentary (vṛtti) are attributed to the Buddhist grammarian and lexicographer Rabhasanandin (recorded in the text as rabhasanaṃda).
SA_GS24_ilx_ws_satkarakam.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising the 15 root kārikās followed by the continuous prose vṛtti on all 15 verses, closing with an authorial verse stating the grantha extent (420 anuṣṭubh measures) and a scribal closing formula.

SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sodasaslokisiksa.title: Ṣoḍaśaślokīśikṣā
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sodasaslokisiksa.author: Rāmakṛṣṇa
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sodasaslokisiksa.summary: The Ṣoḍaśaślokīśikṣā is a concise Vedāṅga phonetic treatise in sixteen verses attributed to Rāmakṛṣṇa. It describes the traditional 63-sound inventory, classification and accents of vowels (svara), consonants, pratyāhāras, and places of articulation (sthāna). It concludes with guidelines for proper articulation, citing the classic simile of a tigress carrying her cubs without biting or dropping them.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sodasaslokisiksa.attribution: Attributed to Rāmakṛṣṇa in the text's final colophon line.
SA_GV06_ilx_ws_sodasaslokisiksa.coverage: complete — Contains all 16 verses of the text and the final colophon.

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_bhargavatantram.title: Bhārgavatantra
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_bhargavatantram.summary: The Bhārgavatantra is a canonical Pāñcarātra Āgama text structured as an instruction delivered by Paraśurāma (Bhārgava) to Agastya on Mount Mahendra. Across 25 adhyāyas, it details Vaiṣṇava temple architecture, iconography, icon consecration (pratiṣṭhā), daily and festival rituals (utsava, snapana), and expiatory rites (prāyaścitta/niṣkṛti) centered on Vāsudeva.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_bhargavatantram.attribution: A Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava āgama framed as a teaching imparted by Paraśurāma (Bhārgava) to the sage Agastya.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_bhargavatantram.coverage: complete — Complete in 25 adhyāyas (concludes at 25.37: 'iti bhārgavatantre pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ').

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyadhikara.title: Kriyādhikāra (incomplete; breaks off in chapter 34)
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyadhikara.summary: The Kriyādhikāra is a canonical text of the Vaikhānasa tradition, framed as taught to the sage Bhṛgu following Vikhanas. It provides instructions on temple ritual, deity installation, worship, offerings, and expiations.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyadhikara.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the sage Bhṛgu as taught by Vikhanas.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyadhikara.coverage: partial — Breaks off after verse 34.87 in the middle of a verse ('iha loke sukhaṃ bhuṅktvā patnīputrāsamanvitaḥ') with no colophon.

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyakairavacandrika.title: Kriyākairavacandrikā
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyakairavacandrika.author: Varāhaguru
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyakairavacandrika.summary: The Kriyākairavacandrikā is a Pāñcarātra ritual handbook (prayoga) composed by Varāhaguru. Arranged in 37 chapters (paricchedas), it provides practical guidelines for Vaiṣṇava temple rites, including site selection (bhūparīkṣā), plowing (karṣaṇa), layout, temple architecture, installation (pratiṣṭhā) of icons and ancillary shrines, daily worship (nityotsava), and annual purification rites such as pavitrāropaṇa.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyakairavacandrika.attribution: Consistently attributed to Varāhaguru in internal chapter colophons (e.g. chapters 28, 33, 37).
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_kriyakairavacandrika.coverage: complete — Complete work in 37 chapters (paricchedas), terminating with 'iti śrī varāhaguruṇā viracitāyāṃ kriyākairava candrikāyāṃ pavitrāropaṇa mahotsava vidhiḥ nāma saptatriṃśaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptoyaṃ kriyākairava candrikā'.

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramapurusasamhita.title: Paramapuruṣasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramapurusasamhita.summary: The Paramapuruṣasaṃhitā is a Vaiṣṇava Āgama text belonging to the Pāñcarātra corpus, presented as an exposition given by Nārada to sages on the banks of the Bhāgīrathī. In ten adhyāyas (comprising roughly one thousand verses), the text addresses the duties, qualifications, and classifications of temple priests (arcaka) and temple servants (paricāraka), the ritual worship of Viṣṇu, and the significance of the Ekādaśī vrata.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramapurusasamhita.attribution: Canonical saṃhitā of the Pāñcarātrāgama tradition, cast as an instruction delivered by Nārada to sages on the banks of the Bhāgīrathī.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramapurusasamhita.coverage: complete — Complete in 10 adhyāyas (concluding with 'iti śrīpāṃca rātrāgamarahasyasāreśrīparamapuruṣasaṃhitāyāṃ ekādaśī vratamahimābhivavarṇanaṃ nāma daśamodhyāyaḥ saṃpūrṇam', aligning with the text's own mention in 10.72 of being around 1,000 verses).

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramesvarasamhita.title: Pārameśvarasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramesvarasamhita.summary: The Pārameśvarasaṃhitā is a Pāñcarātra saṃhitā traditionally framed as an instruction on Mount Totādri to the sage Sanaka. Its 26 chapters treat temple worship, installation, festivals, and the worship of the Sudarśana-mahāyantra.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramesvarasamhita.attribution: Canonical Pāñcarātra Āgama scripture, traditionally framed as an instruction delivered on Totādri by the sage Śāṇḍilya to Sanaka.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_paramesvarasamhita.coverage: complete — 26 adhyāyas with colophons ('iti śrīpāñcarātre pārameśvarasaṃhitāyāṃ ...'; chapters from 15 on labelled kriyākāṇḍa), ending with the colophon of ch. 26 (sudarśanamahāyarntrācane agrikāryavidhirnāma ṣaḍviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ).

SA_GR13_ilx_ws_prayogamanjari.title: Prayogamañjarī (fragment)
SA_GR13_ilx_ws_prayogamanjari.author: Ravi
SA_GR13_ilx_ws_prayogamanjari.summary: The Prayogamañjarī is a Śaiva ritual work rooted in the Śaiva Siddhānta that served as one of the foundations for tantric ritual in Kerala alongside the Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati. This digital entry is an unfinished stub preserving only the opening four and a half verses of chapter 1.
SA_GR13_ilx_ws_prayogamanjari.coverage: fragment — Extremely brief fragment containing only 13 lines (verses 1–4 and first half of verse 5 of paṭala 1).

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_purusottamasamhita.title: Puruṣottamasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_purusottamasamhita.summary: The Puruṣottamasaṃhitā is a canonical Pāñcarātrāgama text framed as a discourse delivered by the sage Vasiṣṭha to inquiring ṛṣis, passing down instructions revealed by Puruṣottama (Viṣṇu) to Brahmā. Across 33 chapters, it treats temple architectural planning, iconography, consecration (pratiṣṭhā), daily and festival liturgies (utsava), expiation (prāyaścitta), initiation (dīkṣā), and ritual hand gestures (mudrā).
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_purusottamasamhita.attribution: Canonical Pāñcarātrāgama scripture structured as Vasiṣṭha's exposition of the divine teaching originally given by Puruṣottama to Brahmā.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_purusottamasamhita.coverage: complete — Complete in 33 adhyāyas (closing with the Mudrālakṣaṇa chapter and colophon 'saṃpūrṇaṃ').

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_sattvatasamhita.title: Sāttvatasaṃhitā with the bhāṣya of Alaśiṅgabhaṭṭa
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_sattvatasamhita.author: Alaśiṅgabhaṭṭa
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_sattvatasamhita.summary: The Sāttvatasaṃhitā is one of the earliest canonical scriptures of the Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātra system, counted alongside the Pauṣkarasaṃhitā and Jayākhyasaṃhitā as part of the authoritative Ratnatraya triad.
