Spanning 25 paricchedas, it details the metaphysics of the cāturvyūha, meditative visualization of divine forms, mantra installation, initiation (dīkṣā), and temple consecration rituals. This e-text provides the complete root saṃhitā together with the extensive bhāṣya of the Melkote ritualist-scholar Alaśiṅgabhaṭṭa.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_sattvatasamhita.attribution: The root Sāttvatasaṃhitā is a canonical scriptural work of the Pāñcarātra school. The Sanskrit bhāṣya is by Alaśiṅgabhaṭṭa, son of Yogānandabhaṭṭācārya of the Mauñjyāyana gotra, temple priest of Yadugiri.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_sattvatasamhita.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 25 paricchedas of the Sāttvatasaṃhitā accompanied throughout by Alaśiṅgabhaṭṭa's commentary, ending at pariccheda 25, verse 384 and colophon.
translations: Hiromichi Hikita, Sāttvata Saṃhitā: An Annotated Translation (chapters 3–6, 10–11, 16 in Aichi Gakuin University journals and Tōkai Bukkyō, 1990–1992). (Japanese)

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visvamitrasamhita.title: Viśvāmitrasaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visvamitrasamhita.summary: The Viśvāmitrasaṃhitā is a canonical Pāñcarātra Āgama text structured as a dialogue between the sage Viśvāmitra and Kāśyapa. Across 27 chapters, it covers the core ritual and theological topics of the Pāñcarātra tradition, including initiation (dīkṣā), mantras, mudrās, daily worship (pañcakālapūjā), temple iconography, consecration rites (pratiṣṭhā), utsava ceremonies, and expiatory procedures (prāyaścitta).
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visvamitrasamhita.attribution: Canonical Pāñcarātra Vaiṣṇava Āgama text traditionally cast as an instruction delivered by the sage Viśvāmitra to Kāśyapa.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visvamitrasamhita.coverage: complete — 27 adhyāyas (1.1–27.60), ending with the colophon 'iti pañcarātre mahopani?ṣadi viśvāmitrasaṃhitāyāṃ prāyaścittavidhirnāma saptaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ' and '| | hariḥ om | |'.

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visnusamhita.title: Viṣṇusaṃhitā
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visnusamhita.summary: The Viṣṇusaṃhitā is a canonical scriptural work of the Pāñcarātra tradition. Structured with the sage Aupamanyava questioning on Mount Śrīśaila, it treats temple architecture, iconographic rituals and images, mudrās, and a six-limbed yoga system (ṣaḍaṅgayoga).
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visnusamhita.attribution: Revealed scriptural text (Pāñcarātra Saṃhitā) traditionally presented as divine instruction communicated to the sage Aupamanyava.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_visnusamhita.coverage: complete — Text reaches the colophon 'iti viṣṇusaṃhitāyāṃ triṃśaḥ paṭalaḥ' after 30.89.

SA_GR14_ilx_ws_yajnadhikara.title: Yajñādhikāra
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_yajnadhikara.summary: The Yajñādhikāra is a canonical ritual manual (saṃhitā) belonging to the Vaikhānasa Vaiṣṇava Āgama corpus, traditionally attributed to the sage Bhṛgu. It expounds temple architecture, vāstumaṇḍala preparations, installation of icons (pratiṣṭhā), daily and seasonal oblations, and expiatory rites (niṣkṛti) to counteract procedural blemishes. Alongside the Kriyādhikāra, Khilādhikāra, and Prakīrṇādhikāra, it constitutes one of the four major Ādhikāra treatises of the Bhṛgu division.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_yajnadhikara.attribution: Canonical text traditionally ascribed to Maharṣi Bhṛgu, one of the four legendary disciples of Vikhanas who codified Vaikhānasa ritual doctrine.
SA_GR14_ilx_ws_yajnadhikara.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual in verse covering the Vaikhānasa ritual cycle from site selection through expiations; ends with an editorial note concerning manuscript collation ('tataḥ kośāntarāṇyanu sarasyasamagrā ca|').

SA_K12_Āgama_Vajratuṇḍanāgasamaya_Hidas.title: Vajratuṇḍasamayakalparāja
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajratuṇḍanāgasamaya_Hidas.summary: The Vajratuṇḍasamayakalparāja is a Buddhist dhāraṇī manual (kalparāja) dedicated to weather control and agricultural protection. Set in Vārāṇasī, it provides rites, dhāraṇī spells, and mandalas revealed by the Buddha and Vajrapāṇi to bind, pacify, and compel malevolent serpentine beings (nāgas) to avert drought, hail, and pests, and to release timely rainfall according to their sworn pledge (samaya).
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajratuṇḍanāgasamaya_Hidas.attribution: Buddhist Mahāyāna dhāraṇī-kalpa framed as the word of the Buddha (buddhavacana) delivered at Vārāṇasī in dialogue with Vajrapāṇi and the nāgas.
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajratuṇḍanāgasamaya_Hidas.coverage: complete — Complete text across six chapters, numbered [1.1] to [6.8], from the opening nidāna to the final colophon.

SA_K10_anon_Nānopadeśa.title: Nānopadeśa (fragment)
SA_K10_anon_Nānopadeśa.summary: The Nānopadeśa is an unedited esoteric Buddhist tantric compendium gathering pith instructions (upadeśa) on subtle-body yoga, mahāmudrā, and sahaja realization attributed to various mahāsiddhas and ācāryas. Masters cited include Padmāṅkura, Prajñārakṣita, Nelīpāda, Ravigupta, Kṛṣṇācārya, Sarahapāda, Nāradārya (Nāropa), Kuḍḍāla, Bāṇa, Śabarapāda, Kambala, and Guṇḍārī. Topics treated include the internal caṇḍālī, the manipulation of bindu and nāda across bodily cakras, and non-conceptual awareness.
SA_K10_anon_Nānopadeśa.attribution: Anonymous Buddhist tantric compendium. The title is derived from verse 1b ('nānopadeśaṃ vakṣyāmi nānācāryair nidarśitam').
SA_K10_anon_Nānopadeśa.edition: Unpublished critical transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on IASWR manuscript MBB 1971-91 (Multiple Text Manuscript, second text, fols. 17v2ff.).
SA_K10_anon_Nānopadeśa.coverage: fragment — Preserves verses 1–51 and the first two pādas of verse 52, breaking off abruptly at line 169 ('sarva[explicit]').

SA_K10_Āgama_Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāv.title: Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāvana
SA_K10_Āgama_Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāv.summary: The Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāvana is a short Mahāyāna sūtra also known in Tibetan (D 104) and Chinese (Taishō 289, 290) and closely related to the Avataṃsaka tradition. Spoken by the bodhisattva Acintyaprabharāja with the Buddha's approval, it details a comparative cosmic timescale across pure realms: one kalpa in our Sahā realm is equal to one day and night in Amitābha's Sukhāvatī, which in turn equals one day in successive, ever-more exalted Buddha-fields.
SA_K10_Āgama_Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāv.attribution: A Mahāyāna sūtra presented as spoken by Bodhisattva Acintyaprabharāja with the Buddha's approval; colophon identifies it as the seventeenth text from the Buddhāvataṃsaka / Vaipulyapiṭaka.
SA_K10_Āgama_Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāv.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), ed. (2010). A Unique Collection of Twenty-Two Buddhist Sanskrit Sūtras (Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region, 7). Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences Press, text no. 17.
SA_K10_Āgama_Anantabuddhakṣetraguṇodbhāv.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short sūtra ending with the colophon.
translations: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), trans. (2010). A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences. (English)
phags pa de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi sangs rgyas kyi zhing gi yon tan brjod pa'i chos kyi rnam grangs (Derge Kangyur D 104): translated by Jinamitra, Dānaśīla, sna nam btsun pa ye shes sde (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Bhavasaṃkrānti_Vinītā_2010.title: Bhavasaṃkrāntisūtra
SA_K10_Āgama_Bhavasaṃkrānti_Vinītā_2010.summary: The Bhavasaṃkrāntisūtra is a short Mahāyāna sūtra set in the Veḷuvana at Rājagṛha, in which King Bimbisāra questions the Buddha on how karmic actions yield results across lifetimes without perishability when all conditioned factors (saṃskāra) are empty (śūnya). The Buddha explains rebirth through the simile of a dream, demonstrating that while no enduring entity migrates from one existence to another, karmic fruition occurs within an uninterrupted mental continuum. The sūtra concludes with seven verses detailing the distinction between relative convention (saṃvṛti) and ultimate reality (paramārtha).
SA_K10_Āgama_Bhavasaṃkrānti_Vinītā_2010.attribution: Canonical Mahāyāna sūtra traditionally regarded as Buddhavacana delivered in dialogue with King Bimbisāra.
SA_K10_Āgama_Bhavasaṃkrānti_Vinītā_2010.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), ed. A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. 2 vols. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, text no. 13.
SA_K10_Āgama_Bhavasaṃkrānti_Vinītā_2010.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short sūtra, including the opening nidāna, prose dialogue, seven concluding verses, and concluding colophon.
translations: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, 2 vols., Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010. (English)
phags pa srid pa 'pho ba zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 226): translated by Jinamitra, Dānaśīla, sna nam btsun pa ye shes sde (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Dīrghanakhaparipṛcchā_Vinīt.title: Dīrghanakhaparipṛcchā
SA_K10_Āgama_Dīrghanakhaparipṛcchā_Vinīt.summary: A short Buddhist canonical sūtra set at the Veḷuvana in Rājagṛha, in which the wandering ascetic (parivrājaka) Dīrghanakha questions the Buddha on the karmic causes that produced his bodily perfections and major marks. The Buddha explains that each feature is the fruit of abstaining from specific unwholesome actions in past lives (e.g., abstaining from killing, theft, sexual misconduct, and false speech). Deeply impressed, Dīrghanakha renounces his ascetic paraphernalia, takes refuge in the Three Jewels, and undertakes the eightfold poṣadha vows.
SA_K10_Āgama_Dīrghanakhaparipṛcchā_Vinīt.attribution: Canonical Buddhist sūtra traditionally attributed to Śākyamuni Buddha.
SA_K10_Āgama_Dīrghanakhaparipṛcchā_Vinīt.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), ed., A Unique Collection of Twenty-Two Buddhist Sanskrit Sūtras from the Tibetan Autonomous Region, Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (STTAR).1–8.2, Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences Press, 2010, text no. 11.
SA_K10_Āgama_Dīrghanakhaparipṛcchā_Vinīt.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short discourse from the opening nidāna through to the final colophon.
translations: 'phags pa kun tu rgyu [ ( ]ba [ ) ]sen rings kyis zhus pa zhes bya ba'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 342) (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitādārik.title: Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitādārikāparipṛcchā
SA_K10_Āgama_Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitādārik.summary: A Mahāyāna sūtra in which the young girl Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitā questions the Buddha regarding spiritual obstacles (akalyāṇamitra) facing a beginner on the bodhisattva path. The Buddha warns that followers of the Śrāvakayāna can divert novice bodhisattvas from their aspiration, asserts that maintaining bodhicitta even through rebirth in hell is preferable to entering the Hinayāna arhat state, details the grave karmic retribution of rejecting the Mahāyāna, and expounds twenty-five epithets praising the Mahāyāna. In conclusion, the Buddha instructs Ānanda to remember the discourse under alternative titles such as Mahāyānaguṇānuśaṃsanirdeśa.
SA_K10_Āgama_Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitādārik.attribution: Scriptural Mahāyāna sūtra preserved in a manuscript from the Potala collection.
SA_K10_Āgama_Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitādārik.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), ed. A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. 2 vols. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, text no. 18.
SA_K10_Āgama_Guṇālaṃkṛtasaṃkusumitādārik.coverage: complete — Complete text in 18 numbered sections concluding with the final colophon.

SA_K10_Āgama_Jayamatisūtra_Vinītā_2010.title: Jayamatiparipṛcchāsūtra
SA_K10_Āgama_Jayamatisūtra_Vinītā_2010.summary: The Jayamatiparipṛcchāsūtra is a short canonical Mahāyāna scripture in which the Buddha, residing at Gṛdhrakūṭa in Rājagṛha, instructs the bodhisattva Jayamati. In a sequence of concise aphorisms, the Buddha details the corresponding causes for various religious and worldly aspirations, prescribing veneration of the Tathāgatas for merit, study for wisdom, relinquishment for wealth, patience for beauty, meditation on emptiness for insight (vipaśyanā), and devotion to the Three Jewels for all spiritual virtues.
SA_K10_Āgama_Jayamatisūtra_Vinītā_2010.attribution: Mahāyāna sūtra presented as the buddhavacana spoken to the bodhisattva Jayamati.
SA_K10_Āgama_Jayamatisūtra_Vinītā_2010.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, Text no. 8.
SA_K10_Āgama_Jayamatisūtra_Vinītā_2010.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short sūtra with Sanskrit-Tibetan parallel segments, including nidāna, dialogue, conclusion, and colophons.
translations: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010 (includes English translation). (English)

SA_K10_Āgama_Kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra-vers.title: Kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra (versified)
SA_K10_Āgama_Kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra-vers.summary: A short Buddhist metrical sūtra consisting of 42 anuṣṭubh verses, preserved as the fourth text in a collection of sūtras from the Potala. The work depicts the monk Mahākāśyapa asking the Buddha about the karmic consequences of assuming administrative authority or dominance (ādhipatya) over the monastic community (Saṃgha). The Buddha warns that monks coveting control over the community suffer rebirth in hells and lower realms, while praising virtuous monks as living stupas (jaṅgamastūpa).
SA_K10_Āgama_Kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra-vers.attribution: A short anonymous Buddhist metrical sūtra presenting a dialogue between the Buddha and Mahākāśyapa, preserved as text no. 4 in a Sanskrit manuscript from the Potala collection.
SA_K10_Āgama_Kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra-vers.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), ed., A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, 2 vols., Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, no. 4, pp. 146–166.
SA_K10_Āgama_Kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtra-vers.coverage: complete — Complete in 42 verses and concluding colophon (kāśyapaparipṛcchāsūtraṃ caturthaṃ samāptam).

SA_K10_Āgama_Kūṭāgārasūtra_Vinītā_2010.title: Kūṭāgārasūtra
SA_K10_Āgama_Kūṭāgārasūtra_Vinītā_2010.summary: The Kūṭāgārasūtra is a canonical Buddhist discourse set in Jetavana at Śrāvastī, where the Buddha expounds to Ānanda the vast merit and spiritual rewards resulting from devotional actions. The practices discussed include sweeping the monastic compound, offering maṇḍalas in various geometric configurations, taking refuge in the Three Jewels, holding one's hands in veneration, and erecting even miniature stūpas or fashioning tiny Buddha images. At the close of the text, the Buddha names the discourse the Amṛtadundubhi ('Drum of the Deathless') and the Adbhutadharmaparyāya ('Discourse on the Wondrous Dharma').
SA_K10_Āgama_Kūṭāgārasūtra_Vinītā_2010.attribution: Canonical Buddhist scripture preserving a discourse spoken by the Buddha in response to Ānanda's questions.
SA_K10_Āgama_Kūṭāgārasūtra_Vinītā_2010.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, no. 2.
SA_K10_Āgama_Kūṭāgārasūtra_Vinītā_2010.coverage: complete — Complete text of the sūtra (§§1–26), ending with the colophon 'kūṭāgārasūtraṃ dvitīyaṃ samāptam'.
translations: khang bu brtsegs pa'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 332): translated by Ratnarakṣita (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Maitreyaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2.title: Maitreyaparipṛcchā
SA_K10_Āgama_Maitreyaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2.summary: The Maitreyaparipṛcchā is a brief Mahāyāna sūtra set on Vulture Peak (Gṛdhrakūṭa) near Rājagṛha. In response to a question posed by the Bodhisattva Maitreya concerning the karmic fruit (vipāka) of the gift of Dharma (dharmadāna), the Buddha explains that communicating even a single stanza of Dharma to another out of compassion produces merit far surpassing that of offering innumerable worlds filled with jewels to the Tathāgatas.
SA_K10_Āgama_Maitreyaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2.attribution: Canonical Mahāyāna sūtra traditionally attributed to the historical Buddha (buddhavacana).
SA_K10_Āgama_Maitreyaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), ed. A Unique Collection of Twenty-Two Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, text no. 16.
SA_K10_Āgama_Maitreyaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short sūtra, comprising the standard opening nidāna, prose dialogue, two summary verses, and the closing colophon identifying it as the 16th text in the collection.
translations: 'phags pa byams pas zhus pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 149) (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīnirdeśa_Vinītā_2010.title: Mañjuśrīnirdeśa
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīnirdeśa_Vinītā_2010.summary: A short Mahāyāna sūtra set in Śrāvastī in which the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī holds a vast ten-yojana parasol over the Buddha. When the devaputra Susīma inquires why Mañjuśrī never tires of making offerings to the Buddha, Mañjuśrī analogizes the bodhisattva's pursuit of inexhaustible omniscient gnosis (sarvajñajñāna) to the ocean receiving waters. He then expounds the four orientations (ārambaṇa) through which the Tathāgata must be worshiped: generating bodhicitta, liberating all beings, maintaining the lineage of the Three Jewels without interruption, and purifying all buddha-fields.
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīnirdeśa_Vinītā_2010.attribution: Canonical Mahāyāna sūtra traditionally considered buddhavacana.
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīnirdeśa_Vinītā_2010.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, 2 vols., Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, no. 15.
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīnirdeśa_Vinītā_2010.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short Mahāyānasūtra (segments 0–11), containing the complete nidāna, dialogue, and closing colophon.
translations: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, Beijing / Vienna, 2010. (English)
phags pa 'jam dpal gyis bstan pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 177): translated by Surendrabodhi, sna nam btsun pa ye shes sde (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-incomple.title: Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-incomple.summary: A Mahāyāna sūtra in which Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī asks the Buddha what degree of great merit enables a Tathāgata to possess the Dharma-conch (dharmaśaṅkha) that fulfills the spiritual aspirations of countless disciples. The Buddha explains this through an ascending scale of comparative merit, progressing from all beings practicing the ten virtuous actions, to a ruler of Jambudvīpa, a Cakravartin king, and Śakra.
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-incomple.attribution: Canonical Mahāyāna sūtra presented as a discourse between the Buddha and Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-incomple.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. 2 vols. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, no. 20.
SA_K10_Āgama_Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-incomple.coverage: fragment — Surviving text contains opening sections 1–7.
translations: 'phags pa 'jam dpal gyis dris pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 172) (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Maṇḍalakānuśaṃsāsūtra_Vinīt.title: Maṇḍalakānuśaṃsāsūtra
SA_K10_Āgama_Maṇḍalakānuśaṃsāsūtra_Vinīt.summary: A short Buddhist canonical sūtra discovered in the Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscript collection preserved at the Potala Palace in Lhasa. Set at Jetavana in Śrāvastī, the Buddha explains five benefits (anuśaṃsā) of offering a maṇḍala (maṇḍalapradāna), followed by three verses that correlate the physical preparation of a maṇḍala using cow dung and water with the cultivation of the six perfections (ṣaṭpāramitā).
SA_K10_Āgama_Maṇḍalakānuśaṃsāsūtra_Vinīt.attribution: Canonical Buddhist sūtra, traditionally presented as the word of the Buddha (buddhavacana) delivered at Śrāvastī.
SA_K10_Āgama_Maṇḍalakānuśaṃsāsūtra_Vinīt.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinita Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. 2 vols. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, Text no. 10.
SA_K10_Āgama_Maṇḍalakānuśaṃsāsūtra_Vinīt.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short sūtra (18 segments including nidāna, prose discourse on the five anuśaṃsās, 3 concluding verses, and the final colophon).

SA_K10_Āgama_Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra_Vinī.title: Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra
SA_K10_Āgama_Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra_Vinī.summary: The Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra is a Buddhist discourse in which the lay devotee (upāsaka) Nandika, accompanied by five hundred followers, questions the Buddha on Gṛdhrakūṭa in Rājagṛha regarding the karmic consequences (vipāka) of violating the five lay training precepts (pañcaśikṣāpada). The Buddha details ten perils (daśādīnava) for each infraction—killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, and consuming intoxicants—concluding with verses underscoring moral conduct.
SA_K10_Āgama_Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra_Vinī.attribution: Canonical Buddhist sūtra traditionally regarded as the word of the Buddha (buddhavacana). Translated into Tibetan by Śākyasiṃha and Byin-gyi snying-po (D 334).
SA_K10_Āgama_Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra_Vinī.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng) (ed.), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, pp. 100–140 (Text no. 3).
SA_K10_Āgama_Nandikaparipṛcchāsūtra_Vinī.coverage: complete — Complete sūtra in 11 sections (§1–§11), from the opening nidāna to the final verses and the colophon (āryanandikaparipṛcchāsūtraṃ tṛtīyaṃ samāptam).
translations: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010. (English)
phags pa dga' ba can gyi mdo (Derge Kangyur D 334): translated by Śākyasiṃha, Agniveśa (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Prasenajidgāthā_Vinītā_2010.title: Prasenajidgāthā
SA_K10_Āgama_Prasenajidgāthā_Vinītā_2010.summary: The Prasenajidgāthā (also known as the Prasenajitparipṛcchāsūtra) is a short canonical Buddhist verse work in 33 stanzas set at Jetavana. In reply to an inquiry by King Prasenajit of Kośala regarding the karmic results of worshipping deceased Tathāgatas, the Buddha describes the manifold future rewards—such as physical beauty, bodily health, sovereignty, sweet voice, and spiritual insight—accruing to those who fashion Buddha statues, build and decorate stūpas with parasols, bells, and textiles, and offer food and drink to the Saṅgha.
SA_K10_Āgama_Prasenajidgāthā_Vinītā_2010.attribution: Scriptural Buddhist verse sūtra delivered by the Buddha to King Prasenajit at Jetavana.
SA_K10_Āgama_Prasenajidgāthā_Vinītā_2010.coverage: complete — Complete in 33 verses, ending with the colophon 'prasenajitparipṛcchāsūtraṃ ṣaṣṭamaṃ samāptam'.
translations: gsal rgyal gyi tshigs su bcad pa (Derge Kangyur D 322) (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Siṃhaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2010.title: Siṃhaparipṛcchā
SA_K10_Āgama_Siṃhaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2010.summary: The Siṃhaparipṛcchā is a versified Mahāyāna sūtra featuring a dialogue between the Buddha and Prince Siṃha, son of King Ajātaśatru of Magadha, at Gṛdhrakūṭa. The prince asks about the bodhisattva practices and causes that produce physical perfections (the 32 lakṣaṇas and 80 anuvyañjanas), intellectual acumen, memory, and supernormal knowledges (abhijñā). It forms the 37th assembly of the Mahāratnakūṭa collection.
SA_K10_Āgama_Siṃhaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2010.attribution: Canonical Mahāyāna sūtra traditionally delivered by the Buddha at Gṛdhrakūṭa in Rājagṛha, preserved in Tibetan translation in the Kangyur (Ratnakūṭa collection, D 81 / Toh 81) and Chinese translation (Taishō 310[37] and Taishō 343).
SA_K10_Āgama_Siṃhaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2010.edition: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, 2 vols., Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010, no. 14.
SA_K10_Āgama_Siṃhaparipṛcchā_Vinītā_2010.coverage: complete — Complete text of the metrical sūtra in 57 verses, ending with the colophon 'siṃhaparipṛcchāmahāyānasūtraṃ caturdaśamaṃ samāptam'.
translations: Bhikṣuṇī Vinītā (Vinītā Tseng), A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation, 2 vols., Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House / Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, 2010. (English)

SA_K10_Āgama_Sumatidārikāsūtra-fragment.title: Sumatidārikāsūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_Sumatidārikāsūtra-fragment.summary: The Sumatidārikāsūtra is a Mahāyāna sūtra. This surviving Sanskrit manuscript fragment preserves the end of the sūtra, including the vyākaraṇa (prediction) of bodhisattvas, the entrustment (parindanā) of the text to Mañjuśrī, a simile likening the preservation of the sūtras to the seven jewels of a cakravartin, and the final colophon.
SA_K10_Āgama_Sumatidārikāsūtra-fragment.coverage: fragment — Contains only the final folio (fol. 2) of Cambridge University Library MS Or. 131.1, covering the closing prophecy, the parindanā (entrustment) to Mañjuśrī, and the colophon.
translations: Tibetan: D 74 (Tibetan)

Chinese: Fo shuo xumoti pusa jing 佛說須摩提菩薩經 (Taishō 334, tr. Zhu Fahu [Dharmarakṣa], 266–313); Fo shuo xumoti pusa jing 佛說須摩提菩薩經 (Taishō 335, tr. Jiumoluoshi [Kumārajīva], 402–412); and Da baoji jing 大寶積經 (Taishō 310, tr. Putiliuzhi [Bodhiruci], 693). (Chinese)

SA_K10_Āgama_TathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśaD.title: Tathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśa (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_TathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśaD.summary: The Tathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśa (also known as the Dhāraṇīśvararājasūtra) is an early Mahāyāna scripture expounding the Tathāgata's great compassion (mahākaruṇā), the sixty-four ornaments of compassion, the eighty practices, and the doctrine of tathāgatagarbha; it forms a major canonical foundation for the Ratnagotravibhāgavyākhyā. This e-text provides the preliminary Sanskrit edition by Ye Shaoyong of the sūtra's opening nidāna based on an ancient palm-leaf manuscript preserved in the Tibet Autonomous Region.
SA_K10_Āgama_TathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśaD.edition: Ye, Shaoyong. 2021. A Preliminary Report on a Sanskrit Manuscript of the Tathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśa or Dhāraṇīśvararāja. Journal of Indian and Buddhist Studies 69/3: (76)/1054–(81)/1059.
translations: T398 (Da ai jing 大哀經, tr. Dharmarakṣa [竺法護], 291 CE, 8 juans); T397 (Da fangdeng daji jing 大方等大集經, tr. Dharmakṣema [曇無讖], 414–426 CE, 60 juans). (Chinese)
phags pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying rje chen po nges par bstan pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 147): translated by Śīlendrabodhi, sna nam btsun pa ye shes sde (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭh.title: Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭhānuśaṃsāvarṇanadharmaparyāya (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭh.summary: The Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭhānuśaṃsāvarṇanadharmaparyāya is a short canonical Buddhist scripture detailing the karmic merits and rewards (anuśaṃsā) of fashioning and consecrating images of the Tathāgata (tathāgatapratibimbakaraṇa). In response to questions posed by Ānanda and the monks, the Buddha explains five specific worldly and spiritual benefits resulting from the gift of an image: great authority and majesty, immense wealth and possessions, extraordinary physical beauty, birth as a universal monarch (cakravartin), and rebirth in heaven among the devas with preeminent lifespan, radiance, and bliss. The surviving Sanskrit text corresponds to the Tibetan Kangyur translation (Tōh. 320) and related Chinese versions such as Taishō 692.
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭh.attribution: Canonical Buddhist sūtra (dharmaparyāya) presented as buddhavacana.
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭh.edition: Unpublished diplomatic manuscript transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó from Asiatic Society of Bengal (Calcutta) MS G 4758, palm-leaf manuscript dated Nepāla Saṃvat 384/385 (ca. 1264–1265 CE), folios 1 and 6r–7v.
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭh.coverage: fragment — Folios 1 and 6r–7v only (folios 2–5 are missing due to a manuscript lacuna). The text breaks off after folio 1v and resumes on folio 6r, concluding with the sūtra colophon on folio 7v.
translations: Robert H. Sharf, in Donald S. Lopez, Jr. (ed.), Religions of China in Practice, pp. 261–267 (translating Taishō 692). (English)

phags pa de bzhin gshegs pa'i gzugs brnyan bzhag pa'i phan yon yang dag par brjod pa zhes bya ba'i chos kyi rnam grangs (Derge Kangyur D 320): translated by Dharmakara, ye shes snying po; revised by ska ba dpal brtsegs (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa.title: Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa.summary: The Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa is an influential Mahāyāna sūtra expounding the inscrutable mysteries (guhya) of the Tathāgata's body (kāya), speech (vāc), and mind (citta), delivered primarily as a dialogue between Vajrapāṇi Guhyakādhipati and the Bodhisattva Śāntamati.
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa.edition: Diplomatic transcription of Asiatic Society (Kolkata) manuscript G10765 by Péter-Dániel Szántó (version 1.0, 11 December 2021), unpublished digital transcript (PDSz Sanskrit e-text corpus).
SA_K10_Āgama_Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa.coverage: fragment — Preserves text from folio [2r1] to [41?r4] of Asiatic Society manuscript G10765.
translations: Tibetan translation: D 47 (Tibetan)
Chinese translations: T 312 (佛說如來不思議祕密大乘經, tr. 法護, 惟淨, 宋 dynasty, 1004–1058); T 310 (大寶積經, tr. 菩提流志, 唐 dynasty, 693). (Chinese)

SA_K10_Āgama_Vasiṣṭhasūtra-incomplete.title: Vāsiṣṭhasūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_Vasiṣṭhasūtra-incomplete.summary: A fragmentary canonical Buddhist sūtra set in Kapilavastu in Nyagrodhārāma, recording an encounter between the Buddha and his former householder acquaintance, the brahmin Vāsiṣṭha. After questioning Vāsiṣṭha on his emaciation caused by monthly fasting (māsopavāsa), the Buddha expounds the observance and immense merit of the noble eightfold upoṣatha (āryāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgata upavāsa).
SA_K10_Āgama_Vasiṣṭhasūtra-incomplete.attribution: Canonical discourse corresponding to Tibetan Kangyur D 333 ('phags pa gnas 'jog gi mdo zhes bya ba/).
SA_K10_Āgama_Vasiṣṭhasūtra-incomplete.edition: Diplomatic transcription from Cambridge University Library manuscripts Or. 131.3 and Or. 131.5, fols. 16r4–16v and 17r–18v, by Péter-Dániel Szántó (PDSz corpus, 29 Dec 2025).
SA_K10_Āgama_Vasiṣṭhasūtra-incomplete.coverage: fragment — Manuscript transcription covering Cambridge University Library MSS Or. 131.3 and Or. 131.5, fols. 16r4–16v and 17r–18v; breaks off abruptly at segment 19 ('... etāvad udakaṃ vā u-').
translations: phags pa gnas 'jog gi mdo zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 333): translated by Sarvajñadeva, ska ba dpal brtsegs (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Āryamaitreyaparipṛcchānāmam.title: Maitreyaparipṛcchānāmamahāyānasūtra (fragment)
SA_K10_Āgama_Āryamaitreyaparipṛcchānāmam.summary: A fragmentary Sanskrit passage of the Maitreyaparipṛcchāsūtra. In the passage, Ānanda expresses wonder at Maitreya's eloquence in teaching deep doctrines, whereupon the Buddha explains that Maitreya's accomplishment is rooted in a past aeon when, as the youth Bhadraśuddha, he beheld the Buddha Jyotivikrīḍitābhijña, made the aspiration for awakening, and attained the cognitive receptivity to the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattikadharmakṣānti).
SA_K10_Āgama_Āryamaitreyaparipṛcchānāmam.coverage: fragment — Contains a fragmentary passage depicting the jātaka of Maitreya as the Brahmin youth Bhadraśuddha meeting Buddha Jyotivikrīḍitābhijña.
translations: Tibetan translation: Derge Kangyur D 85 (slight differences) (Tibetan)

SA_K10_Āgama_Śīlasaṃyuktasūtra_Vinītā_20.title: Śīlasaṃyuktasūtra
SA_K10_Āgama_Śīlasaṃyuktasūtra_Vinītā_20.summary: A short canonical Buddhist sūtra setting forth the supreme importance of moral conduct (śīla). Through similes—including comparisons to an ornament, soothing cool water, an unbroken treasure flask, and eyes necessary for sight—the Buddha teaches that entering the monastic life and seeking liberation without protecting one's ethical discipline is fundamentally futile.
SA_K10_Āgama_Śīlasaṃyuktasūtra_Vinītā_20.attribution: Canonical Buddhist discourse traditionally presented as buddhavacana.
SA_K10_Āgama_Śīlasaṃyuktasūtra_Vinītā_20.edition: Vinītā, Bhikṣuṇī (Vinita Tseng), ed. (2010). A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. 2 vols. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House; Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences, no. 9.
SA_K10_Āgama_Śīlasaṃyuktasūtra_Vinītā_20.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short sūtra, consisting of prose nidāna, 18 verses, and closing prose formula with colophon.
translations: Vinītā, Bhikṣuṇī (Vinita Tseng), trans. (2010). A Unique Collection of Twenty Sūtras in a Sanskrit Manuscript from the Potala: Editions and Translation. 2 vols. Beijing: China Tibetology Publishing House; Vienna: Austrian Academy of Sciences. (English)
tshul khrims yang dag par ldan pa'i mdo (Derge Kangyur D 303) (Tibetan)

SA_K12_Bhaṭṭaratnākara_﻿Title-Pañcākāraḥ.title: Pañcākāra (verses 4–14)
SA_K12_Bhaṭṭaratnākara_﻿Title-Pañcākāraḥ.author: Bhaṭṭaratnākara
SA_K12_Bhaṭṭaratnākara_﻿Title-Pañcākāraḥ.summary: A short Vajrayāna stotra or liturgical work comprising 14 verses (verses 4–14 surviving here) describing the five Tathāgatas, their seed-syllables (bīja), colors, families (kula), associated consorts (Locanā, Māmakī, Pāṇḍarā, Tārā, and Vajriṇī), and mudrās, resolving their symbolic manifestations into the non-dual state (yuganaddha).
SA_K12_Bhaṭṭaratnākara_﻿Title-Pañcākāraḥ.attribution: Attributed in verse 14 and the concluding colophon to Bhaṭṭaratnākara.
SA_K12_Bhaṭṭaratnākara_﻿Title-Pañcākāraḥ.coverage: partial — Verses 4–14 only; the e-text notes '[vss. 1-3 desunt]'.

SA_K12_Divākarendra_Daśākuśalakarmaphala.title: Daśākuśalakarmaphalaniścaya
SA_K12_Divākarendra_Daśākuśalakarmaphala.author: Divākarendra
SA_K12_Divākarendra_Daśākuśalakarmaphala.summary: The Daśākuśalakarmaphalaniścaya (also titled Daśākuśalakarmaphala) is a Buddhist didactic verse work in 11 chapters (117 verses) attributed to Divākarendra (possibly Divākaracandra). Drawing directly on the Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra, it presents the specific retributions and infernal torments that result from each of the ten unwholesome actions (daśākuśalakarmapatha), concluding with the rewards of refraining from them.
SA_K12_Divākarendra_Daśākuśalakarmaphala.attribution: The final colophon attributes the text to Śrī-Divākarendra. The transcriber notes this might be an error or variant for the well-known scholar Divākaracandra.
SA_K12_Divākarendra_Daśākuśalakarmaphala.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, unpublished critical transcription and edition (dated 28 December 2025), based on NAK ms. 5-92 (NGMPP A 840/2) and Cambridge University Library mss. Add. 1585 and Add. 1598, incorporating and extending Ratna Handurukande's editio princeps of the opening fragment in Kalyāṇī 5–6 (1986–1987).
SA_K12_Divākarendra_Daśākuśalakarmaphala.coverage: complete — Complete in 11 paricchedas and 117 verses, ending with the final closing colophons.

SA_K12_anon_Pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi.title: Pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi
SA_K12_anon_Pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi.summary: The Pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi is a short anonymous Vajrayāna ritual and doctrinal manual detailing the fivefold awakening (pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi). It presents the iconography, seed-syllables (bīja), mudrās, and purifications of the five Tathāgatas and their consorts, systematically mapping them onto the skandhas, bodily dhātus, and sense faculties, and concluding with verses on overcoming the five obscurations (pañcāvaraṇa).
SA_K12_anon_Pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi.attribution: Anonymous short Buddhist Tantric doctrinal and ritual manual preserved in Nepalese manuscripts.
SA_K12_anon_Pañcākārābhisaṃbodhi.coverage: complete — Complete short text opening with 'namo buddhāya' and ending with 'iti pañcākārābhisaṃbodhiḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_K12_anon_Ācāryādhikāra.title: Ācāryādhikāra
SA_K12_anon_Ācāryādhikāra.summary: The Ācāryādhikāra (also designated Daśakarmādhikāra or Karmādhikāravidhāna) is an anonymous Vajrayāna ritual manual in ten chapters setting out the duties and ritual performances of a master (ācārya). Topics include icon installation and consecration (sthāpana, pratiṣṭhā), ritual flaws and benefits (guṇadoṣokti), renovation of old sanctuaries (jīrṇoddhāra), banner raising (dhvajotsava), and architectural ground-preparation and measuring cord rituals (bhūśalyasūtranimitta). It shares text and verses with classical Buddhist ritual handbooks including the Kriyāsaṃgraha and the Supratiṣṭhāsaṃgraha.
SA_K12_anon_Ācāryādhikāra.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Oxford 2010, Kolozsvár 2015) based on palm-leaf manuscript National Archives Kathmandu (NAK) 3-380/vi (bauddhatantra 8) = NGMPP reel B 30/33, ff. 1v–9v.
SA_K12_anon_Ācāryādhikāra.coverage: complete — Complete text of the Ācāryādhikāra in 10 chapters (adhikāras), running from fol. 1v to the final colophon at fol. 9v (omitting the subsequent unrelated texts preserved in the same codex).

SA_K12_Āgama_Advayasamatāvijaya-selectio.title: Advayasamatāvijaya (selections)
SA_K12_Āgama_Advayasamatāvijaya-selectio.summary: The Advayasamatāvijayamahākalparāja is an Esoteric Buddhist tantra closely associated with the Guhyasamāja and early Anuttarayogatantra cycles. Centered on the realization of the non-dual equality (advayasamatā) of all dharmas, it details maṇḍala visualization, mantra sequences, and ritual procedures delivered by Vajrapāṇi and Samantabhadra. This e-text comprises selected chapters and passages based on Fan Muyou's edition of the unique Sanskrit palm-leaf codex preserved in the Tibet Autonomous Region.
SA_K12_Āgama_Advayasamatāvijaya-selectio.attribution: Canonical Buddhist tantra traditionally framed as a dialogue and revelation involving Vajrapāṇi / Vajradhara and the Tathāgatas.
SA_K12_Āgama_Advayasamatāvijaya-selectio.coverage: partial — Selected passages and chapters (incorporating colophons of chs. 1, 3–6, 8, 9, 12–14, 16, 18–22) up to the concluding work colophon at fol. 14b, with folio 1 missing at the start.

SA_T01_Advayavajra_Caturmudrāniścayaānva.title: Caturmudrānvaya
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Caturmudrāniścayaānva.author: Advayavajra
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Caturmudrāniścayaānva.summary: The Caturmudrānvaya is an influential Vajrayāna doctrinal treatise elucidating the nature, order, and experiential results of the four seals (caturmudrā: karmamudrā, dharmamudrā, mahāmudrā, and samayamudrā) alongside the four joys (ānanda) and four moments (kṣaṇa). Drawing on passages from the Hevajratantra, it clarifies that genuine innate bliss (sahaja) cannot be produced purely through the conditioned karmamudrā, but requires the realization of the dharmamudrā leading to mahāmudrā.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Caturmudrāniścayaānva.attribution: Included as text no. 8 in Advayavajra's works (Advayavajrasaṃgraha). However, an editorial note records that some manuscripts add 'kṛtir iyaṃ Nāgārjunapādānām' and notes Rāmapāla's citation: 'ācāryaNāgārjunapādakṛtaCaturmudrānvayānugataṃ Sekanirdeśaṃ'.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Caturmudrāniścayaānva.edition: Mikkyou-seiten-kenkyūkai (ed.), 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha (2)', Taisho Daigaku Sougou Bukkyou Kenkyūjo Nenpou [Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University], 1989, pp. (92/253)–(106/239); collated with MM Hara Prasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, GOS 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Caturmudrāniścayaānva.coverage: complete — Complete text expounding the four mudrās (karmamudrā, dharmamudrā, mahāmudrā, samayamudrā), ending with the colophon 'samayamudrāpuruṣakāraphalanirdeśaś caturthaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātana.title: Kudṛṣṭinirghātana
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātana.author: Advayavajra
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātana.summary: The Kudṛṣṭinirghātana ('Eradication of False Views') is the opening text of the Advayavajrasaṃgraha corpus attributed to the 11th-century master Advayavajra (Maitrīpāda). The treatise refutes nihilistic misunderstandings of emptiness by outlining the ādikarma (the primary daily liturgical practice incumbent upon both beginners and advanced bodhisattvas), covering poṣadha observances, the moulding of miniature clay stupas (sañcaka / tsa-tsa), scriptural recitations, and dedication of merit within an integrated Mahāyāna and tantric soteriological framework.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātana.attribution: Advayavajra is also identified in the Tibetan tradition with the mahāsiddha Maitrīpāda / Maitrīpa (ca. late 10th to 11th century).
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātana.edition: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai 密教經典研究會 (ed.), 'Kudṛṣṭinirghātana', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō (Annual of The Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University) 10 (1988), pp. (10/225)–(36/199); collated with Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātana.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 41 verses with interspersed prose sections, concluding with colophon '|| kudṛṣṭinirghātanaṃ samāptam iti ||'.
translations: Glenn Wallis, 'Advayavajra's Instructions on the Ādikarma', Pacific World: Journal of the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Third Series (2004). (English)

SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātanādivā.title: Kudṛṣṭinirghātādivākyaṭippinikā
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātanādivā.author: Advayavajra
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātanādivā.summary: The Kudṛṣṭinirghātādivākyaṭippinikā is an extremely brief prose gloss (ṭippinikā) by Advayavajra explaining key Mahāyāna doctrinal terminology associated with his Kudṛṣṭinirghāta. It defines three developmental stages of the path (the causal state [hetvavasthā], the fruition state [phalāvasthā], and the state of activity for sentient beings [sattvārthakriyāvasthā]), lists the four causes of bodhicitta, and enumerates the ten pāramitās and five masteries (vaśitā).
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātanādivā.attribution: Traditional attribution to Advayavajra confirmed by the colophon.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātanādivā.edition: Critical collation by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on: (1) Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927; and (2) Mikkyō-seiten-kenkyūkai (ed.), 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha: Sanskrit Texts (1)', Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University (Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō) 10 (1988), pp. (38/197)–(40/195).
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Kudṛṣṭinirghātanādivā.coverage: complete — Complete short gloss in 36 segments (2 verses and prose commentary), including the colophon.

SA_T01_Advayavajra_Nairātmyāprakāśa.title: Nairātmyāprakāśa
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Nairātmyāprakāśa.author: Advayavajra
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Nairātmyāprakāśa.summary: The Nairātmyāprakāśa is a Vajrayāna ritual manual (sādhana) composed by Advayavajra (Maitrīpa) on the practice of the goddess Nairātmyā, the consort of Hevajra. The work outlines the visualization of the celestial mansion (kūṭāgāra), the eight charnel grounds (aṣṭa śmaśānāni), and the retinue of fifteen yoginīs, guiding the practitioner through both the creation and completion stages (utpattikrama and utpannakrama), sexual yoga (kakkola-bola union), and bali offerings.
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Nairātmyāprakāśa.attribution: Advayavajra is identified in scholarship with Maitrīpa. The Tibetan translation (D 1308) attributes the work to Maitrīpa (dpal paN+Di ta gnyis su med pa'i rdo rje).
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Nairātmyāprakāśa.edition: Unpublished draft edition by Ryan Conlon based on the Ngor codex; distributed in the Péter-Dániel Szántó e-text corpus (release PDSz_202608).
SA_T01_Advayavajra_Nairātmyāprakāśa.coverage: complete — Complete work in 65 segments, preserving the initial namaskāra, the full ritual practice (generation and completion stages), closing verse dedications, and final colophon.
translations: bdag med ma'i rab tu gsal ba (Derge Tengyur D 1308): translated by Vajrapāṇi, mtshur ston ye shes 'byung gnas (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Amṛtavajra_Dohākoṣaṭīkā-to-the-do.title: Dohākoṣa with Dohākoṣaṭīkā
SA_T01_Amṛtavajra_Dohākoṣaṭīkā-to-the-do.author: Kāṇha, Amṛtavajra
SA_T01_Amṛtavajra_Dohākoṣaṭīkā-to-the-do.summary: The Dohākoṣa of Kāṇha comprises Apabhraṃśa couplets. Amṛtavajra's Sanskrit commentary (Dohākoṣaṭīkā, preserved in Tibetan as Toh 2302) provides an Anuttarayogatantra hermeneutical framework, glossing the vernacular verses through internal subtle-body yoga (specifically prāṇa movement through the avadhūtī channel) and correlating them with scriptural citations from tantric literature.
SA_T01_Amṛtavajra_Dohākoṣaṭīkā-to-the-do.attribution: The root verses are attributed to Kāṇha (also referred to in the commentary and colophons as Kṛṣṇapāda, Caryāvajra, or Caryāpāda). The commentary is attributed to Amṛtavajra (colophon: kṛtir iyaṃ paṇḍitaamṛtavajrasya; verse 2: viduṣāmṛtavajreṇa). In the Tibetan tradition (Toh 2302), the commentator's name is rendered as 'Od dpag med (*Amitābha) or Dpag med rdo rje (*Amitavajra).
SA_T01_Amṛtavajra_Dohākoṣaṭīkā-to-the-do.edition: Dohākoṣaṭīkā of Amṛtavajra, in Dhīḥ: Journal of Rare Buddhist Texts Research Unit, vol. 32, Sarnath, Varanasi: CIHTS, 2001, pp. 127–155.
SA_T01_Amṛtavajra_Dohākoṣaṭīkā-to-the-do.coverage: complete — Text of the dohās of Kāṇha along with Amṛtavajra's commentary, concluding with the scribal colophon of Rūparāja.
translations: Shahidullah, Muhammad. Les Chants mystiques de Kāṇha et de Saraha. Paris: Adrien-Maisonneuve, 1928. (French)
dpal nag po rdo rje zhabs kyi do ha mdzod kyi rgya cher 'grel pa (Derge Tengyur D 2302) (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Śokavinodana.title: Śokavinodana
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Śokavinodana.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Śokavinodana.summary: The Śokavinodana ('Dispelling Grief') is a short Buddhist homiletic work of 40 verses in anuṣṭubh meter attributed to Aśvaghoṣa. Designed to console someone suffering from the loss of a loved one, it meditates on the universality of impermanence (anityatā), the inevitability of death across all realms of existence, and the deceptive nature of saṃsāric relations across lifetimes, concluding with an exhortation to turn toward liberation (mokṣa).
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Śokavinodana.attribution: Ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa in the Tibetan Tengyur (Toh 4177 / Toh 4505).
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Śokavinodana.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 40 anuṣṭubh verses (numbered 1–40).
translations: mya ngan bsal ba (Derge Tengyur D 4177): translated by Ajitaśrībhadra, shAkya 'od (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Ṣaḍgatikārikāḥ_Okano_20.title: Ṣaḍgatikārikā
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Ṣaḍgatikārikāḥ_Okano_20.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Ṣaḍgatikārikāḥ_Okano_20.summary: The Ṣaḍgatikārikā is a concise versified Buddhist handbook of 105 stanzas describing the realms of cyclic existence and the karmic causes leading to them, concluding with verses on moral practice. The closing line indicates the verses were drawn from the Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra.
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Ṣaḍgatikārikāḥ_Okano_20.attribution: Colophon attributes the text to Mahāpaṇḍita Aśvaghoṣa, while stating that the stanzas were culled from the Saddharmasmṛtyupasthānasūtra ('āryasaddharmasmṛtyupasthānamahāyānasūtrāntāt samākṛṣṭā mahāpaṇḍitāśvaghoṣeṇa ṣaḍgatikārikāḥ samāptāḥ'). Also associated with D 4179. The Tibetan translation (D 4179) attributes the work to Dhārmikasubhūtighoṣa (btsun pa chos ldan rab 'byor dbyangs).
SA_T01_Aśvaghoṣa_Ṣaḍgatikārikāḥ_Okano_20.coverage: complete — Complete text of 105 verses covering the six destinies and concluding moral exhortations.
translations: dam pa'i chos dran pa nye bar gzhag pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa (Derge Tengyur D 4179): translated by Dharmakara, Devendrarakṣita (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Cakrasaṃvaratantram_D.title: Cakrasaṃvaratantra with Cakrasaṃvaravivṛti
SA_T01_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Cakrasaṃvaratantram_D.author: Bhavabhaṭṭa
SA_T01_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Cakrasaṃvaratantram_D.summary: The Cakrasaṃvaratantra (or Śrīherukābhidhāna) is a foundational Yoginītantra in 51 chapters centered on the semi-wrathful deity Heruka/Cakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī. It treats maṇḍala rites, internal subtle-body yoga, deity mantras, and antinomian yogic discipline (caryāvrata). This e-text provides the complete root scripture accompanied by the Cakrasaṃvaravivṛti of Bhavabhaṭṭa, one of the oldest and most influential surviving Sanskrit commentaries on the Cakrasaṃvara cycle.
SA_T01_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Cakrasaṃvaratantram_D.attribution: The root tantra is considered canonical buddhabhāṣita (revealed by Heruka / Vajradhara). The commentary is attributed in chapter and concluding colophons to Paṇḍitācārya Bhavabhaṭṭa (e.g. line 3734: 'paṇḍitācārya bhavabhaṭṭakṛtā śrīcakrasaṃvarapañjikā samāpteti').
SA_T01_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Cakrasaṃvaratantram_D.edition: Janardan Shastri Pandey (ed.), Śrīherukābhidhānam Cakrasaṃvaratantram with the Vivṛti Commentary of Bhavabhaṭṭa, 2 vols., Rare Buddhist Texts Series 26, Sarnath, Varanasi: Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, 2002.
SA_T01_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Cakrasaṃvaratantram_D.coverage: complete — Complete in 51 chapters (paṭalas 1–51), ending with the final chapter colophon at line 3733 ('iti śrīcakrasaṃvaravivṛtāve kapañcāśattamaḥ paṭalaḥ samāptaḥ || 51 ||') and concluding verses.

SA_T01_Candragomin_Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃ.title: Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃśikā (Sanskrit testimonia and Tibetan)
SA_T01_Candragomin_Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃ.author: Candragomin
SA_T01_Candragomin_Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃ.summary: A work by Candragomin outlining the bodhisattva vows (saṃvara). This e-text compiles the extant Sanskrit verses available in testimonia alongside the Tibetan translation (D4081).
SA_T01_Candragomin_Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃ.edition: Kano, Li, Ye 2015; Tibetan: D4081 (see ed. Fujita)
SA_T01_Candragomin_Bodhisattvasaṃvaraviṃ.coverage: partial — Preserves verses in Sanskrit testimonia along with canonical Tibetan text (D4081).
translations: byang chub sems dpa'i sdom pa nyi shu pa (Derge Tengyur D 4081) (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Candragomin_Praṇidhāna_Ye_2020.title: Praṇidhāna
SA_T01_Candragomin_Praṇidhāna_Ye_2020.author: Candragomin
SA_T01_Candragomin_Praṇidhāna_Ye_2020.summary: The Praṇidhāna (or Candragomipraṇidhāna) is an aspiration hymn attributed to the Mahāyāna master Candragomin. Across 13 verses, the practitioner vows to obtain fortunate rebirths with physical, moral, and intellectual qualities conducive to Buddhist practice, and to maintain ethical conduct, bodhicitta, and compassion until achieving awakening. An appended set of three verses in a manuscript witness summarizes the correlation between the perfections (pāramitā) and the bodhisattva stages (bhūmi).
SA_T01_Candragomin_Praṇidhāna_Ye_2020.attribution: Attributed to Candragomin. Preserved in Tibetan translation in the Tengyur under D 4386.
SA_T01_Candragomin_Praṇidhāna_Ye_2020.coverage: complete — Contains 13 verses ending with colophon 'Candragomipraṇidhānaṃ samāptam', followed by 3 additional verses (vv. 14–16) from a new manuscript witness (annotated as parallel to D 1395).
translations: btsun pa zla ba'i smon lam zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 4386): translated by Jetakarṇa, thar pa lo tsA ba nyi ma rgyal mtshan; at rab tu bsngags pa'i gnas chen po nye ba'i 'thung gcod dpal bal po yam bu'i grong khyer (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Cūḍā-bhikṣuṇī_Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra.title: Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra
SA_T01_Cūḍā-bhikṣuṇī_Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra.author: Cūḍā
SA_T01_Cūḍā-bhikṣuṇī_Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra.summary: The Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra is a short six-verse praise of Śākyamuni Buddha composed by the Buddhist nun Cūḍā. It invokes the Buddha's visit in connection with Svayambhū and Nepal, and celebrates his past deeds (such as Mahāsattva offering himself to the tigress, and merchant Supriya). The transcribed file also contains an Āryaprajñāpāramitāmantradhāraṇī and a five-verse Śrīprajñāpāramitāstuti.
SA_T01_Cūḍā-bhikṣuṇī_Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra.attribution: The Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra names Cūḍā in verse 6 ('sābhilāṣā mudā cūḍātiṣṭhad ekāntam añjaliḥ'). The author is recorded in source metadata as Cūḍā bhikṣuṇī.
SA_T01_Cūḍā-bhikṣuṇī_Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra.edition: Diplomatic transcription from Nepalese manuscript BDRC Nepalese Ms. I1NPL38 by Péter-Dániel Szántó (PDSz_202608).
SA_T01_Cūḍā-bhikṣuṇī_Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra.coverage: complete — Complete text of the 6-verse Śrīśākyasiṃhastotra, accompanied in the transcribed manuscript section by an Āryaprajñāpāramitāmantradhāraṇī and the 5-verse Śrīprajñāpāramitāstuti.

SA_T01_Kṣmādevī-Pṛthivī_Śākyasiṃhastotra.title: Śākyasiṃhastotra
SA_T01_Kṣmādevī-Pṛthivī_Śākyasiṃhastotra.summary: The Śākyasiṃhastotra is a short Buddhist devotional stotra of 23 verses preserved within a Nepalese Jātakamālā manuscript tradition. Attributed in the narrative frame to the Earth goddess Kṣmādevī (Pṛthivī), it praises the Buddha Śākyasiṃha by surveying his past bodhisattva lives and exemplary deeds (including the births as Viśvantara, Maitrībala, and the hare) before concluding with a protective phalaśruti.
SA_T01_Kṣmādevī-Pṛthivī_Śākyasiṃhastotra.attribution: Traditional attribution to the Earth goddess Kṣmādevī (Pṛthivī) as the speaker of the hymn embedded within a Nepalese Jātakamālā manuscript witness (colophon: iti śrījātakamālāyāṃ kṣmādevīkṛtaṃ śrīśākyasiṃhastotraṃ samāptam).
SA_T01_Kṣmādevī-Pṛthivī_Śākyasiṃhastotra.edition: Diplomatic transcription from Nepalese manuscript witness BDRC I1NPL38 by Péter-Dániel Szántó (unpublished e-text).
SA_T01_Kṣmādevī-Pṛthivī_Śākyasiṃhastotra.coverage: complete — Complete hymn of 23 verses followed by a closing colophon.

SA_T01_Nāgabuddhi_Karmāntavibhāga_Tanaka.title: Karmāntavibhāga (Sanskrit fragments and Tibetan text)
SA_T01_Nāgabuddhi_Karmāntavibhāga_Tanaka.author: Nāgabuddhi
SA_T01_Nāgabuddhi_Karmāntavibhāga_Tanaka.summary: The Karmāntavibhāga is an esoteric tantric treatise associated with the Guhyasamāja Ārya lineage and attributed to Nāgabuddhi. It expounds the stages of dissolution of the material elements, sense faculties, and mental factors (prakṛtyābhāsa) into the clear light (prabhāsvara). In this e-text, the surviving Sanskrit verse fragments extracted from the Vajrācāryanayottama are presented alongside the full Tibetan canonical translation.
SA_T01_Nāgabuddhi_Karmāntavibhāga_Tanaka.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to 'phags pa klu'i blo'i zhabs (Ārya Nāgabuddhi).
SA_T01_Nāgabuddhi_Karmāntavibhāga_Tanaka.edition: Tanaka, Kimiaki. 2021. Appendix II, pp. 90–91 (Sanskrit fragments of the Karmāntavibhāga from the Vajrācāryanayottama collated with Degé Tengyur D 1811); with emendations by Péter-Dániel Szántó.
SA_T01_Nāgabuddhi_Karmāntavibhāga_Tanaka.coverage: partial — Contains the complete Tibetan canonical translation (Degé Tengyur D 1811, ff. 146a1–147a1) interlined with surviving Sanskrit verse fragments identified in Tanaka 2021.
translations: las kyi mtha' rnam par 'byed pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1811): translated by Maṇikaśrījñāna, Revendra, chag lo tsA ba chos rje dpal (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Buddhabhaṭṭārakasya-Daṇ.title: Buddhabhaṭṭārakasya daṇḍakavṛttena stotram
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Buddhabhaṭṭārakasya-Daṇ.author: Nāgārjuna
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Buddhabhaṭṭārakasya-Daṇ.summary: Devotional hymn (stotra) in daṇḍaka metre praising the Buddha, enumerating his conquest of the four Māras, his bodily marks, and other qualities.
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Buddhabhaṭṭārakasya-Daṇ.attribution: Ascribed to Nāgārjuna in source headers and Tanjur (P 4604).
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Buddhabhaṭṭārakasya-Daṇ.coverage: partial — Text excerpt contains opening portion of the stotra in daṇḍaka metre.

SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Kalyāṇakāmadhenu-and-°v.title: Kalyāṇakāmadhenu with Kalyāṇakāmadhenuvivaraṇa
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Kalyāṇakāmadhenu-and-°v.author: Nāgārjuna
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Kalyāṇakāmadhenu-and-°v.summary: The Kalyāṇakāmadhenu and its Vivaraṇa is a tantric compendium of 41 verses accompanied by auto-commentary attributed to Nāgārjuna. It details mantric and ritual applications (vidhi, siddhi) centered on various deities and mantras, including the Siddhaikavīra tradition, encompassing rites of pacification, protection, subjugation, and prosperity.
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Kalyāṇakāmadhenu-and-°v.attribution: Traditionally attributed in the Tibetan Tengyur (D 3067) to Nāgārjuna (Klu-sgrub). Both the root kārikās and the vivaraṇa commentary are traditionally ascribed to him.
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Kalyāṇakāmadhenu-and-°v.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, unpublished diplomatic transcription and critical reconstruction of the Kalyāṇakāmadhenu and its Vivaraṇa based on NAK 3-363 vi. jātaka I = NGMPP A 38/13 ff. 3–11r (dated 1104 CE), fol. 4 in NAK 5-20 = NGMPP A 47/17, fol. 5 in Rome, Sankrtyayan (1937) / Dhīḥ 26, and Tibetan D 3067 (completed 23.xii.2025).
SA_T01_Nāgārjuna_Kalyāṇakāmadhenu-and-°v.coverage: complete — Complete in 41 verses with commentary. Lacunae in the first two verses and initial commentary are supplied from Sankrtyayan (1937) / Dhīḥ 26 and the Tibetan translation (D 3067).
translations: dge ba'i 'dod 'jo (Derge Tengyur D 3067): translated by Kṛṣṇa, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_Paramārthasevā-frag-282.title: Paramārthasevā (fragment: verses 282cd–293ab)
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_Paramārthasevā-frag-282.author: Puṇḍarīka
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_Paramārthasevā-frag-282.summary: A Sanskrit manuscript fragment of the Paramārthasevā attributed to Puṇḍarīka (Padma dkar po). Preserved on a single manuscript folio (vv. 282cd–293ab), the verses critique rival ascetic traditions, discussing yajñopavīta, parivrājaka, tridaṇḍin, ekadaṇḍin, and other practices.
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_Paramārthasevā-frag-282.edition: Diplomatic transcript with editorial emendations and collation against the Tibetan translation by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on National Archives Kathmandu MS A 933/1, exp. 172 (lower) – 173 (upper), fol. 31 (PDSz corpus, release PDSz_202608).
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_Paramārthasevā-frag-282.coverage: fragment — Preserves verses 282cd–293ab only, from a single folio (fol. 31) of MS A 933/1.
translations: dpal don dam pa'i bsnyen pa (Derge Tengyur D 1348): translated by Somanātha, 'bro lo tsA ba shes rab grags pa (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_﻿Paramārthasevā.title: Paramārthasevā
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_﻿Paramārthasevā.author: Puṇḍarīka
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_﻿Paramārthasevā.summary: The Paramārthasevā is a Buddhist work in 344 verses attributed to Puṇḍarīka. It opens with homage to Śākyasiṃha, Maitreyanātha, Mañjughoṣa, and Vajradhara, discussing the ṣaḍdarśana and the realization of supreme reality (paramārthasevā).
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_﻿Paramārthasevā.attribution: Attributed in the colophon (kṛtir iyaṃ śrīpuṇḍarīkapādānām) to Puṇḍarīka.
SA_T01_Puṇḍarīka_﻿Paramārthasevā.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved across 344 stanzas, with textual notes, lacunae markers, and critical apparatus.

SA_T01_Ravigupta_Lokasaṃvyavahārapravṛtt.title: Lokasaṃvyavahārapravṛtti
SA_T01_Ravigupta_Lokasaṃvyavahārapravṛtt.author: Ravigupta
SA_T01_Ravigupta_Lokasaṃvyavahārapravṛtt.summary: A Buddhist nīti (didactic/gnomic) work in 293 verses by Ravigupta, focusing on social conduct, worldly wisdom, discerning the virtues of the noble from the traits of the wicked, and moral discernment.
SA_T01_Ravigupta_Lokasaṃvyavahārapravṛtt.attribution: Ascribed to Ravigupta; corresponds to Tibetan D 4331.
SA_T01_Ravigupta_Lokasaṃvyavahārapravṛtt.coverage: complete — Contains 293 verses, ending with verse 24 = 293.

SA_T01_Sahajavajra_.title: Sthitisamāsa (with lacunae)
SA_T01_Sahajavajra_.author: Sahajavajra
SA_T01_Sahajavajra_.summary: The Sthitisamāsa is a doxographical verse work by Sahajavajra, disciple of Maitrīpāda/Maitrīgupta. It covers the Sautrāntika, Madhyamaka, and tantric/mantra teachings.
SA_T01_Sahajavajra_.attribution: Sahajavajra, disciple of Matrīpāda/Maitrīgupta. The Sanskrit is preserved in Nepal (NAK 5/139 = NGMPP B 24/4). The Tibetan translation is in the Derge Tanjur (Tōh. 2227), translated by Dhiriśrījñāna and Rma ban Chos 'bar, and revised by Bar ston, Bla ma Rgya gar ba, and Mtshur Lo tsā ba.
