SA_T01_Saroruhavajra_Hevajrabhaṭṭārakaca.title: Hevajrabhaṭṭārakacakraviṃśikāstotra
SA_T01_Saroruhavajra_Hevajrabhaṭṭārakaca.author: Saroruhavajra
SA_T01_Saroruhavajra_Hevajrabhaṭṭārakaca.summary: The Hevajrabhaṭṭārakacakraviṃśikāstotra is a twenty-verse hymn (viṃśikāstotra) attributed to the Mahāsiddha Saroruhavajra (Saroruhapāda) in praise of the eight-faced, sixteen-armed Hevajra and the goddesses of his retinue (Gaurī, Caurī, Vettālī, Ghasmarī, Pukkasī, Śavarī, Caṇḍālī, and Ḍombī). The hymn describes the iconographical traits, symbolic seed-syllables, and ultimate Mahāsukha realization associated with the Hevajramaṇḍala.
SA_T01_Saroruhavajra_Hevajrabhaṭṭārakaca.attribution: The colophon names the author as Siddhācārya Saroruhapāda (kṛtir iyaṃ siddhācāryasaroruhapādānām iti).
SA_T01_Saroruhavajra_Hevajrabhaṭṭārakaca.coverage: complete — Complete hymn consisting of 21 verses (20 stanzas in praise of Hevajra and his mandala retinue plus 1 dedication stanza) and concluding colophon.
translations: kye rdo rje'i bstod pa (Derge Tengyur D 1222) (Tibetan)
dpal kye rdo rje'i b+ha Da rA ga'i bstod pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1225): translated by Gayādhara, 'brog mi lo tsA ba shAkya ye shes (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Vajraḍākadaṇḍakastotra_CUL.title: Vajraḍākastotradaṇḍaka
SA_T01_Vajraḍākadaṇḍakastotra_CUL.author: Dharmakīrti
SA_T01_Vajraḍākadaṇḍakastotra_CUL.summary: This is an ornate hymn in four long daṇḍaka stanzas to Vajraḍāka/Heruka Cakrasaṃvara. Stanza 1 describes the deity's iconography: blue-black, four-faced and twelve-armed, trampling Bhairava and Kālarātri, embracing Vajravārāhī. Stanza 2 praises him with his retinue of the four ḍākinīs (Ḍākinī, Lāmā, Khaṇḍarohā, Rūpiṇī) and the goddesses of the intermediate directions. Stanza 3 praises him as the nondual embodiment of the three bodies of a buddha. Stanza 4 evokes the eight charnel grounds and dedicates the merit of the praise to the awakening of beings.
SA_T01_Vajraḍākadaṇḍakastotra_CUL.attribution: The Tibetan Tanjur colophon attributes the hymn to Dharmakīrti, 'crown jewel of the logicians' (rtog ge ba'i tshogs kyi gtsug gi nor bu slob dpon chen po dpal ldan chos kyi grags pa). The Tibetan translation is by Maṇikaśrījñāna and Dpal gyi mtha' can (Chos rje dpal).
SA_T01_Vajraḍākadaṇḍakastotra_CUL.edition: Transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó from Cambridge University Library manuscripts: Or. 722.4 (single-folio fragment) and Add. 1697.7 (complete ms.). Collated with the Tibetan translation in the Derge Tanjur, Tôh. no. 1442, vol. WA, folios 242r.4-243v.6.
SA_T01_Vajraḍākadaṇḍakastotra_CUL.coverage: complete — All four numbered daṇḍaka stanzas are present, ending with '|| 4 ||' and the colophon 'śrīcakrasamvaradaṇḍakastuti samāpta'. Stanza 1 begins from CUL Or. 722.4 (a single-folio fragment) and is completed from CUL Add. 1697.7. Each Sanskrit stanza is followed by the Derge Tibetan translation with Derge folio markers ({242a5} ... {243b6}), and the Tibetan colophon and the translators' syllable count are included at the end.
translations: Dpal rdo rje mkha' 'gro'i bstod pa rgyun chags, tr. Maṇikaśrījñāna and Dpal gyi mtha' can (Chos rje dpal), Derge Tanjur Tôh. 1442 (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Vanaratna_Göttingen-Xc-1440b.title: Acalābhisamayasuratābhidhāna (folios 2–9)
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Göttingen-Xc-1440b.author: Vanaratna
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Göttingen-Xc-1440b.summary: The Acalābhisamayasuratābhidhāna is a Tantric ritual and visualization manual (abhisamaya / sādhana) centered on Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa (Acala), composed by Vanaratna. The work details the preliminary visualizations (including the four immeasurables), the generation of the deity mandala and retinue, mantra recitation, and subtle yoga (sūkṣmayoga). This e-text is a diplomatic transcription of the Göttingen palm-leaf manuscript (folios 2–9), with missing portions supplied from the Tibetan Tanjur translation.
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Göttingen-Xc-1440b.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Vanaratna (Nags kyi rin chen), composed at the request of Sarvamitra (sarba mi tra) and others; translated into Tibetan by Gzhon nu dpal.
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Göttingen-Xc-1440b.edition: Diplomatic transcription based on manuscript Göttingen Xc 14/40b, collated with the Tibetan translation in the Derge Tanjur (Tōh. 1783, rgyud, sha 285b2–291a7).
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Göttingen-Xc-1440b.coverage: partial — Preserves folios 2–9 of a 9-folio manuscript (folio 1 is missing in the Sanskrit witness; folio 2 begins mid-sentence in the explanation of the four apramāṇas). Lacunae and missing sections are supplied from the canonical Tibetan Tanjur translation.
translations: mi g.yo ba'i mngon par rtogs pa rab tu dga' bar mngon par brjod pa (Derge Tengyur D 1783): translated by Vanaratna, 'gos lo tsA ba gzhon nu dpal (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Vasubandhu_Saptaguṇavarṇanā-parik.title: Saptaguṇavarṇanāparikathā
SA_T01_Vasubandhu_Saptaguṇavarṇanā-parik.author: Vasubandhu
SA_T01_Vasubandhu_Saptaguṇavarṇanā-parik.summary: A short didactic discourse (parikathā) in 19 verses attributed to Vasubandhu. The text discusses the seven qualities or blessings praised in Buddhist sūtras (long life, good health, physical beauty, good fortune, noble birth, wealth, and wisdom), illustrating how each quality is ineffective or flawed without the others, and concluding with the karmic and ethical causes required to achieve them.
SA_T01_Vasubandhu_Saptaguṇavarṇanā-parik.attribution: Attributed to Vasubandhu (slob dpon dbyig gnyen) in the Tibetan colophon.
SA_T01_Vasubandhu_Saptaguṇavarṇanā-parik.coverage: complete — Complete in 19 verses; includes parallel Tibetan verses from D 4163 / 4507 interleaved as commented lines.
translations: yon tan bdun yongs su brjod pa'i gtam (Derge Tengyur D 4163): translated by Gaṅgādhara, lo chen rin chen bzang po (Tibetan)

SA_T01_anon_Aṣṭaśmaśānāni.title: Aṣṭaśmaśānāni
SA_T01_anon_Aṣṭaśmaśānāni.summary: A brief esoteric Buddhist manual describing the eight great cremation grounds (aṣṭaśmaśāna) associated with anuttarayoga tantric meditation (specifically mentioning the practitioners of Hevajra, śrīmad-hevajrayogibhiḥ). It lists for each of the eight cardinal and intermediate directions the name of the charnel ground, the dominant tree and its spirit (maharddhika), the directional guardian (dikpati), the resident serpent (nāga), and the presiding cloud (megha).
SA_T01_anon_Aṣṭaśmaśānāni.attribution: The Tibetan canonical translation (Degé Tengyur, D 1216 / Toh 1216) attributes the work to slob dpon rnal 'byor pa (*Yogācārya / *Yogin); translated by Buddhākaravajra and 'Gos Khug pa Lhas btsas.
SA_T01_anon_Aṣṭaśmaśānāni.edition: Diplomatic transcription from manuscript Niedersächsische Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek Göttingen, Cod. ms. sansc. 257, fols. 5r1–5v4, transcribed by Ryan Conlon and included in Péter-Dániel Szántó's collection (PDSz_202608).
SA_T01_anon_Aṣṭaśmaśānāni.coverage: complete — Complete short ritual and iconographic tract transcribed from Niedersächsische Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek Göttingen, Cod. ms. sansc. 257, fols. 5r1–5v4.
translations: dur khrod brgyad kyi bshad pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1216): translated by Buddhākaravajra, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T01_anon_Catuḥstotravivaraṇa_Lumucao_.title: Catuḥstotravivaraṇa (folios 1v1–23r1)
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥstotravivaraṇa_Lumucao_.summary: An anonymous Indian Buddhist commentary (vivaraṇa) on Nāgārjuna's Catuḥstotra (Catuḥstava), preserved in a Sanskrit palm-leaf manuscript. This portion (folios 1v1–23r1), which concludes with the section colophon Nirmāṇakāyastutivṛtti, comments upon the Lokātītastava, interpreting it as praise of the Nirmāṇakāya within the Mahāyāna trikāya framework. The commentary cites sūtra and śāstra sources to elucidate Madhyamaka tenets of emptiness, non-arising, and the nature of the Buddha.
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥstotravivaraṇa_Lumucao_.attribution: The commentary is anonymous. It comments on the Lokātītastava (identified in this commentary with praise of the Nirmāṇakāya), one of the four stotras of the Catuḥstotra (Catuḥstava) attributed to Nāgārjuna.
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥstotravivaraṇa_Lumucao_.edition: Lumucao (鲁木草), edition of the Sanskrit manuscript of the Catuḥstotravivaraṇa (2021 [pp. 112ff.], 2023, 2024), covering 1v1–23r1.
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥstotravivaraṇa_Lumucao_.coverage: partial — Contains folios 1v1 to 23r1 of the 47-folio manuscript, covering the opening verses and the commentary ending at the section colophon 'nirmmāṇakāyastutivṛttiḥ'. The overall work finishes on folio 47v4 with 'catu(ḥ)strotravivaraṇaṃ samāptaṃ'.

SA_T01_anon_Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda_Isaacso.title: Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda_Isaacso.summary: The Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda is an extremely short anonymous tantric text treating subtle chronometrical measurement and respiration. It computes the division of the 21,600 daily breaths (prāṇa) during an ahorātra (day and night) across sixty-four time units (daṇḍa/ghaṭikā). The text survives in a Sanskrit manuscript witness and is preserved in Tibetan translation in the Tengyur (Toh 1210).
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda_Isaacso.attribution: Anonymous short tantric text on subtle chronometry and respiration.
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda_Isaacso.edition: HSS 24, 204v2–204v4; transcribed in full in Isaacson 2009
SA_T01_anon_Catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍabheda_Isaacso.coverage: complete — Complete short text of a single segment/paragraph concluding with 'catuḥṣaṣṭidaṇḍasya bhedaḥ samāptaḥ'.
translations: dbyu gu drug cu rtsa bzhi'i bshad pa (Derge Tengyur D 1210): translated by Ratnavajra, 'brog mi lo tsA ba shAkya ye shes (Tibetan)

SA_T01_anon_Legend-of-Śāntideva_Jong_197.title: Legend of Śāntideva
SA_T01_anon_Legend-of-Śāntideva_Jong_197.summary: A short anonymous Sanskrit hagiographical narrative recounting the legendary life of the celebrated 8th-century Madhyamaka master Śāntideva. It relates his birth as prince to King Mañjuvarman, his renunciation following his mother's warning, spiritual attainment under the siddha Mañjuvajra, service as a royal bodyguard (under the name Acalasena) armed with a wooden sword, and admission to the Nālandā monastery under the name Śāntideva (nicknamed Bhusuku). The account culminates in his recitation of the Bodhicaryāvatāra, his levitation into the sky upon reciting 9.34 (9.35), and the subsequent discovery of his written works (including the Bodhicaryāvatāra and Śikṣāsamuccaya) in his monastic cell.
SA_T01_anon_Legend-of-Śāntideva_Jong_197.attribution: Preserved in a manuscript scribed by Bhikṣu Śrīkīrtipaṇḍita of Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa. It is similar to Vibhūticandra's introduction in D 3880.
SA_T01_anon_Legend-of-Śāntideva_Jong_197.coverage: complete — Contains sections I–XVI, concluding with the scribal colophon of Kīrtipaṇḍita.

SA_T01_attributed-to-Vasubandhu_Śīlapari.title: Śīlaparikathā
SA_T01_attributed-to-Vasubandhu_Śīlapari.author: Vasubandhu
SA_T01_attributed-to-Vasubandhu_Śīlapari.summary: The Śīlaparikathā is a brief moral discourse (parikathā) in 11 verses extolling the supreme value of ethical discipline (śīla). It argues that moral purity surpasses material generosity and outer ascetic practices, serving as a protective medicine, an unshakeable refuge at death, and the indispensable foundation for mental calm, insight, and liberation.
SA_T01_attributed-to-Vasubandhu_Śīlapari.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Vasubandhu in the Tibetan Tengyur (D4164 and 4508 / Toh 4164 and Toh 4508).
translations: Anathnath Basu, 'Śīlaparikathā [Tibetan Text, Sanskrit Reconstruction, English Translation and Notes]', Indian Historical Quarterly 7.1 (1931), pp. 28–33. (English)
tshul khrims kyi gtam (Derge Tengyur D 4164): translated by Janārdana, lo chen rin chen bzang po (Tibetan)

SA_T01_various_108-Buddhist-stotras_Pand.title: Bauddhastotrasaṃgraha
SA_T01_various_108-Buddhist-stotras_Pand.summary: The Bauddhastotrasaṃgraha is a collection of 108 Sanskrit Buddhist devotional hymns (stotras) compiled and edited by Janardan Shastri Pandey.
SA_T01_various_108-Buddhist-stotras_Pand.attribution: Anthology of 108 Buddhist hymns edited by Janardan Shastri Pandey.
SA_T01_various_108-Buddhist-stotras_Pand.edition: Janardan Shastri Pandey (ed.), Bauddha stotra Samgrahah, Varanasi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1994.
SA_T01_various_108-Buddhist-stotras_Pand.coverage: complete — Complete e-text containing 108 stotras (BuSto_1 through BuSto_108) of the collection.

SA_T01_Ānandagarbha_Vajrasattvodayā.title: Vajrasattvodayā (fragment)
SA_T01_Ānandagarbha_Vajrasattvodayā.author: Ānandagarbha
SA_T01_Ānandagarbha_Vajrasattvodayā.summary: A Yoga Tantra sādhana and ritual manual dedicated to the propitiation of Vajrasattva according to the system of the Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha (STTS). Composed by Ānandagarbha, the text outlines the practitioner's inner purification, mantra recitations, and the binding of protective seals (mudrās) within the Vajradhātu mandala. While the complete text survives in Tibetan translation (Tōh. 2517), this Sanskrit transcription represents a manuscript fragment containing its opening portion.
SA_T01_Ānandagarbha_Vajrasattvodayā.attribution: Attributed to Ānandagarbha in the notes of the manuscript/transcription and in Tibetan canonical catalogs (Tōh. 2517 / D 2517; Otani 3340). Translated into Tibetan by Subuddhaśrīśānti and Rma Dge-ba'i blo-gros.
SA_T01_Ānandagarbha_Vajrasattvodayā.edition: Diplomatic transcription based on Kathmandu, National Archives MS NAK 5-86 (NGMPP reel B 24/34).
SA_T01_Ānandagarbha_Vajrasattvodayā.coverage: fragment — Fragment containing folios 1v–2r (breaking off at 2v with 'punar abhyantaraprā-'). Preserved in Tibetan translation (Tōh. 2517).
translations: Takahashi, Hisao (高橋 尚夫). 'Ānandagarbha saku Vajrasattvodaya-nāma-sādhanopāyikā wayaku' (アーナンダガルバ作『金剛薩埵成就法広次第』和訳) [A Japanese Translation of Ānandagarbha's Vajrasattvodaya-nāma-sādhanopāyika]. Buzan Gakuhō (豊山学報) (1997). (Japanese)
rdo rje sems dpa' 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i sgrub pa'i thabs (Derge Tengyur D 2517): translated by Buddhaśrīśānti, rma dge ba'i blo gros (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Śīlasāgara_Kaiser-Library-138-=-N.title: Carpaṭistutiṭippaṇī
SA_T01_Śīlasāgara_Kaiser-Library-138-=-N.author: Śīlasāgara
SA_T01_Śīlasāgara_Kaiser-Library-138-=-N.summary: The Carpaṭistutiṭippaṇī is a Sanskrit commentary by Śīlasāgara on the 25-verse Avalokiteśvara hymn (Carpaṭistuti or Carpaṭipādastotra) attributed to Carpaṭipāda. Composed at the prompting of Meghamahāpātra, it provides word-by-word grammatical, semantic, and doctrinal elucidations of the stotra. Śīlasāgara is known as Vanaratna's teacher.
SA_T01_Śīlasāgara_Kaiser-Library-138-=-N.attribution: The text explicitly identifies Śīlasāgara as the author in verse 2, stating it was composed at the request of Meghamahāpātra ('śrīmanmeghamahāpātrapreraṇād vihitā mayā | śrīśīlasāgareṇeyaṃ carpaṭistutiṭippaṇī'). The Tibetan translation (D 2726) attributes the work to Carpaṭi (grub thob chen po tsar+p+pa Ti).
SA_T01_Śīlasāgara_Kaiser-Library-138-=-N.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on all 25 verses of the Avalokiteśvara hymn attributed to Carpaṭipāda, concluding at verse 25 ('ity anantaroktaprakāraiś caturviṃśatibhiḥ ślokaiḥ bhagavataḥ smaraṇaṃ ... || 25 ||').
translations: phags pa spyan ras gzigs dbang phyug la tsar+p+pa Tis bstod pa (Derge Tengyur D 2726): translated by Vanaratna, 'gos lo tsA ba gzhon nu dpal (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Mṛtasugatiniyoj.title: Mṛtasugatiniyojana
SA_T01_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Mṛtasugatiniyoj.author: Śūnyasamādhivajra
SA_T01_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Mṛtasugatiniyoj.summary: The Mṛtasugatiniyojana is an 85-verse esoteric Buddhist funerary ritual manual (antyeṣṭividhāna) attributed to Śūnyasamādhivajra. The first section (vv. 1–34) details a method of post-mortem revival and transference (mṛtasaṃjīvanī) based on Guhyasamājatantra chapter 14, in which the officiant reinstalls the deceased's consciousness into the body to bestow initiation and direct it through the cranial aperture toward liberation or a pure land. The second section (vv. 34–85) details cremation and post-cremation cleansing rituals based on the Sarvadurgatipariśodhanatantra to safeguard the deceased from rebirth in bad states.
SA_T01_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Mṛtasugatiniyoj.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Paṇḍita Śrī Śūnyasamādhivajra (often vocalized as Śūnyatāsamādhivajra in the Tibetan Tengyur traditions). The Tibetan translation (D 1907) attributes the work to Śūnyatāsamādhi (dpal stong nyid ting nge 'dzin rdo rje). The Tibetan translation (D 1908) attributes the work to Śūnyatāsamādhi (dpal ting nge 'dzin rdo rje).
SA_T01_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Mṛtasugatiniyoj.edition: Unpublished transcript/diplomatic edition of Palm-leaf Tokyo composite ms. (new no. 307, old no. 306, dated NS 589 [1469 CE]), prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Oxford, summer 2008).
SA_T01_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Mṛtasugatiniyoj.coverage: complete — Complete work in 85 verses plus introductory and concluding mantras and rubrics, ending with the author colophon and a scribal dating colophon (NS 589 / 1469 CE).
translations: dpal ngan song thams cad yongs su spyang ba'i rgyud las phyung ba spyan ma'i ngan song sbyong pa'i cho ga (Derge Tengyur D 1907): translated by Vairocanavajra, chos grags (Tibetan)
tha ma'i mchod pa'i cho ga (Derge Tengyur D 1908): translated by Digīśanandana, pu rang lo chung (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.title: Āmnāyamañjarī (chapter 10)
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.author: Abhayākaragupta
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.summary: Chapter 10 (daśamī mañjarī) of Abhayākaragupta's Āmnāyamañjarī, a commentary on the Sampuṭatantra. This chapter explicates the meditation and visualization of the goddess Jñānaḍākinī and her retinue, detailing the realization of emptiness, seed-syllables, iconographic forms, mudrās, and mantra recitations.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.attribution: Firmly attributed to Abhayākaragupta. The colophon confirms: āmnāyamañjaryāṃ sampuṭaṭīkāyāṃ daśamī mañjarī.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.edition: Transcription based on facsimile ms. (folios 287r/577 to 296r/595).
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.coverage: partial — Contains only chapter 10 (daśamī mañjarī) of the Āmnāyamañjarī, covering folios 287r–296r (pp. 577–595 in the facsimile witness).
translations: dpal yang dag par sbyor ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po'i rgya cher 'grel pa man ngag gi snye ma zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1198): translated by Abhayākaragupta, tsa mi sangs rgyas grags pa, Śākyaśrībhadra, dpyal lo tsA ba chos kyi bzang po, dpang lo tsA ba blo gros brtan pa; at na le n+d+ra (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.title: Āmnāyamañjarī (chapter 11)
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.author: Abhayākaragupta
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.summary: Chapter 11 (ekādaśī mañjarī) of Abhayākaragupta's commentary Āmnāyamañjarī on the Saṃpuṭatantra. The chapter elucidates the generation stage visualization of the Nairātmyā yoginī maṇḍala, describing the cosmic emergence from elemental maṇḍalas, seed syllables, the palace (kūṭāgāra), the four yogas, and the retinue of twenty-three yoginīs.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.attribution: Firmly attributed in the colophon (āmnāyamañjaryāṃ śrīsaṃpuṭaṭīkāyām ekādaśī mañjarī) and the Tibetan canon (D 1198) to Abhayākaragupta.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Budapest, 6–7 May 2026 / PDSz release 202608), based on a facsimile manuscript.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 11 (ekādaśī mañjarī) only, commenting on the Nairātmyā yoginī maṇḍala section of the Saṃpuṭatantra (corresponding to manuscript folios 296v–308r / facsimile pages 596–619).
translations: dpal yang dag par sbyor ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po'i rgya cher 'grel pa man ngag gi snye ma zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1198): translated by Abhayākaragupta, tsa mi sangs rgyas grags pa, Śākyaśrībhadra, dpyal lo tsA ba chos kyi bzang po, dpang lo tsA ba blo gros brtan pa; at na le n+d+ra (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.title: Āmnāyamañjarī (chapter 12)
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.author: Abhayākaragupta
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.summary: The twelfth chapter (dvādaśī mañjarī) of Abhayākaragupta's Āmnāyamañjarī, an encyclopedic commentary on the Saṃpuṭodbhavatantra. This chapter deals in depth with mandala construction, ritual measurements, the visualization of the thirty-seven deity mandala of Saṃvara surrounded by the eight great cremation grounds (aṣṭamahāśmaśāna), and the attainment of Mahāmudrā.

SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Āmnāyamañjarī-ch1.summary: The Āmnāyamañjarī is Abhayākaragupta's extensive commentary on the Saṃpuṭodbhavatantra (Saṃpuṭatantra), one of the major explanatory tantras (vyākhyātantra) in Late Indian esoteric Buddhism. In this opening chapter (prathamā mañjarī), Abhayākaragupta details the hermeneutical framework of the tantra across its thirty-two chapters using the classical fivefold schema of the Vyākhyāyukti, followed by detailed exposition of the opening nidāna, the nature of Vajrasattva, and the realization of non-dual gnosis.

translations: dpal yang dag par sbyor ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po'i rgya cher 'grel pa man ngag gi snye ma zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1198): translated by Abhayākaragupta, tsa mi sangs rgyas grags pa, Śākyaśrībhadra, dpyal lo tsA ba chos kyi bzang po, dpang lo tsA ba blo gros brtan pa; at na le n+d+ra (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Mūlāpatti.title: Mūlāpatti
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Mūlāpatti.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Mūlāpatti.summary: The Mūlāpatti is a concise seven-stanza Sanskrit treatise defining the fourteen fundamental transgressions (caturdaśa mūlāpattayaḥ) in Vajrayāna Buddhist tantric ethics. The text warns against actions such as despising the guru, violating the Buddha's command, scorning fellow tantric practitioners, abandoning loving-kindness or bodhicitta, divulging secret teachings to the uninitiated, and disparaging women who embody insight (prajñātma-strī). It outlines the severe spiritual and karmic penalties of breaking these commitments and stresses the need for confession, mandalic worship, and renewed vow observance.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Mūlāpatti.attribution: Ascribed to Advayavajra as text 3 in the collected works (Advayavajrasaṃgraha).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Mūlāpatti.edition: Collated edition prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on Mikkyō-seiten-kenkyūkai (密教經典研究會), 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha (1)', Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University (Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō) 10, 1988, pp. (42/193), and Haraprasad Shastri, Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Baroda: Oriental Institute (GOS), 1927, p. 13, with two Nepalese manuscripts: msT (Tokyo colour ms., fol. 12r-v) and msN (NGMPP B 22/24, fol. 8r-v).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Mūlāpatti.coverage: complete — Complete short text of 7 verses, concluding with 'mūlāpattayaḥ samāptāḥ'.
translations: Ronald M. Davidson, Indian Esoteric Buddhism: A Social History of the Tantric Movement, New York: Columbia University Press, 2002, 414. (English)

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sthūlāpatti.title: Sthūlāpatti
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sthūlāpatti.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sthūlāpatti.summary: The Sthūlāpatti is an extremely concise four-verse tantric treatise attributed to Advayavajra. It enumerates the secondary or gross infractions (sthūlāpatti) against the Vajrayāna pledges (samaya) and instructs that a practitioner should candidly confess them without concealment before an ācārya. The work is preserved as text 4 in the Advayavajrasaṃgraha collection.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sthūlāpatti.attribution: Advayavajra is commonly identified in Tibetan and modern historiography with the Buddhist master Maitrīpa.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sthūlāpatti.edition: Critical collation by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927, p. 13; Mikkyō-seiten-kenkyūkai (ed.), Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō 10, 1988, p. (44)/191; and manuscripts ms T (Tokyo colour ms.) and ms N (NGMPP B 22/24).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sthūlāpatti.coverage: complete — Complete text of 4 verses with closing formula (sthūlāpattayaḥ samāptāḥ).

SA_T02_AjitamitraAjitamitragupta-Mi-pham.title: Arapacanamañjunāthapūjāvidhi
SA_T02_AjitamitraAjitamitragupta-Mi-pham.author: Ajitamitra
SA_T02_AjitamitraAjitamitragupta-Mi-pham.summary: A Vajrayāna pūjāvidhi ritual manual dedicated to Arapacana Mañjunātha (Mañjughoṣa). It provides instructions on purification using consecrated water, self-protection (ātmarakṣā) via the Mahāpratisarā mantra, drawing of the circular maṇḍala, invocation (āvāhana) of Mañjughoṣa, offerings to him and his retinue including Upakeśinī, balividhi, and visarjana, followed by an incomplete appended stotra on f. 5r.
SA_T02_AjitamitraAjitamitragupta-Mi-pham.attribution: Attributed in the source headers to Ajitamitra / Ajitamitragupta (Mi pham bshes gnyen).
SA_T02_AjitamitraAjitamitragupta-Mi-pham.edition: Dawa Choezom: A Sanskrit Manuscript of the Arapacanamañjunāthapūjāvidhi from Xizang (SI 1: 67ff.), supplemented by unedited verses on f. 5r.
SA_T02_AjitamitraAjitamitragupta-Mi-pham.coverage: complete — The Arapacanamañjunāthapūjāvidhi text proper ends with the colophon iti śrīmadarapacanamañjunāthapūjāvidhiḥ samāptaḥ, followed by an incomplete 4-verse stotra fragment on f. 5r.
translations: D 2716 (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Alakakalaśa_Upadeśānusāriṇī.title: Upadeśānusāriṇī (chapter 1 and beginning of chapter 2)
SA_T02_Alakakalaśa_Upadeśānusāriṇī.author: Alakakalaśa
SA_T02_Alakakalaśa_Upadeśānusāriṇī.summary: Alakakalaśa's Upadeśānusāriṇī is a commentary on the Yoginīsaṃcāratantra. It opens with an exegesis of the tantra and outlines the chapters. The e-text contains chapter 1 and the beginning of chapter 2.
SA_T02_Alakakalaśa_Upadeśānusāriṇī.coverage: partial — Introductory synopsis of the 17 chapters, chapter 1 complete, then chapter 2 up to the samyakprahāṇas (breaks off at seg. 340: '[29] svarūpaṃ punaḥ |').

SA_T02_Amanasikāraparamparā_Sylvain-Lévi.title: Amanasikāraparamparā
SA_T02_Amanasikāraparamparā_Sylvain-Lévi.summary: An Indian Buddhist tantric lineage text outlining the transmission and practical instructions of the amanasikāra ('non-mentation') tradition connected with Advayavajra (Maitrīpa) and Saraha. The work opens with a lineage chronicle (Buddhabodhisattvasiddhāmnāya) tracing teachings from Śākyamuni and sixteen Bodhisattvas down to siddhas, followed by practice instructions and a concluding liturgical section dedicated to the goddess.
SA_T02_Amanasikāraparamparā_Sylvain-Lévi.attribution: Anonymous late Indian Buddhist tantric lineage text and practice collection.
SA_T02_Amanasikāraparamparā_Sylvain-Lévi.edition: Sylvain Lévi, 'Un nouveau document sur le bouddhisme de basse époque dans l'Inde', in: Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies, University of London, Vol. 6, No. 2 (Edward James Rapson Felicitation Volume), 1931, pp. 417–429; collated with MS Kaiser Library 142 (NGMPP C 14/19) by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Oxford, July 2010).
SA_T02_Amanasikāraparamparā_Sylvain-Lévi.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved in palm-leaf manuscript Kaiser Library 142 (NGMPP C 14/19, 6 ff.), as edited by Sylvain Lévi (1931) and re-collated against the manuscript by Péter-Dániel Szántó.

SA_T02_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Catuṣpīṭhanibandha.title: Catuṣpīṭhanibandha
SA_T02_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Catuṣpīṭhanibandha.author: Bhavabhaṭṭa
SA_T02_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Catuṣpīṭhanibandha.summary: The Catuṣpīṭhanibandha is a Sanskrit commentary by Bhavabhaṭṭa on the Catuṣpīṭhatantra, centering on Jñānaḍākinī. The commentary elucidates tantric verses, detailing mandala visualization, ritual practices, subtle body channels, mantras, and technical terminology.
SA_T02_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Catuṣpīṭhanibandha.attribution: Attributed to Bhavabhaṭṭa (Tibetan canon D 1607 records author as Bhavabhadra, translators Gayadhara and 'Gos).
SA_T02_Bhavabhaṭṭa_Catuṣpīṭhanibandha.coverage: complete — Commentary on the Catuṣpīṭhatantra, from opening verses up to chapter 4.2 and final concluding stanza.
translations: rgyud kyi rgyal po dpal gdan bzhi pa'i 'grel pa dran pa'i rgyu mtshan zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1607): translated by Gayādhara, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Bhūvācārya_Samvarodayā-nāma-maṇḍa.title: Samvarodayānāmamaṇḍalopāyikā
SA_T02_Bhūvācārya_Samvarodayā-nāma-maṇḍa.author: Bhūvācārya
SA_T02_Bhūvācārya_Samvarodayā-nāma-maṇḍa.summary: The Samvarodayānāmamaṇḍalopāyikā is an extensive Vajrayāna maṇḍala ritual manual (maṇḍalavidhi) associated with the Saṃvarodayatantra in the Cakrasaṃvara tradition. Composed by Bhūvācārya at the monastic complex of Ratnagiri in Odisha, it provides comprehensive ritual procedures for maṇḍala layout, consecration (pratiṣṭhā), oblations (homa, bali), visualization, and initiation. The text is preserved in a mid-11th-century Newari palm-leaf manuscript copied at the Śrīmānadevamahāvihāra during the reign of King Baladeva.
SA_T02_Bhūvācārya_Samvarodayā-nāma-maṇḍa.attribution: The Sanskrit colophon verse 790 explicitly names Bhūvācārya ('bhūvācāryeṇa dhīmatā') as author, having composed the work while staying at Ratnagiri ('śrīmadratnagirau sthitvā'). In the Tibetan canonical records (D 1538), the author is given as Dbus-pa blo-ldan; the manuscript header notes *Bhuvamati (Bhu ba blo ldan). The Tibetan translation (D 1538) attributes the work to Bhūvācārtya (dbu ba).
SA_T02_Bhūvācārya_Samvarodayā-nāma-maṇḍa.edition: Diplomatic transcription and working edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on Tokyo University Library MS New 450 (Old 296; palm leaf, Newari script, dated Nepāla Saṃvat 174/176/178 [ca. 1054–1058 CE] under King Baladeva) with reference to the Tibetan translation.
SA_T02_Bhūvācārya_Samvarodayā-nāma-maṇḍa.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual in 790 verses plus interspersed prose and ritual mantras, ending with the author colophon and dated historical scribal colophon.
translations: dpal 'khor lo bde mchog 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga (Derge Tengyur D 1538) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_BodhigarbhaGarbhapāda_Herukasādha.title: Herukasādhana
SA_T02_BodhigarbhaGarbhapāda_Herukasādha.author: Bodhigarbha
SA_T02_BodhigarbhaGarbhapāda_Herukasādha.summary: The Herukasādhana (also known as Hevajrasādhana) is a tantric liturgical manual belonging to the Hevajra cycle, composed by Ācārya Bodhigarbha (Garbhapāda). The text instructs the practitioner on the generation stage of Heruka/Hevajra, opening with the veneration of the lineage, the selection of practice grounds (cremation grounds, isolated trees), preliminary meditations on the four brahmavihāras and emptiness, and the generation of the protection circle. It proceeds to the detailed visualization of eight-faced, sixteen-armed Heruka and the retinue of eight goddesses (Gaurī, Caurī, Vetālī, Ghasmarī, Pukkasī, Śavarī, Caṇḍālī, and Dombī), concluding with deity yoga, mantra recitation, and the yogic realization that all activities and perceptions are inseparable from Heruka.
SA_T02_BodhigarbhaGarbhapāda_Herukasādha.attribution: The Sanskrit scribal colophon attributes the work to Ācāryagarbhapāda (kṛtir iyam ācāryagarbbhapāpādānām [sic]), while the concluding verse weaves the name Bodhigarbha into the verse (śrībodhigarbhātmakāḥ). The Tibetan colophon identifies the author as Slob dpon Byang chub snying po (Bodhigarbha).
SA_T02_BodhigarbhaGarbhapāda_Herukasādha.edition: Transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on manuscript HSS 14, ff. 155v5–160r7, intercalated with the Tibetan canonical translation (Degé Tengyur, D 1227).
SA_T02_BodhigarbhaGarbhapāda_Herukasādha.coverage: complete — Complete sādhana providing the Sanskrit text from MS HSS 14 (ff. 155v5–160r7) intercalated with the Tibetan translation from Degé Tengyur D 1227.
translations: dpal kye rdo rje zhes bya ba'i sgrub pa'i thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1227): translated by Dīpaṅkaracandra, lha btsan po mu ne rA dza (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Buddhajñānapāda_Ātmasādhanāvatāra.title: Ātmasādhanāvatāra
SA_T02_Buddhajñānapāda_Ātmasādhanāvatāra.author: Buddhajñānapāda
SA_T02_Buddhajñānapāda_Ātmasādhanāvatāra.summary: The Ātmasādhanāvatāra is a major doctrinal treatise by Buddhajñānapāda (c. late 8th–early 9th century CE), founder of the Jñānapāda school of the Guhyasamājatantra. Integrating Madhyamaka epistemological analysis and Yogācāra philosophy with Anuttarayogatantra ritual principles, the text argues that saṃsāra is merely conceptual fabrication (vikalpa), refutes external reality, and defends the soteriological validity of self-worship (ātmasādhana/ātmapūjā) through identity with the maṇḍala deities.
SA_T02_Buddhajñānapāda_Ātmasādhanāvatāra.attribution: The Tibetan colophon explicitly attributes the text to Ācārya Buddhajñānapāda (slob dpon sangs rgyas ye shes), translated by Paṇḍita Śāntibhadra and Lotsāwa 'Gos Lhas btsas (Toh 1860).
SA_T02_Buddhajñānapāda_Ātmasādhanāvatāra.coverage: complete — Complete text of the work from opening mangala to the final colophon, presented in an unpublished bilingual working transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó that combines surviving Sanskrit manuscript folios with the Tibetan translation (Degé Tengyur fol. 52b2–62a7) where Sanskrit is lacunose.
translations: bdag sgrub pa la 'jug pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1860): translated by Śāntibhadra, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Buddhaśrījñāna_Prajñāpradīpāvalī_.title: Prajñāpradīpāvalī (chapter 8)
SA_T02_Buddhaśrījñāna_Prajñāpradīpāvalī_.author: Buddhaśrījñāna
SA_T02_Buddhaśrījñāna_Prajñāpradīpāvalī_.summary: The Prajñāpradīpāvalī (or Prajñāpāramitopadeśaśāstrābhisamayālaṃkāravivṛti) is an Indian commentary on the Abhisamayālaṃkāra attributed to Buddhaśrījñāna (Buddhaśrījñānapāda). The surviving Sanskrit manuscript, photographed by Rāhula Sāṅkṛtyāyana in Lhasa in 1935, covers only the eighth chapter (Dharmakāyābhisamaya) and the summary verses, dealing extensively with the four-body (caturkāya) doctrine and the enlightened activities (kāritra). Notably, the Sanskrit text diverges from the canonical Tibetan translation (Toh 3800) and displays significant textual agreement with Abhayākaragupta's Munimatālaṃkāra.
SA_T02_Buddhaśrījñāna_Prajñāpradīpāvalī_.attribution: The colophon explicitly attributes the treatise to 'vyākhyātṛ-mahāpaṇḍita-Buddhaśrījñānapāda'. Scholars note that this Sanskrit text diverges from the canonical Tibetan translation of the Prajñāpradīpāvalī (Toh 3800 / D 3800), exhibiting close parallels to Abhayākaragupta's Munimatālaṃkāra.
SA_T02_Buddhaśrījñāna_Prajñāpradīpāvalī_.edition: Kendai En'ō (健代淵応), Abhisamayālaṃkāra-śāstraṭīkā no kenkyū (『Abhisamayālaṃkāra-śāstraṭīkāの研究』). Osaka: Shitennōji-shiin Seikōin Kiyomizudera (四天王寺支院清光院清水寺), 1973.
SA_T02_Buddhaśrījñāna_Prajñāpradīpāvalī_.coverage: partial — Preserves only chapter 8 (Dharmakāyābhisamaya, ASA 8.1–40) along with the concluding 6-fold and 3-fold summary section (pp. 1–61 of Kendai's edition).
translations: Kendai En'ō, Abhisamayālaṃkāra-śāstraṭīkā no kenkyū (Osaka: Shitennōji-shiin Seikōin Kiyomizudera, 1973; contains Japanese translation and facsimile plates). (Japanese)

bcom ldan 'das ma shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i man ngag gi bstan bcos mngon par rtogs pa'i rgyan gyi 'grel pa shes rab sgron ma'i phreng ba (Derge Tengyur D 3800): translated by Buddhaśrījñāna II, khro phu lo tsA ba byams pa dpal (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Chātrakumāradatta_Cakrasamvara-wo.title: Vīravīreśvarīsaṃjñānirdeśa, Pūjāvidhi and Sādhanopadeśabhāvanāyathānukramaṭīpaṇaka on the Luyīpāda Cakrasaṃvarasādhana (Pūjāvidhi incomplete)
SA_T02_Chātrakumāradatta_Cakrasamvara-wo.author: Chātrakumāradatta
SA_T02_Chātrakumāradatta_Cakrasamvara-wo.summary: A small manuscript (CUL Or. 155) of Cakrasaṃvara texts by the lay devotee (paramopāsaka) Chātrakumāradatta, in the tradition of Luyīpāda's sādhana. It contains a list of the names of the heroes and heroines (vīra/vīreśvarī) of the Cakrasaṃvara maṇḍala; a pūjā manual; and an annotated outline of the stages of the sādhana, from the preliminary pūjā and brahmavihāras through the purification of skandhas, protective circle, emptiness, generation of the maṇḍala, consecration, nectar, nyāsa, mantra recitation and bali. The author names his guru 'residing in Kanyārāma' (Rāḍhā, Bengal) and the mahāmaṇḍalācārya Sauṣṭhavapāda; Szántó dates the toponym's attestation to c. 1100–1150 CE.
SA_T02_Chātrakumāradatta_Cakrasamvara-wo.attribution: Chātrakumāradatta describes himself as a paramopāsaka (Buddhist lay devotee) and follower of the tradition of Luyīpāda. He references his guru 'residing in Kanyārāma' (Rāḍhā, West Bengal) and the mahāmaṇḍalācārya Sauṣṭhavapāda.
SA_T02_Chātrakumāradatta_Cakrasamvara-wo.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of Cambridge University Library MS Or. 155, fols. 1r–5v, with his introductory note and emendations/conjectures (e.g. Nandadāsa). No printed edition exists.
SA_T02_Chātrakumāradatta_Cakrasamvara-wo.coverage: partial — Diplomatic transcription of Cambridge University Library MS Or. 155 (fols. 1r–5v; fol. 5v blank).

SA_T02_Divākaracandra_Guhyasamājoddhṛtay.title: Guhyasamājoddhṛtayāgavidhi (fragment)
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_Guhyasamājoddhṛtay.author: Divākaracandra
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_Guhyasamājoddhṛtay.summary: A fragmentary Tantric Buddhist ritual procedure (yāgavidhi) elaborating healing and apotropaic practices based on Guhyasamājatantra 13.72ff. It includes rituals for dispelling epidemic disease and protecting settlements via the Sarvarogāpanayanavajrasambhava and Buddhasamayameghavyūha samādhis, as well as a concluding śāntika homa, gaṇapūjā, and amṛta visualization for patients.
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_Guhyasamājoddhṛtay.attribution: Attributed to Divākaracandra in the collection metadata; the manuscript witness itself breaks off before the colophon at 'kuśalaṃ yat samu[end]'.
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_Guhyasamājoddhṛtay.edition: Diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on Kathmandu, National Archives MS NAK 1697 2/31 (NGMPP reel A 48/19), 2 folios.
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_Guhyasamājoddhṛtay.coverage: fragment — Preserves approximately two folios from the end of the text, ending abruptly in the dedication verse ('śrīsamājāt samuddhṛ<tya> kṛtvā yāgavidhiṃ mama / kuśalaṃ yat samu[end]').

SA_T02_Divākaracandra_HSS-5-Cihnaviśuddh.title: Cihnaviśuddhi
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_HSS-5-Cihnaviśuddh.author: Divākaracandra
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_HSS-5-Cihnaviśuddh.summary: The Cihnaviśuddhi is a short Buddhist tantric work by Divākaracandra explaining the symbolic purification (cihnaviśuddhi) and esoteric significance of the attributes held by the eight yoginīs of the Hevajra maṇḍala (Gaurī, Caurī, Vettālī, Ghasmarī, Pukkasī, Śavarī, Caṇḍālī, and Ḍombī). Employing nairukta-style hermeneutics, the author interprets each handheld implement as an emblem of non-dual awareness, bodhicitta, or the counteraction of mental afflictions.
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_HSS-5-Cihnaviśuddh.attribution: The closing colophon explicitly attributes authorship to Mahāpaṇḍitācārya Śrī Divākaracandra.
SA_T02_Divākaracandra_HSS-5-Cihnaviśuddh.coverage: complete — Complete short work preserved on folios 61v–62v of MS NSUG Xc 14/39, complete from opening salutation to final colophon.

SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Mitapadā-pañjikā.title: Mitapadāpañjikā (on Catuṣpīṭhatantra 1.1–3.4; with lacunae)
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Mitapadā-pañjikā.author: Durjayacandra
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Mitapadā-pañjikā.summary: Durjayacandra's Mitapadā pañjikā is a commentary on the Catuṣpīṭhatantra, covering up to the Yogapīṭha. It addresses ritual, mantra, and maṇḍala aspects of the tantra.
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Mitapadā-pañjikā.attribution: Colophons attribute the work to Mahāmaṇḍalācārya Durjayacandra ('iti mahāmaṇḍalācāryadurjayacandrakṛtāyāṃ mitapadāyāṃ pañjikāyāṃ...').
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Mitapadā-pañjikā.edition: Formatted diplomatic edition based on codex unicus NAK 3-336 = NGMPP B 23/14 (the Tucci ms. is an apograph), palm-leaf manuscript copied in NS 261 (1141 CE) under Narendradeva by bhikṣu ācārya Suvarṇabhadra.
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Mitapadā-pañjikā.coverage: partial — Commentary ending with the Yogapīṭha colophon: 'iti mahāmaṇḍalācāryadurjayacandrakṛtāyāṃ mitapadāyāṃ pañjikāyāṃ yogapīṭhaḥ samāpta + +' and the scribal colophon of NS 261 (1141 CE, April 1) under Narendradeva by bhikṣu ācārya Suvarṇabhadra. It ends with 'alam bahunā'.

SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana.title: Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana.author: Durjayacandra
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana.summary: The Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana is an Anuttarayogatantra Hevajra practice manual composed by Durjayacandra following the transmission of Dombīheruka. Structured around the six limbs of meditation set forth in the fourth chapter of the Ḍākinīvajrapañjaratantra, the text covers both generation-stage visualizations (mandala, Hevajra, and Nairātmyā) and completion-stage contemplation. It played an influential role in early Tibetan translations and the Sakya Lamdré (Lam 'bras) exegetical tradition.
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana.attribution: Colophon explicitly credits the work to Vajrācārya Durjayacandra (samāptam idaṃ vajrācāryadurjayacandroddhṛtaṃ ṣaḍaṅgasādhanam iti). Verse 12 notes transmission according to Dombīpāda (ḍombīpādakramāyātaṃ śrīhevajrasya sādhanam).
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Ṣaḍaṅgasādhana.coverage: complete — Complete text of the sādhana, spanning from initial namaskāra through the colophon and concluding benedictory verses.
translations: yan lag drug pa zhes bya ba'i sgrub thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1239): translated by Ratnaśrījñāna, 'brog mi lo tsA ba shAkya ye shes (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Jayabhadra_Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā-of.title: Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā
SA_T02_Jayabhadra_Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā-of.author: Jayabhadra
SA_T02_Jayabhadra_Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā-of.summary: The Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā by Jayabhadra is a commentary on the Cakrasaṃvaratantra. It provides glosses and doctrinal expositions on the tantra's verses, clarifying ritual practices, mantras, and yogic symbolism. In the closing verses, the author identifies himself as Jayabhadra, native of Sri Lanka, and states that the work was composed at the Agrabodhi vihāra.
SA_T02_Jayabhadra_Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā-of.attribution: Colophon verses (9–11) explicitly identify the author as Jayabhadra, native of Śrī Laṅkā, composing at the Agrabodhi vihāra.
SA_T02_Jayabhadra_Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā-of.edition: Tsunehiko Sugiki, 'On the making of Śrīcakrasaṃvaratantra --- with a critical sanskrit text of Jayabhadra's 'śrīcakrasaṃvarapañjikā'', Chisan Gakuho 50, 2001, based on Sugiki's unpublished revised version.
SA_T02_Jayabhadra_Cakrasaṃvarapañjikā-of.coverage: complete — Complete commentary running from the opening maṅgala verses down to the final colophon and authorial verses (samāptā śrīcakrasaṃvarapañjikā).

SA_T02_Jñānapāda_Samantabhadrasādhana.title: Samantabhadrasādhana
SA_T02_Jñānapāda_Samantabhadrasādhana.author: Jñānapāda
SA_T02_Jñānapāda_Samantabhadrasādhana.summary: The Samantabhadrasādhana, also known as Caturaṅgasādhana-Samantabhadrī, is a generation-stage (utpattikrama) sādhana composed by Jñānapāda. It sets out ritual worship and visualization practices, concluding in 164 verses.
SA_T02_Jñānapāda_Samantabhadrasādhana.attribution: Attributed to Jñānapāda (Buddhajñānapāda / Sangs rgyas ye shes).
SA_T02_Jñānapāda_Samantabhadrasādhana.coverage: complete — 164 verses of the sādhana are present, from the opening maṅgala (v. 1) to the closing dedication (vv. 163–164). Lacunae are marked '[...]' in places.
translations: kun du bzang po zhes bya ba'i sgrub pa'i thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1855): translated by Śraddhākaravarman, lo chen rin chen bzang po (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kambala_Sādhananidhi-chapter-1_Su.title: Sādhananidhi (chapter 1)
SA_T02_Kambala_Sādhananidhi-chapter-1_Su.author: Kambala
SA_T02_Kambala_Sādhananidhi-chapter-1_Su.summary: The Sādhananidhi (or Sādhananidhipañjikā) is an early tantric commentary by Kambalapāda on the Herukābhidhāna / Cakrasaṃvaratantra. This first chapter explains the opening verses of the tantra (Laghuśaṃvara chapter 1), providing semantic analyses of terms such as ḍākinījālasaṃvara, elaborating the threefold division of tantra (hetu-, upāya-, and phalatantra), and explicating maṇḍala symbolism.
SA_T02_Kambala_Sādhananidhi-chapter-1_Su.attribution: Identified in the chapter colophon as the Sādhananidhi pañjikā on the Śrīherukābhidhāna.
translations: dpal 'khor lo sdom pa'i dka' 'grel sgrub pa'i thabs kyi gleng gzhi zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1401): translated by Sūryagupta, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kambala_—-Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasa.title: Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasaṃvaranāmapañjikā
SA_T02_Kambala_—-Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasa.author: Kambala
SA_T02_Kambala_—-Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasa.summary: The Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasaṃvaranāmapañjikā (also known as Sādhananidhi) is an early commentary on the Herukābhidhāna / Cakrasaṃvaratantra attributed to the mahāsiddha Kambala (Lwāvapā). This e-text is an unpublished diplomatic transcription prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó from a 73-folio palm-leaf manuscript in the National Archives, Kathmandu.
SA_T02_Kambala_—-Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasa.attribution: Colophons and the Tibetan Tanjur attribute the text to Ācārya Kambala (Lwāvapā / Lawapa). Notes in the Göttingen manuscript fragment Xc 14/30 record an alternative attribution to Devagupta.
SA_T02_Kambala_—-Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasa.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription / working edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on palm-leaf manuscript NAK 4-122 / vi. bauddhatantra 87 (NGMPP reel B 31/20, 73 ff.), with comparative readings from Göttingen MS Xc 14/30 and the Tibetan translation (Derge Tanjur Toh 1401).
SA_T02_Kambala_—-Sādhananidānaśrīcakrasa.coverage: complete — Complete diplomatic transcription of the commentary from Kathmandu MS NAK 4-122 (73 folios), from the initial verse down to the final colophon.
translations: dpal 'khor lo sdom pa'i dka' 'grel sgrub pa'i thabs kyi gleng gzhi zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1401): translated by Sūryagupta, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā_ṭhe-devatāyo.title: Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā (Devatāyoga section)
SA_T02_Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā_ṭhe-devatāyo.author: Kuladatta
SA_T02_Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā_ṭhe-devatāyo.summary: The Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā of Kuladatta contains this devatāyoga section, covering the yoga performed by the practitioner, including samvaragrahaṇa, abhiṣeka, mudrās, and maṇḍala dismissal.
SA_T02_Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā_ṭhe-devatāyo.coverage: partial — Only the devatāyoga section of the Kriyāsaṃgrahapañjikā, from 'tad anu samādhitrayabhāvanārthaṃ devatāyogo vidheyaḥ' to 'iti devatāyogaḥ'. Sub-sections include the samvaragrahaṇa, vajrābhiṣeka, the four mudrās, and the dismissal (visarjayet).

SA_T02_Kumudākaramati_Trisamayarājasādha.title: Trisamayarājasādhana
SA_T02_Kumudākaramati_Trisamayarājasādha.author: Kumudākaramati
SA_T02_Kumudākaramati_Trisamayarājasādha.summary: The Trisamayarājasādhana is a detailed ritual manual (sādhana) composed by Kumudākaramati dedicated to the practice of Trisamayarāja. It lays out the requirements of initiation, samaya vows, maṇḍala construction, mantra recitation, and visualization techniques associated with Kriyā/Caryā tantric traditions. It is famously preserved as the opening text of the Sādhanamālā collection.
SA_T02_Kumudākaramati_Trisamayarājasādha.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Paṇḍita Kumudākaramati (Tibetan: ku mu da 'byung gnas blo gros).
SA_T02_Kumudākaramati_Trisamayarājasādha.edition: Diplomatic working edition/transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on NGMPP manuscript reel B 24/11, collated with the Tibetan Derge Tanjur translation (Tōh. 3144 / D 3400, rGyud, vol. phu, fols. 163r1–169v2).
SA_T02_Kumudākaramati_Trisamayarājasādha.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved from initial salutation to final closing colophon, accompanied by interlinear Tibetan text.
translations: dam tshig gsum gyi rgyal po'i sgrub pa'i thabs (Derge Tengyur D 3144): translated by Abhayākaragupta, pa tshab lo tsA ba tshul khrims rgyal mtshan (Tibetan)
sgrub thabs kun las btus pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 3400): translated by Kīrticandra, yar lung lo tsA ba grags pa rgyal mtshan (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kumāracandra_Katipayākṣarā-pañjik.title: Katipayākṣarā Herukābhyudayapañjikā (chapters 1–28 and opening of 29)
SA_T02_Kumāracandra_Katipayākṣarā-pañjik.author: Kumāracandra
SA_T02_Kumāracandra_Katipayākṣarā-pañjik.summary: The Katipayākṣarā is a brief pañjikā by Kumāracandra on the Herukābhyudayatantra. Its witness is a Vikramaśīla palm-leaf manuscript preserved in the Kaiser Library (229). It glosses selected words chapter by chapter, including the yuga/ānanda scheme of ch. 1, and in ch. 28 contains a ranking of tantra classes ('paripācanaṃ yogatantreṇa, mocanaṃ yogottareṇa') with criticism of kriyātantras and their practitioners. This e-text reaches the beginning of ch. 29.
SA_T02_Kumāracandra_Katipayākṣarā-pañjik.attribution: The Tibetan translation in the Derge Tengyur is Toh 1421, where the Sanskrit title is given as Śrīherukābhyudayamahāyoginītantrarājakatipayākṣarapañjikā and the author's Tibetan name as Zla-ba gshon-nu. The Tibetan translation (D 1421) attributes the work to *Candrakumāra (zla ba gzhon nu).
SA_T02_Kumāracandra_Katipayākṣarā-pañjik.edition: PDSz e-text based on Kaiser Library 229 (a Vikramaśīla ms.) and the publication in Dhīḥ 37: 149–170.
SA_T02_Kumāracandra_Katipayākṣarā-pañjik.coverage: partial — The e-text covers commentary on chapters 1–28 and stops after the first gloss on 29.1, with no colophon.
translations: dpal he ru ka mngon par 'byung ba rnal 'byor ma'i rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po'i dka' 'grel yi ge nyung ngu (Derge Tengyur D 1421): translated by Tathāgatarakṣita, glan dar ma blo gros; at dpal bi kra ma shrI la (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kāṇeripā_Śucikaraṇa_2008.title: Śucikaraṇa
SA_T02_Kāṇeripā_Śucikaraṇa_2008.author: Kāṇeripā
SA_T02_Kāṇeripā_Śucikaraṇa_2008.summary: The Śucikaraṇa is a short polemical treatise in 104 Sanskrit verses attributed to the Mahāsiddha Kāṇeripā. It critiques Brahmanical conceptions of external ritual purity (śauca), bodily washings, caste distinctions, and dietary restrictions, arguing that the physical body is by nature impure and that genuine purification resides solely in the mind.
SA_T02_Kāṇeripā_Śucikaraṇa_2008.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Kāṇeripā.
SA_T02_Kāṇeripā_Śucikaraṇa_2008.edition: Dhīḥ 46 (2008), pp. 131–141, based on MS no. 13267, Gaekwad Oriental Institute, Baroda.
SA_T02_Kāṇeripā_Śucikaraṇa_2008.coverage: complete — Complete text in 104 verses, including opening verse, manuscript pagination markers, and closing colophon.

SA_T02_Kṛṣṇācārya_Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana.title: Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana
SA_T02_Kṛṣṇācārya_Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana.author: Kṛṣṇācārya
SA_T02_Kṛṣṇācārya_Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana.summary: The Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana is a core Anuttarayogatantra meditation manual (sādhana) focused on Cakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī, attributed to Mahāsiddha Kṛṣṇācārya. In 66 verses interspersed with mantra rubrics, it describes the preliminary rites, protection circle, self-generation of the twelve-armed Heruka, body-maṇḍala deities, and internal offerings.
SA_T02_Kṛṣṇācārya_Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana.attribution: Attributed traditionally to Mahāsiddha Kṛṣṇācārya. Marginal annotation by the transcriber notes that verse 1 is borrowed from Lūyīpāda's sādhana.
SA_T02_Kṛṣṇācārya_Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana.edition: Sugiki, Tsunehiko. 2000. “Kṛṣṇācārya's Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana—Critical Edition with Notes—” Chisan Gakuho 49: 45–62.
SA_T02_Kṛṣṇācārya_Śrīcakrasaṃvarasādhana.coverage: complete — Complete Sanskrit text in 66 verses plus mantras and prose rubrics, corresponding to the text preserved in Nepalese MS NGMPP D 34/41 as edited by Sugiki (the Tibetan canonical version Toh 1445 contains an additional mantra collection at the end).
translations: dpal 'khor lo sdom pa zhes bya ba'i sgrub thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1445) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Lūyī_Śmaśānavidhi_Finot_1934.title: Śmaśānavidhi
SA_T02_Lūyī_Śmaśānavidhi_Finot_1934.author: Lūyīpāda
SA_T02_Lūyī_Śmaśānavidhi_Finot_1934.summary: The Śmaśānavidhi is a concise iconographical and ritual verse guide composed by Lūyīpāda outlining the charnel grounds in the Yoginītantra and Cakrasaṃvara systems. For directions, it enumerates the charnel ground name, dominant tree, guardian deity (dikpāla), serpent king (nāga), and cloud formations, followed by descriptions of terrifying creatures, yoginīs, and siddhas inhabiting the grounds.
SA_T02_Lūyī_Śmaśānavidhi_Finot_1934.attribution: Attributed in the final colophon to Lūyīpāda (kṛtir iyaṃ lūyīpādānām).
SA_T02_Lūyī_Śmaśānavidhi_Finot_1934.edition: Louis Finot, “Manuscrits Sanskrits de Sādhana’s Retrouvés en Chine.” Journal Asiatique 225 (1934), pp. 1-86.
SA_T02_Lūyī_Śmaśānavidhi_Finot_1934.coverage: complete — Complete short text of 28 stanzas plus closing verse, dedication, and colophon (with a minor lacuna noted between vv. 28 and 29).

SA_T02_Lūyīpāda_Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya_Sa.title: Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya
SA_T02_Lūyīpāda_Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya_Sa.author: Lūyīpāda
SA_T02_Lūyīpāda_Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya_Sa.summary: The Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya is an influential generation-stage (utpattikrama) visualization treatise composed by the mahāsiddha Lūyīpāda. It details the internal and external purification rites, the generation of the protective vajra enclosure and the eight cremation grounds, and the manifestation of the sixty-two-deity maṇḍala arranged across the body, speech, and mind cakras. This text forms the liturgical and doctrinal foundation of the Lūhīpāda lineage of the Cakrasaṃvara Tantric corpus.
SA_T02_Lūyīpāda_Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya_Sa.attribution: Attributed to Lūyīpāda, confirmed by the closing colophon: 'śrīlūyīpādaviracitaśrīcakrasaṃvarābhisamayaḥ samāptaḥ'.
SA_T02_Lūyīpāda_Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya_Sa.edition: Munenobu Sakurai (桜井宗信), 'Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya研究(2)', Mikkyō Zuzō (密教図像), 1997.
SA_T02_Lūyīpāda_Cakrasaṃvarābhisamaya_Sa.coverage: complete — Text with numbered verses, concluding stanza and colophon.
translations: dpal bcom ldan 'das mngon par rtogs pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1427): translated by Śraddhākaravarman, lo chen rin chen bzang po; revised by Navikoṭa, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Mekhalāṭīkā_Mekhalāṭīkā-to-Kāṇhap.title: Dohākoṣa with Mekhalāṭīkā
SA_T02_Mekhalāṭīkā_Mekhalāṭīkā-to-Kāṇhap.author: Kāṇhapāda, Amṛtavajra
SA_T02_Mekhalāṭīkā_Mekhalāṭīkā-to-Kāṇhap.summary: The Dohākoṣa of Kāṇhapāda is a cycle of 32 rhymed Apabhraṃśa verses (dohā) teaching non-dual realization and sahaja. It criticizes external scholastic and Vedic rituals while elucidating esoteric internal yogic physiology (including the channels lalanā, rasanā, and avadhūtī). The accompanying Sanskrit commentary, the Mekhalāṭīkā (attributed to Amṛtavajra), provides word-for-word grammatical and doctrinal interpretations supported by citations from Buddhist tantric texts such as the Caturdevīparipṛcchā.
SA_T02_Mekhalāṭīkā_Mekhalāṭīkā-to-Kāṇhap.attribution: The root dohā verses are attributed to Kāṇhapāda (self-named in verse 31 as Kṛṣṇavajra, and referenced in the commentary as Kṛṣṇācārya). The Sanskrit commentary was published anonymously in Bagchi 1938, but is attributed to Amṛtavajra in an edition in Dhīḥ.
SA_T02_Mekhalāṭīkā_Mekhalāṭīkā-to-Kāṇhap.coverage: complete — Complete text of all 32 dohā verses of Kāṇhapāda with the full Sanskrit commentary Mekhalāṭīkā, ending with the colophon 'ity ācāryapādīyadohākoṣamekhalāṭīkā samāptā'.

SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Viṃśatividhi.title: Samājamaṇḍalopāyikā
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Viṃśatividhi.author: Nāgabuddhi
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Viṃśatividhi.summary: The Samājamaṇḍalopāyikā (commonly known as Viṃśatividhi) is a fundamental ritual manual (maṇḍalopāyikā) of the Guhyasamāja Ārya tradition (Āryasaṃgha/Āryapakṣa), attributed to Nāgabuddhi (Nāgabodhi). The text systematically expounds the twenty ritual stages (viṃśatividhi) required to prepare, consecrate, and construct the thirty-two deity Guhyasamāja sand maṇḍala (rajomaṇḍala), followed by the procedure for admitting and conferring tantric initiations (abhiṣeka) upon disciples.
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Viṃśatividhi.attribution: Attributed to the Guhyasamāja Ārya-lineage master Nāgabuddhi (Nāgabodhi), traditionally considered a close disciple of the tantric Nāgārjuna.
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Viṃśatividhi.edition: Diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó from a palm-leaf manuscript preserved in the Giuseppe Tucci Collection, written at or originating from Vikramaśīla (commissioned by the scholar-monk Jinaśrīmitra), right after Rahaḥpradīpa.
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Viṃśatividhi.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the work across all 20 ritual procedures (vidhis), from opening invocation to the concluding verses and scribal colophon.
translations: Tibetan translation by Tilakakalaśa and Ba-tshab Ñi-ma grags: Dpal gsaṅ-ba-ḥdus-paḥi dkyil-ḥkhor-gyi cho-ga ñi-śu-pa shes-bya-ba (Śrīguhyasamājamaṇḍalaviṃśatividhi-nāma / Toh 1810 / Otani 2675). (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Vyavastholi.title: Vyavastholi (incomplete, ends at fol. 27v1 of the manuscript)
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Vyavastholi.author: Nāgabuddhi
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Vyavastholi.summary: The Vyavastholi of Nāgabuddhi (Nāgabodhi), a work of the Ārya school of Guhyasamāja exegesis, expounds the steps of generation (utpattikrama). It correlates steps of the sādhana with cosmic destruction and re-formation as well as the intermediate state (antarābhava), and was an authoritative source for later Indian and Tibetan exegetes.
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Vyavastholi.attribution: Canonical attribution to Nāgabuddhi (Nāgabodhi), figure in the Ārya school of Guhyasamāja practice and commentary.
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Vyavastholi.edition: Transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of manuscript Göttingen Xc 14/30, fols. 21v2–27v1, with reference to the Tibetan translation (Tōh. 1809).
SA_T02_Nāgabuddhi_Vyavastholi.coverage: partial — Transcription of Göttingen Xc 14/30 fols. 21v2–27v1 breaking off mid-word ('āvāhanaṃ ((ā))veśena tvaritena vi[27v1]'); Derge 131a5 added at the end. Tanaka's 2016 edition covers the text. Some akṣaras in the last lines are marked illegible ('? ? ?').
translations: dus pa'i sgrub pa'i thabs rnam par gzhag pa'i rim pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1809) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Nūtanānaṅgavajra_Hevajrasādhana.title: Hevajrasādhana
SA_T02_Nūtanānaṅgavajra_Hevajrasādhana.author: Nūtanānaṅgavajra
SA_T02_Nūtanānaṅgavajra_Hevajrasādhana.summary: The Hevajrasādhana of Nūtanānaṅgavajra ('Anaṅgavajra the Younger') is an Anuttarayogatantra ritual manual (sādhana) for the visualization and realization of Hevajra/Heruka and his retinue of eight ḍākinīs (Gaurī, Caurī, Vettālī, Ghasmarī, Pukkasī, Śavarī, Caṇḍālī, and Ḍombī). It details the yogin's qualifications, generation of the deity through seed-syllables, offerings, and mantra practice for four-armed and six-armed forms.
SA_T02_Nūtanānaṅgavajra_Hevajrasādhana.attribution: The closing verse names Nūtanānaṅgavajra ('nūtanānaṅgavajreṇa … ādeśāl likhitaṃ'), and the colophon reads 'kṛtir iyaṃ yoginaḥ śrīmadanaṅgavajrasya'. The header references Toh. 1264, attributed to Yan lag med pa'i rdo rje.
SA_T02_Nūtanānaṅgavajra_Hevajrasādhana.coverage: complete — Complete sādhana from initial homage (fol. 114r3) to final dedication verses and colophon.
translations: dgyes pa'i rdo rje'i sgrub pa'i thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1264): translated by Samantabhadra, nag 'tsho lo tsA ba tshul khrims rgyal ba (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Padmavajra_Advayavivaraṇaprajñopā.title: Advayavivaraṇaprajñopāyaviniścayasiddhi
SA_T02_Padmavajra_Advayavivaraṇaprajñopā.author: Padmavajra
SA_T02_Padmavajra_Advayavivaraṇaprajñopā.summary: The Advayavivaraṇaprajñopāyaviniścayasiddhi is a short Vajrayāna text in mixed prose and verse attributed to Padmavajra. It expounds the non-duality (advaya) of wisdom (prajñā) and skillful means (upāya), demonstrating how sensual pleasures and daily actions are integrated into non-dual gnosis via the svādhiṣṭhāna stage. The treatise cites the Guhyasamājatantra and Hevajratantra, concluding with Apabhraṃśa dohā verses on the inseparability of compassion and emptiness.
SA_T02_Padmavajra_Advayavivaraṇaprajñopā.attribution: Ascribed in the final colophon to Ācārya Padmavajra.
SA_T02_Padmavajra_Advayavivaraṇaprajñopā.coverage: complete — Complete short treatise, pp. 211–218 of the Sarnath edition, from the opening analysis of prajñā and upāya to the closing title colophon and 'kṛtir iyam ācāryapadmavajrapādānām'.

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-1-Tan.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 1)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-1-Tan.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-1-Tan.summary: The Maṇḍalopāyikā by Padmaśrīmitra is an esoteric Buddhist ritual manual detailing the construction, preparatory rites, and consecration of a maṇḍala in the tradition of the Guhyasamājatantra. This first chapter, the Saṃvaragrahaṇādividhi, describes preliminary services (pūrvasevā), dietary requirements, the generation of bodhicitta, and the reception of vows (saṃvara) by both householders and renunciants.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-1-Tan.coverage: partial — Contains an outline of the ten chapters based on a palm-leaf manuscript (folios 1r1–15v11) and the critical text of chapter 1 (Saṃvaragrahaṇādividhiḥ, vv. 1.1–1.24/26).

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-10-Ta.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 10: Antasthitikarmoddeśa)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-10-Ta.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-10-Ta.summary: Chapter 10 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā provides instructions for the funerary and post-mortem rites (antasthitikarma) of deceased Vajrayāna masters and practitioners. It discusses the transmigration signs depending on which of the nine bodily orifices the consciousness exits, the procession to the cremation ground, the construction and preparation of a funerary maṇḍala, summoning and consecrating (abhiṣeka) the deceased's consciousness, consciousness transference (utkrānti), cremation, and closing dedications of merit.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-10-Ta.attribution: Attributed to Padmaśrīmitra, author of the Maṇḍalopāyikā.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-10-Ta.edition: Tanemura, Ryūgen. (2012). Padmaśrīmitra作MaṇḍalopāyikāのAntasthitikarmoddeśa. 現代密教.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-10-Ta.coverage: partial — Contains only the 10th chapter (Antasthitikarmoddeśa), concluding with 'antasthitikarmoddeśaḥ', consisting of 54 verses on Buddhist funerary rites.

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-2-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 2)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-2-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-2-ms.summary: Chapter 2 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā, a Buddhist tantric manual on maṇḍala installation. This chapter describes site examination, ground purification (bhūmiparīkṣā and bhūmiśodhana), the preparation of powders and construction materials, and concludes with the rite of vase-consecration (kalaśādhivāsana).
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-2-ms.edition: Tokyo University Library ms. 280, transcribed by Péter-Dániel Szántó.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-2-ms.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 2 only (verses 2.1–2.87), ending with 'iti kalaśādhivāsanavidhiḥ'.

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-3-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 3)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-3-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-3-ms.summary: Chapter 3 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā, titled Vihārārāmapaṭapustakasādhāraṇārghavidhi, details shared preliminary rituals for establishing sacred spaces, shrines, cloth paintings (paṭa), and religious manuscripts (pustaka). It describes soil and ground examination (bhūmiparīkṣā), pegging the site (kīlana), propitiating the earth goddess Pṛthivī and directional spirits, installing the ten wrathful deities (daśakrodha) to avert hindrances, and concluding offerings (argha) and dismissals (visarjana).
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-3-ms.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 3 only (verses 3.1–3.49), concluding with the chapter colophon: 'iti vihārārāmapaṭapustakasādhāraṇārghavidhiḥ'.

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-4-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 4)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-4-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-4-ms.summary: Chapter 4 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā, concluding as a Pratiṣṭhāvidhi. The text describes Buddhist Tantric consecration rituals associated with maṇḍalas, including site preparation, pacification of vighnas, drawing with coloured powders, cord-laying (sūtrapāta), and the concluding dismissal (visarjanavidhi).
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-4-ms.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 4 only, dealing with pratiṣṭhā (concluding with 'iti pratiṣṭhāvidhiḥ').

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-5-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 5)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-5-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-5-ms.summary: Chapter 5 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā describes the rites of tantric empowerment (abhiṣekakrama). It details the qualifications and preliminary consecration of pupils (śiṣyādhivāsana), entry into the maṇḍala (maṇḍalapraveśa), purifications (maṇḍalaviśuddhi), the name empowerment (nāmābhiṣeka), and higher consecrations concluding with the wisdom-gnosis initiation (prajñājñānābhiṣeka), incorporating citations from texts including the Hevajratantra and the Kālacakratantra.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-5-ms.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó (PDSz corpus, release PDSz_202608, input July 9–10, 2025, Kolozsvár), based on Tokyo University Library ms. 280.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-5-ms.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 5 only (treating abhiṣekakrama / tantric initiation rituals), based on Tokyo University Library ms. 280.

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-6-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 6: Homavidhi)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-6-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-6-ms.summary: Chapter 6 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā, dedicated to the homavidhi (fire-offering ritual) within late Indian Vajrayāna practice. It describes the dimensions and forms of fire hearths (kuṇḍa) for peaceful (śāntika), enriching (pauṣṭika), subjugating (vaśya), and destructive/wrathful (abhicāra) rituals, the selection and preparation of ritual firewood (samidh), and deities invoked during the rite.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-6-ms.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 6 only, dealing with the homavidhi (fire-offering ritual), ending with 'homavidhiḥ || ||'.

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-7-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 7)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-7-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-7-ms.summary: Chapter 7 of Padmaśrīmitra's Maṇḍalopāyikā, presenting the water-offering ritual (jalahomavidhi) according to the transmission of the Catuṣpīṭhatantra. The text details the construction of a four-cubit maṇḍala, the arrangement and preparation of nine water vessels, the visualization of Jñānaḍākinī and surrounding yoginīs, associated mudrās and mantras, and oblations into water for pacification, prosperity, and longevity.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-7-ms.attribution: Tantric ritual text attributed to Padmaśrīmitra within the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-7-ms.coverage: partial — Chapter 7 only (vv. 7.1–7.35), describing the jalahoma (water offering ritual).

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-8-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 8)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-8-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-8-ms.summary: The Maṇḍalopāyikā of Padmaśrīmitra is a late tantric ritual manual. Chapter 8 describes the purification bathing ritual (snānavidhi), specifying mantras, mudrās, visualizations of wrathful deities (krodha) such as Vajrayakṣa and Amṛtakuṇḍalin, and the protective binding of the cardinal and intermediate directions (vighnabandha).
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-8-ms.edition: Tokyo University Library ms. 280, transcribed by Péter-Dániel Szántó (PDSz corpus).

SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-9-ms.title: Maṇḍalopāyikā (chapter 9)
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-9-ms.author: Padmaśrīmitra
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-9-ms.summary: Chapter 9 of the Maṇḍalopāyikā, a ritual manual by Padmaśrīmitra describing maṇḍala procedures. This section details the rajovisarjanavidhi (rite of dismantling the sand maṇḍala): meditating on the ultimate empty nature of the deities, sweeping up the colored powders, processing with music and offerings to a water body (river or nāga-lake), invoking and making offerings to the eight great nāgas, and submerging the sand in the water.
SA_T02_Padmaśrīmitra_Maṇḍalopāyikā-9-ms.coverage: partial — Chapter 9 only (vv. 9.1–9.29), covering the rite of dismantling and disposing of the maṇḍala powders (rajovisarjanavidhi).

SA_T02_Parahitarakṣita_Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī.title: Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī
SA_T02_Parahitarakṣita_Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī.author: Parahitarakṣita
SA_T02_Parahitarakṣita_Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī.summary: The Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī is an exegetical gloss explaining the visualization process (bhāvanākrama) of the Piṇḍīkramasādhana (attributed to Nāgārjuna), representing the generation stage (utpattikrama) in the Ārya tradition of the Guhyasamājatantra. It outlines the preliminary purification of ordinary conceit, the generation of the protective enclosure, the internal mapping of bodily aggregates and sensory faculties to the thirty-two mandala deities, and the dissolution back into the clear light (prabhāsvara).
SA_T02_Parahitarakṣita_Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī.attribution: The colophon reads 'samāptā piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī'. Edited by La Vallée Poussin in 1896 from Bibliothèque nationale Devanāgarī 82. In the Tibetan tradition, a work titled bsDus pa'i rim pa'i dka' 'grel (Pindikramatippani) is attributed to sGeg pa rdo rje.
SA_T02_Parahitarakṣita_Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī.edition: Louis de La Vallée Poussin (ed.), 1896, from Bibliothèque nationale Devanāgarī 82.
SA_T02_Parahitarakṣita_Piṇḍīkramaṭippaṇī.coverage: complete — Complete text of the short commentary as edited by Louis de La Vallée Poussin (pp. 15–17).

SA_T02_Pramuditākaravarman_Candraprabhā-.title: Candraprabhā (fragment)
SA_T02_Pramuditākaravarman_Candraprabhā-.author: Pramuditākaravarman
SA_T02_Pramuditākaravarman_Candraprabhā-.summary: A Sanskrit fragment of the Candraprabhā, an esoteric Buddhist tantric commentary attributed to *Pramuditākaravarman (Rab-tu dgaH-baHi HbyuN-gnas go-cha), preserved in the Tibetan Tengyur as D 1852. The surviving Sanskrit excerpts cover sections of chapters 14 and 17, dealing with protective visualizations, abhicāra rituals, sexual yogic mudrās, and the non-emission of bodhicitta as the source of transcendent bliss. The Sanskrit text survives on six manuscript leaves preserved in the Giuseppe Tucci photograph collection.
SA_T02_Pramuditākaravarman_Candraprabhā-.attribution: The Sanskrit author name is reconstructed as *Pramuditākaravarman (Tibetan: Rab-tu dgaH-baHi HbyuN-gnas go-cha in D 1852).
SA_T02_Pramuditākaravarman_Candraprabhā-.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó (ed.), Tucci photographs, 6 leaves (unpublished transcription).
SA_T02_Pramuditākaravarman_Candraprabhā-.coverage: fragment — Fragments from six manuscript folios photographed in the Giuseppe Tucci collection, containing commentary on chapters (paṭalas) 14 and 17, concordant with Derge Tengyur D 1852, fols. 230v–303a.
translations: pal gsang ba 'dus pa rgyud kyi rgyal po'i bshad pa zla ba'i 'od zer zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1852) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-22-1-7_Tanem.title: Padminī (chapter 22.1–7)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-22-1-7_Tanem.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-22-1-7_Tanem.summary: The Padminī is Ratnarakṣita's commentary on the Saṃvarodaya. In this short passage on chapter 22, verses 1–7, the text discusses the quantification and canonical categorization of Buddhist scriptures (Vinayapiṭaka, Sūtrānta, Pāramitānaya, Yogatantra, and Yoginītantra), defending the distinctive status and rapid efficacy of the Mantranaya with citations including the Nayatrayapradīpa.
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-22-1-7_Tanem.coverage: excerpt — Contains only the root verses and commentary for chapter 22, verses 1–7.

SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch15_CA17-co.title: Padminī (chapter 15: Pātralakṣaṇa)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch15_CA17-co.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch15_CA17-co.summary: The Padminī is a commentary on the Saṃvarodaya by Ratnarakṣita. This file preserves chapter 15 (Pātralakṣaṇa), which deals with the ritual characteristics, faults, and classification (analogous to the four castes) of skull-cups (kapāla) and vessels used in esoteric assemblies (gaṇacakra) and maiden worship (kumārīpūjā). The digital text provides Szántó's collation of Sanskrit manuscript witnesses alongside the parallel Tibetan rendering.
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch15_CA17-co.edition: Unpublished working edition and transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on Cambridge University Library MS Add. 1698 (CA17, ff. 24v6–25r3), Oriental Institute Baroda MS (ff. 43v10–44v3), and National Archives Kathmandu MS 5-203 (NGMPP reel B 113/8, pp. 105.13–107.10).
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch15_CA17-co.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 15 (pañcadaśapaṭalavyākhyā, Pātralakṣaṇa) collated with the corresponding Tibetan translation.

SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch24_CA17.title: Padminī (chapter 24)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch24_CA17.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch24_CA17.summary: Commentary on chapter 24 from Ratnarakṣita's Padminī, an extensive pañjikā on the Buddhist Saṃvarodayatantra. The excerpt discusses preliminary mantra recitation (pūrvasevā) for siddhi and ritual procedures (uccāṭana) using symbolic diagrams and plant ingredients. The e-text alternates the Sanskrit text of manuscript Nagoya Takaoka CA 17 with the Tibetan Tengyur translation.

SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch27_CA17.title: Padminī (chapter 27)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch27_CA17.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch27_CA17.summary: Chapter 27 of Ratnarakṣita's Padminī, a commentary on the Saṃvarodaya Tantra. This chapter explains mantroddhāra (extraction and encoding of mantras, including the 10-syllable hṛdaya, 7-syllable upahṛdaya, and 13-syllable devīhṛdaya mantras) using grid and number-code systems, and concludes with an exposition of the fourteen root transgressions (mūlāpatti) and eight gross infractions (sthūlāpatti) of tantric samaya. The e-text provides the Sanskrit text alongside its Tibetan translation.
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch27_CA17.attribution: A commentary by Ratnarakṣita entitled Padminī.
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch27_CA17.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription and parallel Tibetan alignment by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Kolozsvár, 9 March 2025), based on manuscript Nagoya Takaoka CA17, fols. 41v2–42r2.
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch27_CA17.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 27 (saptaviṃśatitamapaṭalavyākhyā) only, transcribed alongside its parallel Tibetan translation.

SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch28_CA17.title: Padminī (chapter 28)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch28_CA17.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch28_CA17.summary: Chapter 28 (Homavidhipaṭala) of the Padminī, Ratnarakṣita's commentary on the Buddhist Yoginītantra Saṃvarodayatantra. This brief chapter explains fire ritual (homa) procedures for attraction (ākarṣaṇa) and subjugation, specifying particular types of fire (caṇḍālagṛhānītāgni, śmaśānāgni), the visualization of Khaṇḍarohā, and accompanying mantras. The e-text alternates Sanskrit phrases from the Nagoya Takaoka manuscript with the Tibetan Tengyur translation.
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch28_CA17.attribution: The e-text aligns the Sanskrit commentary of Ratnarakṣita with the corresponding Tibetan translation from the Tengyur (D 1420 / D 86a7–86b5, translated by Thams-cad mkhyen-pa'i dpal).

SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch32_CA17.title: Padminī (chapter 32)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch32_CA17.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch32_CA17.summary: Chapter 32 of Ratnarakṣita's Padminī, commenting on the 32nd chapter of the Saṃvarodaya tantric tradition. The text explains the ritual procedure for the bali offering (alibali) and the feast assembly (gaṇacakra), detailing deity visualizations of the Cakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī mandala, seed syllables, ritual offerings, and the dedication of merit.
