SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch9_BangKura.title: Padminī (chapter 9)
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch9_BangKura.author: Ratnarakṣita
SA_T02_Ratnarakṣita_Padminī-Ch9_BangKura.summary: The Padminī is Ratnarakṣita's commentary (pañjikā) on the Śrīsaṃvarodayatantra, a vital Yoginītantra work belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. This excerpt comprises the commentary on chapter 9 (navamapaṭala), treating esoteric signs and hand gestures (chommā, saṃketa) used to recognize and communicate with ḍākinīs, as well as the internalization of sacred tantric pilgrimage sites (pīṭha) within the subtle body.

SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti-Paṇḍitāśoka_Vidagd.title: Vidagdhavismāpana with Vidagdhavismāpanaṭippita
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti-Paṇḍitāśoka_Vidagd.author: Ratnākaraśānti, Paṇḍitāśoka
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti-Paṇḍitāśoka_Vidagd.summary: The Vidagdhavismāpana composed by Ratnākaraśānti is a work on Sanskrit riddles, verbal puzzles, and enigmas (prahelikā, praśnottara, vyastasamasta), frequently weaving in praise of Buddhist figures such as the Sugata, Avalokiteśvara, Mañjughoṣa, and Mārīcī. The text is accompanied throughout by the Vidagdhavismāpanaṭippita of Paṇḍitāśoka, which resolves each riddle, clarifies double entendres (śleṣa), and provides the necessary grammatical derivations.
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti-Paṇḍitāśoka_Vidagd.attribution: The root text Vidagdhavismāpana is attributed in the colophon to Mahāpaṇḍita Ratnākaraśānti; the embedded commentary (ṭippita) is attributed to Paṇḍitāśoka.
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti-Paṇḍitāśoka_Vidagd.coverage: complete — Complete text of 178 verses of the Vidagdhavismāpana together with Paṇḍitāśoka's commentary (ṭippita).

SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Guṇavatī-Mahāmāyāṭ.title: Guṇavatīmahāmāyāṭīkā
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Guṇavatī-Mahāmāyāṭ.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Guṇavatī-Mahāmāyāṭ.summary: The Guṇavatī is Ratnākaraśānti's commentary on the Mahāmāyātantra, a yoginītantra. It explains the tantra's title, the maṇḍala and deities, visualisation, mantra and ritual applications, and interprets them in terms of a view of mind (cittamātra).
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Guṇavatī-Mahāmāyāṭ.attribution: Attributed to Ratnākaraśānti in the final colophon ('guṇavatī nāma mahāmāyāṭīkā mahāpaṇḍitaratnākaraśāntipādānāṃ samāpteti').
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Guṇavatī-Mahāmāyāṭ.coverage: complete — Commentary on the Mahāmāyātantra, ending with the colophon of the third nirdeśa and the author colophon.

SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Khasamā-ṭīkā.title: Khasamāṭīkā
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Khasamā-ṭīkā.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Khasamā-ṭīkā.summary: The Khasamāṭīkā is Ratnākaraśānti's commentary on the five-chapter Khasamatantra. Synthesizing Yogācāra-Mādhyamika philosophy with Anuttarayoga Tantric hermeneutics, the text opens with a celebrated exegesis of the basis-transformation (āśrayaparāvṛtti) of body and consciousness into the three Buddha-kāyas, glossing the luminous and sky-like nature of mind (prakāśamātratā khasama). It also provides crucial grammatical and metrical explanations of Apabhraṃśa verses (dohā/dvipadī) embedded within the tantra.
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Khasamā-ṭīkā.attribution: The colophon explicitly attributes the work to Mahāpaṇḍita Śrī Ratnākaraśāntipāda. The text is a commentary on the Khasamatantra (extant in Tibetan, Toh 441; Tibetan translation of the commentary is Toh 1424, Peking 2141). Translators of the Tibetan translation are Śūnyatāsamādhi and Shes rab ye shes.
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Khasamā-ṭīkā.coverage: complete — Complete commentary across 5 paṭalas, concluding with the fifth chapter colophon 'khasamāyāṃ khasamatantrasya ṭīkāyāṃ pañcamaḥ paṭalaḥ' and the work colophon 'samāptā ceyaṃ khasamā nāma ṭīkā'.
translations: nam mkha' dang mnyam pa zhes bya ba'i rgya cher 'grel pa (Derge Tengyur D 1424): translated by Śūnyatāsamādhi, shes rab ye shes (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Mahāmāyāsādhana.title: Mahāmāyāsādhana
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Mahāmāyāsādhana.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Mahāmāyāsādhana.summary: The Mahāmāyāsādhana is a tantric visualization ritual (sādhana) dedicated to the four-faced, four-armed deity Mahāmāyā and a retinue of yoginīs (such as Vajraḍākinī, Ratnaḍākinī, Padmaḍākinī, and Viśvaḍākinī), preserved as sādhana no. 239 in the Sādhanamālā. Composed by Ratnākaraśānti, the work details preliminary purifications, deity generation prompted by vajragītikā songs, bindu meditation, mantra recitation, and daily post-meditation conduct.
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Mahāmāyāsādhana.attribution: Attributed to Ratnākaraśānti in the opening header.
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Mahāmāyāsādhana.edition: Transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of Sādhanamālā no. 239 [ = NGMPP B 24/12, DSCN9071 = 986 ff.].
SA_T02_Ratnākaraśānti_Mahāmāyāsādhana.coverage: complete — Text of Sādhanamālā no. 239 from opening invocation down to the final colophon line (mahāmāyāsādhanaṃ samāptam).

SA_T02_Sādhuputra-Śrīdharānanda_Sekoddeś.title: Sekoddeśaṭippaṇī
SA_T02_Sādhuputra-Śrīdharānanda_Sekoddeś.author: Sādhuputra Śrīdharānanda
SA_T02_Sādhuputra-Śrīdharānanda_Sekoddeś.summary: The Sekoddeśaṭippaṇī is a Sanskrit sub-commentary (ṭippaṇī) by Sādhuputra Śrīdharānanda on the Sekoddeśa, the initiation chapter belonging to the Kālacakra Paramādibuddhatantra. The work glosses the verses describing the initiations, the inner channels (nāḍī), breath retention (prāṇāyāma), and higher gnosis. Extant in Sanskrit in a unique manuscript preserved at the Asiatic Society of Bengal (ASB G-10744).
SA_T02_Sādhuputra-Śrīdharānanda_Sekoddeś.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Sādhuputra Paṇḍita Śrīdharānanda. In the Tibetan Tengyur (Toh 1352 / D 1352), his name is translated as Dpal 'dzin dga' ba. The Tibetan translation (D 1352) attributes the work to Śrīdharasena (sA hU pu tra dpal 'dzin dga' ba).
SA_T02_Sādhuputra-Śrīdharānanda_Sekoddeś.edition: Raniero Gnoli, 'La Sekoddeśaṭippaṇī di Sādhuputra Śrīdharānanda. Il testo sanscrito', in Rivista degli Studi Orientali (RSO), vol. 70 (1997), n. 1-2, pp. 115–146.
SA_T02_Sādhuputra-Śrīdharānanda_Sekoddeś.coverage: complete — Complete commentary, opening with the mangala verses and concluding with verse 174 explanation and author colophon.
translations: Philip Lecso, English translation of the Sekoddeśa with the Sekoddeśaṭippaṇī. (English)

dbang mdor bstan pa'i mdor bshad (Derge Tengyur D 1352): translated by Vanaratna, lo tsA ba'i cha shas su gyur pa gzhon nu dpal; at chos 'khor dpal bsam yas kyi dben gnas dam pa mchims phu'i dben gnas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Tatakaragupta_Ādikarmikavidhi.title: Ādikarmikavidhi (incomplete)
SA_T02_Tatakaragupta_Ādikarmikavidhi.author: Tatakaragupta
SA_T02_Tatakaragupta_Ādikarmikavidhi.summary: The Ādikarmikavidhi (also entitled Ādikarmakṛti) by Tatakaragupta is an Indian Buddhist ritual manual for beginners (ādikarmika). Extant here from folio 9r onwards, the text outlines daily Mahāyāna and Mantrayāna religious duties, including taking refuge in the Three Jewels, receiving the bodhisattva vows (bodhisattvasaṃvara) and poṣadha vows, expounding the ten unwholesome actions (daśākuśalakarmapatha), conducting daily Buddha worship (buddhapūjā), making bali and water offerings to pretas, and performing funerary rites (śrāddhavidhi).
SA_T02_Tatakaragupta_Ādikarmikavidhi.attribution: The concluding verse explicitly attributes the composition to Tatakaragupta ('Tatakaraguptena kṛtā lokadvayasakalasugatisukhadātrī | Prajñākaraguptacirapraṇayavaśāt Ādikarmakṛtiracanā ||') and praises Śubhākaragupta.
SA_T02_Tatakaragupta_Ādikarmikavidhi.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on National Archives, Kathmandu 3/363 = Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project reel no. A1165/7.
SA_T02_Tatakaragupta_Ādikarmikavidhi.coverage: partial — Acephalous text preserving folios 9r to the end. Folios 1r–8v are missing.

SA_T02_Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi_Fragment-of-.title: Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhiṭīkā (fragment)
SA_T02_Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi_Fragment-of-.summary: Fragment of an unidentified Sanskrit commentary on the Tantric treatise Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi (or its associated sādhana). The preserved text contains opening verses in praise of Vajravilāsinī/Vajravārāhī and the Buddha, followed by word-by-word grammatical and yogic exposition of the opening verse. Transcribed diplomatically by Péter-Dániel Szántó from a single palm leaf in the National Archives of Nepal.
SA_T02_Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi_Fragment-of-.attribution: The root text Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi is traditionally attributed to Śūnyasamādhivajra. The author of this commentary is unknown; a tentative note in the transcription queries whether it could be by Daśabalaśrīmitra.
SA_T02_Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi_Fragment-of-.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó from National Archives of Nepal ms. NAK 1-1679 (vi. bauddhadarśana 31 = NGMPP reel B 23/7), single palm leaf.
SA_T02_Tattvajñānasaṃsiddhi_Fragment-of-.coverage: fragment — A single palm leaf (recto and verso) containing the opening maṅgala, introductory kārikās, and the beginning of the commentary on the initial verse.

SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañ.title: Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañjikā (fragment)
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañ.author: Vibhūticandra
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañ.summary: A Sanskrit fragment of Vibhūticandra's commentary (pañjikā) on Nāgārjuna's Piṇḍīkṛtasādhana (a core Āryasādhanakrama text of the Guhyasamājatantra). The surviving excerpt discusses the three isolations (kāyaviveka, vāgviveka, and cittaviveka) in the context of subtle breath control and mantra recitation (vajrajāpa) in completion stage practice. The text was identified and edited from an embedded citation in the Vajrācāryanayottama by Tanaka (2021).
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañ.attribution: Attributed to Vibhūticandra, matching the Tibetan Tengyur attribution (D 1832).
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañ.edition: Tanaka 2021, appendix I, pp. 84–88 (extracted from the Vajrācāryanayottama)
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Piṇḍīkṛtasādhanapañ.coverage: fragment — A short fragment commenting on the three isolations (kāyaviveka, vāgviveka, cittaviveka), extracted from the Vajrācāryanayottama.
translations: sgrub thabs mdor byas kyi dka' 'grel (Derge Tengyur D 1832): translated by bu ston rin chen grub; at dpal ri phug gi dben gnas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Svapnādhyāya.title: Svapnādhyāya (fragment)
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Svapnādhyāya.author: Vibhūticandra
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Svapnādhyāya.summary: The Svapnādhyāya is a versified treatise on dream interpretation (oneiromancy). Attributed in verse 1 to Bṛhaspati, it details the expected timing of dream fruition according to the watch of the night, followed by an enumeration of auspicious and inauspicious signs. It is translated into Tibetan (Tōh. 1749) by Vibhūticandra.
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Svapnādhyāya.attribution: The opening verse designates the work as composed by Bṛhaspati ('svapnādhyāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi bṛhaspativinirmitam', v. 1b). The e-text header notes 'possibly by Vibhūticandra' and 'tr. by Vibhūticandra, Tōh. 1749'.
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Svapnādhyāya.edition: Saerji, 'Sanskrit manuscript of the Svapnādhyāya preserved in Tibet', in Ernst Steinkellner et al. (eds.), Sanskrit Manuscripts in China, Beijing: 2009, pp. 241–257.
SA_T02_Vibhūticandra_Svapnādhyāya.coverage: fragment — Folios 1b–2b, verses 1–30 and 31ab; breaks off at 'sa vyādhimukto nirujo'. About four verses are missing at the end in Sanskrit but survive in the Tibetan translation.
translations: rmi lam brtag pa (Derge Tengyur D 1749): translated by Vibhūticandra (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Vilāsavajra_Nāmamantrārthāvalokin.title: Nāmamantrārthāvalokinī
SA_T02_Vilāsavajra_Nāmamantrārthāvalokin.author: Vilāsavajra
SA_T02_Vilāsavajra_Nāmamantrārthāvalokin.summary: The Nāmamantrārthāvalokinī by Vilāsavajra (fl. late 8th century) is an early commentary on the Mañjuśrīnāmasaṃgīti. Structured in fourteen topics/sections (adhikāras), it interprets the text's verses and epithets in terms of the five gnoses (pañcajñāna), the Buddha families, and Yoga/Māyājāla tantric frameworks. It is also noted for preserving citations of early Buddhist tantric scriptures (including the Guhyendutilakatantra).
SA_T02_Vilāsavajra_Nāmamantrārthāvalokin.attribution: Vilāsavajra (c. late 8th century) is identified in the final colophon as a resident of Ratnadvīpa, nephew of Agrabodhi, and also named Viśvarūpa.
SA_T02_Vilāsavajra_Nāmamantrārthāvalokin.edition: Unpublished working transcription and critical collation by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on manuscript Cambridge University Library Add. 115 (copied by Sarvamitra, dated NS 115) with collations and Tibetan references.
SA_T02_Vilāsavajra_Nāmamantrārthāvalokin.coverage: complete — Complete commentary across 14 chapters (adhikāras), ending with upasaṃhāra and the scribal colophon of Sarvamitra.
translations: Tribe, Anthony H. F. The Names of Wisdom: A Critical Edition and Annotated Translation of Chapters 1–5 of Vilāsavajra's Commentary on the Nāmasamgīti. (English)

Smṛtijñānakīrti (tr.), 'Phags pa mtshan yang dag par brjod pa'i rgya cher 'grel pa mtshan gsang sngags kyi don du rnam par lta ba zhes bya ba (Ārya-nāmasaṃgīti-ṭīkā nāmamantrārthāvalokinī-nāma), Otani No. 3356. (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Vāgīśvarakīrti_Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavi.title: Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavidhi
SA_T02_Vāgīśvarakīrti_Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavi.author: Vāgīśvarakīrti
SA_T02_Vāgīśvarakīrti_Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavi.summary: The Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavidhi is a concise initiation manual by the Vikramaśīla gatekeeper-scholar Vāgīśvarakīrti (fl. ca. 1000 CE) outlining tantric consecration according to the Guhyasamāja system (designated as 'Sāmājika' in the colophon). It details the qualifications and preliminary examination of disciples, maṇḍala entrance, samaya pledges, and the transmission of the four consecrations: vase (kalaśābhiṣeka), secret (guhyābhiṣeka), wisdom-gnosis (prajñājñānābhiṣeka), and the fourth (caturthābhiṣeka).
SA_T02_Vāgīśvarakīrti_Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavi.attribution: Vāgīśvarakīrti names himself in verse 2 (ato 'bhiṣekakrama eṣa vistaraṃ vihāya Vāgīśvarakīrtinocyate) and in the closing colophon.
SA_T02_Vāgīśvarakīrti_Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavi.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved from the opening maṅgala through the concluding verses and final author colophon.

SA_T02_anon_Abhisamayakrama.title: Abhisamayakrama (incomplete; end only in Tibetan)
SA_T02_anon_Abhisamayakrama.summary: The Abhisamayakrama is an anonymous Tantric manual of subtle-body physiology and internal realization (*abhisamaya*) affiliated with the Hevajra Tantra tradition. It describes the thirty-two subtle channels (*dvātriṃśannāḍī*) conveying bodhicitta, their somatic distribution, elemental natures, and correspondences with syllables, the four cakras, and the marks of a great being (*mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*), integrating internal yogic anatomy with generation- and completion-stage practice.
SA_T02_anon_Abhisamayakrama.attribution: Anonymous. The Sanskrit opening calls it the abhisamaya of the 'Hevajratantraratna that came from Oḍiyāna' (śrīoḍiyānavinirgatahevajratantraratnasyābhisamayaḥ). Neither the Sanskrit nor the Tibetan in the e-text names an author.
SA_T02_anon_Abhisamayakrama.edition: Unpublished transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of manuscript 'HSS 23', fols. 202r4–204v2 (siglum as given in PDSz; repository not identified here), with the Tibetan translation D1209 (Degé fols. 309a–311b) interleaved.
SA_T02_anon_Abhisamayakrama.coverage: partial — The Sanskrit runs from the beginning to seg. 93 (HSS 23, fols. 202r4–204v2). After that the e-text continues only with the Tibetan translation (D1209, up to fol. 311b) to the end of the work. The whole file interleaves Sanskrit and Tibetan (ACIP-style transliteration) segments.
translations: mngon par rtogs pa'i rim pa zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1209): translated by Ratnavajra, 'brog mi lo tsA ba shAkya ye shes (Tibetan)

SA_T02_anon_Avalokiteśvaravajroli_2010.title: Avalokiteśvaravajroli
SA_T02_anon_Avalokiteśvaravajroli_2010.summary: A short Vajrayāna esoteric instructional text outlining yogic-alchemical techniques under the heading of vajrolī associated with Avalokiteśvara. It sets forth five upadeśa sections—dhāraṇa, māraṇa, jāraṇa, kāraṇa, and prastāraṇa—blending internal subtle body physiology, sexual yoga (sahajānanda), and mantra recitation.
SA_T02_anon_Avalokiteśvaravajroli_2010.attribution: Anonymous Buddhist tantric/hathayogic text preserved on a single stray palm-leaf folio.
SA_T02_anon_Avalokiteśvaravajroli_2010.edition: Diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Oxford, 7 July 2010) from Kathmandu, Kaiser Library MS 160 (NGMPP reel C 17/4), palm-leaf, Maithilī script, folio 13r–v.
SA_T02_anon_Avalokiteśvaravajroli_2010.coverage: complete — Complete short text of five upadeśa sections (dhāraṇopadeśa, māraṇopadeśa, jāraṇopadeśa, kāraṇopadeśa, prastāraṇopadeśa) followed by an end section and final colophon on folio 13r–v.

SA_T02_anon_Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī_2022.title: Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī (chapters 1–8)
SA_T02_anon_Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī_2022.summary: An anonymous Sanskrit gloss (ṭippaṇī) on Śāntideva's Bodhicaryāvatāra, preserved uniquely in a fragmentary palm-leaf manuscript from Nepal (NAK 1-772 / NGMPP B 23/4). The text provides brief lemmatic commentary, grammatical analysis, and doctrinal glosses covering BCA chapters 1 through 8 (breaking off at verse 8.12).
SA_T02_anon_Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī_2022.attribution: The author of this commentary is unknown. The unique surviving manuscript bears no author colophon.
SA_T02_anon_Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī_2022.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, unpublished draft edition of an anonymous Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī based on manuscript NAK 1-772 = NGMOO B 23/4, latest revision 10 October 2022.
SA_T02_anon_Bodhicaryāvatāraṭippaṇī_2022.coverage: partial — Preserved on fols. 1v–21v of NAK 1-772 (NGMPP B 23/4), commenting on Bodhicaryāvatāra 1.1 through 8.12. Folio 2 is missing (covering 1.2–1.14), and the manuscript breaks off incomplete at 8.12.

SA_T02_anon_Kumārīkārcananimittoddeśa.title: Kumārīkārcananimittoddeśa
SA_T02_anon_Kumārīkārcananimittoddeśa.summary: A Tantric Buddhist manual on the worship (arcana) of virgin girls (kumārī) and the divination of omens (nimitta) arising from their actions during the ritual feast. Framed in the context of the Saṃvara traditions, it outlines the selection of girls of different castes for specific ritual objectives (śānti, puṣṭi, vaśya, vidveṣa), their bathing, ornamentation, seating, and offerings, followed by detailed interpretations of their gestures, emotional reactions, and eating behaviors as prognostications of health, disease, success, or death for the patron.
SA_T02_anon_Kumārīkārcananimittoddeśa.attribution: The work does not name an author; verse 3 states that the worship and interpretation of omens are drawn down from the Śrīsaṃvara and other tantras (śrīsaṃvarādiṣu kumārakumārikāṇāṃ pūjā ... saṃvarṇitātra vilikhāmi tato 'vatārya).
SA_T02_anon_Kumārīkārcananimittoddeśa.edition: Diplomatic transcription / working edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on National Archives Kathmandu (NAK) MS 1-1697 vi (Bauddhakarmakāṇḍa, NGMPP reel B 24/22, palm-leaf, ff. 3r–5v; cf. Cambridge University Library MS Add. 1697.3).
SA_T02_anon_Kumārīkārcananimittoddeśa.coverage: complete — Complete text spanning folios 3r–5v of NAK 1-1697 vi, concluding with a dedicatory verse and standard closing colophon.

SA_T02_anon_Subhāṣitasaṃgraha_Bendall_19.title: Subhāṣitasaṃgraha
SA_T02_anon_Subhāṣitasaṃgraha_Bendall_19.summary: The Subhāṣitasaṃgraha is an anonymous late Buddhist Sanskrit anthology that synthesizes Mahāyāna doctrine (Madhyamaka and Yogācāra) with Tantric and Sahajayāna teachings. It is an invaluable source for preserving otherwise lost Sanskrit quotations of key philosophical and tantric treatises, notably Candrakīrti's Madhyamakāvatāra, Āryadeva's Caryāmelāpakapradīpa, and numerous Anuttarayogatantra texts.
SA_T02_anon_Subhāṣitasaṃgraha_Bendall_19.attribution: The compiler of this late Buddhist anthology is anonymous. The primary manuscript was copied by Vidyāpatidatta at Vaḍagrāma.
SA_T02_anon_Subhāṣitasaṃgraha_Bendall_19.edition: Cecil Bendall (ed.), Subhāṣita-saṁgraha, Le Muséon, n.s. 4 (1903), 5 /1905), Louvain.
SA_T02_anon_Subhāṣitasaṃgraha_Bendall_19.coverage: complete — Complete text of the two-part anthology as edited by Cecil Bendall from the manuscript witness, concluding with: iti subhāṣitasaṃgrahaḥ samāptaḥ.

SA_T02_anon_Tantraślokasaṃgraha.title: Tantraślokasaṃgraha
SA_T02_anon_Tantraślokasaṃgraha.author: Jīvaharṣa
SA_T02_anon_Tantraślokasaṃgraha.summary: The Tantraślokasaṃgraha is a late Nepalese Sanskrit anthology of 154 verses compiled by Vajraguru Jīvaharṣa. It gathers stanzas on guru devotion, the nature of mind, bodhicitta, and tantric praxis, quoting Buddhist and non-Buddhist gnomic and tantric texts including the Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā, Nāmasaṃgīti commentaries, and the Advayasiddhi.
SA_T02_anon_Tantraślokasaṃgraha.attribution: Compiled by Vajraguru Jīvaharṣa (written 'jivaharkha' in Newar orthography). It is an anthology of 154 verses plus post-colophon additions compiled from various Buddhist and tantric scriptures and treatises.
SA_T02_anon_Tantraślokasaṃgraha.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on London, Royal Asiatic Society, MS Hodgson 52 (paper, 13 ff., Nepālākṣara).
SA_T02_anon_Tantraślokasaṃgraha.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript (RAS Hodgson 52, ff. 1–13, comprising 154 verses followed by the Pratītyasamutpādagāthā and two verses from Lakṣmīṅkarā's Advayasiddhi).

SA_T02_anon_Yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhi.title: Yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhi
SA_T02_anon_Yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhi.summary: A concise Vajrayāna ritual manual (kramavidhi) associated with the Heruka / Cakrasaṃvara and Yoginīsaṃcāra tantric literature. It describes the preliminary taking of refuge, generation of the protective vajra enclosure, and visualization of Śrī Heruka in union with Vajravārāhī surrounded by the retinues of yoginīs across the mind, speech, and body cakras. It maps these deities to the standard tantric sacred sites (pīṭha, upapīṭha, etc.) and provides the corresponding kavaca mantras.
SA_T02_anon_Yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhi.attribution: Anonymous Buddhist Tantric ritual manual (kramavidhi) belonging to the Yoginīsaṃcāra / Cakrasaṃvara cycle.
SA_T02_anon_Yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhi.edition: Pandey 1998 (159–161), MS = NAK 4-20/vi. bauddhatantra 66 = NGMPP A 48/5
SA_T02_anon_Yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhi.coverage: complete — Complete short ritual work closing with the work colophon (iti yoginīsaṃcārakramavidhiḥ) and scribal verses mentioning Jinacaraṇa and gaganaśararase 'bde.

SA_T02_anon_Yuktipradīpa.title: Yuktipradīpa
SA_T02_anon_Yuktipradīpa.summary: The Yuktipradīpa ('Lamp of Reasoning', also referred to in its final verse as Yuktidīpa) is a short anonymous Mahāyāna/Vajrayāna treatise vindicating ritual action, meditative practice, and moral exertion against quietist positions asserting that guru instruction alone confers awakening without regular observances (nityakarman). It defends the necessity of mantracaryā and quotes authorities including Nāgārjuna's Yuktiṣaṣṭikā, Śāntideva's Bodhicaryāvatāra, and Apabhraṃśa dohā verses.
SA_T02_anon_Yuktipradīpa.attribution: The work is anonymous; no author name appears in the opening verses, scribal notes, or concluding dedication.
SA_T02_anon_Yuktipradīpa.edition: Unpublished manuscript transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó (September 2012, Oxford), based on photographic reproductions of the manuscript from Giuseppe Tucci's collection (originally located at Sa skya monastery; cf. Sāṅkṛtyāyana 1937: 27–28).
SA_T02_anon_Yuktipradīpa.coverage: complete — Complete short treatise spanning from the opening maṅgala verse through the concluding praṇidhāna verse, with occasional akṣara lacunae due to out-of-focus areas on the manuscript photograph.

SA_T02_anon_Ḍākinīvajrapañjaraṭippati.title: Ḍākinīvajrapañjaraṭippati
SA_T02_anon_Ḍākinīvajrapañjaraṭippati.summary: An anonymous Sanskrit commentary (ṭippatī) on the Ḍākinīvajrapañjaratantra, a prominent explanatory tantra (vyākhyātantra) closely tied to the Hevajra cycle. The commentary spans fifteen chapters, explicating difficult lexical items, maṇḍala structures, abhiṣeka rituals, and yogic practices. This e-text is transcribed from an 8-folio manuscript preserved in the Kaiser Library, Kathmandu, with Tibetan root text verses provided for reference.
SA_T02_anon_Ḍākinīvajrapañjaraṭippati.attribution: Anonymous Sanskrit gloss (ṭippatī) on the Ḍākinīvajrapañjaratantra.
SA_T02_anon_Ḍākinīvajrapañjaraṭippati.coverage: complete — Complete commentary across 15 chapters (paṭala), covering all 8 folios of Kaiser Library MS 230 up to the final colophon (pañcadaśaḥ paṭalaḥ || o || ḍākinīvajrapañjaraṭippatiḥ samāptā).

SA_T02_unknown-VaidyapādaVitapāda_Kīlana.title: Kīlanavidhi (end missing)
SA_T02_unknown-VaidyapādaVitapāda_Kīlana.summary: A short anonymous Buddhist ritual text for "nailing" (kīlana) the guardians of the directions (lokapālas: Indra, Viṣṇu, Agni, Yama, etc.) and their retinues. The ten wrathful deities (daśakrodha), emanated from the practitioner's heart, pin them with kīlas, with a mantra for each. A bali offering, its consecration mantra and dismissal formulas follow. Szántó regards it as based on the *Mahābalividhi attributed to Vaidyapāda/Vitapāda (Tōh. 1876).
SA_T02_unknown-VaidyapādaVitapāda_Kīlana.attribution: No author is named in the surviving text. The transcriber's note in the e-text: the text is "not exact match, but similar to" the *Mahābalividhi attributed to Vitapāda/Vaidyapāda (Tōh. 1876, from fol. 76a3), and "I have no doubt that this is based on Vaidyapāda's work". It is therefore an anonymous adaptation; Vaidyapāda is not its author.
SA_T02_unknown-VaidyapādaVitapāda_Kīlana.edition: Unpublished e-text (transcription with apparatus of ante/post correctionem readings) by Péter-Dániel Szántó from the single palm-leaf manuscript IASWR MBB-II-185 ("Kīlanavidhi", palm-leaf, 5 × 30 cm, 5 folios, numbered 42–46), microfilmed by the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions. No printed edition.
SA_T02_unknown-VaidyapādaVitapāda_Kīlana.coverage: partial — Surviving 5 folios (42r–46v) of IASWR MS MBB-II-185, which once belonged to a composite codex (folio numbering 42–46). The text has the iconography of the lokapālas (vv. 1–16), the kīlana of the lokapālas and their retinues by the ten krodhas with mantras, bali consecration and offering, and dismissal. It breaks off mid-word at the end of 46v (seg. 134 "mukārāntatryakṣareṇa vā vi-"), so the last line(s) and any colophon are lost; the loss is probably small, since the text has reached the concluding visarjana.

SA_T02_various-siddhas_Jñānamālā.title: Jñānamālā
SA_T02_various-siddhas_Jñānamālā.summary: The Jñānamālā is a Sanskrit anthology of brief tantric aphorisms and yogic instructions (mostly one or two stanzas each) attributed to various Mahāsiddhas, including Lūyīpā and Mīnanātha. The verses focus on esoteric yogic practice, breath control, the dissolution of conceptualization, and the realization of non-dual gnosis. Preserved in a single late 13th-century palm-leaf manuscript from Nepal, it represents an important direct Sanskrit witness for Indian mahāsiddha lineages.
SA_T02_various-siddhas_Jñānamālā.attribution: Ascribed to various mahāsiddhas, featuring short yogic teachings attributed individually to siddhas such as Lūyīpā, Mīnanātha, Līlāpā, Ḍheṅkīpā, Abhavabhūti, and others.
SA_T02_various-siddhas_Jñānamālā.edition: Diplomatic transcription of National Archives Kathmandu MS 4-1171 (NGMPP reel A 59/20, palm-leaf, ca. late 13th c.) by Péter-Dániel Szántó (unpublished, PDSz corpus release PDSz_202608).
SA_T02_various-siddhas_Jñānamālā.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript from the opening salutation through the manuscript text and editorial index notes.

SA_T02_Ānandagarbha_Vajrajvālodayā.title: Vajrajvālodayā
SA_T02_Ānandagarbha_Vajrajvālodayā.author: Ānandagarbha
SA_T02_Ānandagarbha_Vajrajvālodayā.summary: The Vajrajvālodayā is a Heruka sādhanopāyikā composed by Ānandagarbha, based on the Sarvabuddhasamāyogatantra (Sarvabuddhasamāyogadākinījālaśaṃvara). It provides liturgical and yogic instructions for Heruka meditation, maṇḍala generation, mantras, mudrās, and ritual recitation. The text survives uniquely in a single Sanskrit codex and has no known Tibetan translation.
SA_T02_Ānandagarbha_Vajrajvālodayā.attribution: Attributed to Ānandagarbha in the colophon and final dedication verse.
SA_T02_Ānandagarbha_Vajrajvālodayā.edition: Diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of manuscript Göttingen, Niedersächsische Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Ms. sanscr. Xc 14/39, folios 170r6–186r3.
SA_T02_Ānandagarbha_Vajrajvālodayā.coverage: complete — Complete text transcription preserved on folios 170r6–186r3 in Göttingen Ms. Xc 14/39.

SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Ekavṛkṣādipañji.title: Ekavṛkṣādipañjikā
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Ekavṛkṣādipañji.author: Āryadeva
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Ekavṛkṣādipañji.summary: The Ekavṛkṣādipañjikā is a short esoteric Buddhist commentary attributed to (pseudo-)Āryadeva that serves as a satellite text to the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle. It provides an internalized yogic interpretation of the 'solitary tree' (ekavṛkṣa) motif, identifying the tree with the physical and subtle human body (śarīra) and mapping botanical features onto energy centers, channels, and drops, drawing upon and adapting earlier Śaiva esoteric models.
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Ekavṛkṣādipañji.attribution: Attributed in the Tibetan tradition (Tōh. 1614 / D 1614) to Āryadeva ('Phags-pa lha), identified as [pseudo-]Āryadeva.
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Ekavṛkṣādipañji.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, transcription in 'Selected Chapters from the Catuṣpīṭhatantra' (DPhil thesis, University of Oxford, 2012, section 3.4.2).
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Ekavṛkṣādipañji.coverage: complete — Synoptic transcription of two Sanskrit manuscript witnesses (Tokyo University Matsunami 312 and Asiatic Society Calcutta G 9993) collated with the Tibetan translation (Tōh. 1614).
translations: dpal gdan bzhi pa'i zab don ston pa shing gcig gi dka' 'grel (Derge Tengyur D 1614) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Āryadeva_Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhed.title: Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabheda
SA_T02_Āryadeva_Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhed.author: Āryadeva
SA_T02_Āryadeva_Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhed.summary: The Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabheda (also known as Svādhiṣṭhānaprabheda) is a 60-verse treatise of the completion stage belonging to the Guhyasamāja cycle of the Ārya tradition, attributed to the tantric Āryadeva. It describes the progressive dissolution of the elements into the four stages of emptiness and the clear light (prabhāsvara), followed by the manifestation of the illusory body through illusory contemplation (māyopamasamādhi).
SA_T02_Āryadeva_Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhed.attribution: Attributed to the tantric Āryadeva of the Ārya (Guhyasamāja) lineage, distinct from the c. 3rd-century Madhyamaka author Āryadeva.
SA_T02_Āryadeva_Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhed.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó's working collation of Janardan Pandey's editio princeps ('Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhedaḥ', Dhīḥ 10, 1990, based on National Archives Kathmandu MS 3/366) with Tokyo University Library MS 517.
SA_T02_Āryadeva_Svādhiṣṭhānakramaprabhed.coverage: complete — Complete work in 60 verses with closing colophon.
translations: bdag byin gyis brlab pa'i rim pa rnam par dbye ba (Derge Tengyur D 1805) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_ŚrībhūṣaṇaAlaṃkāraśrī_Mahāmāyāpañ.title: Mahāmāyāpañjikā (incomplete)
SA_T02_ŚrībhūṣaṇaAlaṃkāraśrī_Mahāmāyāpañ.author: Śrībhūṣaṇa
SA_T02_ŚrībhūṣaṇaAlaṃkāraśrī_Mahāmāyāpañ.summary: A commentary (pañjikā) on the Mahāmāyātantra, ascribed in Tibetan to Dpal rgyan (*Śrībhūṣaṇa). It glosses the tantra's terms, discusses Vajraḍāka and the goddesses, and quotes the Samājottara. The Sanskrit survives in a six-folio palm-leaf fragment in Tokyo University Library.
SA_T02_ŚrībhūṣaṇaAlaṃkāraśrī_Mahāmāyāpañ.attribution: The Tibetan colophon (D 1625) ascribes the work to slob dpon mkhas pa chen po Dpal rgyan; Sanskrit reconstructions *Śrībhūṣaṇa or *Alaṃkāraśrī. The Tibetan translation (D 1625) attributes the work to dpal rgyan (identified as *Vibhūṣita or Alaṃkāraśrī or Alaṃkaraśrīpāda).
SA_T02_ŚrībhūṣaṇaAlaṃkāraśrī_Mahāmāyāpañ.edition: Unpublished working transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of the palm-leaf fragment in the Tokyo University Library (TUL) Sanskrit manuscript collection (6 folios, Māgadhī script, undated, perhaps 11th century; bundle not identified in the catalogue), aligned with the Tibetan translation Derge D 1625. No printed edition of the Sanskrit text used.
SA_T02_ŚrībhūṣaṇaAlaṃkāraśrī_Mahāmāyāpañ.coverage: partial — Sanskrit from surviving palm-leaf folios (Tokyo University Library): fol. *2r(?), unnumbered leaf Xv, etc.; text breaks off mid-word at the end. Each Sanskrit passage is followed by the corresponding Tibetan of D 1625; the Tibetan also supplies the colophon.
translations: sgyu ma chen mo zhes bya ba'i dka' 'grel (Derge Tengyur D 1625) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Śrīdhara_Yamārimaṇḍalopāyikā.title: Yamāritantramaṇḍalopāyikā
SA_T02_Śrīdhara_Yamārimaṇḍalopāyikā.author: Śrīdhara
SA_T02_Śrīdhara_Yamārimaṇḍalopāyikā.summary: The Yamāritantramaṇḍalopāyikā is a Buddhist tantric ritual manual (maṇḍalavidhi) by Ācārya Śrīdhara detailing the ritual performance of the Kṛṣṇayamāri maṇḍala. It guides the master through site selection (bhūmiparigraha), earth pacification, drawing the colored powder mandala (rajaḥpāta), jar consecrations, fire offerings (homa), entrance into the mandala, and the full sequence of empowerments (abhiṣeka) through the prajñājñānābhiṣeka.
SA_T02_Śrīdhara_Yamārimaṇḍalopāyikā.attribution: Attributed to Ācārya Śrīdhara in the colophon (segment 586). Corresponds to Tibetan Tanjur D 1924 (gshin rje gshed nag po'i dkyil 'khor gyi sgrub thabs).
SA_T02_Śrīdhara_Yamārimaṇḍalopāyikā.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, semi-critical edition/transcript based on MS Kathmandu, National Archives of Nepal (NAK 5-85 / vi. bauddhatantra 64 = NGMPP reel no. B 31/26, palm-leaf, dated reign of Indradeva) and Kenichi Kuranishi's collation/edition.
SA_T02_Śrīdhara_Yamārimaṇḍalopāyikā.coverage: complete — Complete ritual text spanning topical sections from bhūmiparigraha through the higher initiations and concluding verses.
translations: gshin rje gshed nag po'i dkyil 'khor gyi sgrub thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1924): translated by Dānakīrti, nag 'tsho lo tsA ba tshul khrims rgyal ba (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Śubhākaragupta_Abhisamayamañjarī.title: Abhisamayamañjarī
SA_T02_Śubhākaragupta_Abhisamayamañjarī.author: Śubhākaragupta
SA_T02_Śubhākaragupta_Abhisamayamañjarī.summary: The Abhisamayamañjarī is an extensive Anuttarayogatantra ritual manual (sādhana) dedicated to the visualization and realization of Vajrayoginī / Vajravārāhī within the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. It outlines purification procedures, mantra recitations, bali offerings, the generation of the maṇḍala with accompanying retinue deities, and internal yogic meditations. Produced in late North Indian Buddhist circles (ca. 11th–12th century), it represents an important source for the development of late medieval Vajrayoginī practice.
SA_T02_Śubhākaragupta_Abhisamayamañjarī.attribution: The 1993 edition and the concluding colophon attribute the text to Mahācārya Śubhākaragupta. However, secondary literature and manuscript evidence (e.g. English, Steinkellner) attribute the Abhisamayamañjarī to Śākyarakṣita.
SA_T02_Śubhākaragupta_Abhisamayamañjarī.edition: Samdhong Rinpoche & Vrajavallabha Dwivedi (eds.), Abhisamayamañjarī of Śubhākara Gupta. Rare Buddhist Text Series. Sarnath, Varanasi: Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, 1993.
SA_T02_Śubhākaragupta_Abhisamayamañjarī.coverage: complete — Complete text of the sādhana from the opening homage through concluding verses and final colophon.

SA_T02_Śākyarakṣita_Hevajrābhisamayatila.title: Hevajrābhisamayatilaka (opening section; remainder in Tibetan translation)
SA_T02_Śākyarakṣita_Hevajrābhisamayatila.author: Śākyarakṣita
SA_T02_Śākyarakṣita_Hevajrābhisamayatila.summary: The Hevajrābhisamayatilaka is an extensive sādhana/abhisamaya manual of the Hevajra cycle by Śākyarakṣita, focused on Hevajra in the form Trailokyākṣepavīra. The Sanskrit part covers the opening: preliminary protection, outer/secret/reality worship with Gaurī and the other yoginīs, the sevenfold supreme worship, refuge, bodhicitta and the brahmavihāras, and the consecration of the visualised deity. The remainder, transmitted in Tibetan, treats armouring, offerings and bali rites, rosaries and mantra recitation, and the samayas.
SA_T02_Śākyarakṣita_Hevajrābhisamayatila.attribution: Attributed in the Tibetan tradition (Tôhoku 1277) to Mahāsthavira Śākyarakṣita (Tib. Shākya srung ba; historically sometimes reconstructed as *Śākyapāla or *Buddharakṣita).
SA_T02_Śākyarakṣita_Hevajrābhisamayatila.coverage: partial — Sanskrit text covers only the opening portion; the remainder is supplied in Tibetan translation from the Derge Tanjur (Tōh. 1277, vol. ta, running to fol. 130a6).
translations: dpal kye rdo rje'i mngon par rtogs pa'i thig le zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1277): translated by skyob pa dpal bzang po (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Cakrasaṃvarasād.title: Cakrasaṃvarasādhana (fragment)
SA_T02_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Cakrasaṃvarasād.author: Śūnyasamādhivajra
SA_T02_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Cakrasaṃvarasād.summary: A Tantric Buddhist ritual meditation manual (sādhana) dedicated to the Heruka Cakrasaṃvara maṇḍala, composed by a disciple of Ratnākaraśānti (most likely Śūnyasamādhivajra / Divākaracandra). It details the preliminary accumulations of merit and knowledge, the generation stage (utpattikrama) visualization of the Heruka maṇḍala, and the internal body-maṇḍala correspondences of the kāya-, vāk-, and cittacakras with bodily channels (nāḍīs). The text exhibits substantial textual parallels with the Bhramahara and the Bhugmalokeśvarasādhana, and utilizes the Jñānodayatantra for its completion stage.
SA_T02_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Cakrasaṃvarasād.attribution: Identified as very likely composed by Śūnyasamādhivajra (also known as Divākaracandra), a student of Ratnākaraśānti.
SA_T02_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Cakrasaṃvarasād.edition: Unpublished transcript and diplomatic edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó (ELTE Budapest, version 2024.iv.28), based on manuscript NAK 1-1697 11/7 bauddhatantra (NGMPP Reel A 994/7, palm-leaf, hook-topped script).
SA_T02_Śūnyasamādhivajra_Cakrasaṃvarasād.coverage: fragment — Preserved on folios 2r–27v (folio 1 missing, text breaks off on folio 27v with 'yadi [vā?] [explicit]').

SA_T04_Ratnākaraśānti-attribution-lots-o.title: Prajñāpāramitābhāvanākrama
SA_T04_Ratnākaraśānti-attribution-lots-o.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T04_Ratnākaraśānti-attribution-lots-o.summary: The Prajñāpāramitābhāvanākrama is a short meditation manual outlining the stages of cultivating the perfection of wisdom from a Yogācāra-Mādhyamika perspective. It guides the practitioner through the arousal of bodhicitta, refutation of external objects using the ekāneka-svabhāva argument, the realization of mind-only and the three natures (trisvabhāva), the counteracting of the six obstacles of samādhi (samādheḥ ṣaṭ caurāḥ), and the concluding praṇidhāna.
SA_T04_Ratnākaraśānti-attribution-lots-o.attribution: The colophon names Ratnākaraśānti ('kṛtir iyaṃ kalikālasarvajñapūrvadeśīyamahāpaṇḍitaratnākaraśāntipādānām'). The file tag notes that large sections borrow directly from Muktāvalī, along with citations of Kambalāmbarapāda, the Laṅkāvatārasūtra, and the Bodhicaryāvatāra.
SA_T04_Ratnākaraśānti-attribution-lots-o.coverage: complete — Complete text preserved in 11 sections from the opening mangala verse to the final colophon.

SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.title: Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā (chapter 1: Āyatanasamuccaya)
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.author: Saṅghatrāta
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.summary: The opening chapter (Āyatanasamuccaya) of Saṅghatrāta's Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā, a Sarvāstivāda verse manual. It expounds the twelve sense fields (āyatana), their classifications, relations to causes and conditions (hetu, pratyaya, phala), primary elements, and stages of dhyāna.
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.coverage: partial — Chapter 1 (Āyatanasamuccaya) only, consisting of 34 verses.

SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.title: Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā (chapter 2: Dhātusamuccaya)
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.author: Saṅghatrāta
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.summary: Chapter 2 (Dhātusamuccaya) of Saṅghatrāta's Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā. In 35 verses (continuous numbering 35–69), it presents an Abhidharma classification of the eighteen sensory elements (dhātu) and their distribution across the realms of existence (kāma-, rūpa-, and ārūpyadhātu), the stations of consciousness (vijñānasthiti), dependent origination (pratītyasamutpāda), and the bodily and mental faculties (indriya).
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.attribution: Attributed to the Buddhist master Saṅghatrāta (distinct from the Mahāyāna Abhidharmasamuccaya of Asaṅga).
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.edition: Francesco Sferra (ed.), preliminary edition/study of the Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā, 2022.
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 2 (Dhātusamuccaya) complete in 35 verses (continuous numbering 35–69), concluding with 'dhātusamuccayaḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.title: Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā (chapter 6: Mārgasamuccaya)
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.author: Saṅghatrāta
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.summary: Chapter 6 (Mārgasamuccaya, 'Compendium of the Path') of Saṅghatrāta's Abhidharmasamuccayakārikā expounds the soteriological path according to non-Mahāyāna Abhidharma. It systematically treats the four supports (adhiṣṭhāna: satya, tyāga, śama, prajñā), calm and insight practices including ānāpānasmṛti and smṛtyupasthāna, the stages of the noble path (darśana- and bhāvanāmārga), the spiritual fruits (phala), and the classification of noble disciples (āryapudgala).
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.attribution: Attributed to the Vaibhāṣika/Sarvāstivāda master Saṅghatrāta (Saṃghatrāta), distinct from Asaṅga's Mahāyāna Abhidharmasamuccaya.
SA_T07_Saṅghatrāta_Abhidharmasamuccayakā.coverage: partial — Chapter 6 (Mārgasamuccaya) only, comprising 70 verses numbered 6.1–6.70 (cumulative verses 208–277).

SA_T09_anon_Divyabhojana-avadāna.title: Tathāgatapratibimbapratiṣṭhānuśaṃsavarṇana (incomplete)
SA_T09_anon_Divyabhojana-avadāna.summary: A short dharmaparyāya set in the Jetavana at Śrāvastī on the merit of devotional acts towards the Buddha: Ānanda asks about sweeping, making a maṇḍalaka, taking refuge and making images, and, after a lacuna, the Buddha lists five benefits for a donor who has an image of the Tathāgata made (majesty and long life, wealth, beauty, rule as a cakravartin, and superior rebirth among the gods). The e-text is a diplomatic transcription of an incomplete manuscript dated saṃvat 384.
SA_T09_anon_Divyabhojana-avadāna.attribution: Canonical Mahāyāna scripture presented as the discourse of the Buddha delivered at the Jetavana monastery in Śrāvastī.

SA_T09_anon_Jātakamālāṭīkā_Basu_1989.title: Jātakamālāṭīkā (chapters 1–10)
SA_T09_anon_Jātakamālāṭīkā_Basu_1989.summary: The Jātakamālāṭīkā is an anonymous Sanskrit commentary on Āryaśūra's classic campū, the Jātakamālā. It provides word-for-word glosses, grammatical analysis, and discussions of poetic genre (notably citing Daṇḍin's definition of campū and discussing jātibandha in the prologue). This e-text comprises the critical edition of the commentary on the first ten stories (jātakas 1–10) edited by Ratna Basu.
SA_T09_anon_Jātakamālāṭīkā_Basu_1989.attribution: The commentary on Āryaśūra's Jātakamālā is anonymous in the surviving Sanskrit manuscript tradition.
SA_T09_anon_Jātakamālāṭīkā_Basu_1989.edition: Ratna Basu, Eine literatur-kritische Studie zu Āryaśūras Jātakamālā zusammen mit einer kritischen Edition der anonymen Jātakamālāṭīkā und einer kritischen Edition der Jātakamālāpañjikā des Vīryasiṃha, Inaugural-Dissertation, Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität zu Bonn, 1989, pp. 241–424.
SA_T09_anon_Jātakamālāṭīkā_Basu_1989.coverage: partial — Covers commentary on Jātakas 1–10, edited across pp. 241–424 of Ratna Basu's dissertation.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-04-2.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (section 4.2: Anusmṛti)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-04-2.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-04-2.summary: Section 4.2 (Anusmṛti) of the Buddhist ritual anthology Tridaṇḍamālā. The text preserves a short canonical prose sūtra in which the Buddha at Śrāvastī explains that recollecting the Tathāgata and his qualities (tathāgatam ākārataḥ samanusmarati) even for a fleeting moment brings mental clarity, concentration, and spiritual faculties.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-04-2.attribution: The ritual compilation/anthology Tridaṇḍamālā is attributed to Aśvaghoṣa/scriptural in source metadata. Section 4.2 is a canonical prose sūtra quotation on buddhānusmṛti.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-05-1-2-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 5, sections 1–3)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-05-1-2-3.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-05-1-2-3.summary: Chapter 5 (sections 1–3) of the Tridaṇḍamālā, a Buddhist poetic and liturgical anthology traditionally ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa. The text opens with stotras dedicated to the Three Jewels, presents an exposition on the impurity and impermanence of the physical body (aśucibhāvanā, including the metaphor of the body as an anthill / valmīka), and concludes with protective benedictory verses.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-05-1-2-3.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 5, sections 1 to 3 (verses 5.1.1 to 5.3.15).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-07-1-2-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 7, sections 1–3)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-07-1-2-3.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-07-1-2-3.summary: The Tridaṇḍamālā is a Buddhist compilation of devotional, didactic, and liturgical stanzas associated with Aśvaghoṣa. This extract covering chapter 7 (sections 7.1–7.3) opens with veneration of the Three Jewels (Triratna) and didactic warnings against carnal desire and infatuation with women—largely drawn from Aśvaghoṣa's Saundarananda—concluding with protective verses and an aspiration (praṇidhāna) for the longevity of the Buddhist teachings.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-07-1-2-3.attribution: Attributed in source header to Aśvaghoṣa/scriptural.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-07-1-2-3.coverage: partial — Contains sections 7.1, 7.2, and 7.3 of chapter 7 (ending with 7.3.20).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-08-1-2-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 8)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-08-1-2-3.summary: Chapter 8 of the Tridaṇḍamālā. The chapter presents doctrinal arguments refuting the permanent self (ātman) and the Sāṃkhya conception of kṣetrajña, preserving Sanskrit stanzas from cantos 12 and 16 of Aśvaghoṣa's Buddhacarita.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-08-1-2-3.attribution: The Tridaṇḍamālā quotes extensively from cantos 12 and 16 of Aśvaghoṣa's Buddhacarita.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-08-1-2-3.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 8 (sections 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3) of the Tridaṇḍamālā, concluding with verse 8.3.7 and the closing formula 'yānīha bhūtānīti vācyam || 8 ||'.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-10-1-2-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 10)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-10-1-2-3.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-10-1-2-3.summary: The tenth chapter/tridaṇḍa of the Tridaṇḍamālā. Contains introductory verses, a sūtra section on persons of great help, and concluding verses on the gift of the Dharma and a protective benediction.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-10-1-2-3.attribution: Ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa/scriptural in the source catalog header.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-11.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 11)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-11.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-11.summary: Chapter 11 of the Tridaṇḍamālā, a Buddhist liturgical anthology attributed to Aśvaghoṣa. The chapter contains verses in praise of the Three Jewels (Triratna), vivid poetic reflections on the defects of bodily existence, old age (jarā), sickness, and mortality, concluding with aspirations for the eternal endurance of the Dharma lamp (dharmolkā) and the protection of the teachings.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-11.attribution: Attributed to Aśvaghoṣa / scriptural in source headers.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-15-1-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 15: sections 1 and 3)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-15-1-3.summary: The Tridaṇḍamālā is a Buddhist didactic text compiled in verse. This excerpt from chapter 15 contains verses warning against spiritual torpor and sloth (kausīdya, vv. 15.1.4–8, quoting Aśvaghoṣa's Saundarananda 16.95–96) followed by an exhortation to unwavering energetic effort (vīrya, vv. 15.3.1–12) as an essential condition for spiritual success and awakening.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-15-1-3.attribution: Formerly attributed to Aśvaghoṣa in the file metadata because the text includes two verses quoted from Aśvaghoṣa's Saundarananda (16.95–96 at 15.1.6–7). The compilation itself is anonymous.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-15-1-3.coverage: excerpt — Excerpts from chapter 15 only: section 15.1 (vv. 4–8) on sloth (kausīdya) and section 15.3 (vv. 1–12) on vigor (vīrya).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-17-1.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (verses 17.1.5–30 on śīla)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-17-1.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-17-1.summary: Twenty-six stanzas (17.1.5–30) praising moral discipline (śīla): its fruits, the futility of ascetic and ritual practices without it, and its value regardless of caste. Several stanzas parallel Buddhacarita canto 23 and Vasubandhu's Śīlaparikathā.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-17-1.attribution: In these stanzas the e-text notes parallels with Buddhacarita 23.17–21, Vasubandhu's Śīlaparikathā (vv. 5–9) and quotations in Dharmakīrti's Jātakamālāṭīkā (17.1.5–6, there attributed to Parahitaghoṣa per the e-text note).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-17-1.coverage: excerpt — Verses 17.1.5–17.1.30 only (26 stanzas on śīla, ending 'itīha śīlaṃ parikīrtitaṃ mayā …').

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-21-2.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (section 21.2: Śivapathikāsūtra)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-21-2.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-21-2.summary: Section 21.2 of the Tridaṇḍamālā, preserving the Śivapathikāsūtra, a canonical Buddhist discourse. Located at the Jetavana in Śrāvastī, the Buddha instructs newly ordained monks to visit a charnel ground (śivapathikā) to contemplate corpses in various stages of decomposition (aśubhā bhāvanā) and reflect on the components of the human body in order to eliminate passion, hatred, and delusion.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-21-2.attribution: The Tridaṇḍamālā is traditionally ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa. Section 21.2 contains a canonical discourse spoken by the Buddha (Śivapathikāsūtra).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-21-2.coverage: partial — Contains section 21.2 of the Tridaṇḍamālā (Śivapathikāsūtra, complete prose setting and 12 verses).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-23-1-2-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 23.1–3)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-23-1-2-3.summary: The Tridaṇḍamālā is a Buddhist anthology and homiletic manual preserved in Sanskrit manuscript material, comprising scriptural quotations and verses on moral practice. This portion (chapter 23, sections 1–3) focuses on the true definition of a śramaṇa, the dangers of moral laxity, and the preeminence of śīla (virtue), drawing upon canonical texts and classical works such as Aśvaghoṣa's Saundarananda and Vasubandhu's Śīlaparikathā.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-23-1-2-3.attribution: Formerly catalogued under Aśvaghoṣa because verses from his Saundarananda are quoted in this section (e.g. 7.48–49). The Tridaṇḍamālā is a multi-author ritual/homiletic anthology compiling canonical sūtras and diverse Buddhist authors (including Vasubandhu).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-23-1-2-3.edition: Edition by Kazunobu Matsuda et al. (2025). Transcribed and annotated by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Budapest, 2 December 2025).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-23-1-2-3.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 23, sections 1 to 3 (numbered 23.1.1 to 23.3.25).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-26-1-2-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapter 26)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-26-1-2-3.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-26-1-2-3.summary: The twenty-sixth tridaṇḍa of the Tridaṇḍamālā, a Sarvāstivāda liturgical compilation ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa. After homage to the Three Jewels and to the Sarvāstivāda teachers, verses develop the simile of the four poisonous snakes (the elements) and the murderous aggregates; the recited sūtra is the Āśīviṣopama (simile of the snakes, executioners, empty village and raft), and the closing verses treat the emptiness of the sense-bases and the absence of a self, ending with a wish for the endurance of the teaching.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-26-1-2-3.attribution: Verse 26.1.4 salutes the Sarvāstivāda teachers ('tān vande … sarvāstivādān gurūn') and lists Sarvāstivāda tenets.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-26-1-2-3.coverage: partial — Introductory verses 26.1.1–18, the Āśīviṣopama-sūtra (four snakes in a basket, five executioners, empty village, raft) in sections [1]–[8], and concluding verses 26.3.1–10 ending with the incipit of 'yānīha bhūtāni'. Some akṣaras illegible (marked x).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-27-1-2.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (chapters 27.1–2)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-27-1-2.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-27-1-2.summary: Excerpts from chapter 27 of the Tridaṇḍamālā, attributed to Aśvaghoṣa. The text opens with stanzas on the perils of saṃsāra, defilements, and the Buddha as healer, followed by a canonical discourse illustrating the journey across the dangerous alkaline river (kṣāranadī) and its symbolic interpretations (adhivacana) corresponding to the Buddhist path.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-27-1-2.attribution: Intersperses verses attributed to Aśvaghoṣa with canonical scriptural prose passages.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-27-1-2.coverage: excerpt — Contains sections 27.1 and 27.2 from chapter 27 of the Tridaṇḍamālā: verses 27.1.4–13 followed by prose discourse and allegory (§1–19).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-29-2.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (section 29.2: Akṣaṇasūtra)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-29-2.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-29-2.summary: This text constitutes section 29.2 of the Tridaṇḍamālā anthology, preserving the Sanskrit text of the canonical Akṣaṇasūtra. The Buddha enumerates the eight inopportune states (aṣṭāv akṣaṇāḥ) that impede the practice of religious life (brahmacaryavāsa)—such as rebirth in hell, as an animal, as a preta, among long-lived gods, in borderlands, with sensory/intellectual disability, or holding wrong views—and contrasts them with the rare opportune moment (kṣaṇa) of human birth during the dispensation of a Buddha, concluding with eight didactic verses.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-29-2.attribution: The Tridaṇḍamālā is an anthology attributed to Aśvaghoṣa / scriptural. Section 29.2 quotes the canonical Akṣaṇasūtra, a sūtra spoken by the Buddha on the eight inopportune conditions.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-29-2.coverage: excerpt — Contains section 29.2 of the Tridaṇḍamālā, preserving the text of the canonical Akṣaṇasūtra (prose listing the eight akṣaṇas and the opportune kṣaṇa, followed by 8 summary verses).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-30-2.title: Pañcasthānasūtra
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-30-2.summary: The Pañcasthānasūtra is a canonical Buddhist discourse prescribing five facts that householders and monastics alike should frequently contemplate (abhīkṣṇaṃ pratyavekṣitavyam): vulnerability to disease (vyādhidharmatā), aging (jarādharmatā), death (maraṇadharmatā), separation from loved ones (viprayoga), and ownership of one's own actions (karmasvakatā). Contemplation of these realities dismantles pride in health, youth, and life, and motivates cultivation of the Noble Eightfold Path to eliminate the fetters (saṃyojana).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-30-2.attribution: A canonical discourse spoken by the Buddha, preserved in Sanskrit within the manuscript tradition of the Tridaṇḍamālā (anthology traditionally attributed to Aśvaghoṣa).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-30-2.coverage: complete — Complete text of the sūtra from opening nidāna (evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavāñ chrāvastyāṃ viharati...) to the concluding rejoinder (idam avocad bhagavān...).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-34-1.title: Buddhacarita (canto 15)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-34-1.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-34-1.summary: Canto 15 of Aśvaghoṣa's Buddhacarita, preserved in the Tridaṇḍamālā (34.1).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-34-1.attribution: Aśvaghoṣa is listed as the author in the source header.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-36-2.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (section 36.2: Asārasūtra)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-36-2.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-36-2.summary: This excerpt constitutes section 36.2 of the Tridaṇḍamālā, presenting the Sanskrit text of the Asārasūtra. Set in the Jetavana at Śrāvastī, the Buddha instructs the monks on how to extract that which has essence (sāra) from three essenceless things (asāra): body (kāya) via reverent salutation and homage, wealth (bhoga) through charitable giving to ascetics and the needy, and life (jīvita) through the realization of the Four Noble Truths. The sūtra concludes with three summarising verses.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-36-2.attribution: The Tridaṇḍamālā is traditionally ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa. Section 36.2 embeds the canonical Asārasūtra.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-36-2.coverage: excerpt — Contains only section 36.2 (the Asārasūtra in prose and three verses) from the Tridaṇḍamālā.

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-37-3.title: Tridaṇḍamālā (verses 37.3 on the ten epithets of the Tathāgata)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-37-3.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-37-3.summary: Twelve stanzas from section 37.3 of the Tridaṇḍamālā giving etymological explanations of the epithets of the Buddha (including bhagavat, tathāgata, arhat, samyaksaṃbuddha, vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, sugata, lokavid, anuttara, naradamyasārathi, śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, buddha).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-37-3.attribution: Ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa in the header metadata. Matsuda 2020 connects these stanzas to the Sūtrālaṃkāra.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-37-3.coverage: excerpt — Twelve stanzas (explaining bhagavat, tathāgata, arhat, samyaksaṃbuddha, vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, sugata, lokavid, anuttara, naradamyasārathi, śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, buddha) forming section 37.3. A few akṣaras illegible (x).

SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-anthology_.title: Buddhacarita (selected verses from the Tridaṇḍamālā)
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-anthology_.author: Aśvaghoṣa
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-anthology_.summary: Fifty Sanskrit verses from the later, otherwise lost cantos of Aśvaghoṣa's Buddhacarita (14.35–44 on the fall of gods from heaven, 19.19–22 and 20.33 on karma and impermanence, 24.13–45 the Buddha's consolation of Ānanda, 26.49 and 26.60 from the final teaching). Until their identification the Sanskrit text was known only up to 14.31 from the Nepalese manuscript tradition. The verses were recovered by Kazunobu Matsuda from quotations in the Tridaṇḍamālā.
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-anthology_.attribution: The verses belong to Aśvaghoṣa's Buddhacarita (cantos after 14.31 otherwise lost in Sanskrit and known only from the Tibetan translation and the Chinese Fo suoxing zan, T 192).
SA_T10_Aśvaghoṣa_Tridaṇḍamālā-anthology_.coverage: excerpt — 50 verses: Bc 14.35–44, 19.19–22, 20.33, 24.13–45, 26.49, 26.60, as edited in Matsuda 2023. The e-text's opening list also names Bc 15.1–58, 16.76, 80–93 and 18.62–78 (TDM 34.1, 8.1, 8.3, 16.1), but these are marked 'published separately' in Matsuda's article and their text is NOT included in the e-text (ending is Bc 26.60). The Buddhacarita originally had 28 cantos.
translations: Matsuda 2023 (Japanese)

SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.title: Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā (chapters 1–2)
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.author: Sarvarakṣita
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.summary: The Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā is a Buddhist ornate kāvya by Sarvarakṣita describing cosmology, world destruction (saṃvarta), and re-evolution (vivarta) in accordance with the Abhidharma tradition. Chapters 1 and 2 comprise the introductory narrative frame (Nidānakāṇḍa) recounting the Buddha's descent and background, followed by an account of the cosmic evolution and appearance of human beings (Vivartamānāvasthākāṇḍa).
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.coverage: partial — Contains the first two chapters: kāṇḍa 1 (Nidānakāṇḍa) and kāṇḍa 2 (Vivartamānāvasthākāṇḍa, ending at 'dvitīyaṃ ca vivartamānāvasthākāṇḍam').

SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.title: Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā (chapters 3–4)
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.author: Sarvarakṣita
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.summary: The Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā by Sarvarakṣita is an ornate Buddhist Sanskrit narrative kāvya outlining cosmic evolution and destruction according to the cosmology of the Saṃmatīya school. Chapters 3 and 4 treat the re-evolution of the world (vivṛttāvasthā), the physical and moral devolution of sentient beings as material foods are consumed, the appearance of sex differentiation and private dwelling, and the descent into the degenerate age (kali).
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.attribution: Composed by Sarvarakṣita, a Buddhist poet associated with Saṃmatīya cosmological traditions.
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.coverage: partial — Contains chapters (kāṇḍas) 3 (Vivṛttāvasthāyā ekāntasukhāvasthānakāṇḍa) and 4, concluding with viśrāma 2 (Kalipraveśa, verse 4.2.19).

SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.title: Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā (chapters 4.3–6)
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.author: Sarvarakṣita
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.summary: The Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā is a Buddhist narrative poem (kāvya) by Sarvarakṣita describing traditional Buddhist cosmology, focusing on the periodic destruction and evolution of the world (saṃvarta and vivarta). This portion comprises the second half of the poem (kāṇḍas 4.3 to 6.4), detailing intermediate dissolutions caused by famine, disease, and war, followed by world recovery, moral decay and regeneration, and the concluding lineage and dedication verses.
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.attribution: Attributed to the Buddhist poet and master (ācārya, bhadanta, mahākavi) Sarvarakṣita in the text's end colophon.
SA_T10_Sarvarakṣita_Mahāsaṃvartanīkathā-.coverage: partial — Contains kāṇḍa 4.3 through kāṇḍa 6.4 (end of work), terminating with the final work colophon and total verse/grantha count.

SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-11.title: Saddharmaparikathā (chapter 11)
SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-11.summary: Chapter 11 of the Saddharmaparikathā, a Buddhist homiletic discourse (parikathā) in mixed prose and verse (campū). This chapter is intended for dispelling grief over the loss of a friend or relative (śokavinodanārtha), expounding how sorrow destroys virtue, mental clarity, and health, and encouraging steadfast reflection on the universal transience of conditioned existence.
SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-11.attribution: The work is an anonymous Buddhist homiletic text; author is unknown.
SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-11.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, unpublished working critical edition/transcription (Szántó 2021).
SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-11.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 11 only (54 numbered verses with intervening prose commentary/exhortations on śokavinodana).

SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-12.title: Saddharmaparikathā (chapter 12)
SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-12.summary: Chapter 12 of the Saddharmaparikathā, a prosimetric Buddhist homiletic text (parikathā). This chapter focuses on warning against the dangers and moral defects of gambling (dyūtādīnavapradarśana), citing figures such as Nala, Puṣkara, Śakuni, and the yakṣa Pūrṇaka to demonstrate how gaming destroys wealth, reputation, and virtuous mental dispositions.
SA_T10_anon_Saddharmaparikathā-12.coverage: partial — Contains only chapter 12 on the perils of gambling (dyūtādīnavapradarśane vācyam), comprising 14 verses (numbered 12.1–12.14) with intervening prose commentary/exegesis.

SA_T12_Ratnākaraśānti_Chandoratnākarasvo.title: Chandoratnākara with Svopajñavṛtti
SA_T12_Ratnākaraśānti_Chandoratnākarasvo.author: Ratnākaraśānti
SA_T12_Ratnākaraśānti_Chandoratnākarasvo.summary: The Chandoratnākara is a Buddhist treatise on Sanskrit metrics (chandaḥśāstra) by Ratnākaraśānti, accompanied by his own prose autocommentary (Svopajñavṛtti). Spanning six chapters, it systematically describes meters, claiming eight structural improvements over earlier treatises by Piṅgala and Jayadeva. Preserved in manuscripts as well as in Tibetan translation (D 4459).
SA_T12_Ratnākaraśānti_Chandoratnākarasvo.attribution: Ratnākaraśānti composed both the root treatise and the prose autocommentary, attested in opening verses, chapter colophons, and the final colophon (kṛtir iyaṃ śrīratnākaraśāntipādānām).
SA_T12_Ratnākaraśānti_Chandoratnākarasvo.coverage: complete — Complete text in six adhyāyas, ending at segment [703] '[iti ratnākaraśāntikṛte chandoratnākare ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ]' and closing verse 6.15, followed by the scribal colophon dated NS 179 (ca. 1059 CE).
translations: sdeb sbyor rin chen 'byung gnas zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 4459): translated by stag tshang lo tsA ba shes rab rin chen (Tibetan)

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Akṣas.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (akṣasūtrapratiṣṭhā section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Akṣas.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Akṣas.summary: This excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual manual Kriyāsamuccaya details the consecration of a rosary (akṣasūtrapratiṣṭhā), including visualizations assigning deities to the cords and beads, followed by an excerpt from chapter 45 of the Vajraḍākatantra outlining beads, cord materials, and finger placements appropriate for pacifying, enriching, subjugating, and wrathful rituals (nānākarmākṣasūtravidhiḥ). The Sanskrit text is accompanied sentence-by-sentence by the canonical Tibetan translation from the Tengyur.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Akṣas.attribution: Attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa. Involves material from Abhayākaragupta's Vajrāvalī.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Akṣas.edition: Critical transcription and alignment prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó (Kolozsvár, 5 July 2025; PDSz corpus release PDSz_202608). SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Argha.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Arghavidhi section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Argha.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Argha.summary: A Vajrayāna ritual text attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa. This section focuses on arghavidhi (the offering of ritual water and oblations), detailing rites for foundational ceremonies: constructing vihāras, caityas, and monasteries, transcribing scriptures (saddharmalikhana), renovating dilapidated shrines (jīrṇoddhāra), and presenting the sequence of argha, pādya, and ācamana libations. The e-text features the Sanskrit text interlineally aligned with its Tibetan Tanjur translation.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Argha.coverage: excerpt — Contains only the arghavidhi section of the Kriyāsamuccaya (including vihāracaityagandhakuṭisaṅghāśramādyarghavidhi, saddharmalikhanārghavidhi, jīrṇoddhārārghavidhi, and arghādidānalakṣaṇavidhi), aligned line-by-line with its Tibetan translation from the Derge Tanjur (D 3305, fols. 56b4–59b7).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bali.author: Jagaddarpaṇa

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Bhūmiparigrahavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.summary: This text contains the Bhūmiparigraha (taking possession of the ground) section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya, an extensive manual for Vajrayāna sacerdotal rituals. It lays out the preparatory rituals for constructing a maṇḍala, focusing especially on dramatic sacred dance (tāṇḍava, buddhanāṭaka), character representation, gestures (abhinaya), mudrās, and ritual chants cited from scriptures such as the Ḍākinīvajrapañjara and Māyājālatantra.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.attribution: The Kriyāsamuccaya (also known as Vajrācāryakriyāsamuccaya) is an extensive Vajrayāna ritual compendium by the Indian master Jagaddarpaṇa. Translated into Tibetan in the Tengyur (D 3305 by Mañjuśrī and Blo-gros rgyal-mtshan).
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.edition: Diplomatic transcription / edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó based primarily on Kaiser Library no. 110, with lacunae supplied from Lokesh Chandra's facsimile, collated with the Tibetan translation (D 3305).
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.coverage: partial — Contains only the section on ritual ground preparation and acquisition (bhūmiparigrahavidhiḥ) out of the Kriyāsamuccaya compendium.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Bhūmiparīkṣā)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.summary: This text comprises the Bhūmiparīkṣāvidhi (site examination ritual) from Jagaddarpaṇa's Vajrācāryakriyāsamuccaya. It provides tantric vāstu and ritual procedures for inspecting the soil qualities (color, odor, taste, slope), determining auspicious and inauspicious trees around the perimeter, digging and water-filling tests, and performing water oblations and the visualization of Jāṅgulī prior to laying the foundation of a vihāra or caitya.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūmi.edition: Unpublished working edition and transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on MS Kaiser Library 110 and Lokesh Chandra's facsimile edition, collated with the Tibetan translation in the Degé Tengyur (Toh 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūśa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Bhūśalyasūtrapātananimitta)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūśa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūśa.summary: The Bhūśalyasūtrapātananimitta is a section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. This excerpt treats the divination of omens (nimitta) during the line-marking (sūtrapātana) on the ground to detect subterranean impurities (śalya). The bilingual text presents Sanskrit verses alongside their classical Tibetan translation (D 3305).
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūśa.attribution: Attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa. The Sanskrit verses are accompanied line-by-line by their Tibetan translation from the Tanjur (D 3305).
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Bhūśa.coverage: excerpt — A section of the Kriyāsamuccaya concerning omens and divination during the line-marking ritual for subterranean obstacles (bhūśalyasūtrapātananimittavidhi), including Sanskrit verses and corresponding Tibetan translation.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Caity.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Caityalakṣaṇavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Caity.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Caity.summary: The Caityalakṣaṇavidhi is a short section from Jagaddarpaṇa's Vajrācāryakriyāsamuccaya specifying the architectural proportions and iconographic elements of Buddhist stūpas (caityas). It classifies caityas into four types (kumbha, kanaka, dhānyarāśi, and latā) and details the proportions of the base, dome, harmikā, and umbrellas (chattras), along with the placement of Vairocana and the directional Buddhas.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Caity.attribution: Attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa, author of the Vajrācāryakriyāsamuccaya (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Devat.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Devatādhivāsanavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Devat.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Devat.summary: A short ritual excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya prescribing the devatādhivāsana rite (habitation/preliminary consecration of the deities of the maṇḍala). The officiant prepares the maṇḍala ground, invokes the principal and retinue deities, and recites verses requesting permission to paint the maṇḍala for the welfare of disciples and sentient beings. The e-text provides the Sanskrit text interlinear with the Tibetan translation from the Degé Tengyur.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Dhvaj.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Dhvaj.summary: An excerpt from the Kriyāsamuccaya containing the Dhvajādyavaropaṇapratiṣṭhāvidhi, prescribing measurements, mantras, and ritual procedures for erecting and consecrating temple banners (dhvaja, patākā), canopies (chattra), and fly-whisks (cāmara).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gandh.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Gandhakuṭyādilakṣaṇavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gandh.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gandh.summary: The Gandhakuṭyādilakṣaṇavidhi is an architectural section of Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual compendium, the Kriyāsamuccaya. It details proportional measurements, layout, and structural specifications (using standard measuring units such as kāṇḍākāṣṭhī) for constructing a perfumed chamber (gandhakuṭī), temple walls, plinth (jagatī), and surmounting caitya to enshrine sacred images. In this digital edition, the Sanskrit metrical text is presented side-by-side with its Tibetan translation from the Tanjur.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gaṇa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Gaṇacakravidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gaṇa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gaṇa.summary: A transcription of the Gaṇacakravidhi (tantric communal feast) section from Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual compendium, the Kriyāsamuccaya (or Vajrācāryakriyāsamuccaya). The chapter details the classifications, preparations, offerings, and codes of conduct for communal assemblies and feasts, including the saṅghabhojya, gaṇacakra, mahācakra, niśācakra, and yakṣālicakra. The e-text aligns the Sanskrit witnesses with the canonical Tibetan translation preserved in the Tengyur (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gaṇḍī.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Gaṇḍīlakṣaṇavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gaṇḍī.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Gaṇḍī.summary: This excerpt constitutes the Gaṇḍīlakṣaṇavidhi section from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. It provides prescriptive rules on the dimensions, material specifications, and tantric symbolism of the gaṇḍī, detailing its striking ritual (ākoṭana) and the concluding adhiṣṭhānamantra.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Homa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (homa section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Homa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Homa.summary: This section of Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual compendium Kriyāsamuccaya describes the fire sacrifice (homa). It details the construction and dimensions of fire hearths (kuṇḍa) for peaceful, expansive, magnetizing, and wrathful activities, ritual ladles and vessels, oblations, external offerings to deities, and internalized yogic offering (ādhyātmahoma). The transcription includes an interlinear Tibetan translation from the Tengyur.

The text specifies the placement of water jars in directions outside the mandala perimeter for mandalas including the Mañjuvajra and Kālacakra systems. This digital text presents Szántó's transcription alongside the corresponding canonical Tibetan translation from the Tengyur (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Kalaś.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Kalaśādhivāsana section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Kalaś.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Kalaś.summary: This section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya prescribes the Kalaśādhivāsanavidhi, the ritual preparatory consecration and installation of the ritual vessels (kalaśa) in esoteric Buddhist initiation ceremonies. It provides meticulous measurements and physical specifications for the vessels corresponding to various ritual classes (such as śāntika and pauṣṭika rites), their spatial placement outside the maṇḍala, the arrangement of threads and coloring powders, and the visualization of inner deities and seed syllables accompanied by purificatory mantras.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Khaṭi.summary: A short excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual compendium Kriyāsamuccaya detailing the Khaṭikāsūtrapātana (the ceremonial snapping of chalk cord lines to lay out the geometric perimeter of a tantric maṇḍala). The text quotes canonical sources such as the Ḍākinīvajrapañjaratantra and closely follows Abhayākaragupta's Vajrāvalī, presented here with interlinear Tibetan translation from the Tanjur.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.summary: The Kriyāsamuccaya by Jagaddarpaṇa contains ritual procedures. This excerpt preserves the Maṇḍalagṛhādividhi section, which describes the preparation and construction of the pavilion for the mandala ritual, including examination and selection of the ground, pacification of obstacles, bali offerings, and purification through the invocation of the earth goddess (pṛthivīdevatā). The e-text pairs the Sanskrit text with the Tibetan translation (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Saparikaramaṇḍalasādhana)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.summary: The Kriyāsamuccaya of Jagaddarpaṇa models its structure on Abhayākaragupta's Vajrāvalī. This excerpt contains the saparikaramaṇḍalasādhanavidhi ('ritual procedure for accomplishing the maṇḍala together with its accessories'), detailing mantra recitations, mudrā meditation, circumambulation, and directional banner allocations. The Sanskrit transcription is presented here in parallel with its Tibetan translation from the Tanjur.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Maṇḍalopasaṃhāra section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Maṇḍa.summary: The Maṇḍalopasaṃhāra section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya details the procedures for concluding ritual ceremonies and dismantling the esoteric Buddhist maṇḍala. Following the gaṇacakra feast and the dismissal of disciples, the master recites the hundred-syllable mantra, releases the wisdom-circle (jñānacakra), reabsorbs the emanated maṇḍala, removes the ritual pegs (kīlaka), and erases the colored powder designs. The e-text features Szántó's composite Sanskrit transcription along with an interlinear Tibetan translation from Degé Tanjur Toh 3305.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Mānas.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Mānasamaṇḍalavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Mānas.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Mānas.summary: The Mānasamaṇḍalavidhi is a short section from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. It explains that mental execution (mānasavidhi) of the maṇḍala ritual is fully efficacious and even superior to external construction, particularly when requisite ritual implements or conditions are lacking, corroborating this rule with citations from texts such as the Buddhakapālatantra.
