SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Parāb.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (chapter 32: Parābhiṣeka)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Parāb.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Parāb.summary: The Parasyābhiṣekavidhi is the initiation ritual chapter (chapter 32) of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. It provides liturgical instructions for conferring tantric initiations, detailing the vase initiation (kalaśābhiṣeka) and its sub-divisions, secret initiation (guhya), wisdom-gnosis (prajñā), and fourth (caturtha) initiations, citing texts such as the Sārdhatriśatikā, Saṃpuṭatantra, and Dvikalparāja.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Prati.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (pratimādipratiṣṭhā section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Prati.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Prati.summary: This section of Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual digest Kriyāsamuccaya describes the procedures for consecrating sacred icons (pratimādipratiṣṭhā), reliquaries, and esoteric ritual partners (vidyāpratiṣṭhā). Drawing substantially upon the Vajrāvalī, it covers the construction and decoration of the bathing pavilion (snānavedī), purification, mirror-reflection bathing, bestowal of the initiation sequence (abhiṣekas) onto the image, and concluding offerings.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Puṣka.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Puṣkariṇyādipratiṣṭhāvidhi section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Puṣka.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Puṣka.summary: This text comprises the puṣkariṇīvāpīkūpādipratiṣṭhāvidhi section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. It details the consecration rites for water bodies such as ponds (puṣkariṇī), stepwells (vāpī), and wells (kūpa), including the visualization of Varuṇa and the eight great Nāgas, the erection of a central sacrificial post (mahāyūpa) in the water, and milk-bali offerings accompanied by their respective dhāraṇīs.

This section prescribes the ritual procedures, seed syllables (bījas), and mantras for empowering and meditating upon the five-colored powders (raṅga/rajas) representing the Tathāgatas prior to laying down the lines of a maṇḍala. The e-text presents a bilingual edition with the parallel Tibetan canonical translation.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svast.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Svastyayana section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svast.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svast.summary: The Svastyayana section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya outlines propitiatory and apotropaic rituals intended to pacify malefic planetary influences (grahadoṣa), eradicate poverty, and increase longevity. It specifies the geometric construction, color arrangement, and deities for three maṇḍalas—the Grahamātṛkāmaṇḍala, the Vasudhārāmaṇḍala, and the Uṣṇīṣavijayācakra—followed by ritual procedures and dhāraṇī recitations. The e-text presents a bilingual edition matching Sanskrit passages with the corresponding canonical Tibetan translation from D 3305.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svābh.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (svābhiṣeka section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svābh.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svābh.summary: A brief excerpt from the Kriyāsamuccaya, an extensive Buddhist ritual compendium by Jagaddarpaṇa. The passage details the procedure for self-initiation (svasyābhiṣekavidhi / svābhiṣeka), allowing an adept who has impaired their samaya vows to receive initiation directly before a mentally visualized maṇḍala when a qualified master is inaccessible due to distance or perilous travel. The digital text provides the Sanskrit sentences alongside the canonical Tibetan translation from Degé Tengyur D 3305.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Svābh.edition: Diplomatic transcription from Kathmandu, Kaiser Library MS 110, fol. 250r, collated with Degé Tengyur D 3305, fol. 207b, by Péter-Dániel Szántó (PDSz, unpublished transcript, 2025).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtra.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Maṇḍalasūtraṇavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtra.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtra.summary: The Maṇḍalasūtraṇavidhi is the section of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya that sets out the technical and ritual guidelines for drawing and measuring maṇḍalas (maṇḍalasūtraṇa). It outlines the geometric layout, cord measurements, and proportions of the courtyard, gateways, architraves, decorative bands, and surrounding charnel grounds across various tantric traditions, citing authoritative texts such as the Vimalaprabhā.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtra.attribution: The Kriyāsamuccaya is attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtra.edition: Kaiser Library no. 110, where lacunose supplied from Lokesh Chandra's facsimile ed. and N: NAK 4-123 = NGMPP B 31/5; Tibetan: D 3305.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtrā.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Sūtrādhivāsana section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtrā.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Sūtrā.summary: This excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya details the Sūtrādhivāsanavidhi, the preliminary consecration and spinning of the five-colored measurement cords (jñānasūtra) used in maṇḍala construction. It describes the visualization and invocation of the wisdom threads corresponding to the five Tathāgatas, the twist/thickness requirements according to different maṇḍala dimensions (citing Ānandagarbha), and the concluding protective recitation.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Upāsa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (chapter 31: Upāsakasaṃvarādi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Upāsa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Upāsa.summary: Chapter 31 of Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. This chapter details the procedure for conferring lay Buddhist vows (upāsakasaṃvara), commencing with the preliminary purification rites and gurumaṇḍala offering, followed by the three refuges (triśaraṇa), the arousing of the bodhicitta, the undertaking of the five moral precepts (pañcaśikṣāpada), and the temporary fasting observance (poṣadhavidhi). Szántó's e-text offers a working Sanskrit text aligned with the corresponding Tibetan translation from the Tanjur.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Utthā.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (utthāpana sections)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Utthā.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Utthā.summary: This file contains an excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya detailing rituals for the construction and erection (utthāpana) of architectural members in Buddhist sanctuaries, specifically the erection of the central mast (yaṣṭi), gates/doors (dvāra), pillars (stambha), and lintels/roof beams (śirodāru). Each Sanskrit verse and mantra is accompanied by its corresponding Tibetan translation from the Derge Tanjur.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Utthā.edition: Diplomatic transcription based on Kaiser Library (Kathmandu) MS no. 110 collated with the Tibetan translation in D 3305.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vajra.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Vajravajraghaṇṭālakṣaṇa section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vajra.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vajra.summary: This excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Vajrayāna ritual compendium Kriyāsamuccaya details the precise iconometrical measurements, proportions, and symbolic anatomy of ritual implements, specifically the vajra (sceptre) and vajraghaṇṭā (bell). It also outlines the associated mantras and mudrās employed when wielding and sounding the bell during esoteric ceremonies.

This excerpt preserves the vanayātrā ('forest journey') ritual, outlining astrological preparations and ritual observances for the master and artisans venturing into the forest to select suitable timber and stone.

The Sanskrit text is accompanied line-by-line by its Tibetan translation from the Derge Tanjur (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vighn.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Vighnakīlanavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vighn.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vighn.summary: This excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's ritual compendium Kriyāsamuccaya describes the rite of pacifying obstacles by driving the ten wrathful kīlas (kīlanākoṭana/vighnakīlanavidhi) into lumps of clay placed in the cardinal and intermediate directions, closely related to parallel sections in Abhayākaragupta's Vajrāvalī. The e-text was transcribed by Péter-Dániel Szántó, collating Sanskrit manuscript evidence with the Tibetan translation (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vighn.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Vighnanivāraṇavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vighn.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vighn.summary: A brief excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya. This section outlines the Vighnanivāraṇavidhi (rite for averting obstacles) during the drawing of a powdered mandala (rajomaṇḍala), detailing visualization of the ten wrathful deities (daśakrodha) within the protective perimeter, and noting that meditators who constantly cultivate compassion and emptiness (śūnyatā) naturally dissolve all impediments. The e-text aligns the Sanskrit manuscript witness with its Tibetan translation.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vāstu.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Vāstunāgaparīkṣāvidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vāstu.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vāstu.summary: An excerpted ritual section from Jagaddarpaṇa's Vajrayāna ritual compendium Kriyāsamuccaya detailing the examination of the Vāstunāga (the ground serpent deity). It describes the layout, directional orientations, and seasonal positions of the subterranean serpent on a square ground plot, rituals and offerings to the eight nāga kings situated across its body parts, proper excavation procedures, and omens encountered during digging that determine site suitability.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Vāstu.attribution: Attributed in the colophons of the full work to Jagaddarpaṇa.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Ākāśa.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Ākāśasūtrapātana)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Ākāśa.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Ākāśa.summary: This excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya details the ritual of 'laying the cord in the air' (ākāśasūtrapātanavidhi), an indispensable preparatory phase in maṇḍala construction where ritualists snap consecrated cords in mid-air to demarcate cosmic dimensions and summon deities. The e-text contains the Sanskrit text critically edited alongside its Tibetan canonical translation.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Āpatt.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (mūlāpatti and sthūlāpatti section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Āpatt.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Āpatt.summary: This excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya lists the fourteen root transgressions (mūlāpatti) and eight gross transgressions (sthūlāpatti) of Vajrayāna tantric vows, followed by instructions for renewal through offerings, confession, and re-taking vows before a preceptor. The text contains the Sanskrit transcription from Kaiser Library MS 110 alongside the Tibetan canonical translation from the Derge Tengyur (D 3305).

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Ārāmā.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Ārāmādipratiṣṭhā section)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Ārāmā.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Ārāmā.summary: A brief excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Vajrayāna ritual manual Kriyāsamuccaya describing the consecration ritual (ārāmādipratiṣṭhāvidhi) for orchards, gardens, and groves. The procedure instructs the practitioner to visualize the principal tree as Vairocana, invoke the jñānasattva, perform anointings with vase water, make offerings to the presiding deities, and distribute directional offerings (digbali). It concludes with a general paribhāṣā prescribing the all-purpose mantra (sārvakarmikamantra) wherever a specific mantra is not stated.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Āyudh.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Āyudhalakṣaṇavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Āyudh.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Āyudh.summary: The Āyudhalakṣaṇavidhi is an iconometrical section excerpted from Jagaddarpaṇa's Kriyāsamuccaya, an authoritative compendium of Tantric Buddhist rituals. It specifies the measurements, proportions, and manufacturing guidelines for various ritual weapons and ritual hand implements, such as the ḍamaru, triśūla, khaṭvāṅga, kartrī, kapāla, cakra, kaṇaya, and tomara. The e-text consists of Szántó's transcription from Nepalese manuscripts collated interlinearly with the Tibetan Tanjur version.

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śalyo.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Śalyoddharaṇa)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śalyo.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śalyo.summary: The Śalyoddharaṇavidhi forms the fourth chapter of Jagaddarpaṇa's late Indian Vajrayāna ritual compendium, the Kriyāsamuccaya. It provides a ritual method for detecting and excavating buried impurities or bones (śalya) before temple or vihāra construction by interrogating an inspired young girl (kumārikā) positioned in a nine-square directional grid, followed by ritual pacification using stakes (kīla).
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śalyo.attribution: Attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa in manuscript colophons of the full Kriyāsamuccaya and in the Tibetan translation (D 3305).

translations: rdo rje slob dpon gyi bya ba kun las btus pa (Derge Tengyur D 3305): translated by Mañjuśrī, sa bzang ma ti paN chen blo gros rgyal mtshan; revised by badzra shrI (Tibetan)

SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śiṣya.title: Kriyāsamuccaya (Śiṣyasaṃgrahavidhi)
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śiṣya.author: Jagaddarpaṇa
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śiṣya.summary: An excerpt from Jagaddarpaṇa's Vajrayāna ritual compendium Kriyāsamuccaya detailing the Śiṣyasaṃgrahavidhi (ritual procedure for accepting disciples). It outlines auspicious astrological requirements (months, tithis, and nakṣatras) for consecration and rituals, followed by protective apotropaic visualisations (invoking Amṛtakuṇḍalin, Vajrahūṃkāra, and Māmakī) to expel and bind obstacles from the disciple.
SA_T14_Jagaddarpaṇa_Kriyāsamuccaya-Śiṣya.attribution: Attributed to Jagaddarpaṇa, supported by the Tibetan translation in the Tanjur (D 3305, where the author is named as 'Hgro-baHi me-loN').

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch01.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 1)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch01.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an extensive Buddhist Yoginītantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara (Heruka) cycle, framed as an explanatory successor (uttaratantra) to the fundamental Laghuśaṃvara. This first chapter (Avatāraṇasamayaguhyarahasyapaṭala) sets forth the nidāna, introduces the dialogue between the Bhagavān/Vajrasattva and Vajrapāṇi, and outlines the nature of supreme bliss (paramasukha), deity yoga, and secret samaya obligations.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch01.attribution: Canonical Yoginītantra of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, traditionally revealed by the Bhagavān/Vajrasattva.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch01.edition: Diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on NGMPP MS E 1517/7 (Mānavajra Vajrācārya collection E 29260), reproduced in facsimile in: Sharada Rani (ed.), Abhidhānottara-tantra: A Sanskrit Manuscript from Nepal, Śata-Piṭaka Series vol. 263, New Delhi: International Academy of Indian Culture, 1981.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch01.coverage: partial — Chapter 1 only (Avatāraṇasamayaguhyarahasyapaṭala, verses 1–20 and colophon).
translations: mngon par brjod pa'i rgyud bla ma zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 369): translated by Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, lo chen rin chen bzang po; revised by bla ban chos kyi brtson 'grus, Ānanda, rngog lo chung legs pa'i shes rab (Tibetan)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch02.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 2)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch02.summary: This e-text comprises chapter 2 (Prārthanāpaṭala) of the Abhidhānottaratantra, detailing Vajrasattva's entry into samādhi, the extensive assembly of vīras and yoginīs/ḍākinīs, and a supplication (prārthanā) requesting the revelation of the tantra.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch03.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 3)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch03.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an explanatory tantra (vyākhyātantra) belonging to the Yoginītantra class of the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka cycle. Chapter 3, titled Hṛdayatattvaparamārthapaṭala, details purification mantras and visualizations identifying internal states, body elements, and sacred sites with primordial purity, concluding with the construction of the protective vajra enclosure.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch03.attribution: Canonical scripture of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch03.coverage: partial — Chapter 3 only, concluding with colophon: 'abhidhānottarottare hṛdayatattvaparamārthapaṭala tṛtīyaḥ'.
translations: Kalff, Martin Michael. Selected Chapters from the Abhidhānottara-Tantra: The Union of Female and Male Deities. Ph.D. dissertation, Columbia University, 1979. (English)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch04.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 4)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch04.summary: Chapter 4 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an influential Anuttarayogatantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara (Heruka) cycle. Designated as the Kāyasaṃvaravidhipaṭala, this chapter sets out the ritual and meditative realization of the 'body-saṃvara' (kāyasaṃvara), including seed-syllables, the transformation of the skandhas and dhātus into Heruka and associated yoginīs, and the installation of the protective mandala.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch04.edition: Unpublished working transcription/edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó, collated from an unidentified palm-leaf manuscript and Lokesh Chandra's facsimile reproduction of Raghu Vira's manuscript.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch04.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 4 (concluding with the colophon 'iti kāyasamvaravidhipaṭalaḥ prathamaḥ', designating it as the first chapter of the kāyasaṃvara section).
translations: Martin Kalff, Selected Chapters from the Abhidhānottara-Tantra: The Union of Female and Male Deities, Ph.D. dissertation, Columbia University, 1979. (English)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch05.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 5)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch05.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an explanatory scripture of the Cakrasaṃvara (Saṃvara) cycle of Yoginītantras. This chapter teaches the contemplation of the speech-maṇḍala (vāṅmaṇḍala/vākcakra) of the lotus family: the twelve-armed Heruka in union with Padmaḍākinī, the heroes and goddesses stationed at the pīṭhas (Kāmarūpa, Oḍra, Triśakuni, Kośala, Kaliṅga, Lampāka, Kāñcī, Himālaya), their mantras, and ends with an ecstatic song of great bliss.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch05.attribution: Anonymous explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara/Saṃvara cycle; no human author.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch05.coverage: partial — One chapter (counted as chapter 5 in Szántó's file name) on the vāṅmaṇḍala / vākcakra contemplation, from 'athānyat saṃpravakṣyāmi vāṅmaṇḍalabhāvanām' to the colophon. The chapter itself appears complete in the e-text (with folio references including (*21r), (*24r), (*24v), (*25r2)). Note that the closing colophon reads 'mahāsuratapadmajālasamvara abhidhānottarapaṭalo dvitīyaḥ'.
translations: mngon par brjod pa'i rgyud bla ma zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 369): translated by Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, lo chen rin chen bzang po; revised by bla ban chos kyi brtson 'grus, Ānanda, rngog lo chung legs pa'i shes rab (Tibetan)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch06.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 6)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch06.summary: Chapter 6 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an uttaratantra of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. The chapter presents the visualization of the mind-circle (cittacakra), the surrounding ḍākinīs and vīras residing at internal and external sacred seats (pīṭhas such as Pullīramalaya, Jālandhara, and Oḍiyāna), their physical forms, mantras, and nyāsa rites.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch06.attribution: Canonical Buddhist Anuttarayogatantra (Ḍākinījāla / Cakrasaṃvara explanatory tantra [uttaratantra]), traditionally transmitted as buddhavacana.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch06.edition: Transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on a palm-leaf manuscript and Raghu Vira's manuscript reproduction by Lokesh Chandra.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch07.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 7)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch07.summary: Chapter 7 of the Abhidhānottaratantra. The chapter describes the Samayottama-maṇḍala, incorporating songs evoking Vajrasattva, followed by an iconographic description of deities and retinue (including Kākāsyā and other yoginīs), concluding with nyāsa and armor mantras.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch07.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 7 (marked as 'Abhidhānottara 7.' at line [0], though the manuscript colophon reads 'ity abhidhānottarottare samayasamvarapaṭala caturthaḥ').

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch08.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 8)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch08.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is a major Buddhist Yoginītantra of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, serving as an explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) to the fundamental Cakrasaṃvaratantra (Laghuśaṃvara). Chapter 8 (subtitled 'pīṭhaparvakramapaṭala pañcamaḥ' in the colophon) describes the visualization and evocation of twelve-armed, five-faced Heruka embraced by Vajravārāhī in an eight-petaled lotus mandala. It specifies the retinue of yoginīs (Ḍākinī, Lāmā, Khaṇḍarohā, Rūpiṇī), their seed syllables, mantras, and the placement of the armors (kavacadvaya).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch08.edition: Working edition / transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on a palm-leaf manuscript and Raghu Vīra's manuscript reproduction by Lokesh Chandra (Abhidhānottara-Tantra, Śata-Piṭaka Series 263, New Delhi, 1981).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch08.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 8 only (colophon: 'ity abhidhānottara pīṭhaparvakramapaṭala pañcamaḥ'), folios 32r3 to 34.
translations: mngon par brjod pa'i rgyud bla ma zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 369): translated by Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, lo chen rin chen bzang po; revised by bla ban chos kyi brtson 'grus, Ānanda, rngog lo chung legs pa'i shes rab (Tibetan)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch09.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 9)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch09.summary: Chapter 9 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, titled Sarvānasthitakarmabhedavidhānapaṭala. The chapter expounds the Ekavīra visualization of twelve-armed Śrī Heruka in union with Vajravārāhī, details the internal placement of yoginīs across the sacred pīṭhas and bodily cakras (dehamandala), and prescribes rites and mantras for bali offerings.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch10.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 10)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch10.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is a prominent explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara (Heruka) corpus belonging to the Anuttarayoga class of Buddhist tantras. Chapter 10, identified in its colophon as the Mañjuvajravidhipaṭala, delineates the structure and visualization of the Mañjuvajra / Vajrasattva maṇḍala, the retinue of ḍākinīs, internal seed syllables, and associated ritual and meditational practices.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch10.attribution: A Buddhist scripture belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka cycle of Anuttarayoga Tantras, traditionally considered the word of the Buddha (buddhavacana) / Mahāsamantabhadra Mahāvajradhara.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch10.edition: Unpublished working edition / manuscript transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on a palm-leaf manuscript and the manuscript facsimile published by Lokesh Chandra (Śata-Piṭaka Series 263, New Delhi, 1981).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch10.coverage: partial — Chapter 10 only (folios 42r–47r5). Internal colophon designates it as 'mañjuvajravidhipaṭalaḥ tricakroli saptamaḥ'.
translations: Kalff, Martin Michael (1979). Selected Chapters from the Abhidhānottara-Tantra: The Union of Female and Male Deities. Phil. Diss. Columbia Univ., New York. (English)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch11.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 11)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch11.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an explanatory tantra (vyākhyātantra) belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara cycle of Indian Vajrayāna Buddhism. Chapter 11 (designated in the manuscript colophon as the Pīṭhasiddhipaṭala) describes the maṇḍala centered on Heruka and Vajravārāhī, setting out the sacred geography (pīṭhas, kṣetras, upapīṭhas, etc.) along with the presiding vīras and yoginīs, mantras, and visualization practices for obtaining siddhi.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch11.edition: Unpublished transcript and working edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on a Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript and Lokesh Chandra's facsimile reproduction of Raghu Vīra's manuscript.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch11.coverage: partial — Chapter 11 only (folios 47v–53r2 in the referenced manuscript); the internal colophon designates it as 'abhidhānottarottare pīṭhasiddhipaṭalo 'ṣṭamaḥ'.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch12.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 12)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch12.summary: Chapter 12 of the Abhidhānottaratantra (colophon title: Yoginīpīṭhasiddhikramanimittanirdeśa), a prominent Ḍākinītantra / Yoginītantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara literature. The text details the maṇḍala and visualization of twelve-armed Vajravārāhī accompanied by her retinue of ḍākinīs, their correlations with the sacred geographic sites (pīṭhas), and esoteric samaya practices and yogic applications.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch18-2.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 18)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch18-2.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an important explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara / Heruka cycle of late Indian Buddhist tantra (anuttarayogatantra). This text contains chapter 18 (the Pratyaṅgirāpaṭala, numbered chapter 21 in the Tibetan translation), presenting apotropaic rituals, protective diagrams (cakra/maṇḍala), mantra syllables, and consecrations of Pratyaṅgirā / Vajraheruka to repel hostile sorcery, curses, and obstacles.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch18-2.attribution: Canonical Vajrayāna scripture belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara cycle of anuttarayogatantras, traditionally regarded as buddhabhāṣita.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch18-2.edition: Diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on the dated 1138 CE palm-leaf manuscript reproduced in Lokesh Chandra (ed.), Abhidhānottara-tantra: A Sanskrit Manuscript from Nepal, Śata-piṭaka Series 263, New Delhi: Sharada Rani, 1981.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch19-2.summary: Chapter 19 of the Abhidhānottaratantra (corresponding to chapter 22 in the Tibetan recension), titled 'Mṛtasaṃjīvanī sarvakarmakarī nāma bhāvanāpaṭala'. SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch22-i.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 22)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch22-i.summary: Chapter 22 (Kāyavākcittapīṭhānukramapaṭala) of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an influential explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka cycle. It sets forth the visualization of Heruka and Vajravārāhī with their retinue of yoginīs (ḍākinīs, Gaurī, etc.), the tripartite arrangement of the body, speech, and mind cakra mandalas, and the esoteric mapping between external sacred sites (pīṭha, upapīṭha) and the internal subtle channels of the practitioner.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch22-i.attribution: Canonical Buddhist Yoginītantra/Anuttarayogatantra text of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, traditionally regarded as the word of the Buddha (buddhavacana) in the form of Heruka.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch22-i.coverage: partial — Chapter 22 only (Kāyavākcittapīṭhānukramapaṭala, corresponding to chapter 25 of the Tibetan translation).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch23-2.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 23)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch23-2.summary: Chapter 23 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. Titled Samayotthāpaṇabuddhakāpālotpatti, this chapter describes the visualization (utpattikrama) of Buddhakāpāla and his retinue of ḍākinīs, his mantras, and the ritual purification method for rehabilitating practitioners who have broken their tantric pledges (samayabhraṣṭa).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch23-2.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 23 only, titled Samayotthāpaṇabuddhakāpālotpatti, from folio [1024'] to [1046'].

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch24-2.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 24)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch24-2.summary: Chapter 24 (Vajrasattvotpattipaṭala) of the Abhidhānottaratantra. It outlines the visualization, iconography, vowel-matrix (ālitattva), and seed syllables of Vajrasattva Mahāsukha and his retinue of goddesses (Locanā, Samayatārā, Pāṇḍaravāsinī, Ratnolkā, and sensory offering goddesses).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch24-2.coverage: partial — Contains chapter 24 (Vajrasattvotpattipaṭala), corresponding to Tibetan chapter 27.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch25-2.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an Anuttarayoga Buddhist tantra of the Cakrasaṃvara (Heruka) cycle, serving as a primary explanatory tantra (vyākhyātantra) to the Laghusaṃvara / Cakrasaṃvaratantra. This brief excerpt preserves the final lines of chapter 25 (Mañjuvajrasādhanapaṭala; corresponding to chapter 28 in the Tibetan canon), which teaches the visualization, heart mantra, and breath-control practices associated with Mañjuvajra.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch26-2.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 26)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch26-2.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an Anuttarayoga Yoginītantra scriptural text belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka corpus, functioning as an uttaratantra (explanatory continuation) to the primary Saṃvara root tantra. This short excerpt covers chapter 26 (corresponding to chapter 29 in the Tibetan canonical version), titled Kṣaḍākavajrasādhanapaṭala. It presents the sādhana, visualization, and nine-syllable mantra of Kṣaḍākavajra (Jñānaḍāka) conjoined with Vajravārāhī, accompanied by ḍākinīs located in cremation ground sites.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch26-2.edition: Transcription prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on the palm-leaf manuscript dated 1138 AD reproduced in Lokesh Chandra facsimile edition (pp. 175.6–178.3).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch27-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 27)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch27-3.summary: Chapter 27 of the Abhidhānottaratantra describes the sādhana and visualised maṇḍala of Āliḍāka (an eight-faced, sixteen-armed form of Heruka) embracing Āliḍākinī, surrounded by directional ḍākinīs associated with seed syllables, progressing through the twelve stages (bhūmi) up to Vajrasattvabhūmi.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch27-3.attribution: Canonical Buddhist tantra of the Heruka / Cakrasaṃvara class, traditionally spoken by Vajrasattva / Vajradhara.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch28-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 28)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch28-3.summary: Chapter 28 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an important Yoginītantra / Anuttarayogatantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. This chapter (entitled Praṇavaḍākasiddhinimittanirdeśa, and counted as chapter 31 in the Tibetan translation) sets forth the visualization of the deity Praṇavaḍāka (Viśvapadmeśvara) with his consort Vajradevī and the ḍākinīs Dharmottarā and Sāgarottamā, detailing their iconographic forms, seed-syllables, mantras, and internal esoteric yoga along with samaya observances.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch28-3.attribution: A major explanatory tantra (uttaratantra / ḍākinījālasaṃvara) of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, traditionally regarded as buddhavacana.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch28-3.coverage: partial — Chapter 28 only (Praṇavaḍākasiddhinimittanirdeśa; numbered ch. 31 in the Tibetan translation and Indian commentaries).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch29-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 29)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch29-3.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an important explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara / Heruka cycle belonging to the Anuttarayogatantra class. Chapter 29 describes the Samayasamvarottama Mahāmaṇḍalarāja, detailing the visualization and iconography of the central Vajraḍāka embracing Vajravārāhī, the four directional ḍākas (Buddhaḍāka, Karmaḍāka, Padmaḍāka, Ratnaḍāka), the retinue of directional and auxiliary ḍākinīs, and their mantras for ritual accomplishments (siddhi).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch29-3.attribution: Canonical Anuttarayogatantra of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, traditionally attributed to the Buddha (Buddhavacana).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch30-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 30)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch30-3.summary: Chapter 30 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, titled Dhutaguṇotpattipaṭala, describes the visualization of Mahāsukhavajraheruka and his surrounding retinue of wrathful ḍākinīs and goddesses (Mātaṅgī, Ḍombikā, Rajakī, etc.). The retinue deities are allegorized as the ascetic virtues (dhūtaguṇa/dhutaguṇa), and the text supplies their descriptions, seed-syllables, mantras, and contemplative realization.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch30-3.coverage: partial — Contains only chapter 30 (Dhutaguṇotpattipaṭala, corresponding to chapter 33 in the Tibetan translation and the commentary of Śāśvatavajra).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch31-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 31)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch31-3.summary: Chapter 31 (corresponding to chapter 34 in the Tibetan translation and Śākyarakṣita's commentary) of the Abhidhānottaratantra / Abhidhānottarottara. This chapter sets forth the ritual for causing rain (varṣāpaṇavidhi), describing the visualization of Mahāvajra/Heruka and Vārāhī, the propitiation of the eight great nāga kings and Varuṇa through milk offerings, and recitation mantras and related magical powers (siddhis) associated with tantric implements.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch31-3.coverage: partial — Contains only chapter 31 (Varṣāpaṇavidhipaṭala; numbered as chapter 34 in the Tibetan translation and Śākyarakṣita's commentary), covering folios 121v–124v of the 1138 AD palm-leaf manuscript.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch32-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 32)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch32-3.summary: Chapter 32 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, a major explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. This short chapter (Viśvarūpasādhanapaṭala) describes the visualization (sādhana) of the twelve-armed, multi-faced wrathful Heruka in his 'Viśvarūpa' aspect, standing on one foot in sexual union with Vārāhī and surrounded by animal-faced ḍākinīs.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch32-3.attribution: A Buddhist Anuttarayoga tantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka cycle, regarded as an uttaratantra (explanatory tantra) to the Laghusaṃvaratantra.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch33-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 33)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch33-3.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an extensive Buddhist Yoginītantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara corpus, elaborating ritual, maṇḍala, and yogic instructions. This short excerpt comprises chapter 33 (entitled Śrīguhyasamayottama-paṭala; corresponding to chapter 36 in the Tibetan Kangyur), which describes the sādhana, visualization, and mantras of twelve-armed or six-armed Vajravārāhī surrounded by a retinue of directional goddesses (Vajraguhyottamā, Vajrasamayottamā, etc.).
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch33-3.attribution: Canonical Yoginītantra scripture of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, traditionally regarded as buddhabhāṣita.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch34-3.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 34)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch34-3.summary: Chapter 34 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an uttaratantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka cycle of Highest Yoga Tantra (Anuttarayogatantra / Yoginītantra). This chapter (reckoned as chapter 37 in the Tibetan Kangyur and Śākyarakṣita's commentary) expounds the visualization and mantras of the six Yoginīs (Vārāhī, Yāminī, Mohinī, Sañcālinī, Saṃtrāsinī, Caṇḍikā) and six Vīras/Cakravartins (Vajrasattva, Vairocana, Padmanartteśvara, Heruka, Vajrasūrya, Paramāśva), forms of Mañjuvajra, and correlates the practice with the ten Bodhisattva stages (daśabhūmi), ten perfections (daśapāramitā), and the four Noble Truths.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch34-3.coverage: partial — Contains only chapter 34 (paṭala 34: Kavacadvayayogotpattibhāvanāpaṭala), which corresponds to chapter 37 in the Tibetan translation and the commentary of Śākyarakṣita.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch37-4.summary: Chapter 37 of the Abhidhānottaratantra (corresponding to chapter 40 in the Tibetan canonical numbering and Śāśvatavajra's commentary), an explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara tantric cycle. Entitled Ḍākinīlakṣaṇapaṭala, the chapter delineates the somatic, behavioural, and symbolic marks (lakṣaṇa) of ḍākinīs associated with various tantric families (kula), including Vajrakula, Padmanarteśvarakula, Śrīherukakula, Vajravārāhīkula, Khaṇḍarohākula, and Vināyakakula.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch37-4.attribution: A major explanatory tantra (uttaratantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara corpus, considered canonical revelation (buddhavacana).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch43-4.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 43)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch43-4.summary: Chapter 43 (Dūtasaukhyāmbuparatala; chapter 46 in Tibetan reckoning) of the Abhidhānottaratantra, an important explanatory scripture (uttaratantra) belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara (Heruka) corpus. This chapter expounds esoteric samaya observances, the roles and ritual conduct with female partners (dūtī), and purification practices (śauca) according to the Mahāyoga / Heruka tradition.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch44-4.summary: The Abhidhānottaratantra is an Anuttarayoga / Yoginī tantra of the Cakrasaṃvara corpus, functioning as an explanatory tantra (vyākhyātantra) to the Herukābhidhāna. This brief excerpt comprises chapter 40 (numbered 37 in the manuscript), the Ḍākinīvīrahṛdayādvayapaṭala, which presents the mantras and meditative visualization of the ḍākinīs and twenty-four vīras within the Ḍākinījālasaṃvara mandala.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch44-4.attribution: A Buddhist Yoginītantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, traditionally treated as canonical scripture (buddhavacana).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch45-4.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 45)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch45-4.summary: Chapter 45 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, titled 'Paṭapratimāvidhipratiṣṭhādhivāsana', prescribing ritual requirements for producing and ritually consecrating painted cloth scrolls (paṭa) and sculptural images (pratimā), specifying materials (cloth, wood, animal skins), offerings, and introductory preliminary consecration rites (adhivāsana).

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch46-4.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 46)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch46-4.summary: Chapter 46 of the Abhidhānottaratantra, titled the Maṇḍalavidhipaṭala, provides instructions for the construction, drawing, and ritual consecration of the Herukābhyudaya mandala. It outlines the qualification of the vajrācārya, the site preparation utilizing cremation-ground ash and nectars, the geometric layout of the mandala palace, and the visualization of central Heruka and Vajravārāhī surrounded by the twenty-four ḍākinīs.
