SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch64.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 64)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch64.summary: This e-text comprises the 64th chapter, titled Vajrabhairavakrodhādhipatisampuṭodghāṭapaṭala, of the Abhidhānottaratantra, focusing on the deity Vajrabhairava.

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch65.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 65)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch65.summary: Chapter 65 of the Abhidhānottaratantra (entitled Ātmabhāvapūjāpaṭala), an important explanatory tantra within the Cakrasaṃvara / Heruka cycle. The chapter teaches internal worship (adhyātmayoga / ātmabhāvavidhikrama), presenting the body as the dwelling of female deities and enlightened beings. It privileges inner meditative absorption (dhyāna, tattvavrata) over external pilgrimages to physical pīṭhas.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch65.attribution: Canonical Buddhist Anuttarayoga tantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara / Heruka cycle; traditionally considered Buddhavacana and therefore anonymous.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch65.coverage: partial — Only chapter 65, the Ātmabhāvapūjāpaṭala, complete with its colophon 'abhidhānottarottare ātmabhāvapūjāpaṭalaḥ pañcaṣaṣṭitamaḥ'.
translations: mngon par brjod pa'i rgyud bla ma zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 369): translated by Atiśa Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, lo chen rin chen bzang po; revised by bla ban chos kyi brtson 'grus, Ānanda, rngog lo chung legs pa'i shes rab (Tibetan)

SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch66.title: Abhidhānottaratantra (chapter 66)
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch66.summary: Chapter 66 is the concluding chapter (paṭala) of the Abhidhānottaratantra (also called Abhidhānottarottaratantra), an important scripture of the Cakrasaṃvara / Ḍākaḍākinījālasaṃvara class of Yoginītantras. In this chapter, the Tathāgatas praise the non-dual realization of this tantra, concluding with the scripture's final approbation formula and scribal colophons.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch66.attribution: Canonical Yoginītantra of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, framed as spoken by Vajrasattva / the Bhagavān.
SA_K12_Āgama_Abhidhānottaratantra-ch66.coverage: partial — Contains only the 66th (final) chapter (ṣaṭṣaṣṭhitamaḥ paṭalaḥ) of the tantra, followed by scribal colophons from two manuscripts.

SA_K12_Āgama_Hevajratantra_Snellgrove_19.title: Hevajratantra
SA_K12_Āgama_Hevajratantra_Snellgrove_19.summary: The Hevajratantra is a pivotal scripture of the Buddhist Yoginītantra (Anuttarayogatantra) class. Composed in two kalpas (parts), the tantra delineates the visual generation of the deity Hevajra and his maṇḍala retinue, purification of internal channels (nāḍīs) and cakras, and rituals of initiation. It elucidates non-dual awareness through the synthesis of prajñā and upāya and the experience of the four joys (ānanda) in tantric praxis.
SA_K12_Āgama_Hevajratantra_Snellgrove_19.attribution: Canonical Buddhist Yoginītantra scriptural dialogue between the Bhagavān and Vajragarbha.
SA_K12_Āgama_Hevajratantra_Snellgrove_19.edition: David L. Snellgrove, The Hevajra Tantra: A Critical Study. Part 2: Sanskrit and Tibetan Texts. London Oriental Series. London: Oxford University Press, 1959.
SA_K12_Āgama_Hevajratantra_Snellgrove_19.coverage: complete — Complete tantra in two parts (Part I: 11 chapters ending at segment 711; Part II: 12 chapters ending at segment 1681 with 'mahātantrarājamāyākalpo dvitīyaḥ').
translations: David L. Snellgrove, The Hevajra Tantra: A Critical Study. Part 1: Introduction and Translation. London Oriental Series. London: Oxford University Press, 1959. (English)

SA_K12_Āgama_Vajraḍākottaratantra_Sander.title: Vajraḍākottaratantra (notes and partial transcription)
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajraḍākottaratantra_Sander.summary: A working document containing partial transcription and philological notes by AGJSS (dated 17–18 February 2008) on the Vajraḍākottara from the Derge Kanjur, collated with Sanskrit parallels from the Vajraḍāka / Vajraḍākatantra.
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajraḍākottaratantra_Sander.attribution: Canonical tantra of the Vajraḍāka cycle. The e-text is a partial transcription and notes prepared by Alexis G. J. S. Sanderson (AGJSS).
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajraḍākottaratantra_Sander.edition: Unpublished working transcription and notes by AGJSS (17–18 February 2008), based on Sde dge bKa' 'gyur, rgyud 'bum, kha, ff. 125v–136v (pp. 250–272; W22084; 372 toh; 372 sde dge) with Sanskrit parallels.
SA_K12_Āgama_Vajraḍākottaratantra_Sander.coverage: partial — Partial transcription and notes by AGJSS (17–18 February 2008) of the Tibetan text from the Derge Kanjur (vol. 78, ff. 125v–136v) with Sanskrit parallels from the Vajraḍākatantra.
translations: dpal mkha' 'gro rgya mtsho rnal 'byor ma'i rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 372): translated by Jayasena III, sum pa lo tsA ba dar ma yon tan; at dpal bal yul grub pa'i gnas mchog chen po yu tung lhun gyis grub pa'i gtsug lag khang chen po (Tibetan)

SA_K12_Āgama_Yoginīsaṃcāratantra.title: Yoginīsaṃcāratantra
SA_K12_Āgama_Yoginīsaṃcāratantra.summary: The Yoginīsaṃcāratantra is an important Buddhist explanatory tantra (vyākhyātantra) of the Cakrasaṃvara/Heruka cycle. Across seventeen chapters, it expounds esoteric doctrines and rituals of the yoginī mandala, correlating the thirty-seven aids to awakening (bodhipākṣikadharmāḥ) with specific goddesses, mapping sacred sites (pīṭha) onto the yogic body, and detailing tantric observances (caryā), hand gestures, and dramatic performance (nāṭya).
SA_K12_Āgama_Yoginīsaṃcāratantra.attribution: Canonical Buddhist Anuttarayoga tantra belonging to the Cakrasaṃvara (Heruka) cycle.
SA_K12_Āgama_Yoginīsaṃcāratantra.coverage: complete — Complete in 17 paṭalas (1.1 to 17.31), ending with the colophon of the 17th paṭala: 'iti yoginīsaṃcāre tattvaviśuddhipīṭhasthānanāṭyacaryānirdeśaḥ saptadaśamaḥ'.
translations: rnal 'byor ma'i kun tu spyod pa (Derge Kangyur D 375): translated by 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T01_Vanaratna_Acalakramadvayastotra_D.title: Acalakramadvayastotra
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Acalakramadvayastotra_D.author: Vanaratna
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Acalakramadvayastotra_D.summary: A short 12-verse praise (stotra) of Acala (Caṇḍaroṣaṇa / Ekallavīra) attributed to Vanaratna. The hymn interprets the iconography and attributes of the deity through the framework of the two stages (kramadvaya: utpattikrama and utpannakrama / niṣpannakrama), including a tantric etymological breakdown of the name A-ca-la symbolizing śūnyatā, mahāsukha, and their non-dual union.
SA_T01_Vanaratna_Acalakramadvayastotra_D.coverage: complete — Complete 12-verse stotra followed by closing title and author colophons.

SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Varṣāpaṇavidhi.title: Varṣāpaṇavidhi
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Varṣāpaṇavidhi.author: Abhayākaragupta
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Varṣāpaṇavidhi.summary: A short Vajrayāna ritual manual for weather control (varṣāpaṇa) attributed to Abhayākaragupta. The practitioner visualizes Vajragaruḍa standing upon Varuṇa and a serpent tail, surrounded by eight principal nāga lords, and offers milk in a homa sacrifice to induce rainfall within seven days, followed by a smokeless/fireless procedure to stop excessive rain.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Varṣāpaṇavidhi.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to Abhayākaragupta. Tokyo MS 1016 provides a post-colophon lineage: Vanaratna, Sarvamitra, Ravicandra, and the scribe Rūparāja.
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Varṣāpaṇavidhi.edition: Unpublished synoptic manuscript transcription prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó from two composite codices preserved in the Tokyo University Library: MS 936 (new no. 307 V, palm leaf, dated NS 589, fol. 25r1) and MS 1016 (old no. 293, paper, dated NS 901, fols. 209v5–211v3).
SA_T02_Abhayākaragupta_Varṣāpaṇavidhi.coverage: complete — Complete synoptic diplomatic transcription of the short text from two Tokyo University Library manuscripts, accompanied by English preliminary summary and manuscript sigla notes by Péter-Dániel Szántó.

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Amanasikārādhāra.title: Amanasikārādhāra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Amanasikārādhāra.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Amanasikārādhāra.summary: The Amanasikārādhāra ('Justification of Non-Mental Engagement') is a short doctrinal treatise by Advayavajra (Maitrīpa) vindicating the term and practice of amanasikāra ('absence of conceptual mental engagement') against critics. Defending the formation grammatically against the charge of being ungrammatical (apaśabda) through Pāṇini 6.3.14 (aluksamāsa) and semantic analysis of negation, Advayavajra demonstrates the valid usage of the term. Drawing citations from canonical Mahāyāna scriptures (Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkāra) and tantras (Hevajra), he establishes that amanasikāra culminates in the realization of inseparable emptiness and compassion (śūnyatākaruṇābhinnayuganaddhādvayavāhisaṃvedanam).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Amanasikārādhāra.attribution: Attributed to Advayavajra (Maitrīpa / Maitrīgupta) as text no. 23 of the collection preserved in the Advayavajrasaṃgraha.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Amanasikārādhāra.edition: Advayavajrasaṃgraha, ed. Mikkyō-seiten-kenkyūkai (Study Group on Sacred Tantric Texts), in: Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō; collated with Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Amanasikārādhāra.coverage: complete — Ends with the colophon 'amanasikārādhāraḥ samāptaḥ'.
translations: Mathes, Klaus-Dieter. 'Maitrīpa's Amanasikārādhāra ("A Justification of Becoming Mentally Disengaged").' Journal of the Nepal Research Centre 13. (English)

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Māyānirukti.title: Māyānirukti
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Māyānirukti.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Māyānirukti.summary: The Māyānirukti ('Discourse on Illusion') is a short 12-verse philosophical and practical treatise by Advayavajra (Maitrīpa). It demonstrates that phenomena lack intrinsic nature like magical illusions, showing that realizing unoriginated emptiness avoids both eternalism and annihilationism. The work concludes by emphasizing that theoretical understanding of illusion must be matched with dedicated yogic conduct (caryā).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Māyānirukti.attribution: Advayavajra is also known as Maitrīpa.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Māyānirukti.edition: Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927, p. 44; collated with Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai (ed.), Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō 3.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Māyānirukti.coverage: complete — Complete text of 12 verses with introductory salutation and closing colophon.

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Nirvedhapañcaka.title: Nirvedhapañcaka
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Nirvedhapañcaka.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Nirvedhapañcaka.summary: The Nirvedhapañcaka is a short work of five verses with prose explanations attributed to Advayavajra (Maitrīpāda), discussing sahajanirvedha, śūnyatā, and anābhogakṛpā.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Nirvedhapañcaka.attribution: Advayavajra is associated with Maitrīpāda; Shastri notes that the Tibetan Catalogue attributes the work to Maitrīpāda.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Nirvedhapañcaka.edition: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai, 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha (4)', in Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō 13 (1991), pp. (82/255)ff., collating Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, GOS 40, Baroda, 1927.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Nirvedhapañcaka.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising 5 verses along with prose commentary/explanations and concluding colophon.

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Premapañcaka.title: Premapañcaka
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Premapañcaka.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Premapañcaka.summary: The Premapañcaka ('Five Verses on Love') is a short five-verse tantric-philosophical poem attributed to Advayavajra (Maitrīpa). Utilizing the allegorical motif of a bride and groom—appearance (pratibhāsa) as the suitor and emptiness (śūnyatā) as the bride—it describes how they are brought into non-dual, innate union (sahajaṃ prema / yuganaddha) through the guidance and skill of the true guru.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Premapañcaka.attribution: Traditionally attributed to Advayavajra (Maitrīpa, 11th century) and included as text 21 in the Advayavajrasaṃgraha collection / Amanasikāra cycle.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Premapañcaka.edition: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai (ed.), 'Advayavajra's Works (3)', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō (Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University) 11 (1989), pp. (80)–(82) [285–283], with page reference to Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927, p. 58.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Premapañcaka.coverage: complete — Complete text comprising all 5 verses.
translations: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai, 'Advayavajra's Works (3)', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō 11 (1989), pp. (80)–(82) [285–283]. (Japanese)

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sahajaṣaṭka.title: Sahajaṣaṭka
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sahajaṣaṭka.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sahajaṣaṭka.summary: A concise Buddhist Tantric work of six stanzas attributed to Advayavajra, belonging to the Advayavajrasaṃgraha. The text presents true reality (tattva) as free from eternalism and nihilism, defining the connate/innate state (sahaja) as unconditioned, non-attached (niḥsaṅga), and inherently blissful.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sahajaṣaṭka.attribution: Attributed in the colophon to the paṇḍita and avadhūta Advayavajrapāda: 'kṛtir iyaṃ paṇḍitāvadhūtaśrīmadadvayavajrapādānām iti'.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sahajaṣaṭka.edition: Transcription/collation by Péter-Dániel Szántó based on Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927, and the critical edition by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai (密教聖典研究会), published in Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō (Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sahajaṣaṭka.coverage: complete — Contains all 6 verses and the colophon.
translations: Klaus-Dieter Mathes, A Fine Blend of Mahāmudrā and Madhyamaka: Maitrīpa's Collection of Texts on Non-conceptual Realization (Amanasikāra). (English)

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sekatātparyasaṃgraha.title: Sekatātparyasaṃgraha
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sekatātparyasaṃgraha.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sekatātparyasaṃgraha.summary: The Sekatātparyasaṃgraha is a short Vajrayāna treatise by Advayavajra analyzing the four tantric empowerments (abhiṣeka). It examines the six varieties of the flask initiation (kalaśābhiṣeka) and their correspondences with the five tathāgatas and their pure gnoses (jñāna), followed by concise expositions of the secret (guhya), wisdom-gnosis (prajñājñāna), and fourth (caturtha) empowerments.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sekatātparyasaṃgraha.attribution: The colophon explicitly attributes the work to paṇḍitāvadhūta-śrī-Advayavajrapāda (Advayavajra / Maitrīpa).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sekatātparyasaṃgraha.edition: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai (密教聖典研究會), 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha: New Critical Edition with Japanese Translation (2)', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō (Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University), 1989, pp. (108/237)–(120/225); recording page breaks from Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927 (GOS 40).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Sekatātparyasaṃgraha.coverage: complete — Complete short treatise consisting of opening verse, prose explanations, and closing benedictory verse with concluding colophon.
translations: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai, 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha: New Critical Edition with Japanese Translation (2)', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō, 1989, pp. (108/237)–(120/225). (Japanese)

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Svapnanirukti.title: Svapnanirukti
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Svapnanirukti.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Svapnanirukti.summary: The Svapnanirukti ('Exposition of Dream') is a concise nine-verse philosophical work by Advayavajra (Maitrīpa) from his Amanasikāra collection. It analyzes the canonical simile comparing all phenomena to a dream across six philosophical perspectives, refuting both eternalism and nihilism to elucidate non-abiding awareness (apratiṣṭhāna).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Svapnanirukti.attribution: Advayavajra is also known as Maitrīpa. The work belongs to his Amanasikāra corpus.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Svapnanirukti.edition: Advayavajrasaṃgraha, ed. Haraprasad Shastri, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927, p. 45; and Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai, 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha (4)', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Svapnanirukti.coverage: complete — Complete work comprising 9 verses with mangala and final colophon.

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Tattvadaśaka.title: Tattvadaśaka
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Tattvadaśaka.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Tattvadaśaka.summary: The Tattvadaśaka is a concise doctrinal poem in ten anuṣṭubh verses by Advayavajra (Maitrīpa). It defines ultimate reality (tathatā, tattva) beyond the extremes of existence and non-existence, as well as beyond Sākāra- and Nirākāra-Madhyamaka, describing it as non-dual luminosity (prabhāsvara) realized via guru instruction rather than conceptual analysis. The treatise serves as a key Indian locus for the Mahāmudrā and amanasikāra traditions, and forms the basis of Sahajavajra's famous commentary, the Tattvadaśakaṭīkā.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Tattvadaśaka.attribution: Advayavajra is identical with the master Maitrīpa (Avadhūti). In Tibetan tradition, the text is associated with the amanasikāra tradition.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Tattvadaśaka.edition: Advayavajrasaṃgraha, ed. MM Hara Prasad Shastri, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927, p. 59; collated with the edition by Mikkyō-seiten-kenkyūkai 4 in Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Tattvadaśaka.coverage: complete — Complete work in 10 anuṣṭubh stanzas (verses 1–10).

SA_T02_Advayavajra_Yuganaddhaprakāśa.title: Yuganaddhaprakāśa
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Yuganaddhaprakāśa.author: Advayavajra
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Yuganaddhaprakāśa.summary: The Yuganaddhaprakāśa is a 10-verse philosophical text by Advayavajra (Maitrīpa) on the principle of indivisible union (yuganaddha). Synthesizing Madhyamaka reasoning with Tantric Mahāmudrā view, it explains that appearances and emptiness, as well as compassion and voidness, are intrinsically non-dual rather than artificially combined. Because all entities arise dependently and lack intrinsic existence, the yogin transcends the extremes of existence and non-existence.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Yuganaddhaprakāśa.attribution: Advayavajra is also known as Maitrīpa. The work is no. 15 in the collected corpus conventionally known as the Advayavajrasaṃgraha.
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Yuganaddhaprakāśa.edition: Haraprasad Shastri (ed.), Advayavajrasaṃgraha, Gaekwad's Oriental Series 40, Baroda: Oriental Institute, 1927; collated with Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai [Study Group on Tantric Texts], 'Advayavajrasaṃgraha (3)', Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō [Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taisho University] 13 (307–309).
SA_T02_Advayavajra_Yuganaddhaprakāśa.coverage: complete — Complete in 10 verses, concluding with '|| yuganaddhaprakāśaḥ samāptaḥ ||'.

SA_T02_Amitavajra_Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā.title: Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā
SA_T02_Amitavajra_Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā.author: Amitavajra
SA_T02_Amitavajra_Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā.summary: The Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā is a Vajrayāna ritual manual composed by Amitavajra, belonging to the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle and focusing on the worship of the deity Yogāmbara. It details the practitioner's preparatory rites, hand gestures (mudrā), body purification, seed syllables (bīja), visualization sequences, and maṇḍala offering according to Catuṣpīṭha conventions. The primary palm-leaf manuscript transcribed here preserves a historical colophon dating the copy to regnal year 13 of the Pāla monarch Vigrahapāladeva.
SA_T02_Amitavajra_Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā.attribution: Amitavajra (Tib. Dpag med rdo rje) was associated with the Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā. The transcriber's transcription notes a possible identification with Vijayendrasena.
SA_T02_Amitavajra_Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, unpublished diplomatic transcript and collation of the Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā based on palm-leaf manuscript NAK 3-366/vi (bauddhadarśana 74, NGMPP B 23/10, dated regnal year 13 of Vigrahapāladeva), collated with Matsunami 312 and NAK 3-366 (NGMPP A 935/3).
SA_T02_Amitavajra_Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā.coverage: complete — The core text of the Yogāmbarasādhanopāyikā is complete from the opening maṅgala verse to the concluding colophon. The manuscript contains the final verses and colophon of the preceding text (Kriyāsaṃgrahakārikā) and scribal additions including a stotra fragment to Cakrasaṃvara.
translations: Tib. Toh. 1619, translated by Dīpaṅkararakṣita and Mar pa Chos kyi dbang phyug. (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Cintā_Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasidd.title: Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasiddhi
SA_T02_Cintā_Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasidd.author: Cintā
SA_T02_Cintā_Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasidd.summary: The Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasiddhi ('Attainment of Reality through Manifest Phenomena') is an esoteric Vajrayāna treatise attributed to Yoginī Cintā, counted among the eight texts of the classical Aṣṭasiddhi collection. Composed in mixed prose and verse, it teaches Sahajayāna non-dual philosophy, demonstrating how great bliss (mahāsukha) and innate gnosis are discovered in and through manifest sensory experiences and worldly existence rather than their renunciation. The work outlines tantric cosmogony, subtle embryology, and the transformation of cyclic existence into Vajrasattva.
SA_T02_Cintā_Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasidd.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the female tantric master Yoginī Cintā, associated with the tradition of the mahāsiddha Dārikapāda and the Oḍḍiyāna lineage.
SA_T02_Cintā_Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasidd.edition: Guhyādy-aṣṭasiddhisaṃgraha, ed. Samdhong Rinpoche and Vrajvallabh Dwivedi, Sarnath: Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (CIHTS), 1987.
SA_T02_Cintā_Vyaktabhāvānugatatattvasidd.coverage: complete — Complete text of the work from the opening maṅgala (p. 169) to the final colophon, comprising mixed prose and 20 numbered verses.
translations: Toh 2223 / D 2223, translated by Zhi ba bzang po (Śāntibhadra) and 'Gos Lhas btsas, revised by Nag tsho. (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Devakula-Mahāmati_Tattvaviṣadā.title: Tattvaviṣadā
SA_T02_Devakula-Mahāmati_Tattvaviṣadā.author: Mahāmatideva
SA_T02_Devakula-Mahāmati_Tattvaviṣadā.summary: The Tattvaviṣadā is a Sanskrit commentary (pañjikā) by Mahāmatideva on the Ḍākinīvajrapañjaratantra. The author refers to earlier authorities including Ānandagarbha and the Catuṣpīṭhatantra.
SA_T02_Devakula-Mahāmati_Tattvaviṣadā.attribution: The surviving Sanskrit colophon explicitly names the author as Mahāmatideva. In Tibetan tradition, the name was translated as Lha'i rigs Blo gros chen po (whence Devakula-Mahāmati).
SA_T02_Devakula-Mahāmati_Tattvaviṣadā.edition: Unpublished working transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó, based on three manuscript fragments in Kathmandu: Kaiser Library MS 134 (NGMPP C 14/4, f. 1), National Archives Kathmandu (NAK) MS 5-20 (NGMPP A 47/17, ff. 2–15), and NAK MS 5-23 (NGMPP A 47/18, final folio).
SA_T02_Devakula-Mahāmati_Tattvaviṣadā.coverage: complete — Reconstructed from three matching parts of a dispersed Nepalese manuscript.
translations: Tibetan canonical translation: rGyud kyi rgyal po mkha' 'gro ma rdo rje dra ba'i dka' 'grel de kho na nyid rgyas pa, translated by Gayādhara and 'Gos Lhas btsas. (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Saptākṣarasādhana.title: Saptākṣarasādhana
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Saptākṣarasādhana.author: Durjayacandra
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Saptākṣarasādhana.summary: The Saptākṣarasādhana is a concise meditation manual dedicated to Saptākṣara-Heruka (a seven-syllabled form of Cakrasaṃvara/Vajraḍāka) and his retinue of six yoginīs (Herukī, Vajrabhairavī, Ghoracaṇḍī, Vajrabhāskarī, Vajraraudrī, and Vajraḍākinī) arranged upon a six-spoked wheel. Composed by Durjayacandra, the ritual outlines the generation-stage visualization, protective perimeter, iconography, mantra recitation, and the correlation of the seven mandala deities with the seven factors of awakening (sambodhyaṅga) as well as the six bone ornaments with the six perfections (pāramitā).
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Saptākṣarasādhana.attribution: Attributed in the text colophon to Durjayacandra ('durjayacandroddhṛtaṃ saptākṣarasādhanaṃ samāptam'). The Tibetan translation (D 1461) attributes the work to *Durjayālabhyacandra.
SA_T02_Durjayacandra_Saptākṣarasādhana.coverage: complete — Complete text of the sādhana in 19 metrical verses interspersed with mantra formulas, nyāsa instructions, and symbolic correlations.
translations: yi ge bdun pa'i sgrub thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1461) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Dārikapāda_Yogānusāriṇī-vajrayogi.title: Yogānusāriṇīvajrayoginīṭīkā (incomplete, with Tibetan parallel)
SA_T02_Dārikapāda_Yogānusāriṇī-vajrayogi.author: Dārikapāda
SA_T02_Dārikapāda_Yogānusāriṇī-vajrayogi.summary: A Sanskrit commentary-cum-manual on the sādhana of Vajrayoginī/Vajravārāhī. It opens with an introduction that mentions Indrabhūti's Ḍākinīrahasya and the author's master's Svādhiṣṭhāna, and then treats sādhana, mantroddhāra, japa, bali, tilaka, unguent (udvartana), collyrium (añjana) and finally caryā. The Sanskrit survives in incomplete Nepalese manuscripts and is given here in parallel with the Tibetan translation of Tōh. 1565.
SA_T02_Dārikapāda_Yogānusāriṇī-vajrayogi.attribution: Tōh. 1565 is attributed in its Tibetan colophon to Dārikapa (grub thob chen po dā ri ka pa), translated by Dānaśīla. In the Sanskrit manuscripts the title and author are lost. The e-text's header maps 'Dārikapāda –> *Kuṭali, disciple of Saraha': the author says he wrote a Svādhiṣṭhānavyākhyā on his master's Svādhiṣṭhāna, and that commentary probably survives in China under the name *Kuṭali. A line quoted from the master matches Tōh. 2275, ascribed to Saraha.
SA_T02_Dārikapāda_Yogānusāriṇī-vajrayogi.edition: Unpublished transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó of the Nepalese palm-leaf manuscripts NGMPP B 31/8 (incomplete, with a one-folio fragment in A 49/18) and B 30/32 (incomplete), aligned with the Tibetan translation, Derge Tanjur Tōh. 1565 (rgyud, vol. za, 225r6–237r1).
SA_T02_Dārikapāda_Yogānusāriṇī-vajrayogi.coverage: partial — Sanskrit: introduction, sādhana, mantroddhāra, japa, bali, tilaka, udvartana, añjana, and the beginning of the caryā section, where the testimony ends ('the testimony breaks off, probably not much is lacking'). Ms. B also contains a one-folio fragment on Mahāmudrā that may belong to this work. The Tibetan translation (Derge Tanjur, rgyud, vol. za, fols. 225r6–237r1) is aligned, with a note '[the rest of Tib. does not match!]', followed by Tibetan text to fol. 237b including an appended section by Klu'i sbyin pa translated by Dānaśīla.
translations: rnal 'byor gyi rjes su 'brang ba zhes bya ba/_rdo rje rnal 'byor ma'i 'grel pa (Derge Tengyur D 1565): translated by Dānaśīla; at bod yul kyi dbus drang srong srin po ri (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Jagadānandajīvabhadra_Yogāmbarasā.title: Yogāmbarasādhanavidhi
SA_T02_Jagadānandajīvabhadra_Yogāmbarasā.author: Jagadānandajīvabhadra
SA_T02_Jagadānandajīvabhadra_Yogāmbarasā.summary: The Yogāmbarasādhanavidhi is an extensive ritual and meditative manual (sādhana) dedicated to Yogāmbara, the principal male deity of the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle. Composed by Jagadānandajīvabhadra based on the Ātmapīṭha section of the Catuṣpīṭha literature, it became the foundation for surviving Newar Buddhist liturgical traditions of Yogāmbara and corresponds closely to the ritual portion of the Nepalese Yogāmbaramahātantra.
SA_T02_Jagadānandajīvabhadra_Yogāmbarasā.attribution: Colophons identify the author as the Nepalese paṇḍita Jagadānandajīvabhadra. His disciple/son Mahābodhi transmitted the Sanskrit exemplar to Tibet, where it was translated at Sakya by dPal ldan smra ba'i seng ge with paṇḍita Mahābodhi.
SA_T02_Jagadānandajīvabhadra_Yogāmbarasā.edition: Unpublished multi-witness working edition / synoptic collation by Péter-Dániel Szántó, collating NAK 3-280 (= NGMPP A 134/6), Kaiser 125 (= NGMPP C 14/3), MBB-I-142, MBB-III-5, Āśā Saphū Kājī 994, Asha Saphu Kuti 3387 / 3933, Matsunami 310 / 311, and the Tibetan canonical translation Toh. 1611.
SA_T02_Jagadānandajīvabhadra_Yogāmbarasā.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual in verse and prose, comprising the Ātmapīṭha worship of Yogāmbara extracted from the Catuṣpīṭha cycle, down through the final colophons.
translations: dpal rdo rje gdan bzhi'i sgrub thabs zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1611): translated by Mahābodhi, dpal ldan smra ba'i seng ge, sa bzang ma ti paN chen blo gros rgyal mtshan; at dpal sa skya'i gtsug lag khang chen po (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Jitāri_Catustattva.title: Catuṣpīṭhacatustattva
SA_T02_Jitāri_Catustattva.author: Jitāri
SA_T02_Jitāri_Catustattva.summary: The Catuṣpīṭhacatustattva is a four-chapter tantric manual by the Buddhist scholar-monk Jitāri. Belonging to the exegesis of the Catuṣpīṭhatantra, it expounds the four realities (catustattva) mapped onto four cakra systems, detailing visualization practices centered on Jñānaḍākinī and Yogāmbara as well as the transition from external ritual to internal yogic realization.
SA_T02_Jitāri_Catustattva.attribution: Verse 4.20 names ācārya Jitāri as the author (likhitaṃ tu svasaṃvedyam ācāryeṇa Jitāriṇā).
SA_T02_Jitāri_Catustattva.coverage: complete — Complete text in four paricchedas (concluding at verse 4.20 and chapter 4 colophon), followed by brief post-colophon mantras and notes.
translations: gdan bzhi'i de kho na nyid bzhi pa (Derge Tengyur D 1620): translated by Gayādhara, 'gos lo tsA ba khug pa lhas btsas (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kalyāṇavarman_Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā.title: Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā
SA_T02_Kalyāṇavarman_Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā.author: Kalyāṇavarman
SA_T02_Kalyāṇavarman_Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā.summary: The Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā (also titled Catuṣpīṭhāloka or Gūḍhagranthivibodhanī) by Kalyāṇavarman is a Sanskrit commentary on the Catuṣpīṭhatantra, commenting on pīṭhas up to Yogapīṭha. The Sanskrit witness is a dated palm-leaf codex from Nepal (NAK 3-360 / NGMPP B 30/37 dated 1012 CE).
SA_T02_Kalyāṇavarman_Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā.attribution: The Tibetan translation in the Tengyur (D 1608) preserves a continuation on the fourth pīṭha composed by translator Smṛtijñānakīrti.
SA_T02_Kalyāṇavarman_Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā.edition: Kalyāṇavarman's Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā Formatted Diplomatic Edition, based on codex unicus NAK 3-360 = NGMPP B 30/37 (PDSz e-text corpus).
SA_T02_Kalyāṇavarman_Catuṣpīṭhapañjikā.coverage: complete — Complete for Kalyāṇavarman's commentary, which covers pīṭhas 1–3 (ending with Yogapīṭha).
translations: phags pa gdan bzhi pa'i rnam par bshad pa (Derge Tengyur D 1608): translated by Kalyāṇavarman, Smṛtijñānakīrti (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Kṣitigarbha_Daśatattvasaṃgraha.title: Daśatattvasaṃgraha (excerpts: rakṣācakra, cakra and seka sections)
SA_T02_Kṣitigarbha_Daśatattvasaṃgraha.author: Kṣitigarbha
SA_T02_Kṣitigarbha_Daśatattvasaṃgraha.summary: The Daśatattvasaṃgraha of the paṇḍita Kṣitigarbha (in the retinue of Vanaratna) is a manual in the Jñānapāda tradition of the Guhyasamāja. It sets out ten ritual 'principles' (tattva): protective circle, maṇḍala (cakra), recitation, the two higher consecrations, haṭha, bali, the two pratyaṅgirā rites and the opening of the box (puṭodghāṭa). The e-text gives the opening verses, the rakṣācakra and much of the maṇḍala visualisation, and the guhya and prajñājñāna consecrations with the vidyāvrata. The remainder is untranscribed apart from the final colophon.
SA_T02_Kṣitigarbha_Daśatattvasaṃgraha.attribution: The colophon reads 'kṛtir iyaṃ daśatattvasaṃgrahaḥ paṇḍitakṣitiga[rbha]sya' ([260]). The Dharmamitra header ([1]) adds that Kṣitigarbha was in the retinue of Vanaratna and died at mChims phu. The work follows the Jñānapāda tradition of the Guhyasamāja ('jñānapādakrameṇa', [5]).
SA_T02_Kṣitigarbha_Daśatattvasaṃgraha.edition: Unpublished partial transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó (PDSz corpus, release PDSz_202609) from the manuscript IASWR MBB-II-208 (missing fol. 2).
SA_T02_Kṣitigarbha_Daśatattvasaṃgraha.coverage: excerpt — The manuscript runs to fol. 41r, and folio 2 is missing in the manuscript itself (header [2]; lacuna at [13]). The transcription covers fols. 1v–ca. 9 (introductory verses, rakṣācakra, maṇḍala/cakra visualisation up to [177]). It then jumps ('[on 22r]', [178]) to the seka section (guhyābhiṣeka, prajñājñānābhiṣeka, vidyāvrata, [179]–[255]) and stops at '[on 28r]' ([256]). Only the final colophon of fol. 41r follows ([257]–[260]). Of the ten tattvas listed in v. 2, the rest of the cakra section, japa, haṭha, bali, the two pratyaṅgirās and the saṃpuṭodghāṭa are not transcribed, except for the closing line 'iti saṃpuṭodghāṭavidhiḥ'.
translations: Klein-Schwind, S.G., diss., Hamburg University, 2012. (English)

SA_T02_Samantabhadra_Sāramañjarī.title: Sāramañjarī
SA_T02_Samantabhadra_Sāramañjarī.author: Samantabhadra
SA_T02_Samantabhadra_Sāramañjarī.summary: The Sāramañjarī is an extensive Sanskrit commentary by the master Samantabhadra on Buddhajñānapāda's Caturaṅgasādhana (also known as the Samantabhadrasādhana), a fundamental manual of the Guhyasamāja creation stage (utpattikrama). It provides detailed exegesis of the four limbs of yoga (caturaṅga) according to the Jñānapādamata tradition, elucidating visualization, deity generation, mantra recitation, and the philosophical defense of tantric deity yoga.
SA_T02_Samantabhadra_Sāramañjarī.attribution: Samantabhadra was a master in the Jñānapāda lineage of the Guhyasamāja tantra.
SA_T02_Samantabhadra_Sāramañjarī.edition: Unpublished working edition / diplomatic transcript of the 'Pāla recension' prepared by Péter-Dániel Szántó from a 45-folio manuscript.
SA_T02_Samantabhadra_Sāramañjarī.coverage: complete — Complete commentary on the 164 verses of Buddhajñānapāda's Caturaṅgasādhana (fol. 1a to fol. 45b3), concluding with the author's closing verse, colophon, and scribal Pratītyasamutpāda verse.
translations: yan lag bzhi pa'i sgrub thabs kyi rgya cher bshad pa snying po snye ma zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1869): translated by Nyāyaśrī, rngog blo ldan shes rab; at bal yul mthil (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Tathāgatarakṣita_Saṃcāratantranib.title: Saṃcāratantranibandha
SA_T02_Tathāgatarakṣita_Saṃcāratantranib.author: Tathāgatarakṣita
SA_T02_Tathāgatarakṣita_Saṃcāratantranib.summary: The Saṃcāratantranibandha is a 17-chapter Sanskrit commentary by Tathāgatarakṣita on the Yoginīsaṃcāratantra. The work elucidates the thirty-seven-deity maṇḍala correlated with the thirty-seven bodhipākṣikadharmas, the movement (saṃcāra) of yoginīs across subtle channels and sacred sites (pīṭhas), armor mantras, and tantric observances.
SA_T02_Tathāgatarakṣita_Saṃcāratantranib.attribution: Attributed to Tathāgatarakṣita in source headers and the Tibetan Tanjur record for D 1422.
SA_T02_Tathāgatarakṣita_Saṃcāratantranib.edition: Ms NAK 5-22 = NGMPP A 47/19 palm leaf; Input: Péter-Dániel Szántó 2.vii.2024 Budapest
SA_T02_Tathāgatarakṣita_Saṃcāratantranib.coverage: complete — Complete commentary across 17 chapters (nirdeśa) on the Yoginīsaṃcāratantra, concluding with the 17th nirdeśa (iti saptadaśo nirdeśaḥ), closing praśasti verse, and final colophon.
translations: rnal 'byor ma kun du spyod pa'i bshad sbyar (Derge Tengyur D 1422): translated by Tathāgatarakṣita, ba ri lo tsA ba rin chen grags (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Virūpa_Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana.title: Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana (fragment)
SA_T02_Virūpa_Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana.author: Virūpa
SA_T02_Virūpa_Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana.summary: The Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana ('Sādhana of the Severed-Headed Goddess') is an esoteric Buddhist tantric visualization manual dedicated to the severed-headed form of Vajrayoginī / Vajravārāhī. It details the self-generation of the goddess holding a cleaver (kartrikā) and severed head / skullcup. Previously considered lost in Sanskrit and known through its Tengyur translation (D 1555), a two-folio Sanskrit fragment was identified in Kaiser Library MS 139.
SA_T02_Virūpa_Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana.attribution: Attributed in the Tibetan colophon to the master Bar bi pa (Virūpa). The Tibetan translation was produced by the Nepalese paṇḍita Bharendraruci and the Tibetan translator rMa Chos 'bar (Rma-ban chos-'bar).
SA_T02_Virūpa_Chinnamuṇḍāsādhana.coverage: fragment — The Sanskrit original survives only as a two-folio fragment in Kathmandu, Kaiser Library MS 139 (beginning at folio 10r); missing portions at the beginning and end are supplied in Tibetan transcription from D 1555.
translations: dbu bcad ma'i sgrub thabs zhes bya ba (Derge Tengyur D 1555): translated by Varendraruci, rma lo tsA ba rma ban chos 'bar (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Virūpa_Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana.title: Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana
SA_T02_Virūpa_Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana.author: Virūpa
SA_T02_Virūpa_Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana.summary: A short Vajrayāna sādhana dedicated to Trikāyavajrayoginī (the decapitated Vajrayoginī flanked by Vajravarṇanī and Vajravairocanī), attributed to the Mahāsiddha Virūpa. The text details the visualization (bhāvanā) of the self-decapitated deity drinking her own blood alongside her two attendants, worship (pūjā) with offerings directed to the sacred sites (pīṭhas) and four Buddha bodies (kāyas), japa recitation, and bali offering. It represents one of the earliest Buddhist witnesses to the severed-headed goddess motif shared with the Hindu Chinnamastā tradition.
SA_T02_Virūpa_Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana.attribution: Traditionally attributed to the Mahāsiddha Virūpa (Virūpapāda). The sādhana presents the severed-headed form of Vajrayoginī (Chinnamuṇḍā / Trikāyavajrayoginī) flanked by Vajravarṇanī and Vajravairocanī, closely related to Sādhanamālā nos. 232, 234, and 238, as well as Guhyasamayasādhana no. 25.
SA_T02_Virūpa_Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana.edition: Max Nihom, 'The Goddess with the Severed head: a recension of Sādhanamālā 232, 234 and 238 attributed to the Siddhācārya Virūpā.' In: A. W. van den Hoek, D. H. A. Kolff, M. S. Oort (eds.), Ritual, State and History in South Asia – Essays in Honour of J. C. Heesterman. Leiden: E. J. Brill, 1992, pp. 222–243 (text on pp. 226–229).
SA_T02_Virūpa_Trikāyavajrayoginīsādhana.coverage: complete — Complete ritual text including sections on bhāvanā, pūjā, japa, and bali, concluding with the final dedication and author colophon.

SA_T02_anon_Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā-ms.title: Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā
SA_T02_anon_Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā-ms.author: Subhūtipālita
SA_T02_anon_Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā-ms.summary: The Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā (also designated in the colophons as Bhūtaḍāmarabhaṭṭārakasādhana and Pūrvasevāvidhi) by Subhūtipālita is a Vajrayāna ritual text describing the mandala rite and preparatory service (pūrvasevā) associated with the fierce deity Bhūtaḍāmara. It explains site preparation, boundary protection (sthānarakṣā), deity visualization, ground consecration, mandala draughtsmanship, disciple initiation (abhiṣeka), and homa offerings for achieving various tantric accomplishments (siddhis).
SA_T02_anon_Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā-ms.attribution: Colophon explicitly identifies the author as Subhūtipālita ('kṛtir iyaṃ mahāpaṇḍitamahāmaṇḍalācāryaSubhūtipālitapādānām'). The opening line and scribe/owner note indicate that the codex belonged to the paiṇḍapātika bhikṣu Śīlākaragupta ('pustakeyaṃ paiṇḍapātikabhikṣuŚīlākaraguptasya' / 'pustakeyaṃ bhikṣuśīlākaraguptasyeti').
SA_T02_anon_Bhūtaḍāmaramaṇḍalopāyikā-ms.coverage: complete — Complete ritual text extending from the initial maṅgala verse down to the concluding siddhi rites, colophon, and ownership statement.

SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhabalihomayāga.title: Catuṣpīṭhasādhanasaṃkṣepa (fragment)
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhabalihomayāga.summary: A ritual fragment belonging to the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle covering bali, homa rites, mantras, and mudrās. The manuscript colophon identifies the scribe as Śākyabhikṣu Kumāracandra at the Dharmacakramahāvihāra founded by Guṇakāmadeva during the reign of King Bhāskaradeva.
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhabalihomayāga.attribution: Anonymous ritual text associated with the Catuṣpīṭhatantra. The colophon reads: 'saṃkṣepato balihomayāgavidhayaḥ śrīcatuṣpīṭhatantrāmnāyena likhitā iti || catuṣpīṭhasādhanaṃ saṃ<x ((ṅkha)) x>kṣe + + + samāpteti || samvat a cu hya śrāvaṇaśukladaśamyāṃ śukradine || rājñe śrībhāskaradevasya | śrīguṇakāmadevakāritaśrīdharmacakramahāvihāre sthitaḥ śākyabhikṣukumāracandreṇa likhitam iti'.
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhabalihomayāga.coverage: fragment — Fragment preserved across two folia in NAK 3-359 (NGMPP A 38/8). It contains ritual instructions, verses/songs cited from Catuṣpīṭhatantra 2.3, homa and bali procedures, and scribal colophons.

SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā.title: Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā.author: Caryāvratin
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā.summary: The Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā is a Buddhist tantric manual associated with the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle, composed by Caryāvratin. It details the preparation and rituals for the mandala, including disciple qualification, preliminary service (pūrvasevā), deity visualisations, seed syllables, mudrās, and ritual songs and dances (nṛtya and geya).
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā.attribution: Attributed to Caryāvratīpāda (Caryāvratin) in the closing colophon.
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, 'Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā - Draft Edition -', unpublished critical draft edition based on manuscripts A, B, C, D, T (Balliol College, Oxford).
SA_T02_anon_Catuṣpīṭhamaṇḍalopāyikā.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual running from the opening salutation through the final author colophon at line 1137.

SA_T02_anon_Gaṇacakravidhi.title: Gaṇacakravidhi
SA_T02_anon_Gaṇacakravidhi.summary: An anonymous manual for the gaṇacakra feast and bali offering in the Hevajra tradition. It covers the proper times and places, the qualities of the presiding master, the participants and the karmavajrin, the seating rows, the entrance song in Apabhraṃśa, and the purification of the sacramental substances with HA, HO and HRĪḤ. It ends with verses on enjoying the sacraments as purified passions and on the bliss of the yoginīcakra.
SA_T02_anon_Gaṇacakravidhi.attribution: Anonymous Hevajra-cycle gaṇacakra manual (v. 3: 'gaṇacakravidhiṃ vakṣye baliṃ hevajrasaṃgatam'; homage to Nairātmyā).
SA_T02_anon_Gaṇacakravidhi.coverage: complete — Complete: from the maṅgala ('oṃ namaḥ śrīnairātmikāyai') to the final colophon 'balicakravidhiḥ samāptaḥ'.

SA_T02_anon_Herukasādhopāyikā-SM248.title: Herukasādhanopāyikā
SA_T02_anon_Herukasādhopāyikā-SM248.summary: An anonymous sādhana of the four-faced, four-armed Heruka (Vajraḍāka) embraced by Buddhaḍākinī, following the Mahāmāyātantra. The four directional ḍākinīs (Vajra-, Ratna-, Padma- and Viśvaḍākinī) rouse the deity with an Apabhraṃśa song. The text describes the generation of the deity, ṣaḍaṅga nyāsa, entry of the jñānamaṇḍala, consecration, worship and praise, followed by post-meditative conduct, the amṛtāsvāda food offering and practice at the four junctures of the day. It is no. 248 of the Sādhanamālā.
SA_T02_anon_Herukasādhopāyikā-SM248.attribution: Anonymous sādhana of Heruka in the Mahāmāyā form ('mahāmāyātantrānusāreṇa', colophon). The Dharmamitra header calls it 'Mahāmāyāsādhana (anon)' and equates it with Tōh. 1627.
SA_T02_anon_Herukasādhopāyikā-SM248.edition: Unpublished transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó from manuscript NGMPP B 24/12 (digital images DSCN9071 ff., as given in the header), keyed to Bhattacharyya's Sādhanamālā numbering (no. 248).
SA_T02_anon_Herukasādhopāyikā-SM248.coverage: complete — Complete (segs. 3–108), from 'vajraḍākaṃ namaskṛtya' to the colophon 'mahāmāyātantrānusāreṇa herukasādhanopayikā samāptā'. Segs. 0–2 are PDSz header lines.
translations: sgyu 'phrul chen mo'i rgyud kyi rjes su 'brang ba'i he ru ka'i sgrub pa'i thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1627) (Tibetan)

SA_T02_anon_Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi.title: Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi
SA_T02_anon_Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi.summary: The Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi (also known as Saṃkṣiptahevajrapūjāvidhi) is a concise Tantric Buddhist ritual manual detailing the external worship (bāhyapūjā) of the sixteen-armed Hevajra and his retinue, including Nairātmyā, the eight goddesses (Gaurī, Caurī, Vetālī, Ghasmarī, Pukkasī, Śabarī, Caṇḍālī, Ḍombī), and the guardian deities of the eight cremation grounds (aṣṭaśmaśāna). The liturgy prescribes visualisations, protective mantras, flower offerings, the eight-line praise, the mālāmantra, and concludes with a samayagīti ('kollaïre ṭṭhia bola...') and dismission rites.
SA_T02_anon_Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi.attribution: No author is named in the text or colophon; the author refers to themselves in the first person in the opening and closing verses.
SA_T02_anon_Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi.edition: Manuscript transcription based on Berlin, Staatsbibliothek Preußischer Kulturbesitz (PSB) Hs. or. sim. 1504 [= NGMPP X 1504/1], palm-leaf manuscript originally from the private collection of Śrī Hemrāj Śākyavaṃśa, Patan (Devanāgarī copy in the collection of Dr. Gustav Roth, Göttingen), transcribed by Péter-Dániel Szántó.
SA_T02_anon_Hevajrabāhyapūjāvidhi.coverage: complete — Complete ritual manual concluding with the colophon 'saṃkṣiptahevajrapūjāvidhiḥ samāptaḥ' and the ye dharmā formula.

SA_T02_anon_Pratipattisāraśataka.title: Pratipattisāraśataka (second half)
SA_T02_anon_Pratipattisāraśataka.author: Āryadeva
SA_T02_anon_Pratipattisāraśataka.summary: The Pratipattisāraśataka is a Vajrayāna treatise attributed to Āryadeva dealing with the wisdom of bliss and emptiness in the context of the Hevajra Tantra, prajñā and upāya, the avadhūtī channel, and the ultimate interpretation of the pāramitās. In Sanskrit it survives in a fragmentary Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript containing the second half.
SA_T02_anon_Pratipattisāraśataka.attribution: Attributed in the scribal colophon to Āryadevapāda.
SA_T02_anon_Pratipattisāraśataka.edition: Diplomatic transcription and working edition by Péter-Dániel Szántó from Kathmandu, National Archives of Nepal (NAK) ms. 1-1697 (vi bauddhastotra 14) / NGMPP reel B 24/27 (palm-leaf, 3 ff. [4–6], Gauḍīya script).
SA_T02_anon_Pratipattisāraśataka.coverage: partial — Folios 4r–6v (56 verses, numbered x+1 to x+56) of an original manuscript likely consisting of 6 folios; covers the second half of the work.
translations: go bar byed pa snying po brgya pa (Derge Tengyur D 2334): translated by Vanaratna, byams gling paN chen bsod nams rnam rgyal (Tibetan)

SA_T02_anon_Vajradhātumukhākhyāna.title: Vajradhātumukhākhyāna
SA_T02_anon_Vajradhātumukhākhyāna.summary: The Vajradhātumukhākhyāna is an illustrated ritual handbook (vidhi) preserved in the Newar Buddhist tradition of Nepal. It details the liturgy, mantras, protective circles (rakṣācakra), nyāsa rituals, and hand gestures (mudrā) associated with the Vajradhātumaṇḍala. In Nepalese manuscript culture, copies of this handbook typically accompany iconographical drawings illustrating the mudrās and deities of the Vajradhātu system.
SA_T02_anon_Vajradhātumukhākhyāna.attribution: An anonymous Newar Buddhist ritual and iconographical manual associated with Vajradhātumaṇḍala practice.
SA_T02_anon_Vajradhātumukhākhyāna.edition: Diplomatic transcript by Péter-Dániel Szántó (dated 2009-01-15, Bombay) based on manuscript Asha Archives MS 2334 (Kathmandu). Unpublished e-text.
SA_T02_anon_Vajradhātumukhākhyāna.coverage: unclear — Diplomatic transcription of MS Asha Archives 2334 (pages 1–43); contains liturgical formulas, mudrā descriptions, and markers for illustrations, breaking off without a formal final colophon.

SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbaramukhākhyāna.title: Yogāmbaramukhākhyāna
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbaramukhākhyāna.summary: A short Vajrayāna Buddhist ritual manual (pūjāvidhi/sādhana) dedicated to the tantric deity Yogāmbara, a central figure in the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle. The work details introductory salutations, seed-syllables, hand and sense purification, protective circle formation, maṇḍala visualization, offerings, and dohās in mixed Sanskrit and Apabhraṃśa.
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbaramukhākhyāna.attribution: Anonymous Buddhist tantric ritual text centered on Yogāmbara, connected to the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle.
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbaramukhākhyāna.edition: Diplomatic manuscript transcription of National Archives Kathmandu MS 4-258 (NGMPP reel 119/14) by Péter-Dániel Szántó, unpublished e-text (PDSz corpus).
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbaramukhākhyāna.coverage: complete — Complete transcription of the manuscript NAK 4-258 / NGMPP 119/14 (ends 8v1), ending with the colophon and concluding ritual verses.

SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā.title: Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā (incomplete; with fragments of other works)
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā.summary: The Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā ('Ratnamālā') is an anonymous Catuṣpīṭha-cycle text, written by a disciple of Kalyāṇavarman. The sole source for this text is an incomplete Sanskrit manuscript in a composite codex.
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā.attribution: Anonymous. In the opening verses the author honours Nāgārjuna. He provides an essential clue that he was a disciple of Kalyāṇavarman, who Szántó suggests is most likely the same as the author of the Catuṣpīṭha Pañjikā.
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā.edition: Péter-Dániel Szántó, Selected Chapters from the Catuṣpīṭhatantra, DPhil thesis, University of Oxford, 2012, §3.4.15 'The Ratnamālā (anonymous) with fragments'.
SA_T02_anon_Yogāmbarīsādhanaratnamālā.coverage: partial — Szántó proposes that of what must have been twenty leaves, extant are fols. 1–6, 8, 11–12, and others. The text is incomplete and found in a composite codex with fragments of other works.

SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Catuṣpīṭhamantr.title: Catuṣpīṭhamantrāṃśa (chapter 4 onwards)
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Catuṣpīṭhamantr.summary: An explanatory tantra (bshad pa'i rgyud) associated with the Catuṣpīṭhatantra cycle, dealing with mantra practices, yoga, and ritual.
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Catuṣpīṭhamantr.attribution: Scriptural explanatory tantra (bshad pa'i rgyud); catalogued under Āryadeva tāntrika in source header.
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Catuṣpīṭhamantr.coverage: partial — Contains from chapter 4, verse 1 onwards through chapter 7, concluding with Tibetan text.
translations: dpal gdan bzhi pa'i rnam par bshad pa'i rgyud kyi rgyal po zhes bya ba (Derge Kangyur D 430): translated by Smṛtijñānakīrti (Tibetan)

SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Pañcakrama-unid.title: Unidentified work in the Pañcakrama tradition (fragment)
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Pañcakrama-unid.summary: A brief metrical Buddhist tantric fragment (18 complete verses and one incomplete line) expounding internal yogic practices associated with the Guhyasamāja completion stage (Pañcakrama). It discusses the control of vital winds (prāṇavāyu), vajrajāpa, the experience of clear light (prabhāsvara), the realization of all phenomena as devoid of inherent existence (sarvaśūnya) and like an illusion (māyā/svapna), and the attainment of the unified state (yuganaddha).
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Pañcakrama-unid.attribution: Unidentified and anonymous in the manuscript. The tentative attribution to Āryadeva-tāntrika in earlier metadata has no manuscript basis.
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Pañcakrama-unid.edition: Unpublished diplomatic transcription by Péter-Dániel Szántó from Kathmandu, National Archives, MS 1-1697 (NGMPP reel B 31/6), ff. 29r1–30v.
SA_T02_Āryadeva-tāntrika_Pañcakrama-unid.coverage: fragment — Preserves verses 1–18 and the beginning of verse 19 (fol. 29r–30v of NAK 1-1697), breaking off abruptly at 'iti kurva[]'.

SA_T02_Ḍombīheruka_Amṛtaprabhā-sādhanopā.title: Amṛtaprabhāsādhanopāyikā
SA_T02_Ḍombīheruka_Amṛtaprabhā-sādhanopā.author: Ḍombīheruka
SA_T02_Ḍombīheruka_Amṛtaprabhā-sādhanopā.summary: The Amṛtaprabhāsādhanopāyikā is a Vajrayāna ritual text detailing the visualization and realization of the fifteen-deity maṇḍala of Nairātmyā, based on the Hevajratantra. Attributed to the mahāsiddha Ḍombīheruka, it guides the practitioner through the protective circle, bījamantras of the yoginīs, generation stage (utpattikrama), and completion stage (utpannakrama).
SA_T02_Ḍombīheruka_Amṛtaprabhā-sādhanopā.attribution: Explicitly attributed in verse 1 (ḍombīherukapādair devīcakrasya bhāvanā kathitā) and in the final verses mentioning the author riding a tiger and ornamented with serpents.
SA_T02_Ḍombīheruka_Amṛtaprabhā-sādhanopā.coverage: complete — Text of the sādhanopāyikā concluding with the colophon '|| amṛtaprabhā nāma sādhanopāyikā samāptā ||'.
translations: bdag med ma'i dkyil 'khor gyi 'khor lo'i sgrub thabs (Derge Tengyur D 1313) (Tibetan)
